He topped the charts last Ranji Trophy season with 950 runs, yet that was not enough to earn a place in the India A side for the two unofficial Tests against Australia A. Smaran, 23, is not thinking about call-ups. Im not expecting any call-ups from India A. Honestly, Im just looking to score as many runs as possible, help my team and win every trophy that we have. I cant think about what can happen in the future. Its not in my hands. The goal doesnt change. In the Ranji Trophy, my goal is to score 1,000 runs and be back-to-back on the top of the run-scorers list. Red-ball cricket is not the only format he thinks about. His century in the final won Karnataka a fifth Vijay Hazare Trophy title in 2025, and his T20 strike rate is 155.82. It is a very good challenge for guys who want to excel in three formats. In this day and age, T20 has gone to a whole other level, where the demands are entirely different. You have to get your strike rate to more than 200. As batters who want to play three formats, we also have to evolve and ensure that we are right up there. We have to be in pace with the demands of the game. ALSO READ Barbed wire, sniffer dogs and 40 years of waiting Srinagar readies for Irani Cup Smaran is yet to make his mark in the IPL, but he finds a link between his Sunrisers Hyderabad stint and his red-ball batting. Definitely, IPL has improved my game. Even in red-ball games, there are situations where you have to take on bowlers, like today. The white-ball game of mine came into play when I was batting with the tail. His one let-off came on 104, when Umar Nazir had him lbw off a no-ball. His father, Ravichandran S, and his coach, Syed Zabiullah, were watching from the stands. Im really grateful that I could get a hundred in front of them, he said. Rest of India lead by 265 runs. The Ranji Trophy champions have won the last two editions of the Irani Cup. Smaran may have just rewritten the script. Brief scores Rest of India 237 3068 Ravichandran Smaran 126 not out Sahil Lotra 371 lead Jammu Kashmir 278 by 265 runs.

articleTitle: ABVP seeks Ashoka Chakra for Captain Smit Machchhar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Smit Machchhar Ashoka Chakra
description: The Ashoka Chakra is India's top peacetime award for extreme bravery and self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.
body_raw: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ABVP, after its All-India Office Bearers Meeting in Itanagar on Saturday, called on the Indian government to honour Captain Smit Machchhar with the Ashoka Chakra, for his exemplary courage in averting a catastrophic mid-air disaster earlier this week. Machchhar, an Indian commercial pilot, was commanding flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv when the aircrafts co-pilot allegedly attacked him in an attempt to hijack or crash the plane. During the violent struggle, the Boeing 737 MAX plummeted nearly 14,000 ft in less than 30 seconds. Despite his injuries, the 39-year-old fought back and managed to unlock the cockpit door, allowing alert passengers and crew to storm in and overpower the attacker. Two off-duty flydubai pilots, who were travelling as passengers, then helped level the aircraft, which was carrying 174 passengers, and diverted it for an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The incident had made headlines across the world and Machchhar was hailed globally as a hero for averting a disaster and saving hundreds of lives. The Ashoka Chakra is Indias top peacetime award for extreme bravery and self-sacrifice away from the battlefield. Civilians are eligible for the decoration and there is no requirement that the act of gallantry take place in India. Incidentally, there are historical precedents for Indian civilian aviation personnel receiving the Ashoka Chakra during emergencies abroad. In 1987, Pan Am flight attendant Neerja Bhanot was posthumously awarded the Ashoka Chakra for her actions during the hijacking of Pan Am Flight 73 at Karachi the previous year. D N Jatar, captain of the Air India-chartered Kashmir Princess, was awarded the Ashoka Chakra after the aircraft was bombed in 1955 while flying from Hong Kong to Jakarta. Jatar, who died in the crash, was among the earliest civilian recipients of the award. The ABVP meeting, held on October 2 and 3, was its first All India Office Bearers Meeting in Itanagar. A substantial part of it dwelled on the recent student elections, wherein ABVP made significant gains, most notably, at Delhi and Panjab Universities, where it won the presidents post. In Uttarakhand, the organisation emerged victorious in 64 of the 92 colleges that went to polls there, securing the presidents post in 54 of them and at Haryana University, 33 of the 38 seats. The student wing of the RSS, ABVP also claimed a clean sweep of all 14 seats at Sanskrit College in Kerala, and won three seats at Gauhati University. ABVP National General Secretary Virendra Singh Solanki said, Indias Gen-Z is rooted in values, has a nationalist outlook and believes in social harmony. ABVPs success at Panjab University, Delhi University, Kerala, Uttarakhand and various other campuses reflects the active participation of this young generation, Solanki said. The discussions also covered the state of hostels in Arunachal Pradesh and the Northeast, scholarships, student union elections, the organisations All India Student Hostel Survey 2026, and upcoming campaigns.

articleTitle: AAP MLA flags teacher shortage in govt school his son goes to, party suspends him
articleFeaturedImageAlt: **Aam Aadmi Party suspends Maur Member of Legislative Assembly Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana over anti-party activities after video flags teacher shortage in Punjab government schools**
description: Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana is the only MLA in the 117-member Punjab Vidhan Sabha who sends both his children to government schools
body_raw: The Aam Aadmi Party AAP on Saturday suspended Maur MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana for alleged anti-party activities, barely an hour after he released an emotional video accusing the Punjab government of failing to address teacher shortage in state-run schools, including those attended by his two children. Maiserkhana is the only MLA in 117-member Punjab Assembly who sends both his children to government schools, an investigation by The Indian Express had found in March this year. The suspension order, issued by AAP state general secretary Harchand Singh Barsat, read It has come to the notice.that you have been found involved in anti-party activities and indiscipline. In view of the above, your primary membership from the party is suspended with immediate effect. Going live on Facebook, the first-time MLA said he regretted enrolling his children in government schools, claiming their future was at stake because of the shortage of teachers. Maiserkhana alleged that repeated pleas to senior party leaders, including former Delhi education minister and Punjab affairs in-charge Manish Sisodia, had failed to resolve the shortage. The MLA further claimed that even Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann did not meet him. How long will I tolerate? What did I do wrong to the party? he said, adding the party leaderships apathy forced him to raise the issue publicly. The AAP MLA said he knows he will be denied a ticket for contesting the upcoming polls. But I will continue to fight for people, he said and added that he may be booked too. My children study where the children of 3 crore common Punjabis also study. and thats why I am speaking today as a father. The future of my children is at stake. The issue of teacher shortage is not being addressed in the schools where my children study, he said. Questioning the governments claims of an education revolution, he said even the Schools of Eminence, set up by the AAP government as model institutions, lacked adequate teachers. I have got tired of saying that please give teachers, please give teachers. I called Manish Sisodia and told him that my kids study in government schools and even in those schools, there arent enough teachers.I always worked for the partys betterment. and now they are isolating and ignoring me, removing me from everywhere. Why? Just because I am fighting for the schools, for my own children, and for the children of all those who send their children to government schools, he said. Declaring that he would not remain silent, Maiserkhana dared the government to do wrong to me, but not my children. If nothing has been done in schools, how will we ask for votes from people? In entire Punjab, I am the only MLA whose kids study in government schools. If I wont raise voice, who will? Did I do anything wrong by enrolling my kids in a government school? I think it was a big mistake. Arrest and jail me but I will speak for my and peoples children who study in government schools, he added. Maiserkhanas son is enrolled in a School of Eminence in Bathinda district and the daughter in another state-run primary school. AAP insiders meanwhile claimed that the MLAs outburst came after he got to know that the party would be denying him ticket for 2027 polls due to non-performance. The AAP, in an official statement, denied the allegations and said Maiserkhana had attempted to defame the party by making a false statement that only one teacher was doing duty at the School of Eminence in Bathinda. The claim was contrary to the official record issued by the school principal on September 29, 2026. According to the record, the school has 30 sanctioned teaching posts, of which 25 are currently filled. The staff posted at the school includes one principal, seven lecturers, 15 teachers from the Master Cadre and two Computer Science teachers. The school currently has 580 students studying from Classes 6 to 12 across 19 sections, read the statement. It said five sanctioned posts are presently vacant, and the school principal has already submitted a written request for filling these vacancies and sanctioning additional posts wherever required. The official record clearly establishes that the claim of there being only one teacher in the entire school was factually incorrect, the party statement said, and reiterated that discipline is paramount in the organisation and that every elected representative is expected to uphold the partys principles and maintain factual accuracy while speaking in public. Attempts to spread misinformation among the public or damage the partys image would not be tolerated, irrespective of the position held by the person concerned, it added. Latching on to Maiserkhanas statement, the BJP said the AAP MLAs remarks have punctured the education revolution narrative by the ruling party in the state. Former Union Minister Ravneet Singh Bittu said the ruling partys MLAs tears expose the ground reality in state. When a ruling-party MLA has to come on social media and appeal for adequate teachers in schools in his own constituency, it raises serious questions about the situation faced by ordinary families and lakhs of students across Punjab, Bittu wrote on X. SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal said AAPs fake Sikhya Kranti has been exposed by its own MLA. Four years on, they cant even provide teachers in classrooms. What is the point of renaming schools as Schools of Eminence when there are no basic facilities? Their own MLA says his children complain about the lack of teachers principals come begging, but the government doesnt listen. Instead of wasting crores of rupees in the advertisement of these schools, they should have recruited the staff, Badal said. Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh said, What we have been saying for the past four and a half years, the AAPs false education revolution built on publicity and its dictatorship has today been laid bare by Maiserkhana himself. Like many Punjabis, Maiserkhana too had been influenced by AAPs Delhi model and its false claims of an education revolution. Today, he himself has brought to light the reality of teachers and facilities in schools, he said Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa too said that a sitting AAP MLA says he has repeatedly raised basic issues like repairing schools and appointing teachers, yet nobody listened. Now, he says that despite being a sitting MLA of the ruling party, he cannot even get an appointment with the chief minister. If an Aam Aadmi MLA cannot even meet his own chief minister, then what does that say about the ordinary people who are trying to be heard?, Randhawa asked. The Indian Express investigation in March had found that during the 2025-26 academic session, 36 MLAs had school-going children, including 31 from the AAP, but the others sent their wards to private schools in India or institutions abroad. Maiserkhana, an agriculturist by profession, had won the Maur seat in Bathinda district by a margin of more than 35,000 votes in 2022. When asked by The Indian Express why he had chosen government schools for his children, Maiserkhana had said If we wont admit our own children in government schools, how can we convince the people to do that? That is how chain reaction starts. 50 more parents had followed me. He had said the decision was intended to keep his children connected to their community and mother tongue and build public confidence in government schools. He shifted his son from a local convent school to a government school during the Covid pandemic, while his daughter was enrolled directly in a state-run school.

articleTitle: Asian Games hockey: Why the men’s gold tells the tale of triumph and relief
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gold medallist Indian players, from left, Vivek Sagar Prasad, Manpreet Singh, Yashdeep Siwach, Hardik Singh, Rajinder Singh and Mohith HS during the medal ceremony after the men's final hockey match, at the ongoing 20th Asian Games, in Kakamigahara, Japan, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. (PTI Photo/Atul Yadav) (PTI10_03_2026_000555A) *** Local Caption ***
description: India defended men's hockey gold for the first time in Asian Games' history, but fewer field goals and defence shrinking to shell are worrying
body_raw: As the final hooter blew in Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, India mens hockey team started celebrating after winning the Asian Games gold defeating Malaysia 5-1. The celebration had mixed hues of triumph and relief. Triumph because the gold medal from last edition was defended and an Olympic berth for 2028 was secured relief because the win salvaged some pride in an otherwise disappointing year. The gold was historic in the sense this is the first time the Indian mens hockey team have defended their gold medal in the Asian Games. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage In the final against Malaysia, it was a near flawless performance with the Indian forward-line scoring five goals past Malaysia. The 14th-minute field goal from Shello Silverius being the only blip. Skipper Harmanpreet Singh opened the scoring in the 11th minute with his impeccable flick that breached the Malaysian defence but Shello restored the parity in the 14th minute as Indian defence switched off for a moment. Jugraj Singh made it 2-1 in the 23rd minute with another thunderous drag-flick and India went into the halftime with a 2-1 lead. India penetrated deep inside the Malaysian defence multiple times in the third quarter but the only goal came when Hardik Singh wrongfooted goalkeeper Mat Zalmi to score the penalty stroke, which was awarded after a deflection from Mandeep Singh hit the Malaysian defender on the face. The Indian team was relentless in the last quarter with seven penalty corners but India converted only one after Harmanpreet scored in the 57th minute, the last nail in the coffin for the Malaysian hopes. Youngster Shilanand Lakra had already given India a big cushion with a well taken field goal in the 54th minute. There is nothing much to write about the overall campaign apart from the fact that it was the only way for India to mask the disappointment at the World Cup earlier this year and the poor show in the FIH Pro League. At the Asian Games, India was troubled in just one game, which was against Pakistan. The arch-rivals produced a thrilling match after ages. Going into the shell The match just exposed the long-sitting problems in the Indian defence. The Indian defence goes into shell the moment the opposition starts attacking with intensity. Against Pakistan, India were leading 3-0 but went down to 3-3 and constantly lost shape in the fourth quarter before a late strike from Abhishek saved the day. A team that was deemed fittest at one point of time now struggles to catch breath at times in the fourth quarter. It was not the case against Malaysia today, but it is there every time the opposition starts attacking in the last quarter. Coach Craig Fultons mantra is to defend to win. But the team is winning right now but are not able to defend conceding to the likes of Indonesia and Sri Lanka. Field goals paucity If you look at the statistics from the tournament, India scored 58 goals from seven games. The breakup of the goals read 34 field goals, 20 penalty corners, and four penalty strokes. On paper, the stay looks really good but in reality, India scored those 30 field goals against oppositions like Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh. Only four field goals came against Pakistan, Malaysia and Japan. India had to rely on penalty corners once a quality defence came up against them. Out of 47 goals against Indonesia, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Korea, India scored overwhelmingly 30 field goals and only 17 penalty corners and strokes. But against Pakistan, Malaysia, and Japan, India scored seven penalty corners and strokes and just four field goals. India needs to find more field goals or more ways to break oppositions defence when things start getting tough instead of relying just on Harmanpreet or Jugraj to score a penalty corner. All is not lost on the team though. With 2028 Olympics qualification done, the Indian team and coach Fulton have a lot of time on their hands to go back to the drawing board and fix things if they want to continue the Olympic medal winning streak at Los Angeles. Nevertheless, the gold had many meanings today, for the Indian team it meant salvaging a poor year overall.

articleTitle: Parliamentary Committees reshuffle: TMC loses both chairperson posts
articleFeaturedImageAlt: dola sen, kirti azad, tmc,
description: The Parliamentary Committee on Commerce, which was headed by TMC Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen has now gone to BJP Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi.
body_raw: In a major reshuffle of chairpersons of six of the 24 Standing Parliamentary Committees, the Trinamool Congress on Saturday lost both its chairperson berths owing to a group of their MPs switching camps after the recently concluded West Bengal Assembly elections. The Parliamentary Committee on Commerce, which was headed by TMC Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen will now be headed by BJP Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi. The Committee on Chemicals, which was headed by TMC MP Kirti Azad, will now be headed by Lok Sabha MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, who led the TMC rebel faction and claimed to have merged with lesser-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India NCPI. Soon after the BJP swept the West Bengal Assembly elections in May, a group of TMC MPs led by Dastidar approached the Speaker, claiming that they had merged with the NCPI, a Tripura-based outfit, and sought to be recognised as a separate bloc in Lok Sabha. A decision on the breakaway factions fate is pending before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. TMC slams move Reacting strongly to the reshuffle, TMC Parliamentary Leader Derek OBrien wrote a letter to Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan, saying that the Parliament is being turned into a deep, dark chamber. The leader of the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction maintained that theirs is the third largest party in the Upper House, but is being deprived of a chairperson berth. In Rajya Sabha, the BJP is the largest party, followed by the INC second largest and AITC third largest. And yet, the Chairpersonship, which we held in 2024-25 and 2025-26, has been taken away. This is not the first time we have been treated in this manner In 2019, when we were also the third largest party in Rajya Sabha, we were deprived. That was rectified a few years later and now it is back to square one, said the TMC leader in his letter. Other panel chief changes Other changes announced by Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Saturday include Congress Rajya Sabha member Digvijaya Singh being replaced by party colleague Mukul Wasnik to head the committee on education. Meanwhile, the BJP has reshuffled three of its committee chairpersons, with party MP Brij Lal being replaced by party colleague Sujeet Kumar to head the committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice. Rajya Sabha member Brij Lals term in the Upper House is set to end in November. The BJP has replaced Lok Sabha MP Basavaraj Bommai with Shashank Mani to head the Labour, Textiles and Skill Development Committee. The third change that the BJP has made is in the Committee on Railways, with the party appointing its MP Sudhir Gupta instead of C M Ramesh. Those retained Among those who have retained their chairpersonships include DMK MPs Tiruchi Siva and K Kanimozhi who will continue to head the Parliamentary Committee on Industry, and the Committee on Food, Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution, respectively. Congress MPs Shashi Tharoor and Charanjit Singh Channi, have also been retained as chairpersons of Committees on External Affairs, and Agriculture, respectively. Meanwhile, party MP Mukul Wasnik will continue to head the Committee on Education, Women, Children and Youth. Samajwadi Partys Ram Gopal Yadav has also been retained as the chairperson of the Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The leaders of some key BJP allies such as the JDU, Shiv Sena and TDP have also been retained as heads of different Parliamentary Committees. The Parliament has a total of 24 department-related Standing Committees with members from both the Houses while eight come under the Rajya Sabha Chairman, the other 16 are under the Lok Sabha Speaker. The Committees serve a one-year term, after which they are reconstituted.

articleTitle: In tit-for-tat move, India, Pakistan summon top envoys
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India-Pakistan Ferozepur infiltration
description: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) also rejected the “baseless and motivated allegations” by Pakistan regarding an incident in Punjab’s Ferozepur sector along the International Border on Friday.
body_raw: A day after the Border Security Force BSF killed two suspected Pakistani intruders along the International Border in Punjabs Tarn Taran district, India and Pakistan summoned each others Charge dAffaires and lodged strong protests on Saturday. While India protested over the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration, Pakistan claimed the two who were killed were unarmed civilians. The Pakistani diplomat in Delhi was summoned hours after Islamabad summoned the Indian official there. The Ministry of External Affairs MEA today summoned the Charg dAffaires of the Pakistan High Commission to lodge Indias strong protest over the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan. India also categorically rejected the baseless and motivated allegations regarding an incident in the Ferozepur sector, Punjab, along the International Border on October 2, 2026, the MEA said in a statement. It said the Pakistani side was informed that three individuals infiltrated into Indian territory and despite multiple warnings by BSF to return to Pakistan, continued to move towards the border fence. The BSF was compelled to engage them for posing an imminent security threat. The MEA said the incident highlights a clear pattern of repeated cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan. Government of Pakistan was urged to investigate these cross-border infiltration, drug smuggling activities and the complicity of Pakistan border guarding forces therein, and to take appropriate remedial measures. It said Pakistan was further urged to ensure respect for the sanctity of the International Border, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements, mandate its forces to exercise effective control to prevent unauthorised movement from its side, and take definitive measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents. Meanwhile, the Pakistan Foreign Office said the Indian Charge dAffaires was summoned to its Ministry of Foreign Affairs to lodge Pakistans strong protest over the killing. The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives, it said. It further said the incident amounted to a serious violation of fundamental human rights, including the right to life, and raised serious concerns regarding the protection of civilian life under international law. It called upon the Indian side to conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation into the incident, take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against those found responsible, and formally communicate the findings and action taken to the Pakistani government. With PTI inputs from Islamabad

articleTitle: Maximum temperature rises in Pune as rains stay away
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Heat
description: Across Maharashtra, the maximum temperature is above normal. The highest maximum temperature on Saturday was recorded at Malegaon, 38.4 degrees Celsius, which was 5.9 degrees Celsius above normal.
body_raw: The maximum temperature in Punes Shivajinagar touched 34.8 degrees Celsius on Saturday, 3.5 degrees Celsius above normal for the weather station. In Lohegaon, the maximum temperature was 4.1 degrees Celsius above normal, at 35.4 degrees Celsius. The daytime temperature was around 34.7 degrees Celsius in Chinchwad and Wadgaonsheri, among others, on Saturday. Hadapsar, NDA, Pashan and Magarpatta recorded marginally lower maximum tenperatures, around 33.5 degrees Celsius. This comes even as the India Meteorological Department IMD has announced that, in October, maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal in most parts of the country except some regions of the northeast India and isolated pockets of central and northwest India where normal maximum temperatures are expected. Across Maharashtra, the maximum temperature is above normal. The highest maximum temperature on Saturday was recorded at Malegaon, 38.4 degrees Celsius, which was 5.9 degrees Celsius above normal. IMD said that the 24 hour rainfall on Saturday morning was nil across the city, except in Talegaon, where 21 mm of rain had fallen. The weather office has also said that there is unlikely to be any rain in Pune and its suburbs in the days till October 9 at least. During this time, there will be mainly clear sky that could become cloudy as the day progresses. According the IMD, the maximum temperature is likely to rise to 36 degrees Celsius over the next few days at almost all weather stations, from Shivajinagar, Pashan and Lohegaon to Chinchwad, Magarpatta and Koregaon Park. The minimum temperature is still normal or almost normal in most of Maharashtra. Shivajinagar recorded 21.1 degrees Celsius morning temperature on Saturday, which was 0.5 degrees Celsius above normal, while Lohegaons minimum temperature of 21.9 degrees Celsius was 1.3 degrees Celsius above normal. Magarpatta abd Chinchwad experienced the warmest morning in the city on Saturday, recording 25.3 degrees Celsius and 23.8 degrees Celsius, respectively. Jalgaon, in Central Maharashtra, recorded a minimum temperature of 17.2 degrees Celsius, which was 4.1 degrees Celsius below normal and the lowest minimum temperature recorded in the state on Saturday. IMD says that the city is likely to feel around degrees Celsius warm in the mornings for the next few days though some parts of the city, such as Magarpatta and Chinchwad are expected to record minimum temperatures of 24 degrees Celsius some days till October 9.

articleTitle: India show spark, create some chances, but Brazil a cut above on big day
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Samuel Lino scored the first two goals of his international career (Express Photo By Partha Paul)
description: Brace from Samuel Lino and goals from Pedro and Estevao Willian script 4-0 win for five-time football world champions
body_raw: The last time a world-famous South American star set foot at Salt Lake Stadium, the occasion was marked by unimaginable chaos at the Lionel Messi event late last year, when disgruntled fans took out their ire on the fixtures and fittings of the hallowed venue. On Saturday, some of the stain was washed away as soon as the Hino Nacional Brasileiro was played. History was made when the five-time football world champions played their first-ever match against India. Though India conceded four unanswered goals, there were encouraging signs from Khalid Jamils men, especially in the early stages. But the game also showed how far India still has to go to be considered on an equal footing with the elites. Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti had said in the build-up to the match that there are no friendlies for the Selecao. Even then, there was scepticism over whether he would risk his big names in a match against the 138th-ranked team, especially with big clubs anxious about the fitness of their star players as the international window comes to a close. But the Italian fielded a relatively strong side, handing starts to Vinicius Jr, who garnered the biggest cheer from the crowd, Marquinhos and Estevao. The Blue Tigers started brightly, even going toe to toe with Brazil on occasions with Apuia Ralte coming closest for India when his long-ranger just went dangerously past the Brazilian post. They were even finding spaces in the visitors half but indecision in the final third cost them. India also earned four corners in the first half, just one less than Brazil. The Indian backline, meanwhile, employed the offside trap expertly, limiting the ever-sprightly Vinicius to just one big chance in the early stages, which drew a save out of goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu at his near post. But as the match progressed, Brazil wrested control. The gulf in quality became apparent when Estevao, who had missed a chance in just the second minute, opened the scoring in the 28th, skipping past Ashique Kuruniyan and smashing his shot past Gurpreet, who got a hand to it but couldnt keep it out. Pedro doubled Brazils lead when he latched on to a pass from Estevao and let fly at Gurpreet. The ball went under the keepers palms and trickled into the net. Predictable After halftime, Brazil made as many as four changes, withdrawing Vinicius and bringing on Flamengos Samuel Dias Lino. Premier League stars and regular Selecao starters Arsenals Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes were introduced in defence and midfield respectively. Jamil made three changes as well with the biggest being subbing off Gurpreet for Prabhsukhan Singh Gill. The second half followed the same script as the first with India getting two early chances through Manvir Singh and Ryan Williams, squandering both, before Brazil made them pay with a curler from Samuel, making it 3-0 in the 58th minute. India had a great chance of reducing the margin and scripting a big moment in the 63rd minute, but a goalmouth melee resulted in a Brazilian clearance off the line. Williams got another opportunity four minutes later when Manvir floated in another delicious ball from the left but the volley couldnt get the desired impact. Manvir got another chance of his own in the 74th minute but his shot aimed at the near post went over the bar. Thereafter, the match settled into a pattern in which Brazil poured forward, kept the ball and made the Indians chase shadows. The Selecao came close to a fourth goal twice in added time as Gill pulled off a spectacular save off a rocket from Vanderson before another effort hit the side-netting. India, however, could not hold on as Samuel made it four with a low drive, incidentally the last shot of the game, past Gill and into the Indian net. India were valiant, even making fans believe in moments, but the result, if not the scoreline, was written in the stars as soon as the fixture was announced in July.

articleTitle: Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 chases down 352 as India’s bowling leaves questions
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shai Hope played captain's knock, leading his team to a win with an unbeaten 162 vs India during 3rd ODI in New Chandigarh. (Express Photo by Kamleshwar Singh)
description: KL Rahul's century and Rohit Sharma's 92 went in vain as West Indies won by five wickets in the first men's ODI at the New PCA Stadium
body_raw: The New PCA Stadium was decked up for its first mens ODI, expecting local boy Shubman Gill to extend his dream streak. The law of averages was cruelly overdue after West Indies had dismissed him only once in 241 deliveries in two games. Gill deprived his home crowd of a spectacle. Instead, the day belonged to his counterpart Shai Hope, who watched Gill butcher a 406-run chase from behind the stumps three nights ago in Guwahati. Switching positions three times in six days, Hope went back to his sweetest spot at the top. He made his fifth century against India, his highest score at 162 not out, to power a consolation five-wicket win in an emphatic 352-run chase on Saturday. The Indian team management ticked off a few boxes on its batting wish-list, through a sparkling KL Rahul century and Rohit Sharmas 92. The bowling unit left more questions unanswered in a botched defence. Despite a batting order trimmed by injuries, the Windies top order kept Gills bowlers on their toes, matching the asking rate from the start. Indias new-ball struggles eased briefly when Sirajs inswinger castled John Campbell in the fifth over. The search for able back-ups hit a wall again when Hope and Amir Jangoo took apart debutant Anshul Kamboj in his opening spell. Kamboj had been pulled out midway through India As first-class fixture in Pondicherry on Thursday as Prasidh Krishnas replacement. He leaked 41 in five overs. ALSO READ Averages 68.58 at 5, four hundreds, best strike rate after AB KL Rahul is Indias Mr Indispensable Only a run-out, from Virat Kohlis quick reflexes, looked likely to end Jangoos 111-run association with Hope. Kuldeep Yadav skimmed without reward, and Naman Dhir emerged as an unlikely wicket-taker with a contentious caught-behind. Moving up from No. 3 in the previous game, Hope moved smoothly towards his fifth century against India and a second in succession. With few proven hitters in the lower half, an injury to Jewel Andrew and cramps in his legs, Hope slowed down drastically, taking 44 balls without a boundary from 87 to 126. That phase partly dented the chase before the captain waded into the last four overs. Gurnoor Brar and Kamboj traded control for a batch of looseners, and Hope and Gudakesh Motie carted them for eight boundaries in 14 deliveries, which took the chase away. Earlier, a full reveal of the middle order brought India a fourth centurion of the series in KL Rahul, who walked out with the bat for the first time this series. He picked up from where Rohit stopped, after Rohit had braved a sharpened new-ball barrage on length from the West Indies pacers. Jayden Seales and Matthew Forde combined to tempt Gill into an unusual adventure early on. It took only four consistent length deliveries before Gill impatiently missed a charged slap through cover. Seales pounded the deck harder next time, the angle cramping Gill as he nicked behind his hips to the keeper. Virat Kohli was gone the next ball, his fourth golden duck in over 300 outings, when Seales vicious in-ducker found the middle stump. With the pacers lengths rarely overspilling, Rohit measured his release after a watchful spell and pulled impulsively for six over square-leg in the 12th over, though the vision behind his favourite shot has fluctuated this series. He had nearly fallen to the stadium DJs plea for a maximum in the 10th over, miscuing a pull just over mid-wicket. Fifty balls in, Rohit slouched and pumped Alzarri Joseph over the square-leg fence, the same over that produced a reckless heave across the line before a leading edge parried over backward point. The venom of the pacers had dissipated by then, and Rohit switched gears against the left-arm spinners. Vitel Lewis and Gudakesh Motie bled boundaries as Rohit unfurled the sweep, the conventional and the slog, with brutal accuracy. Another abrupt swipe proved fatal, against seamer Keemo Pauls innocuous length ball, and he holed out at deep mid-wicket eight short of a third ton in four innings. Surviving a string of four dropped catches between his 13th and 69th delivery, Ruturaj Gaikwads weary half-century held the fort until Rahul shifted gears at five. With dismissive drives off the seamers at regular intervals, he reached fifty in 41 deliveries. Shepherding the lower order with a calm head, Rahul bought himself vital game time at number five after a patchy England series two months ago. He timed a chilling overdrive towards the close, five sixes in his last 12 deliveries, which reiterated his worth. It still fell short against another keeper-batters riposte. Brief scores India 3517 in 50 overs KL Rahul 129 not out, Rohit Sharma 92 Jayden Seales 362 lost to West Indies 3525 in 48.2 overs Shai Hope 162 not out, Amir Jangoo 67 by five wickets.

articleTitle: ‘We should find our own lexicon’: Nalanda Vice-Chancellor Sachin Chaturvedi on India’s soft power
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nalanda Vice-Chancellor Sachin Chaturvedi, Nalanda University, Nalanda University library, Nalanda Vice-Chancellor interview, Nalanda Vice-Chancellor Sachin Chaturvedi interview, Nalanda University Press, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Amid debates over the saffronisation of education, Nalanda Vice-Chancellor Sachin Chaturvedi speaks to The Indian Express about Nalanda’s new library, the revival of ancient traditions of scholarship and debate, and the university’s evolving academic vision
body_raw: Nalanda University NU Vice Chancellor Sachin Chaturvedi speaks to The Indian Express about the universitys planned library, its research on Shastra weapons and shaastra philosophical treatises, the revival of Shaastrartha debate and the Nalanda University Press. He also addresses ongoing debates on Sanatan and the saffronisation of education and explains why the international university is taking longer to establish itself than institutions like JNU. Edited Excerpts 12 years after Nalanda Universitys first academic session in September 2014, it is finally getting a library. Will it be in sync with the ancient Nalanda library? We have planned our library meticulously. The five-storey, stupa-shaped library - with quadrants on each floor - will begin with approximately 3.5 lakh books. The first floor will be devoted to handwritten works such as the Pragya Paramita by Acharya Nagarjuna, one of the foremost among 28 Nalanda masters whose works are being translated into English. We will also have transcriptions of these texts by students, digital analytics and coding of works by experts from IIIT Hyderabad. Since these texts are in Pali, Prakrit, Sanskrit, and other languages, they will first be translated into English. There are about 1,500 to 1,800 volumes of such works. PM Narendra Modi is likely to inaugurate the library in December. There will also be a floor devoted to complete digitisation - to help avoid the destruction that befell the ancient university. We will have segments on commentators on Nalanda University, physical dissertations from our students and a range of contemporary books across genres. How does Nalanda University contribute to shaping our foreign policy and international relations in terms of frequent use of soft power, especially in the context of the post-Hormuz world? Western philosophy talks about the rule of law, but we need to talk about the rule of justice - drawn from Kautilyas philosophy. The Hormuz crisis and South China Sea crisis are fundamentally cases of rule of law versus rule of justice. We have to revisit the concept of global governance. Soft power is a Western concept, we need to find our own lexicon from the ways ancient India practised diplomacy. Soon, we are opening the Gandhi Zayed Centre for Peace, Tolerance and Sustainability, engaging Indian and UAE experts. We are also adding Jain philosophy alongside Buddhist and Hindu philosophy for a comprehensive understanding of statecraft. We have to understand the growing binary in the post-Hormuz world while reading along the works and interpretations of Indian masters of the past. Could you elaborate on Shastra, Shaastra, and Shaastrartha? PM Modi spoke about Nalanda University introducing Shaastrartha as part of an ancient tradition. The Hormuz crisis witnessed the use of both shastra and shaastra . We will launch our own publication, the Nalanda University Press on the inauguration day with an edited volume on Shastra and Shaastra by eminent scholar Amrita Narlikar, with contributions from 20 leading foreign policy experts. The idea is to amalgamate and differentiate philosophical inquiry and statecraft. Shaastrartha - structured intellectual debate in the tradition of the ancient university - is all the more important in an era of AI overdose. How do you view the introduction and promotion of courses in Hinduism and Sanatan studies, given the allegations of saffronisation of education? There is a delicate line to follow - between restraint and ensuring that arguments are placed on the altar of intellectual discussion rather than misinformation. It is important for academics to put facts, history, and wider public understanding together. The fact that Gautam Buddha himself practised several elements of Sanatan Sanskriti culture may be contextualised against the differences within Buddhist philosophies. Nalanda University always supported multiple knowledge traditions - Buddhist, Hindu, Jain - from the 7th century onwards. Even now, students from 36 countries are studying here, including religious courses, and we received applications from 72 countries. The response has been strong enough to help us meet our target of 1,000 students. What does the course on International Relations and Peace Studies cover, and what is the Bay of Bengal studies about? The idea for a separate peace studies centre came from the former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar - a mark of pragmatic statecraft. Initially, he held back some portion of the university land to make us fulfill his condition of a separate centre as he was not happy with our formulation of the International Relations and Peace Studies centre, but eventually gave us the land. Yet, we are thankful to him for the idea, which is the mark of statecraft from a pragmatic politician. IRPS has been a big draw for students, alongside archaeology, history, data science and AI. In terms of international relations, data analysis gives us multiple facets of the past, present, and future and we are arriving at computable analysis of our ancient texts. We will hold a meeting this month bringing together linguists from Northeastern India and Southeast Asia to understand the linguistic dynamics of the region, in line with the Act East policy endorsed by the Prime Minister. What are the key elements of the Indian Knowledge System which has become a buzzword these days? Its manifestation is visible in architecture, philosophy and economics. Instead of borrowing from colonial structures, Nalanda Universitys architecture reflects ancient design principles - our buildings are oriented so that the purvaiya easterly wind flows through them. In terms of economic thinking, our framework is more oriented towards well-being than GDP - an approach emulated by the UN in 2023. We also need to rethink trade metrics if India has 80 trade with Nepal, 95 with Bhutan and 68 with Sri Lanka, it reflects our trade growth old metrics depicting it unfavourably have to be changed and viewed through our own indigenous and ancient methodology. In language, we have incorporated Malayalam, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Hindi to revive regional languages and prevent their erosion. Ancient Nalanda did not travel to 200-odd neighbouring villages merely to procure rations - it went there to learn Pali, Prakrit and Sanskrit. Unlike JNU, which established itself within a decade of opening, why is Nalanda University, a flagship MEA venture, taking longer to arrive? It is happening, it is just a matter of time. IRPS has been a major preference of students from several states who preferred NU over JNU or DU. In CUET preference rankings, Nalanda University is among the top six or seven institutions. It is difficult to draw students from metro cities to a rural setting. But those who stay here know that the campus ambience is comparable to that of any top university in the world, with significantly better AQI than large metros.

articleTitle: ‘Blows kept coming’: Smit Machchhar recalls flydubai cockpit attack
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News Live Updates:
description: In a phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the injured Indian pilot described the moment his co-pilot attacked him, the aircraft began plunging and he made one final attempt to open the cockpit door
body_raw: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar has described how he was attacked by his co-pilot aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, telling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that the assault began after the co-pilot asked to pray. Machchhar said he suffered repeated blows to the back of his head before realising that the aircraft was plunging and making a final attempt to open the cockpit door. In a phone call with Netanyahu on Saturday, Machchhar said he initially thought the repeated blows to the back of his head were caused by a problem with the aircraft. It was only after several blows that he realised the other person in the cockpit was attacking him. The captain, who was seriously injured, eventually managed to open the cockpit door while the aircraft was plunging, allowing passengers to enter and help subdue the co-pilot. Two other flydubai pilots who were travelling on the aircraft then helped stabilise the plane before it made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. zzoe zY - c z z, Y z z c oe, coe oe. zzY s zzoe z oe z cz oe zoes - z z c, zzoe oe z s oe -oe,. pic.twitter.comysnK5mxJNX - zzoe oe IsraeliPMheb October 3, 2026 How did the flydubai cockpit attack begin? Machchhar told Netanyahu that the flight had been normal before the incident. The co-pilot, identified in media reports as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, told him that he wanted to pray. Machchhar said he turned away out of respect. A few minutes later, he felt a blow to the back of his head. Suddenly, after four or five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head, Machchhar said. He initially thought the aircraft had suffered catastrophic damage. But after that, the blows kept coming, one after the other, he said. Thats when I realized its not the aircraft, its the other guy who was in the cockpit with me. Machchhar said he tried to stop the co-pilot, but the initial blows had severely affected his vision. I was completely blurred out, he said. He then realised that the aircraft was sharply descending. What did Smit Machchhar tell Netanyahu? Machchhar said his memory of the attack remained fragmented. He recalled making an initial attempt to open the cockpit door, but said the co-pilot managed to close it again. He was eventually lying on the cockpit floor as the aircraft descended and he could hear people screaming. I had one last fight left in me, Machchhar told Netanyahu. He said he knew that he had to make another attempt to reach the door. Thats when I pushed against everything, I gave everything that I had, and just went for the door and opened the door and people were waiting to pounce back, and take control, and the rest is what you know, sir. Machchhar had earlier given Prime Minister Narendra Modi a similar account, saying he realised the aircraft was going down and made a final effort to open the cockpit door. An unforgettable conversation with Captain Smit, filled with pride and emotions. pic.twitter.comCCf46PKOWR - Narendra Modi narendramodi October 2, 2026 How did Machchhar open the cockpit door? During the conversation, Netanyahu asked Machchhar how he had managed to open the cockpit door while seriously injured. Machchhar explained that the door could be opened from inside using a twist mechanism, while those outside normally needed a code to enter. He said passengers and crew outside tried to use the code, but the co-pilot prevented them from gaining access. Machchhar said he eventually managed to reach the internal knob and twist it open. The opening of the door allowed passengers to enter the cockpit and intervene as the aircraft was in a severe descent. What happened after the cockpit door opened? Once the cockpit door was opened, passengers moved in and helped subdue the co-pilot. Flydubai has said that on-duty crew members travelling on the aircraft helped stabilise the plane and land it safely. The airline has not publicly identified the two pilots. Two pilots were reportedly travelling as passengers as part of a routine aviation practice known as deadheading, in which crew members are repositioned for a subsequent assignment. They were expected to operate the aircraft on its return journey. The aircraft had plunged thousands of feet during the incident before being stabilised and diverted to Tabuk. Netanyahu invites Machchhar to Israels Independence Day ceremony Netanyahu told Machchhar that he was amazed by his courage and ability to remain composed under extreme circumstances. You saved so many souls . You saved the spirit of the world, Netanyahu said. He described Machchhar as a hero of Israel, India and the wider world and wished him a speedy recovery. Netanyahu also invited Machchhar and Modi to participate in Israels next Independence Day ceremony by lighting a ceremonial torch. You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel, Netanyahu told him. And youre a hero of the entire world. What happened to Smit Machchhar? During the conversation, Netanyahu also spoke about the medical treatment Machchhar received after the emergency landing. He said he had spoken to the dentist who treated the injured pilot and described the medical professionals account of Machchhars courage. Machchhar said he wanted to meet the dentist. I would love to meet him as well. He saved my life, to be honest, he said. The flight eventually landed safely at Tabuk after the cockpit attack. The Indian pilot and the co-pilot were subsequently taken to the UAE. Machchhar is recovering in the UAE The Indian Embassy in the UAE said Saturday that Machchhar remained under medical care and was recovering well. The pilots latest account comes as the UAE-led investigation into the incident continues. UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said investigators had determined that the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with the aircrafts crash axe and attempted to take control of the plane. The UAE has described the incident as an attempted terrorist attack and said investigators are examining its circumstances, motive and possible connections. The co-pilot has been identified by multiple media reports as Hamam al-Hammami. Associated Press reported that he had previously been barred from flying in Oman over concerns about extremist views, although the investigation has not established his motive or whether he had links to any militant group.

articleTitle: The sal and the beetle: Why Madhya Pradesh is cutting 1.4 lakh trees to save the forest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Madhya Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh tree felling, Madhya Pradesh tree cutting, Dindori-Mandla road, sal heartwood borer, longhorn beetle, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh government, Indian express news, current affairs
description: The trees in Dindori forests are witnessing a major infestation of the sal heartwood borer this year, compelling the government and local communities to undertake a mega exercise to tackle the pest
body_raw: At first light, the most noticeable sound in the sal forests off the Dindori-Mandla road in Madhya Pradesh these days is of feet on dry leaves. Villagers fan out toward trees that were felled and stripped of bark three days earlier, its sap drawn out. And there it lies, exposed on the trunks, their culprit-the sal heartwood borer, a longhorn beetle that has been a bane for these trees for over a century. The villagers pick them by hand, drop them into bags or jars, and later turn them into necklaces-the beetles long feelers aiding the braiding process. The necklaces are not for any ornamental reason but to make it convenient for the villagers to carry them to eight collection centres in the district. Each beetle is worth Rs 2. So far, this season, 19,25,118 of them have been collected, generating a bill of Rs 38.5 lakh for the states forest department. Hoplocerambyx spinicornis, commonly known as the sal heartwood borer, is a destructive pest first recorded as a threat to the trees in 1897. Now, it is at the centre of one of the largest sal-tree felling operations in Dindori in recent years following a major infestation. A couple of weeks ago, Centre approved the felling of 1.47 lakh infected sal trees. Sal, or Shorea robusta, is among the dominant tree species of central Indias dry deciduous forests, forming the backbone of tracts that run across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand and parts of Uttar Pradesh. Its canopy makes up much of the habitat inside tiger reserves, such as Kanha and Pench. Sal timber has historically been prized for construction and for railway sleepers because of its strength and resistance to decay. The tree continues to support a range of non-timber produce on which forest-dwelling and tribal communities depend - sal seed, pressed for oil and used in cooking and in the soap and confectionery industries sal leaves, stitched into plates and bowls sold across local markets and resin tapped from the trunk, used as dhoop in religious offerings. In much of central India, sal groves also carry cultural and religious significance for tribal communities. It is this combination of ecological weight and economic dependence that gives a sal-borer epidemic consequences beyond the forest departments felling ledger. Over 21 epidemics recorded so far The insect does not attack indiscriminately it tends to target weaker, less vigorous trees, though it becomes capable of killing sal of varying ages once a trees girth exceeds 20 cm. Mortality is largely concentrated among trees between 91 and 150 cm in girth, and the highest losses recorded is in the 121-150 cm range - precisely the mature, canopy-forming trees that anchor a sal forests structure and constitute the greatest share of its timber and non-timber yield. More than 21 sal-borer epidemics have been documented across India to date. MP and neighbouring Chhattisgarh experienced a major outbreak between 1997 and 2000, during which roughly 3 lakh hectares of sal forest were affected out of the regions 16.84 lakh hectare cover. Mandla - the district adjoining Dindori, and part of the same forest landscape now under felling orders - was the worst-hit at the time, with around 8 lakh trees damaged. Dindori Divisional Forest Officer Ashok Solanki said, We are dealing with a substantial number of affected trees. Working in tandem The trapping and the felling are two distinct interventions running in tandem. The insect-collection campaign, carried out through what the department calls trap trees, is organised to pull adult borers out of the population before they can lay eggs and multiply. The felling of already-infected standing trees is a separate, larger sanitation operation, aimed at removing wood that is beyond saving and could otherwise seed further infestation. Dindori SDO Forest Surendra Jatav explained the method in detail. When the rains start, we start the trapping operation, he said. Selected trees are felled and debarked to draw the insect out. It comes and feeds on the sap and becomes exposed at night, Jatav said. The trees are left for three days before villagers return to collect the insects that have surfaced. When they come out after sunrise, around 5-6 in the morning, we go and catch them by hand and put them in a bag, he said. The felling of infected standing trees, Jatav said, is being carried out manually with axes, through an agency, with villagers doing the actual cutting. The operation is expected to take around four months. The felled wood goes to the timber market, said Jatav. The scale of the current outbreak, according to Jatav, is unusual but not without precedent. It is an epidemic-type cycle. It repeats every 30 years, he said, describing how infestation levels can swing sharply from one year to the next. Last year it was very low this year it has become very high, he said. Unusually high rainfall a factor Dr Uday Homkar, Senior Research Officer and in-charge of the Conservation Division at the State Forest Research Institute SFRI, Jabalpur, has tracked sal borer outbreaks in MP for more than a decade. He pointed to weather as one contributing factor behind this years spike. He said that unusually high rainfall in the Dindori-Mandla region last year had helped create conditions favourable to the insect. According to Homkar, the first and most decisive step in controlling an outbreak is catching it early. As soon as the infection develops, it has to be detected, he said. We practise this detection. Once a tree is confirmed infected, removing it becomes necessary to prevent the infestation from spreading to its neighbours. But, he cautioned, control should not begin only when large numbers of trees were already affected - preventive trapping needs to continue year-round. Homkar said researchers have also studied whether biological control - introducing natural predators of the borer instead of relying primarily on felling and trapping - could offer a more sustainable path. Large-scale rearing and release have been studied, but their side-effects have not been studied enough.

articleTitle: Accomplices, a military armoury, a plan to sell guns: Inside Secunderabad arms heist
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to the police, the suspect first broke open the armoury lock and took out 12 weapons, hiding them in the thick foliage outside. (Image: DGP Telanagana Police/X/Express Photo)
description: On August 31, 12 military-grade weapons were stolen from the armoury of the 20 Madras Regiment at Bolarum in Secunderabad Cantonment. A subsequent police investigation has alleged an elaborate plan involving seven people -- one ex-havildar, three serving army personnel and four civilians
body_raw: The retired army man arrested in the Secunderabad arms heist case allegedly had seven accomplices, including three serving army personnel, police have said. Investigators have alleged that the theft was part of a larger plan to rob banks, jewellers and wealthy people. At a press conference Saturday, Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B Sumathi ruled out a terror angle in the case, alleging instead that 37-year-old retired Havildar Upputholla Mallesh alias Raju had plotted and executed the heist at the armoury of the 20 Madras Regiment at Bolarum in Secunderabad Cantonment with seven others for financial reasons. According to police, he also planned to sell some of the weapons on the black market. The revelations come a month after the theft of 12 military-grade weapons and over 1,900 rounds of ammunition, all of which the Telangana Police later said they had recovered. The stolen weapons included four AK-203 assault rifles, seven pistols and an INSAS rifle. Mallesh was arrested on September 11. At the time, police had said they suspected he had acted alone. At Saturdays press conference, police announced the arrest of seven people in connection with the case. They will be produced before the magistrate soon, Sumathi said. The eight-member team also intended to sell some of the weapons in the black market, for prices ranging from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh. Police said the others arrested are 36-year-old Konduri Sheshulu, a Sepoy 34-year-old Vinod Kumar, a Naik and 37-year-old Kucharakanthi Praveen, a Havildar - all serving army personnel. Sheshulu and Vinod Kumar are from Markapuram in Andhra Pradesh, while Praveen is fromGundlapotlapally in Mahabubnagar district, Telangana. The four civilians arrested in the case, according to police, are 32-year-old Avi Dey alias Obi of Barrackpore, West Bengal 27-year-old Birbal Shaw, who ran a sugarcane juice shop near Barrackpore Cantonment Malleshs 39-year-old cousin Upputholla Mallikarjun, a mason from Padara in Nagarkurnool district and 39-year-old Chemmakar Niranjan, a kirana shop owner from Nagarkurnool. According to police, Mallesh was facing financial difficulties and allegedly involved his cousin Mallikarjun and friend Niranjan, who police said had similar financial problems. He had received Rs 22 lakh as retirement benefits, which he partly used to build a house and buy a car. He faced financial difficulties and felt that robbery and extortion could be the way out, Sumathi said. Police said Mallesh had met Dey and Shaw when he was posted in Barrackpore in 2022 and had allegedly purchased a country-made firearm and one live round of ammunition from the former. In the recent past,he reached out to his friends Sheshulu, Vinod Kumar and Praveen, and they extended support for the theft. Once the deal was brokered, Mallesh contacted Dey and Shaw, who informed him that some of the weapons could also be sold in the black market - for Rs 3 lakh for pistols and Rs 5 lakh for rifles, Sumathi said. Police alleged that Mallesh broke the armoury lock and magazine with the help of the three other army personnel. Police also claimed that Mallesh had a previous criminal record, citing a history of extortion and house burglary in Nagarkurnool district. The proceeds of these burglaries were also kept at his fathers residence in Achampet. We have also recovered the country-made weapon he purchased from Dey, Sumathi said. The police will soon take custody of the other accused. Our investigation into the heist will continue once we get custody of the other accused for interrogation, Sumathi said. The police, however, said they had found no terrorist or extremist links in the case. No such links have been established. The motive of the crime was to amass wealth, Sumathi said.

articleTitle: Rajasthan HC cites Gandhi, denies bail to 5 in Kanhaiya Lal case: ‘Terrorism a weapon of the weak’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajasthan High Court, Kanhaiya Lal case, Rajasthan High Court denies bail in Kanhaiya Lal case, Terrorism, Kanhaiya Lal Teli murder case, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Denying them bail Saturday, the court says that the paradigm of bail shifts entirely when the crime in question ‘is not aimed at an individual, but at the very soul of the nation’.
body_raw: The Rajasthan High Court on Saturday denied bail to five accused in Udaipurs Kanhaiya Lal Teli murder case, invoking Mahatma Gandhis words that terrorism and deception are weapons not of the strong, but of the weak. A Bench of Chief Justice Sanjay Agrawal and Justice Sameer Jain denied bail applications of Wasim Ali, 34, Muslim Khan, 43, Mohsin Khan, 27, Mohammad Mohsin, 34, and Asif Hussain, 25, saying that we find that the gravity of the offence, the specific roles attributed to the appellants in the larger criminal conspiracy, and the heinous nature of the terrorist act disentitle the accused-appellants to the benefits of bail. On June 28, 2022, two people - Mohammed Riyaz Attari and Ghouse Mohammad - had allegedly posed as customers and hacked to death Kanhaiya Lal Teli at his shop in Udaipur over a post shared by him on social media in support of Nupur Sharma, a BJP spokesperson who was suspended for her objectionable remarks about the Prophet during a live television debate. The Bench also quoted a poem by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar on tolerance and, in prefatory remarks, said The seat of a judge is surrounded by an invisible, yet crushing weight, the weight to protect the rights of the citizens and people of this country which are enshrined under the Constitution of India. The paradigm of bail shifts entirely when the crime in question is not aimed at an individual, but at the very soul of the nation, the Bench said, adding Terrorism is not merely an assault on a physical body it is a calculated, theatrical assault on the psychological sovereignty of the country. Its ultimate objective is not just to commit an offence, but the assassination of peace. It seeks to replace the Rule of Law with the Rule of Fear. The NIA had filed a charge sheet, and the trial court framed charges against the five accused in 2024. They have been in judicial custody since their arrest in the days and weeks following the murder. They had filed bail applications before a Special Court, which had rejected their pleas in October and November 2024. Representing the accused, Syed Saadat Ali and others primarily contended that there is no cogent evidence on record to demonstrate that the accused were present in or around the vicinity of the deceaseds shop during the relevant period leading up to the incident, specifically between June 10 and June 28, 2022. Next, they said that there is no evidence on record to suggest that the accused had sent any message, voice note, or text on any WhatsApp group that could be construed as hurting the religious faith of any community or promoting enmity. They also relied on bail granted to two other accused, Farhad Mohammed and Mohammed Javed, by the trial court and by the High Court on the exact same set of charges as framed against the present accused-appellants. They also said that the accused have been in custody for over four and a half years and that the trial will take its own considerable time. although the charge-sheet was filed on 22.08.2022 and charges were framed in early 2024, the trial is far from conclusion. Senior counsel Raja Thakare, appearing on behalf of the National Investigation Agency, said that the five accused played an active, indispensable, and integral role in the commission of the alleged crime. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, Thakare and others said that the court is not required to conduct a mini-trial or weigh the evidence meticulously at the bail stage. The Court must look at the material provided by the investigative agency at its face value, and if it discloses reasonable grounds for believing the accusation to be prima facie true, bail must be rejected. The high court said that the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act places a statutory embargo on the grant of bail if the court, on a perusal of the charge-sheet, is of the opinion that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accusation against such person is prima facie true. It said that the NIA has completed a detailed and comprehensive investigation, filed the charge-sheet, and the trial court has already framed charges against the accused This establishes that upon a prima facie evaluation, there exists sufficient material to proceed against the appellants, and therefore, the foundational test laid down by the Honble Supreme Court. is squarely met at this stage. The high court, however, clarified that its observations are solely for the purpose of deciding the present bail and that the trial court shall proceed with the trial uninfluenced by the observations made hereinabove.

articleTitle: ‘Unease factor’ in Congress-Samajwadi Party ties ahead of UP polls: Who is Imran Masood
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress MP Imran Masood
description: Congress's move to name Saharanpur MP as UP working president has been seen by SP camp as its “pressure tactic” to bargain for more seats as Masood has been putting heat on Akhilesh over seat-sharing
body_raw: The Congresss decision to appoint Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president of its Uttar Pradesh unit ahead of the Assembly elections seems to have caused some unease in ally Samajwadi Party SP, which sees the move as a pressure tactic to bargain for more seats in the polls. While SP spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary told The Indian Express that Masoods appointment would have no adverse impact on his partys seat-sharing talks with the Congress, some other SP leaders privately expressed discomfort over the development. I dont understand what is in the mind of the top Congress leadership. The new UP Congress president, Aradhana Misra Mona, and her father, Pramod Tiwari, have cordial relations with the SP. Her appointment will only help in smoothening dialogue between the two parties regarding the UP polls. But Masood, through his remarks on the SP, often creates uneasiness. Now, things will depend on how much authority senior Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra give Masood in seat-sharing talks, said an SP insider. He said the Congress wanted an early decision on seat-sharing, as any delay could leave it with little choice but to accept whatever seats the SP would offer. The UP elections are due in February 2027. A senior SP leader said Masoods appointment appeared to be both a Congress tactic to secure more seats and an attempt to compete for the Muslim vote, traditionally seen to be with the SP. Masood is influential in Saharanpur but not across western UP. He will not be able to disturb the SPs Muslim votes in this region. But his public remarks about the alliance and Muslim issues will build pressure on the SP to finalise seat-sharing early and share Muslim-dominated seats with the Congress. The Congress is eyeing anti-BJP votes of regional parties, the leader said. Another SP leader said the Congress should clarify whether Masood would have any role in alliance talks.He is continuously demanding early finalisation of the alliance. He should speak first with Gandhi before speaking about the SP in the media. All Opposition parties want Muslim votes but none is trying to make inroads into the 42 non-Muslim votes of the BJP, the leader said. An SP leader from western UP said Masoods attempts to put pressure on the party would not work. The SP will demand all Assembly seats falling under the Saharanpur Lok Sabha constituency. The SP is prepared to contest there, he said. Seat-sharing hurdles Seat-sharing in Saharanpur could be a point of contention between the SP and the Congress. Last month, Masood said the Congress would fight the five seats in Saharanpur that it had contested in 2017. Hamara majboot jila hai, apna majboot jila thode hi chhod denge The district is our stronghold. We will not leave it, he said. The Congress leaders declined to officially respond to the concerns expressed by SP leaders over Masoods appointment. SP leaders are irritated more with Masood because he had quit them after the 2022 Assembly polls, and later became a Congress MP with the SPs support in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. But we are hopeful that things will settle down between both camps soon because the Congress leadership has directed Masood to refrain from further attacks on the SP, said a senior Congress leader. Masoods journey A first-time MP, Masood, 56, has been a prominent face in western Uttar Pradesh politics for several years. Carrying forward his familys political legacy, he was earlier known for controversial remarks. Over the last few years, however, he has sought to shed the image of a Muslim hardliner and has reached out to Hindu voters. He has often been heard saying Ram milenge maryada se jeene mein, Ram milenge Hanuman ke seene mein Ram is found in living a life of dignity, Ram resides in Hanumans heart. Masood was first elected MLA as an Independent from the Muzaffarabad Assembly seat in 2007. In 2012, the Congress picked him as a youth face in Rahul Gandhis team. The same year, he contested the Nakur Assembly seat but lost to the BSPs Dharam Singh Saini. Just before the 2014 Lok Sabha polls, a video clip surfaced in which Masood was purportedly seen threatening then BJPs prime ministerial candidate Narendra Modi while blaming the BJP and RSS for the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots. A case was registered against him for hate speech. In the Lok Sabha polls, he lost to the BJPs Raghav Lakhan Pal in Saharanpur. Ahead of the 2022 UP Assembly polls, Masood ended his association with the Congress and joined the SP. He quit the SP in October that year after SP chief Akhilesh Yadav did not give a ticket to him or any of his associates for the Assembly polls. He then joined the BSP, where Mayawati immediately appointed him coordinator for western UP, with additional responsibility for working among Muslims in Uttarakhand. In August 2023, however, Mayawati expelled Masood from the party, accusing him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. He returned to the Congress later that year. Recent row On September 21, speaking to ANI, Masood said Akhileshs political activity was meaningless unless the alliance was finalised. Finalise the alliance if you have to have an alliance. If it the alliance is not to be done, we Congress are going ahead with our preparations. Akhilesh ji should finish this work alliance finalisation immediately. If you have to lead, the responsibility is on you. Dil bhi aapko bada karna padega You will have to have a large heart, Masood said. He said the SP should not think of moving ahead without the Congress. Because if you are going ahead without the Congress, defeating the BJP is not in your mind. Only the Congress can fight the BJP, he said. In June 2025, Masood had also stirred the alliance debate by saying the 62-17 formula would not work in the 2027 Assembly polls, referring to the seat-sharing arrangement between the two allies for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

articleTitle: Tariffs, sanctions becoming policy instruments, sometimes weaponised: P K Mishra
articleFeaturedImageAlt: P K Mishra, Tariffs, sanctions, policy instruments, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, Kautilya Economic Conclave, Trump Tariffs, trump tariff impositions, India-US ties, trade war, us trade war, donald trump, reciprocal tariffs, Trump India trade deal, India US tariff cuts, Trump India tariffs announcement, India US trade agreement, Modi Trump trade talks, India US economic relations, India lowers tariffs for US, US India trade negotiations, Trump Modi tariff deal, India US import export policy, Trump on India tariffs, US India business ties, trade war India US, India trade policy changes, India US tariff reduction, Indian express news, current affairs
description: He said the future will belong to those who can be “steady without being closed, careful without being fearful, and ambitious without being naïve”, and India intends to be such a country.
body_raw: The Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, P K Mishra, on Saturday said tariffs, export controls and other restrictions are increasingly being used not only for conventional commercial objectives but also for strategic purposes, and these instruments of economic policy are sometimes even weaponised. He said the future will belong to those who can be steady without being closed, careful without being fearful, and ambitious without being naive, and India intends to be such a country. Speaking at a session on A World Priced for Risk during the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave, Mishra said, We are increasingly confronted, not merely with risk, but also with uncertainty. The events of this decade have brought this distinction into sharp focus. We have seen a pandemic disrupting production and mobility across the world, wars disrupting energy and food markets. Shipping routes and geographical chokepoints become sources of economic vulnerability. Export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy, even sometimes they are weaponised. Critical minerals, technologies and even financial infrastructure require a new strategic significance. Discussing risks associated with energy availability, Mishra said, For decades the principal question for an energy importing country or energy importing economy was often price of energy. Today, there is another question - will the energy be available or can it reach us? A disruption in a major shipping route can affect the price of crude oil thousands of kilometres away. Geography has, therefore, become an economic variable.The economic logic of globalisation was built around specialisation - produce where costs are lowest and move the goods efficiently across borders. The logic remains relevant and even powerful, but the experience of the pandemic, geopolitical conflict and more recent disruptions have highlighted another consideration the cost of interruption. A supply chain that is efficient in normal times may be fragile if the single-node supplier or geography becomes unavailable, he said. We are seeing similar development in critical minerals. Lithium, cobalt, rare earths and other minerals are essential to batteries, electronics, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing, but their extraction, processing and refining are highly concentrated geographically. Geography, we thought technology has made it irrelevant, but it has returned to the centre of the table, and it is not only oil, the minerals of energy transition are held in very few hands. For nearly all of them, a single country does most of the refining. So, the clean energy future, which was meant to free us from oil dependence, risks creating new ones, Mishra said. The result is a world in which economic policy and geographical considerations are becoming more closely intertwined. The question before policymakers is therefore not whether globalisation has ended. It has not. The question is how we preserve the gains from openness, while making economies less vulnerable to concentrated and unpredicted shocks. On Indias response to global supply chain shocks in the wake of disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, Mishra said, India is a major energy importer and any prolonged disruption to an important maritime route can affect the economy adversely. Indias response has combined several layers of protection. We have maintained substantial stocks, increased domestic production and ensured that alternative supply routes and suppliers are available. For example, the number of countries from which we import crude oil has increased from 27 to 43, which is very large, he said. He said India has also responded through greater diversification of our external economic relationships. An open economy will always depend on other economies. The objective is not to eliminate that dependence, but to avoid excessive concentration. Indias recent trade policy illustrates this approach. India now has a broader network of trade agreements, including agreements with the UAE, Australia, AIFTA ASEANIndia Free Trade Area and more recently, the United Kingdom, Oman, New Zealand and the European Union. There is one more form of resilience that is perhaps less visible, and that is macroeconomic resilience, he said. I believe the world that is coming will belong to those who can be steady without being closed, careful without being fearful and ambitious without being naive. India intends to be such a country. I hope that together we can help build such a world.
