articleTitle: VHP claims 254 Hindus killed in attacks this year, calls for fast-track trials, surveillance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hindus killed in attacks, Hindus killing in attacks, Hindu killings, Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), jihadis, VHP joint general secretary Surendra Jain, Surendra Jain, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Claiming that 254 Hindus had been killed by “jihadis” across the country in the first eight months of this year, the RSS affiliate called upon Hindus living in sensitive areas to “remain vigilant and prepared for self-defence”.
body_raw: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad VHP on Saturday called for fast-track trials in cases of alleged religiously motivated attacks on Hindus, tighter regulation of madrasas and installation of high-resolution surveillance cameras at mosques and madrasas in sensitive areas. Claiming that 254 Hindus had been killed by jihadis across the country in the first eight months of this year, the RSS affiliate called upon Hindus living in sensitive areas to remain vigilant and prepared for self-defence. At a press conference in New Delhi, VHP joint general secretary Surendra Jain released a 26-page list of 254 cases that the organisation said it had compiled from media reports of killings between January and August 31, 2026. The document gives the date and place of each incident, names of the victim and accused, and links to reports published by various media organisations. The VHP has classified those on the list as Hindus killed by jihadis. The document itself, however, includes cases arising from a range of circumstances. For instance, some of the linked reports concern murders following personal or financial disputes, while others involve allegations of communal or religiously motivated violence. The classification is VHPs. Jain said the list covered only cases that were reported in the media and claimed that several other such incidents had not received media coverage. The fact that such a large number of Hindus have been killed by jihadis, despite efforts by Ram-bhakt governments in several states to curb this deadly trend over the past decade, should be a matter of concern for all patriotic and nationalist Bharatiyas, Jain said. The VHP demanded that cases of attacks on Hindus found to have been driven by religious hatred be sent to fast-track courts and that those convicted receive swift and stringent punishment. It also demanded that minors accused of murder and serious offences allegedly motivated by religious hatred be tried as adults, alleging that minors were being used to commit violence in the expectation that they would receive lighter punishment. Calling madrasas centres for the propagation of religious fanaticism and hatred, the VHP sought stringent regulation of such institutions. It also called for high-resolution cameras to be installed in sensitive areas, mosques and madrasas, with their monitoring linked to local police stations. Jain said Hindus were the principal targets of jihadis in India and called upon those living in and around sensitive areas to remain alert and watchful and prepared for self-defence. The VHP and Bajrang Dal, he said, were considering constitutional measures for the protection of Hindus, without elaborating. Jain praised Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his actions in thwarting an alleged terror plot, saying the VHP gave him a standing ovation for his bravery and nerve. The organisation claimed his actions had prevented a 911-style attack and called for a coordinated international strategy against Islamist terrorism. The statement came on the same day that the ABVP, another Sangh-affiliated organisation, demanded that Machchhar be awarded the Ashoka Chakra. Jain further alleged that appeasement pursued in the name of secular politics had aggravated the problem of Islamist radicalism in India. Citing attacks on Hindu religious events, alleged love jihad cases and attacks on Hindu settlements, he called upon people to rise above partisan considerations to confront what the VHP described as a growing threat.

articleTitle: GST arrest powers on way out amid concerns over taxmen’s overreach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: In 72,393 cases of GST offences from 2021-22 to 2024-25, 887 arrests were made by central GST formations. (Source: File)
description: GST Council to discuss issue on October 7, Govt may bring amendment in Winter Session
body_raw: More than nine years after its rollout in July 2017, the Goods and Services Tax GST regime is set to see a major overhaul - removal of arrest powers. In a bid to boost investor sentiment and allay concerns about overreach by tax authorities, the upcoming GST Council meeting, on October 7, will take up the proposal to decriminalise offences under the indirect tax regime, two persons aware of the development told The Indian Express. The Centre and the states are learnt to have held several meetings over the last eight-nine months, including involvement at the top levels of the Union government, to reach a broad consensus on removal of the arrest provisions under GST, which were being seen as a major impediment for traders and businesses. The move is viewed as urgent as several arrests of high-ranking functionaries were made in recent times under the GST provisions that were termed by industry leaders as an overreach. For intentional frauds and deceit under GST, the authorities will proceed with prosecution and arrests will be through the countrys criminal code, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, a source said. The consultations had been going on since the last eight-nine months. The feedback from businesses about the arrests has been taken into account to move ahead with this discussion. The GST Council will take up the matter and the final decision will be taken after that, following which there will be legislative changes to allow removal of arrest provisions under GST laws, said a source. After the rollout of GST in July 2017, authorities have grappled with multiple instances of frauds, involving broadly similar modus operandi. Typically, such cases involve fake identities or mule accounts to undertake fraudulent GST transactions in a bid to avail input tax credit, or fake bills without actual supply of goods. Many suppliers also undervalue their final goods and show purchase of raw materials at lower rates. Or, they supply taxable goods and services without due payment of GST to the central and state governments. In 72,393 cases of GST offences from 2021-22 to 2024-25, 887 arrests were made by central GST formations. The arrests by state authorities will be in addition to this number. Under the Central GST Act, non-compliance can result in penalty under Section 122, interest under Section 50, and recovery of tax. However, violations involving deliberate intent to evade tax attract arrest and prosecution under the criminal provisions of the CGST Act. Section 69 of the CGST Act provides for the power to arrest after approval by the Commissioner. Sub-section 1 provides that where the Commissioner has reasons to believe that a person has committed any offence related to fake invoices, fraudulent availment of input tax credit, he may, by order, authorise any officer of central tax to arrest such person. The reasons to believe have to be backed by credible material and evidence, and mere suspicion is not sufficient, with all the reasons required to be recorded in writing. According to sources, after the GST Council discusses the issue at its upcoming 57th meeting slated on Wednesday, the Centre is expected to bring in an amendment in the Winter Session of Parliament to enable the removal of arrest powers. Industry experts said arrests had become a harassment tool, especially in the services sector, including banking and insurance, and would often be deployed as a bargaining tool for businesses to pay penalty in order to avoid prolonged legal battles. An official said the removal of arrest powers would be a taxpayer-friendly measure and remove any perceptions of fear and harassment. The concern about arrest powers under GST laws is not new. It was flagged by several states in the early meetings of the GST Council, even before the 2017 rollout of the indirect tax regime. In the fifth GST Council meeting held in December 2016, the Maharashtra Additional Chief Secretary had observed that the power of arrest and confiscation was not in tune with the concept of ease of doing business, according to the minutes of the meeting. A minister from West Bengal had said that under VAT law, there was no power of arrest and that First Information Report FIR could be lodged only with the police, and it may not be prudent to give such powers to the tax authority. The Commissioner, GST Council, had said that under GST, the provision of arrest was highly restricted and the power could be exercised only where combined evasion of duty was Rs 2 crore or more and where offence was very severe - where supplies were made without any invoice invoice was made without any supply tax collected but not paid to the government tax collected in contravention of provisions of the GST Act but not paid to the government and taking input tax credit without receiving goods and services. An official document from the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs CBIC stated that in the administration of taxation, the provisions for arrests are created to tackle the situations created by some unscrupulous tax evaders. To some, these may appear very harsh, but these are necessary for efficient tax administration and also act as a deterrent and instill a sense of discipline. The provisions for arrests under GST law have sufficient inbuilt safeguards to ensure that these are used only under authorisation from the Commissioner. Besides this, the GST law also stipulates that arrests can be made only in those cases where the person is involved in offences specified for the purposes of arrest and the tax amount involved in such offence is more than the specified limit, it said. The government has been moving towards decriminalisation of offences on the direct tax side as well. The Central Board of Direct Taxes CBDT had, in September, removed arrest and detention provisions from the tax recovery rules with retrospective effect from April 1, 2026, barring tax officials from undertaking arrest in case of tax default. In a notification dated September 17, the CBDT had brought in Income-Tax Fourth Amendment Rules, 2026, which also removes arrest and detention from the tax recovery rules in case of death of the defaulter.

articleTitle: Inside Track: Lessons From Past

description: It is important to know whether CEC Gyanesh Kumar in fact held formal three-member meetings with documented minutes on contentious issues.
body_raw: The BJP has downplayed the gravity of The Indian Express investigations, highlighting 14 occasions in 10 months when two ECs differed with the Chief Election Commissioner over the implementation of the election process, including changes to the ECIN software, by terming it as a normal part of institutional deliberation leading to unanimous decisions. The history of past differences between EC members suggests otherwise. When the three-member commission concept was introduced in 1993 under PM PV Narasimha Rao, the two new ECs, MS Gill and GVG Krishnamurthy, protested that CEC TN Seshan continued to conduct the commission as a one-man show. They were not consulted, and no meetings were held before important decisions were taken. Seshan ignored their objections and approached the Supreme Court to affirm his supremacy. But the court held that each member of the constitutional body had equal rights. Following Seshans term, the rule of majority has always prevailed. On the rare occasion when two commissioners, the late Navin Chawla and SY Qureshi, concurred in 2009 against then-CEC N Gopalaswamis decision on serving a notice to Sonia Gandhi for receiving the Order of Leopold in 2006 from the Belgian government, the CEC was overruled. During the 2019 Lok Sabha election, Ashok Lavasa disagreed with then CEC Sunil Arora about giving a clean chit to the PM and home minister for alleged violations of the model code of conduct. Lavasa subsequently insisted he would not attend meetings unless his minority decisions were recorded. It is therefore important to know whether CEC Gyanesh Kumar in fact held formal three-member meetings with documented minutes on contentious issues. Tata September Coup Those who choose to view the confrontation between the Tata Trusts and the runaway Tata Sons Board as a mere personality clash between the trusts chairperson, Noel Tata, and Tata Sons executive chairperson, N Chandrasekaran, fail to read between the lines. It is fairly obvious that powerful interests are at work to hobble Noel Tata, who seems to be running a three-legged race against unseen opponents who have strong tailwinds propelling them forward. September was indeed a star-crossed month for the legendary House of Tata with a pincer attack from all sides. Surely, not just a coincidence? To begin with, the RBI, on September 11, rejected the Tata Sons application to surrender its Core Investment Company CIC status, even though the Tatas had faithfully completed a significant financial restructuring by clearing Rs 21,813 crore of debt in order to ensure that the holding company had no access to public funding. The Tatas followed the precedent set by Shanghvi Finance, which owns Sun Pharma, and had been permitted to surrender its registration and get regulatory relief in 2023. However, the RBI immediately rejected the Tata Sons application for exemption from its revised 2022 regulations for the public listing of Tata Sons. The RBI simply changed the goal post The second shock was a sudden U-turn by the Tata Sons Board from its long-stated position of opposing public listing of the group. The board mysteriously decided not to challenge the RBIs September 11 decision. A month earlier, Chandrasekharan had informed the board that he would be stepping down as chairperson when his second extended term expired in February, but on September 17, the Tata Sons board voted to reappoint Chandrasekharan, despite the objections of the Sir Dorabji Tata and Sir Ratanji Tata trusts that own 66 per cent of Tata Sons It is unlikely that any court would eventually rule the proceedings of this meeting legal, but litigation can drag on. In September, the Maharashtra charities commissioner, mysteriously, prohibited the Sir Ratanji Trust from holding a board meeting and taking formal decisions while the commission conducted an inquiry into frivolous charges trumped up by disgruntled persons being eased out of Tata trusts. Now trustee Venu Srinivasan, who falls in this category, has demanded the charities commissioner inquire into the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust as well. For over 150 years, founder Jamsetji Tatas simple mandate to his descendants was to do good for India. Do those at the helm of government reciprocate this trust? Whats in a Number? Famous personalities often apply for numbers for motorcar license plates that they deem lucky. For instance, Amitabh Bachchan is believed to favour numbers that end in two add up to two Sanjay Dutt opts for 4545 and Shahrukh Khan 555. The late NTR chose 9999, as his descendants now do. Arun Jaitleys preference was 6666. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay has started a new trend. In his 2024 film, The Greatest of All Time GOAT, the hero drove a limousine with the number plate TN CM 2026. Seeing how prophetic that number turned out to be, Vijays ally Thol Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, has been in a video-shoot in a car with a TN 07 CM 2031 number plate. Now NTK leader Seeman has applied for the number TN 08 CM 2031.

articleTitle: What do we tell a girl who asks ‘was it me?’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: women Crime in India, Crime in India against women, Crime against women, sexual assault, Sexual assault cases, Harassment case, girl harassment, sexual harassment cases, editorial, Indian express, opinion news, current affairs
description: Women do not need a handbook that instructs them in avoiding violence. We need a handbook, as a society, to prevent violence.
body_raw: I was seven years old. My swimming class had ended, and I was walking to the changing room when I sensed a presence behind me. I turned and found a member of the swimming complex staff charging towards me. In that split second, I shouted. My mother came rushing, and the man made an excuse about being there to protect me. As a cops daughter, I have grown up around men. And the prepubescent me, informed about good and bad touch, could instinctively identify an improper gaze. While I immediately told my parents what had happened, in the hullabaloo that followed, the incident was resolved. My parents were careful not to let me or themselves become paranoid, because even though nothing untoward happened, the trauma could have set in. As I confided in my parents, however, the incident made me aware of a reality that I was not just a child, but a girl. I wish this realisation had not come to me so early in my life. After losing my father as an adult, I became acutely aware of some older men who tried to show me unwanted avuncular affection. Again, there was no incident, but my skin crawled each time, and I began despising any conversation with them. What changed over the years? Only that my awareness of this reality grew deeper. So, when I read a news report about a minor rape survivor who told a court that the man she called uncle should be kept in jail until he grows old, my skin crawled again. The matter pertained to an incident that took place in July 2023, when the girl was seven. After announcing the verdict, the judge read out a personal message to the child, and now the Delhi High Court has ordered that the message be delivered to the child along with the compensation. My skin crawls while writing this article too. The judge further wrote that the court cannot give the child her childhood back but that the court had heard her words. The judge also lauded the childs courage in identifying the man, recounting the truth and speaking up. Even today, some of my relatives dismiss the incident at the swimming complex, arguing that a child couldnt have known. They remain firm in their belief that the man had indeed been there to protect me. This is infantilisation. Would we say the same to a seven-year-old boy who alleges that he has been attacked? If the answer is no, we need to ask why our lens is coloured for girls and gendered crimes. As per the National Crime Records Bureaus Crime in India 2024 Report, in cases pertaining to Section 4 penetrative sexual assault and Section 6 aggravated penetrative sexual assault of the POCSO Act, only 1,492 cases of a total of 44,126 involved an unknown or unidentified offender. This effectively puts the focus on why these wounds go so deep. Studies have documented how childhood trauma can lead to the development of insecure attachments, emotional dysregulation, and relational challenges in adult relationships. The judges message of encouragement goes beyond that one child. It acknowledged the wound that the seven-year-old was carrying. I have forgotten much, but that evening after the swimming class remains fresh in my memory. It came as a baton of strength to the woman who, after losing her father, had to battle the unwanted male attention that came in the garb of concern. When the judge lauded the childs courage, I felt exonerated, vicariously and personally. How can we tell the child that there will be a time she will have to devise her own handbook on how to deal with the male gaze? That she will have a drill of what to wear when using public transport? That she will be asked whether she asked for it? That she will need nerves of steel, veins of iron and a numb mind to ignore the stray palms that brush against her, even inside her home. How can we tell her this, for she will ask us the question we are unprepared to answer Was it my clothes? Was it my body? Was it me? Did I do anything to ask for it? Women do not need a handbook that instructs them in avoiding violence. We need a handbook, as a society, to prevent violence. The writer is an officer of the Indian Revenue Service Income Tax

articleTitle: LGBTQ influencer and makeup artist Madhu Sudan shot dead in Amritsar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: LGBTQ influencer makeup artist shot dead in Amritsar, LGBTQ influencer makeup artist shot dead, LGBTQ influencer Madhu Sudan shot dead in Amritsar, Amritsar, Madhu Sudan shot dead in Amritsar, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Around two to three rounds were fired, with an eyewitness claiming that Sandhu was shot at close range. A purported video of the incident showed Sandhu lying in a pool of blood. He was rushed to a private hospital where he succumbed to his injuries, police said.
body_raw: Punjabi LGBTq social media influencer and makeup artist Madhu Sudan, popularly known as Mad Sandhu, was shot dead by unidentified persons in Amritsar on Saturday with police saying they have some leads and the accused will be nabbed soon. The incident took place at Loharka road at around 6 pm, while Sandhu, the son of retired Punjab Police inspector, was waiting outside a car wash centre for his his vehicle. Two unidentified assailants on a motorcycle opened fire at Sandhu, before fleeing the spot, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sirivennela said. Around two to three rounds were fired, with an eyewitness claiming that Sandhu was shot at close range. A purported video of the incident showed Sandhu lying in a pool of blood. He was rushed to a private hospital where he succumbed to his injuries, police said. Based on a statement from the family, police registered an FIR and initiated the preliminary investigation. The motive of the attack was yet to be ascertained, a senior police officer said, adding they were working on multiple angles. DCP Investigation, Amritsar Commissionerate, Prabhjot Singh Virk said, .We have leads and will solve the case soon. We have recorded the familys statement. Sandhu had over 2 lakh followers on Instagram and was the founder of Mane Lane Unisex Salon in Amritsar and operated beauty academies offering courses ranging from self-makeup to professional bridal artistry. He faced homophobic trolling on his gay identity, and would hit back saying God has made me the way I am. A few months ago, an audio-video clip went viral featuring a confrontation between Sandhu and a Nihang Singh with the latter objecting to the Sandhus social media activities and older video reels, warning him to refrain from content deemed harmful to Punjabi culture and youth. Although Sandhu issued a public clarification stating he had changed his content style and stopped repeating past mistakes, he maintained that old clips were being recirculated intentionally to manufacture unnecessary controversy.

articleTitle: Rahul Gandhi launches ‘Satyagraha’ digital platform
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi (Source: PTI Photo)
description: “Across the country, people are fighting for their rights and too often, fighting alone. Gen Z, students, farmers, Adivasis, Dalits, women — every struggle has its own story. But a lone voice is often easier to silence,” Gandhi wrote in a post on X.
body_raw: Congress MP and Leader of Opposition LoP Rahul Gandhi launched the Satyagraha digital platform on Saturday, describing it as an initiative to consolidate issue-based protests unfolding across the country. Across the country, people are fighting for their rights and too often, fighting alone. Gen Z, students, farmers, Adivasis, Dalits, women - every struggle has its own story. But a lone voice is often easier to silence, Gandhi wrote in a post on X. The LoP invoked the ethos of Bapu and made an appeal to the people to register their protests against the government on Satyagraha. Bapu taught us that truth is our greatest weapon. But an even greater weapon is standing together with the truth. If you too are fighting against any injustice, share your story. It will take just two minutes, he said. He added, We want to help organise these protests, put them together and work with you to see if we can help you resolve what youre fighting for. Take a look at the Satyagraha website. Fill out the form. Enroll your movement, and we will try to see how we can support you. Well be in touch.

articleTitle: Flydubai attacker studied at British university, backed violence against women, Russia’s war
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News Live Updates:
description: A Flydubai co-pilot held over an attempted hijacking wrote posts backing violence against women while at a UK university.
body_raw: A day after the alleged attacker on flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv flight has been identified as Hamam Al-Hammami, fresh details have started to emerge of the Omani national. Al-Hammamis social media posts, especially his stance on women and Russias war on Ukraine, and his extremist views during this study at a British university have now surfaced. During his aviation study at Buckinghamshire New University, Al-Hammamis social media posts backed violence against women and harsh religious punishments. He also backed Russias war in Ukraine. The accused is now in custody in Abu Dhabi. The UAE prosecutor general has called the incident an attempted terrorist attack. Passengers embark on a FlyDubai aircraft at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel. Photo AP This comes days after a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv turned into an emergency on Wednesday, when the co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain with the crash axe kept in the cockpit. The Boeing 737 Max dropped about 17,000 feet before passengers and crew overpowered the co-pilot, and the plane landed in Saudi Arabia. Since then, the questions have moved from what happened in the cockpit to who the co-pilot is, and how he came to fly passengers. Israels defence minister has described it as a jihadist attack, The Telegraph says. The captain who was attacked, Smit Machchhar, is Indian. What al-Hammamis social media posts show? The Telegraph reviewed more than 2,000 posts from an account that appears to be linked to him, written between November 2021 and August 2022, while he was enrolled at Buckinghamshire New University BNU. The posts backed violence against women and harsh religious punishments. The Independent reports that he earned a distance-learning degree in aviation management at BNU in 2023, and the university says he did no pilot training there. The Conservatives are now asking for tighter checks on international students, including those who study online. The account used the name Pilot Hamam al-Hammami and the handle PilotHamam. Its owner described himself as an Omani civilian pilot from Muscat, and gave details that match al-Hammami, including that his mother is Syrian. According to The Telegraph, the posts include backing for violence against women, support for harsh punishments based on Islamic law, abuse of gay people and sexual insults. In one reply to a woman, the account said it would stomp on her head. In another exchange, about a man who hit a woman, the account compared the act to Russias invasion of Ukraine, which it appeared to praise. The paper says the account also argued that a man accused of blackmailing women should be executed instead of jailed for five years. It cited a Koran passage on offenders being killed or crucified. The Telegraph says these posts were all made while al-Hammami was a student at BNU, which he is believed to have attended remotely from Muscat. A pilot who took the same course at the time told the paper he never met any other student. A former lecturer said al-Hammamis name did not ring a bell, and that many online students do not attend live sessions because lectures are recorded. What does the university say, and why are tighter checks being called for? The Telegraph understands that no one raised a concern or complaint about al-Hammami while he was at BNU. The university has told the paper it will review his time there in light of the material now emerging. A BNU spokesman said the course covered aviation operations, such as mergers, sustainability and finance, and that entry was based on standard requirements. He said pilot training is checked separately, through airport security clearance and airline hiring checks. The university also said it has safeguarding and Prevent policies. A FlyDubai aircraft carrying Israelis who experienced an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia is seen parked at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel. Photo AP On the day of the attack, BNU said the Home Office had suspended its licence to sponsor international students over concerns about its compliance. The Home Office and the university both told The Telegraph the suspension had nothing to do with al-Hammami or the attack. The university has 20 days to respond before the licence is revoked. Chris Philp, the shadow home secretary, told the paper that universities should do more vetting at admission, because people on online courses can still influence others and use their British credentials. Figures from the Higher Education Statistics Agency show BNU had 1,530 students from outside the UK in 2024-25, about 8 per cent of its 18,490 students. What happened on the flight, and what are investigators asking? The Independent reports that about two hours into the flight, al-Hammami took the crash axe and slashed at Captain Machchhar. The plane dropped about 17,000 feet. The Telegraph says Machchhar, though badly hurt, opened the cockpit door so passengers and crew could overpower al-Hammami. The plane landed in Saudi Arabia, in Tabuk. However, al-Hammami allegedly told investigators he meant to crash the plane in Israel. Israeli investigators arrived in the UAE on Saturday to question him. Officials in both countries are trying to learn whether he acted alone or with a network. Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said accomplices will pay a heavy price. Some former US diplomats and regional analysts have said the attack may have aimed to damage the 2020 Abraham Accords, The Independent adds. The joint investigation is currently focused on how al-Hammami passed employment background checks. Oman Air previously removed Hammami from flight duties after intelligence officials discovered extremist materials on his devices and noted visits to radical websites, according to reports by The Wall Street Journal and ABC News. It remains unclear whether Omani officials shared these security concerns with neighbouring states or international carriers. The paper adds that supporters of al-Qaeda have used the incident in their propaganda, though no group has claimed it.

articleTitle: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dies at 94
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dead
description: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao died in Chennai on Saturday night due to age-related health complications.
body_raw: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, who directed some of the most innovative and genre-defining films in Indian cinema including the dialogue-free Pushpaka Vimanam, and the time-travel epic Aditya 369, died at Kauvery Hospital in Chennai on Saturday night. He was 94. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao was admitted to the hospital after his health deteriorated recently. He had been receiving treatment for age-related ailments. Born on September 21, 1931, in Gudur, Andhra Pradesh, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao began his career as an assistant to director L.V. Prasad before making his directorial debut with Neeti Nijayiti 1972. Also Read From Indias first time-travel epic to SSR61 How the 94-year-old filmmaker is set to disrupt cinema again Across a career spanning six decades and five languages, he directed some of the most innovative films in Indian cinema. Even at 94, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao refused to stop. His final film, Sing Geetham, a musical fantasy produced by Nag Ashwin, was completed earlier this year, making him among the oldest active filmmakers in the world. Actors, filmmakers and industry veterans across South Indian cinema have begun sharing tributes and condolences on social media. Actor Jr NTR called him a visionary who thought ahead of his time, delivering films that feel fresh even across generations. Composer Devi Sri Prasad wrote on X, Dearest SINGEETAM SIR..We wil MISS YOU Sir.. You will always live in our Hearts. You are an Unparalleled LEGEND..An Everest of Positivity filled with Evergreen Youth..The Movies You made with such Fururistic Ideas and Techniques are lessons to all of us and the Future Generations of Film Makers too. Thankyou Love You for Everything Sir..Iam blessed to have known You worked with You Sir. Singeetham Srinivasa Raos most notable films include Mayur, a biographical drama on amputee classical dancer Sudha Chandran that won several awards. Pushpaka Vimanam, a dialogue-free black comedy starring Kamal Haasan, won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Aditya 369, starring Nandamuri Balakrishna and featuring music by Ilaiyaraaja, was the first Telugu science fiction film to depict time travel. Bhairava Dweepam, also starring Balakrishna, was a high-fantasy adventure that completed a 100-day run in 28 centres. He also worked extensively in Kannada and Hindi cinema.

articleTitle: Campus gate shut, food for protesters stopped: Ambedkar University students claim ‘manhandled by guards’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The confrontation is the latest flashpoint in a protest that began with a five-point demand charter but has since widened into students voicing concerns about how the university is run.
description: The Indian Express had reported on August 7 that AUD has sought “attendance-cum-whereabouts records” for PhD scholars receiving fellowships and had said that unauthorised absence from on-campus research work could affect their fellowship.
body_raw: At the gates of Dr B R Ambedkar Universitys Kashmere Gate campus, students gathered on Saturday with packed food in their hands. It was meant for students and PhD scholars who had been sitting in an indefinite protest for six days inside the campus with demands ranging from drinking water and classrooms to faculty shortages, student representation, and access to campus areas. But those outside the gate alleged that security guards stopped them from entering the campus and they could not hand over food to the protesters. Blessy, an MA student of Gender Studies, said students were stopped from entering the campus despite many having classes and exams. While alleging that the campus was closed to students on Saturday, she claimed that guards stopped students outside from passing food to the protesters and manhandled those trying to receive it. The Public Relations Office of the university, however, said in a statement on Saturday that items being delivered at the gate beyond normal hours were checked by security personnel on safety grounds. It also said that its medical team was monitoring the protesting students and providing assistance. It further said that the library, computer laboratories and some blocks had been closed for maintenance and that students had been informed in advance. Students have manhandled security guards, and the issue is already in the cognisance of the Delhi Police. University security guards have not initiated any action on their own. Their role is limited to maintaining campus security as per standard protocol, the PRO office said. Further, the AUD said that while it had designated a place for peaceful protests, students are sitting in the area close to the library and classrooms, which is also adversely affecting other students. It said its Proctors office had appealed to the protesters to move to the designated area. Maintaining that it was in continuous dialogue with the protesters, the university said it had positively responded to their permissible and legitimate demands. The confrontation is the latest flashpoint in a protest that began with a five-point demand charter but has since widened into students voicing concerns about how the university is run. At the heart of the protest are demands to reopen the universitys main gate for students, remove iron gates separating the administration and student areas, reinstate the PhD fee waiver, withdraw a July 31 circular requiring students to inform the university four days in advance about holding public gatherings and remove compulsory attendance requirements for PhD scholars. The Indian Express had reported on August 7 that AUD has sought attendance-cum-whereabouts records for PhD scholars receiving fellowships and had said that unauthorised absence from on-campus research work could affect their fellowship. Aameen Amitoj, a PhD scholar in Urban Studies, said, For PhD students, the fee waiver was discontinued, with the university citing the stipend received by research scholars as the reason. He added that the closure of the main gate had forced students to use the back gate. The main gate of the university has been shut off for students. Only VC, Proctor and Registrar can enter from that gate, he said. Vivek, Treasurer of the Karampura Campus Council and an MA Performance Studies student, pointed to another gate-installed inside the campus about one-and-a-half years ago. It literally divided the campus into two parts. On one side is the student community, and on the other side is the administration, he said. He added that students are struggling for basic facilities at AUDs Karampura campus. Drinking water remained unsafe for nearly six months as RO systems and water coolers were not functioning. Students were forced to buy water from the canteen, he said. Vivek also flagged faculty shortages. It has been almost two-and-a-half months since my third semester began, and we still do not have a teacher for one of our subjects. A masters student from the Karampura campus said students were dealing with poor facilities, inadequate classrooms and faculty shortages. We dont have drinking water. We dont have clean bathrooms. Some students dont even have any faculty to teach them. Timetables are always clashing because there arent enough classrooms., the student said, adding that PhD scholars lacked dedicated spaces to work and hold discussions.

articleTitle: El Nino may push up food prices, but India better prepared than in 2009: Scientists
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The researchers said that El Nino's impact could extend to the winter monsoon as well. (File)
description: This was one of the assessments made during a session
body_raw: Indias history with the El Nino and an understanding of the countrys advances in agricultural policies, such as insurances and resilient seeds, suggests that there could be limited food and cattle fodder inflation and a small potential dip in the economy. This was one of the assessments made during a session, El Nino Meets a Warming Indian Ocean Understanding the Impacts on Extreme Events and Society, organised by IIOE-2 Early Career Scientists Network ECSN, a global community of early career researchers, dedicated to advancing the understanding of the Indian Ocean. Panelist Dr Roxy Mathew Koll, a climate scientist at IITM Pune, said that India had confronted a strong El Nino in 2009, when the monsoon deficit was around 22. Food inflation after that was around 20 percent. Since then, we have around 56 per cent or more of agricultural land irrigated. We have good stocks, which buffer the inflation prices for rice and wheat. Other crops, like oilseeds and pulses, are getting affected by a rainfall deficit, he added. According to Dr Smita Bal, a scientist at the Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology, there was a possibility of a negative impact on the availability of the fish due to the rainfall deficit. Dr Himadri Saini, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Melbourne in Australia, added that no two El Nino are the same. The researchers said that El Ninos impact could extend to the winter monsoon as well. They pointed out that, with El Nino, there is, generally, an above-normal Western disturbances that bring the winter rainfall in North India. The Western Himalayas recently got very heavy rainfall, especially Uttarakhand and Nepal. Satellite images from 10 days ago show hardly any snow in the area. Now, it is packed with snow due to the recent depression-induced moisture dump and also the Western disturbance. We can hope for more rainfall or snowfall in North India areas, said Dr Vineet Singh, who moderated the event.

articleTitle: Noida’s Supernova society asks owners to give bachelor, student tenants one month’s notice
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Noida
description: The policy also seeks to regulate short-term and commercial use of residential premises, with the association aiming to ensure that flats remain within sanctioned residential use.
body_raw: Homeowners at Supertechs Supernova in Noida Sector 94, who have rented their flats to students or bachelors, have been asked to give the tenants one months notice and replace them, preferably with families, under new tenancy rules introduced by the apartment owners association. The association has also asked homeowners to refrain from renting flats to students and bachelors in the first place, and to prefer families, working professionals or members of any other lawful category. However, if the owners wished to continue with such a tenant, they may need to get their decision reviewed by the tenancy committee. If the committee doesnt give the clearance to the studentbachelor, then the owner cant let out the property to the said studentbachelor and they have to get their premises vacated within a month from the date of notice from the said committee, said the policy issued recently. On October 1, a video went viral on social media showing Tushar Sharma, a Sector 15 resident who allegedly operated a rented facility in Spira, a Supernova tower, arguing with a security guard after reaching the wrong gate. Sharma allegedly forced his way into the Supernova premises in his car. Noida Police later arrested him on preventive grounds, while his vehicle was seized and challans issued. In the policy, the association noted complaints of increasing nuisance at Supernova East and West-a residential complex of around 500 flats-including playing of loud music, smoking and drinking. It also listed alleged illicit activities like drug consumption as well as running illegal call centres involved in online fraud and prostitution rackets. Naresh Nandwani, adviser to the Supernova Apartment Owners Association SNAOA, said there had been several instances of flats being rented out for short-term stays. Further, the Policy for Regulation of Tenancies, Occupancy and Resident Conduct, 2026 stated that an apartment cannot be occupied by a number of people inconsistent with its size or sanctioned residential use. The association said the provisions would help prevent the society from being converted into a hostel. The policy also seeks to regulate short-term and commercial use of residential premises, with the association aiming to ensure that flats remain within sanctioned residential use.

articleTitle: ‘Further custody necessary’: ED gets Vatika promoters’ custody for 3 more days
articleFeaturedImageAlt: vatika
description: The Bhallas, arrested on September 28, were produced before Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (PMLA) Narender Sura after their initial four-day remand expired.
body_raw: A special Prevention of Money Laundering Act PMLA court in Gurugram on Friday extended the Enforcement Directorates ED custody of Vatika Limited chairman-cum-managing director Anil Bhalla and promoter Gautam Bhalla by three days in an alleged Rs 154-crore money laundering case linked to plot transactions in Gurugram. The Bhallas, arrested on September 28, were produced before Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge PMLA Narender Sura after their initial four-day remand expired. Seeking seven more days of custody on behalf of the ED, special public prosecutors Simon Benjamin and Atul Agarwal, along with Assistant Director Dilip Singh Shaktawat Investigating Officer, submitted that although statements of several individuals, including the accused, were recorded during the four-day custody, interrogation could not be concluded due to paucity of time and bulky record. The ED argued that custody was essential to confront the promoters with documentary evidence and with 10 other individuals acquainted with the case who have been summoned for recording statements. It said further custody was required to unearth and trace the proceeds of crime and verify the involvement of other persons in the alleged transactions. Opposing the plea, the defence argued that ED had sufficient time to complete its interrogation and alleged that notices issued on October 1 summoning witnesses were intended just to get the ED custody extended. The defence also submitted that the accused had not been confronted with any of the individuals whose statements had been recorded during the four-day remand. Instead, they were questioned about extracts of statements and contractual agreements already in the EDs possession, it was alleged. Maintaining that the investigation is entirely grounded in documentary evidence, including public documents, the defence urged the court to decline any extension. Partly allowing the EDs application, Judge Sura said that further custody of the accused was needed for the probe. After perusing the record produced before this court, the nature of investigation conducted till date, and the fact that for the purpose of thorough investigation, some other persons have been summoned for making statements under Section 50 of the Act, which may be required to be put to the accused for clarification of the facts, further custody is necessary, the court said. The court directed that both accused be produced before it on October 5 at 4 pm. The EDs probe, initiated in March on the basis of Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing FIRs, concerns allegations arising from plot transactions involving residential plots of Vatika India Next in Sectors 82 to 85 and Vatika India Next-2 in Sector 88A. The agency has alleged that land contracted for plots collected for between 2010 and 2012 was not substantially delivered and that some plots were redeveloped and sold to third parties. It has valued the allegedly undelivered plots at Rs 140.73 crore. The second allegation concerns a 2024 agreement with Scaler Ventures for 165 plots in Vatika India Next-2, where 14 plots were allegedly sold to third parties without consent. The agency has pegged the total alleged proceeds of crime in the case at around Rs 154.36 crore.

articleTitle: As activists try to return to Jantar Mantar, around 150 detained amid heavy security
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police detained the Protesters during protest against CEC near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Saturday.
description: Around 150 people, including AISA national president Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan were detained.
body_raw: For the second consecutive day, protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and raising concerns over the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls were stopped from reaching Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site, on Saturday. Around 150 people, including AISA national president Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan were detained. The police action drew a response from Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, who alleged that there were allegations of misconduct with women protesters during Saturdays demonstration. In a post on X, Gandhi referred to a female journalists allegation against a police officer. And this isnt the first time-weve seen video evidence before of police officers engaging in disgusting misconduct with women, said Gandhi. He said that Delhi Police comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs, and added that Union Home Minister Amit Shah should answer for this. After the journalist alleged that Delhi Police was not registering an FIR, several people allegedly squatted outside the Parliament Street police station. Later, a policemen told the gathering that the journalists complaint has been received and a probe was underway. The protesters had gathered near Patel Chowk and began marching towards Jantar Mantar, a day after around 550 people were detained while attempting to reach the designated protest site. Police had denied permission for Fridays demonstration and imposed prohibitory orders in the New Delhi district. Saturdays mobilisation followed a call by Bora after she was among those detained on Friday. Among those joining her were Congress leader Kapil Sibal, advocates Nitya Ramakrishnan and Pallav Sisodia, Bhushan and Yadav, besides members of student and civil society groups. Police began detaining protesters as they gathered and attempted to move towards Jantar Mantar. Multiple layers of barricades were put up on roads leading to the area, while police and paramilitary personnel were deployed at several points. Those detained were taken to different police stations across Delhi and later released, police said. AISA members alleged that a male police officer manhandled Bora and that another officer abused her. The police, however, rejected the allegations. Meanwhile, Delhi Police has registered three FIRs against unidentified persons in connection with the attempts to hold the demonstration on Friday. Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station. The FIRs invoke provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to disobedience of an order issued by a public servant, obstruction of a public servant in the discharge of duty, use of criminal force against a public servant and acts committed by several people in furtherance of a common intention. By afternoon, a familiar sight had returned to Central Delhi barricades blocking the roads towards Jantar Mantar, police and paramilitary personnel deployed across the area, buses waiting to take detainees away, and groups of protesters attempting to regroup. CPI MP writes to Shah over cops concealing IDs Meanwhile, the Communist Party of India CPI Rajya Sabha member P Sandosh Kumar on Saturday wrote to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, flagging the issue of Delhi Police personnel removing or concealing their identity tags and name badges before detaining or using force against protesters. The letter comes a day after more than 500 protesters were detained while making their way towards Jantar Mantar during a protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in the revision of voter rolls. In his letter, Kumar sought Shahs intervention into repeated use of violence, arbitrary detentions, manhandling and other unlawful practices by the Delhi Police while dealing with democratic protests. Kumar said he himself was detained on Friday along with CPI workers and cadres of the All India Students Federation AISF and the All India Youth Federation AIYF. Kumar called for an investigation into the use of force, arbitrary detentions, removal or concealment of identity badges, manhandling of protesters, deployment of plain-clothes personnel and the use of facial-recognition systems. He urged the Home Minister to ensure that police personnel deployed at Jantar Mantar remain identifiable and accountable and that constitutional safeguards, Supreme Court directives and Delhi Polices own rules are strictly followed.

articleTitle: Eiffel Tower row: ‘Never asked for removal of female staff’, says BAPS monk
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Eiffel Tower protest
description: The statement follows the September 29 announcement by the chief of the company operating the Eiffel Tower that he will be stepping down at the end of this year, following the controversy, AFP reported.
body_raw: Nearly a month after the Eiffel Tower controversy, a senior monk of the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Sect BAPS has said that the organisation had been given a clean chit and that it had never asked for the removal of female staff, referring to an investigation by the Parisian authorities. Eiffel Tower was closed for a day on September 7 after employees protested the removal of female staff during a private visit by a delegation of the Ahmedabad-headquartered BAPS on September 5. The delegation was led by its chief Mahant Swami. The visit was part of the Festival of Culture organised in Paris as part of the opening of the groups temple last month. In a video statement on Friday, Brahmavihari Swami said, Thecity of Paris had nominated an independent agency - the Inspector General of the city of Paris -whichconducted a completely neutral investigation, and BAPShas a clean chit.They BAPS never asked for the removal of female staff.Authoritieshave mentioned that the probe clears BAPS. He added, Somebody created a misunderstanding regarding the spiritual disciplines of a sadhu. Brahmacharya is one of the four stages of the Hindu dharma, and a little confusion was created across the world. The General Inspectorate of the City of Paris IGVP investigation reportedly found that there had been no explicit request from BAPS regarding the removal of female staff. The statement follows the September 29 announcement by the chief of the company operating the Eiffel Tower that he will be stepping down at the end of this year, following the controversy, AFP reported. Patrick Branco Ruivo has been the director general of the Socit dExploitation de la tour Eiffel SETE since 2018. SETE said the probe found operational flaws and shortcomings that resulted in the unacceptable exclusion of female staff, as per the report. Reacting to the investigation report, BAPS Paris issued a statement. From the outset, BAPS has consistently stated that it never asked for female employees to be hidden, removed or excluded. The investigation establishes the fact that BAPS made no such request for women to be excluded along the visitor route. We hope this clarification will contribute to a better understanding of the circumstances and allow everyone involved to move forward respectfully, it said. The BAPS delegation of nearly 100 monks visited at the end of a week of celebrations ahead of the inauguration of the Swaminarayan Hindu Temple in Bussy-Saint-Georges, in Seine-et-Marne, an eastern suburb of Paris, on September 6. The investigation report The investigation by the General Inspectorate of the City of Paris IGVP, as reported by French newspaper Le Parisien, found that the incident was the result of a collective dysfunction. The General Inspectorate, which was tasked with the investigation on September 8, conducted 14 interviews and examined documents provided by SETE at its request. At the end of its investigation, Le Parisien reported that the IGVP was categorical no, there was no explicit request from the Hindu religious delegation aimed at excluding women throughout the visit. The paper also reported that the investigation found that women were indeed sidelined during this visit.

articleTitle: Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh box office collection day 58
description: The Neem Karoli Baba biopic Hanuman Ansh's screens were reduced by more than half, but the sleeper hit continues to hold its own in front of Drishyam 3 even in its eighth weekend.
body_raw: Hanuman Ansh box office collection day 58Vishal Chaturvedis devotional film Hanuman Ansh, featuring Shobhinaw Satyaa as revered spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba, continues to hold its own in front of new tentpole releases at the domestic box office. Its latest threat is Abhishek Pathaks much-anticipated crime thriller Drishyam 3. Even the Ajay Devgn-starrer hasnt managed to slow down the sleeper hit, which is in its eighth weekend. Its now amassed Rs 379.96 crore gross and Rs 321.73 crore net at the domestic box office, and Rs 419.46 crore worldwide. Hanuman Ansh box office collection - Weekend 8 On its eighth Saturday day 58, Hanuman Ansh added another Rs 2.10 crore from 1339 screens to its domestic box office collection, a 6.7 drop from its eighth Friday day 57 earnings of Rs 2.25 crore from 1166 screens. Drishyam 3 did take away most of the holdover releases screens, as the latter earned Rs 2.90 crore from 4345 screens on its seventh Thursday day 56. Given the reduction in screens by more than half, Hanuman Ansh has managed to hold its own in front of a juggernaut like Drishyam 3, which amassed over Rs 66 crore on its opening day at the domestic box office, as per Sacnilk. Given its current momentum, Hanuman Ansh could manage to earn over Rs 6 crore in its eighth weekend despite stiff competition from the Ajay Devgn-starrer. In terms of its domestic net collection, Hanuman Ansh is now just Rs 20 crore away from overtaking Anurag Singhs period war drama Border 2 to become the second-highest-grossing Indian film of 2026. The Sunny Deol and Varun Dhawan-starrer ended its domestic run with a net collection of Rs 341.70 crore. The years highest-grossing Indian film remains Aditya Dhars spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge, starring Ranveer Singh, with a domestic net collection of Rs 1,108.90 crore. Hanuman Anshs historic box office run Hanuman Ansh has had an unprecedented box office journey. It released in cinemas on August 7. However, in the absence of any stars and scale, it managed to earn only Rs 25 lakh on its opening day and Rs 1.08 crore in its opening week. It then slipped down to Rs 40 lakh in its second week, facing fresh competition from Independence Day releases - Sunny Deols Batwara 1947 and Emraan Hashmis Awarapan 2. The trajectory changed in the third week when Hanuman Ansh finally crossed the daily threshold of Rs 1 crore on its third Sunday, collecting Rs 2.50 crore. It ended up earning Rs 10.40 crore in week 3, Rs 61 crore in week 4, and 90.25 crore in week 5, snowballing despite competition from tentpoles like Yashs Toxic A Fairytale for Grownups, Akshay Kumar and Saif Ali Khans Haiwaan, Kareena Kapoor and Prithviraj Sukumarans Daayra, Kunal Kemmus Vibe, Ali Fazals Mirzapur The Movie, and Sidharth Malhotras The Vvaan Force of the Forrest. Also Read - Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 2 Live Updates Ajay Devgn film crosses Rs 177 crore mark Hanuman Ansh slipped down to Rs 80.25 crore in week 6, followed by 44.80 crore in week 7. At the conclusion of the eighth week, itll now also release in its dubbed Telugu version, which may further aid its total box office collection. Since its overseas release by Hombale Films on September 11, its earned Rs 39.50 crore internationally.

articleTitle: Government nod for reserved forest status for 112 ha of Ridge, 2,073 ha still unprotected
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The move assumes significance as records show that over 2,073 hectares of encroached forest land in the Capital will remain unprotected even after this first set of notifications is set into effect. (File Photo)
description: This is despite the government making several announcements in recent months to notify several parts of the Ridge as reserved forest.
body_raw: To bolster formal legal protection granted to one of the Capitals most ecologically sensitive zones, the Delhi government on Friday approved the Phase-I notification to declare 112.3 hectares of the Northern Ridge-an extension of the Aravalli range-as a reserved forest under Section 20 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927. However, the government excluded 8.61 hectares of demarcated land from the reserved forest status. The move assumes significance as records show that over 2,073 hectares of encroached forest land in the Capital will remain unprotected even after this first set of notifications is set into effect. This is despite the government making several announcements in recent months to notify several parts of the Ridge as reserved forest. In May, the government declared 673.32 hectares of the Central Ridge as reserved forest. Then, in September, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced the approval of a draft notification to declare 400.541 hectares across 15 villages in the Southern Ridge as Reserved Forest. Weeks later, on October 2, a similar Phase-I notification was approved for 112.328 hectares of the Northern Ridge. The exclusions Despite this push, land parcels that were earlier demarcated remain left out from the notifications. For instance, in the Northern Ridge, the Delhi Forest departments approved Working Plan, which was formally sanctioned by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change MoEFCC, records the Northern Ridge area under Delhi Development Authority DDA jurisdiction at 138 hectares. Yet, only 121 hectares were brought to the table for demarcation, and barely 112.3 hectares would make it into the final Phase-I Section 20 notification and be designated as a reserved forest. Similarly, when the Delhi government issued its May 2026 gazette notification for the 991.9-hectare expanse of demarcated land at Central Ridge, it only approved 673.32 hectares under Section 20. Specifically, four pockets within a block were excluded from the notification the Presidents Bodyguard Ground 12.6 ha, an ISRO Earth Station 0.68 ha, the 14th-century Malcha Mahal monument 0.09 ha and a water pump station 0.15 ha. The gazette recorded that these were excluded from Phase-I and will be taken in subsequent phases of notification. Meanwhile, in an affidavit submitted last month to the National Green Tribunal NGT by the Deputy Conservator of Forests PM, defending its phase-wise approach, the Forest department admitted that final notifications under Section 20 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 are being delayed by a combination of encroachments, pending litigation and incomplete revenue Tatima proceedings. While the 400.541-hectare Phase-II A of the Southern Ridge currently awaits the Lieutenant Governors approval, vast tracts under Phase-II Part B remain entirely unnotified. According to the NGT submission, these excluded land parcels are heavily compromised by village abadis, unauthorized colonies, jhuggi jhopri JJ clusters and religious structures. Furthermore, it stated that these Phase-II B areas are undergoing joint ground re-verification with the Revenue department to determine their legal status. In addition, the Delhi Ridge Management Boards meeting minutes from June 29 this year also reveal that, out of 7772.3 demarcated hectares across all Ridge zones, 2073.226 hectares remain out of the proposed land for notification as it consists of khasras under Government allotments, Min Khasras parts of khasras pending Tatima Proceedings, khasras under stay due to Court Cases, FSO Matters, private khasras etc are under process of settlement. Although Delhis Ridge areas were first notified under Section 4 of the Indian Forest Act on May 24, 1994, statutory protection is only finalised through Section 20 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, which gives the area its enforceable reserved forest status after the claims and settlement process is completed. The legal contention Over the years, the pending matter of reserved forest status has been repeatedly flagged by courts. For instance, the Supreme Court-enabled Central Empowered Committee, in a May 2024 report, flagged that at least five per cent of Delhis Ridge area is under encroachment and four per cent has been diverted, while only 1.33 per cent had been notified under Section 20. In November 2025, in a judgement, Chief Justice B R Gavai and Justice K Vinod Chandran had observed It cannot be said that the effect of non-notification of Ridge as Reserve Forest deprives the said area of any protection. We are, therefore, of the view that without proper statutory protection, it would not be possible to properly preserve the integrity of the Ridge. We find that the GNCTD has not acted with swiftness in protecting the Ridge. not much has been done even after a lapse of almost three decades therefrom. Following this, in May this year, the NGT directed the Delhi Forest department to submit an update regarding the Central Ridge notification status and urged that the Delhi Ridge Management Board DRMB expedite its function to clear large-scale encroachments across the Ridge. Earlier, in a 2021 order, the tribunal had said there was an urgent need to finalise Section 20 notification for Ridge protection and directed that notification be issued within three months for areas where there were no contestations.

articleTitle: The silence that makes room for rape
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rape
description: What unsettles the writer is the frequency of hearing violence in a place where others are close by— and how few came forward.
body_raw: I keep returning to an image a woman walking towards a park gate behind her, a man holds out a covered platter. The headline calls him a hungry animal and her his food. I understand the anger, but not the metaphor. A rapist is a man making a choice, and he must answer for it. I was born, raised, and educated in Delhi. Both my parents were born here too. My mothers parents came from Punjab, and my fathers from Uttar Pradesh. I left for New York at 20 and returned when I was 46. I turn 54 in November. Delhi is not somewhere I observe from a distance. It is home. I have spoken against rape in America, in classrooms and at public gatherings. I remember the Cornell case in which a woman accused several men of raping her. It shook that community and stayed with me. A former student has since sued over allegations tied to a 2024 assault they have not been established in court. I kept asking what do people do when they see someone being harmed? Rape is not an Indian crime alone. People compare national statistics, but laws, definitions, and willingness to report differ numbers cannot settle the moral question. What unsettles me is how often we hear of violence in a place where others are close by- and how few came forward. I remember the 2012 Delhi bus rape. A young woman and her friend were attacked by six men on their way home. We came to know her as Nirbhaya. Delhi was filled with candles and anger strangers stood in the winter air and demanded change. Laws changed, but rape did not end. Nirbhaya is not Abhaya, the name used in the 2024 Kolkata case. A woman is a life, not a label in a file. The woman in the image is going somewhere ordinary into a park, into the evening. That catches me. A woman should be able to walk without becoming a warning or a debate about her clothes. The platter is not appetite. It is entitlement dressed up as metaphor. The man holding it is accountable. What troubles me is the publicness of some assaults a street, a bus, a park, with witnesses nearby. Some watch, film or look away. In the worst cases, some join in. Confronting an assailant can be dangerous, but we can call for help, make noise, draw others in, stay with the survivor if safe. A camera is not a conscience. A crowd is not protection if everyone waits for someone else to move. The rapist is someones son, brother, husband, father, uncle, neighbour, classmate, colleague or friend. Violence does not arrive from another species. I have asked in anger what kind of women raise these men. I no longer think that is the right question. A woman is not responsible for the crime of a son, brother or husband. That question shifts the burden back onto women. Women are not the only ones who shape a boy. Fathers, schools, friends, teachers, public figures and courts teach what a man may get away with. A boy who hears that no means try harder, that a girls freedom is an insult, or that male desire is a joke learns a dangerous script. A daughter may be told to return before dark while her brother gets the keys. We are responsible for what we teach and excuse. A sari is not consent No womans clothes cause rape. Neither do her confidence, work, language, independence, or the hour at which she walks. A sari is not consent a short skirt is not consent marriage is not permanent consent. She may drink, dance, change her mind, leave or refuse. If she freezes, goes quiet, fights, or tells someone later, none of that makes the crime hers. Why didnt she fight? is for the person asking, not the survivor. The other day, students at Lovely Professional University protested reports that a woman student had been sexually assaulted on campus. The police registered a First Information Report FIR based on student statements and promised an investigation. But the university called the reports rumours. By evening, the police said they had found no evidence to substantiate the allegation. Facts must be established fairly. Students fear deserves to be heard. Trust is hard to rebuild when young people feel they must block a highway before anyone listens. In Delhi, women students marched after the alleged gang rape of a teenager at Aastha Kunj Park, calling for safer streets and the right to move freely. Reports say Fridays march was moved from Siri Fort Road to Arun Jaitley Park to avoid traffic, where students continued their protest and drafted demands. The march was also a refusal to let womens lives shrink to the distance between a hostel gate and home. They were asking to occupy public space without fear. What does it cost a country when a man convicted of rape can still command followers? Former MP Prajwal Revanna was sentenced to life in one rape case. Asarams life sentence was upheld by the Rajasthan High Court he was later granted parole. Parole is not acquittal, and a sentence is not the same as having served it. Survivors see how long a powerful mans influence can last. The law must be exact. Public memory must be honest. When a politician, teacher, healer, massage therapist, yoga instructor, or godman abuses the trust attached to his role, the harm spreads beyond one woman. It tells others a title or following may count for more than their safety, that rules can bend for a man with influence. This is one cost rape leaves behind a life wounded and trust worn thin. Men and women have been each others companions for generations, standing together through grief, danger and ordinary days. In my classes and public appearances, I return to this subject because we can speak plainly about it. A man who stops a cruel joke, calls for help when a woman is harassed, or refuses to laugh along is doing what friendship asks of him. What should a woman do when she is being raped, harassed, molested, or taken advantage of? In the moment, she does what she can to survive. Afterwards, she deserves belief, protection and care. Ask what the perpetrator must answer for, who will stand beside her, and what must change so she is not left alone with the consequences. I want boys to learn consent I have lived in Delhi and New York. Both places have seen outrage fill a street and fade into routine. I do not want another night of candles followed by the old daylight. I want boys to learn consent before entitlement, witnesses to act, police stations to receive survivors with care, and courts to reach the truth without making a woman relive the crime endlessly. This is the minimum a society owes. I began with the woman walking towards a park. She should not look over her shoulder because a man mistakes freedom for invitation. The man in the image is not hungry. He is accountable. So is the witness who can safely help and chooses silence, and every institution that sends a survivor from one closed door to another. Rape is committed by the rapist. The silence that leaves him room belongs to all of us, and it is ours to break.

articleTitle: Punjabi LGBTQ influencer and makeup artist Mad Sandhu shot dead in Amritsar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjabi social media influencer and makeup artist Madhu Sudan
description: Police say they have some solid leads and will soon crack the case
body_raw: Punjabi social media influencer and makeup artist Madhu Sudan, popularly known as Mad Sandhu, was shot dead by unidentified persons in Amritsar on Saturday, with police saying they have some leads and the accused will be nabbed soon. The incident took place at Loharka Road at around 6 pm, while Sandhu, the son of a retired Punjab Police inspector, was waiting outside a car wash centre for his vehicle. Two unidentified assailants reached there on a motorcycle and opened fire at Sandhu before fleeing the spot, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sirivennela said. Around two to three rounds were fired, with an eyewitness claiming that Sandhu was shot at close range. A purported video of the incident showed Sandhu lying in a pool of blood. He was rushed to a private hospital where he succumbed to his injuries, police said. Based on a statement from the family, police registered an FIR and initiated the preliminary investigation. The motive of the attack was yet to be ascertained, a senior police officer said, adding they were working on multiple angles. Deputy Commissioner of Police DCP, Investigation, Amritsar Commissionerate, Prabhjot Singh Virk said, The investigation is currently in its initial stages. We have leads and will solve the case very soon. We have recorded the familys statement. Sandhu used to speak about make-up artistry and gender issues on podcasts and had built a strong digital presence, accumulating around 2.4 lakh followers on Instagram. The make-up artist was also the founder of Mane Lane Unisex Salon in Amritsar and actively operated beauty academies offering courses ranging from self-makeup to professional bridal artistry. Sandhu, who often faced homophobic trolling on his gay identity, would hit back, saying God has made me the way I am, and would remind his audience that if coming from a Jat Sikh family and living in a city like Amritsar, he could achieve success in life, then they too could. His follower base was highly polarised. While admirers supported his creativity, self-expression, and professional artistry by leaving encouraging comments on his tutorials and on his gender-fluid fashion choices, the posts also frequently attracted aggressive online harassment, homophobic trolling, and derogatory commentary questioning his credibility as an educator. A few months ago, an audio-video clip went viral featuring a confrontation between Sandhu and a Nihang Singh, with the latter objecting to the influencers social media activities, cross-dressing choices, and older video reels, warning him to refrain from content deemed harmful to Punjabi culture and youth. Although Sandhu issued a public clarification stating he had changed his content style and stopped repeating past mistakes, he maintained that old clips were being recirculated intentionally to manufacture unnecessary controversy. Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka slammed the AAP government over Sandhus murder, saying the law and order has completely collapsed in Punjab. The AAP government has failed to protect the life of the common man.There is an atmosphere of fear. Meanwhile, Bhagwant Manns government puts up massive hoardings proclaiming a magnificent government and an honest government. It is astonishing that neither Arvind Kejriwal nor Bhagwant Mann said a word about this, he said. Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had openly mentioned these threats on social media as well. Despite this, the government and police failed to take the matter as seriously as they should have, he said, adding that if the threats had been taken seriously in time and necessary security measures had been put in place, perhaps an innocent life could have been saved. Aujla demanded the early arrest of the accused and a thorough investigation into the case.

articleTitle: OpenAI safety employee quits, says ‘time for trial and error is over’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: OpenAI says its upcoming Astra model has triggered tougher cybersecurity safeguards because of its advanced capabilities. (Express Image/Agencies)
description: Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what ‌it calls "iterative deployment," releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge.
body_raw: A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the companys approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures. Writing in I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken, published by the Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being nearly careful enough and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems. The time for trial and error is over, Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation. Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls iterative deployment, releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge. The comments add to a debate within the AI industry over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed, or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly. Robinson, who said he spent 3-12 years at OpenAI, helped draft the companys preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches, wrote As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed. Were making sure our models dont become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down, an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement. Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

articleTitle: Amazon promises more local funding and less secrecy around data centers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AWS
description: Amazon also tried to separate the anxiety over AI from the debate over data centers.
body_raw: Amazon has become the latest big technology company to promise money for local communities and policy changes in reaction to anti-data-center sentiment that has become a political flashpoint around the country. In a lengthy blog post Friday, the company pledged 1 billion over five years to communities for workforce development, energy efficiency projects and other local priorities. Amazon also said it no longer used nondisclosure agreements with government agencies, a common practice that has created distrust with local residents. Without mentioning China by name, Matt Garman, the head of Amazons cloud computing division, said in the post that other countries were gunning to be at the forefront of artificial intelligence development. More than 100 data center moratoriums are being considered across the country, he wrote, and if these measures are enacted, the U.S. could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations. The tech industry has been on a data center building spree despite intense pushback around the country. The biggest tech companies will spend more than 750 billion on capital expenditures this year, with Amazon the top builder.
