Some of the facilities are traditional data centers that power online computing. Others, like a flagship Amazon data center in Indiana, have been tailored to the immense computing needs of AI. Other large tech companies have made similar commitments this year. Meta, for example, pledged 1 billion for communities and job training programs, and Microsoft pledged this year to stop using nondisclosure agreements with local governments. Rising local opposition has scuttled or delayed projects and has created a new bottleneck for tech companies looking to build quickly. Data centers have become a hot-button issue in the midterm elections, including in states that have generally welcomed data centers, like Ohio, Texas and Oregon. They have become a particularly difficult problem for Republicans trying to balance local concerns and President Donald Trump, who said the only reason communities would not want data centers was if they want to end up being backwards and poor. Distrust has grown with public fears of AI. A Quinnipiac University national poll released this week found that 71 of Americans would oppose the building of an AI data center in their community, up from 65 in March. Much of Garmans post focused on making the case that data centers are misunderstood. He argued that they used little water - far less than a typical golf course - and that the idea that data centers drive up power costs was misleading because the nations utility infrastructure was overdue for an upgrade. Amazon also tried to separate the anxiety over AI from the debate over data centers, arguing that data centers are the backbone of modern life, powering hospitals and banking systems. Amazons ban on nondisclosure agreements includes its dealings with public utilities. If it is involved in a project initiated by a third-party developer, the company said it would try to avoid having a developers NDA limit what Amazon or a government entity can say about the project. The companys commitments focused almost entirely on communities near data centers and did not wade into the bigger debate around AI safety that has consumed Washington. The Quinnipiac Poll released Wednesday found that most Americans thought AI would do more harm than good, and that almost three-quarters of Americans did not have much or any trust in the leaders of AI companies.

articleTitle: ‘So we don’t end up in jail’: Kapil Sharma on why he watches younger comics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sidharth Malhotra, Tamannaah, and Kapil Sharma on The Great Indian Kapil Show.
description: Tamanaah Bhatia and Sidharth Malhotra lauded Kapil Sharma for pulling off roasting without offending anyone, and asked if younger comics are learning from him.
body_raw: On Saturday, the cast of Deepak Kumar Mishras action adventure fantasy film The Vvaan Force of the Forrest, appeared as guests on The Great Indian Kapil Show on Netflix India. The films lead actors - Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia - couldnt help but heap praises on not only Kapil and his team, but also their co-star Maniesh Paul, for pulling off the art of roasting without offending anyone. Talking about Kapil and Maniesh on the show, Tamannaah said,Seeing you two made me realise hosting is on one side, but you guys are the original roasters. There are a lot of people who roast today, but you do the roast that families can also watch, When she asked Kapil if younger comics have learnt how to roast from them, the comedian quipped, Were observing these younger kids to learn what not to speak so that we dont end up in jail. Sidharth Malhotra also joined Tamannaah Bhatia in praising Kapil Sharma, his team, and Maniesh Paul for keeping comedy clean. Hats off to Kapil and team, and even Maniesh, for doing comedy and roasting in a clean way, for using clean words so that the one its targeted at can laugh instead of getting offended. There are no abuses at all. Thats the USP of the writing of this show, he remarked, as a flattered Kapil accepted the compliments. The Vvaan Force of the Forrest is co-produced by Ekta Kapoors Balaji Motion Pictures and Arunabh Kumars The Viral Fever. Also starring Sunil Grover, Anup Soni, and Shweta Tiwari, among others, it has collected Rs 58.85 crore at the domestic box office within 10 days of release, thus emerging as the fifth highest grossing film of Sidharths career so far. Samay Rainas roast vs Kapil Sharmas comedy Kapil Sharmas cheeky response to Tamannaah Bhatias question on young comics learning roasting from him might be a reference to Samay Raina, who hosts the roast show Indias Got Latent season 2, which also streams on Netflix India along with his YouTube channel. The show was removed from YouTube last year after a controversy following guest and Samays fellow YouTuber Ranveer Allahbadias inappropriate remarks during an episode. That led to three FIRs being filed against Samay, Ranveer, and a couple of others after massive online trolling. Samay took a year-long break from standup comedy before making his return with the special, Still Alive. He announced the return of Indias Got Latent during that show, which kicked off with Alpha stars Alia Bhatt and Sharvari as special guests. Also Read Archana Puran Singhs family, earning more than ever with YouTube, buys another Mumbai villa On Still Alive, Samay also responded to senior stand-up comedian Sunil Pals criticism that he should learn clean comedy from Kapil Sharma, claiming that even Kapil personally expressed his desire to appear on Indias Got Latent before it was forced to go off air. Samay and Ranveer also appeared as guests on a special World Laughter Day episode of The Great Indian Kapil Show earlier this year, when Kapil lauded Samays talent and even got Sunil to forgive both Samay and Ranveer for the controversy.

articleTitle: In conversation with Gulzar on the home he lost and his ‘longest home’, Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gulzar at his home in Mumbai
description: Veteran poet Gulzar on the home he lost, the city he found and all the words in between.
body_raw: On a day of pelting rain in Mumbai, when the highrises fade into grey silhouettes, a small slope on Nargis Dutt Road in the ritzy Pali Hill leads us to the storied home of one of Indias most definitive modern poets. Boskyana, 92-year-old poet and filmmaker Gulzars home, sits as a quiet haven amid glass and concrete reaching the sky. The raised road, reminder of a city that has been built several times over, has led the quaint white bungalow to live in a somewhat sunken space, somewhat tucked in the past and uninterested in the vertical growth of the frantic world above. As is well known, Boskyana is named after the poets daughter, Bosky filmmaker Meghna Gulzar. What is little known is that she is named after boski, a prized Chinese silk variety known for being soft and delicate. The idea, however, is from another time and place. Gulzars father was a textile trader in Pakistans Dina, an unassuming village located along the Grand Trunk Road in the heart of Pakistans Jhelum district. The poet once joked that if hed had a son, he would have named him Lattha crisp white budget-friendly cotton. It is the warp and weft of this metaphorical silk that runs through Gulzars life, with decades spent spinning language into an artform making the ordinary feel just as fine, weaving those pashmina-like phrases of love and loss Geeli hansi, waqt ke paanv, khwabo ki pudiya, seeli hawa and chand ki bindi wali ratiya, which continue to linger. A large bust of Mirza Ghalib carved in white marble stands guard at one end of the book-lined, exposed-stone wall in the poets living room. A screen divides the study from it. The poets voice drifts in from his book-drowned study - a discussion on the matter of his current iPad. He arrives on the other side in his trademark white, starched kurta pyjama, the frame frailer now, hair a shade greyer. But just as he speaks in that familiar, deep voice, the years seem to melt away. Ive just changed my iPad. And this old cover didnt fit. So a new one needs to be bought, he says, settling on an ottoman. For a writer who has spent decades measuring the weight of ink on paper, it is striking how technology seems to fit seamlessly into this otherwise handcrafted world. Like Online, one of his newer stories, where 11-year-old Suhani is telling her grandfather, Mr Syal, to play Patience on the iPad and not step out during COVID. There is a hint of Gulzar in it. He may be steeped in the rhythms of the past but has embraced the new phases with curiosity. Sitting in Gulzars home that is about half a century old, four days before his 92nd birthday and clutching his latest book Aamchi Mumbai My City in Stories and Poems Harper Collins, Rs 3,999, with English translation by Rakhshanda Jalil, home becomes an obvious subject to open with one that is built and another that is left somewhere and preserved in memory. Gulzars story also has these two homes, ones that have shaped him and his oeuvre, while getting infused into the syntax and cadence of his work. There is one that he left behind in Dina during a bloody Partition, the home that has been a constant refrain in his writing, including Raavi Paar and Footprints on Zero Line Writings on the Partition, among others. It is also a home he didnt revisit for a long time. He couldnt get himself to. His friend Paul Mahindra, who also assisted Bimal da Bimal Roy, told him not to go back. He said something which remained with me. Woh badla huya hoga It would have changed and those images which you are retaining in your head. when you wont find them, toh bohot taqleef hogi. So I did not go. I was about 70 when I went back for the first time, says Gulzar, whose visit was prompted by the hospitalisation of Pakistani poet and journalist Ahmad Nadeem Qasmi. Gulzar often refers to Qasmi as his guru. When I went to Lahore, my friends and I drove to Jhelum. I found my gali bylane soon and it was the same as it was. I visited the primary school where we sat on durries and studied. And suddenly I saw a block named after me. The inscription read Sampooran Singh Kalra urf Gulzar. It was next to another named after Fatima Jinnah. The farmland was gone but someone said of a tree-Ye ped murjha gaya hai, par ye ped abhi tak aapka hai the tree has wilted but it is still yours, says Gulzar, recipient of the Jnanpith Award and Sahitya Akademi fellowship, among numerous other accolades. After Gulzars family moved to Delhi and he was admitted to United Christian School, their house became almost like a refugee camp. People would keep coming from our village. Then my father would keep searching the camps to find anyone of his own. He was affected a lot, says the poet who was packed off on the Frontier Mail to Mumbai that would become the longest home I know, he writes in Aamchi Mumbai. What a strange city this is, and how strangely it rears those who come here. It fights and quarrels. It beats and bruises you. But it also gives you the fondness and affection of a friend. Gulzar writes in Aamchi Mumbai, comprising his impressions about Mumbai - from its Irani hotels, monsoon rain and ocean to its footpaths and people who live on them. When Saleem Sinai, the protagonist of Salman Rushdies Midnights Children, returns to Bombay, he says, Yes, it was my Bombay, but also not mine, capturing a city transformed by time. Does Gulzar, who has spent seven decades in what Rushdie calls the most Indian of Indian cities, feel the same from the time he alighted from the train, a frightened young boy? He sees the change through an unlikely lens the disappearance of Irani hotels from everyday Bombay. Once my toothpaste got over and my elder brother said, go get it from the Irani restaurant. I told him, I need toothpaste, not a pastry. So he told me, for any general store items, go to the Irani hotel, says Gulzar. The leitmotif reappears through his writing on Mumbai. Irani hotel was a complete culture in itself. You could go anywhere in the city and find an Irani restaurant. The North has always had places to drink water a pyau water kiosk or communal tap. In Bombay, Irani hotels put out free drinking water. Then, in chaar aana, I could have my lunch keema pav and tea was a full meal. That is what the Iranis were doing here, says Gulzar, who noticed how leftover food, paid for but untouched, was kept for fakirs, for the poor who would queue up at night for what was called the Irani biryani. Bhookha koi nahi rehta tha No one went hungry. As times changed, all of it got lost somewhere. These hotels and that culture are gone. That is what I miss, says the poet, who adds that in this city, if one is able bodied, they will survive. Aur kuch nahi toh smandar ke kinaare seepiyaan bun kar bhi log guzara karte rahe hain If nothing else, people have managed to sustain themselves simply by gathering seashells along the coastline He recalls the time when Morarji Desai was chief minister and amid prohibition, the clandestine, underground bars emerged. Illicit liquor was available at Pascal ka Adda and Aunty Bars, where alcohol was served with salt to be licked along, says the poet. Characters drinking this illicit liquor often appear in his stories, including in Mez ke Upar, Mez ke Neeche. The way people lived in jhopadpattis, it was full of life. Poverty was there but you never felt ashamed of it. There was a pride and dignity of life to it, says Gulzar. The conversation pauses when old friends Sukhwinder and Jyoti arrive unannounced to wish him ahead of his birthday. The room changes colour, with almost a childlike happiness that takes over Gulzar. Not all of it is to do with the bottle of scotch theyve brought as a present. Aye meri dhee hai, meri maangi huyi beti she is my daughter, my asked-for daughter he introduces Jyoti, also his tennis partner. Giddy, with the rare chance to speak in Punjabi with everyone in the room, he introduces us. This girl is also from Punjab. te Punjabi bol lendi hai she can speak in Punjabi, he tells Jyoti. Like the shade of an old tree, Punjabi occupies a prized place in Gulzars literary life. It is not just his ma boli mother tongue, but one he was encouraged to return to even as he moved through Urdus literary world as a young poet in the Bombay of 50s and 60s. Filmmaker and writer Balraj Sahni, who had also spent time in Santiniketan, would urge him to attend the meetings of the Punjabi Sahit Sabha. Balraj saab told me, Gurudev ne kaya si mainu, madri zubaan ch likh Gurudev had told me to write in the mother tongue, he says. Once in Mumbai, Gulzar lived with his elder brother before moving out and making ends meet by working in a motor garage. The two had their differences. The best part of that motor garage job was that in the time that the paint dried, I could sit and read, says Gulzar, who still regrets having to leave his education at Delhis St Stephens College, where he studied for a few months before joining Khalsa College in Mumbai. But they didnt have Urdu and I didnt want to study Hindi, says Gulzar, who soon moved to National College. Gulzar ended up living in Coover Lodge in Andheris Chaar Bangla, where distinguished writer Krishan Chander lived in the main house. Sahir Ludhianvi rented the first floor and he rented the outhouse for Rs 18 a month. The Progressive Writers meetings were held on Sundays, while the Punjabi Sahit Sabha met on Saturdays. It was at these meetings that literature on social inequality, religious hypocrisy and marginalisation was discussed. Both these associations were very well-knit. Most of the Leftists were there. Poet and lyricist Shailendra was a unionist since he worked in the Railways. As for films, they were never the aim of any of these writers, says Gulzar, who was pushed into films by Shailendra. He would say, achhe khaase writer ho, jaate kyun nahi You are such a competent writer, why dont you go? All these big writers - Ali Sardar Jafri, Krishan Chander, Rajinder Singh Bedi, Sahir Ludhianvi - inki kitaabein padhi huyi hain and then seeing them in person as a young boy was huge, says Gulzar. Another space he frequented was the Bombay Youth Choir. This is how he met composer Salil Chowdhury, founder of the orchestra, who later collaborated with Gulzar on Hrishikesh Mukherjees Anand 1971, among many others. The choir was interwoven with a certain cultural awakening in post-Independence India. In National College, his batchmate was writer Sagar Sarhadi and soon literature became a passion. At that time, if you carried a book on the Russian Revolution, you were considered an intellectual, he says with a chuckle. The two were surrounded by Punjabi writers like Sukhbir, a committed communist, Harnam Singh Naaz, among others. This is when Sagar and I took an oath of sorts we will not take up a job we will only write. Aur nahi hai isme kamai toh dekhenge, says Gulzar. That is how the journey began. People ask me if I was fond of writing since childhood. Its all a myth. Life takes its own time. to adapt your talents and aptitude, he says. He fondly remembers his literary life in Bombays trams. How all of his young writer friends would settle on the upper deck of a tram and continue discussions and recitations as the city rolled past. A one-anna ticket allowed them to ride through the day, so if the discussion continued, so did the journey. From Charni Road to Dadar, hum afsaane sunaate the wed narrate stories. People turned to listen in conductors began to recognise us, knew we would turn up on Sunday. It became so interesting. So this is the city I have spent more than 60 years in, says Gulzar. When American writer Howard Fasts The Naked God came out, explaining why he had left the Communist Party, there was a commotion in our world Howard Fast was the only conversation then. When Faiz would write a nazm from jail, ek leher si daud jaati thi. Wed say, Faiz saab is a very optimistic man, how can he write this. everything was discussed in great detail, he says. Eventually Gulzar found his way into Bimal Roys world. His first screenwriting and lyrics credit came with Bandini 1963. He would go on to make his directorial debut with Mere Apne 1971, about the growing disillusionment among unemployed youth. Decades later, in 2026, its central theme remains relatable. The films that followed - Parichay, Aandhi, Maachis, among others - brought the same literary sensibility to stories of a changing India. As for the songs, his were away from familiar tropes. Gulzar was expanding the vocabulary. Also Read - Gulzar didnt write women to be liked, he wrote them to be understood Not far from Ghalib is a harmonium that RD Burman once brought to Boskyana so that he and Gulzar could experiment with music late at night. The kind of partnership where Gulzar would bring abstract, free-verse poetry, and Burman would somehow compose those into brilliant tunes. The non-rhyming, prose-like lyrics of Mera kuch samaan, tumhaare paas pada hai Ijaazat, 1987 are a fine example of that partnership. Tomorrow you will bring a copy of the newspaper and ask me to make a tune out of it, Burman had told Gulzar before creating one of his most minimalist and haunting melodies. In the poets six-decade career as a lyricist, that song remains a masterpiece that broke every known rule in songwriting. Then there was the equation of the material and non-material - Sawan ke kuch bheege bheege din, khat mein lipti raat. are the belongings a beloved is asking back from her companion. A couple of months ago, he wrote a song for India Ek akela Hindustani, do mile toh Hindustan, a quami tarana a patriotic song for todays generation. The song invokes Hindustan, a term that belongs to an older, more layered vocabulary of the nation. Main sa ki umr mein tha, aur main ni se bhi aage nikal gaya hoon. Ab main upar ka sa ho gaya hoon, he told a few young music students in Kolkata. At 92, Gulzar now has his own musical analogy for age, using ascending notes of the alankaar to describe life. But this upar ka sa may just be the beginning of another octave. After all, he keeps finding words for a changing world. The world where AI may generate Gulzar-like poetry in seconds. But can it live inside those words, or the spaces in between? For that, well always need Gulzar.

articleTitle: ‘Everyone was thrashing me’: Salman Khan recalls how Dus Ka Dum saved him from career downfall
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Salman Khan talks about Dus Ka Dum on Bigg Boss 20
description: Salman Khan recently recalled how he had almost turned down the 2008 television game show Dus Ka Dum as he was going through a difficult phase at the time.
body_raw: In the latest Weekend Ka Vaar episode of Bigg Boss Season 20, host Salman Khan recalled how he had almost turned down the 2008 television game show Dus Ka Dum as he was going through a difficult phase at the time. However, his father, writer Salim Khan advised him to take up the show. Salman also spoke about how Amitabh Bachchan found a new level of popularity through Kaun Banega Crorepati KBC. Advising the housemates to be their true selves inside the Bigg Boss house, Salman said, I want to give you an example from my own life. I did Maine Pyaar Kiya and many other films, and then I came on TV after I got a show. And at that time, there was a lot of negativity about me everywhere - from court cases, relationship, to my films. It was amid this difficult phase that Salman Khan was offered the opportunity to host Dus Ka Dum, but the actor admitted that he initially had reservations about taking it up. I wasnt going to do it because there was so much being talked about against me. Every newspaper, TV channel was thrashing me left, right and center. I spoke to my father about it and asked for advice. Salman then recalled a piece of advice from his father, Salim Khan, that helped him deal with the negativity, reshape his public image and connect with audiences on a more personal level. He said, Dont you trust your personality, heart, and upbringing? I said yes and he asked me to say yes to the show. He told me to be myself in the show. In that one show, they got to know who I was. Also Read - Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 2 Live Updates Ajay Devgn film sees 13.7 drop earns over Rs 177 cr The host continued, Everyone forgot Maine Pyaar Kiya, Hum Aapke Hain Koun, Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam, Karan Arjun, and all my other films. They just watched me on Dus Ka Dum because they didnt see an actor, they saw a person. Drawing a parallel with Amitabh Bachchans television journey, Salman pointed to how Kaun Banega Crorepati allowed audiences to see a different side of the veteran actor. The same thing happened with Mr Bachchan. The day he did KBC, he became Kaun Banega Crorepati uncle. So, they forgot all my film work and only remembered only Dus Ka Dum. I did two seasons there and then I have been hosting Bigg Boss since 17 seasons. My image in the media was cleared in one episode. There were ups and downs after that as well, but you have to show who you truly are, Salman concluded.

articleTitle: Six lanes to two: What Barapullah can learn from traffic solutions abroad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: View of Barapullah Face-3, after the inauguration, in New Delhi (Express Photo by Praveen Khanna)
description: In 2003, a six-lane highway over Cheonggyecheon River – used by around 160,000 vehicles every day – was demolished to revive the water body. The expectation was that the traffic would be in a deadlock.
body_raw: Did Delhi need another flyover? Four days after the Barapullah Phase 3 flyover opened, the question is no longer just about the bottleneck at its merging point, where traffic from six lanes is forced into two. It is about the larger idea of putting more traffic on flyovers in a city where congestion keeps shifting from one road to another. The project was originally scheduled for completion in 2017, but construction delays pushed its opening to 2026. Over these nine years, while vehicle numbers rose significantly, East Delhi and the wider NCR also grew, changing vehicular movement between East Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, and South Delhi. The result The new stretch is meeting an older, narrower road and the traffic has nowhere to go. Barapullah Phase 3 has six lanes, one in the Mayur Vihar direction and the others towards South Delhi. The six lanes merge into a three-lane carriageway. Ideally, the combined carriageway should have been five lanes wide. It is not and the traffic has to further merge into the two-lane Phase 2 flyover, with vehicles from all lanes competing for space. This is the problem with flyovers, says urban practitioner Hitesh Vaidya, who used to be associated with the National Institute of Urban Affairs. A flyover is like shifting the traffic from the ground floor to the first floor, he said. Other countries have tried different approaches. In 2006, near Birmingham in the United Kingdom, bottlenecks in a stretch was solved using a dual system Hard Shoulder Running HSR and Variable Mandatory Speed Limit VMS. The systems ensured that no more lanes were made and no additional flyovers came up. Under HSR, an emergency breakdown lane is opened to traffic when sensors detect congestion. VMS uses sensors to change speed limits according to traffic conditions, helping maintain gaps between vehicles and keep traffic moving. A Transportation Research Board assessment found that the system reduced average travel time by more than 32, while accident rates also fell. In 2003, a six-lane highway over Cheonggyecheon River-used by around 160,000 vehicles every day-was demolished to revive the water body. The expectation was that the traffic would be in a deadlock. But as per an article published in Behavioural Design Academy, the move saw a reduction in congestion with vehicular traffic reducing by over 45. According to experts, in India, better planning was needed to solve the Barapullah fiasco. A detailed survey needs to be done to assess the volume of traffic on the flyover and where its moving. I dont know if they have been done properly. Because the plan was made over 20 years ago, its not feasible now, said Prof P S N Rao, former director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Delhi. Rao said that in India, the best possible solution is to bolster public transport rather than continuing to build flyovers. People take the Barapullah because other routes, like through Nizamuddin or ITO, are already choked. You create more alternative routes, more vehicles come. Now that we know that even Barapullah is not going to cut it, just take the Metro, he said. With flyovers, you are shifting traffic from one road to another. Instead of putting more resources to sort the flyover, we need to invest in more Metro lines. Most Western countries are doing it. Even the well-off take public transportation. Why not us? he asked. As of now, the solution with the Delhi Police is putting up barricades and an extra traffic light. Based on their drone survey, they are set to manually manage the merging of lanes using the traffic lights and personnel, so that all lanes dont empty together, say officials.

articleTitle: Israel had names before flydubai FZ1073 took off, failed to flag Omani co-pilot: Report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Netanyahu
description: Israeli officials had the Flydubai crew list before the Tel Aviv flight, says Haaretz, but the Omani co-pilot was not flagged. The Transport Ministry will not say whether it checked the names.
body_raw: Before Flydubai flight FZ1073 left Dubai for Tel Aviv on Wednesday, Israeli officials already had the names of everyone on board. The list of crew and passengers had been sent to them in advance, according to Israeli newspaper Haaretz. Yet the Omani co-pilot, who is now accused of attacking Indian Captain Smit Machchhar and trying to crash the plane, was not flagged. Here are the key facts and figures 174 people were on the Boeing 737 Max, most of them Israelis. 705 am The flight left Dubai on Wednesday, 30 September, and climbed to 34,000ft, according to Flightradar24. Just over two hours later the plane began to descend and fell more than 17,000ft in about two minutes. 15,000ft the height at which the plane levelled out, after passengers and crew overpowered the co-pilot. Code 7500 The transponder was set to this code, which signals unlawful interference. 2 reserve pilots on board took the controls and landed the jet at Tabuk, in northwest Saudi Arabia, at 945 am local time. 1 captain, Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, was hurt in the cockpit and is now in hospital in Abu Dhabi. Now the questions are about who knew what before take-off, and why a man who had reportedly been barred from flying in his own country was in the cockpit at all. Haaretz, quoting security sources, reported that Israels Transport Ministry and the Mossad were meant to check the crew list. The Israel Tax Authority confirmed it received the list. The Transport Ministry would not say whether it went through it. What did Israel know before the flight? According to Haaretz, Israeli government officials received the crew and passenger list ahead of the flight. Here is what is known and what is not What is confirmed Israeli officials received the list of crew and passengers before the flight. The Israel Tax Authority confirmed to Haaretz that the list reached it. Security sources told the paper that the Transport Ministry and the Mossad were supposed to check the crew names. The Omani co-pilot was not flagged before the flight. What has not been confirmed Whether the Transport Ministry went through the list. It declined to say. Whether the Mossad checked the crew names. The part of the Haaretz article seen here does not say. Whether any Israeli body raised a concern about the co-pilot before take-off. None has said so publicly. Whether Oman told Israel or any airline about its reported concerns over the co-pilot. Al Jazeera reported that it is unclear. Who is the co-pilot, and what is known about his past? Three people with knowledge of the matter, including a Gulf diplomat and a Western diplomat, told the AP news agency that the co-pilot is Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national. They spoke without giving their names. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, said Omani authorities had barred him from flying in Oman over concerns about alleged extremist views. It is not clear what those views were, or whether Oman told other countries or airlines. CNN, citing a source and an Israeli official, said he was born in the UAE to a Syrian mother and spent several years there. CNN also quoted a regional diplomatic source who said he had been removed from flight training over similar concerns and moved to another role. A LinkedIn profile with his name, seen by CNN, says he spent seven years at Oman Air and left in February 2025. It says he joined Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and left in January 2026. Buckinghamshire New University has confirmed he finished a distance-learning course in aviation management there, and says he did no pilot training with it. A Gulf diplomat told AP that investigators are trying to learn whether he acted as a lone wolf or had links to extremist groups. What happened on flight FZ1073? According to Flightradar24, the plane left Dubai at 705 am on Wednesday and climbed to 34,000ft. A little over two hours later, it began to descend, and the data showed it fell more than 17,000ft in about two minutes before it climbed and dropped again. Inside the cockpit, the co-pilot had attacked Indian pilot Machchhar. The UAE says he used the emergency crash axe, a tool kept in cockpits to cut through the aircraft in an emergency. Machchhar later told Prime Minister Narendra Modi, from a hospital in Abu Dhabi, that he was on the floor and could feel the plane dropping. He said he knew it was the last chance to do something. He told PM Modi he reached the door and opened it, and people came in. Passengers and crew overpowered the co-pilot. The plane levelled out at about 15,000ft, and its transponder was set to code 7500, which signals unlawful interference. Two reserve pilots on board took the controls and landed the jet at Tabuk at 945 am local time. Saudi authorities said Captain Machchhar was taken to a hospital and then airlifted to Abu Dhabi after medical clearance. What is the UAE saying, and what happens next? UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi said on Saturday that investigators found the co-pilot had begun what he called a terrorist act. He said the co-pilot attacked the captain with the crash axe and tried to take control of the aircraft. On Thursday, he had ordered investigators to check whether the incident was tied to terrorist activity or intent, or to planning or direction by others. Abu Dhabi is leading the case because the plane is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag. Al-Shamsi said UAE law covers crimes on board even outside the country. Investigators are looking at the motive, any links to others, and physical and digital evidence. The UAE has not said what the motive was, or whether it thinks al-Hammami acted alone. UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on X that the attack shows the regions fight against extremism is not over. Flydubai flights to Israel remain suspended while the investigation is ongoing. Did Netanyahu miss a warning before 7 October as well? The questions about the Flydubai crew list come at a bad time for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces a close election on 27 October. He is also dealing with a second security question, this one about the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023. On Sunday, the Wall Street Journal published a report saying Netanyahu had been warned of that attack by Egypts intelligence chief, Abbas Kamel. According to the report, Kamel phoned the prime minister a few days before the attack. It adds to earlier claims that Kamel flew to Israel in September 2023 to tell security officials in person that Hamas was planning an attack. Netanyahu is alleged to have received warnings before 7 October, and the claim has followed him since.

articleTitle: It rained the day after he died. For a farmer family in Yavatmal, it was too late, again
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nima Malekar sits on a bed in the hall of her home, pictures of her two sons hang on the wall above, while that of her husband is placed on the floor; The agricultural land of Malekars that shows no water retention. (Express Photos by Ankita Deshkar)
description: Nima Malekar has now lost both her children and her husband to suicides, reportedly caused by farm distress and the wait for a borewell electricity connection. Meanwhile, drought has returned
body_raw: The Tulsi plant outside her house in the brown and dry Pimplapur village in Yavatmals Ralegaon is unusually green. Nima Dnyaneshwar Malekar has barely noticed. In five years, the 58-year-old cant remember a time when she was not in mourning. First it was for her elder son Nikhil, 28, who died of suspected suicide in March 2021. Younger by three years, Tapaveen, her only other child, followed his brother in October 2024. On July 22 this year, Nimas husband Dnyaneshwar, 65, took his own life. Her voice breaking, Nima says she had no idea what was going on in their minds. We worked so hard. My children worked, their father toiled. But what was the use? There is nothing left. Nimas nephew Harish Choudhary says the reasons for all three deaths, by hanging, were the same-recurring crop losses, inadequate rainfall and difficulties in securing an electricity connection to operate a borewell. The Malekars are not alone in this, as large parts of Maharashtra, including Yavatmal, again stare at drought. Last week, the state declared drought in 265 of its 358 tehsils-or about three-fourths of Maharashtra. As per official figures, between January and June this year, even before this years drought cycle actually hit, Yavatmal had witnessed 128 farmer suicides. Nima and Dnyaneshwar had built their house only this year after getting funds under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. Left all alone in it now, Nima spends half her time at her brothers home in Kosala village, as neighbours and family help look after her land. She is just carrying on, she says. I will live for as long as God chooses to keep me. The day He takes me, I will go. I am going mad Sarpanch Ravindra Choudhary, who is related to the family, says Nikhil, who worked on the familys five-acre land, where they grow cotton, had been trying for long to get his application approved for an electricity connection to draw water from their borewell. He would say, I am going mad. I dont understand how the crop will grow, Nima recalls. Then, in 2021, excess rain washed away their crops. When Nikhil was found hanging from a tree, it was just a month to go for his marriage. Villagers cut down the tree later. Tapaveen was meant to take a different course, having finished BA and enrolled for post-graduation. But, after Nikhils death, he started helping on the land too, studying on the side and preparing for competitive examinations. But then came 2024. It was a particularly bad year, the family recalls, and their crop failed in the absence of rains. He too started saying, What should I do? My mind is not working, Nima says. One day while she and her husband were away in the field, Tapaveen hanged himself from a rope at their home. This year, they sowed three times, Nima says, putting in the seed, spending money on fertilizers. But there was no rain for nearly two months after that. The crop dried up. Her husband did not share his despair, Nima says, recalling how she slept before him that night. Sometime in the early hours, Dnyaneshwar went to the adjacent room and hanged himself. Nima discovered the body at about 5 am. Grampanchayat Adhikari of the village R R Dhage says farmers here are at the mercy of the weather. During the elder sons time, there was excess rain. During the younger sons, there was a drought. Its still the same. A familys pride Dnyaneshwar worked as a farm labourer on other peoples land for years before saving enough to buy the five acres he owned in 2018. It was all fallow land, Harish says. Dnyaneshwar made it cultivable almost single-handedly. For a few years, the family thought their troubles were behind them. But the battles with the rain-and to get electricity-just dragged on. The family says it first applied for an electricity connection in 2021, when the government came out with a scheme. The sarpanch says around 40 farmers in the village benefited, but not Dnyaneshwar. The Malekars tried again when the government came up with a solar-powered system in 2023. While Nima has written to the Tehsildar again now, Harish says solar is hardly the answer. Pointing out that the Malekar borewell is deep and requires a high-capacity pump to draw water, he says How can we run the pump on it? Solar starts dipping by around 4 pm when the sun starts going down. It does not work at night. The family also says that, without any subsidy from the government, the cost of installing a solar system is beyond their means. Sarpanch Ravindra admits only three people in the village have gone for solar. Promises and grants After all three deaths, Nima was visited by representatives from political parties. The BJP, the Congress, the Shiv Sena all came, says the sarpanch. But nothing was done. Recently, Nima was issued a certificate under the Niradhar Scheme and told she would receive Rs 1,500 a month. The payment is yet to start, family members say. A cheque of Rs 20,000 was also given by the tehsildar under the Rashtriya Kutumb Labh Yojana. Ralegaon Tehsildar Amit Bhoite says The scheme offers immediate financial support to bereaved BPL families who have lost their main bread winners. We have also sanctioned over Rs 1 lakh for her husband, under the aid for families in case of farmer suicides. The amount of Rs 1,500 has been sanctioned under the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Yojana. Bhoite adds that he is trying to rope in some NGOs to provide additional financial assistance to Nima. The only significant aid they ever received, the family says, was Rs 1 lakh after Nikhils death. It all went into paying their debts, Harish says. Nima still goes to the farm when she can, he adds. She just goes and sits. Her eyes looking into the distance, her face blank, Nima says The day after he Dnyaneshwar died, it rained. But, since then again, there has been no water.

articleTitle: ‘He’s a sweet killer’: Kumar Taurani reveals three most expensive albums had one name in common
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tips Music's most expensive albums yet -- Taal, Pardes, and Yaadein.
description: Tips Music’s Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani revealed that their most expensive album acquisitions were for Subhash Ghai’s films Pardes (1997), Taal (1999) and Yaadein (2001).
body_raw: Tips Music, co-founded by brothers Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani, went from a small music shop in 1975 to one of Indias biggest music labels by the 1980s. The two brothers, who have also entered film production, recently revealed their three most expensive acquisitions over the years. And all three albums have one name in common - veteran filmmaker Subhash Ghai. Tips Musics most expensive albums Talking about Tips Musics most expensive albums on the Game Changers podcast, Kumar shared, Back in the time, it was Yaadein, Taal, and probably Pardes. Pardes 1997, starring Shah Rukh Khan and Mahima Chaudhry, had music by Nadeem-Shravan and lyrics by Anand Bakshi. It included memorable songs like Kumar Sanus Do Dil Mil Rahe Hain, Sanu and Alka Yagniks Meri Mehbooba, Sonu Nigams Yeh Dil Deewana, and Kavitha Krishnamurthy and Hariharans I Love My India. Two years later came Taal, starring Aishwarya Rai, Akshaye Khanna, and Anil Kapoor. Composed by AR Rahman, the album boasts of evergreen tracks like Yagnik and Udit Narayans title track Taal Se Taal, Anuradha Sriram and Nigams Ishq Bina, Hariharans Nahin Saamne Tu, Asha Bhosles Kahin Aag Lage Lag Jaaye, and Sukhwinder Singh and Yagniks Ramta Jogi, among others. Besides Subhash Ghai, legendary lyricist Anand Bakshi is another common link between the three albums, having written the lyrics for Yaadein as well. The 2001 romantic drama, starring Hrithik Roshan and Kareena Kapoor, didnt work at the box office, but Anu Maliks compositions like Jab Dil Mile, Eli Re Eli, and the title track Yaadein Yaad Aati Hai stood the test of time. Films success and albums success go hand in hand Reflecting on Tips Musics long-standing association with Subhash Ghai, Kumar Taurani said their successful collaborations were rooted in mutual respect and continuity. Subhash Ghai would respect us a lot. We were happy with him. Hes a sweet killer. But Ive observed over the years that with whichever director or producer our kundali matches, those films work as well as their music. There should be continuity. And whenever that continuity has broken, those films havent worked. Responding to the observation that Yaadein didnt work at the box office, Kumar said, There can be exceptions in life, but generally speaking, the banners which continued to work with us succeeded. Our record is that 80 to 90 of films that we acquired got a good opening because of our promotional strategy. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark He then quoted the instance of late filmmaker Kuku Kohli, with whom they collaborated on three to four films, right from his directorial debut, 1991 action romance Phool Aur Kaante, which marked the debut of Ajay Devgn. But there was one film which we didnt like the look of, and he was also asking for a lot of money, that didnt work at the box office. There are a lot of films like that. I think there should be a taalmel between the label and the producer, added Kumar Taurani.

articleTitle: Who is Jay Clayton, a Trump loyalist tapped as new US AI czar?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jay Clayton
description: Clayton’s appointment as the new AI czar follows shortly after AI industry leaders met with Trump, and signed onto an agreement of voluntary safety standards.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump has reportedly chosen Jay Clayton, the countrys Director of National Intelligence, as the new artificial intelligence AI czar amid growing concerns about the risks of the rapidly evolving technology. In his role as AI czar, Clayton will primarily head up a new White House task force that will be called Super Intelligence Force. Super Intelligence or SI is the term Trump prefers to use over AI. The group will have 120 days to research and report on the risks and opportunities of AI, and offer recommendations on the US governments responsibilities regarding the new technology, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. Clayton succeeds venture capitalist David Sacks, who resigned from his position as AI and crypto czar in the Trump administration in March this year. Currently, the All-In podcast co-host serves as co-chair of the US Presidents Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, an advisory committee comprising outside experts on technology, scientific research, and innovation policy. Claytons appointment follows shortly after AI industry leaders met with Trump at the White House last week, and signed onto an agreement of voluntary safety standards that Trump said was morally binding. It comes in the backdrop of a critical moment for the AI industry as safety concerns have reached a fever pitch, driven by the spate of hacking incidents involving so-called rogue AI agents and doomsday warnings from AI researchers. While AI industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have called for federal guardrails on frontier AI models, Trump has so far opposed regulation. The president asked that a group be put together that was going to ensure exactly what he said, which is that we stay the leaders in superintelligence, and that the interests of the American people are put first, Clayton was quoted as saying by WSJ. Trump is yet to publicly announce Claytons appointment as the new AI czar of the US government. However, in a September post on Truth Social announcing plans to hire an AI czar, he said, We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows Only High I.Q. individuals need apply Who is Jay Clayton? Walter Jay Clayton grew up in Pennsylvania, and has degrees in engineering and law from the University of Pennsylvania, and a Masters in Economics from Kings College, London. He began his career as an attorney specialising in mergers and acquisitions transactions and capital offerings. Between 1992 to 2001, Clayton worked at the law firm Sullivan Cromwell and became a partner. During the 2008 financial crisis, he oversaw the sale of business assets of the doomed investment banking firm Bear Stearns to JPMorgan Chase in 2007, Barclays in acquiring Lehman Brothers assets following the latters bankruptcy, and Goldman Sachs in settling a 5 billion investment by Warren Buffetts Berkshire Hathway. In 2016, Claytons name was recommended for the post of the US Securities and Exchange Commission SEC chair by the legal firms then-senior chairman Joseph Shenker to Trumps son-in-law, Jared Kushner. The firm had a prior relationship with Kushner, having long represented his family business, according to a Reuters report. He chaired the countrys financial market regulator between 2017 and 2020. Clayton is also reportedly golfing buddies with Trump, and in 2020, he made his intent to be the next Attorney of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York SDNY known on a golfing trip with the US president. Following a confirmation by the US Senate, Clayton got the top job at SDNY and served in the role for a year. The Trump nominee made headlines at the time as the SDNY was a court that had long evaded the presidents interference. In July 2026, Clayton was confirmed by the US Senate as the new Director of National Intelligence, a role that involves overseeing 18 different US intelligence agencies.

articleTitle: 3 murders in 48 hours rock Punjab’s Ludhiana, among victim an ex-sarpanch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ludhiana sarpanch
description: Navtej Singh, a former sarpanch of Manewal village, was allegedly shot dead by two motorcycle-borne assailants near Ladhowal in Ludhiana while driving home late Saturday.
body_raw: At least three men, including a former village sarpanch, were murdered in Punjabs Ludhiana district in a span of about 48 hours, with two of the victims shot dead and the third allegedly hacked to death with sharp-edged weapons, police on Sunday said. The latest incident took place in Lodhowal area where two unidentified motorcycle-borne men shot dead Navtej Singh alias Neetu, a former sarpanch of Manewal village, on Saturday evening. Police suspect a family land dispute was behind the killing and have booked seven people, including relatives of the deceased. Navtej, in his sixties, was travelling alone in his SUV from Manewal to his residence in Krishna Nagar when the assailants intercepted him near the Punjab Agro farm around 7 pm and opened fire. He was taken to Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. Police sources said at least six rounds were fired at the spot, though it was yet to be established how many bullets struck Navtej. Prima facie, the deceased had a land dispute within the family, ACP West Jatinderpal Singh said. Seven people have been booked in a murder case registered at Ladhowal police station on the statement of Navtejs son, he said. Ladhowal SHO Inspector Sukhwinder Singh said some of those booked were relatives of Navtej with whom he had a dispute. A probe is on, he said. Navtej had served as sarpanch of Manewal during the SAD-BJP government and later extended political support to both the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party. A day earlier, 29-year-old Laddi Khan was shot dead in Mullanpur Dakha under Ludhiana Rural Police, with investigators suspecting an old rivalry between two groups. Laddi was travelling in a car with his friend Manpreet Singh when another vehicle intercepted them late Friday and its occupants allegedly opened fire. Laddi suffered at least three bullet injuries, including to his chest and shoulder, and died. The car went out of control after the firing and rammed into a roadside pole. Dakha SHO Inspector Nirmaljit Singh said two of the accused had been identified as Harpreet Happy and Arshdeep Singh, both residents of Majri. Three unidentified persons have also been booked. Both sides have criminal backgrounds. The deceased was a driver and had a previous FIR registered against him. We are trying to arrest the accused, the SHO said. The third murder was reported in Sahnewal, where 35-year-old Dinesh Kumar of Anant Vihar Colony was allegedly stabbed repeatedly with a knife and other sharp-edged weapons late Thursday night. Dinesh had stepped out to go to the market around 11 pm when he was attacked near an ATM kiosk in Purana Bazaar. His brother Deepak Kumar told police that the assault was so severe that Dineshs intestines protruded. He was declared dead after being taken to a hospital. Police booked Umesh Kumar, Sanjeet Kumar and Golu for murder on the complaint of Dineshs brother. Sahnewal SHO Inspector Guljinderpal Singh said both the deceased and accused had criminal backgrounds. The SHO said the two sides were allegedly involved in drug use and snatching and robbery cases. One suspect has been detained, he said.

articleTitle: Shubman Gill admits India don’t have time to ‘experiment’ ahead of World Cup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India captain Shubman Gill of India during the 3rd ODI match against the West Indies (BCCI Photo)
description: India beat the West Indies in a three-match series that ended on Saturday. However, the series ended with them suffering their first ODI defeat to the West Indies at home since December 2019.
body_raw: India captain Shubman Gill has admitted that the side now dont have too much time to experiment going into the 2027 World Cup and wants to field the team that is likely to play in the tournament the next time a series comes around. India beat the West Indies in a three-match series that ended on Saturday. However, the series ended with them suffering their first ODI defeat to the West Indies at home since December 2019. I honestly think there is not that much time to experiment, the combination that we want to play, hopefully, we get all the players that are available from the next series, and the combination that we would like to play in the World Cup, we want to start playing with that combination, Gill said in the press conference after the third ODI which India lost by five wickets. India were missing their pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, who was part of the team that won gold at the 2026 Asian Games, with the cricket tournament coinciding with the series against the West Indies. Apart from this, India were missing the injured Hardik Pandya. Gill said that the absence of players due to multiple factors was frustrating. I would say its been unfortunate, you know, with the injuries and with the scheduling with the other matches being around, its been a little bit unfortunate that we have been not able to play the bowling lineup that we would like to, he said. But Gill said it also gives an opportunity to the new set of bowlers to showcase their skills. I think its a good chance for the other players, you know, the players who might have not been in the team had the full-strength bowling lineup been there, so its a great chance for them to showcase their skills, he said. Gill also felt that India dropping catches affected their momentum, particularly in the third ODI, in which West Indies captain Shai Hope scored an unbeaten 162 and powered his teams record chase of a target of 352. I think we dropped around three or four catches today, and I dont think Shai Hope was dropped, still dropping three or four catches breaks the momentum of the team. Our fielding in the series has not been up to the mark. I think in the whole series, we dropped around seven catches if Im not wrong. And even in the field today, we gave away many runs, we were quite sloppy. And I think leading up to the World Cup, these are the areas where we definitely need to get better at, said Gill.

articleTitle: A for Alert, B for Bunker: How Maharashtra’s school kids are learning disaster ABCs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The chart was developed by Palghar District Disaster Management Officer Vivekanand Kadam to make disaster preparedness familiar to children through simple words, repetition and visual learning.
description: It began as an alphabet a disaster management officer made for his toddler. Now it's in government classrooms across Maharashtra, teaching children words like evacuation and tsunami warning.
body_raw: For children in several government schools in Maharashtra, the alphabet no longer stops at Apple, Ball and Cat. A colourful classroom chart begins with A for Alert, B for Bunker and C for Cyclone, and introduces terms such as evacuation, mitigation, search and rescue, and tsunami early warning systems. The chart was developed by Palghar District Disaster Management Officer Vivekanand Kadam to make disaster preparedness familiar to children through simple words, repetition and visual learning. The idea took shape in 2024, when Kadam began thinking about the impact of climate change and disasters over the next two to three decades. He first made the alphabet for his toddler, Vedansh, and later expanded it into a school learning tool. It was formally launched on July 26, 2025, Kargil Vijay Diwas. Kadam, who studied disaster management as part of his policy and management education, said he consulted a United Nations climate dictionary while selecting the terms. What the alphabet teaches Each letter pairs a term with a short explanation. Some cover natural hazards F for Flood, L for Landslide, G for Glacier Melting and Z for Seismic Zone, which explains that regions differ in their vulnerability to earthquakes. E for Environmental Degradation links damage to forests, soil and water to higher disaster risk. Others introduce the people and systems that respond to emergencies N for National Disaster Response Force, O for Operation Centre, P for Public Address System, Q for Quick Response Team and V for Very High Frequency, the radio band used by emergency teams. U stands for United Nations Office, and W for World Meteorological Organization. The chart also covers the ideas behind preparedness, such as D for Disaster Management Cycle, H for Hazard, M for Mitigation and R for Risk Reduction. K for Know Your Strengths asks children to understand their abilities and limits so they can act safely and seek help. Some letters are more specific. I is for Isolation Ward, J for Jumping Net, a safety net used in rescues from heights, X for Xylene, which introduces chemical hazards, and Y for Yachting Accident, on water safety while boating. The alphabet is not part of the formal syllabus. It is used as a supplementary resource, with teachers explaining the terms in Marathi. Other districts have taken it up. Parbhani District Disaster Management Officer Pawan Khandke said the charts had been distributed in 50 Zilla Parishad primary schools. Children are given homework and assignments based on the alphabet, and those who do well are recognised, he said.

articleTitle: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta lays foundation of waste processing, biogas plant; inspects Okhla landfill
articleFeaturedImageAlt: waste plant
description: Delhi generates around 13,500 tonnes of municipal waste every day, while MCD currently processes around 60 per cent of the waste generated in the city.
body_raw: In a move aimed at increasing Delhis capacity to process fresh waste, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi MCD is setting up three new waste-processing plants at Okhla, Singhola and Ghazipur, along with a 300-TPD tonnes per day biogas plant at Ghazipur. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday laid the foundation stones for the three plants and the biogas facility, virtually from the Okhla landfill site and carried out a site inspection as well. Delhi generates around 13,500 tonnes of municipal waste every day, while MCD currently processes around 60 per cent of the waste generated in the city. The three new plants will add 2,900 TPD of fresh-waste processing capacity, helping bridge the gap between the waste generated and the quantity being scientifically processed. The Okhla plant will have a capacity of 1,400 TPD, while the Singhola and Ghazipur plants will process 800 TPD and 700 TPD, respectively. The civic bodys survey identified approximately 125,000 cattle across Delhi, which generate roughly 1,500 tons of dung daily. MCD was directed by central and state authorities to intercept this waste and prevent it from entering city drains and polluting the Yamuna. A 300-TPD biogas plant for biodegradable waste is being set up at Ghazipur to prevent this waste from entering and polluting Yamuna. The projects are aimed at strengthening Delhis fresh-waste processing infrastructure and preventing waste generated each day from adding to the burden of the existing landfills. The civic body is also constructing two more decentralised fresh-waste processing plants with a combined capacity of nearly 3,000 TPD, which will be operational in the coming year, officials said. Biogas plants at Goyla and Ghoga are set to be operational in the next two months, they added. Meanwhile, Gupta, during her inspection of Okhla landfill site on Saturday, reviewed the status of waste disposal, land reclaimed and the capacity of the new processing facilities. She directed officials to make the new units operational at the earliest and at their full capacity. The expansion of fresh-waste processing capacity comes alongside efforts to clear legacy waste from Delhis three landfill sites. According to government figures, 217.17 lakh metric tonnes of waste have been disposed of from Okhla, Bhalswa and Ghazipur over the past 18 months, freeing nearly 100 acres of land.MCD officials said the Okhla and Bhalswa landfill sites are expected to be cleared within three months, while the target for clearing Ghazipur is December 2027. Gupta said clearing the existing landfills would not be sufficient and that the system for processing fresh waste generated every day needed to be strengthened to prevent new garbage mountains from forming.

articleTitle: ‘One last fight left in me’: Smit Machchhar recounts Flydubai cockpit horror
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News Live Updates:
description: Recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, Indian pilot Smit Machchhar told Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu how he fought through blurred vision to open the cockpit door, allowing the crew to intervene.
body_raw: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who survived a violent assault by his Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, inside a Flydubai cockpit and averted a catastrophic crash on September 30, revealed harrowing details of the incident during a phone conversation with Israels Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday night. Recovering at a hospital in Abu Dhabi, Machchhar recounted how he fought through blurred vision and severe disorientation to unlock the cockpit door from the inside, allowing crew members to intervene. Omani pilot asks to pray It just was a normal flight, and the co-pilot wanted to pray, which a lot of locals do pray, and which is not out of the ordinary. But while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back. Attack from behind And suddenly, after I think I would say about 4-5 minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft, and something is not right. But then after that, the blows kept coming one after the other, and thats when I realised that its not the aircraft its the other guy who was in the cockpit with me, Machchhar said. I did try to stop him, but because of his initial blows, my vision was almost like nothing, and I was completely blurred out, and at that point, the next thought I had was that the aircraft was sharply going down. So my memory is still in bits and pieces right now, but this is what I remember from that time. Machchhar tried to open the door And I did try to I did try and manage to open the door once, but I think he shut it back. And at this point, I remember I was lying down on the cockpit floor, and I felt the aircraft and the whooshing sound and people screaming. And as I was telling the ambassador here that I had that one last fight left in me. That, you know, call it personal or call it for people. But lets say I did it. That if I dont do it, Im gonna die, he said. And thats when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had, and just went for the door and opened the door. And thankfully, people were waiting to pounce back and take over the control, and the rest is what you know, sir, he told Netanyahu. Omani pilot resisted The door from the inside has a twist-to-open mechanism, and from the outside it cannot. It can only be opened with a code. So my colleagues from outside were trying to.. but the guy was not allowing.. Machchhar finally opens the door And the only way to open the door was to reach the knob, and like any other knob, just to twist it open, and it opens on its own. So there is no pin, but yes, the door. It was a short, quick twist, but the point was to reach that place, and once I had my hand on the knob, I guess I twisted it, and I opened it. Flydubai attack Flight FZ1073 left Dubai for Tel Aviv on September 30 with 174 people on board, most of them Israelis. Midway through the flight, the Boeing 737 Max dropped sharply after co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked the captain. Passengers and other crew took back control of the cockpit, and the plane landed in Tabuk, in northwest Saudi Arabia. Authorities in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel are now investigating. Netanyahu has invited Machchhar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Israel for the countrys Independence Day, and called the pilot a hero of Israel, India and the world. He also said the co-pilot went through Islamist radical indoctrination. The UAE is looking into the facts, the motive and whether the attack was planned or linked to terrorism.

articleTitle: Tom Cruise’s Digger gets crushed by Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3, grosses Rs 1.30 crore in India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Digger box office collection day 2: Tom Cruise's lowest opening in 19 years.
description: Digger box office collection day 2: Alejandro Inarritu's satire is likely to be Tom Cruise's lowest opening weekend in North America since his 2007 war drama Lions for Lambs.
body_raw: Digger box office collection day 2Alejandro Inarritus satire Digger, starring an unrecognisable Tom Cruise as a greedy oil tycoon, has failed to meet expectations at the box office, both in North America and at the Indian box office. Even though it was quite a swing for the A-lister, the film has managed to open at only a minor fraction of the final instalment of his blockbuster spy thriller franchise Mission Impossible from last year. Digger domestic box office collection Digger opened in North America this past Friday at just 3.3 million, including paid preview shows from Thursday, from 3300 screens. Given its current momentum, its likely to score only 8 million during its opening weekend domestically. That figure is far below the range predicted by production house Warner Bros - 12 million to 15 million. This makes Digger Tom Cruises lowest North America opening weekend in 19 years, the last one being Robert Redfords 2007 war drama Lions for Lambs, as per The Hollywood Reporter. That movie, also starring Redford and Meryl Streep, opened at 6.7 million, and went on to earn 64.8 million during its lifetime. However, the budget of that film was far less, at 35 million. On the other hand, Digger has been made and mounted on a massive budget of 125 million. Compared to that, Cruises last release from 2025 - Christopher McQuarries Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning - was made on a budget of 300 million to 400 million, but it opened at 64 million, and went on to amass 599 million during its lifetime. The reasons behind Tom Cruise registering his lowest opening weekend in almost two decades could be attributed to the polarizing reviews of Digger, as well as Cruise trading his action superstar persona for the role of a potbellied, 65-year-old oil tycoon. The actor will now return to his familiar turf - the second instalment of his popular action franchise, Days of Thunder, slated to release in cinemas in 2028. In fact, Michael Showalters erotic psychological thriller Verity, starring Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson, is estimated to emerge as the highest grossing Hollywood film at the North America box office this weekend. It opened at 15.1 million on Friday including Thursday previews, and is likely to score an opening weekend of 33.6 million from 3510 screens, more than four times than that of Digger. Digger India box office collection Even in India, Digger has managed to open at only a small fraction of Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning. On its first Saturday day 2, the film earned only Rs 45 lakh from 468 screens, an over 30 drop from its opening day collection of Rs 65 lakh from 579 screens. After two days, the Tom Cruise-starrer has managed to earn only Rs 1.30 crore gross and Rs 1.10 crore net at the India box office, as per Sacnilk. This figure pales in comparison to Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning, which earned Rs 33.50 crore from over 9,000 screens within its first two days at the India box office last year. The low box office opening of Digger at the India box office could also be owing to a major clash with an Indian tentpole release, Abhishek Pathaks crime thriller Drishyam 3. The Ajay Devgn-starrer amassed over 115 crore from over 16,000 screens in the first two days of its domestic box office run. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark Digger revolves around the misadventures of a third-generation American oil tycoon, which set off an impending calamity in Europe. That pushes the dictatorial US President and the White House, whove been in bed with the titular character of Digger Rockwell, towards damage control. The movie also stars Riz Ahmed, Sandra Huller, John Goodman, and Jesse Plemons among others.

articleTitle: Why the Thackerays are marching without party flags against Gyanesh Kumar’s ECI in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shiv Sena (UBT) and MNS workers stage a joint protest near CSMT in Mumbai, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. (Express photos by Akash Patil)
description: Uddhav and Raj Thackeray's joint march carries only the tricolour, borrowing from the Cockroach Janta Party's playbook. For Uddhav, the fight with the Election Commission goes back to losing his party's name and symbol.
body_raw: As the Shiv Sena UBT and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena MNS took to the streets against the Election Commission of India ECI on Sunday, their demand was loud and clear Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar should resign. An autonomous institution like the ECI, they say, cannot become a convenient weapon for the ruling BJP. The joint rally, led by cousins Uddhav and Raj Thackeray, started from Richardson Cruddas in Byculla on Sunday morning and headed to the BMC headquarters at CSMT. Neither partys flag or symbol is on display. Both leaders asked their cadres to carry only the tricolour. It is a break from past protests. By setting aside their flags, the two regional parties are trying to reach beyond ideological lines and make the agitation more inclusive, built around one agenda the ECI. The Commission is under fire over its Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, which began in Bihar in June 2025 and has struck more than 13 crore names off the draft rolls of 30 states and Union Territories, with crores of voters served notices and asked to produce documents to stay on the list. In Maharashtra, the August 31 draft left out 2.07 crore electors whose enumeration forms were not collected, and a further 1.22 crore have been served notices. The Opposition, led by the Congress, has called it vote theft. The questions are not only from outside. An investigation by The Indian Express last month found that two of the Commissions three members, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had objected on record at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken in the Commissions name without their knowledge, on the form new voters fill, on the software that holds every roll, and on lakhs of appeals filed against restored voters in West Bengal. Their most serious notes were copied to CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The Commission first called the notes suggestions, then, within days, met and issued nine decisions that read like them, and last week ordered a special drive in 20 states to bring back voters left out of the rolls. No individual flags. Only tricolor. The agenda is only ECI and its working. Therefore, anybody including BJP can come and join the rally on the issue, Raj said. In some ways, it is the model used by the Cockroach Janta Party CJP, a satirical youth movement launched online in May by political communications strategist Abhijit Dipke. Dipke had urged people to bring only tricolours to the CJPs protest at Shivaji Park on Friday, and Uddhav had extended his partys support to it. More the merrier seems to be the oppositions approach. Everybody is trying to raise the issue in their own way. But the agenda is one, Uddhav said. The NCP SP has also pledged support. We are supporting Shiv Sena UBTMNS joint rally, said its working president Supriya Sule. A grievance that goes back to the split For Uddhav, the fight with the ECI is personal. In June 2022, a revolt led by Eknath Shinde split the party founded by his father, Bal Thackeray. In February 2023, the ECI awarded the Shiv Sena name and its bow-and-arrow symbol to the Shinde faction. Uddhav strongly questioned the ECIs role, and the anger and hurt over losing the name and the symbol his father conceptualised have stayed with him. ECI has been one topic on which all national and regional parties have been raising questions. Our reasons may vary. The Shiv Sena split was a body blow for Uddhav Thackeray even before SIR mismanagement. The ECI awarding the original title and symbol to rebel deputy CM Eknath Shinde faction was a devastating development. We overcame that and contested 2024 elections on the new symbol mashal, a Shiv Sena UBT insider said. While the Congress and the CJP have targeted the ECI over alleged vote theft and mass deletions from electoral rolls, the Sena UBT feels the ECI let it down during the split. That, sources said, has made the Thackerays more determined to take the fight to the streets. With Lok Sabha and Assembly elections not due till 2029, the electoral impact of the agitation is hard to judge. For now, the two regional parties, trying to consolidate, see little to gain from asserting their individual identities. The fight against the ECI gives them a reason to speak in one voice, set aside differences within the Maha Vikas Aghadi, and take their concerns to as many people as possible.

articleTitle: Farmers’ Column: BBA grad turns 2 failed wheat sowings into Rs 1 crore from vegetables
articleFeaturedImageAlt: vegetables
description: For Baldhir Singh Bhullar, 5 acres under protected cultivation generate revenue nearly as much as 60 acres of wheat-paddy
body_raw: For Baldhir Singh Bhullar, a 35-year-old BBA graduate and a farmer by choice, two failed wheat sowings in a single season in 2021 became a turning point towards diversification - shifting him to vegetables in open fields and protected cultivation. Now, 13 acres under vegetables generate more than Rs 1 crore annually, compared to about Rs 75 lakh he used to get from 60 acres under wheat and paddy. A resident of Basti Nanaksar in Faridkot district, Bhullar had sown wheat on 25 acres in 2021 using a Crop Residue Management machine for the first time without burning stubble. The crop on 20 acres was attacked by a stem borer, forcing him to uproot it. He sowed wheat again, but within three days, heavy rain damaged the freshly sown crop. After we faced heavy losses, my father wanted to lease out the land, but I had a different plan, Bhullar said. He planted tomatoes on 13 of the 20 acres where the wheat crop was destroyed. That year, tomato prices were high enough for him not only to recover the losses, but also to earn nearly four times more than he could have earned from wheat production in that area. That was the year I decided to move towards vegetables, he said. He initially grew seasonal vegetables on a couple of acres. Within five years, he expanded open-field vegetable cultivation to eight acres. In 2023, he added five acres under protected cultivation - one acre in a polyhouse and four acres in net houses - to grow vegetables under controlled conditions, taking the total area under vegetables to 13 acres. Bhullars joint family, including his first cousins, own about 75 acres in Faridkot district. Of this, around 60 acres are used for Punjab Agricultural University-recommended short-duration paddy varieties during kharif and wheat during rabi. In the open fields, he grows cabbage, cauliflower, tomato, chilli and other seasonal vegetables. Under protected cultivation, he grows green, yellow and red capsicum, seedless cucumber and Japanese melon. Capsicum, a year-round crop, occupies about one acre. Seedless cucumber is grown on 3.5 acres in two cycles - February to April, with harvesting beginning around 35 days after planting and continuing until July, and August to December. Japanese melon is grown on about three kanals in two cycles - from spring to summer and again from August to early December. Bhullar said protected cultivation gives him greater control over temperature, humidity, irrigation and pests. He uses drip irrigation and fertigation, while biological pest-control methods have reduced his dependence on pesticides. I am dreaming of increasing polyhouse and net-house farming to 15 acres, he said. The economics have encouraged Bhullar to expand. Vegetables under protected cultivation can generate Rs 15-20 lakh per acre annually, while open-field vegetables earn around Rs 5-6 lakh per acre from two crops a year, with a net margin of about 50 per cent after all expenses. From around 60 acres under wheat and paddy, we generate about Rs 75 lakh annually, with a profit of Rs 90,000 to Rs 1 lakh per acre. In comparison, five acres under protected cultivation generate Rs 74-75 lakh, while the remaining eight acres under open-field vegetables generate another Rs 40-45 lakh, depending on the crop and season, Bhullar said. The returns vary by crop. Capsicum yields 250-300 quintals an acre, worth Rs 15-16 lakh at an average Rs 50-55 per kg cucumber yields 500-600 quintals in the summer cycle, worth about Rs 9 lakh per acre at Rs 15-18 per kg, and 180-250 quintals in winter, worth around Rs 7 lakh per acre at Rs 28-32 per kg. Japanese melon yields 40-60 quintals from three kanals, worth Rs 4-5 lakh annually. After all expenses, vegetables provide an overall 50-55 per cent profit margin. Even when prices fall, returns remain higher than wheat and paddy, he said. The initial investment in protected cultivation, however, is substantial a polyhouse costs around Rs 40 lakh per acre and a net house about Rs 28.4 lakh, with 50 per cent subsidy support available under government schemes. But the investment is worth it. With proper management, one can recover the entire cost within the first two seasons, Bhullar said. Bhullar employs around 25-30 people for about 10.5 months a year. His efforts towards crop diversification, water conservation and not burning paddy stubble recently earned him the Pravasi Bharatiya Award from Punjab Agricultural University PAU.
