articleTitle: ‘I thought I was going to die’: Flydubai flight FZ1073 pilot Smit Machchhar tells Netanyahu what he did next
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai pilot attack:
description: In a call with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar says he thought he was going to die, then opened the cockpit door a second time and let passengers in.
body_raw: When Smit Machchhar lay on the floor of his cockpit on September 30, hurt, unable to see well and with the plane dropping, he had one task left get to the door. In a video call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday, the Indian captain of Flydubai flight FZ1073 said he thought he was going to die and used what strength he had to open it. The Boeing 737 Max was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 people on board, most of them Israelis. Machchhar, who has flown for 17 years, says he opened the door twice. The first time, the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, shut it and he fell to the floor. The second time, people were waiting outside. They came in, overpowered al-Hammami and helped bring the cockpit back under control. The plane landed in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia. VIDEO Jerusalem Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu invites PM Modi and Indian pilot Smit Machchhar to light celebratory flame on Israels next independence day. Source Israel PMO X account Full video available on PTI Videos - httpst.conG6m5y1Stx- Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 What did he feel when the first blow came? Machchhar said the plane was flying normally when the co-pilot stood up to pray. He did not think it unusual and, out of respect, chose not to look behind him. After about four to five minutes, he felt a hard blow to the back of his head. It was so sudden that he thought the aircraft itself had been hit. When a second blow came, he understood the attack was from the person behind him. The co-pilots initial blows had completely blurred my vision, he told Netanyahu. He could feel the plane going sharply down. I thought I was going to die what made him try the door again? Machchhar said he reached the door and opened it once. Al-Hammami closed it, and he fell to the floor. He knew then that he had one more chance. I thought Im going to die, and thats when I pushed against everything, he said. When the door opened again, he saw people waiting outside. They rushed in, and the fight ended. VIDEO Jerusalem Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu calls Indian FlyDubai pilot Smit Machchhar a hero of the entire world. Source Israel PMO X account Full video available on PTI Videos - httpst.coLVJdyNq6ci- Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 In an earlier call, on 2 October, he told Prime Minister Narendra Modi that he was fighting for his own life, but was not going to let others die. He also said he recited the Hanuman Chalisa during the attack. How does the cockpit door work? Netanyahu asked about pulling the pin on the door. Machchhar said there is no pin. Inside the cockpit, the door opens with a twist of a knob. People outside need a code. His colleagues were trying the code, but al-Hammami was keeping the door shut. The hard part was reaching the knob. Once his hand was on it, one short, quick twist was enough. Hero of Israel, India and the world Netanyahu used those words for Machchhar and invited him and PM Modi to Israel for the countrys Independence Day. He also said the co-pilot had gone through Islamist radical indoctrination. Machchhar has been moved from Saudi Arabia to the UAE, where he is recovering. Authorities in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel are looking into the facts, the motive and whether the attack was planned or linked to terrorism.

articleTitle: Protest against Gyanesh Kumar: Journalists allege sexual harassment by cops; Crime Branch to probe claim
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police personnel detain a protester during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar near Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)
description: Officers said statements of the women were recorded on Sunday. CCTV footage from the protest site will be examined, they added.
body_raw: A day after three female journalists - who were covering protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter rolls, near Jantar Mantar - accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment, the Crime Branch has been tasked with investigating into the matter, officers said Sunday. Officers said statements of the women were recorded on Sunday. CCTV footage from the protest site will be examined, they added. The police, meanwhile, also requested people with video evidence, if any, to come forward. Deputy Commissioner of Police Neha Yadav said the protesters were informed about the implementation of Section 163 of the BNSS in the New Delhi area, under which public gatherings of five or more people, demonstrations and other activities without prior written permission are prohibited. She said police personnel on Saturday acted only after the protesters, who were directed to leave the spot, refused to do so. Later in the day Saturday, three women, who identified themselves as journalists, filed a complaint alleging manhandling by Delhi Police officials and staff during the detention. Their complaints were taken they underwent medical examinations and all the complaints were sent to the Crime Branch. I request all of you . that if you have any video footage related to this, please share it with the Crime Branch, she said. On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints and the same are transferred to Crime Branch for fair and impartial enquiry. PTINews ANI DPUpdates - Delhi Police DelhiPolice October 4, 2026 According to statement issued by the Delhi Police that was posted on X, On October 3, during the protest in the New Delhi area, while in a law-and-order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints, and the same have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a fair and impartial enquiry. Sources said the three female journalists run news portals and work as freelancers. On Saturday, over 150 people, including AISA president Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, were detained for allegedly attempting to return to Jantar Mantar after being held a day earlier while demanding the resignation of CEC Kumar. According to the complaint filed by one of the journalists, a copy of which is with The Indian Express, she had spotted Neha Bora and other female protesters being detained. She alleged there was no female police officer present. She alleged that when she pointed this out an officer pushed and shoved her. According to the complaint, when she confronted him, the officer fled the scene. Another journalist said she was covering the protest on Ashoka Road at 3 pm. I was recording the detention of Yogendra Yadav and Prashant Bhushan when I felt someone touching my back, she alleged in her complaint, adding that she turned to find an officer standing very close to her. According to the complaint, when she confronted him about the alleged inappropriate touching, he dismissed her claim. On Saturday evening, several freelance journalists and representatives of news portals had gathered outside the Parliament Street police station, demanding action against the officers involved in the alleged incidents of sexual assault. Around midnight, Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ratna Singh also reached the spot and demanded action against the officers. To press for their demands - the CECs resignation and the registration of an FIR over the alleged assault on female journalists - members of AISA and other activists had called for another protest on Sunday. Das said his party extended complete support and would stand by every journalist and protester. The FIR is a must, he said. On Sunday, the two CJP leaders reached the spot again. They were later joined by SFI leader Aishe Ghosh and CPIM leader Brinda Karat. Das was later allowed to meet the Station House Officer at Parliament Street Police Station and the complainants.

articleTitle: Kerala reopens probe against Gyanesh Kumar in 2006 graft case that saw Malaysian engineer’s suicide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Police denies permission for Jantar Mantar protest over SIR issue, tightens security
description: The chief project manager of the road project had left a purported suicide note naming Kumar, who was the secretary of the state PWD at the time
body_raw: The Kerala Home Department has ordered the reopening of a Vigilance probe into alleged corruption in a road-related work from 2006 - when Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar served as the secretary of the state Public Works Department PWD. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered a reinvestigation in the case, wherein a probe was launched against Kumar following the suicide of a Malaysian engineer, Lee See Been, who was then chief project manager of a major road work undertaken by PATI-BEL, an Indo-Malaysian venture, in the state. Kumars name had allegedly figured in two notes he purportedly left behind before dying by suicide in Kuala Lumpur. Kumar was sent to central deputation soon after. The road project, known as Kerala State Transport Project KSTP, was funded by the World Bank. Chennithala told the media on Sunday that he received a complaint alleging the 2006 Vigilance probe had been compromised under external pressure. I have directed the Vigilance to probe into the matter thoroughly. Gyanesh Kumars name had figured in the suicide note that the Malaysian engineer addressed to his wife and the company director. He said, Vigilance had examined the matter in 2006. However, the probe did not go ahead, although Kumar was transferred out of the PWD. Now, I have got a complaint from Congress leader Malayankeezhu Venugopal regarding the issue. I had discussed the matter with Chief Minister V D Satheesan and decided to order a comprehensive probe in this regard. The Indian Express reached out to the CEC and the EC spokesperson through email but did not receive a response. Senior CPIM leader M Vijayakumar, who had served as law minister in 2006 under the then V S Achuthanandan government, said Vigilance had begun probe into the matter, but no FIR was registered as the purported suicide notes were not made available in Kerala. Senior IUML leader M K Muneer, who was the state PWD minister from 2001 to 2006, said, It was being said that the engineer had left behind a suicide note. Nobody had seen it and what it contained. We do not know what he had written. Speaking to the media in Kozhikode, he said, A comprehensive probe is required into the entire issue. The then government led by the CPIM did not take the probe forward. I welcome it. Chennithala said that the 2006 probe was abandoned midway but Vigilance is capable of taking the probe ahead after two decades. When I get a complaint as the minister in charge of the Vigilance, I am duty-bound to order a probe, he said. PATI-BEL had undertaken the renovation of a few stretches of major roads in the state at a cost of Rs 216 crore. However, construction of the assigned roads got delayed due to alleged laxity in land acquisition from 2001 to 2006.

articleTitle: Why Mumbai police held back on ECI protests while Delhi cracked down
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police personnel detain a protester during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar near Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)
description: With the Thackerays and the Cockroach Janta Party on the streets, why has the Fadnavis government told police to hold back, and why does a senior minister concede the BJP stands alone on the ECI?
body_raw: As opposition parties and citizens groups take to Mumbais streets against the Election Commission of India ECI, the BJP-led Maharashtra government is working on two fronts keeping the police in check and taking on the oppositions narrative. The government has decided not to use police force to thwart protests, as was done at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also holds the home portfolio, knows law and order is his primary responsibility. Whether it was the Cockroach Janta Partys CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Friday or the Thackeray cousins rally on Sunday, the home department has decided against excessive force. Its directive to the police top brass is to ensure there is no untoward incident and that gatherings pass off peacefully. A senior BJP functionary, requesting anonymity, explained the difference between the partys approach in Mumbai and Delhi by recalling the September 2023 police lathicharge on Maratha quota protesters. Fadnavis, then deputy chief minister and home minister in Eknath Shindes government, had to apologise publicly. Fadnavis knows he cannot afford to make mistakes in Maharashtra, sources said. The contrast was voiced by CJP founder Abhijit Dipke at Shivaji Park on Friday. Praising the Mumbai police as the best force in the country, he said, Mumbai police is so cute. Fadnavis had earlier said, In democracy everybody has the right to voice their views. The police will take the decision based on situation. But he strongly rejected the oppositions and the CJPs charges against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as baseless. Countering the narrative With an aggressive opposition and a series of protests, the BJP has decided to counter the opposition politically, taking its arguments to people through meetings, public forums and media interactions. At a meeting this week, state BJP chief Ravindra Chavan shortlisted half a dozen leaders, including ministers, to speak to the media regularly. The strategy is to respond to every opposition criticism immediately, and collectively rather than individually. Minister Ashish Shelar has been asked to hold press conferences more often. Others on the list include Sanjay Kute, Pravin Darekar, Chitra Wagh, Devyani Farande, Niranjan Davkhare, Vikram Pachpute, Navnath Ban and minister Nitesh Rane. With 230 MLAs, the BJP-led government in Maharashtra is stable. But the party is worried about the anti-government sentiment surfacing through these protests. In this battle BJP is isolated. Entire opposition is against us questioning misuse of ECI. Our alliance partners Shiv Sena and NCP clearly have stayed away from the issue, a senior BJP minister said.

articleTitle: Market analyst claims Shah Rukh Khan’s Rs 12,500 crore net worth is 4x his contemporaries

Shah Rukh, Salman, Aamirs net worth From the data that I could last decipher, Salmans net worth is around Rs 3,000 crore to Rs 3,200 crore, said JS Khepar in a conversation with Siddharth Kannan, adding that Aamirs net worth is between Rs 1,900 to Rs 2,000 crore. Between both is Akshay Kumar, whose net worth lies between Rs 2,700 crore and Rs 2,800 crore, as per Jassi Tech. However, he dropped the biggest bomb when he revealed Shah Rukhs net worth. Hes the king I dont think his net worth is less than Rs 12,000 crore to Rs 12,500 crore. Thats why he the king, said Khepar on Siddharth Kannans podcast. Hes the badshah emperor in not only films, but also business. Look at KKR Wherever he has investments, theyre all zabardast outstanding, added the analyst. Shah Rukh Khans astronomical net worth includes his Indian Premier League cricket team Kolkata Knight Riders, his sea-facing palatial bungalow Mannat on Bandra Bandstand and a 4BHK sea-facing apartment in Shree Amrit Society on Carter Road in Mumbai, properties in London and Dubai, production house Red Chillies Entertainment, a VFX studio, and salaries from film projects and brand endorsements, among others. Aamir a test player, Akshay a T20 batsman JS Khepar also pointed out the differences between the investing and working styles of Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar, and Aamir Khan. Aamir is a test player, and Akshay is a T20 player. The approach is different in both the games. A T20 player is supposed to bat recklessly. A Test player is all about class. Aamir has that class. Whether his films work or not, he should remain Mr. Perfectionist, said Khepar. Hailing Akshay as a khiladi player even in the way he invests, the analyst said the actor has a presence everywhere. If there was a T5 format, he would have aced it too, he said, adding, And Salman is like a one-day cricketer. Kheper also lauded Akshays incredible fitness, which also allows him to pack in around four films within a year. JS Khepar also revealed that Salmans primary investment is in the real estate of Mumbai. Salman has a Midas touch. He turns mud to gold in real estate, and earns a lot of money there. One should learn that from him. The whole world loves him, including real estate. Theres only money and more money in Mumbais real estate. If not here, then where?, he added. Besides other properties on Carter Road and in Worli, Salmans net worth also boasts of a massive 150-acre farmhouse in the suburb of Panvel.

articleTitle: Concerns over women’s safety at Kolkata 5-star hotel after back-to-back arrests
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Man held for harassing woman at nightclub of 5-star hotel in Kolkata
description: The Kolkata police have arrested a 56-year-old Noida businessman for allegedly molesting two women from Nagaland in the lobby. Last week, the police had arrested a man for allegedly assaulting a woman at the hotel's nightclub.
body_raw: Safety concerns have surfaced at a luxury five-star hotel in Kolkata for the second time in a single week following the arrest of a 56-year-old man for allegedly molesting two women from Nagaland in the hotel lobby. The Kolkata police arrested Palash Ray, a businessman from Noida, after identifying and tracking him using CCTV footage. According to the Kolkata police, the incident took place between 12.30 am and 1 am Sunday, while the complainant and her companion were in the hotel lobby. The victims submitted a signed written complaint alleging that an unknown man touched them inappropriately, outraging their modesty. During the investigation, CCTV footage of the hotel lobby was thoroughly checked. The complainant duly identified the accused, and his movements were tracked down before he was apprehended from his room, a senior Kolkata police officer said, confirming that the investigation is ongoing. The police charged the accused with assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty. Second incident at same hotel The arrest marks the second serious criminal offence reported at the prominent luxury hotel within a week. In an earlier incident, the police arrested Mohammad Rafe Azim, 24, a resident of Beniapukur, for allegedly assaulting a 20-year-old woman and using obscene language inside the hotels nightclub around 2 am on September 27. In that case, the victim alleged that the accused and his associates blocked her path, physically assaulted her, and used abusive language before fleeing. That case was booked under charges of outraging modesty, insulting modesty of a woman, voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, and abetment. The police arrested him from Tiljala, and the probe is underway, Kunal Agarwal, Additional Commissioner of Police Crime, then said.

articleTitle: Two captive-bred great Indian bustards released in Rajasthan national park
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajasthan Minister of Forest, Environment, and Climate Change Sanjay Sharma was also present on the occasion. (Image: @byadavbjp/X)
description: Only about 150 birds of the critically endangered species remain in the wild.
body_raw: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Wildlife Institute of India WII scientists released two male great Indian bustards GIB in Rajasthans Desert National Park on Sunday morning, marking the first step in rewilding captive-bred GIBs raised at two conservation breeding centres at Ramdevra and Sam, Jaisalmer, under Project GIB. The project is being implemented for the long-term recovery of the critically endangered bird. Only about 150 GIBs remain in the wild. Rajasthan Minister of Forest, Environment, and Climate Change Sanjay Sharma was also present on the occasion. In a milestone move, released two male Great Indian Bustards in Sam, Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, today morning. This landmark success has been made possible by the nearly decade-long unwavering dedication of our scientists, researchers and ground staff who have spent years to ensure GIB reclaims the deserts of Rajasthan, Yadav wrote on X. The conservation breeding centres were established to raise a founder population of GIBs that could be rewilded, a measure against the declining wild population. From 2019 onwards, wild-collected eggs were incubated artificially, and chicks were hand-reared. Later, these hand-reared birds mated in captivity. At present, there are 98 such captive-bred birds in these facilities. Around 86 of them are being maintained for captive reproduction, and 11 have been earmarked for release into the wild. Of these 11, two birds were released into the wild at Desert National Park today. Captive reproduction has resulted in 24 live chicks in 2025 and 29 in 2026. Species recovery programme The release of captive-bred GIBs represents the next critical step in the species recovery programme and will provide important scientific learnings for progressively developing and refining protocols for reintroduction of captive-bred birds into their natural habitat, the environment ministry stated in a press release issued Saturday, after the initiation of the rewilding process. Yadav said Saturday that the GIB was important for grassland conservation, land degradation neutrality, and working as an important stopover for migratory birds that travel from the Central Asia flyway. The Central Asian flyway is a large migratory corridor stretching across 30 countries from North to South Asia, connecting the Arctic and Indian Oceans. Besides captive breeding, the project also includes habitat restoration by the Rajasthan forest department, including the establishment of around 200 square kilometres of fenced grassland enclosures inside the Desert National Park. Long-term telemetry studies by WII have identified these enclosures as prime breeding habitats for the species.

articleTitle: Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 review: Is this the ultimate Gen Z snapshot camera?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 Review
description: With simple controls, a playful design and a new self-timer, the Mini 13 puts the fun back into photography.
body_raw: Instant cameras have never really been about image quality, advanced controls, or getting the perfect shot. They are about taking a photo, hearing the motor whirr, and watching the image slowly roll out. The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 understands that better than most. At Rs 8,499, the Mini 13 does not reinvent the instant-camera experience. Most of it will feel familiar if you have used the Instax Mini 12, but Fujifilm has made a few small changes, including a mechanical self-timer, while keeping the camera simple enough for almost anyone to use. The result is an instant camera that prioritises the experience over technical precision. Design The Instax Mini 13 has a rounded, almost pillowy design that makes it clear this is not aimed at serious photographers. It is designed for parties, travel, casual snapshots and selfies, and the design fits that purpose well. It comes in five colours, Dreamy Purple, Frost Blue, Candy Pink, Lagoon Green, and Clay White. The metallic Instax logo adds a little polish, although the overall look remains playful. Despite accommodating instant film, the Mini 13 weighs around 306 grams and is reasonably comfortable to hold. It is still bulkier than a smartphone, but the rounded body makes it easy enough to carry around. The control layout remains familiar. There is a lens barrel at the front, a shutter button in the centre, a selfie mirror beside it and a flash above the lens. Twisting the lens barrel turns the camera on and extends the lens. The biggest new addition is the mechanical self-timer around the shutter button. A quick flick activates a two-second timer, while twisting and holding it for two seconds activates a 10-second countdown. An orange LED indicates the selected mode. The rear houses the viewfinder, film compartment, confirmation window and film counter. The bottom is completely flat, with no tripod mount, which limits how useful the 10-second timer can be for properly staged group photographs. Performance Getting started with the Mini 13 is straightforward. It runs on two AA batteries, so there is no charging cable or proprietary battery to worry about. Load a Fujifilm Instax Mini film pack into the rear compartment, check the film counter, and twist the lens barrel to switch the camera on. There is no menu system or manual setup to deal with. The camera handles exposure and flash automatically, with shutter speeds ranging from 12 to 1250 of a second depending on the lighting. For close-up photographs, twisting the lens ring activates Close-Up mode, which also brings in parallax correction to help with framing nearby subjects. After taking a picture, the print physically comes out from the front of the camera and takes roughly 90 seconds to develop. This remains a big part of the Instax experience. There is no app, editing interface or instant preview you simply take the photograph and wait for the physical print. The Mini 13 uses a 60mm f lens and Instax Mini film rated at ISO 800. The relatively sensitive film helps in indoor and lower-light environments, where the built-in flash also plays an important role. Image quality This is where expectations need to be realistic. The Mini 13 is not designed to compete with a smartphone or a dedicated camera, and its images have the soft, slightly retro character that has become synonymous with Instax. Photos are generally pleasing indoors, particularly at parties, bars and evening gatherings. The flash helps illuminate subjects in darker environments and gives the photographs a consistent look. Bright sunlight is less predictable. Since the flash fires with every photograph and there are no manual exposure controls, some images can look slightly overexposed. This lack of control can be limiting if you want to deliberately adjust the look of your photographs. For most users, however, the appeal is less about technical perfection and more about the character of the finished print. The occasional imperfect exposure is part of the experience, rather than something the Mini 13 is trying to eliminate. Verdict The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 costs Rs 8,499 and delivers a straightforward instant-camera experience without unnecessary complexity. The self-timer is a useful addition, the rounded design is comfortable to hold, and the automatic shooting system makes the camera particularly accessible to beginners. At the same time, the fixed flash, lack of a tripod mount, and basic imaging system mean it is best viewed as a fun snapshot camera rather than a serious photography tool. If you already own an Instax Mini 12, the changes are modest enough that there is little reason to rush into an upgrade. For someone buying their first instant camera, though, the Mini 13 captures what makes the format appealing simple operation, imperfect photographs and, most importantly, a physical print that you can hold in your hand. The Mini 13 is not trying to make instant photography technically better. It is trying to make it enjoyable and for the most part, it succeeds.

articleTitle: UPSC Ethics Simplified | Civic Virtue on Indian roads: What does it say about us?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Ethics Simplified | Civic Virtue on Indian roads: What does it say about us?
description: Roads are not merely physical infrastructure. They are also spaces where citizens practise, or fail to practise, values such as self-restraint, justice, responsibility and respect for others. Our ethicist, Nanditesh Nilay, explores what our conduct on the road tells us about civic virtue.
body_raw: UPSC Ethics Simplified, a special series under UPSC Essentials by The Indian Express, explores ethical concepts relevant to the Civil Services Examination. In todays article, we examine what our conduct on the road reveals about civic virtue and ask a larger question What happens when citizens fail to exercise self-restraint, responsibility and respect for others in public spaces? Our ethicist examines the issue through the lenses of civic virtue, good citizenship, self-restraint and moral duty. What happens when a person is involved in an accident on the road? If someone is hit, intentionally or unintentionally, an immediate ethical response should be to stop, check on the person and take responsibility for ones actions. The recent Gurugram case involving a woman biker raises questions about these basic civic responsibilities. The Indian Express reported that a woman biker was allegedly chased and rammed by a car on Golf Course Road. Video footage showed the car following the biker before colliding with her motorcycle. The police later added sections relating to attempt to murder, stalking and insulting the modesty of a woman to the FIR. The incident is therefore not only about road safety. It also provides an opportunity to examine a larger ethical question What do our everyday actions on public roads tell us about our civic virtues? What are civic virtues? A virtue is a set of traits, habits and qualities that enable individuals to fulfil their responsibilities effectively. Civic virtues are qualities that help individuals act as responsible members of a political community. They include concern for the common good, participation in public life, respect for institutions, opposition to corruption and responsibility towards fellow citizens. The importance and formation of civic virtues have been central questions in political philosophy from ancient times. Roads provide a simple but powerful setting in which these virtues are tested. Patience, self-restraint, respect, responsibility and concern for another persons safety are not abstract ethical concepts when we are behind the wheel. They directly influence the safety and dignity of other citizens. Aristotle Good person and good citizen Aristotle drew a subtle distinction between a good person and a good citizen. The virtues of a good person are universal or absolute in character, while the virtues of a good citizen are also related to the constitution and the responsibilities of living in a political community. Aristotle further connected the two through virtue of character. Qualities such as courage, temperance, justice and practical wisdom are cultivated through habituation in a well-ordered community and expressed through civic engagement. This idea of habituation is particularly relevant to civic life. Ethical conduct is not developed merely by knowing what is right. It is strengthened by repeatedly practising the right behaviour. For instance, stopping after an accident, helping an injured person, controlling anger during a traffic dispute or respecting another persons right of way may appear to be small acts. But repeated acts of self-restraint and responsibility help build civic character. Thus, the question is not merely whether a person knows the rules. It is whether the person has developed the character to follow them, especially when emotions run high. W.D. Ross Duties that guide moral action British moral philosopher W.D. Ross rejected the idea that all moral decisions can be reduced to one supreme principle. He proposed the idea of prima facie duties. These are genuine moral duties that normally carry weight, although in a particular situation one duty may have to take precedence over another. Ross identified duties such as fidelity, reparation, gratitude, justice, beneficence, self-improvement and non-maleficence. The idea is important because real-life ethical situations often involve competing considerations. Determining which duty should take precedence requires moral judgement and practical wisdom. It cannot always be reduced to a mechanical formula or an algorithm. Self-restraint and self-improvement Rosss idea of self-improvement also has a direct connection with civic virtue. Self-improvement is not limited to acquiring knowledge or professional skills. It includes cultivating ones virtues, character and capacity for self-control. A person must understand ones own intentions and limitations well enough to fulfil promises, avoid causing harm and prevent personal desires from overriding ones duties. This is where self-restraint becomes important. On a road, anger, impatience, ego or the desire to assert ones power can quickly affect another persons safety. A mature ethical response requires an individual to recognise these emotions and exercise control over them. The principle of non-maleficence, or the duty to avoid causing harm, becomes particularly relevant. If an action can seriously harm another citizen, the individuals responsibility cannot end with saying that the harm was unintended. Ethical conduct also requires us to consider the foreseeable consequences of our actions and our responsibility towards others. When civic virtue is missing The Gurugram incident brings these questions into sharp focus. The woman biker questioned why the driver did not stop to help her if the collision had been unintentional. The police investigation later examined video footage and escalated the charges. The ethical lesson goes beyond one individual or one incident. When self-restraint, justice, responsibility and concern for others are absent from civic conduct, public spaces can become places where power, aggression or privilege determine who feels safe. This is why civic virtue matters in both personal and professional life. A society cannot depend only on laws and punishment. Laws provide an external framework for behaviour, but civic virtues help create the internal willingness to act responsibly even when no one is watching. Development is more than roads and highways India often views roads, highways and other infrastructure as visible symbols of development. They are important indicators of economic progress and connectivity. But development cannot be measured only by the quality or length of our highways. A developed society also requires citizens who can share public spaces with discipline, empathy, responsibility and respect for others. If physical infrastructure advances while civic virtues remain weak, development remains incomplete. The road, therefore, becomes more than a means of transportation. It becomes a test of citizenship. The fundamental question is not only How good are our roads? It is also How good are we as citizens while using them? Compassion and civic life The Dalai Lamas emphasis on cultivating a compassionate mindset provides another dimension to this discussion. When our thoughts are dominated by excessive preoccupation with the self, emotions such as fear, anger, jealousy and mistrust can become stronger. Concern for the well-being of others, on the other hand, can make our minds clearer and our conduct more peaceful. This idea has relevance for civic life. A road is shared by strangers. We may never know the person driving beside us, walking across the road or riding a motorcycle ahead of us. Yet our actions can directly affect their safety. Civic virtue begins with recognising that the stranger on the road is also a citizen with equal dignity and rights. What should an ethics aspirant remember? The Gurugram case can be used to connect several concepts in UPSC Ethics GS Paper IV Civic virtue Responsibility towards the common good and fellow citizens. Self-restraint Controlling anger, ego and impulses. Non-maleficence Avoiding actions that cause harm to others. Justice Respecting the equal rights and dignity of other citizens. Self-improvement Cultivating ethical character and emotional control. Compassion Recognising and responding to the vulnerability of others. For a future civil servant, these values matter not only in extraordinary situations but also in everyday public life. Roads can testify to a countrys physical development. But the way citizens behave on those roads can testify to its civic character. Post-Read Questions 1. A good citizen is not merely one who obeys the law, but one who possesses civic virtues. Discuss with reference to Aristotle and contemporary public life. 2. How can self-restraint, non-maleficence and compassion contribute to safer and more ethical public spaces? The writer is the author of Being Good, Aaiye, Insaan Banaen, Kyon and Ethikos Stories Searching Happiness. He teaches courses on and offers training in ethics, values and behaviour. He has been the expertconsultant to SAARC countries, UPSC, Central Bureau of Investigation CBI,National Judicial Academy, ATI, RAKNPA, Haryana Institute of Public Administration, ISA MountAbu, National Centre for Good Governance,Competition Commission of India CCI, etc. He has PhD in two disciplines and has been a Doctoral Fellow in Gandhian Studies from ICSSR. His second PhD is from IIT Delhi on Ethical Decision Making among Indian Bureaucrats. He writes for the UPSC Ethics Simplified concepts and caselets weekly. articleTitle: 5 gadgets I recommended to help my friends build the perfect WFH setup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WFH gear
description: From the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i and Samsung Galaxy S26 FE to the Logitech MK250 keyboard, here are five gadgets to give your work-from-home setup a makeover.
body_raw: A month ago, two of my friends told me they were off to South Goa and Pabbar Valley. I assumed it was a short trip to recharge after their hectic work schedules. But then they told me they had recently switched to freelancing gigs with a US-based company and wanted to temporarily move away from the city, working remotely from offbeat locations instead. More and more people in my circle are either becoming independent contributors or choosing freelancing over full-time work. Maybe thats what the future of work looks like in the AI era. In fact, during a recent group video call, my friends, who are all writers and editors but arent tech nerds like me, asked about the essential tech they would need to set up a work-from-home WFH space and give their workspaces a makeover. As someone who travels frequently for work and occasionally works from home, I know what its like to work remotely. Based on my own experience of working from home on a regular basis, I have found that you need the right gear and other essentials to stay productive and comfortable. I recommended five gadgets, including essential peripherals, to my friends to help them set up their home offices-and tested them over several weeks. The list includes the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i, Samsung Galaxy S26 FE, Logitech MK250 keyboard and mouse combo, Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 earbuds, and Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W. Together, I feel these devices helped them build a mobile office that allows them to work productively from virtually anywhere Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i 15-inch, Intel Ultra 5 322 processor Rs 1,17,791 A computer is the bare minimum for setting up a mobile office at home, whether you are a developer, coder, or writer. Since my friends are writers, I recommended the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i, which I tested for several weeks. This is a mid-tier Windows laptop and has its share of flaws but my overall experience has been pretty impressive. Perhaps one of the most impressive things about the IdeaPad Slim 3i is its keyboard. I have spent the past week typing on it, including most of this review, and at no point have I felt that the keyboard was underwhelming. For writers, the keyboard is where their hands live, so it had to be good. The trackpad is good, although its missing haptic feedback. The chip is an Intel Core Ultra 5 322 processor, one of Intels newer processors. In everyday use, its plenty fast. Browsing, writing, email, SlackWhatsApp, video calls, light photo editing, dozens of browser tabs, a music app - all running together-were handled without complaint. The 16GB RAM is the one that most likely matter to most people, since companies these days are shipping laptops with 8GB RAM due to memory crisis. The 15.3-inch display isnt colour-graded for creative work, nor does it have an OLED panel, but its sharp, bright, and pleasant to use. To my surprise, the battery lasted 12 hours, which is enough to get through a full workday on a single charge with the brightness at a usable level and meaningful workloads running. Where I do have a few complaints about the IdeaPad Slim 3i is its build quality, which lacks a premium feel. The chassis isnt as refined as the MacBook Air, which is a letdown considering the notebooks asking price of over a lakh. At 1.5kg, the notebook is reasonably portable. It can easily be slipped into a backpack and carried while travelling. However, when it comes to design, it reminds me of notebooks from the pre-Covid era. The IdeaPad Slim 3i isnt a cheap laptop, and its asking price may seem high. But honestly, if you are in the market for a new laptop, almost every notebook can feel overpriced these days. I will leave the final decision to my readers. That being said, I do think the IdeaPad Slim 3i is a laptop for normal people. It delivers on the things that matter without making unnecessary compromises. For most people, the IdeaPad Slim 3i could be the answer. Samsung Galaxy S26 FERs 72,999 onwards When my friends asked me which smartphone they should buy, two options immediately came to mind. However, this time around, they wanted to stick to their budget while also looking for a phone that would last for several years and still have a premium feel. Its a shame about the recent price increase, but even at the new price, my top pick remains the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE for a reason. The S26 FE has the looks that matches the latest flagship S26 devices, meaning the phone has the same glass back and the triple-camera island on the back at the top left. I liked the design and build of the device. It has aluminum sides and an all- flat screen and a an IP68 rating that can survive a dunk in water. The phone has a 6.7-inch OLED display, which is impressive, and supports a smooth 120Hz refresh rate. I wish it came with an LTPO panel, as that would allow the refresh rate to automatically adjust from 1Hz to 120Hz, helping to conserve battery life. The peak brightness is also good, at around 1,900 nits. Inside, theres an Exynos 2500, Samsungs own processor, which I found to deliver better performance and efficiency than the S25 FEs Exynos 2400. For everyday tasks such as browsing, gaming, and photography, I found the performance to be reasonably good. The S26 FEs 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM may feel limiting for some users, especially those who take a lot of photos or play demanding games. Unfortunately, this is the only configuration available in India. I wish Samsung had offered a 12GB RAM variant, even at a higher price. At least then, consumers would have had the option to choose. The 4,900-mAh battery can easily last a day on a single charge. The phone supports 45-watt wired charging or 15-watt wireless charging. And while its is Qi2-compatible, there are no magnets for easy docking. Samsungs One UI 9 is clean, highly customisable, and comes with a number of AI features. I particularly liked Now Brief, which creates a personalised feed combining weather, health updates, videos, and calendar events throughout the day. The S26 FE retains the same camera setup as last year, with a 50MP main camera, 12MP ultrawide, 8MP telephoto, and 12MP selfie camera. Dont expect it to beat the S26 Ultra or iPhone 18 Pro Max- it simply isnt in the same league. However, I liked the picture quality I got in broad daylight, with plenty of detail, sharpness, and a good dynamic range. I also noticed improvements to the night mode, as well as the phones video-recording capabilities. The telephoto camera, which supports 3x optical zoom, is another useful addition, particularly for capturing subjects from a distance without sacrificing too much detail. The S26 FE is a really good phone if youre an Android user. Its not a flagship-grade device, but its a solid choice for the average user looking for a semi-premium smartphone. Keep an eye out for deals and discounts on the S26 FE in the coming days, and you may be able to get the device for even less. Logitech MK250 Rs 2195 One of my friends had been working from home for five years when he started experiencing neck pain. He was advised to raise his laptop to eye level and use a standalone keyboard and mouse. I have tried a variety of keyboards over the years, and a few days ago, the new Logitech MK250 caught my eye. This is a wireless keyboard and mouse combo that costs just Rs 2,195. The best part is that I dont have to worry about USB dongles anymore. Both the keyboard and mouse connect via Bluetooth, so neither device takes up a USB port. The MK250s Bluetooth connectivity is especially useful on modern laptops with limited ports. It keeps both USB-C ports free for charging and other accessories, while allowing me to easily switch the keyboard and mouse between a laptop, tablet, and desktop without having to search for or carry a USB receiver. The keyboard features a full-size layout with a dedicated number pad. If you work with spreadsheets or frequently enter numerical values, having a dedicated number pad makes data entry much faster. The keys are spacious and quiet to type on, making the keyboard suitable for both home-office and open-office environments. The mouse is ergonomically shaped to fit either hand. It uses optical tracking for smooth movement across various surfaces, including desks, tables, and mouse pads. It has three buttons, which should be enough for most people, while the scroll wheel provides smooth and precise scrolling without requiring you to click through every line. Both devices are battery-powered, but the battery life should be long enough that you will forget they even need batteries. Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 Rs 29,990 While finalising the list, I came across a pair of old-school headphones with a built-in microphone that I initially wanted to recommend to my friends. But after hearing about their typical day and their love for music, I thought the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 might be the perfect fit for them, which I also happen to test them for weeks. The Momentum True Wireless 5 are expensive pair of wireless earbuds, but they provide the best audio quality of any true wireless earbuds I have tried recently and a reasonably better noise cancellation. The Momentum 5s have a sleeker, more rounded design that makes them comfortable to wear for hours. They arent designed for intense workouts, but they are well suited to everyday activities such as walking. I tested the Copper colourway and liked its distinctive look, which stands out from Apples AirPods Pro and Sonys wireless earbuds. The earbuds have an IP54 rating for dust and water resistance, so they should be fine in most everyday conditions. The outer shell of the earbuds features capacitive touch controls that work extremely well. The controls can be customised for single, double, and triple taps, as well as tap-and-hold gestures. Where I think they really shine is in audio quality. They feature 7mm TrueResponse dynamic transducers. While the specifications may look similar to those of their predecessor, I found that software and processing improvements have helped improve the overall sound quality. In my testing, the Momentum 5s performed particularly well with pop and dance music. Madonnas Danceteria and Mikas Relax, Take It Easy sounded excellent, with well-balanced vocals. The bass is deep, while the highs are crisp and clear. The Sennheiser Smart Control Plus app offers basic EQ settings, which I found adequate but nothing exceptional. The earbuds also support aptX codecs and offer Hi-Res and Lossless audio modes for better sound quality. However, these settings can cause connection dropouts, especially in crowded or busy areas. They can last up to 40 hours on a single charge with the included charging case. The Momentum TW 5 also delivers improved noise cancellation, providing stronger noise isolation without relying as much on a tight seal. That being said, Apple and Bose are still ahead of Sennheiser when it comes to delivering superior noise cancellation. Overall, I felt the Momentum True Wireless 5 offer the best of both worlds, delivering impressive sound quality and effective noise cancellation. They are a premium pair of wireless earbuds that offer luxe features such as Dolby Atmos for a more immersive listening experience, as well as a replaceable battery that helps extend their lifespan. Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W Rs 5499 Once, I was working remotely from the hills, and I vividly remember it was dusk. There was no power, and the deadline for submitting my story was fast approaching. That day, what saved me was the portable laptop charger I had with me, something I never thought I would need it. Since then, I have always kept a long-lasting power bank with me, and I recommend one to my friends who work remotely or from home. The latest addition to my mobile workflow is the Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W, which was recently launched in India for Rs 5,499. I have it and been testing it for a week or so. With a boxy form factor, the power bank is technically pocketable, but I would recommend keeping it in a sling bag or backpack. The design is quite nice- it feels premium and solid, while the glass front with the built-in display adds to its appeal. The screen is operated using a button that is large, indented, and easy to find without looking. One press turns on the display, allowing you to scroll through battery information. The power bank comes with a compact USB-C cable capable of supporting charging speeds of up to 120W. The second USB-C port on the side can deliver up to 45W to another device. Performance from the Xiaomi 20,000mAh Power Bank has been solid. The 20,000mAh capacity is enough to charge two smartphones alongside a MacBook Air and AirPods and a smartwatch. The power bank supports up to 165W charging and a range of standards, including PD 3.0 with PPS and QC 2.0, 3.0, and 3.5. For me, though, the screen on the power bank is the real star of the show. Sure, it isnt necessary for a power bank, but its the easiest way I have seen to check how much battery remains or how long the power bank will take to recharge. Another good thing is that I can fly with the power bank, though it depends on the rules set by each airline.

articleTitle: NEET PG answer keys out, but candidates call it ‘eyewash’; here’s why
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NEET PG answer keys out, but candidates call it 'eyewash'; here is why
description: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences earlier said it would release the answer keys and candidates' response sheets to comply with a Supreme Court order ensuring transparency.
body_raw: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences NBEMS has released the answer keys for NEET PG 2026, the postgraduate medical entrance examination held on August 30 and September 5. Earlier this week, the NBEMS clarified that it issued candidates scorecards along with section-wise question IDs and their corresponding answer keys. Soon after the answer keys were released, candidates who had initially welcomed the move found themselves questioning the boards approach to disclosure. While the document included candidates responses alongside the questions and answers, the release of the answer keys, with only the question IDs and other limited details visible, left many questioning how far the move actually went in ensuring transparency. On social media, several candidates described the exercise as eyewash and merely a formality, arguing that making only the question IDs available did little to clarify the evaluation process and, in some cases, only added to the confusion. Also Read NEET PG 2026 cut-off falls to 6-year low Why does it change? The NBEMS had earlier announced through the NEET PG 2026 information bulletin that it would release the answer keys and candidates response sheets in compliance with the Supreme Courts April 29, 2025, order that directed the board to make raw scores, answer keys, and normalisation details publicly available to ensure transparency. Speaking to indianexpress.com, a 30-year-old aspirant from Jaipur and a former junior resident at Guru Nanak Eye Centre, New Delhi, said, I was hopeful that when the answer keys are out, if I am not able to make the cut-offs, I will still be able to understand where I lost marks. This would help in preparing for any subsequent rounds. What is visible in NEET PG 2026 answer keys? As announced by the NBEMS and as confirmed by candidates, upon accessing the answer keys in the candidate login, only these fields are shown - Section-wise question IDs in the sequence in which they appeared in the candidates question paper. - Status of each response, including whether the question was answered or not attempted. - Correct answer key ID 1234 for every question. - Response marked by the candidate against each question. - Score awarded for each question as per the examination scheme. Why are these details insufficient for candidates? The aspirant clarifies, In NEET PG, the order in which the questions and their options appear is not the same for all candidates. During the actual exam, the questions are shuffled within the section. Examination authorities often resort to jumbling the order of questions and answer options to protect the tests integrity and, to a large extent, restrict chances of malpractice. According to the aspirant, Since the sequence of questions within a section was shuffled, question IDs and their corresponding correct option ID appeared differently for candidates. We have no way of knowing or recalling which question ID is against what actual question, and what we have answered. Also Read NMC releases institute and course-wise seat matrix While the NBEMS has released the correct answer key ID, the information remains irrelevant for candidates because the explicit questions and their correct answers have not been disclosed. Without knowing the exact question and its corresponding correct answer, candidates cannot independently verify whether the answer has been marked correctly. Another candidate, a practising junior doctor at a hospital in Madhya Pradesh, told Indianexpress.com that other nationally organised public entrance and qualifying exams issue answer keys where the questions and their answers are visible to candidates. CUET UG and PG, NEET UG, JEE Mains and Advanced - all these exams issue answer keys. Why can we not expect the same rigour for NEET-PG? he said. Can candidates raise objections? Neither of the notices issued by the NBEMS on September 24 and October 1 mentions an objection window or any procedure for candidates to challenge the answers. In its circular issued on September 24, the board said, Each and every question asked in both the question papers of NEET PG 2026 was reviewed by faculty members from the concerned speciality area after the conduct of NEET-PG 2026 to recheck for technical correctness of the questions as well as answer keys. The board announced that none of the questions was found technically incorrect, further eliminating any provision for candidates to challenge the question paper. IMA official challenges answer key in Supreme Court Meanwhile, Dr Dhruv Chauhan, national spokesperson of the Indian Medical Associations Junior Doctors Network IMA-JDN and founder of the Legal Cell for All India Doctors, has moved the Supreme Court with a public interest litigation PIL challenging the NEET-PG 2026 answer keys. The petition seeks greater transparency in the evaluation process, demanding that the complete question paper be made available along with the corresponding answers and the options actually marked by candidates, rather than merely the serial numbers of the questions and responses. Dr Chauhan told indianexpress.com, The aspirants wanted only one thing, that is transparency in the exam. He added, Our legal team will pursue this in the larger benefit of the medical students, and have also called for a time-bound objection window to address any discrepancies. With the matter now before the Supreme Court, candidates await clarity on whether directions will be issued to make the complete question paper and answer details available, and whether that happens before counselling begins.

articleTitle: ‘Lacklustre, sleepy, sluggish…’: Brazilian media on 4-0 win over India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vinicius played in the first half of the match between India and Brazil. (Express Photo by Partha Paul)
description: Brazilian media didn't seem to be too impressed with the national team's 4-0 win over India at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.
body_raw: Brazil beat India 4-0 in the first-ever senior mens football friendly between the two sides at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata. While that scoreline normally points out to a thrashing, in this case, it was a respectable scoreline for India. Ranked 138th in the world, India have never even come close to qualifying for the World Cup since they qualified by default for the 1950 edition before withdrawing. Brazil, on the other hand, are famously the most succesfull team in the history of the competiton and ranked sixth in the world. This reality seems to have not escaped the Brazilian media either, in which a majority of the opinions expressed after the match seemed to be criticising the Selecao. UOL, an outlet owned by the Folha group which is among Brazils media conglomerates, said Once again failing to impress, the Brazilian national team thrashed the weak India team - ranked 138th in the FIFA rankings - 4-0 in a routine manner in Kolkata. Even against a weak opponent, the Brazilian team started the match in a sleepy, sluggish, and uninspired manner. Vini Jr. had plenty of space on the left, but couldnt take advantage of it and made mistakes in his playmaking. Translated from Portuguese. Terra news said that Brazil left a lot to be desired in their win over one of the weakest rivals the Canarinhos have ever faced. Leading daily O Globo says that the match looked like a training session and that Brazil lacked offensive impetus. Despite their superiority and the scoreline, the Brazilian team failed to translate their control of the match into offensive numbers, creating few chances throughout the game, said the report. Former Former Brazil midfielder Felipe Melo was critical of how they played in this game and the two friendlies they played in Australia before that. Brazil only managed to draw the first of the two matches 1-1, which was their first game after their stunning 2-1 defeat to Norway in the World Cup round of 16. They won the second match 4-2. Brazil has been taking steps backward. The first game against Australia was below what they showed in the World Cup, the second, even though they improved, was also below par. And this third game, despite four goals, was also below par. Im hopeful that Brazil will improve, but in practice, theyve regressed compared to their last World Cup game against Norway, said Melo on Sportv. Melo accepted the fact that the Brazilians may not be used to playing in the kind of humidity that they had to deal with in Kolkata. However, the former Inter Milan midfielder felt that the players didnt seem to have the right attitude. A guy can play badly, but he needs to have the right attitude. Martinelli came on and showed attitude, as did others. Samuel Lino had a bit more attitude and scored two goals. If he had more time, he would have scored more, Melo concluded. Trivela, the Brazilian football news outlet, questioned the sense behind the match for the Brazilian Football Confederation CBF, considering the empty seats that could be seen at the stadium. A lackluster 4-0 victory for the Brazilian team marked the friendly against India this Saturday. It will be a friendly match remembered for failing to achieve even the main objective of the Brazilian Football Confederation CBF, wrote Trivelas report Carlos Vinicius Amorim in the piece. The stadium not being very full raises questions about the CBFs choice. The friendly match in India is justifiable, something long awaited by the population, but only if it were affordable for fans. The report goes on to state that a number of regions in Brazil has not hosted the national teams matches for decades. Instead of playing twice in Australia and once in India with inaccessible tickets, they could serve the population of some of these states. Furthermore, the president of the CBF Brazilian Football Confederation, Samir Xaud, promised to get closer to the Brazilian people after the World Cup. For now, its just talk, the piece concluded.

articleTitle: GNWL vs RLWL vs PQWL vs TQWL: Which railway waitlist has the best chance of confirmation?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GNWL 20 vs RLWL 20 vs PQWL 20: Why the same number doesn't mean the same thing (Image generated using AI)
description: Railway Waitlist Explained: GNWL, RLWL, PQWL and TQWL are different railway waitlist categories. Know which waitlist generally has the best chance of confirmation and why the same WL number can have different outcomes.
body_raw: Two passengers can have the same waiting-list number on a railway ticket, but their chances of getting a confirmed berth may not be the same. The reason is the waitlist category - whether the ticket is under GNWL, RLWL, PQWL or TQWL. These codes represent different types of railway waiting lists and are linked to different quota arrangements. So, a GNWL 20 ticket cannot automatically be considered equal to an RLWL 20 or TQWL 20 ticket. So, which railway waitlist has the best chance of confirmation? Here is what GNWL, RLWL, PQWL and TQWL mean, how they differ and what passengers should know before relying on their waitlist number alone. GNWL vs RLWL vs PQWL vs TQWL Which waitlist has the best chance? The train ticket confirmation depends on several factors. Speaking to Indianexpress.com, a senior railway official said the actual movement of a waiting list depends on factors such as cancellations and the release of unutilised quota. Indian Railways reservation rules shows that these are not merely different names for the same waiting list. They represent different reservation quotas and different pools of accommodation. Consequently, their movement towards confirmation can also be very different, the official said. GNWL Usually the strongest position GNWL stands for General Waiting List and is associated with the general quota. Among the commonly seen waitlist categories, it generally offers the strongest position for confirmation.The official said that GNWL generally has an advantage because it draws from the main pool of accommodation and benefits from cancellations and release of certain unused quotas. Railway reservation material specifically states that RLWL and PQWL are confirmed after the General Waiting List, giving GNWL an important structural advantage over these smaller quota-based waiting lists, the official noted. The official, however, added that this does not mean GNWL 100 is automatically better than RLWL 2. The actual waiting-list number, train, class, journey sector, day of travel and expected cancellations still matter. But when comparable waiting-list numbers are being considered, GNWL is generally the more favourable category to hold, the official told Indianexpress.com. RLWL stands for Remote Location Waiting List When a passenger books a train from an important intermediate station rather than the originating station, the ticket may be placed under the RLWL quota. Indian Railways keeps a separate quota for certain remote or important stations on a route. The key difference is that RLWL has a smaller, separate pool of seats. Its confirmation therefore depends largely on cancellations or the availability of accommodation in that particular quota. Railway reservation rules also place RLWL behind the General Waiting List in the confirmation order. Railway reservation instructions make the hierarchy clearer RLWL is cleared after the General Waiting List. This explains why an apparently small RLWL number should not automatically be treated as equivalent to the same GNWL number, the official explained. PQWL stands for Pooled Quota Waiting List This quota is meant for passengers travelling between certain intermediate stations on a route. The available seats are shared among these station combinations.Because the number of seats in this pool is limited, PQWL may move more slowly than the General Waiting List. Its confirmation depends on cancellations and the availability of seats in the pooled quota. Railway reservation rules also place PQWL after the General Waiting List for confirmation. Thus, a passenger comparing two otherwise similar booking options should not assume that WL 10 means exactly the same thing under GNWL and PQWL, the official said. TQWL means Tatkal Quota Waiting List Tatkal Waitlist applies when the seats available under the Tatkal quota have already been booked and further Tatkal bookings are placed on the waiting list. It is a separate quota meant mainly for passengers making last-minute travel plans. This means TQWL follows a different confirmation pattern from the General Waiting List. The chances of a TQWL ticket getting confirmed depend on factors such as cancellations and the availability of berths under the Tatkal quota. For passengers, the practical lesson is straightforward TQWL should not be treated as having the same confirmation dynamics as GNWL merely because its numerical waiting-list position is smaller, the official added. Indian Railways waiting ticket confirmation prediction When asked about the actual confirmation percentages, the official said Indian Railways has previously informed Parliament that confirmation and cancellation trends vary depending on factors such as peak and lean travel periods, the type of train, journey details and passenger demand. A GNWL 25 on one train may therefore clear comfortably while GNWL 10 on another heavily booked service during a festival rush may remain uncertain. Other variables include the class of travel, day of the week, boarding and destination stations, cancellations by confirmed passengers, quota releases, additional coaches and the time remaining before departure, the official replied. The railway official also explained that GNWL generally has the strongest position for confirmation. RLWL and PQWL depend on smaller quota pools and are cleared after the General Waiting List, while TQWL follows the Tatkal quota and depends on available berths and cancellations. However, the waitlist number also matters.A GNWL 120 cannot automatically be described as safer than RLWL 2 simply because GNWL has higher priority. There is no mathematically valid comparison without looking at that trains historical and current booking pattern, the official said. Indian Railways waitlist prediction AI Indian Railways RailOne application provides an AI-based prediction of whether a wait-listed ticket is likely to be confirmed or not. According to the national transporter, the accuracy of its waitlist confirmation prediction has increased from 53 per cent earlier to 94 per cent now. The concept itself is not entirely new. Indian Railways introduced a machine-learning-based confirmation prediction facility years ago, using historical PNR data to identify booking and cancellation patterns. The prediction remains an estimate rather than a guarantee. Indian Railways own PNR enquiry system warns passengers that prediction is indicative and based on current and past trends, and that the actual status can differ, the official said.

articleTitle: ‘Organised and difficult’: Carlo Ancelotti on India after Brazil’s 4-0 victory
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vinicius Junior in action against India at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday. (Express photo by Partha Paul)
description: Brazil are currently the world’s 6th ranked team while India are languishing in 138th spot. Despite that, Brazil only opened the scoring in the 28th minute
body_raw: The Indian football teams friendly against five-time world champions Brazil ended with a 4-0 scoreline in favour of the visitors at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday, but Selecao boss Carlo Ancelotti praised the Indian team for being organised and making it difficult for them to score their opening goal. Brazil are currently the worlds 6th ranked team while India are languishing in 138th spot. Despite that, Brazil only opened the scoring in the 28th minute, through a goal from Estevao. Then, the floodgates opened. A goal from Pedro ensured the teams went to the half-time break with Brazil leading 2-0. Samuel Lino scored a second half brace to complete the rout. India played their part well. They tried to play their game they defended, they were organised, they tried to play counter-attack. I think that they played a good game. We had difficulty opening the score, but the moment we opened the score with Estevao, we had more opportunities to control the game better, Ancelotti said at the post-match press conference. We feel good. It was a good experience. I think it was a good game, entertaining, with good intensity, and India did their part. Talking about his own team, Ancelotti said I think we defended well. We could have defended better if we had a couple of chances in the counter-attack, but I think for us its important not to concede a goal. Obviously we have to improve some mechanisms in defence, but we had a new defence that never played together, so maybe not everything was perfect. Again, the message is that we are happy to be here. We tried to do our best we tried to show our best quality to all the people who love Brazil and love football, and I hope they enjoyed the night.

articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | India’s UNESCO Tentative List gets new sites: What you must know for UPSC Exam
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | India’s UNESCO Tentative List gets new sites: What you must know for UPSC Exam
description: What are the newly added sites? What is a Tentative List? How does a site get UNESCO World Heritage status? What is India’s latest addition to World Heritage List? Here's what you need to know. Also, go “Beyond the Nugget” to know about the World Heritage in Danger list.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on new heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List. Knowledge Nugget New heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List Subject Art and Culture Why in the news? Recently, five new sites and transnational proposals have been included in Indias UNESCO Tentative List and it increases Indias count to 78. In this context, it becomes essential to know about the newly added sites and understand what Tentative List of UNESCOs World Heritage Sites is all about. Key Takeaways 1. According to the World Heritage Conventions operational guidelines, a tentative list is an inventory of properties a country believes deserves to be a World Heritage Site. 2. After the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation UNESCO includes a property in the Tentative List, that country has to prepare a nomination document that will be considered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee. 3. In India, the Indian National Commission for Co-operation with UNESCO INCCU, and the Archaeological Survey of India ASI are the bodies which play a key role in this regard What are the new heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List? 4. The newly added sites include the Buddhist murals of Bagh Cave Paintings, Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley, the Gupta-era Udaigiri Caves, the tribal legacy of Ginnorgarh, and Sites of Satyagrah. 5. Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley It is unique cluster of early medieval temples built between the 8th and 11th centuries CE, representing an important phase in the evolution of regional Nagara-style temple architecture. 6. Udaigiri Caves It is a rock-cut sacred ensemble developed under Gupta patronage in the 4th and 5th centuries CE. The site includes 20 caves, sculptures and inscriptions, including the Varaha form of Vishnu in Cave 5 and Anantasayana Vishnu in Cave 13. 7. The Sites of Satyagraha It is a serial transnational proposal connecting India and South Africa. It includes nine properties across South Africa and India, including Sabarmati Ashram, Mani Bhavan Complex, Harijan Sevak Sangh Complex, Sevagram Ashram, Aga Khan Palace and Gandhi Smriti Residence in India, along with Pietermaritzburg Railway Station and Phoenix Settlement in South Africa. 8. Ginnorgarh Fort It was a major political and administrative centre of the Gond kingdom from the early 16th to early 18th century. The fort includes palace buildings, stepwells, reservoirs, wall paintings and an ingenious water management system. 9. Bagh Cave Paintings It is a group of nine rock-cut Buddhist caves, mainly in use from the 4th to 6th century CE. Their murals, particularly those in Cave 4, are significant examples of post-Ajanta Buddhist cave paintings. What is a UNESCO World Heritage Site? 10. UNESCO plays a vital role in safeguarding cultural and natural heritage across the globe. Its primary objective is to identify, protect, and preserve sites that hold outstanding value for humanity. 11. It is guided by the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, an international treaty adopted by UNESCO in 1972. As of 2024, 196 States Parties have ratified the World Heritage Convention. 12. The World Heritage Site is a location recognised for its outstanding universal value. This signifies cultural andor natural significance which is so exceptional as to transcend national boundaries and to be of common importance for present and future generations of all humanity. 13. The World Heritage Site falls into three categories cultural heritage, natural heritage, and mixed heritage cultural as well as natural. 14. Cultural heritage entails an Outstanding Universal Value from the point of view of history, art or science, and includes monuments, groups of buildings, and sites which are the combined work of nature and human agency. Examples include the Taj Mahal, the Statue of Liberty, and the Sydney Opera House. 15. The Sites under natural heritage are those having an Outstanding Universal Value from the point of view of science, conservation or natural beauty, such as the Sundarbans Natural Park or the Victoria Falls. 16. Notably, the concept of World Heritage is universally applicable. According to UNESCOs website, World Heritage sites belong to all the peoples of the world, irrespective of the territory on which they are located. What is Indias latest addition to the World Heritage List? 17. In the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee which was held in Busan South Korea, 25 new properties were inscribed in the World Heritage list, out of which 19 are cultural, 5 are natural, and 1 is mixed. 18. Sarnath has been inscribed on UNESCOs World Heritage List in the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee. 19. With the inscription on UNESCOs World Heritage List, Sarnath becomes Indias 45th and Uttar Pradeshs fourth World Heritage Site. Sarnath is the sacred land where Lord Buddha, after attaining enlightenment, delivered his first sermon to humanity and set in motion the Dharmachakra Pravartan. Counted among the holy pilgrimage sites of Buddhism, Sarnath is described in ancient Buddhist scriptures such as Rishipattan. 20. Notably, Sarnath was included in UNESCOs tentative list on July 3, 1998. Twenty-eight years on, it has been officially designated a World Heritage Site. Until now, the UPs three World Heritage Sites were the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri - all in the Agra region. BEYOND THE NUGGET What is the List of World Heritage in Danger? 1. The List of World Heritage in Danger is designed to inform the international community of conditions which threaten the very characteristics for which a property was inscribed on the World Heritage List, and to encourage corrective action. 2. Dangers can be ascertained, referring to specific and proven imminent threats, or potential, when a property is faced with threats which could have negative effects on its World Heritage values. 3. At its 43rd session Baku, 2019, the World Heritage Committee recalled that the inscription of a property on the List of World Heritage in Danger, aims to marshal international support to help the State Party effectively address the challenges faced by the property by engaging with the World Heritage Centre and the Advisory Bodies to develop a programme of corrective measures to achieve the Desired state of conservation for the property. 4. Armed conflict and war, earthquakes and other natural disasters, pollution, poaching, uncontrolled urbanization and unchecked tourist development pose major problems to World Heritage sites. 5. Some sites inscribed on the List of World Heritage in Danger are Bamiyan Valley in Afghanistan, the Historic Town of Zabid in Yemen, the Iranian city of Bam, etc. Post Read Question Consider the following statements regarding UNESCOs Tentative List of World Heritage Sites 1. It is an inventory of properties that a country considers to have potential Outstanding Universal Value. 2.Inclusion in the Tentative List automatically grants a property UNESCO World Heritage Site status. 3. Indias UNESCO Tentative List has total 78 sites. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 and 2 only b 2 and 3 only c 1 and 3 only d 1, 2 and 3 Answer Key c Sources whc.unesco.org, UPSC Issue at a Glance Indias UNESCO World Heritage Sites - criteria, categories, and recent additions, Sarnath joins UNESCO World Heritage List How it was rediscovered and other facts Click here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026.
