articleTitle: Why Odisha vs Chhattisgarh over Mahanadi row is back in spotlight
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mohan Charan Majhi
description: After Amit Shah-chaired meeting, Odisha CM Majhi says framework for resolution would be released “very soon”; BJD questions these talks, seeks clarity on water-sharing
body_raw: The Mahanadi water dispute between Odisha and Chhattisgarh is back in the spotlight, with the Odisha government signalling that the two BJP-ruled states are moving closer to an amicable solution, even as the Opposition BJD has called this bid an eyewash. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who attended a meeting chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi on Thursday along with Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai and Union Jal Shakti Minister C R Patil, said a framework for resolving the dispute would be released very soon. We are gradually moving closer to a resolution. Alongside the legal process, administrative and political resolution pathways have also been expanded. A path to a resolution will be found keeping the interests of both states in mind. This resolution will serve as a model dispute resolution mechanism for other states too, Majhi said. The BJP, which had favoured an amicable settlement while in Opposition in Odisha, has accelerated such efforts since coming to power in the state in June 2024, even as the dispute remains pending before the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal. The latest round of talks began in July-August 2025, with several meetings between officials of the two states, including at the level of the chief secretaries and water resources secretaries, to discuss technical aspects of the dispute. A meeting between the two CMs was also held in July under the chairmanship of the Union Jal Shakti Minister. At the meeting, the states agreed to share data and information on their respective water requirements with the Central Water Commission. It was provisionally decided in that meeting to find a path to a resolution within three months. Two months have passed in the meantime and there has been satisfactory progress, Majhi said. Sai also indicated that the two states were looking at a cooperative approach. It is our life-giving river, intrinsically linked to the daily lives, agriculture, and culture of the people of both Chhattisgarh and Odisha. Our collective effort is to strengthen irrigation systems in both states through improved water management and to open the doors for new projects, he posted on X. Lifeline of Odisha For Odisha, the Mahanadi is more than a water-sharing dispute. The river is central to irrigation, drinking water, flood management, hydropower and the states broader negotiations with Chhattisgarh and the Centre. At Thursdays meeting, Majhi stressed that the Mahanadi was the lifeline of Odisha and said the states demand was that it receive an adequate share of the rivers water. Issues including irrigation, flood control, hydropower generation, drinking water and environmental concerns were discussed, he added. The Mahanadi river originates near Pharsiya village in Chhattisgarhs Raipur district and flows for about 851 km before merging with the Bay of Bengal. Of this, around 357 km lies in Chhattisgarh and 494 km in Odisha. The river flows through several districts in Odisha, while its wider basin covers 14 districts in the state. The prospect of an early settlement of the Mahanadi dispute has political significance for the BJP, with panchayat and urban local body elections in Odisha scheduled for early next year. The BJP is seeking to contrast its approach with that of the Naveen Patnaik-led BJD, which governed Odisha when the dispute entered the legal process in 2016. Bargarh BJP MP Pradeep Purohit accused the previous BJD government of deliberately keeping the dispute alive for political reasons. The BJD government didnt want the dispute to be settled. They wanted to continue the dispute with Chhattisgarh and make it a political issue. Thats the reason they opted for the tribunal route even as the NDA government at the Centre initiated the process to resolve the matter amicably, Purohit said. Referring to the BJPs governments in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and at the Centre, he said the triple engine dispensation would help resolve the dispute and secure Odishas due share. The BJD, however, has questioned the substance of the latest talks and demanded that the decisions taken at Thursdays meeting be made public. Senior BJD leader and former minister Arun Kumar Sahoo said the meeting should not be reduced to an exercise aimed at the upcoming local body elections. Since there is a triple-engine government, the possibility of resolving the Mahanadi water dispute had increased. However, no urgency was seen towards resolving the issue. There has been no clarity as to whether the dispute will be resolved through a tribunal or through mutual discussions, Sahoo said. The BJD has also sought clarity on whether Odisha would receive the water it requires during the non-monsoon period, and on the status of the barrages built by Chhattisgarh, which the party has described as illegal. Odisha Congress president Bhakta Charan Das also criticised the BJP governments, saying the state was yet to receive its due share of Mahanadi water. What is the dispute? The dispute dates back to 2016, when Odisha objected to Chhattisgarhs construction of a series of barrages and other structures on the Mahanadi and its tributaries. Odisha argued that the projects would reduce downstream flows, particularly during the non-monsoon period. Chhattisgarh has maintained that, given the rivers catchment area in the state, it is within its rights to use Mahanadi water for its requirements. The Centre initiated efforts at an amicable settlement in 2016, but the then Naveen Patnaik government pursued a legal route and approached the Supreme Court seeking constitution of a tribunal. Chhattisgarh favoured the creation of a joint control board. Following the Supreme Courts intervention, the Centre constituted the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal in March 2018. Its tenure has since been extended, with the latest extension running until January 13, 2027. The Majhi government has now initiated a parallel effort towards a negotiated settlement and has informed the Tribunal about the process.

articleTitle: 10 am to 5 pm: Karnataka High Court fixes parole window for murder convicts’ wedding
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court murder convicts parole wedding
description: Observing that moral objections cannot override legal entitlements, the Karnataka High Court granted a seven-hour parole window to two life convicts who murdered the woman's husband so they can marry.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court last week granted a limited one-day parole to two life convicts, a man and a woman convicted of conspiring and murdering the womans husband, allowing them to solemnise their marriage. The court observed that moral objections cannot override a legal entitlement when no statutory prohibition exists. Justice MG S Kamal at the Dharwad bench passed the order on September 28 on a writ petition filed by Shridhar Arjun Talawar and Siddavva alias Priyanka Jagamutti, both aged 23 and residents of Bhairanatti in Mudalagi taluk, Belagavi district. Currently lodged in the Belagavi central jail, the duo sought directions for their release or, alternatively, 90 days of general parole to conduct their marriage and related ceremonies. Siddavva was married to Shankar Siddappa Jagamutti, 25, but developed a relationship with Sridhar Talawar. Considering Shankar an obstacle to their relationship, the duo conspired to eliminate him. On July 17, 2023, shortly after Shankars birthday, Shridhar stabbed Shankar to death at a temple with Siddavvas assistance before fleeing. Following their arrest, a local court in Belagavi district convicted both of murder on July 30, 2024, sentencing them to life imprisonment alongside a fine of Rs 3 lakh. Moral question and legal rights Addressing the unique circumstances, the High Court noted that the petitioners decision to marry aligns with the prosecutions original conspiracy theory regarding their motive. The petitioners have now decided to get married, which was indeed the conspiracy theory proposed by the prosecution. This poses a moral question as to whether they are entitled to parole to get married when the accusation against them was that they had conspired to eliminate the husband of petitioner No.2 Siddavva. However, legally, there is no such prohibition. Moral consciousness cannot overtake the legal entitlement to get married, the order stated. The court further noted that the right to marry serves a recognised social function and cannot be denied purely on moral considerations in the absence of explicit statutory bars. While the state government argued that the prison manual contains no provisions for granting parole on marriage grounds, it also confirmed upon the courts query that jail regulations do not permit solemnising marriages within prison premises. The court directed prison authorities to grant parole between 10 am and 5 pm on a date chosen by the petitioners, subject to administrative convenience. An adequate number of police personnel, to be deputed by the jailer, shall accompany the petitioners and remain present during the ceremony. The petitioners must be returned to jail by 5 pm on that day, the court directed.

articleTitle: Want Rohit Sharma to have more ODI centuries than his age when he retires: Sunil Gavaskar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rohit is 39 years old and has scored 35 centuries thus far in his illustrious ODI career. (PTI/File Photo)
description: Rohit Sharma fell on 92 off 85 balls in the third ODI and had he scored a century, it would've been the 36th of his illustrious career in the format.
body_raw: Rohit Sharma nearly scored a second ODI century in a row during Indias match on Saturday against the West Indies in Mullanpur, falling for 92 in 85 balls. Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar said that he was quite disappointed that Rohit fell eight runs short of his century, for a rather unique reason. The reason I was disappointed with Rohit getting out on 92 is because he didnt get a hundred and he might possibly quit international cricket after the end of the ICC Mens Cricket World Cup 2027. And at that particular point in time, when he decides to call it a day, I personally would like Rohit to have more ODI hundreds than his age, said Gavaskar. Rohit is 39 years old and has scored 35 centuries thus far in his illustrious ODI career. Had he gotten a century in the third ODI, he would have moved closer to achieving that feat with his 36th hundred. For me, its a special thing when a players hundreds outnumber his age at retirement. It shows the kind of career they have had and the standard they have maintained for so many years. That is why I really want Rohit to reach that mark. In my last year of international cricket, I wanted to get as many Test centuries as my age, and I got out in the 90s thrice. If Id got those hundreds, then my centuries would have matched the age of my retirement, which was 38, Gavaskar said on JioStars Haier Cricket Live. Gavaskar, the first player to score more than 10,000 career runs in Test cricket, retired with 34 centuries in the format. India went on to put up a score of 3517 thanks to Rohits 137-run partnership with Ruturaj Gaikwad and KL Rahuls unbeaten 129 in 87 balls. However, they went on to lose the match five wickets with West Indies captain Shai Hope notching up an unbeaten 162 in 143 balls.

articleTitle: In Maharashtra, the story of a drought foretold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: drought
description: What took three failed monsoons to produce in 1972 has taken just one bad season today — a measure of Maharashtra’s deepening fiscal and agricultural vulnerabilities
body_raw: Its easy to spot a few familiar patterns - and some surprises - here. As Maharashtra confronts a water shortage after a weak monsoon, many are comparing the situation with 1972, when the state experienced its toughest drought on record. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has expressed concerns that this years drought could be worse than 1972. But theres a bit more to it. Back in 1972, three successive years of poor monsoons led to a real crisis. Things are different this time Last year brought plenty of early rain, topping up all the dams and reservoirs. In 1972, it took three years of failed rains to spark trouble more than half a century later, just one bad season has left the state in a spot of bother. This neatly sums up how things have shifted in a state once celebrated for its farming progress. The 1972 drought brought out the best in politicians who truly cared about ordinary people. Troubled by the harsh conditions, Vitthal Sakharam Page, then chairman of the state Legislative Council, asked his wife how much cash she had at home. Mrs Page found just about Rs 700. He then asked how many labourers that might support, and she replied, Around 10 for two weeks. A dedicated Gandhian, Page quickly raised the matter with the then chief minister, Vasantrao Naik, calling for Rs 100 crore to help the states poor. Naik invited Krishnarao Dhulap of the Peasants and Workers Party PWP, the Leader of the Opposition, to discuss raising the sum. In a rare and heartening move, Dhulap and the entire Opposition proposed a tax raise, which the treasury backed. The Assembly unanimously agreed to add a 15 paise surcharge per passenger on state transport bus tickets. This fund created the Employment Guarantee Scheme EGS, recently renamed VB-G RAM G Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission. Its pretty rare to see the opposition calling for a tax rise. Cut to 2026. Even before the formal conclusion of the monsoon, the state - already constrained by a debt of Rs 11 lakh crore - is securing additional borrowing to fund a Rs 45,000 crore drought relief programme. Although the central government has set a borrowing ceiling of Rs 1.20 lakh crore for the current financial year, the state has already consumed Rs 50,000 crore in loans over five months - much before the drought was officially declared. At the time of the budget presentation in March, a revenue deficit of Rs 40,552 crore and a fiscal deficit of Rs 1.5 lakh crore were projected. This year, the state has allocated a substantial Rs 70,000 crore solely for interest servicing on its borrowings - a figure expected to rise as further debt is incurred. Against this backdrop, Fadnavis, who also holds the finance portfolio, presented supplementary demands totalling Rs 97,000 crore during the first quarter of the current financial year. This is no less than a habitual profligate begging for funds the day after payday. Welcome to todays Maharashtra, which is safe to characterise as fiscally imprudent and entrapped in self-imposed challenges. Money matters arent the only hurdle the state faces. The state is missing figures like V S Page, who could dream up clever ideas for everyones benefit, and opposition leaders such as Krishnarao Dhulap, who showed real generosity by suggesting a tax to help tackle the drought. A discernible shortage of competent personnel and leaders demonstrating public accountability is evident, as Fadnavis is compelled to address every issue personally. He has few ministers on whom he can depend. The three-party coalition presents significant challenges for the administration. Representatives from the governing parties are predominantly occupied with securing drought-affected status for their constituencies. The power-sharing arrangement has fostered a competitive environment concerning the number of regions obtaining this designation. Every prominent leader is endeavouring to ensure their constituency is included. A formal declaration of drought triggers automatic financial, administrative and social support from the state. This enables them to shower political largesse on the electorate at public expense, regardless of whether all areas are genuinely affected. This, in a state which, despite having the largest number of dams of any state in the country, has just about 17 per cent to 18 per cent of the total cropped area under irrigation. It leaves the vast majority of the farming community reliant on delayed or insufficient rainfall. From 2012, Maharashtra has recorded a negative agriculture growth for quite a few years. Even this years Economic Survey projects moderate growth of just around 3.4 per cent compared to the high of 9.1 per cent recorded in the previous fiscal year. Its worth mentioning that Maharashtra received over 100 per cent rains in the year gone by. So far this year, the state has announced drought in 265 out of 358 talukas. Its quite likely the government will soon label the whole state - apart from Mumbai and its nearby suburbs for obvious reasons - as drought-hit. In contrast to 1972, the current expectation is for increased state intervention, given that the administration is aligned with the central governing party. When electoral appeal becomes the overriding imperative for political survival and victory the exclusive objective, it is scarcely feasible for the authorities to remain indifferent. Where the double-engine government has struggled to demonstrate tangible development, its commitments will be rigorously tested during drought conditions. The writer is editor, Loksatta

articleTitle: Jackie Shroff reveals why actors rejected the role of Chunnilal in Shah Rukh Khan’s Devdas

body_raw: Jackie Shroff recently opened up about playing the iconic Chunnilal in Sanjay Leela Bhansalis Devdas, revealing that the role came to him only after several other actors had turned it down. To those whom the film had been offered, they said, My characters name isnt even there.Devdas is his name. So, when nobody accepts the role, it comes to me, and I said, Yes, Ill do this role. They filmmaker said There is one song for you and these are the dialogues. articleTitle: Thackerays demand Gyanesh Kumar’s scalp; Raj calls for ballot paper polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uddhav Thackeray protest, Raj Thackeray protest,
description: At an Opposition protest, Uddhav Thackeray questions the centralisation of SIR voter verification, while Raj Thackeray alleges ‘vote chori’ since 2017-18.
body_raw: Shiv Sena UBT chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray led a joint protest march in Mumbai on Sunday against Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his resignation and the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter lists in Maharashtra. At the concluding meeting of the Virat Garjana Morcha, Raj also demanded that electronic voting machines EVMs be replaced with ballot papers in elections. The march began from Metro Cinema and proceeded towards the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters. State leaders of the Congress and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP SP also participated. Organisers had asked participants to carry only the tricolour and not party flags. Referring to a letter by former Union Home Secretary R K Singh, Raj said, According to former Union Home Secretary R K Singh, special revision can be done in exceptional circumstances by recording the reasons in writing and for a specific constituency. It is illegal to conduct SIR across India. There is no provision in the law in this regard, he said. Raj said such circumstances could include a major natural disaster, migration, large-scale duplication of names or complaints regarding the voter list. Therefore, the case that is going on now is illegal, he said. Voters were to be increased during the Assembly elections and now two crore people have been taken out in SIR. Are these our voters? Who are they? Raj said, asking all political parties to demand that the exercise be cancelled. Raj also called for an end to voting through EVMs. The voting machines in this country should be shut down and voters should vote on ballot papers. If these two things happen, it will be clear who is right and who is wrong. It doesnt matter who comes to power tomorrow, he said. Raising vote chori since 2017-18 Raj Thackeray Raj said he had spoken about vote theft with Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, and NCP leaders long back. Today, we are here for vote chori. I have been saying since 2017-18 that vote chori is happening, he said. He claimed that he had told Opposition leaders at the time to boycott elections so that the alleged irregularities would come to light. Raj also questioned the increase in voter numbers between the 2024 Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, citing the difference to allege manipulation. The Election Commission, however, has maintained that the increase in Maharashtras electorate was within the normal range and has said the 2.07 crore enumeration forms that could not be collected during SIR should not be treated as final deletions. The draft roll contained about 7.72 crore electors against 9.79 crore before the exercise. Raj also asked the Election Commission to spell out how many of the people left out of the draft rolls had been identified as illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. Are those two crore people Bangladeshis? How many Bangladeshis have you found? Give us their details, we ourselves will find them and throw them out of the country, he said. Manufacturing a dictator under Make in India Uddhav questioned the centralisation of decisions relating to voter verification. Referring to a communication from Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam to the Election Commission, he said local election officials should have greater powers. Our states Chief Election Officer has written to the Election Commission asking to give rights to local officers after he realised that the right to decide voting rights is not with the local BLOs but has been centralised. It is with Gyanesh Kumar. Who is he to decide this? Uddhav said. Gyanesh Kumar is their weapon. Using him, they are taking away the right to vote also. You can control institutions, but the streets belong to us. The SIR must be scrapped, he said. Uddhav also questioned Kumars appointment as the CEC, alleging bias in the selection process. He criticised the change in the composition of the selection committee for election commissioners and alleged that Kumar was appointed despite Opposition objections. Targeting the government, Uddhav said, If, under Make in India, you are also going to manufacture a dictator in our country, then we have gathered here today to bury that dictatorship and put an end to it. He also alleged that the exclusion of around 13 crore names from draft rolls across the country during the wider SIR exercise amounted to disenfranchisement. The march was held amid a wider Opposition campaign against the Election Commission over SIR and the functioning of the poll panel. In Maharashtra, the Election Commission has extended the deadline for filing claims and objections on the draft voter list to October 12, with the process of issuing and deciding notices extended to November 10.

articleTitle: ‘Had 27 paise in his pocket’: Shabana Azmi recalls Javed Akhtar’s early struggles in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shabana Azmi celebrates 62 years of Javed Akhtar moving to Mumbai.
description: Shabana Azmi marked 62 years since her husband, veteran poet, screenwriter and lyricist Javed Akhtar, first arrived in Mumbai with just 27 paise in his pocket.
body_raw: On this day, 62 years ago, veteran screenwriter, lyricist, and poet Javed Akhtar first stepped foot into Mumbai. He left home in Gwalior, Uttar Pradesh, and took a train to Mumbai, the proverbial city of dreams, getting down at the Mumbai Central station on October 4, 1964. More than six decades later, his wife and veteran actor Shabana Azmi celebrated the occasion with an Instagram post on Sunday. Shabana Azmi recalls Javed Akhtars early Mumbai days 4th Oct 1964. A young lad arrived at Bombay Central Station with 27 naye paise in his pocket but with big dreams in his eyes, wrote Shabana in the Instagram caption, along with the picture of a young Javed Akhtar. Life gave him several hard knocks. He slept on the footpaths, at the railway stations, and in the compound of many a studio. A day came when he had nothing to eat for 3 days and the only clothes he had were the shreds on his body, she added. Recalling how Javed refused to give up despite those hardships, Shabana continued, On the edge of despair, when he could have given up, he said to himself, Main yunhi marne ke liye nahin paida nahin hua tha. Yeh din badlenge I wasnt born to die like just like that. These days will change, as they did. 4th October, 1964 a 19-year-old, almost penniless. 4th October, 2026, decades later a life that has given India some of its most memorable words. This is the story of Javed Akhtar. Shabana Azmi ended the post by turning Javed Akhtars journey into a message of hope for others Some journeys begin with almost nothing. Except a dream. If he can do it, so can you. Never give up. In the comments section of the video, celebrities including Javed Akhtars daughter and filmmaker Zoya Akhtar, actors Hrithik Roshan, Dia Mirza, Divya Dutta, and Amruta Subhash, among others, shared red heart emojis. The boy continues to dream and build fire emoji, commented music composer Ankur Tewari. Javed Akhtar on his early days of struggle In the 2024 Amazon Prime Video India docuseries Angry Young Men, Javed Akhtar also looked back at his early days of struggle in Mumbai. I decided that after my graduation, Id go to Mumbai and work as an assistant director, hopefully with either Guru Dutt or Raj Kapoor. I was sure that after a couple of years of doing this, Id definitely become a director, he recalled. After living with his father and legendary poet Jan Nisar Akhtar, Javed then moved out and slept wherever he found a place, from friends homes to railways stations, parks, studio compounds, corridors, and benches. Some days, Id walk all the way from Dadar to Bandra, because I didnt have money for bus fare. Some days, it would strike me that I hadnt eaten for two days. I would always think to myself that if one day, a biography were to be written about me, this would make for an incredible moment, he added. After Javed Akhtar swore to himself that hed see better days, better days did follow. Eventually, he joined forces with Salim Khan to become arguably Indias most formidable writer duo. Salim-Javed wrote seminal films like Hathi Mere Sathi 1971, Yaadon Ki Baaraat 1973, Seeta Aur Geeta 1973, Zanjeer 1973, Deewaar 1975, Sholay 1975, Don 1978, Trishul 1978, Shaan 1980, and Shakti 1982, among others. However, Javed confessed that the days of hunger left such an indelible impact on his psyche that even after having all the luxuries in the world today, hes unable to believe its true at times. I stay in five-star hotels, in huge suites with large double beds. And I look back on how I came to Mumbai, in a third-class compartment that didnt even have any room to sit. I remember how I was deprived of sleep, and how tired I was. All I needed was a fraction of the room I had now, he said. Also Read - So we dont end up in jail Kapil Sharma on why he watches younger comics The veteran poet also admitted that he still experiences imposter syndrome and sometimes feels as though he is having an out-of-body experience while enjoying the luxuries he has earned after a lifetime of hard work. They bring out so much food, and I always wonder where this food was on the days I had nothing to eat. To this day, I feel like I havent deserved this food. I cant get over that, he added, teary-eyed, in the docuseries.

articleTitle: ‘Was doing my duty’: BLO who stopped bulk submission of pre-printed SIR Form 7s in Hyderabad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The first instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency.
description: The video of this BLO rejecting the Form 7s went viral when Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee raised the matter on Saturday. “If some are targeting people by filing bulk Form 7s, we will take strict action,” the CEO’s office said.
body_raw: His voice may have gained unlikely attention, with Telangana Congress sharing a now-viral video of him rejecting a bunch of Form 7s allegedly filed by a BJP booth-level agent BLA, but this BLO from Hyderabad chooses not to make much of it, simply saying, I was just doing my duty. He was posted at Booth 173 in the Goshamahal constituency of Telangana Capital when the said Form 7s of the Special Intensive Revision SIR were filed by a BLA in September-end. Its not possible to accept these Form 7s, he is heard saying. Speaking to The Indian Express, the BLO, who works as a Junior Assistant at Osmania Medical College, said, The forms had printed EPIC numbers. There were no names on them. I had no instructions to receive such forms from my superior officers. Hence, I decided not to accept these. The video of this BLO rejecting the Form 7s went viral three days later, when Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee TPCC on Saturday released the video of pre-printed Form 7s of SIR surfacing in Hyderabad. I dont know how that video went viral. I was only stating my point of view, the BLO said. When asked whether he was scared to reject the forms, he said, No, I was not. I was doing my duty. He, however, did not want to be identified as he did not want publicity for an act which was done as part of the BLO duty. TPCC released the video two days after they complained to the Chief Electoral Officer CEO about apprehensions of a larger conspiracy to bulk delete voters as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls 2026. The forms, which the TPCC had accessed, had no names. They were in the last stages of being filed by the BJP BLA, a Congress source alleged. In a press conference on Sunday, BJP state president N Ramchander Rao said his partys BLAs have not submitted bulk Form 7s. The Congress is spreading malicious propaganda against constitutional institutions like the Election Commission, he added. Form 7s are used by electors if they want to delete their own name or to object to any other elector in their constituency. Similar instances The first instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency. Pre-printed applications were allegedly filed by a BLA of the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP, seeking deletion of a total 31 electors, who included a Congress BLA and his family members. In another case, a pre-printed Form 7 surfaced in Bahadurpura constituency. This, too, was flagged by the TPCC. In the Goshamahal case, the BLO refused to accept the bulk pre-printed forms, a TPCC leader told The Indian Express. When asked about the complaints, Chief Electoral Officer Sudarshan Reddys office told The Indian Express that an inquiry into the matter is on. If some are targeting people by filing bulk Form 7s, we will take strict action, the CEOs office said. According to TPCC, as per the original plan of BJP BLAs, the forms were to be submitted only after October 1, to inundate the election authorities who are already under the weight of lakhs of pending hearings from the notice phase. The period for filing claims and objections comes to an end on October 7. A TPCC source said, If the CEO does not take action, we will approach the police. This is a matter of protecting peoples right to vote. Telangana BJPs chief spokesperson NV Subhash told The Indian Express that bulk Form 7s are being submitted against Rohingyas who are not citizens of the country. He said, Political parties, including the AIMIM, the Congress and the BRS are supporting enrolment of Rohingyas. There is nothing wrong in filing Form 7s to deny them voting rights. He said AIMIMs Asaduddin Owaisi should personally ensure that the Rohingyas dont get voting rights in India. If he is a true Indian, he should see to it, Subhash said. Earlier in the day, Owaisi, the MP from Hyderabad, said, If false Form 7s are being filed, we appeal to the Election Commission to take action against those responsible for it. If this drama does not stop, remember protests bigger than those at Delhis Jantar Mantar will take place on the roads and streets of Hyderabad.

articleTitle: UP quacks get life imprisonment 9 years after woman died following C-section
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UP quacks sentenced, woman dies after C-section,
description: The Amroha woman’s son, who survived the incident, is now nine years old.
body_raw: Nine years after a 22-year-old woman died following a C-section performed by an unqualified practitioner at an unauthorised medical centre in Uttar Pradeshs Amroha district, a court on Saturday sentenced two quacks to life imprisonment. The court convicted Wilson and Ghulam Mustafa, both in their 30s, on September 29 on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, cheating and violation of provisions of the Indian Medical Act. The two men, who had been out on bail, were taken into custody following their conviction and sent to jail. According to the prosecution, the case dates back to October 3, 2017, when farmer Nem Singh took his pregnant wife Ruby to a medical centre after she developed labour pains. Wilson, an unqualified medical practitioner running the centre, and his wife admitted Ruby to the facility, assuring the family that she could have a normal delivery, according to the prosecution. Wilson administered medicines to her and put her on a drip. When her condition subsequently deteriorated, the family informed Wilson. Wilson subsequently told the family that Ruby required an operation and, according to the prosecution, called Mustafa, an unqualified medical practitioner from Naya Gaon village, to the medical centre. At around midnight, Wilson and Mustafa performed the operation on Ruby without obtaining her familys consent, the prosecution said. Ruby died shortly after the procedure. The district administration subsequently sealed the facility, and an FIR was registered against Wilson, his wife, and Mustafa. The police arrested Wilson and Mustafa and sent them to jail, although both were later released on bail during the trial. No evidence against quacks wife During the investigation, the police found no evidence warranting prosecution of Wilsons wife and gave her a clean chit. A chargesheet was subsequently filed against Wilson and Mustafa. Rubys son, who survived the incident, is now nine years old. During the trial, the court examined 12 prosecution witnesses, of whom six, including the complainant, turned hostile. However, we cross-examined the hostile witnesses and were able to establish the prosecution case before the court, said Sanjeev Chaudhary, Additional District Government Counsel, Amroha. The court has directed that notices be issued to the then district magistrate and chief medical officer of Amroha, who were serving in the district in October 2017, seeking their response on the alleged non-compliance with the directions of the Supreme Court and High Court, Chaudhary said.

articleTitle: ‘I danced wearing frocks on local stages in Agra’: Dupahiya 2 actor Sparsh Shrivastava
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sparsh Shrivastava
description: In Dupahiya, Sparsh Shrivastava’s character Bhugol Jha is an aspiring actor who makes reels dressed as a girl to attract followers.
body_raw: Dupahiya Season 2, set in the fictional village of Dhadakpur in Bihar, is now streaming on Amazon Prime Video. When SCREEN pointed out that Sparsh was almost unrecognisable in those scenes, he laughed, prompting the producers to intervene and say, Its a compliment. Elated by the comment, Sparsh looked at the camera and recorded a message for his mother Mom, you always wanted a daughter, right? Asked if he faced any challenges while portraying a girl, the 27-year-old shared, I think they were already within me because when I was small, my mother taught me the dance form, Kathak. Watch the full video interview with Dupahiya Season 2 cast and crew here Despite his early training in Kathak, Sparsh said getting back into the groove for the role took some time. And finally, now its so in me now that sometimes I speak Hindi like that. Because I find it so interesting that you can say the most hard-hitting things, and say it in a way, succinctly its delightful. So, now I am very comfortable. articleTitle: ‘Sent 6.3 ft cake in tempo’: How Tips Music won over Subhash Ghai after Saudagar rejection
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ramesh Taurani, Subhash Ghai, Prakash Jha and Mahesh Thakur at an event
description: In a recent interview, Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani recalled why Subhash Ghai did not give Tips the music rights to his 1991 film Saudagar. They also revealed how they convinced the filmmaker to rope in Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes.
body_raw: Tips Music, co-founded by brothers Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani, has released several hit soundtracks from Subhash Ghais films, including Khal Nayak 1993, Pardes 1997, Taal 1999 and Yaadein 2001. In a recent interview, the Taurani brothers recalled why Ghai did not give Tips the music rights to his 1991 film Saudagar. They also revealed how they convinced the filmmaker to rope in composer duo Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes. When the Saudagar cassette was released, we sent Subhash ji a 6-foot-3-inch cake During a chat with Komal Nahta, Ramesh Taurani recalled approaching Subhash Ghai before he sold the music of his film Saudagar to HMV. Subhash jis film Saudagars music wasnt sold yet, but he told me that he had commited to HMV. I asked him to give the music to us, so he asked me to come next time. He gave the music to them. When the Saudagar cassette was released, we sent Subhash ji a 6-foot-3-inch cake, which said, Saudagar, Saudagar, TIPS ke saath Sauda kar, he shared. When the cake reached his house, the filmmaker was very happy and promised to sign Tips Music for his next film. My associate went to deliver the cake, but it wasnt fitting in a car, so it got delivered in a tempo. He Subhash Ghai went to his house, he was so happy, and he called all the distributors to his house at night. He praised me in front of them, saying that this man doesnt have my music or anything, but still sent such a beautiful letter to me with a cake, Ramesh said. Later, Ramesh Taurani reached out to Subhash Ghai for the music rights of Khalnayak. Then, I went to him for Khalnayak. Subhash ji told me that all the distributors had asked him to take Nadeem-Shravan instead of Laxmikant-Pyarelal for the film. Subhash ji called Nadeem, but he kept negotiating on the price. Subhash ji got angry that he was not talking about music but only money. He eventually went to Laxmikant ji and said that hes ready to pay double the amount. He signed him on by paying a token amount of Rs 5 lakh, he recalled. While Ramesh lied to his brother Kumar Taurani about the actual price demanded by Laxmikant, the success of the song Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai made everything fruitful. Finally, Laxmi ji said that I will not take less than Rs 1 crore. I asked him to take Rs 70, 80 lakhs. Kumar had said that we wont pay more than Rs 75 lakhs. I gave him a nod for Rs 1 crore. When I came back, I told Kumar that the deal was done in Rs 81 lakhs. He complained why I paid Rs 6 lakhs over and above the decided amount. As soon as I left Subhash jis office, the news was everywhere in the media, Khalnayaks music has been sold at Rs 1 crore. I told Kumar that it is false news, he said. The producer continued, When Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai was released, it was a superhit the same day without any promotions. We released the song in the morning and it was being played in a party at night. I told Kumar that we will have to pay Rs 10 lakhs more because the song is already a hit. Years later, Subhash Ghai considered Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes, but his previous experience with the duo made him wary of negotiating their fees. Later, when Trimurti and its music flopped, Subhash Ghai asked for my advice for his film Pardes. He took the names of 2-3 music directors and asked for my suggestion, I told him to take Nadeem-Shravan. He then told me the Saudagar story. I gave him the guarantee that Nadeem will not talk money with you he will just received whatever youll give, Ramesh Taurani shared. Ramesh further added, I spoke to Nadeem and told him to do Subhash jis film without talking about his fees, and he agreed. He said, You will give me the money, na. He had the perspective that if hes giving great music, he should get his due. Everyone used to complain that his music is repetitive, but still everyone went back to him because it used to work. The best part about Pardes music was that it had Subhash Ghais touch. The music of Pardes, Khalnayak and Saudagar, all directed by filmmaker Subhash Ghai, was hugely successful.

articleTitle: 1965 war postscript: Inside Lahore-Amritsar ceasefire talks and mind games
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Military Digest 1965 India Pakistan War Ceasefire Talks
description: During the post-1965 ceasefire negotiations in Lahore and Amritsar, cross-border military diplomacy saw unexpected moments—from personal reunions at the airfield to a surprising discourse at the Golden Temple.
body_raw: An interesting postscript to the 1965 India-Pakistan war was the series of joint military meetings held in Lahore and Amritsar, where delegations from both nations discussed the fine print of the ceasefire and coordinated the withdrawal of forces. Held under the auspices of the United Nations and in accordance with the Security Council resolution of November 5, 1965, the talks alternated between the two cities and were coordinated by Brigadier-General Tulio Marambio, the UN Secretary-Generals representative. The Indian delegation was led by Lt Gen Harbaksh Singh, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Western Command, accompanied by Lt Col TS Padde GSO-1, Western Command and Captain Amarinder Singh, ADC to the Army Commander. The Pakistani side included Lt Gen Bakhtiar Rana GOC 1 Corps, Lt Col SA Hasan, Lt Col Riaz Azim, and Brigadier Gul Hassan Khan. Initially, the UN representative proposed meeting at a neutral camp midway between Lahore and Amritsar. However, Lt Gen Harbaksh rejected the site as barren and inhospitable, suggesting instead that the Indian team visit Lahore first, followed by the Pakistani delegation visiting Amritsar. When the UN envoy asked whether he had the Indian governments permission to go to Lahore first, Harbaksh replied that he did not need to seek permission and that his decision was final, as he wrote in his book In the Line of Duty-A Soldier Remembers. Diplomatic protocols in Lahore The Indian delegation arrived in Lahore in February 1966 aboard a UN aircraft with General Marambio. Upon arrival, Lt Gen Harbaksh inspected a Pakistan Army guard of honour. At the airfield, a personal connection surfaced the Indian Army Commander recalled seeing his ADC, Captain Amarinder Singh, scion of the Maharaja of Patiala, embracing the young Pakistani Captain commanding the Guard of Honour. Amarinder later explained that the officer was the son of Colonel Majeed, his fathers former Military Secretary, and that the two had played together as children on the Patiala palace grounds. While guiding Lt Gen Harbaksh through Lahore to refresh his pre-partition memories, Pakistani officials attempted psychological one-upmanship. Banners in Urdu were put up across the road advertising rides in a captured Indian vehicle for eight annas. The vehicle was the Jonga jeep of Maj Gen Niranjan Prasad, GOC 15 Infantry Division, which had been captured in a sugarcane field on Lahores outskirts after the officer narrowly escaped an ambush, leaving behind his starred plate, flag, and personal papers. Lt Gen Harbaksh objected to the provocative banners and urged his hosts to turn the car around. When the Pakistani counterpart mentioned making over Rs 10,000 from the rides, Harbaksh denied losing a Jonga jeep and warned that if such trickery continued, he would produce ten Jongas adorned with Pakistani flags for inspection when the Pakistani delegation visited Amritsar. Flowers and spiritual discourses during Amritsar visit When the Pakistani delegation made its reciprocal visit to Amritsar, Lt Gen Harbaksh arranged a tour of the Golden Temple. The visit occurred while Akali leader Sant Fateh Singh was staging a protest inside the shrine premises, preparing for a fast unto death and self-immolation to demand Punjabi Suba a separate Sikh-majority state. Despite the political tension, locals were informed in advance. The reception given to us was tremendous. The shopkeepers of Amritsar were all standing in front of their shops and showered us with flowers. On arrival at Harmandir Sahibs gate, we were received by the whole Prabandhak Committee Shiromani Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee, which had lined up with garlands of flowers, to be presented to every member of the delegation, and the United Nations officers, wrote Lt Gen Harbaksh. Towards the end of the tour, the Pakistani General requested a meeting with Sant Fateh Singh, expecting the leader to make critical remarks about the Indian government. Instead, speaking in Punjabi, Sant Fateh Singh stated that the people of India and Pakistan should not fight each other, offered a discourse on the principles of the Sikh faith, and presented sets of Punjabi religious books to the leaders of the Pakistani and UN delegations.
