articleTitle: Jharkhand woman still in detention centre despite court order. Now HC asks, ‘under what law?’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: jharkhand woman
description: In 2025, the woman, after allegedly being sexually assaulted multiple times by a constable, escaped from the centre with two other detainees. Though a trial court convicted her in the escape case, she was acquitted of the charge under the Foreigners Act
body_raw: A Jamtara woman, then in her early 20s, was arrested in an alleged child kidnapping case in 2018. Sentenced to two years in prison, she was supposed to walk out free in 2020. Instead, she ended up becoming the first and, for a while, the only detainee at the Foreigners Holding Centre in Hazaribag-over 190 kilometres from her hometown. Police accused her of being a Bangladeshi national and, for the next several years, she remained at the centre inside the Hazaribag prison. In June 2025, the woman, after allegedly being sexually assaulted multiple times by a constable, escaped from the centre with two other detainees. On July 20 this year, an Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court convicted her of escaping from custody but acquitted her of the charge under the Foreigners Act. However, on completion of her sentence, instead of being released from the prison, she was sent back to the detention centre. On October 1, the Jharkhand High Court asked a question that has followed the woman since she completed her first sentence in 2020 under what law is she still being detained? A division bench of Justices Sujit Narayan Prasad and Akhil Kumar questioned under what authority of law the woman was continuing to be kept at the detention centre after the completion of her sentence. Hazaribag SP told the HC that an inquiry would be initiated into the matter. According to social worker and lawyer Apurva Vivek, who filed a habeas corpus petition on the 30-year-olds behalf in the HC, the woman told her that she had been sexually assaulted multiple times by a police constable. The ordeal had caused her severe mental distress and was part of the circumstances behind her decision to escape. Ordeal began in 2018 Married young after her fathers death, the womans life took a turn when she was arrested on February 2, 2018, relating to the alleged kidnapping of a child. The same year, in December, she was convicted under Section 363 of the IPC and sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment, with the period already spent in custody set off against the sentence. On February 4, 2020, the woman completed the sentence. But instead of being released, she was shifted to the foreigners holding centre at the Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan Central Jail also known as JP Central Jail campus in Hazaribag. It was there that authorities began treating her as a Bangladeshi national. For several years, the woman remained at the holding centre. According to the chronology placed before the HC, she was initially the only detainee there. In November 2024, another woman, Nina Akter alias Khushi, was brought to the centre. On June 10, 2025, the duo along with another detainee escaped. They were apprehended the following day at Dhanbad railway station. A fresh case was registered at Lohsinghna police station in connection with the escape. It is at this point that Vivek noticed something odd. Instead of the womans real name, she was registered in case records as someone from the minority community. Her fathers name was also found to be different that what it is in her original records. The case subsequently came before the Hazaribag court. The prosecution accused the three women of escaping from the foreigners holding camp and invoked Section 14 of the Foreigners Act. On July 20, the trial court stated that the prosecution had proved the charge relating to escape from custody and convicted all three accused under Section 262 read with Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS. But the Foreigners Act charge did not stand, and the court acquitted the Jamtara woman. The judgment recorded several gaps, including the absence of authenticated cross-border records, original travel documents or validated nationality verification material establishing their foreign status. The investigating officer also admitted that documents including an Aadhaar card and SIM allegedly connected to the woman had not been verified with the issuing authorities. The court, therefore, while convicting her of the escape, acquitted her of the Foreigners Act offence. In its October 1 judgment, the court made a broader observation on personal liberty We are living in the era of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the inherent liberty conferred upon a human being cannot be taken away without any authority of law. The court directed the Hazaribag District Legal Services Authority DLSA to record the womans statement. It also sought an inquiry by the Hazaribag Superintendent of Police SP into the allegation against the constable and directed the Inspector General of Prisons to participate in the proceedings. The SP told the court that a thorough inquiry into the allegation would be initiated. The Home Secretary of Jharkhand has been directed to appear before the court on October 5. Reports from the DLSA and the SP have also been sought. SP, Hazaribag, could not be contacted for comment despite attempts.

articleTitle: AI Alerts to ‘Plan Bee’: How Railways saved 255 elephants from train collisions in northeast
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Railways have stepped up efforts to prevent elephant-train collisions across vulnerable sections in the Northeast. (Image generated using AI)
description: Northeast Frontier Railway says 255 elephants were saved from train collisions between January and September 2026 using AI-based alerts, 'Plan Bee', speed restrictions and enhanced vigilance.
body_raw: Northeast Frontier Railway NFR has used AI-based alerts, speed restrictions, enhanced patrolling and its Plan Bee system to prevent train-elephant collisions. It helped in saving 255 elephants between January and September 2026. According to Kapinjal Kishore Sharma, Chief Public Relations Officer, NFR, the elephants were saved across four divisions - Alipurduar, Rangiya, Lumding and Tinsukia - through timely interventions and coordination with the Forest Department. Timely interventions by NFR personnel helped save 255 elephants across its divisions, including 106 in Alipurduar Division, 14 in Rangiya, 122 in Lumding and 15 in Tinsukia Division, Sharma said. How AI alerts are helping detect elephants near railway tracks AI-based Intrusion Detection System One of the key measures adopted by NFR is an AI-based Intrusion Detection System IDS that uses Distributed Acoustic System DAS technology. It provides real-time alerts when elephant movement is detected near railway tracks. This allows railway personnel to take timely preventive action and alert train crews in vulnerable sections. The zonal railway is also using other measures, including temporary speed restrictions and night-time speed restrictions when elephant movement is reported. Plan Bee used to keep elephants away from tracks The railway has also installed the Plan Bee system at vulnerable locations. The system uses amplified honeybee sounds to discourage elephants from approaching railway tracks.NFR has also taken up the construction of underpasses at identified locations to provide safer routes for wildlife and reduce the need for elephants to cross railway tracks. Along with these measures, railway teams are carrying out regular patrolling, clearing vegetation at vulnerable locations and installing cautionary signs. Train crews and passengers being sensitised The Railways is also focusing on preventing human activities that could attract elephants towards railway tracks. According to Sharma, railway staff, train crews, pantry car personnel and passengers are being sensitised against throwing food waste near tracks, as discarded food can attract elephants and other animals. The railway is also maintaining continuous communication with the Forest Department. Continuous coordination and real-time communication with the Forest Department further enable timely action whenever elephant movement is detected, he said. Probe of train-elephant collisions The CPRO also added that all cases involving train-elephant collisions are treated seriously and investigated according to prescribed safety procedures. All cases involving trainelephant dashing are treated with utmost seriousness and investigated as per the prescribed safety procedures. NFR continues to strengthen technology-based monitoring, frontline vigilance and coordination with wildlife authorities to protect elephants while ensuring safe and efficient train operations across the Northeast, he said in a statement.

articleTitle: Canadian vlogger’s post prompts footpath repair in Bengaluru’s Indiranagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru footpath viral video Canadian vlogger
description: While Caleb Friesen's video garnered more than 2.1 million views, the Lokayukta took up a case suo motu and directed its police officers to visit the place.
body_raw: A day after a Canadian vloggers video on the poor condition of a footpath in Bengalurus busy Indiranagar went viral and the Lokayukta took cognisance of it, the civic authorities swung into action to repair the footpath on Sarturday. Vlogger Caleb Friesen posted a video on Friday highlighting that the damaged footpath on 12th Main Road inconvenienced pedestrians. Such footpaths would be totally unacceptable in any other country, he added. On Instagram, he posted, Indiranagar shouldnt be like this. The footpaths should be walkable, safe, pedestrian-friendly, impressive, and a reflection of all the innovation that happens in the city. Instead, theyre a mess. 12th Main in Indiranagar features rubble to rival a conflict zone, holes so big they look extraterrestrial, slabs that seem like they could give way at any moment, and trees that double as dustbins. Why are the footpaths at the centre of Indias tech ecosystem so pathetic? Why doesnt Bengaluru seem to care about its reputation both locally in India and internationally? I dont have answers to these questions. All I know is what I see, and what I experience as a pedestrian any time Im in the city. I think its high time for a footpath upgrade in Bengaluru. Something bigger and more comprehensive than the city has ever seen in all its centuries of existence. Something that Bengaluru can be proud of. Something that sets an example for the rest of the country. I do wonder if the city will rise to this challenge, or continue to be a national and international pedestrian infrastructure embarrassment the way that it is currently. Lets see. While the video garnered more than 2.1 million views, the Lokayukta took up a case suo motu and directed its police officers to visit the place. The officials found that construction debris had been lying there for three days. Lokayukta warning for engineers Later, the Lokayukta issued directions for the chief engineer of Bengaluru Central City Corporation and other engineers concerned. The officials informed the Lokayukta that they initiated action on Saturday evening, but not against the person who put construction debris on the footpath obstructing the road. The Lokayukta was not satisfied with the response and stated, This clearly shows that, despite this matter being taken very seriously by this authority and the case regarding waste disposal in the city in different zones is being monitored intensively for the last more than 2 years, the concerned officials of the Bengaluru Central City Corporation, are showing such apathy. Therefore, all the engineers are hereby cautioned and instructed to ensure that no such incident occurs or recurs again. This shall be treated as a final warning before initiating any action against them personally for their dereliction and resultant maladministration. The Lokayukta also directed its police team to carry out random inspections of the area under the Bengaluru Central City Corporation and report any such lapses before September 9. Voting not paying taxes not enough Vlogger Caleb Friesen later posted another video on Instagram and said, So glad to see the rapid response from GBA Like so many in the comments, I too wish that the city authorities were more proactive instead of reactive fixing things before anyone needs to complain. That said, I commend their effort and the ongoing work theyre doing to fix up the problematic spots. Also I have said this before and will continue to say it my skin colournationality plays a role insofar as it acts as masala, helping my content to go viral. But anyone can create their own personal masala as a creator Baadal Nanjundaswamy dressed up as an astronaut to highlight moon crater-like potholes. Residents of Cox Town organised a pothole pooja to raise awareness. Anyone can complain creatively to get things done - very few people do though. They believe that if they pay taxes and vote, thats enough. It isnt. If you want positive change to happen, you need to, 1. Make it known that youre not satisfied with the status quo in a respectful, peaceful way, and 2. Do whatever is within your power to make a positive change. Virendra Suryawanshi placed many calls before and while this video went live, and has been working alongside GBA. Arun Pai mobilises volunteers to beautify spaces and discourage further neglect and degradation. Please think about how you the reader of this comment can contribute to positive change. India isnt going to improve on its own.

articleTitle: Andhra CM calls on IIT alumni to unite for nation-building, signs deal with PanIIT
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu
description: While addressing the valedictory session of the two-day PanIIT summit, Naidu said "for nation-building, all IITians can unite together. We will network together. Wherever you are, think of your country for five minutes or 10 minutes or one hour."
body_raw: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday called on IIT graduates to unite for the country, as the southern state and PanIIT inked several deals, including establishing a PanIIT Amaravati Council. PanIIT is an alumni network of five lakh IIT graduates. The chief minister underscored that he needs the creative, innovative ideas and sometimes disruptive thought process of IITians. For nation-building, all IITians can unite together. We will network together. Wherever you are, think of your country for five minutes or 10 minutes or one hour, said Naidu, addressing the valedictory session of the two-day PanIIT summit. If five lakh brilliant IIT brains are with me, then I can imagine what I can do, Naidu stressed. Read IIT Guwahati taught me more than engineering Coffin dances, Maggi and an events head title The deals inked by PanIIT and the southern state include setting up 10 industry chairs in Andhra Pradesh varsities, a 100-mentor startup network and others. The other agreements include-transferring technology from IITs, deep tech policy package and others. Naidu also announced the Amaravati PanIIT Declaration. The Chief Minister noted that PanIIT Amaravati World Council will be set up in the greenfield capital city of Amaravati and the establishment of a Rs 500-crore PanIIT Amaravati Deep Tech Venture Fund. Following a meeting with venture capitalists earlier in the day, the CM promised to match their funding to startups in the southern state if they bring capital and mentors. Naidu said an IIT Research Park will be established in Amaravati and underscored that the premier institutes will mentor state varsities and set up Centres of Excellence CoE in each university. The CM said a student exchange programme will be instituted and announced that AI and entrepreneurship skills will be taught from class 6 onwards in Andhra Pradesh. Also Read IITs, IIMs see more women joining than ever as placements and salary packages rise Further, Naidu launched five Q-Shiva quantum computers made in Amaravati and released Shrusti processor and a childrens book to kindle interest in quantum computing. Observing that everybody talks about the Silicon Valley now, the CM emphasised that everybody should talk about the Quantum Valley in Amaravati from tomorrow, adding that the first quantum computer will start functioning from the greenfield capital city on February 3, 2027. Naidu said Indians are capable and we have to work with consensus, as he listed out the industrial and technological initiatives of Andhra Pradesh, which encompass a space city, drone city, defence corridor, aerospace corridor and others at various places in the state. He underlined that the state is planning for semiconductors in a big way in Tirupati and underscored that we have achieved so many things, we have to achieve many things. Further, the CM said a water grid is the missing link in India and proposed the interlinking of Ganga and Cauvery rivers, which should precede by the interlinking of Godavari and Cauvery.

articleTitle: Punjab Congress’s September jinx, AAP’s ‘Imaandaar CM’ shift and cash crunch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab CM: The aim is to uphold the highest standard of Satkar and reverence for Sri Guru Granth Sahib, it said.
description: Corridors of power: From the Congress changing state presidents months before the 2027 polls to ED raids making bureaucrats switch to disappearing messages, this week's column tracks Punjab's top political and administrative developments.
body_raw: September has not been particularly kind to the Congress in Punjab. In September 2021, barely five months before the Assembly elections, the party removed then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and handed the reins to Charanjit Singh Channi. What followed in February 2022 is history. The Congress lost power and the Aam Aadmi Party AAP swept the state. Cut to September 2026. Again, barely five months before the 2027 Assembly election, the Congress has changed its state president, replacing Amarinder Singh Raja Warring with Pargat Singh. The move followed months of differences and consultations within the party. The similarity is hard to miss a major leadership change just months before an election, after prolonged internal uncertainty. Whether the change turns the jinx into a blessing remains to be seen. Officers discover disappearing message After the Enforcement Directorates 50-hour-long questioning of Greater Mohali Area Development Authority GMADA officials and the confiscation of their phones during the searches, Punjabs bureaucracy appears to have discovered a new favourite feature on messaging apps disappearing messages. Bureaucrats who once happily exchanged long messages, documents and political gossip on WhatsApp are suddenly becoming rather conscious of what remains on their phones. Times are unpredictable. We dont know which chat will spell doom, an officer said, summing up the new mood in the corridors of power. The GMADA episode has clearly had a chilling effect. For bureaucrats, a casual message written months ago suddenly acquired significance it never had when it was sent. So messages are now being made to disappear. Whether that will make conversations disappear too is another matter. Decisions still have to be taken, files still have to move and, sooner or later, somebody has to put something in writing. Government vehicles run short of fuel amid cash crunch Punjab governments cash crunch was reflected in an unusual way in September, when official vehicles of several government functionaries were left without fuel for a few days as petrol pumps stopped supplying fuel over non-payment of dues. With the government unable to clear the pending bills, some secretaries were forced to pay for fuel out of pocket to keep their official vehicles running, sources said. The issue was eventually resolved after the Finance Department released the pending payment to the petrol pumps. An official put the amount released at less than Rs 1 crore. The episode has once again highlighted the governments cash-flow problems, with departments facing delays in clearing even relatively small routine payments. The fuel supply to government vehicles resumed after the payment was released. For officials, however, the episode offered a glimpse of how the governments financial constraints are beginning to affect day-to-day functioning. A spokesperson said the fuel issue was not due to a funds crunch but a glitch. Kattar Imaandaar AAP, now an Imaandaar CM Punjabs AAP had built much of its political messaging around the title Kattar Imaandaar. The epithet is meant to describe its claim to maintain a clean image in public life. Now, with the Assembly elections only a few months away, the phrase appears to have taken on a new, more personalised form in Punjab. Billboards describing Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann as an Imaandaar CM have come up across the state over the past few days. The timing has naturally drawn attention, coming months before the 2027 Assembly elections, with the Opposition mocking the self-certification. The message is simple the partys earlier Kattar Imaandaar branding is now being attached directly to the Chief Minister. As elections approach, the AAP is turning to its old-school image plank.

articleTitle: Rajya Sabha polls: BJP fields Dinesh Arya from Uttarakhand, Koel Mallick from Bengal
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Trinamool leader Koel Mallick has quit her Rajya Sabha MP's post.
description: Ahead of the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections, the BJP finalised candidate names for Uttarakhand and West Bengal.
body_raw: The BJP Sunday announced Dinesh Arya and former Trinamool Congress TMC leader and actor Rukmini alias Koel Mallick as its candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections from Uttarakhand and West Bengal, respectively. Biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, are scheduled for October 16, alongside a bypoll in West Bengal. Mallick will contest the West Bengal bypoll to retain the seat after joining the BJP following the TMCs defeat in the Assembly elections. Arya, an organisational leader with ties to both the RSS and Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, currently serves as vice chairperson of the states Water Resources Management and Regulatory Commission, a position equivalent to a state Cabinet minister. TMC split and Mallicks nomination Mallick, a prominent figure in Bengali cinema, was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the TMC in April. She subsequently resigned and joined the BJP in July as part of a split within TMC ranks, during which 18 MPs separated, merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India NCPI, and extended support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance NDA government. With the October 6 deadline for filing nominations approaching, BJP leaders held discussions at the party headquarters in New Delhi to finalise candidates for the remaining seats, particularly in Uttar Pradesh. Party sources said the BJP is prioritising women candidates and experienced organisational workers as it seeks to expand its current tally of 116 seats in the 245-member House. In Uttar Pradesh, 10 seats are falling vacant, eight of which are currently held by the BJP, while the Samajwadi Party SP and the Bahujan Samaj Party BSP hold one each. The single seat falling vacant in Uttarakhand is held by BJP MP Naresh Bansal. While BJP leaders expressed confidence in retaining all eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, party insiders noted that one seat could be contested. With 256 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, the party falls slightly short of the required first-preference votes 37 per seat to secure all eight seats outright without opposition. Currently, the BJP-led NDA holds 150 seats in the 245-member Rajya Sabha, while non-NDA parties account for just over 100 seats.

articleTitle: Who can be Kohli’s successor at 3 in ODI’s? Wasim Jaffer says southpaw can do it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Virat Kohli
description: "When Virat and Rohit leave, Rohit, obviously, is a top-order batter, and Yashasvi Jaiswal is there to replace him, but I feel there will be a left-handed batter in Virat's place," Jaffer observed
body_raw: Since becoming the number three in the Indian ODI batting line-up, Virat Kohli has had no looking back. He has been one of the greatest players of all time, not just in the format but in that position too. He has been a master of chases for India over the years, but the 37-year-old said the 2027 World Cup will be his last, leaving a big void in that position. Former Indian cricketer Wasim Jaffer said Tilak Varma might be the right guy to replace Kohli in that spot for India. It feels great to see his versatility. He previously scored a century at No. 3, and now he has adapted to the No. 5 and No. 6 positions so beautifully. This is an amazing quality, Jaffer said on his YouTube channel. Its about time. When Virat and Rohit leave, Rohit, obviously, is a top-order batter, and Yashasvi Jaiswal is there to replace him, but I feel there will be a left-handed batter in Virats place. He has that game we saw the way he scored runs in the Duleep Trophy. His first-class average is around 55. So, he can fit into all three formats pretty easily, Jaffer said. For me, its the last World Cup Im going to play for India, Kohli told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday. That is my motivation and like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup and whatever it takes, Im absolutely ready, he added. The upcoming World Cup will be Kohlis fifth ODI World Cup. The intensity of a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything. Because now, its about 10 games at a Twenty20 level of intensity, he said. Jaffer also spoke about Abhishek Sharma and noted his observations on how the batter has matured in recent times. It seems that Abhishek has matured a bit. He takes a little time, and the assurance is visible now, although this format doesnt give you a lot of time. His earlier approach was to try to hit a six on the first ball. Now, he has understood that it was the wrong approach, Jaffer observed.

articleTitle: Ex-MP Kuldeep Bishnoi’s ‘Sneh Milan’ without BJP flags sets Haryana abuzz
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kuldeep Bishnoi outreach programm
description: While Kuldeep Bishnoi has maintained that he continues to be with the BJP, the events have nevertheless been seen as a show of strength.
body_raw: For the past three months, former MP Kuldeep Bishnoi, younger son of three-time former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal, has been on an intensive public outreach across Haryana-but without BJP flags, banners, or other party symbols. Since launching the campaign from Sirsa on July 21, Bishnoi has held gatherings in parts of Panipat, Kurukshetra, Jind, Kaithal, and Dadri districts, drawing political attention and triggering speculation about his next move, particularly after he was not nominated to Rajya Sabha a few months ago. While Bishnoi has maintained that he continues to be with the BJP, the events have nevertheless been seen as a show of strength. Bishnois gatherings have been named Sneh Milan. The manner in which these programmes are being held across districts, with old political associates and supporters seen alongside him, has raised questions about their political significance. There are no party flags on the stage, no formal political rally format, and no indication of any major political announcement. A close associate said he was reaching out to old contacts and supporters separately from the BJPs formal programmes. Old political relationships associated with the Bhajan Lal family, former associates and people from various social groups are being seen at these gatherings. It would not be appropriate at present to view these programmes as a sign of his distance from the BJP, the aide said. Bishnoi himself has given no indication of breaking away from the BJP and has reiterated that he remains with the party. Addressing his supporters in Dadri on Friday, Bishnoi said, Struggle has taught me not to bow down, but to keep moving forward. With your faith and support by my side, my courage is high, and my resolve is strong. Dadri has given this journey new energy today now the caravan will move forward. Expressing gratitude to his supporters for the gathering, Bishnoi said he viewed the honour as a reflection of the peoples continued support and blessings throughout his long political journey, including during difficult times. He said, In politics, I have seen both good times and difficult times. Circumstances changed, paths changed, but I never stopped trying to remain honest to my principles, my colleagues and my relationship with the people. I never let go of the hands of my people, and you too never withdrew your hand of affection from my shoulder. Nothing anti-party about Bishnois programmes BJP However, BJP leaders point out that Bishnoi currently holds no post in the party organisation, while his son and former MLA Bhavya Bishnoi is the partys state vice-president. Haryana BJP media head Bhupeshwar Dayal said, All political programmes being done by Bhavya are held under the banner of the BJP. Kuldeep Bishnoi is a very senior leader who is doing a lot of social activities. There is in no way anything anti-party about it, as social outreach is the right of any political leader. The ongoing outreach comes a few months after Kuldeep Bishnoi expressed anger over remarks made by BJP Rajya Sabha MP Rekha Sharma about Bhajan Lal on April 25. Her remarks drew a sharp reaction from Bishnoi, his supporters and members of the Bishnoi community, who sought an apology. Sharma expressed regret, saying she would withdraw her statement if it had caused pain to Bhajan Lals family and supporters. In an apparent effort to ease tensions, Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini visited Adampur in Hisar district in June to attend Bhajan Lals birth anniversary programme. Four-time MLA and two-time MP Bishnoi has also been a prominent Congress leader, a four-time MLA, and a two-time Lok Sabha MP. He eventually fell out with the Congress leadership after he was not considered for the post of the state party chief and joined the BJP in 2022 after resigning as an MLA. Later that year, his son Bhavya was elected MLA from Adampur on a BJP ticket but, contrary to expectations among their supporters, was not inducted into the Cabinet. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP chose Ranjit Singh Chautala over Kuldeep Bishnoi for the Hisar seat. Later that year, Bhavya lost the Adampur Assembly election.

articleTitle: Gyanesh Kumar row: Key takeaways from Kerala probe, protests against ECI and SIR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gyanesh Kumar protests
description: Kerala’s Home Department ordered the reopening of a probe into alleged corruption in a road-related work from 2006, when Kumar was the state’s PWD secretary. Meanwhile, protests by different groups continue across the country.
body_raw: After an investigation by The Indian Express revealed the extent of discord within the three-member Election Commission of India ECI, protests in different parts of the country have demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar. In Kerala, the state Home Department has ordered the reopening of a probe by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau into alleged corruption in a road-related work from 2006, when Kumar served as the secretary of the state Public Works Department PWD. Here are the key takeaways about the developments so far. What happened in the 2006 Kerala probe involving Gyanesh Kumar? Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered a reinvestigation in the probe, which was launched two decades ago against Kumar following the suicide of a Malaysian engineer, Lee See Been. Been was then chief project manager of a major road work undertaken by PATI-BEL, an Indo-Malaysian venture, in the state. PATI-BEL had undertaken the renovation of a few stretches of major roads in the state at a cost of Rs 216 crore. Construction of the assigned roads got delayed due to alleged laxity in land acquisition from 2001 to 2006, putting pressure on PATI-BEL and project engineer Been. Kumars name had allegedly figured in the suicide note. The Malaysian national had alleged that Kumar sought a bribe for clearing payment for the work. The road project, known as the Kerala State Transport Project, was funded by the World Bank. A month after Beens death in November 2006, Kumar was moved out of the PWD by the then CPIM-led government. He was eventually posted in the Defence Ministry during the UPA-1 government. Chennithala, who also handles the Vigilance Department, told the media on Sunday October 4 that he had received a complaint from Congress leader Malayankeezhu Venugopal that the Vigilance probe held in 2006 had been compromised due to external compulsion. He added that after a discussion with Chief Minister V D Satheesan, he had decided to order a comprehensive probe based on the fresh complaint. Thackerays reunite again, CJP protests at Mumbais Shivaji Park On Sunday, the opposition parties Shiv Sena UBT and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena MNS took to Mumbais streets in a joint protest march - called the Virat Garjana Morcha - demanding Gyanesh Kumars resignation. But in a break from past protests, the rally saw neither partys flag or symbol on display. Cadres were instructed by their leaders - UBT chief Uddhav Thackeray and MNSs Raj Thackeray - were told to carry only the tricolour. This was an attempt at an outreach beyond ideological lines to make the agitation more inclusive, built around one agenda the ECI. The protest march had two key demands Kumars resignation and the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter lists in Maharashtra. At the concluding meeting of the march, Raj also demanded that electronic voting machines EVMs be replaced with ballot papers in elections. Earlier, Mumbai witnessed protests by the Cockroach Janta Party CJP, a pressure group founded by activist Abhijeet Dipke, at Shivaji Park on Friday. After the Mumbai Police had denied permission to gather for a protest against the ECI and CEC Kumar, the CJP had announced that it would do a jail bharo andolan if necessary. In spite of the lack of police permission, the CJP went ahead with its demonstration on Friday and the Mumbai Police - unlike its Delhi counterparts - didnt use force against the protesters. On the contrast between the approaches of the two forces, The Indian Express reported that the Maharashtra Home Department, a portfolio that CM Devendra Fadnavis himself holds, had directed the police top brass to ensure there is no untoward incident and that gatherings pass off peacefully. How Delhi Police blocked protests at Jantar Mantar The Delhi Police blocked protests against the ECI and CEC Kumar at Jantar Mantar for two consecutive days - on Friday and Saturday October 2 and 3 - and detained hundreds of people. Around 700 people were detained on Friday, including former Delhi CM Atishi, her Aam Aadmi Party AAP colleague and former Delhi minister Saurabh Bharadwaj, activists Neha Bora and Yogendra Yadav, and Left leaders such as Brinda Karat. Earlier on Thursday October 1, Delhi Police had refused permission for this protest, prompting criticism over stifling of protests by the authorities. The Delhi Metro on Friday temporarily closed entry and exit at 12 stations in central Delhi, including Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, and Janpath. Internet services were also suspended in and around Jantar Mantar. Over 150 people - including activists Neha Bora and Yogendra Yadav, and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan - were detained on Saturday for allegedly attempting to return to Jantar Mantar a day after being detained during protests demanding CEC Kumars resignation. The same day, Delhi Police acknowledged that it had received complaints from three female journalists, who had accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering protests near Jantar Mantar. That evening, several freelance journalists and representatives of news portals had gathered outside the Parliament Street police station, demanding action against the officers involved. The female journalists submitted written complaints at the station before leaving. On October 3, during the protest in the New Delhi area, while in a law-and-order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints, and the same have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a fair and impartial enquiry, the Delhi Police said in a statement. Opposition rallies together at INDIA bloc meeting The leaders of the Opposition INDIA bloc on Wednesday September 30 announced a joint action plan against various alleged poll irregularities and the SIR of electoral rolls. Their planned agitation would include protests across the country, a march by the Opposition MPs to the ECI headquarters, and a mega rally in Delhi on November 1. These decisions were taken at a three-and-a-half-hour meeting of the grouping in Delhi, which was attended by the leaders of 19 parties and Independent MP Kapil Sibal. Addressing a joint press conference later, Congress president and Rajya Sabha MP Mallikarjun Kharge said the parties agreed to work together and involve young people and civil society organisations in their campaign. Save Democracy marches would be held from October 2 to 8, followed by demonstrations outside district magistrates offices, across the country. On October 6, Opposition MPs from both Houses of Parliament would march to the ECs office in New Delhi, he said. He added that the Leaders of the Opposition of both Houses would seek an appointment with the President in the second week of October to submit a representation against what he alleged was a vote chori government.

articleTitle: Two heads, one body: Rare turtle hatchling found on Cape Cod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: turtle
description: A rare two-headed diamondback terrapin hatchling has been discovered on Cape Cod, Massachusetts. Here’s what bicephaly means and why it occurs.
body_raw: A tiny turtle hatchling with two heads has been discovered on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, in a rare case that has caught the attention of wildlife experts. Researchers monitoring diamondback terrapins, a turtle species native to the salt marshes and coastal areas of the eastern United States, found the unusual terrapin. What made this hatchling different was immediately visible it had two distinct heads attached to a single body. The condition is known as bicephaly, a form of conjoined development in which an embryo develops two heads. It happens when an embryo doesnt fully separate during early development. While two-headed animals are exceptionally rare, this is not the first such turtle to turn up on Cape Cod. According to Live Science, the newly discovered hatchling is the third bicephalic terrapin found on Cape Cod in the past five years. The discovery is particularly unusual because researchers already closely monitor diamondback terrapins in the region. Finding multiple hatchlings with the same rare developmental abnormality has therefore raised questions about what might be happening during their development. A two-headed turtle does not necessarily have two completely separate bodies. Instead, the hatchling generally shares organs and other body structures, even though the two heads may function independently. That can make movement, feeding and other basic behaviours more difficult. The survival of such animals can also be uncertain. Depending on how extensively they share internal organs and other structures, some may struggle to survive long, while others can live considerably longer. For researchers, however, unusual hatchlings such as this one offer a rare glimpse into how development can sometimes take an unexpected turn. And while the sight of a tiny turtle with two heads may look almost otherworldly, the phenomenon itself is a developmental abnormality rather than evidence of a new or separate species. articleTitle: Nagoya barely embraced the Asian Games. Then everyone turned up to say goodbye
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nagoya
description: Nagoya’s Asian Games overcame early organisational problems, but the compact, low-key event never quite captured the city’s imagination — a contrast underscored by the biggest crowd arriving only for the closing ceremony.
body_raw: On the final night, Nagoya finally looked like it was hosting the Asian Games. The stadium wasnt full. But after two weeks of competition in compact arenas with empty blocks of seats, more people turned up on Sunday to say goodbye. The noise rose into the night, the lights flashed, and the city seemed to have discovered the sporting festival that had been sitting on its doorstep. They roared when Qatari equestrian rider Jassim al Kuwari, astride Red Raiden, a six-year-old gelding, trotted into the Mizuho Park for the closing ceremony and took the Asian Games flag from high-jump great Mutaz Barshim. Then he pranced out, carrying the flag toward Doha - from the real world into the reel world, from one host city to the next. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage They sang and danced and clapped as the fireworks went off, bringing a short, crisp ceremony to a close. Rocky start For much of the fortnight, the Asian Games had felt like a guest Nagoya had agreed to accommodate rather than a party it had decided to throw. That was partly by design. Aichi-Nagoya wanted to make a point about how major sporting events should be hosted in the future. There would be no grand new athletes village that would become a white elephant once the athletes left. No unnecessary stadiums. No attempt to reshape the city for a fortnight. Existing venues would be used, temporary structures would fill the gaps and money would be saved. For a while, it looked like the experiment had gone badly wrong. The Games arrived amid a series of problems that were jarring in Japan. There were accommodation mix-ups, transport troubles, accreditation issues and complaints about temporary facilities. Athletes were moved around. Buses were late. The number of participants grew beyond what organisers had planned for. And then, slowly, almost imperceptibly, the Games got better. There was no great moment of redemption. No announcement that the crisis was over. But the buses began to arrive. The competitions ran. Athletes stopped talking about where they were sleeping and started talking about what they were trying to win. The noise around the organisation faded as the noise inside the arenas grew louder. Nagoya fixed what had looked like a broken Games. There are no Games without challenges. There is no Games without initial interruptions, said Tayyab Ikram, chair of the coordination committee. The way they were addressed should be more important to highlight. In future, we would like to see more sustainable solution, more improvement and innovation . but without compromising on the athletes conditions. The sport was good. Spectacular, sometimes. The compact venues could create an intimacy that enormous stadiums cannot. There were 54 world records, 11 junior records, and 89 Asian records. But the empty seats told another story. They were most striking because the venues were often so small. A few hundred missing spectators could make an arena feel half-empty. There were sessions when the athletes had the strange experience of competing in front of more officials and volunteers than supporters. There were banners. There were mascots. There were athletes in tracksuits wandering through railway stations. However, the Asian Games never seemed to consume Nagoya in the way the Olympics can swallow a host city. People went to work. Trains ran. Shops opened. Life continued. Perhaps that was another unintended success of the model. The organisers had spent years trying to make sure the Asian Games would not overwhelm the city. They did not want to build a temporary Nagoya that would disappear after the closing ceremony. They wanted the Games to fit into the city that already existed. And it did. Perhaps, a little too well. A major sporting event is not only about the buildings it leaves behind. It is also about the memories it creates while it is there. It needs people who suddenly become interested in sports they had never watched, strangers shouting together, restaurants filling up after the last event, a city discovering new heroes. Nagoya had some of that. But never quite enough. An analysis of spectator movement by Kyodo, a Japanese news agency, suggested that the crowds were predominantly local, with Aichi residents accounting for more than half of the domestic spectators at several venues. Late goodbye And then came the closing ceremony. The stadium was more packed than it had been at any point since the flame was lit. It was difficult not to smile at the timing. The biggest crowd of the Games had arrived when there was nothing left to watch. Maybe they came to celebrate. Maybe they had finally become curious. Maybe they wanted one last glimpse before the circus packed up and left. Or maybe Nagoya, having spent two weeks politely living alongside the Asian Games, had finally decided it was time to say goodbye.

articleTitle: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner: Avinash Mishra takes home trophy and Rs 20 lakhs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner Avinash Mishra
description: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner: Along with the Khatron Ke Khiladi Season 15 trophy, Avinash Mishra won prize money of Rs 20 lakh, a trip to Europe and a car.
body_raw: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner Rohit Shetty-hosted stunt-based reality show Khatron Ke Khiladi returned with Season 15 in August this year after a one-year break. With the theme Darr Ka Naya Daur, the season brought together former contestants and new participants to compete against each other. After weeks of taking on challenging stunts, television actor Avinash Mishra has emerged as the winner of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15. Avinash Mishra wins Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 Avinash Mishra defeated fellow top 3 finalists Rithvik Dhanjani and Orry to lift the Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 trophy. Along with the title, Avinash won prize money of Rs 20 lakh, a trip to Europe and a car. The top 3 finalists were also given a bike. Talking about his win, Avinash said in a statement, Winning Khatron Ke Khiladi feels special because I thought I signed up for the show with a point to prove, but along the way, the person I ended up proving it to, was myself. I have spent years being associated with television and, yes, with being the good-looking guy on screen. I enjoyed that journey, but I also knew there was so much more I wanted people to see in me. This show gave me the chance to put everything else aside and literally let my actions speak. He continued, Most of this journey was actually about the mind. You can prepare yourself physically, but when you are standing at the edge of something terrifying, there is no performance left-it is just you, your fear and the decision you make in that moment. I had to learn to tune out the noise, trust myself, and keep going. There were days when I surprised myself, and those are the moments I will cherish. And to win the show after everything I have discovered about myself here is the kind of ending I could only have hoped for. I came to Khatron Ke Khiladi wanting to test myself I am leaving with a belief in myself that I didnt have before. That, for me, is the biggest victory. Right from the beginning, Avinash Mishra emerged as one of the strongest performers on the show. In fact, he did not abort a single task throughout the season and also won the Swift Immunity Jacket, which gave him the power to either save a contestant from elimination or opt out of performing a task. Despite his consistent performance in the stunts, Avinash faced stiff competition from Farrhana Bhatt and Orry from the new batch, as well as returning contestants Karan Wahi and Rithvik Dhanjani. Also Read Bigg Boss 18 finalist Avinash Mishra on his negative image I have no regrets About Avinash Mishra Avinash Mishra has been working in television for nearly a decade. Before becoming an actor, he worked as a DJ. Avinash made his acting debut in 2016 with Sethji and later appeared in Ishqbaaz in 2017. In 2018, his performance in Mariam Khan Reporting Live brought him wider recognition. A turning point in his career came with the 2022 show Nath. Avinash followed up its success with a stint on Bigg Boss 18 in 2024, where he emerged as one of the strongest contenders and finished fourth. While he was still inside the Bigg Boss 18 house, Avinash was finalised as a contestant for Khatron Ke Khiladi 15.

articleTitle: France high school students’ protest: What sparked violence, what’s next
articleFeaturedImageAlt: France schools protests
description: France Student Protests News: French students began protesting over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and poor school infrastructure. But with elections months away, the unrest has a political undertone. We explain.
body_raw: France Student Protests Around 500 schools stayed shut across France on Monday October 5, amid raging students protests. According to the French government, around 500 high schools, out of the countrys 3,700, are fully or partially closed. The countrys education minister, Edouard Geffray, has announced a feedback programme for high school students, along with an action plan to quickly hire more teachers beginning today. The protesters have blockaded schools, set fire to waste bins, and in some cases smashed furniture, doors and windows. According to French officials, damage across 40-odd schools is worth around E3million Rs 32.5 crore. Among the high school students complaints is that there are up to 40 students in a class. The unrest has taken on political colours, coming around six months before the Presidential elections and coalescing with grievances across other sections of the public. On Tuesday, more protests by different unions are planned in support of the students. What is the scale of the students protests in France? The protests began on September 17 at the Saint-Exupry high school in Crteil, a Paris suburb, where students joined teachers protesting a lack of staff and resources. They quickly spread through the Paris region and then to cities including Marseille, Strasbourg, Tours and Lille. The demonstrations have increasingly involved fires, thrown projectiles and clashes with police. In some places, rubbish bins and other objects were set alight, while police used tear gas and rubber bullets. The Education Ministry said 65 education staff, including 40 school principals, had been injured students have also been injured. More than 4,000 people had been arrested since Monday, according to the Interior Ministry. The government has said the students grievances are legitimate but that violence cannot be tolerated. Students, meanwhile, have accused police of using excessive force. What do the protesting French high school students want? The major grievances are overcrowded classrooms, fewer teachers, no nurses or social workers in some schools, and crumbling infrastructure. Inequality is also a factor, with students from poorer suburbs saying their address is impacting their education. A French government report on education from April this year says, During the 2024-2025 school year, 9.8 of teaching hours were not provided in public secondary schools, of which 7.5 was due to the non-replacement of absent teachers and 2.3 was due to the total closure of the establishment. The report adds that the proportion of teaching time not provided increased by 0.7 points compared to the previous year due to a greater number of days of school closures. Some of the protesting students have said there are 40 of them packed in a classroom, when the average for French high schools is around 30 in a class. The length of the school day is another complaint - French high school days can extend from 8 am to 5 pm, with a lunch break, which many say is too long. The extreme heat wave France saw earlier this year has added another dimension. Students have complained about having to sit examinations in classrooms reaching 35C to 40C, while others said classrooms became unbearable during the heatwaves in May and June. French public schools are often not air-conditioned and built to keep heat in rather than out, so 40C in poorly ventilated classrooms for children not accustomed to such temperatures can feel difficult. What is the political angle behind France school protests? While in many schools, teachers have protested side by side students, in other cases, school staff have said the protesters are not from among their pupils. This, the scale of the violence, and flags of Palestine and Algeria at some of the protests have led those on the right wing and even the centre to claim that the hard left party France Unbowed LFI is playing its part in the protests. France will go to polls next year as the centrist government of Emmanuel Macron is under unprecedented stress from both the right and the left, over the issue of migration and identity politics on one hand and rising inequality and spending cuts by the government from the other. While support for the hard right party National Rally led by Marine Le Pen has surged, the LFIs presidential candidate, Jean-Luc Mlenchon, is popular among the youth. However, the French youth often do not turn up to vote in large numbers. Some analysts believe that the LFI is fuelling the high school students protests to rally the youth and make them vote for it next year. For the government, it is a tight spot. In its 2027 budget, education spending is set to rise by 1.7 to E65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions - an increase below inflation. Now, it has to balance students demands while remaining committed to its programme of cutting government spending.

articleTitle: Domestic capacity, reforms key amid global uncertainty: Shaktikanta Das
articleFeaturedImageAlt: On the external front, Das said India's financial sector and prudent management had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. (Image: Ministry of Finance)
description: India is within striking distance of 8% growth, said Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister at the Kautilya Economic Conclave
body_raw: Amid sustained shocks and global uncertainties, India seeks to emphasise on sustained structural reforms, building domestic capacity and competence in areas where there is large import dependence, and continuously focusing on fiscal, monetary, macroeconomic and macrofinancial stability, Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, said on Sunday. Das further said that the country stands at a pivotal moment in its development journey and a leap to Viksit Bharat 2047 is in the realm of realisation, adding that India is within a striking distance of 8 growth. There can never be a moment where you can say that, whatever I have done is sufficient. There is always something more to do but in the current context. The emphasis has been to build our domestic capacity, competence in areas where we are largely import dependent. So, whether it is energy or fertiliser and so many other areas, the government is now focusing on such areas. the focus of the government is also to take measures and to develop long-term capacity in areas where again we are dependent on imports, Das said while answering a question on day two of the three-day Kautilya Economic Conclave organised by the Ministry of Finance and the Institute of Economic Growth. Calling for strategic self-reliance, Das said self-reliance or Atmanirbharta should not mean isolation. Rather, it stands for building stronger domestic capabilities while remaining integrated with global markets and concluding more free trade agreements, he said. Das underlined that Indias real GDP grew by an impressive 7.8 in Q1 of 2026-27, adding that if the period from July-September 2025-26 to April-June 2026-27 is taken into account, real GDP growth in India just exceeds 8. This resonates with my statement to Financial Times London a few months ago that India is within a striking distance of 8 growth, he said. Reforms undertaken over the past decade were not one-off measures but were designed to build buffers that would help the economy absorb disruptions and recover rapidly, he said. Indias resilience is not accidental. It is the outcome of broad and mutually reinforcing reforms, he said. The former Reserve Bank of India governor cited flexible inflation targeting, the introduction of the goods and services tax, fiscal prudence, the push for digital payments and banking sector reforms among such measures. On the external front, Das said Indias financial sector and prudent management had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. External sector indicators have remained broadly resilient, supported by export diversification, free trade agreements, a sustained surplus in services trade and steady inward remittances, he said. Going ahead, Das said India must harness the artificial intelligence AI revolution to sustain high growth. Indias AI strategy rests on two complementary pillars. First, sovereign AI capability through investments in indigenous foundation models, high-performance computing infrastructure, semiconductor developments and robust innovation ecosystem, he said. He also called for deepening the financial sector to support Indias expanding economic weight. While Indias financial sector has evolved significantly, the next phase of growth will require strengthening of long-term finance and patient capital, Das said. This would require further deepening of the corporate bond market, pension and insurance funds, municipal finance and innovative infrastructure financing, he added.

articleTitle: Why are thousands of French students protesting, and why is Macron worried?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: france protests
description: France student protests have spread across high schools, with clashes, arrests and disruptions reported amid demands for better education facilities and funding.
body_raw: Thousands of students have blocked high schools across France in a protest movement rattling President Emmanuel Macrons government in recent days to protest the state of education, triggering violent clashes and riots with police. The Paris police chief has said that student protests have spread across the country and are now out of control. Since the protests began last week, dozens of people have been wounded, and nearly 5,000 have been arrested, officials said, adding that most of those held are minors. According to spokesperson for Frances national police Agathe Foucault, more than 600 police officers have also been injured. Riot police clash with students as teachers join protests The riot police clashed with high school students on Friday, and the unions in the country called for teachers to strike as the administration struggled to contain the violent protests being held over classroom conditions and funding in the education sector, Reuters reported. Property damage from the protests is estimated at tens of millions of euros. Over 400 schools closed as protests disrupt education Because of massive protests, one-third of Frances nearly 3,700 high schools were closed or disrupted on Thursday, while more than 400 schools were closed on Friday, France education minister Edouard Geffray said, the New York Times reported. To extend solidarity with protesters, the teachers union and some political figures have joined the movement. Macron government condemns urban violence The French government has said that some of the demands raised by the students are legitimate but condemned urban violence and accused France Unbowed, a far-left party, of endorsing the protest movement. However, the party has rejected the allegations. In an open letter published on X, Paris police chief Patrice Faure said that those who launched the demonstration no longer controlled it, and called on protesting students to abandon school blockades and unrest in favour of peaceful forms of protest. Saying that parents also have a responsibility to keep their children away from the influence of professional rioters, Faure said, It is time to return to peaceful forms of action. This comes as the student union is planning to return to the barricades for a national day of demonstrations on Tuesday. Why are French students protesting? Enlisting some of the reasons behind the student demonstrations across France, a student union which is part of the movements main organisers said Overcrowded classrooms Crumbling infrastructure Overloaded schedules Unfunded schools Shortage of teachers and staff Education is a right, not a privilege Protest slogans Some of the placards held by the students during the demonstration read Too many inequalities, were disgusted, Education is a right, not a privilege, Were not poorly educated, were just not listened to, and Sorry to bother, its for our future.

articleTitle: Army officer died of illness. On way home with body, family loses 3 more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Army officer family killed Purvanchal expressway
description: The body of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh was being taken from Chandigarh to Deoria when the ambulance hit a parked truck on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur.
body_raw: An Army officers three family members were killed when an ambulance carrying his body met with an accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur district early on Sunday. The ambulance driver also died in the accident. The police suspect that the ambulance hit a parked truck on the expressway. The police said the ambulance was carrying the body of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh, 50, a resident of Rudrapur in Deoria who was posted in Meerut. He had been receiving treatment for kidney disease at the Command Hospital in Chandigarh. The police identified the victims as the Army officers brother Ram Samujh, son Gaurav Singh, nephew Rajan Singh, and the ambulance driver, Jaspal. The impact of the accident was so severe that the front portion of the ambulance was mangled. Two people seated in the front, including the driver, died on the spot. Their bodies were trapped inside the wreckage and had to be extricated by cutting open the vehicle. The others died during treatment at a government hospital in Ayodhya. The bodies have been sent for postmortem examination. District Magistrate Indrajeet Singh said the bodies would be sent to Deoria after the completion of formalities. We are coordinating with officials in Deoria and the Army to facilitate the process, he added. According to the Sultanpur police, they received information from the police control room on Sunday morning about an ambulance accident involving an unidentified vehicle on the Purvanchal Expressway. A police team reached the spot and rushed the injured occupants to a hospital, where doctors declared them dead. Other family members of the officer were travelling in a separate vehicle that was following the ambulance.

articleTitle: 2 killed, van torched over cattle theft suspicion near Bengal’s Siliguri
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengal cattle theft mob attack
description: The West Bengal Police have launched a probe to identify the perpetrators of the mob violence.
body_raw: Two men were killed and three others injured after a violent mob allegedly attacked a group accused of cattle theft near West Bengals Siliguri during the early hours of Friday. The incident unfolded between 2.30 am and 3 am when a crowd began chasing four to five men suspected of stealing cattle in the Matigara and Bagdogra areas. The chase spanned from Tarabari in Matigara to Dhimal Basti in Bagdogra, where the victims were allegedly cornered and assaulted. Near the Balason River in the Tarabari area, under the jurisdiction of Matigara police station, a pickup van was allegedly intercepted and set ablaze by the mob. The driver of the vehicle, identified as Md Shahid Akhtar, 45, a resident of Chopra in West Bengal, was dragged out and beaten to death on the spot, the local police confirmed. A second victim, identified as Shad Mohammad alias Sajjad Mohammad from Haryana, 28, succumbed to multiple severe injuries while undergoing treatment at the North Bengal Medical College and Hospital. Police rescue victims, launch search for accused Police personnel rescued three injured victims from the scene and transported them to the hospital, while one person managed to escape the attack and sought refuge inside a nearby police station. We are trying to trace the accused. So far, no one has been arrested. The case has been filed based on a complaint filed by the dead persons wife, Syed Waquar Raza, Commissioner of Police of Siliguri, told The Indian Express. The FIR includes charges of murder by mob, voluntarily causing grievous hurt, mischief causing property damage, and mischief by fire or explosive substance. According to the police, a family member of one of the victims acknowledged that the men were allegedly involved in cattle smuggling and had previously visited the area. Investigations remain ongoing to identify and apprehend the perpetrators of the violence.

articleTitle: RBI likely to raise rates: Why inflation, crude and global rates matter
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI
description: Most analysts expect the RBI to raise the policy rate, repo rate, by 25 basis points (bps) to 5.50%, potentially marking the beginning of a more aggressive rate-hiking cycle. Here is why.
body_raw: After nearly two years of monetary accommodation, the Reserve Bank of India RBI appears poised to begin withdrawing policy support, with the Monetary Policy Committee MPC expected to take the first steps at its October 7 meeting. Most analysts expect the RBI to raise the policy rate, repo rate, by 25 basis points bps to 5.50, potentially marking the beginning of a more aggressive rate-hiking cycle. Such a move would push up borrowing costs across the economy, raising interest rates on deposits as well as loans, including personal, home and vehicle loans. The MPC could also revise its projections for GDP growth and inflation, with both likely to be higher than previously estimated. Why the RBI rate hike now? The central banks August MPC minutes had already indicated such a move. Since then, incoming data on domestic inflation and growth, coupled with a global backdrop of higher US interest rates, bond yields and commodity prices, has left little room for the RBI to wait. The US Federal Reserve recently raised its policy rate by 25 bps to 3.75-4. US benchmark yields have also risen sharply, by 49 bps to 5.27 and by 25 bps to 7.21 over the past month. After holding through 2026, the RBI faces growing pressure to raise rates at its October review, and a 25-basis point hike to 5.50 is now a real possibility, which would be the first increase since early 2023, said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings. In our baseline, the RBI hikes by 25 bps in each of October and December to a terminal rate of 5.75, though there is some risk of a one-and-done hike, Nomura Global Market Research said. Market expectations are now converging on two themes removal of liquidity and RBI rate hikes, said Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist, HSBC Global Investment Research. There are also analysts who expect the RBI to hold rates. The RBI may not move rates in October, but it may move the markets expectations. The policy decision could remain unchanged even as the policy message becomes incrementally cautious, said Sneha Pandey, Fund Manager, Fixed Income, Quantum AMC. Inflation getting broad-based Domestically, retail inflation is showing signs of becoming more broad-based. Price pressures are being driven by elevated energy prices and a rise in food inflation, while the impact of El Nino-related disruptions is becoming increasingly visible. Maharashtra has declared drought in about 265 of the states 358 talukas, covering nearly 74 of the state. The Union Agriculture Minister has also flagged the possibility of drought in other states, including Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan. Lower reservoir levels, weather-related disruptions and higher energy prices are adding to inflationary pressures. Reservoir levels across India are about 20 below last years levels, which could also affect the rabi crop. The possibility of El Nino conditions extending into 2027 remains a key monitorable. Besides, global headwinds continue to weigh on the outlook. The conflict in West Asia and the Russia-Ukraine war have added to economic uncertainty, while crude oil prices have risen above 100 a barrel, raising concerns over imported inflation and the impact on the countrys external balance. CareEdge Ratings projects retail inflation to peak at 6 in the third quarter and average around 5 in FY27. Weather-related risks and volatile energy prices remain the key risks, it said. Retail inflation which was at 4.82 in August, is expected to be around 5.5. It could remain above 5 for nearly three quarters. With WPIPPI inflation around 10, elevated crude oil prices and the possibility of a strong El Nino, markets have begun pricing in the prospect of rate hikes. With inflation rising and gaining breadth, and global interest rates and yields remaining elevated, the backdrop has become risky for India to allow the interest-rate differential with the US to narrow further. Food inflation is becoming increasingly broad-based and moving beyond typical perishable prices. The increase in wholesale inflation is slowly spilling over into farming and non-farming sectors, creating a large wedge between CPI and WPI inflation, Bank of America Securities economists Rahul Bajoria and Smriti Mehra said. Whats the impact of an RBI rate hike? If the repo rate rises, lending and deposit rates are expected to increase in near term. Loans linked to external benchmarks - particularly those directly linked to the repo rate - will see the impact almost immediately. Borrowers with such loans could see their equated monthly instalments EMIs rise, increasing their repayment burden. Interest rates on loans linked to the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate MCLR are also likely to rise. Banks have the flexibility to revise MCLR-based lending rates depending on their funding costs, liquidity conditions and deposit mobilisation. On the deposit side, rates are also expected to rise marginally. However, a sharper or sustained increase would depend on changes in liquidity and funding conditions that prompt banks to reassess deposit pricing. The RBIs likely shift to a rate-hike cycle comes when the economy is facing a combination of rising inflationary pressures, elevated crude oil prices, tighter global financial conditions and strong domestic growth. The move would help contain demand and inflation expectations, but could also weigh on consumption and investment if borrowing costs remain elevated for an extended period. Will the growth forecast be revised? The Indian economy remained resilient in the first quarter of FY27, with GDP growth coming in at a better-than-expected 7.8 despite a challenging global environment. Consumption, investment and robust export growth supported the momentum, while high-frequency indicators such as GST collections, auto sales and bank credit remained healthy. Following the strong Q1 growth momentum, we now project FY27 growth at 7.3, CareEdge Ratings said. It expects the RBI to raise its GDP growth projection closer to its estimate, from the central banks previous forecast of 6.7. In the August review, MPC marginally raised its GDP growth forecast for FY27 to 6.7 from 6.6 and lowered its inflation projection to 5 from 5.1, indicating that it expected price pressures to moderate over the course of the year despite near-term risks. The stronger-than-expected Q1 print, however, has changed the starting point for the full-year growth outlook. A higher-than-expected first-quarter performance means that even if growth moderates in the remaining quarters, the annual average could still come in above the RBIs existing projection. This raises the possibility of an upward revision in the central banks growth forecast. There are, however, risks to the outlook. Higher crude oil prices, elevated global interest rates, geopolitical tensions, trade-policy uncertainty and weather-related disruptions could weigh on growth in the coming quarters. Growth is likely to moderate in the second half of FY27.

articleTitle: 3 years after Umesh Pal murder, UP Police trace wanted accused to Bihar jail
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Umesh Pal murder case
description: The Uttar Pradesh Police are moving court for a warrant to bring Mohammad Arman from Bihar's Gaya jail to Prayagraj in connection with the February 2023 Umesh Pal murder case.
body_raw: Three years after advocate Umesh Pal and his two police security personnel were shot dead in Prayagrajs Dhoomanganj area, the Uttar Pradesh Police have traced a wanted accused carrying a reward of Rs 5 lakh to a jail in Bihar. The police said the accused, Mohammad Arman, was allegedly associated with the gang of slain Prayagraj mafia figure Atiq Ahmed. The Uttar Pradesh Police had been searching for Arman for the past three years after his alleged role in the murder of advocate Umesh Pal and his two security personnel emerged during the investigation. Arman was allegedly riding the motorcycle on which another wanted accused, Guddu Muslim, was travelling as a pillion rider. A senior police officer said they learnt about a week ago that Arman was lodged in a jail in Bihars Gaya district in connection with an old case. A police team subsequently verified the information with their counterparts in Gaya. We will approach the Prayagraj court on Monday seeking a B-warrant to bring him to Prayagraj in connection with the murder of Umesh Pal and his two security personnel, the senior police officer said. The police said that during the preliminary inquiry, they learnt that after the murder of Umesh Pal and his two security personnel, Arman went to Gaya and surrendered before a court in connection with an old firing case after getting his bail cancelled. He has remained lodged in Gaya jail since then. During the preliminary inquiry, police found that Arman, a native of Bihar, allegedly ran a food stall in Prayagrajs Civil Lines area, where he came into contact with associates of Atiq Ahmed who visited the stall. Police said he later began working with Atiq Ahmed and expanded his business with money he allegedly earned through criminal activities. Arman is among the six accused wanted in connection with the murder of advocate Umesh Pal and his two police security personnel on February 24, 2023, in Prayagrajs Dhoomanganj area. Umesh Pal was attacked as he got out of his car near the entrance to his house. The assailants opened fire and hurled bombs at him and his two police bodyguards before fleeing the spot in a vehicle. Four accused killed in encounters The police have so far gunned down four accused in the case in crossfire. Atiq Ahmed and his younger brother Ashraf, also accused in the case, were shot dead in April 2023 while they were in police custody, in an incident that was broadcast live on television. Among the six wanted persons are three members of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmeds family - his wife Shaista Parveen, sister-in-law Zainab Fatima Ashrafs wife and elder sister Ayesha Noori. Shaista Parveen carries a reward of Rs 50,000, while a reward of Rs 25,000 has been announced for Ayesha Noori. Two other wanted accused in the case, Guddu Muslim and Sabir, carry a reward of Rs 5 lakh each for information leading to their arrest. Umesh Pal was a witness in the murder case of Bahujan Samaj Party BSP MLA Raju Pal, who was shot dead in Prayagraj in 2005, in which Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf were accused.

articleTitle: Himachal man who trafficked drugs from Europe by post gets 10-year jail
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Himachal drug trafficking Pankaj Sharma
description: The convict was arrested after he accepted a consignment that the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) used in a controlled-delivery operation.
body_raw: A special court in Himachal Pradesh convicted a Solan resident on Saturday in a drug-trafficking case involving consignments sourced from the United Kingdom, France, and Germany, sentencing him to 10 years rigorous imprisonment and imposing a fine of Rs 1 lakh. Special Judge Abhay Mandiyal convicted Pankaj Sharma in a case registered on July 4, 2023, in which a team from the Narcotics Control Bureau NCB arrested him for possessing a commercial quantity of MDMA. The NCB action followed intelligence that an international postal parcel originating from the UK was suspected to contain narcotic drugs. After obtaining requisite authorisation, the NCB team recovered the original contents of the parcel, which included 4.7 grams of cocaine, and used it in a controlled-delivery operation at the Head Post Office in Solan. Under Section 50A of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, authorities may allow a consignment containing narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances to continue to its destination under surveillance so they can identify and arrest the people involved in the wider trafficking network. Sharma took delivery of the parcel and was apprehended on the spot. The NCB team also intercepted a parcel from France that Sharma was receiving at the same time. The search resulted in the recovery and seizure of 56.2 grams of MDMA-more than five times the commercial-quantity threshold prescribed for the drug, an NCB officer said. The officer added, The investigation subsequently led the agency to identify a third international parcel originating from Germany and intended for delivery to Sharma. The parcel was intercepted, resulting in the recovery of another 4.4 grams of cocaine. Further investigation revealed that Sharma was procuring narcotic drugs through international postal channels from multiple European countries. The NCB subsequently filed a complaint before the special judge on December 19, 2023. During the trial, the prosecution relied on the testimony of postal witnesses, delivery and identification records, seizure proceedings, malkhana records and scientific evidence to establish Sharmas conscious possession of the contraband. However, the court acquitted Sharma of charges related to manufacturing drugs and the illegal import, export, and transhipment of narcotics. The NCB appealed to the public to report suspected drug trafficking through the MANAS National Narcotics Helpline at 1933, assuring confidentiality of informants.
