articleTitle: Ambedkar University Delhi revises attendance guidelines for PhD scholars amid students’ protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ambedkar University Delhi revises attendance guidelines for PhD scholars amid students' protest
description: The university's July 31 notification had introduced attendance requirements for full-time PhD scholars receiving fellowships, which had led to concerns among research scholars over restrictions on their academic and research-related activities.
body_raw: Ambedkar University Delhi has revised its guidelines for full-time PhD scholars receiving fellowships, superseding an office order issued on July 31 that had triggered a protest by students. The universitys July 31 notification had introduced attendance requirements for full-time PhD scholars receiving fellowships, which had led to concerns among research scholars over restrictions on their academic and research-related activities. The Ambedkar University administration has now said that the notification has been superseded by the revised office order issued on September 30, which provides greater flexibility while requiring scholars to attend coursework and seminars and maintain academic engagement and research progress. Attendance records will be maintained by the research supervisor and programme coordinator and verified by the dean of the concerned school. The research supervisor will also be responsible for ensuring satisfactory academic engagement and progress of the scholars research work under the overall guidance of the dean, the administration said. Also Read DU relaxes 28-credit promotion rule What changes for students The guidelines are purely academic in nature and in line with UGC regulations and practices followed by other central and state universities, it said, adding that the objective was to strengthen the research ecosystem and ensure participation of research scholars in academic and research activities. The clarification comes amid a week-long protest at the university by students associated with AISA on the attendance issue, campus restrictions, access to facilities and other demands. The situation had escalated late Friday night after protesters alleged that security personnel restricted the entry of food and water and that a student who collapsed around 3 am faced delays in medical evacuation. The university, however, said its medical team was continuously monitoring the health of protesting students and providing necessary medical assistance. The All India Students Association AISAhad also alleged that students were subsequently denied access to the campus, affecting those attending classes and examinations. The university said the library, laboratories and certain other blocks had been closed for maintenance and safety purposes and that students had been informed in advance. The administration said the indefinite sit-in was being held without prior permission and that a designated space had been provided for peaceful protests. It also alleged that some protesting students had manhandled security guards, a matter which it said had been brought to the notice of Delhi Police. Also Read Rs 1,668 Crore investment approved for Ambedkar Universitys futuristic new campus in Dheerpur AISA has demanded removal of the physical barriers, restoration of what it describes as campus democracy, accountability over the alleged obstruction of emergency medical access and unrestricted entry for all registered students. In its latest statement, the university appealed to students and other stakeholders against spreading misinformation and said it remained open to dialogue and clarification. Many students and their guardians have placed their hope, future and career in this University, the administration said, urging all stakeholders to avoid creating panic or tarnishing the institutions image through misleading information.

articleTitle: FSSAI declares ‘low-fat dairy whitener’ unsafe at top Delhi hotel — note the risks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Is your dairy whitener adulterated?
description: A dairy whitener is not milk. It is a processed food designed to look and feel like milk, and the real health question is what it adds to the diet when it is used several times a day
body_raw: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India recently issued a non-compliance notice and banned the sale of Nestles Low Fat Dairy Whitener after a sample taken from a Delhi hotel was declared unsafe and substandard. Taking to X, the regulatory body shared A sample of Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener collected from Ms Bharat Hotels Ltd. The Lalit, New Delhi, has been declared unsafe and substandard by Food Analyst reports under the FSS Act, 2006. A sample of Nestl Low Fat Dairy Whitener collected from Ms Bharat Hotels Ltd. The Lalit, New Delhi, has been declared UNSAFE amp SUBSTANDARD by Food Analyst reports under the FSS Act 2006. Directives have been issued to immediately prohibit the sale of product FSSAINotice - FSSAI fssaiindia October 3, 2026 What exactly makes it risky? We reached out to Kanikka Malhotra, clinical nutritionist and diabetes educator, who shares that whatever the adjudication decides, this story should make us look at the cup, not just the lab report. A dairy whitener is not milk. It is a processed food designed to look and feel like milk, and the real health question is what it adds to the diet when it is used several times a day, she tells indianexpress.com, adding that phosphorus is the key point to understand. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. It is a nutrient our bodies need, and it occurs naturally in milk, pulses and nuts. But the phosphorus in food and the phosphorus in additives behave differently in the body, she says, further stressing that naturally occurring phosphorus is bound in protein and phytate, so we absorb only about half of it. Phosphate additives, used as stabilisers and emulsifiers, are absorbed almost completely. Therefore, a cup of tea with a whitener sachet is a small dose, but three or four cups a day, every day, are not. Who is at risk? Malhotra says this matters most for people whose kidneys are already under strain. Diabetes is a leading cause of chronic kidney disease in India, and when kidney function falls, the body struggles to clear surplus phosphate. High phosphate levels are linked to vascular calcification and heart risk in people with kidney disease, she elaborated. In the general population, the evidence for harm from phosphate additives is largely observational, so Malhotra says she would not overstate it. But for diabetic and kidney-risk clients, it is reason enough to be cautious, she adds in warning. As for the brand in focus, Malhotra adds Nestle has said that its product is compliant and that the labs reading reflects total phosphorus, which includes the natural contribution of milk. That is a technical question for the regulator and the company to settle, and consumers should wait for the outcome. How can you make sure your dairy whitener is safe? Malhotra shares some practical advice to tackle this problem Use fresh milk or plain curd-based options whenever you can. Read the ingredient list for phosphate or INS numbers such as 338 to 343 and 450 to 452. If you have diabetes, kidney disease or high blood pressure, ask your doctor how much additive phosphate is appropriate for you. Good health is rarely lost in one dramatic exposure. It is shaped by small things repeated every day, and the humble cup of tea is one of them, she concludes. articleTitle: Akmal slams Ayub’s celebration after Sooryavanshi’s wicket: ‘Doing things for social media’

body_raw: Pakistan off-spinner Saim Ayub took the wicket of Indian teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Saturday in the gold medal match of the Asian Games 2026, and after the wicket, Ayub immediately made a baby cradle gesture. These things have been happening for a long time. Our performance hasnt been great, but we are doing things for social media, Akmal said on sports discussion show. After being one of the youngest ever Indians to play First-Class cricket, Sooryavanshi was swooped up by the Rajasthan Royals for Rs 1 crore ahead of the IPL 2025 season. articleTitle: Why TVK joins INDIA bloc, hits pause on Vijay as PM face
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay
description: TVK's move to formally join the national Opposition alliance led by its key Tamil Nadu ally Congress pushes DMK further into a corner and with fewer allies
body_raw: For Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, joining the INDIA bloc was less a dramatic turn than the formal acknowledgement of where Tamil Nadus post-election arithmetic had already taken him. His Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK governs the state with the Congress as an ally. The VCK and IUML are also part of the arrangement that enabled Vijay to form the government after TVK won 108 seats, short of the 118 needed for an absolute majority. A national third front has not taken shape. Remaining outside the BJP-led NDA while simultaneously keeping away from the principal national Opposition grouping was becoming an increasingly narrow political space. On Saturday, TVK stepped out of it. TVK representatives Aadhav Arjuna and Marie Wilson attended an INDIA bloc meeting at the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee headquarters in Chennai, alongside the CPI, CPIM, VCK, MDMK and IUML. Tamil Nadu Congress chief president Manickam Tagore declared that Vijays party had formally joined the alliance, calling it a historic day. More questions than answers The announcement settles one question but opens several others-including where the DMK, until recently the principal Tamil Nadu component of the national Opposition alliance, now fits. The immediate occasion was electoral rolls rather than alliance arithmetic. The parties adopted resolutions against the Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and announced demonstrations across Tamil Nadu on October 13 and 14, followed by a larger Chennai protest on October 15. The TVK is expected to participate. Whether Vijay himself will attend remains unclear. Until recently, even this relationship had remained deliberately undefined. Tagore had maintained that the TVK could not technically be treated as an INDIA bloc constituent because it had no representation in Parliament. The party was not invited to the INDIA blocs national meeting in New Delhi last week. Saturday therefore marked a change not merely in TVKs position but in the Congresss willingness to recognise it formally. For Vijay, the move also provides a national structure for an alliance that already exists at home. The Congress has five MLAs and is part of the TVK-led government. The next Lok Sabha election in 2029 now provides a larger horizon an INDIA bloc arrangement potentially gives TVK a framework for negotiating parliamentary seats without having to construct another national partnership from scratch. Vijay-for-PM plans on hold Inside the TVK, that transition has also required some message control. According to senior party sources, the leadership has instructed functionaries before the by-election campaign not to project Vijay as a future prime ministerial candidate. Resources that had been going towards Instagram reels and social-media material presenting Vijay in that role have also been curtailed, a senior TVK leader told The Indian Express. The intervention is partly practical. The TVK is fighting immediate Assembly by-elections Vijay is barely months into his first term as Chief Minister. The national ambition can wait. Politics occasionally requires social media to observe seniority. DMKs dilemma The more consequential effect of Saturdays decision may instead be on the DMK. After losing power, the party has found itself without the coalition structure that surrounded it before the Assembly election. The CPI and CPIM, now contesting the by-elections independently after distancing themselves from Vijays alliance, might under different circumstances have found a return to the DMK politically natural. The TVKs entry into INDIA complicates that route. The Left parties attended Saturdays meeting alongside the TVK. So did the VCK and MDMK. In other words, the national Opposition platform now contains several parties whose Tamil Nadu relationships are considerably less tidy than their seating arrangement at the Congress office suggested. That distinction, between a national alliance and a state alliance, will matter increasingly. The INDIA bloc gives its members a common national opponent in the BJP without automatically resolving who should fight whom in Tamil Nadu. For the Congress, however, Vijay is already its governing partner. For the TVK, Congress provides both legislative support today and a potential bridge to parliamentary politics in 2029. Slim chances for Third Front For the DMK, the situation is more awkward. Its leaders can continue engaging INDIA parties nationally, but Vijays formal arrival means the coalition can no longer be assumed to be a political space in which the DMK is Tamil Nadus default representative. Recent contacts by DMK deputy general secretary Kanimozhi with non-Congress INDIA leaders had also triggered speculation about whether another Opposition configuration could emerge. But without the Congress, and with several potential partners now sitting at an INDIA table that includes the TVK, the room for a viable third formation appears limited. The irony is that Vijay entered the Assembly election as the leader of a new party arguing against Tamil Nadus established political arrangements. Five months after the result, governing has steadily required arrangements of its own. First came the partners needed for a majority. Now comes a national coalition. Saturdays meeting did not resolve all of those contradictions. It merely gave them a name INDIA bloc.

articleTitle: Unchecked high-rises strain Pune: PIL challenges rules permitting more construction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: pune high rise, construction, indian express
description: A bench of the Bombay High Court has issued notices to the Maharashtra government, Pune civic body, and the central pollution control body after prominent Pune citizens, including former MP Vandana Chavan, filed a petition to halt extra FSI provisions.
body_raw: As Pune witnesses rapid vertical growth driven partly by redevelopment, concerns over liveability and civic infrastructure have prompted a group of prominent citizens to petition the Bombay High Court. The petition challenges rules that permit increased real estate construction and seeks to abolish additional buildable potential to prevent severe urban strain. The matter requires consideration. The court and the petitioners issue notices to the Maharashtra government, Pune Municipal Corporation PMC and the Central Pollution Control Board CPCB, stated a bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna in its order on the petition. Former Rajya Sabha MP and ex-mayor Vandana Chavan filed the petition along with prominent citizens Vijay Paranjpye, Ajit Abhyankar, Vishwambhar Choudhari, and Abhay Chhajed. It challenges the provisions allowing extra real estate construction through additional Floor Space Index FSI under the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations, 2020 UDCPR 2020. The petitioners argue that these regulations were introduced without essential prior evaluations-including regional carrying capacity, infrastructure adequacy, environmental impact, and public liveability- rendering them arbitrary, unconstitutional, and environmentally unsustainable. Pointing out that Pune already faces acute deficits in water supply, sewage treatment, waste management, open spaces, and traffic control alongside rising pollution, heatwaves, and flooding, they warned that unscientific densification will aggravate public health and safety risks. Call to revert to 2017 rules pending studies The petition appeals to the High Court to quash the chapters of UDCPR 2020 that allow extra FSI for construction in Pune and order the temporary implementation of the 2017 Development Control Rules instead. The petitioners contend that the PMC should be permitted to implement additional FSI provisions only after conducting comprehensive impact studies. The court should issue direction to restrain the PMC from issuing any development permissions under UDCPR 2020 till detailed studies on the regions carrying capacity are carried out, which should include population density projections, infrastructure and utilities capacity assessment, public utilities and infrastructure capacity study and deficit analysis, traffic and transportation network study, environment and climate impact assessment, urban heat island effect and disaster risk mitigation, socio-economic impact evaluations, geotechnical and structural feasibility study, natural features, biodiversity and sustainability studies, said Chavan. The petition further requests the court to restrain the PMC from granting development permissions for Transit Oriented Development TOD without completing a city-wide impact assessment and finalising local area plans, and to stay UDCPR chapters on FSI increases in the interim. Ecological and structural risks While UDCPR 2020 incentivises the redevelopment of old, dilapidated, or dangerous buildings by offering higher FSI, the petitioners warned that this approach carries hidden structural and environmental costs. They noted that UDCPR-driven growth leads to taller structures requiring deeper foundation excavations for underground parking. This process threatens to cut into crucial underground aquifers while significantly worsening construction and demolition waste disposal across the city.

articleTitle: 54 years, five languages, zero repetitions: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao was one of a kind
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao
description: In a career spanning 54 years and five languages, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao attempted things no other Indian filmmaker dared to try: A dialogue-free comedy, a time-travel science fiction, a high-fantasy adventure rooted in folklore. And at 94, a musical fantasy.
body_raw: The easiest way to understand what Singeetham Srinivasa Rao meant to Indian cinema is to list what he did and then try to find another filmmaker who did the same. He made a film without dialogue. He made a film with a time machine. He made a film set on a mythical island ruled by a sorcerer. He made a film about a classical dancer who lost her leg and returned to the stage. He made a film where the comedy was entirely physical, entirely visual, entirely dependent on the audiences ability to follow a story through images alone. And then, at 94, he made one more film because he was not done. Find another Indian filmmaker who did all of this. Not one of these. All of these. Across five languages. Across six decades. Without a single repetition. You will not find one. Because there is no one else. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, who died at Kauvery Hospital in Chennai on Saturday night at the age of 94, was not merely an experimental filmmaker. He was the filmmaker against whom every other attempt at innovation in Indian cinema must be measured, and one who, measured against anyone else, invariably comes out ahead. Also Read Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dies at 94 The experiment nobody believed in The story of Pushpaka Vimanam is the story of Singeetham Srinivasa Rao in miniature. A filmmaker walks into a room and says I want to make a film with no dialogue. Not a silent film. A film with sound, music, ambient noise, everything except spoken words. The story will be told entirely through images. In 1987, this was not a pitch that anyone wanted to hear. Indian cinema, in every language, was built on dialogue. Take away dialogue, and you take away the scaffolding that the entire commercial film industry stood on. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao could not find a producer. Nobody wanted to fund a film that could not be marketed with a single quotable line. So he produced it himself, partnering with Shringar Nagaraj, a Kannada producer who was willing to take the risk. The idea for the film came to Singeetham while he was in the shower. He wrote the screenplay in two weeks. Also Read Made for Rs 15 lakh, Kamal Haasan, Singeethams pathbreaking film earned 6.6x its budget The result was a black comedy starring Kamal Haasan, Amala and Tinnu Anand that told a complex, funny and emotionally engaging story without a single word being spoken on screen. Because there was no dialogue, the film did not need dubbing. It was released simultaneously across all Indian languages under different titles Pushpaka Vimana in Kannada, Pushpaka Vimanam in Telugu, Pushpak in Hindi. Same film. Same audio track. Every audience understood it. The film won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. The time machine nobody expected Four years later, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao did it again. This time, the experiment was science fiction. Aditya 369, starring Nandamuri Balakrishna and Mohini, was the first Telugu film to feature a time machine. The concept was inspired by H.G. Wells The Time Machine, which Singeetham had read during his college years at the University of Madras. The film sent its characters back in time to the court of Sri Krishnadevaraya in the Vijayanagara Empire, mixing historical drama with futuristic technology in a way that nobody in Telugu cinema had attempted before. The film was presented by S.P. Balasubrahmanyam, the legendary playback singer who was also Singeetham Srinivasa Raos frequent collaborator. The combination of talents was extraordinary, but the concept was the real risk. In 1991, Telugu cinema was defined by family dramas, action films and romantic comedies. Science fiction was not a genre anyone believed the audience would accept. However, they accepted it. The film that proved the audience was willing to go wherever the filmmaker took them, as long as the maker knew where he was going. Singeetham always knew. Thirty-five years later, time travel is a common device in Telugu cinema. The lineage traces back to Aditya 369 and, by extension, to a filmmaker who read HG Wells in a Madras university library and decided that Telugu cinema deserved a time machine. The fantasy world nobody had built Bhairava Dweepam was the third experiment in three consecutive decades, each in a different genre, each doing something Indian cinema had not done before. Also Read Sing Geetham movie review At 94, Singeetam Srinivasa Rao delivers a musical fable The film, starring Balakrishna, was a high-fantasy adventure set on a mystical island ruled by a malevolent sorcerer seeking immortality. It drew from Indian folklore, mythology and adventure storytelling to create a world that was entirely self-contained its own geography, its own rules, its own visual language. The screenplay was co-written with Raavi Kondala Rao, one of Telugu literatures most respected writers, and produced under the Chandamama Vijaya Pictures banner. In 1994, Indian cinema did not make high-fantasy films. The genre was considered too expensive, too risky and too unfamiliar for audiences raised on realism-adjacent commercial cinema. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao ignored all of that. He built the island. He populated it with wizards, warriors and magical creatures. He created set pieces that were elaborate by any standard, let alone the standards of a mid-budget Telugu film in the early 1990s. Bhairava Dweepam completed a 100-day theatrical run in 28 centres. It proved a full two decades, before Baahubali made high fantasy commercially viable on a massive scale, that Telugu audiences were ready for mythology, magic and world-building. They just needed a filmmaker who was willing to try. The biography that changed lives Before the dialogue-free comedy, before the time machine, before the fantasy island, there was Mayuri. The film that made Singeetham Srinivasa Raos name and, in the process, changed a young womans life. Mayuri was inspired by the true story of Mumbai-based Bharatanatyam dancer Sudha Chandran, whose right leg had to be amputated after she was injured in a road accident in Tamil Nadu in 1981. Doctors fitted her with a Jaipur foot prosthetic, and Chandran returned to the stage, performing classical dance with an artificial limb. Singeetham saw the story and knew it was a film. Sudha, who had never acted, played herself. The film was a critical and commercial triumph. It was remade in Hindi as Naache Mayuri with the same cast. It launched Sudha Chandrans career as a film and television actress, a career that continues to this day. And it demonstrated that Singeetham could take a real-life story, handle it with sensitivity and turn it into a mainstream film without compromising either the storys truth or the audiences entertainment. The Tamil connection Singeetham Srinivasa Raos versatility extended beyond genres to languages. While Telugu was his primary language, his Tamil filmography includes some of the most significant films in that industrys history. Also Read Why Singeetham Srinivasa Rao banned Sing Geetham crew from referencing his masterpieces Anand, a romantic comedy starring Kamal Haasan and Revathi, was a commercial hit that was later remade in multiple languages. His collaboration with Kamal on Pushpaka Vimanam remains one of the most critically acclaimed actor-director partnerships in South Indian cinema. Magalir Mattum was a Tamil film that addressed womens issues. He also worked in Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi, making him one of the very few Indian filmmakers to direct films in five languages. The question that lingers after reviewing Singeetham Srinivasa Raos filmography is why did nobody else attempt what he did? The answer is not that other filmmakers lacked talent. It is that they lacked the specific combination of traits that Singeetham Srinivasa Rao possessed technical knowledge deep enough to execute his ideas, creative ambition wild enough to conceive them, and a stubborn indifference to whether the market was ready for them. Most filmmakers work within genres. They find what works and refine it. They make action films, or comedies, or romances, and they get better at making those specific things over time. Singeetham never did this. Each one of his films was a fresh start. Each one required learning a new visual language, a new set of production challenges and a new way of engaging with the audience. The commercial film industry does not reward this behaviour. It rewards consistency, predictability and brand identity. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao offered none of these. He offered surprise. And surprise, while thrilling for the audience, is terrifying for the people who invest money in films. The fact that he continued to find producers willing to back his experiments, decade after decade, is itself a testament to the power of his track record. The last experiment In February 2026, at the age of 94, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao announced his return to directing with Sing Geetham, a musical fantasy that marked his first film in over a decade. The project was produced by Nag Ashwin, the director of Kalki 2898 AD. Sing Geetham was completed. It was released. And it was the work of a man who, at an age when most people have forgotten what ambition feels like, walked onto a set and made one more film. Because he had one more story to tell. Because cinema was not something he did, it was something he was. Also Read Singeetham Srinivasa Rao 1931-2026 Kamal Haasan pays last respects to filmmaker Chiranjeevi, Jr NTR mourn demise The measure of the man Singeetham Srinivasa Raos career cannot be reduced to awards, it can only be understood as a body of work that is unlike any other in Indian cinema. Not because every film was a masterpiece, but every film was an attempt to do something that had not been done before. Indian cinema has produced filmmakers who are more commercially successful. It has produced filmmakers who are more critically acclaimed. It has produced filmmakers who are more consistently brilliant. But it has not produced another filmmaker who spent 54 years refusing to make the same film twice, who treated every project as a first film, who looked at the boundaries of what Indian cinema could do and, every single time, decided to step past them. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao did not push boundaries. He made the films he wanted to make, in the way he wanted to make them, for 54 years. And then, at 94, he made one more. Because one more was still not enough. That is not experimentation, that is devotion. And Indian cinema will not see its like again.

articleTitle: Born in Bihar, made in Bengal: Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep behind RoI’s Irani Cup triumph
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mukesh
description: The two seamers ran through Ranji champions Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup final, making a strong case for a India recall ahead of the Tests against New Zealand
body_raw: Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep are rarely at a loss for words. Alongside seam movement and pace, humour comes naturally to them, and never more so than when they are paired together. Yet asked when they first met, both had to rummage through their memories. They have been bowling together for so long that the answer simply would not come. Laced with wit, a riposte arrives from Mukesh. Pehli baar kab mile hataiye usko. Bas jab bhi mile hai, gale mile hai Forget when we first met. Just that whenever we did, we hugged one another. It has been nearly seven years since the pair first shared the ball in a senior domestic match - on the Christmas Day of 2019. Bowling in tandem, they took five wickets against Andhra. In the cold of Kolkata, Bengal had to settle for a draw. They would reach the final for the first time in 13 years, carried by the 67 wickets the two shared between them, but the silverware remained elusive. In the cold of Srinagar, here at the Sher-I-Kashmir stadium, the silverware is theirs. Mukeshs 633 and Akashs 325 steered Rest of India to the Irani Cup, their first since 2024, with a 167-run defeat of the defending Ranji Trophy champions, Jammu Kashmir. This was the first time we played together for Rest of India. Whenever we bowl together, it is so much fun. When something happens off the pitch from my end, I communicate it to him, and when the ball does something from his end, he comes and tells me Bhaiya, aisa kar sakte hai brother, we can do this. Saamne waale to pata chal jaata hai ki hum jab saath bowling karte hai, runs banana kitna mushkil hai the batter knows how difficult it is to score when we bowl together, says Mukesh. Akash, three years his junior, offers the quintessential younger brothers nod of agreement. Our strength has been that weve played together for quite a while against great teams and top batters. We talk through things, which makes it simple whenever theres any confusion about what to do. Sometimes conditions favour the batters, and discussing things between us makes handling those situations much easier, he adds. Their journeys run along parallel tracks. Akash, hailing from Bihars Sasaram, arrived in West Bengal in 2010 to live with his uncle. Mukesh, also from Bihar, relocated from Gopalganj a couple of years later, to help his father in his taxi business. Neither set of parents approved of their cricketing ambitions, yet both made the Bengal side, and then India. Our backstories are the same, says Mukesh. He would have continued, if not for the interjection from Akash. Our story is such that things for both of us seem to happen in parallel. Whatever happens, happens together. Dont know if this is a stroke of destiny. Hum do alag jism hai, par ek hi kismat hai we share separate bodies, but the same fortune. It is hard to explain. Even we dont understand why everything turns out so similar for us, he says. For both men, the match carried a weight beyond a single trophy. For Mukesh, who has not played for India since July 2024, it was the opportunity to raise a case against his exile. For Akash, the challenge was to prove himself fit before the selectors - two of whom monitored him closely from the sidelines - pick the team for the New Zealand series. It was his first match in nearly eight months, having recently recovered from a lower-back stress fracture. What I felt during those six months was that my body needed a break. God perhaps gave that to me in the form of an injury, and I utilized that time really well. When I went into training and understood how my body was reacting, I made full use of that period. Diet, sleep, training, skill work-I did everything systematically. The outcome of that is showing now its not like I am exerting extra strain right now just to hit 145 kmph. It is the cumulative result of what I did over those six to seven months. Its not just about what Im doing in this match today or the speed on the radar, says Akash. Mukesh arrived in rich form, having led the wicket-takers charts in the Duleep Trophy with 12 scalps. Im enjoying my bowling immensely because even in the Duleep Trophy, I was bowling with great rhythm. Things went well in the semi-final and final as well. Winning the trophy boosted morale, and in between, I took no time off. I played another fixture in the English County Championship, bowled overs, and practiced in between. That momentum carried over here because the rhythm was never disrupted. Going forward, our goal is the upcoming Ranji Trophy. We will prepare for it, train for it, and do our best to help our team win. For Rest of India, the wait for a title was a mere two years.The task ahead is much steeper. Bengal have not won the Ranji Trophy since 1990. Should the pair keep bowling as they did in the valley on Sunday, though, they are entitled to dream.

According to the Federal Aviation Administration FAA, the Coast Guard was notified about the plane around 2 am local time on Saturday that the Gulfstream G100 jet, tail number CGRJP, had lost contact with air traffic controllers, reports stated. Gulfstream jet lost contact after leaving Bermuda The plane was being used as an air ambulance and had two passengers and four crew members on board when it left for an overnight flight to Massachusetts. articleTitle: We are in talks with both Russia and Ukraine: Jaishankar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JAISHANKAR
description: ‘Gone beyond advocacy, a little more involved in efforts to end conflict’
body_raw: Disclosing that India has gone beyond advocacy to be a little more involved in the efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war raging since February 2022, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said Sunday that Delhi has been in conversations with both Moscow and Kyiv, trying to be helpful on the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports and on non-attack possibilities. His remarks, at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, came days after Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said India had put forward a comprehensive and broad proposal to end the war for the first time. Jaishankar said, We are seeing today an unfortunate conflict. Our position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict, and we believe that this will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months, we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. So we have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, on energy exports, on non-attack possibilities. So those are ongoing conversations right now. He said India and Russia have historically had very good relations, particularly since the 1950s, and that history is not forgotten. For us, Russia and the Soviet Union before that was a country that stood by us in many ways when our security, when our territorial integrity was under threat. And at a time when, you know, much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us, Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and. we are obviously shaped in many ways by that legacy. Today, the relationship has widened beyond that. You know, it is again, the world has changed. We have changed. Our own relationships are not what they were in the 70s and 80s. Neither is the case with Russias, he said. So, like any relationship, it is refreshed. It undergoes a change. New issues come. Old issues sometimes get rebalanced. So it is very much more today an economic relationship as well. So there is a military component. Theres a nuclear component. There are space issues, but there is a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries, and of course, energy and resources as well. So, any country would, when you view another country, you judge it from our experiences. I cant expect Europe, for example, to look at the world and say, okay, what does India think? And my view should be based on Indias experience. Europe will base its judgement on Europes experience. India will base its judgment on Indias experience. So Indias experience has been, frankly, quite positive and consistently positive, he said. On October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas. Later that day, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Ukraines Foreign Minister Sybiha said, We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is Indias proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role. He said Ukraine is prepared to agree to an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, and is also considering an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Besides India, Ukraine has received proposals for a possible ceasefire from Turkey, Egypt and the United States. According to Sybiha, Ukraine will agree to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations, but also an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea.

articleTitle: Flare-up at SRFTI as Hindu outfit protesters hurl bricks, bottles at students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: srfti
description: Students had earlier expressed concerns to I&B Ministry over protest march, and asked Kolkata Police not to give permission for rally
body_raw: A week after clashes at Kolkatas SRFTI over an RSS-linked outfits event on the campus, tension flared up at the film institute again on Sunday evening as members of a Hindu outfit hurled bricks and bottles at the students from outside. Members of the Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch BHJM, who held a protest march, alleging insults to Swami Vivekananda and Bharat Mata by SRFTI students, also scuffled with the police as they tried to enter the SRFTI campus, leaving some of the policemen injured. According to students, they wrote to Kolkata Police and the West Bengal government on Saturday, asking them not to allow Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch to hold the march, and to deploy adequate police personnel for their safety and security. A similar letter was sent to Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw by students of FTII Pune, SRFTI Kolkata, and FTII Itanagar, expressing serious concerns over the security of students at the institutes Kolkata campus in the aftermath of the September 27 clash on the campus. On Sunday, members of the Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch reached the gates of the SRTFI on the EM Bypass and tried to enter the campus. They shouted slogans against the institute, calling the students of SRTFI Naxalites. They must be thrown out. They have insulted Bharat Maa. We will not tolerate this. They either have to love India or have to leave India, shouted a protester. Inside the campus, the students and teachers were seen deflecting the bottles and bricks thrown at them by protesters and chanting slogans like Go Back, No entry to fascists. A student of the SRFTI alleged that the protesters tore down the pictures of Dr BR Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi and instead put pictures of Bharat Maa on the gates of the institute. In a letter to the Minister of Information and Broadcasting, the students wrote, We have been informed that a rally organised by the Hindu Jagran Manch is proposed to take place on October 4 at 4 pm, approximately 800 metres from the main gate of the SRFTI. This comes barely a week after the violent confrontation on the SRFTI campus, in which several students and members of the institute community were injured. In the present circumstances, the proposed rally in such close proximity to the institute has understandably caused serious concern among the students. The SRFTI students are presently engaging with the concerned authorities to seek that the rally not be permitted within the periphery of the institute. Last Sunday, a group of students objected to an event of Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, an RSS-linked outfit, on the campus, leading to clashes. The students union of the SRFTI said that members of ABGP assaulted students and teachers and called them anti-nationals, urban naxals and terrorists. A day later, three FIRs were registered on Monday-two against unknown students and one against unknown persons. Taking suo motu cognizance of the incident, the Kolkata Police filed an FIR against unknown students. Another FIR, registered on a complaint filed by Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat ABGP, the RSS-linked outfit, also named unknown students. Only the FIR, based on a complaint lodged by SRFTI Dean Film Sukanta Majumder, was filed against unknown persons. All three FIRs more or less include BNS sections of wrongful restraint, assault on public servants, voluntarily causing harm, and criminal intimidation. It was alleged that ABGP members wrongfully restrained students and two faculty members of the institute, voluntarily caused hurt, insulted women students modesty, and also threatened them. Two days later, the BJP government in the state formed a six-member Special Investigation Team to probe the September 27 violence on the campus.

articleTitle: Why edible oils are bearing the brunt of food inflation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A large expanse of monoculture oil palm plantation in Sabah, Malaysian Borneo.
description: The combination of El Niño and Russia-Ukraine war, coupled with aggressive biofuel mandates by major producers such as Indonesia, is impacting this commodity the hardest.
body_raw: War, El Nino and national biofuel mandates-the effects of these are being felt in the global prices of food and, more so, vegetable oils. The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organizations FAO benchmark food price index averaged 136 points in September. That was the highest level for the index-a weighted average of the international prices of a basket of food commodities over a base period value taken at 100 for 2014-16-since November 2022. Even higher, within food, was FAOs index for vegetable oils. At 198.6 points, it was 18.3 up over September 2025 and the highest after the 211.8 points of June 2022. This index, as the accompanying chart shows, scaled an all-time-high of 251.8 points in March 2022 immediately after Russias invasion of Ukraine. From there, it fell to 115.8 points by June 2023, as the supply shock from the war ebbed. The last year and more have witnessed a renewed price flare-up. Blending mandates Vegetable oils-whether palm, soyabean or rapeseed-can be converted into Fatty Acid Methyl Esters FAME through a chemical process called transesterification. It involves reacting triglycerides which make up 95-98 of the fat content in vegetable oils with methanol methyl alcohol in the presence of a catalyst. FAME is basically vegetable oil-based biodiesel, which can substitute or be blended with regular diesel derived from crude petroleum oil. That is similar to ethanol-produced from sugarcane molasses and juice or rice, maize and other starch-containing cereal grains-that can be blended with petrol. According to one estimate made at the Solvent Extractors Association of Indias Globoil India 2026 conference in Mumbai last week, about 25 of the worlds production of soyabean oil, 28 of palm oil and 29 of rapeseed oil goes as feedstock for making biodiesel, i.e. FAME. That is reinforced by national biofuel mandates enforced by governments. These require oil marketing companies to blend a specified minimum percentage or volume of biofuels into fossil transportation products such as petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel ATF. Just as all petrol sold in India has to contain at least 20 ethanol, Indonesia and Malaysia have mandates for the blending of palm oil-based FAME in diesel. Indonesia introduced B20 diesel, with 20 FAME content, on a limited scale in 2016. The B20 blend was made mandatory nationwide in September 2018 and further upgraded to B30 in January 2020, B35 in August 2023 and B40 from January 2025. In July 2026, the Indonesian government raised the blend mandate to B50, with a three-month transition period. Malaysia has a less ambitious biofuel blend programme, with B10 diesel being made compulsory nationwide from September 2019 and a phased rollout of B15 beginning in June 2026. The United States is expected to produce 14.94 million tonnes mt of soyabean oil in 2026-27 October-September, out of which 8.07 mt or 54 would be directed towards biofuels. The European Union will, likewise, see 6.1 mt or 57.2 out of its total 10.67 mt rapeseed oil output being diverted for biodiesel and bio-ATF. The impact Eddy Martono, chairman of Indonesian Palm Oil Association better known as GAPKI, projects the consumption of his countrys palm oil for the production of biodiesel at 14.7 mt in 2026 and 17.4 mt in 2027. Thats up from 12.7 mt in 2025. Moving from B40 to B50 alone will, thus, absorb an additional 4.7 mt of Indonesian palm oil locally, leaving that much less for exports. This could potentially hurt countries like India, which is likely to import roughly 8 mt of palm oil in 2025-26 November-October, largely from Indonesia and Malaysia. For Indonesia, biodiesel not only creates extra domestic demand for palm oil, reducing reliance on the export market, but also helps bring down its energy import bill, an industry source pointed out. The incentive to divert palm or any other vegetable oil for biodiesel is all the more in todays environment of elevated global petroleum prices. The longer Brent crude stays above 100 per barrel, thanks to the intensifying West Asia conflict and tightening restrictions on Russian energy flows, the more the likelihood of such food-to-fuel diversion. War and weather Indonesias aggressive biofuel mandate-making it the worlds first country to implement 50 blending in diesel-comes in an El Nino year. El Nino, already in a very strong phase, is anticipated to peak during October-December and last through March-April next year. Its actual effect on palm oil production would, however, come with a lag of 8-12 months. Oil palm trees typically abort female flowers and young fruit bunches in response to water stress, which then takes time to visibly affect yields. GAPKIs Martono, for now, reckons Indonesias overall palm oil output to dip from 58.5 mt in 2026 to 56.6 mt next year. With higher domestic consumption on the back of biodiesel conversion, the worlds largest palm oil producers exports may come down from 32.3 mt in 2025 to 26.5 mt in 2027 see table. But it isnt just palm oil. Russia and Ukraine are harvesting bigger sunflowerseed crops in 2026-27 21 mt and 13 mt respectively than the previous years levels 17.5 mt and 10.7 mt. Their respective oil production is also slated to go up from 6.9 mt to 7.8 mt and 4.5 mt to 5.4 mt. For the worlds two leading sunflower producers, though, the constraint is logistical-arising from the two belligerents striking at each others port infrastructure and storage terminals. Navigation through the Sea of Azov has stopped since July 10, while operations at Black Sea ports are suspended. Alternative routes, through ports on the Baltic, Caspian and Far East seas or overland rail links, are costly and overloaded. We have a strange situation where the producers are eager to sell their ample supplies and importers want to buy, but both are helpless in the face of war, the earlier-quoted industry source noted. For India, El Nino could bring down domestic edible oil production. Our current estimate for 2026-27 is 9.2 mt, as against 9.7 mt in 2025-26. Imports will correspondingly rise from 16.8 mt to a new record of 17.2 mt. The latter would mainly comprise 8.2 mt of palm, 5 mt of soyabean, 3.5 mt of sunflower oil, said Nirav Desai, managing partner at GGN International, an Indore and Rajkot-based vegetable oil broking house-cum-research firm.

articleTitle: Surfeit of silver paints a picture of ‘what could have been’ for India at Asiad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: (Clockwise) India's Tajinderpal Singh Toor, Esha Singh, Elavenil Valarivan, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Ancy Sojan with their silver medals at 2026 Asian Games. (PTI & AP)
description: Aichi-Nagoya showed that competition has got tougher in the continent, and even personal best performances may not always be enough to challenge the cream
body_raw: Day 1 A 10.4 and 10.1 from Elavenil Valarivan on her last two shots of the 10m air rifle erased the Indians handy 1.5 lead, to see the first gold missed by India at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. What gets lost in the lament over the 27 silvers is acknowledgement that Japans Hinata Taichi shot 10.6 and 10.2 to snatch that gold - coming out of the blue, given Japan didnt have a single medal in this event since 1994. India finished tied on gold with Uzbekistan at 21, and only a last-day scramble helped push it up, with two extra silvers giving it fourth place. But all those silvers were gold medals lost. Accepting that even Indias best-ever showing in womens air rifle, Elavenils silver, might not be good enough for gold is central to understanding why the country was stuck at just four the first week, reaching double digits 10 only on the 11th day of the Games. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The ultimate tally of 21 was seven off the 2023 Asiad with 28 gold, while total medal haul was 21 less than the 106 at Hangzhou. The drop has come in several sports Shooting 22 to 15 4 golds less, Athletics 29 to 24 5 gold less, Tennis 2 to 0 1 gold less, Badminton 3 to 1 1 gold less Rowing 6 to 1 Equestrian 2 to 0 1 gold less. While archery made fantastic gains in recurve, its total count stayed constant at nine from 2023, with five gold medals, the same as last time. Squash retained its five medals, but with a significant drop of two gold. Wrestling has maintained its count of six. While men added two gold to the nil last time, and won five of the six Indian medals, womens wrestling dropped from three last time to the one silver upgrade of Antim Panghal. Sujeet Kalkal and Aman Sehrawat will be expected to carry the momentum to Los Angeles. ALSO READ As the Asian Games close, with a last-minute gold rush, India finish fourth Boxing made real gains, going up from five to six medals-and significantly three gold from none last time. The golf gold for Pranavi Urs is an uptick, as is the womens team silver. However, a few medal drops are worrying. In badminton, Lakshya Sen could not defend HS Prannoy bronze while Ayush Shetty had a poor Games. Asiad medals are toughest in badminton, and Satwik-Chirag gold was missing in the 2026 tally. Shooting sent a star-studded womens air pistol troika, but a medal was nowhere in sight after poor qualifications. While Suruchi Phogat salvaged matters with a strong comeback for the Mixed Team gold and Esha Singh fought four shoot-offs to take sports pistol silver, individual golds were out of reach till Neeru Dhanda won in trap. India had regressed in 50m 3 position since the Paris Olympics, with two silvers in the event, while they had won two gold in Hangzhou, among other medals. Hits and misses Parul Chaudhary recorded her Personal Best PB in 5,000m to take a second bronze. Steeplechaser Avinash Sable, defending a gold medal, did his seasons best but missed a medal by four seconds to finish fourth. The next rung in steeplechase isnt on the horizon. Other freakish circumstances struck. Murali Sreesankar, looking to upgrade his silver, slipped on the takeoff on his fourth attempt and was in no position to contend for gold. Two Chinese did their best in their fifth attempt to leapfrog Ancy Sojan in the long jump. The Indian could not summon a 6.60 jump, though her best this season is a national record. Hurdler Jyothi Yarraji, triple jumper Praveen Chitravel and decathlete Thowfeeq Noushad couldnt register a mark to be in contention in their events. While AFI president Adille Sumariwala had stressed that the athletes would peak at the Asiad, the periodisation seemed to have gone awry as the push for the Commonwealth Games disrupted fitness for Asiad, including taking Neeraj Chopra out of contention. The two big events within two months of each other also saw some athletes bomb at both places. The rowing federation switched up combinations two days before the race, after crews had trained together for four years. They got an Australian expert to convey the news, and he didnt explain why his plan for gold didnt come through, or why the rowers were not kept in the loop. No gold fetched up either it was chaos injected into an erstwhile well-oiled unit. Equestrian was blighted by contested selections. A gold and bronze from Hangzhou got casually tossed out, finishing at zero. Some losses are nuanced - could Gulveer Singh have focused on one event and gone all out for gold, instead of four races in five days, finishing with two silver and one bronze? Are double-starters in shooting those who are fielded in two events costing India gold? Track and field athletes scored 11 personal bests, nine silvers and three seasons bests. But the net result was one gold. It proves both that the competition has levelled up and Indians, even at their best, are only playing catch-up.

articleTitle: Disenfranchising millions arbitrary, no whataboutery can justify it: SC judge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan warns wholesale disenfranchisement under Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls violates Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution
description: “From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters' list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body,” Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said
body_raw: Amid the row over the SIR of electoral rolls against which petitions have been filed in the Supreme Court, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, a judge of the top court, said Sunday that any process that leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of the Constitution. No amount of whataboutery can justify it, he said. Justice Bhuyan said detaching an Indian citizen from the right to vote would be akin to taking out the soul from the body. Speaking at the valedictory ceremony of Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court competition at Nalsar University of Law, Hyderabad, he said, If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second-class citizens in their own country, in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order, which we have adopted under the Constitution of India, he said. Speaking on the significance of universal adult suffrage, especially in the context of India, Justice Bhuyan said, From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body. He said the earliest articulation of adult franchise in India can be traced to the Constitution of India Bill, 1895, also known as the Swaraj Bill. Speaking about the debate in the Constituent Assembly on universal adult suffrage, he said, In the draft Constitution, which was debated by the Constituent Assembly, there were two articles of relevance, though included subsequently. These were Articles 289A and 289B. Draft Article 289A became Article 325 and draft Article 289B became Article 326 of the Constitution of India. Article 326 gives meaning and content to the equality principle enshrined in Article 14. Article 325 of the Constitution of India declares that there shall be one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for election to the Lok Sabha or to the Legislature of a State no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in any such roll or claim to be included in any electoral roll for any such constituency on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or any of them. As per Article 326 of the Constitution, election to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage. In other words, every person who is a citizen of India and who is not less than 18 years of age prior to March 28, 1989, it was 21 years and who is not disqualified under the Constitution of India or by any law made by the appropriate legislature on the ground of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, shall be entitled to be registered as a voter at any such election, he said. Quoting Dr B R Ambedkar, Justice Bhuyan said, Justifying universal adult suffrage, Dr Ambedkar said since we have taken a very important decision, which practically nullifies the past, it is better that the Constitution should, in express terms, state it is the basis for insertion of Articles 289A and 289B in the draft Constitution, which are now Articles 325 and 326. Dr Ambedkars closing speech warned that the right to vote and the Indian citizens entitlement to adult suffrage should be written into the Constitution of India, instead of being left to the whims of parliamentary legislation, he said. Justice Bhuyan said, Adoption of universal adult franchise reflects the determined opinion of the Constituent Assembly that years of freedom struggle and the revolt against foreign rule made the adoption of universal adult franchise a natural choice and an essential ingredient of democracy, which we have adopted as the form of governance. Therefore, it was an act of faith for our founding fathers in the common man of India and in his pragmatism and wisdom. It was the first step taken to achieve equality in India. One may be a billionaire, and one may be a rickshaw-puller. Yet both will have their votes, and the value of their votes would be equal. Likewise, a socially high-placed temple priest on the one hand and a person belonging to the lowest strata of the society compelled to work as a manual scavenger have an equal vote with equal value. This is the transformational vision of the Indian Constitution, he said. In his concluding remarks, he congratulated Nalsar students for being what students, especially law students, should be.

articleTitle: Are all medals equally significant? The top five out of the 85
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Medals
description: A look at the podium finishes which broke new ground for India and raised hopes for even bigger honours in the future
body_raw: Asian Games 2026 Indias breakthrough medals Not all medals are equal, some carry more importance than others due to the tougher competition in the event or the historical significance of the achievement. Here are five such feats by Indians at Aichi-Nagoya Womens Hockey Gold India finished on the top of the podium when the event made its debut at the 1982 Asian Games. It took 44 years for an encore as the side led by Salima Tete and guided by Dutch coach Sjoerd Marijne put it across 2024 Paris Olympic silver medallists China in the final. What makes the achievement all the more special is that it comes with a direct berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. India had missed out on Paris after finishing narrowly outside the medals at the previous edition in Tokyo. Now, the players, coaches and administrators can put all their focus on doing their best at the Olympics and even vying for a medal. Wrestling Aman Sehrawat Mens 57 kg category gold By beating reigning world champion Han Chong Song of North Korea in the final, Aman has added another feather in his cap after his bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics. It is Indias first-ever gold medal in the 57 kg category, one of the most competitive in the world. Another wrestling medal of note is Nitesh Siwachs silver in the mens 97 kg Greco-Roman category, the first for India in 64 years. Archery Kumkum Mohod Womens recurve individual gold Archery has been there in the Asian Games since 1978 but no Indian woman recurve archer had made the individual final despite the likes of Dola Banerjee and Deepika Kumari featuring in the category. It took 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod to break the jinx. She didnt just enter the final but also defeated Korean shooter Oh Je-yin to win the gold medal, also taking the Olympic quota. The womens team gold meant India ended the 28-year-old Korean stranglehold in the event, raising Indian hopes two years before the Los Angeles Games. Shooting Neeru Dhanda Womens Trap gold Rifle and pistol are disciplines in shooting that usually contribute the bulk of Indian medals at the Asian Games, but for the first time in history, it was the shotgun section that won more gold medals than the other two. The main protagonist was 26-year-old Neeru Dhanda from Haryana. The shooter is having an impressive year with a World Cup gold and now two gold at Aichi-Nagoya. Her trap individual gold was first for India in the discipline since Randhir Singh climbed the top of the podium at the 1978 edition. Athletics Sawan Barwal Mens marathon silver India had never won an Asian Games marathon medal outside the country. National record holder Sawan Barwal clocked 21137 to win the silver in the event, ending a 44-year-old medal drought. In the process, he improved upon his own national mark, doing so at a big stage. Indias previous three medals came in the event had come in 1982 Bronze and 1951 Gold and Bronze, both those editions staged in Delhi. Barwals achievement is all the more praiseworthy as 10 runners on the start list had better personal best timings than him, but yet the Indian managed to better his own and the countrys mark. That too in rainy conditions.

articleTitle: Kumkum, Sujeet named inaugural recipients of Jaspal Rana & Raja Randhir Singh awards
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Archer Kumkum Mohor and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal with their medals at Asian Games 2026. (AP)
description: IOA honours the two standout performers of India's Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya
body_raw: Archer Kumkum Anil Mohod and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal have been named the first-ever recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and the Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively by the Indian Olympic Association, in recognition of their performances at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The awards have been instituted by the IOA to honour the best female and male sportspersons of the Games, and to commemorate the legacy of two stalwarts of Indian sport who passed away earlier this year. Kumkum, 17, making her Asian Games debut, claimed three medals, including two gold, and was central to ending South Koreas long-standing dominance in womens recurve archery. Alongside Ankita Bhakat and Kirti, she won the womens recurve team gold, snapping South Koreas run of seven consecutive Asian Games titles dating back to the 1998 Bangkok Games. ALSO READ Surfeit of silver paints a picture of what could have been for India at Asiad Kumkum then followed it up with gold in the individual event, ensuring South Koreas women failed to win a recurve gold at the Asian Games for the first time in the disciplines history. Her individual gold also secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Sujeet, 23, was named the inaugural recipient of the Raja Randhir Singh Award after winning gold in the mens 65kg freestyle wrestling category. He produced one of the most dramatic performances of the Games, defeating reigning Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semifinal before staging a remarkable comeback in the gold-medal bout against Abdulmazhid Kudiyev, trailing 2-9 with time running out before fighting back to secure a 10-9 victory. ALSO READ How Kumkum Mohod beat best in world to win historic archery gold in Asiad Sujeet also continued Indias strong tradition in the 65kg category, following Olympic medallists Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, who won gold in the same weight class at the 2014 and 2018 Asian Games respectively. The IOA will felicitate Kumkum and Sujeet at a ceremony in the coming days. India finished fourth in the Asian Games medal standings with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Asian Games gold best medal of my life, says Lovlina Borgohain
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lovlina Borgohain poses for photographers during the medal ceremony for the women's 75kg boxing event at the 20th Asian Games, in Nishio, Aichi, Japan, Friday, Oct. 2, 2026. (PTI Photo)
description: After winning an Olympic bronze medal in Japan, Lovlina made a successful return to the country, winning an Asian Games gold half a decade later.
body_raw: Getting punched in the head hasnt worried Lovlina Borgohain for a while now rather, her headspace over the past few years has caused an odd sense of displacement. No Indian boxer barring Mary Kom has the kind of resume the Assamese boxer carried to the Asian Games. Lovlina added another notch to that comparison, becoming only the second Indian woman to win boxing gold at the Asian Games after Kom - a twelve-year wait between the two. The gold, though, came after mental battles that Lovlina has faced in the last two years. The backpack of medals she has won got heavier and heavier until 2024, when the weight, simply, was too much to handle. Losses started to follow and take their toll. The 2025 World Championship brought along with it the final gong of a round lost - for a boxer who had three medals and was the defending champion in her weight category, Liverpool brought her world crashing down. Two full years filled with disappointment left her scarred. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage A lot of things have to be faced when we come back after losing, said Lovlina. Back in Delhi after her successful campaign in Nagoya, it was those difficult moments that she remembered with a gold medal around her neck. Accepting it yourself is very difficult. when we have expectations from ourselves, and the result doesnt come that way, it hurts a lot. Then somewhere that holds us back from moving forward, added Lovlina. Mindset shift The way back to being herself started with a rethink. How she approached the sport had to be restructured. She began framing injuries and losses positively. In a way, Lovlina chose not to care about the result - and just made an attempt to enjoy the process. It led to a therapeutic lack of pressure as she went into her second-ever Asian Games. ALSO READ Surfeit of silver paints a picture of what could have been for India at Asiad First of all, I didnt go into the Games with very high expectations. I had in mind that whatever the result is, I will accept it, but I have to give my best. So when gold came, maybe. I was not overly excited. Whatever happened, I accepted it. I felt it, I was enjoying it-throughout the game, I enjoyed it. Whether gold came or not, even then, this would have been the best Asian Games of my life, admitted Lovlina. But a silver at the Commonwealth Games, a first for her, and now gold at the Asian Games have once again put her back on track. Part of that realignment came from changes she made. Rather than working hard, Lovlina now tends to work smart. Gone are the days when she preferred staying in camp and grinding out sparring sessions. When we play a competition, its not a matter of one or two days of hard work its the whole year. I had faith that overworking myself shouldnt be done. And the biggest thing I feel when we reach this stage, rather than pushing oneself too much, polishing oneself is more important. If you keep rubbing a diamond too much, it will get ruined, says Lovlina. The changes she brought to her mindset were also reflected during her semi-final match. Lovlina has been part of many multi-sport events for India, but this was the first time she won a gold medal. Usually, her campaign would end in the semi-finals or finals. But things felt different this time. Going up against the 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova was no longer as daunting. The semi-final match is very important because - either we have to be satisfied with bronze or we can try to win gold. It stays in your mind because within us, we know whether we could have done better or not. I didnt want that feeling this time, said Lovlina. She won 3-2, arguably weathering the toughest bout of her Games. Till the end, everyone was scared, but I wasnt that scared. I didnt go onto the ring with much stress. The opponent was also very strong, but sometimes it feels good when we play against good opponents and win, said Lovlina. Now that the nonchalance of the end result and the juice of simply performing have come back, Lovlina has thought about all the medals she has won. All the previous World Championship medals, the solitary Olympic bronze and now a Commonwealth silver and Asian Games gold have been added to the collection. When I keep it alongside all my other medals, this one is the one that shines the brightest, admits Lovlina.

articleTitle: AISA chief Neha Bora among 120 detained on Day 3 of protest against CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: neha bora
description: The protest came a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar.
body_raw: Around 120 protesters, including All India Students Association AISA president Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, were detained for several hours on Sunday as the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter rolls entered its third consecutive day. The protest came a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar. On Sunday, while some protested against CEC Kumar, others attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar to demand accountability and a probe into the journalists allegations of sexual assault. Bora was detained while leading a march from Andhra Bhavan Canteen towards Jantar Mantar. The march saw participation from civil society activists such as Yadav, student protesters and political parties like the Indian Youth Congress IYC and the AAP. This has just started and many organisations are now joining this, we wont stop. Even though the Jantar Mantar is closed, were on the streets, even women are here to reclaim them. This is the power of common people. Jab tak Gyanesh Kumar ki chhutti nahi hoti, hum chhutti nahi karnege Until Gyanesh Kumar takes a leave, we will not take a leave, Yadav said while marching towards Jantar Mantar. Flags waved and slogans of Gyanesh has to go pierced the air as the crowd split into groups and moved towards Ashoka Road. With the protest entering its third day, Lutyens Delhi was heavily fortified, with elaborate security arrangements in place since morning. A large fleet of buses and riot action vehicles had been deployed on multiple lanes, and movement on several roads leading to Jantar Mantar and the Parliament Street police station was restricted. The Delhi Police also closed the stretch between Ashoka Road and Parliament Street near Jantar Mantar, while prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS were already put across the New Delhi district. At around 4 pm, as the march progressed towards Jantar Mantar, barricades were put up. When a few protesters tried to cross them, the police began detaining them. Bora was detained in a car by officers, but the vehicle remained stuck for over 20 minutes as protesters stood around it to prevent it from moving. Ashoka Road remained shut and traffic was halted until 6.30 pm as the protests continued. Amid the chaos, police kept detaining protesters, including AISA activists and members of other left-wing parties. As one police bus filled with detainees pulled away, the next quickly took its place in line. Teams of four to five officers lifted and carried protesters to the buses, while some tried to break the bus windows to get out. Even as detentions continued, people kept protesting. Traffic resumed briefly on the roundabout, but police carried on detaining protesters as their numbers grew. According to police sources, around 120 people, including AISA, AAP and IYC workers and Yadav, were detained. Bora was taken to Narela police station, police said, adding that all of the protesters were later released. According to police, around half a dozen of their personnel including women staff were also injured while handling the protesters. The injured officers were given first aid at a hospital as well, police said.

articleTitle: Rs 2,400 crore Mokama rail bridge opens: 2 new lines boost Delhi-Howrah train capacity
articleFeaturedImageAlt: New Mokama rail bridge over the Ganga in Bihar. (Image: East Central Railway)
description: Mokama’s new rail bridge over the Ganga is now open for train operations, adding two railway lines and strengthening North-South Bihar connectivity.
body_raw: Indian Railways has commissioned Mokamas new rail bridge over River Ganga in Bihar. Built at a cost of around Rs 2,400 crore, the new bridge will further strengthen rail connectivity between North and South Bihar. This will also provide an additional route for passenger and freight train operations. The new bridge has been constructed parallel to the existing Rajendra Pul and has a double railway line. It was opened for train operations after receiving the required safety approval from the Commissioner of Railway Safety CRS, Eastern Circle. The CRS conducted the safety inspection of the new bridge and the associated doubled and electrified railway line on October 3 and 4, 2026.Following the safety clearance, train operations have started on the new bridge. Speaking to Indianexpress.com, Saraswati Chandra, Chief Public Relations Officer CPRO, East Central Railway, said the new Mokama rail bridge has been commissioned and train operations began around midnight. He added that train number 15483 Mahananda Express was the first train to cross the newly commissioned bridge. Location of new Mokama rail bridge The new Mokama rail bridge has been constructed about 50 metres towards the Patna side of the existing Rajendra Pul, which has been in service since 1959. The project spans around 15.5 km, including a 1.9-km main bridge over the Ganga connecting Mokama and Barauni. The main bridge comprises 17 steel spans, while the project also includes around 3.6 km of rail viaducts. Besides the main bridge, the project includes eight minor bridges, two road overbridges and three rail-over-rail structures. According to the CPRO, the new bridge has been planned in a way that requires minimum changes to the approaches of the existing bridge. It connects to the existing railway stations on both sides of the Ganga. Existing Rajendra Pul to continue carrying trains The railway official said that the new bridge will not replace the existing Rajendra Pul. Thus, the train operations will continue on the old bridge as well. He added that with the new double-line bridge alongside the existing bridge, the route will now have three railway lines, increasing capacity for train movement. It will significantly boost capacity on the busy Delhi-Howrah rail corridor. Better train connectivity between North and South Bihar The new bridge will provide an additional rail route between North and South Bihar, while also strengthening connectivity towards the northeastern parts of the country. According to the official, railway traffic in the corridor is expected to increase by around 2.5 times. The higher capacity is also expected to make freight movement smoother and reduce transportation time and costs. This could benefit the movement of essential goods as well as trade and commercial activity in the region, he stated. However, for passengers, the two new lines will help Railways manage train operations more efficiently on this important route.

articleTitle: Global capital is no longer cheap, that’s the challenge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Global capital is no longer cheap, that’s the challenge
description: Simply put, investors are demanding higher returns from governments on the tradable debt instruments issued by them that, being backed by the sovereign’s power to tax and print currency, are ostensibly default risk-free
body_raw: Ten-year US and French government bond yields hit 5.34 and 4.99 per cent respectively last week, their highest since 2002, while crossing 3.1 per cent for Japan, the first time after 1996. The increase in borrowing costs for the governments of these countries over the past one year works out to 1.2-1.4 percentage points. Thats roughly twice the 0.7 percentage points rise in the 10-year Indian government security yield, which closed the week at 7.21 per cent. Simply put, investors are demanding higher returns from governments on the tradable debt instruments issued by them that, being backed by the sovereigns power to tax and print currency, are ostensibly default risk-free. And unlike before, they arent differentiating much between the governments of advanced and emerging economies the bonds of the former are the ones that have surged to multi-decade peaks. There are three reasons for this. The first is the persistent deficits run by developed country governments, due to aging populations, expanded social welfare commitments alongside military build-up, and voter resistance to tax increases or entitlement cuts. The USs outstanding public debt has surpassed 40 trillion. Its defence budget for 2026 reached a record 1 trillion, with the Donald Trump administration proposing 1.5 trillion of spending for the coming fiscal year. The Washington-based Institute of International Finance has estimated that advanced economies paid over 3.3 trillion in interest on globally traded government bonds last year. The perception of mounting fiscal risk also explains Chinese holdings of US Treasuries falling to an 18-year-low of 618 billion in July 2016, from the peak 1.32 trillion of November 2013. The second reason is commodity inflation from war and weather-induced supply shocks, driving central banks to raise interest rates as well as signal further increases ahead. The third has to do with the global race for building AI infrastructure.
