articleTitle: ‘Got the law involved’: FBI chief Kash Patel gets engaged to longtime girlfriend Alexis Wilkins
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kash petal
description: FBI Director Kash Patel is engaged to country singer Alexis Wilkins. The couple announced it on X on Sunday, with the caption "Went and got the law involved."
body_raw: FBI Director Kash Patel is engaged to his girlfriend, country singer Alexis Wilkins. The couple announced it in a post on X on Sunday. Wilkins, 27, posted the news with a photo of herself next to 46-year-old Patel, and Patel shared her post on his own account. The two met at a friends event in Nashville in 2022 and began dating in early 2023, according to a separate news report. Patel took over as the head of the FBI in 2025, and she was at his swearing-in on February 21 that year, the Associated Press AP said. - Kash Patel KashPatel October 4, 2026 Their relationship has drawn attention since Patel took charge of the bureau, navigating questions about his use of aircraft and lawsuits filed by Wilkins. On Sunday, Wilkins shared a black-and-white photo of herself standing next to Patel. In the picture, both are smiling as she shows off her engagement ring. Her caption read, Went and got the law involved. Patel shared her post on his own X account with heart and diamond ring emojis, according to the separate report. Went and got the law involved KashPatel httpst.coOjZmOOrVg7- Alexis Wilkins AlexisWilkins October 4, 2026 Last year on the Megyn Kelly Show, Wilkins spoke about their first meeting. Asked about their age gap, she brushed the question aside and said, We just happened to meet. She said she liked him from the start because he is honest and is the same person at all times. She also praised his character and values. Last month she appeared at his Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on FBI oversight on September 15, in what the report called a rare public appearance. Who is Alexis Wilkins Wilkins is a country singer and political commentator. She released her debut work in 2023, which a separate report names as the EP Grit. AP said she has been linked with conservative groups. The other report said she has hosted a show on Rumble and has served on the board of the National Rifle Association. On her website, she describes her music as work that honors country tradition while adding relevance and current commentary, AP said. Questions over FBI aircraft AP reported that Patel has faced criticism for using government aircraft on trips with no known law enforcement purpose. This included an FBI jet flight to State College, Pennsylvania, for a pro-wrestling event where Wilkins sang the national anthem. Photos she posted afterwards showed the couple smiling as she held a large golden championship belt. Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee have criticised Patels use of a private jet after reports said he used one to visit his girlfriend and attend sporting events. Patel has said he is legally barred from flying on commercial airlines. He told The Katie Miller Podcast in December that he and his partner pay for their own personal travel, as other Cabinet members and agency heads do.

articleTitle: Sanjay Dutt says his ‘can’t feel peace in India’ remark a ‘scripted conversation’, Shekhar Suman comments
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt offers a clarification for his India remarks on Shekhar Tonite.
description: Sanjay Dutt offered an explanation for his remarks on Shekhar Tonite, where he confessed that he "doesn't feel peace in India anymore". The actor claimed it was part of a scripted conversation in the form of a satire.
body_raw: Actor Sanjay Dutt ended up inviting the ire of the internet and certain sections of society after his remarks this past weekend on Shekhar Sumans satire show Shekhar Tonite on YouTube. The actor, after confessing he doesnt feel peace in India anymore, went on to deliver a monologue commenting on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump in his signature style of iconic character Munna Bhai from Rajkumar Hiranis seminal social comedy franchise. However, Dutt has now offered an explanation. Dutt lives with his family, wife Maanyata Dutt and two children, in Dubai. Sanjay Dutt offers clarification on India remark I want to clarify that it has never been my intention to hurt the feelings of any individual, community, or institution, to insult them, or to disrespect them, wrote Dutt on his X handle on Sunday. He claimed he made those remarks in context of a scripted conversation intended to engage in lighthearted and humorous dialogue. He further explained that his tone was akin to the humour and satire used in the Munna Bhai franchise, particularly the second part, Lage Raho Munna Bhai 2006, which used Gandhigiri, a modern take on Mahatma Gandhi to comment on the current state of society. He claimed that the intention was to convey a message of love, unity, and goodwill. He reiterated that unfortunately, his words were interpreted out of that context. He wrote on X, I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution. My remarks were made in the context of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous. The spirit behind them was similar to the humour and satire seen in films like Munna Bhai, particularly the concept of Gandhigiri, which was intended to convey a message of love, warmth, togetherness, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted outside of that intended context Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt Hours after Sanjay Dutts clarification, the shows host Shekhar Suman also came out in his defence. Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he said was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never said or meant. I know him for years he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it, Shekhar told NDTV in an interview. What did Sanjay Dutt say on Shekhar Tonite? Before he was asked to deliver a monologue as Indias Prime Minister in the final segment of Shekhar Tonite, Dutt confessed he doesnt feel peace in the country anymore. The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I cant feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shiva ji that those days come back soon, he said. Later, he delivered a monologue as Indias PM in the Munna Bhai style. During that performance, he underlined the criticism towards PM Modi that he takes too many foreign trips instead of spending more time with his countrymen. Aap log ekdum tension nahi lene ka. Apun is khushi ko celebrate karne videsh nahi jaane wala hai. Apun idharich rahega, aap sab logon ke beech. Nahi to PM aur janta mein connection kaise banega You people dont have to worry at all. I am not going abroad to celebrate this happiness. I will stay right here, among all of you. Otherwise, how will there be a connection between the PM and the people?, he said. He also indirectly claimed that PM Modi focuses too much on optics and getting his pictures clicked everywhere. Apun ko desh ke liye bahut kuch karne ka mauka mila hai PM banke, toh apun ek aur kaam karega. Jahaan jahaan uska photo laga hai na, apun usko ekdum kam kar dega. Desh ko desh ka photo dikhna chahiye. I have got the opportunity to do a lot for the country as a PM, so I will do one more thing. Wherever the PMs photograph has been put up, I will cut that down. The country should see a picture of the country, added Dutt. He also proposed replacing PM Modis pictures with those of Gandhi, since the Father of Indias non-violent philosophy is what every contemporary leader should be subscribing to in order to make the world a better place. He didnt spare Trump either, referring to him as mamu and offered him a jadoo ki jhappi. Dekho Trump mamu, zyada tante nahi paalne ka. Duniya mein missile waise hi bahut ho gaya hai. Ab thoda pyaar bhi export karne ka. Kahin missile bhejne ka mann kare to pehle guldasta bhejne ka. Kisi ko dhamki dene ka mann kare na to use phone karke ghar bulane ka aur chai peete-peete baat suljhane ka. Trump, dont create so much trouble. There are already enough missiles in the world. Now export a little love too. If you feel like sending a missile somewhere, send a bouquet first. If you feel like threatening someone, call them home and resolve the matter over a cup of tea, said the actor. Lage Raho Munna Bhai revolved around Dutts gangster character who reads up excessively on Gandhi, in order to impress his love interest and radio jockey Vidya Balan, that he ends up hallucinating Gandhi everywhere. That leads to him treading on the non-violence path of Gandhi, offering bouquets instead of threats to his friend-turned-nemesis Lucky Boman Irani. Also Read - So we dont end up in jail Kapil Sharma on why he watches younger comics Produced by Vidhu Vinod Chopra, and co-written by Hirani and Abhijat Joshi, Lage Raho Munna Bhai earned over Rs 120 crore at the worldwide box office. Its the sequel to Hiranis 2003 gangster comedy Munna Bhai MBBS, and also stars Arshad Warsi, Dia Mirza, Saurabh Shukla, Kulbhushan Kharbanda, and Jimmy Shergill among others.

articleTitle: CBSE ‘hack’, IIT gig and US recognition: Nisarga Adhikary’s incredible year at 19
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nisarga
description: The cybersecurity researcher, who is now working at IIT Kanpur, was recognised by the US Department of Justice for reporting a vulnerability in one of its systems
body_raw: Tuesday, September 22. It was almost an hour past midnight. Nisarga Adhikary was sitting in the Starbucks caf at IIT Kanpur. An email notification flashed across his screen. It was a message from the US Department of Justice, acknowledging his work in finding and reporting a security flaw within their systems. I was having my second cup of coffee when I received the email, he recalls. Nisarga Adhikary is only 19 years old. On paper, this recognition stood as one of the most prestigious accolades he could have ever imagined. Yet, surprisingly, he remained unfazed, showing no trace of excitement. I love to break stuff, Nisarga says. Hacking things is a part of me trying to understand how things work. The security flaw was not something he had been assigned to find. There was no college project or professional brief behind it. He was simply trying to understand how the system worked. Still, the recognition was the latest turn in a remarkable five months for this 19-year-old. In February, he first drew public attention for identifying alleged security flaws in the Central Board of Secondary Educations digital examination system and has since landed a job at IIT Kanpurs cybersecurity hub. Nisarga is from Siliguri, West Bengal. His parents, both senior government officers, wanted him to take the Joint Entrance Examination JEE and he was preparing through a FIITJEE South Delhi programme. Then, his work began attracting attention. His parents were worried, Nisarga says, before they gradually became more accepting of it. The CBSE controversy Earlier this year, Nisarga began examining publicly accessible parts of CBSEs On-Screen Marking OSM system, the digital platform used to evaluate scanned answer sheets. He claims he found several weaknesses in the system. One, its One-Time Password OTP checks could be bypassed, allowing an unauthorised user to access examiner accounts without receiving an actual code. Two, poorly configured storage on Amazon Web Services AWS allegedly gave him access to about 1.8 million scanned answer sheets. Nisarga also demonstrated the account-takeover risk by accessing the account of a physics teacher on the live CBSE system. Asked about the ethics of accessing a real persons account, he says hed blurred the teachers details and used the access only to demonstrate the vulnerability. He reported his findings to the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team CERT-In, the government agency that coordinates responses to cybersecurity incidents, in February. By May, he had published a detailed account of what he had found. He had also come on television to describe and explain his findings. His revelations quickly attracted attention as students, teachers, and parents were already raising concerns about glitches, evaluation inconsistencies, and operational problems linked to the OSM rollout. The board initially denied that its OSM portal had been compromised, but later acknowledged that cybersecurity issues had been flagged in the public domain. Subsequently, on May 31, CBSE stated that it had been closely monitoring the vulnerabilities in the OnMark portal and that a team of cybersecurity professionals drawn from various arms of the government as well as the IITs had been deployed over the last few days to fortify the system. Nisargas findings soon became part of a wider political debate. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi was among those who publicly praised him for raising questions about the CBSE system. Nisarga also participated in protests organised by the Cockroach Janta Party CJP over the NEET-UG paper leak and posted a photograph with CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke. He says he was invited to meet Rahul Gandhi alongside Sarthak Sidhant, who had separately flagged alleged irregularities in CBSEs tendering process, but chose not to go. Sarthak, an 18-year-old student from Jharkhand, had known Nisarga before they became publicly associated with the CBSE controversy. He says they met around three years ago on Reddit and credits Nisarga with supporting him during CBSE times. Kshitij Kapoor, a software engineer at AI research lab Nous Research, says he has known Nisarga since he was 14. He met him through Capture The Flag CTF, competitive cybersecurity exercises where players find hidden text strings called flags inside vulnerable systems or programmes. Hes always had a knack for poking holes in systems. The curiosity hasnt changed much but the scale definitely has, Kshitij says. I was happy to see him get recognition. Having known him since so early on, it felt very personal to me in a way. The teen behind the screen Nisarga describes himself as a nerd all his life. He says he spends almost all his waking hours glued to a screen, claiming that he has no non-technical friends. Outside cybersecurity, he reads young-adult fiction, like The Fault in Our Stars. He is also a big fan of Japanese animation such as Tokyo Ghoul. He reads books about activism and says he is interested in activism for the rights of neurodivergent people, queer rights and internet freedom. His views on technology and society are shaped, he says, by what he calls neoliberal technocratic biases. He describes himself as socially very left and economically right. He looks up to the likes of Sam Altman and Mark Zuckerberg, the heads of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI and technology company Meta, respectively, for their drive to build things. From exam-system sleuth to IIT Kanpur Around the same time, Nisargas views on technology and government brought him to the attention of IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal. When the Centre moved to restrict Telegram before the NEET-UG re-exam, Nisarga criticised the decision, arguing that authorities had failed to prevent paper leaks while trying to restrict a messaging platform that could still be accessed through proxies. IIT Kanpur director Manindra Agrawal responded to his comments, saying he would need to sit Nisarga down and explain. He had already reached out to the teenager earlier, and the interaction eventually led to Nisarga joining C3iHub, IIT Kanpurs cybersecurity-focused technology innovation hub, as an Open-Source Intelligence OSINT and Threat Intelligence Engineer. His job involves identifying and understanding potential security threats. Nisarga, however, remains sceptical of an educational system that measures people through examinations and credentials alone. You can have a PhD and still produce low quality research and do worse than your peers with no degree. It depends on talent and curiosity, he says. For now, he is settling into life at IIT Kanpur. He says the transition has not been difficult, although he describes Kanpur as a bit bad compared with places he has lived before. Eventually, he wants to work across technology, defence and artificial intelligence and may eventually return to formal education, possibly in the US or another country. For someone whose curiosity began with figuring out how computer systems work, the question now is what he will choose to explore next. But when that email from the US Department of Justice arrived, Nisarga did not see it as a defining moment for him. I was unamused. It was like any other normal Hall of Fame mention for me, he says. I think I work a lot and put all my time into research because thats the only coping mechanism I have. Why is he unmoved by this latest recognition? Alex Karp, CEO of Palantir once said that one cannot have a great social life at age 20 and achieve extraordinary career success at the same time, he says. It might sound toxic but hes kind of right, I feel.

articleTitle: Gujarat Hardlook: How do you remake Gandhi’s ashram for Rs 1,200 crore — and keep it simple?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A good part of that pathway is already complete. It is lined with baobabs from Madagascar, black neem from Thailand and exotic flora such as Mayan spinach from Mexico and bird-of-paradise.
description: Visitors can walk through the house where Gandhi and his wife Kasturba once lived — a house that, every year without fail, marks Gandhi Jayanti with an all-faith prayer meeting open to the public.
body_raw: Under the Gandhi Ashram Redevelopment Project, most of the original ashrams buildings have been restored. The project is now deciding how these buildings will tell the Mahatmas story through museums, activities and experiences for visitors within the 55-acre space, write Parimal A Dabhi and Leena Misra. IMAGINE A granite-paved pathway lit by Victorian-style lampposts, with ornate wooden benches along the way, taking visitors on a journey through the life of a barrister who became a Mahatma while fighting to free India from British rule. A good part of that pathway is already complete. It is lined with baobabs from Madagascar, black neem from Thailand and exotic flora such as Mayan spinach from Mexico and bird-of-paradise. The walk through a series of repurposed buildings is designed to culminate in an arboretum called Mohan-to-Mahatma - the plants are colour-coded to mark each phase of Gandhis life. That, though, is all in the extended part of the project. At its heart is a five-acre space that feels frozen in time. The Five Acres Frozen in Time Here, visitors can walk through the house where Gandhi and his wife Kasturba once lived - a house that, every year without fail, marks Gandhi Jayanti with an all-faith prayer meeting open to the public. This year, on October 2, Vijaybhai Joshi arrived at the ceremony dressed in khadi, with a cotton hank around his neck and a walking stick slung over his shoulder. After the prayer meeting at Hriday Kunj - marking Gandhis 157th birth anniversary - he climbed onto the back of a scooter to head home. This country has not seen anyone like Gandhiji. Weve been shaped by his ideology, and because we followed it, here I am before you at 104 years, Joshi says, chuckling. Hard of hearing, Joshi pulls a small contraption from his bag - a funnel attached to a transparent pipe. To speak with him, one must talk into the funnel he listens through the other end, pressed to his ear. Born in Bihar in 1922, Joshi worked for a British firm and was posted in Pakistan. During the partition in 1947, his employer asked if he wanted to stay on. No, he told them, and asked instead to be transferred to his home state of Gujarat. He has lived in Ahmedabad since, where his family sings Gandhis favourite bhajan, Vaishnava Jana To, every evening. Driving the scooter was 84-year-old Jesingbhai Parmar, a former Reserve Bank of India employee who reaches the ashram every Friday - because that is the day Gandhiji died, he says. On his visits, he spins 250 metres of yarn on the charkha at Hriday Kunj for over three hours. This October 2, he sat in the front row of the prayer meeting, spinning alongside children from the ashrams school, which has since relocated outside the complex. One Ashram, Six Trusts Hriday Kunj - the house Gandhi built in 1917 on land he bought along the Sabarmati River a year earlier - was just one structure among several that made up the 120-acre ashram until 1930. Todays redevelopment covers the 55-acre ashram itself, within a wider precinct of roughly 322 acres. After Gandhis death in 1948, the land was divided among six trusts tasked with carrying forward Gandhian thoughts and practices the Harijan Ashram Trust 1939, Gujarat Khadi Gramodyog Mandal 1940, Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust or SAPMT 1950, Gujarat Harijan Sevak Sangh 1952, Sabarmati Ashram Gaushala Trust 1952 and Khadi Gramodyog Prayog Samiti 1958. The Core Hriday Kunj sits within the five acres known simply as Sabarmati Ashram. On an average day, this stretch alone draws 4,000 visitors, says Kartikeya Sarabhai, chairman of SAPMT - whose first chairman, in 1949, was Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Several luminaries succeeded him, such as Ganesh Mavlankar, the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and Kartikeyas late father Dr Vikram Sarabhai known as the father of Indias space mission, to name a few. SAPMT manages this core area, which includes Gandhis and Kasturbas residence, Vinoba Bhave and Mira Kutir, Nandini Guest House, Magan Nivas, and Sanghralaya - a museum designed by late architect Charles Correa that houses the ashrams exhibition and library. A Vision, Delivered Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Rs 1,200-crore redevelopment project in 2024. It envisions the ashram as one contiguous space across 55 acres its buildings restored to how they stood when Gandhi was alive. The project is being executed by the Union Ministry of Culture and the Gujarat government through the Mahatma Gandhi Sabarmati Ashram Memorial Trust MGSAMT, headed by Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. Retired Gujarat IAS officer I P Gautam is leading the projects execution as Chairman of the Executive Council. Another retired IAS officer, I K Patel, is also playing a key role in the project as officer on special duty and member secretary of the Governing Council. It was the Prime Ministers wish that we restore the ashram to how Gandhi left it in 1930, with modern facilities, says a source associated with the project. A public road that once split the land in two has now been closed and a large brick-and-concrete gateway has come up to serve as the new main entrance. Beyond the SAPMT-managed core lies the part of the ashram now under restoration - buildings that once housed schools, hostels, teachers quarters, and units producing cloth, paper, leather and dairy products. This stretch, the source says, will take visitors through Gandhis life, from the Champaran Satyagraha, where he became Mahatma, through the freedom movement, and till the British left India. Restoring 28 Buildings, Developing 24 Museums Inside what used to be the ashrams gaushala cowshed, an artisan, Hirenbhai, dips bunches of coir fibre into a paste of Fullers earth, popularly called Multani mitti, and smooths it over a plinth. We will finish it with lippan, he says, referring to traditional mud plaster. A marble plaque at the entrance notes that the structure was built in 1938 for Rs 7,200, funded by a donation from the Ahmedabad American Cotton Exchange Association Ltd, a private company founded in 1932. It is among the first of 28 buildings to be fully restored. In one room, thatched roofs for a set of representational cowsheds - part of an upcoming museum - are in place. It is the only one of 24 planned museums being developed by the National Dairy Development Board NDDB. The rest have been contracted to Paris-based Museum Studio, which is working in consortium with Ecofirst Private Ltd, a subsidiary of Tata Consulting Engineers. Ahmedabad-based urban planner Bimal Patels firm HCP Design Planning Management Pvt Ltd created the master plan for the project and executed the civil works using traditional methods. Sources say no cement concrete was used in any of the restorations. Of the 28 restored buildings, 24 will house museums. Activities once central to ashram life - papermaking and spinning among them - have been assigned to buildings within the wider precinct. It was Gandhijis idea that these activities should not just survive but also prosper. We will produce more khadi and more paper, so visitors to the ashram can buy them, says a source involved in the project. At the entrance, an interpretation centre will lay out what each space in the new ashram offers, helping visitors plan their visit around the time they have. Keeping the Tranquility SAPMT prepared a concept note meant to guide the MGSAMTs work closely. Kartikeya Sarabhai recalls that Modi, as Gujarats Chief Minister then, had a clear vision for the revamped ashram even back in 2009, when the Trust first approached him. The PM, from the beginning, felt that whatever changes we make should be done in the context of the overall ashram, not as individual ones. He had that vision even then - it got articulated later, Sarabhai says. When Modi became Prime Minister and approached the ashrams trustees about redeveloping the full complex, Our only request was that the ashrams core values - tranquility among them - stay at its heart, Sarabhai says, adding that the government held to that promise. He notes that Hriday Kunj, the Gandhis home from 1917 to 1930, originally stood amid an open maidan. We will keep it in the maidan, he says. The concept note, Sarabhai explains, outlines the need to communicate what the ashram stood for in Gandhis time. It was a site for experiments in truth, non-violence, dignity of labour, respect for all religions and the removal of untouchability. It was to be one of modern Indias most audacious experiments. The uniqueness of this experiment makes this site of immense significance to India and to the world, he says. The new trust has left SAPMTs management of the core area undisturbed. SAPMT has engaged Ahmedabad-based conservation architect Dr Rabindra Vasavda to restore its portion of the buildings. Making Room The Ashramvasis According to sources, 307 claims were made by ashramvasis - long-time residents occupying 256 buildings- who had to vacate the premises. The MGSAMT offered three options compensation by cheque, flats purchased by the trust, or homes in cooperative housing financed by the trust. The trust has spent Rs 190 crore on rehabilitation so far. Of those relocated, 223 families - the largest group - opted for compensation, with payouts of up to Rs 90 lakh per family. We have treated them with respect. They were not encroachers, said a source. Only Krunal Rathod and his family, who occupy a cottage, are yet to evacuate. Their case is under litigation in the Small Causes Court. The Rathods fight concerns three properties which they claim were handed over to their predecessor by the trustee of the relevant Ashram trust around 1930. The PMs Stamp Several personal interventions by Modi shaped the redevelopments final look The pathways colour was changed from red to grey cobblestone Victorian-style wrought-iron lamp posts will be installed throughout red stone benches were replaced with ornate wooden ones. What Visitors Can Expect Original artefacts from SAPMTs collection - a sari Gandhi wove for Kasturba, his cycle, his charkha - may be part of the exhibits, with security details still being worked out parking for 250 cars and 25 buses to serve the higher number of visitors. At present, the Sabarmati Ashram sees nearly 4,000 visitors daily. A food court near the entry gate that will serve sattvik cuisine. A souvenir shop featuring Gandhis three monkeys, carved from wood sourced from the original ashram. A walkthrough rainforest of medicinal plants and trees. The ashrams original trees - peepal, jamun, asopalav, piludi, neem, gundo, mango, moringa - still stand in many places. Retired Deputy Conservator of Forest Jayant Solanki is overseeing this effort, assigned to the Heartfulness Institute, a spiritual organisation. Ticketing still undecided - though Kartikeya Sarabhai suggests non-priced tickets to regulate visitor flow. Residential facilities for visiting Gandhian scholars, an idea still under consideration. An artificial lake connected to stormwater drains to harvest rainwater. The lake was naturally tested in July when the city saw excessive rain, and water drained into it, filling it. The Ashram is my best and only creation. And the world will judge me by its results, reads a quote by the Father of the Nation at the entrance of the MGSAMT office, as if summarising the projects objective. By the time the pathway reaches its end, visitors will have walked through more than a restored ashram - they will have retraced, tree by tree and room by room, the journey of a barrister who became one of historys most enduring symbols of non-violent resistance. Iconic Buildings Being Restored Anand Bhavan Constructed around 1920 as the ashrams needs grew. Gandhis secretary and confidant, Mahadev Desai, lived here for a time. Imam Manzil Built in 1919 for Imam Saheb Abdul Kader Bawazeer, a close companion of Gandhis in both South Africa and India. He gave up his business to join the Satyagraha movement and stayed with Gandhi until he died in 1931. Bal Mandir Inaugurated in 1940 by Madame Montessori, this building trained the children of Dalit craftsmen and workers in the crafts practised in their own homes. Junu Rasodu Built in 1918 as a kitchen and dining hall with a storeroom cellar. Meals followed a strict ritual a bell rang thrice, the kitchen doors closed after the second ring, and prayers began at the third, according to an account by the late Narayan Desai, Mahadev Desais son. Somnath Chhatralaya Built in 1922 to house the growing number of ashram residents, this 100-room facility later served as a hostel for female PTC students after 1955. Jamna Kutir Built in 1924 by industrialist Jamnalal Bajaj as a residence for his family during visits to the Satyagraha Ashram, which Gandhi later renamed Harijan Ashram. It later housed two ashram workers. Restoration of this building is pending due to litigation.

articleTitle: Nearly 200 isolated after lab worker dies of suspected plague in Siberia
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Russia-plague case
description: A lab worker at an anti-plague institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 people are under medical watch. Russia has not confirmed plague.
body_raw: Russian authorities have quarantined medical facilities in Siberia and put nearly 200 people under medical observation after the death of a woman who worked at an anti-plague laboratory. Russian media have said she may have had pneumonic plague, but health authorities have not yet confirmed the illness, according to Axios. The woman is named as Daria Shipilova, 28, a laboratory assistant at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. Local reports say she broke a test tube holding the bacteria. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said none of the people being watched has shown symptoms, and all their tests so far have come back negative. A Trump administration official told Axios on Sunday that the White House is monitoring the case. Russias public health agency says the situation in the region is stable. In a thread on X, health expert Ashish K. Jha said he is concerned and that Russia owes the world more answers. Not all of these claims have been checked, and the cause of the death has not been confirmed by officials. Many of you have been tracking the Irkutsk lab situation over the last few days. Ive been gathering facts and trying to understand what is happening before weighing in. Now that I have, I have to say - Im concerned - Ashish K. Jha ashishkjha October 5, 2026 What happened to the lab worker Local reports say Shipilova broke a test tube containing the pneumonic plague pathogen on September 25. Later, she fell ill on an expedition with other workers near Russias eastern border with Mongolia, The New York Post reported, citing the news outlet Lyudi Baikala. She was admitted to a hospital in the town of Shelekhov on September 29 with signs of severe pneumonia. According to reports in the Post and Axios, Shipilova was placed on a ventilator and died in the intervening night between October 1 and 2 After her death, authorities put quarantines in place at several medical facilities in the region. Workers in protective gear have been testing people and places in Shelekhov, the Post said. What is plague Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It killed tens of millions of people in the Black Death in the Middle Ages, the Post said. There are three main forms bubonic, pneumonic and septicemic. Symptoms can include fever, headache, chills, weakness, shortness of breath and cough. All forms can be treated with antibiotics, especially when treatment starts early, according to the Post and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, as cited by Axios. Claims of a cover-up The Post said the case has led to accusations that Russian authorities are trying to keep details out of public view. The Russian political channel Nezygar said the situation in Shelekhov resembles the Wuhan case. Mikhal Favorov, a senior Russian epidemiologist, disputed the broken test tube account, The Moscow Times reported. He said staff at an anti-plague institute wear protective suits, so the risk of infection from a broken tube is very low. He said the story was one the public would accept, and that Popovas trip suggested the situation was serious. He also said people would not be told what really happened. These are the views of one expert and one Telegram channel. No evidence of a cover-up was given in the sources. White House response A Trump administration official told Axios the administration is aware, monitoring the outbreak, and assessing options. White House spokespeople sent questions to the State Department, which did not reply to a request for comment, Axios said. Ashish K. Jha, a health expert, posted a thread on X on Sunday about the Irkutsk case. He said he had spent days gathering facts before commenting and that he is now concerned. He summed up what is known a 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague institute reportedly broke a tube holding the plague pathogen on 25 September, she died on 1 or 2 October, and nearly 200 people are in medical isolation. Heres what we know. A 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague institute reportedly broke a tube containing plague pathogen on September 25. She died October 1 or 2. Nearly 200 people are now in medical isolation 2n- Ashish K. Jha ashishkjha October 5, 2026 What Russian officials have said Anna Popova, who heads Russias public-health watchdog, travelled about 2,600 miles from Moscow to the Irkutsk region, the Post said. She has not commented in public. Kobzev did not name the illness and called it a dangerous infection. He cancelled all public events in the region and asked people to stay calm after meeting Popova. On Telegram on Friday, he said all identified contacts are under medical observation, show no signs of illness and have tested negative. Russias public health agency said Shipilova had pneumonia of unknown cause, according to Axios. It said further tests found no microorganisms linked to her work and that the epidemiological situation in the region remains stable. The Post also cited reports that antibiotics had run out in the Irkutsk region, which led worried residents to seek help at pharmacies and other medical facilities. This has not been confirmed by officials.

articleTitle: ‘I want to feel safe’: Young women attempt to march towards Jantar Mantar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: jantar mantar protest, gyanesh kumar
description: Meanwhile, many independent journalists and other protesters, who had sat outside the Parliament Street police station till Saturday night demanding accountability, returned on Sunday morning to demand the registration of an FIR into the allegations raised by the three women journalists.
body_raw: As the march from Andhra Bhavan Canteen towards Jantar Mantar reached Ashoka Road on Sunday, Adira 26 stood on the side of the road in silence, clutching her friends hand as she watched the crowd. The final-year law student, originally from Kerala and studying at Delhi University, had initially not planned to join the protest, which has been underway since October 2 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar. However, Sundays march was not focused solely on alleged irregularities in the Election Commission of India. It also voiced concerns over womens safety, coming a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of alleged sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar. Womens safety in the Capital has dominated conversations since the alleged gangrape of a minor girl by three men posing as police officers at a park in Delhi last month. Against this backdrop of rising crimes against women in the Capital, Adira said she felt compelled to join the march. I want to feel safe, she said. I came to Delhi in 2023, and when I was staying in a hostel, there were several restrictions. I wasnt allowed to wear sleeveless tops in our own premises, she said. Her parents were hesitant to send her to the Capital and have grown more worried since the news of the gangrape of the minor at a park in September. They called and told me to discontinue the course and come back, but how can I?, she said. Standing beside Adira was her friend Ayushi 20, also a DU student, from Champawat, Uttarakhand. For Ayushi, the fight has been long and is often unfair. Even in 2026, we have to fight for our basic rights. Crime happens against women but eventually they are the only one that suffers., she said, recalling how classes at DUs Lady Shri Ram College had moved online after the alleged gangrape last month. Already we have very little freedom, dont go here, dont wear such clothes. Even after any crime happens, were the ones that get blamed, she said. Another protester, Saniya Ali 18, said she had lied to her parents, who are based in Bihar, to join the protest in the Capital, telling them she was going to Delhi only for exploring. Today Im here because I think I need to. I stayed here because I have many questions to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi. I want to ask him, what all is not happening here. Votes are being stolen, women are being raped, what is our country doing? Yesterday I was detained, were here to ask for justice. They are scared that were again seeking resignation. I lied because my parents will be scared if I go out and something happens, but I do not blame them completely, she said. Meanwhile, many independent journalists and other protesters, who had sat outside the Parliament Street police station till Saturday night demanding accountability, returned on Sunday morning to demand the registration of an FIR into the allegations raised by the three women journalists. The Crime Branch has now been tasked with investigating the matter, officers said on Saturday. Rishabh Ranjan, who works with the All India Congress Committee AICC law department and represents one of the women journalists who raised the allegation against the officers, said the police still had not registered an FIR, even though she was taken to RML hospital last night for a Medico-Legal Case MLC. We had gone inside with an expectation that a senior police officer at least of a rank of DCP would speak to us and share what was the reason that they transferred the case to the Crime Branch. We dont know whether they have named the person in the complaint registered or not. We wanted them to register a zero FIR, he said.

articleTitle: Who is Alexis Wilkins, country singer engaged to FBI Director Kash Patel
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UFC Freedom 250 Trump
description: FBI Director Kash Patel and country singer Alexis Wilkins have announced their engagement. The couple has been dating since before Patel became FBI director in 2025.
body_raw: FBI Director Kash Patel got engaged to his longtime girlfriend, country singer Alexis Wilkins. The couple announced their engagement in a post on X on Sunday evening. Alexis Wilkins, 27, shared a black-and-white photo of herself with Kash Patel, 46, showing her engagement ring. She captioned the post Went and got the law involved. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Alexis Wilkins alexiswilkins Kash Patel and Alexis Wilkins have been dating since before he became FBI director in 2025, when she attended his swearing-in ceremony. Who is Alexis Wilkins? Alexis Wilkins met Kash Patel in late 2022 at a party hosted by country musician John Rich in Nashville. Patel, then a Truth Social consultant and former Trump aide, was selling KH merchandise and books praising Donald Trump. Wilkins, who was trying to launch her country music career, was introduced to him at the party. They began dating by early 2023. Wilkins grew up partly in London and Switzerland and attended elementary school in Geneva before graduating from Belmont University in Nashville in 2020. She briefly pursued acting in Los Angeles, appearing in two episodes of Modern Family, before focusing on country music. Her debut single, Holdin On, was released in 2020. She now performs patriotic songs at conservative events, though her website lists no upcoming shows. Country music critic Kyle Coroneos described her as an aspiring artist and rated her rendition of the US national anthem 7.5 out of 10. Alexis Wilkins released her debut album in 2023 and has been affiliated with conservative groups. On her website, she describes her music as honouring country tradition while adding contemporary commentary. Wilkins also made headlines as a performer at President Donald Trumps Great American State Fair on the National Mall as part of America 250, as other artists pulled out of the event after finding out it was not a non-partisan celebration. FBI protective team escorted Alexis Wilkins to run errands, hair appointments According to a report by The New York Times, last April, FBI agents in two SUVs stood guard outside a senior centre in Dixon, Illinois, while Alexis Wilkins performed for a few dozen young conservatives. Dianna Muller, founder of Women for Gun Rights, which briefly employed Wilkins as a spokeswoman, said When Kash got confirmed, life changed for her. Kash Patel has faced criticism over his use of government aircraft for trips with no known or apparent law enforcement purpose. This included an FBI jet flight to State College, Pennsylvania, for a pro-wrestling event where Alexis Wilkins performed the national anthem. Alexis Wilkins also had a full-time protective team comprising Special Weapons and Tactics team members from FBI field offices across the US, The New York Times reported. The team accompanied her to engagements including singing appearances and even a hair appointment. In May 2025, Kash Patel attended a secret national security conference at an exclusive resort outside London and invited Alexis Wilkins to a group dinner with King Charles III at Windsor Castle. When UK police declined to pick her up from the airport, the FBI arranged tactical agents and an embassy vehicle for her, according to a report by The New York Times. The disclosure raised questions over the use of taxpayer-funded resources for Patels personal activities. An FBI spokesman told the New York Times that active death threats against Wilkins warranted the level of protection she was receiving.

articleTitle: Jorge Jesus won’t bend, and Cristiano Ronaldo cannot be bent
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Perhaps both Ronaldo and Jesus could look into the mirror and see each other. (AP Photo)
description: Portugal's coach Jorge Jesus picks his team by his own system, even when it means leaving out the country's greatest footballer
body_raw: Some time next week, or next month, Cristiano Ronaldo will reveal his side of the story. Of his latest, dramatic falling out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus. The coach has offered glimpses of his version in a press conference that the countrys greatest footballer didnt suit the tactical demands of the game. Rumours and speculation have swirled like a juicy whodunit. Spanish journalist and Ronaldos close friend Edu Aguirre claims the footballer felt betrayed. There supposedly was a closed-door meeting between the Portuguese football federation, Ronaldo and the coach, in which Jesus apologised to Ronaldo and said he would offer a public apology. Instead, he emphatically defended his decision to not play him against Norway in a press conference, only moments later. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo cristiano Numerous inside stories, half-truth and half-fiction, will spill out, dividing a country and the footballing universe. But the falling out was imminent, considering the collision of two headstrong, egoistic personalities the coach who considers himself a supreme force and a footballer who believes he is gods gift to the sport. Only no one expected the relationship to unravel so fast. There were hints, when you revisit Jesuss first press conference, where he said, I wouldnt stand up to anyone. The coachs methods and his unflinching devotion to his ideals made a clash likely. Jesus, 72 and with flowing silvering locks, might not be the most fabled tactician of his times. He was a modest footballer, a midfielder whose career had more stops than a shuttle train 13 clubs in 17 years, largely in the lower rungs of the Portuguese league. He was an uncelebrated manager, whose best years were spent with Benfica 2009 to 2015, with stops in Brazil, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, in a career that began when Ronaldo was five. But most players he has managed either love or loathe him. To some, including Pablo Aimar, Fabio Coentrao and David Luiz, he is the greatest coach they have played under. To others, he is an autocrat. On his first day at Benfica, he made the players train for four hours without a break, without letting them have a swig of water. He made them train twice a day, would shout and berate, but at the end of the day, former Portugal international Fernando Mendes said, we knew we had a great friend in him. To the players who rebelled, he would say Inside the club, only one person gives me the orders. The president. No one else. Those who revolted against his exhaustive regimen, he ruthlessly relegated to the bench. He was so secretive in his tactics that he revealed them to his assistants only on the morning of the game. The rigorous methods reaped rewards. Benfica won the league the first year he joined them. In the next six years, the club won two more, in what was their most successful era this century. His tactics shape-shifted, but were always thrilling and intense. He claims he doesnt follow prototypes. Some only copy what others do. I dont. God gave me the opportunity to be a creator, Jesus once told ESPN Brazil, after guiding Flamengo to five titles in a year. He has no dogmatic guiding philosophy and swears by no idol, even though he spends hours studying the patterns and principles of all accomplished coaches. But there are core principles, as seen in Portugals demolition of Denmark. They hounded the Danes with fluid aggression and heavy counter-pressing, and defended in a compact mid-block. He used three different formations in four games, but they were less tactical decisions than structural ones. Portugal played with a sense of identity that it had seldom shown before. It was evident why he ignored Ronaldo, and why he could again in the coming matches. He needs pace upfront, he wants his number nine to press aggressively, he demands heavy work off the ball. Ronaldo, at 41, is still a prolific scorer, but he failed to fulfil his off-the-ball shifts in the 67 minutes he played against Wales. Jesus has not shut the door in Ronaldos face. After beating Norway on Sunday he said There are no bad feelings with Cristiano. For the next call-up, if Cristiano is playing and wants to be with the national team, then why not? There are shades of the Ronaldo-Erik ten Hag skirmish, but with a more brazen edge. Perhaps both of them could look into the mirror and see each other. A coach who believes in ultimate supremacy, built on smouldering ego. Its his burnishing hubris that made Ronaldo, Jose Mourinho would say. Its the flaming ego that made Jesus too. It reflected in the words that explained Ronaldos benching I told him I would take him to the bench and that, if I needed him for 30 minutes, he would play. But I saw the game differently, so he didnt come on. It wont be Cristiano, or any other player, who changes my ideas as a coach. Never. Neither him nor anyone else. Not even a president. Never. Zero. Perhaps Ronaldos endgame was written the day the federation chose Jesus to succeed Roberto Martinez, who indulged Ronaldo with disastrous results.

articleTitle: Janhvi Kapoor calls her Chuttamalle AI video with NTR ‘assault’: ‘Reality of being a woman’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor opens up on AI edits of her Devara song "Chuttamalle".
description: Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor were featured in deepfake video of the Chuttamalle song. The actress has finally reacted to the ongoing controversy.
body_raw: Actor Janhvi Kapoor has called out the misuse of AI to objectify women as an AI-generated inappropriate video featuring her with Devara co-star Jr NTR from the track Chuttamalle emerged on social media. She compared the explicit video to assault as many leading voices from the South film industries supported her. The morphed clip showed Janhvi in a sexually explicit scene, that was never a part of the original song. After the video went viral on the internet, NTR criticised such distasteful videos, threatening legal action against them. Chiranjeevi, Khushbu Sundar, Vijay Deverakonda, and others also extended their support to Janhvi. Taking to her Instagram handle, Janhvi Kapoor slammed the criminal misuse of technology. The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulate fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this, and women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it, she started her long note. ALSO READ Janhvi Kapoor lauds Telugu film industrys work hours Nap for 20 minutes The actor continued, Consent, choice and respect for a womans body should be among the most basic notions of humanity. Yet somehow, they continue to be treated as complicated. They are not. It is surprising that it still seems too nuanced for some people to understand that even if a woman says yes five days in a row and no on the sixth, that no must be respected. If she happens to wear a miniskirt, it does not give anyone permission to put a camera up her skirt, capture violating angles or visually exploit her body. What a woman is comfortable with, where she draws the line and what she chooses to do with her body are decisions that belong exclusively to her. This is basic. Janhvi mentioned that the issue goes beyond what she has ever experienced in her entire career. It is about the larger reality of being a woman, the gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety, and the feeling that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere, when we have not even adequately addressed the very real, physical fear that continues to disrupt the lives of women every day. She highlighted that facing such things is a reality of being a woman. To conclude her note, she thanked her co-star NTR, and other actors for their support, including, Chiranjeevi, Vijay Deverakonda and Khushbu Sundar. I am deeply touched by NTR sir for taking such a strong stand and condemning this violation. Thank you, sir. When someone whom millions look up to speaks up about something that may not directly concern him, it makes a difference to every woman who has experienced some degree of this behaviour. Thank you also to Chiranjeevi sir, Vijay and Khushbu maam for amplifying that sentiment and calling for action against this mentality and these immoral practices. Janhvi Kapoor and Jr NTRs film Devara Part 1 released in September 2024. The concerned song Chuttamalle, was composed by Anirudh Ravichander and sung by Shilpa Rao, turning out to be one of the most famous tracks from the film.

articleTitle: IIT Delhi scholar dies of injuries after suicide attempt, FIR filed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The police were subsequently informed and Anand was rushed to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where he remained under treatment. (File Photo)
description: Police said that prima facie, the scholar, identified as Manish Anand who lived in Kishangarh’s Munirka village, attempted to die by suicide.
body_raw: Delhi Police has registered a case of abetment to suicide after an IIT-Delhi PhD scholar, who was allegedly found in an injured and unconscious state inside his rented room in South East Delhi on August 18, died during treatment on Saturday, an officer said on Sunday. Police said that prima facie, the scholar, identified as Manish Anand who lived in Kishangarhs Munirka village, attempted to die by suicide. According to the police, the door of his room was locked from the inside. They said his neighbours had to break the door open. The police were subsequently informed and Anand was rushed to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where he remained under treatment. Anand died on Saturday while undergoing treatment. An FIR was registered at Kishangarh police station under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS on Sunday, a police officer said. The FIR was registered based on directions from the Supreme Court-led National Task Force NTF, constituted in March last year to address mental health concerns and prevent suicides in higher educational institutions, police said. The task force was formed after students and family members of deceased students filed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking inquiries into incidents of suspicious deaths. The case has been registered on the basis of a complaint and the courts directions. An investigation is underway, the officer said. Police said that neither Anands family nor anyone else had, during the course of the initial inquiry, raised suspicion or levelled any allegation against anyone in connection with the incident. Police said they also examined CCTV footage from cameras installed outside the rented accommodation Anand lived in. The footage did not indicate the presence of any suspicious person entering or leaving the premises around the time of the incident, they said. The police are yet to ascertain how Anand sustained the injuries.

articleTitle: CAT 2026 form correction window begins; check last date

description: The form correction facility will remain active for candidates to submit their changes until 5 pm on October 6. IIM Indore has outlined in its notice that the aforementioned deadline will not be extended.
