articleTitle: Supreme Court seeks Election Commission response to plea against chief Gyanesh Kumar after Express investigation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Gyanesh Kumar
description: The petitioner has urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority.
body_raw: Supreme Court Hears Plea on CEC Gyanesh Kumar Highlights The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice on petitions questioning the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, calling for an SIT probe against him and seeking to declare the nationwide SIR of electoral rolls illegal. A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant and also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard the matter today. The petitions were filed days after The Indian Express reported that ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR of electoral rolls. The two commissioners said some of the decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. The two ECs separately wrote to the countrys top bureaucrat, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan, flagging concerns over the integrity of voter software. The ECI said the letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation and were not related to policy or IT division matters. Arguments before Court Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Vikas Singh argued that amendments made to the law governing the Election Commission in 2023 had significantly enlarged the powers and protections available to the Chief Election Commissioner. Singh particularly referred to Section 16, a new provision introduced in the 2023 Act that grants protection from civil and criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge of official duties. Singh argued that the new immunity provision was not present in the earlier law and said that it made the Election Commission even more powerful than any other constitutional functionary in the country. He sought interim measures, including the immediate suspension of CEC Gyanesh Kumar or, alternatively, divesting him of the authority to act as CEC. Let us first have an authenticated information, the CJI said. Justice Bagchi questioned whether the court could, without hearing the respondents, assume that all the decisions in question had been taken unilaterally. Can we ex-parte come to a decision that all the decisions were unilateral?, Justice Bagchi asked. The court thus issued notice to the Election Commission, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the other two Election Commissioners. Pleas before court One of the petitions by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh referred to the alleged differences between CEC Kumar and Sandhu and Joshi and the objections raised by them. Article 3241 of the Constitution does not vest the superintendence, direction and control of elections in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It vests those powers in a Commission, said the plea. The petitioner urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority. The petitioner argued that the SIR was undertaken without the necessary statutory or constitutional authority and without following the procedure required by law. The other petition by Delhi-based lawyer Shailendra Mani Tripathi has sought a probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or an SIT headed by a retired judge of the top court. The petition refers to unprecedented constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the ECI under the CEC as exposed by documentary records published on September 23, 2026. The plea said the alleged act of. CEC Kumar. falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability. The petition seeks directions to declare all decisions, guidelines, directives, and software modifications initiated, approved, or implemented under Gyanesh Kumar without full Commission concurrence or contrary to the majority opinion of the Election Commissioners under Section 18 of the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023 as unconstitutional. It further seeks quashing of the unauthorised modifications made to Form 6 on the ECINetERONet portal requiring ancestrylast-SIR declarations, and directing the immediate restoration of statutory Form 6 as prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and permit all eligible adults to register as voters on the basis of original statutory requirements.

articleTitle: Trump’s Brazil blooper: ‘125 million voted in India’s Presidential Election’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Brazil-India
description: Trump's post came a day after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, 4 October.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that 125 million people voted in the first round of Indias Presidential Election. The vote he described appears to be Brazils election, which was held on Sunday, 4 October. Trump used the post to say that US results take too long to count. He wrote that in Detroit, Philadelphia, California and other cities and states, results with far smaller numbers often take weeks. He ended with Voting in America is CORRUPT. In the post he first wrote the word Rig and then corrected it to calculate. Photo realDonaldTrump About 124.5 million Brazilians cast votes on Sunday, which is close to the figure Trump used, according to figures cited by Courthouse News. The post came a day after Brazils first round, which sent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva and Senator Flvio Bolsonaro to a runoff. In the post, Trump said the results of the vote he described came out soon after polls closed, on the same day. He compared this with the US, where he said counts in some cities and states take weeks even though the numbers are much smaller. He signed off as President DJT. The post gave no evidence for his claims about US vote counting. Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, 4 October. With nearly all votes counted, Flvio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, came first with about 47 of valid votes, Reuters said. Lula came second with about 45. Neither man won more than half of the valid votes, so the two will face each other in a second round on 25 October. Brazil has nearly 159 million registered voters. About 124.5 million of them voted, and about 21 did not, according to figures cited by Courthouse News. The result gave a lift to the Bolsonaro family. Flvio was picked by his father to carry on the familys political work. Other family members and allies also won seats in Congress or state governor races. Meanwhile, India does not choose its president by a nationwide vote. The president is elected by an Electoral College. It is made up of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the state legislative assemblies, including Delhi and Puducherry. The vote uses proportional representation with a single transferable vote, and the ballot is secret.

articleTitle: OpenAI’s Sam Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sam Altman said that OpenAI has signed a deal with the US government to deploy AI models in the Department of War's classified networks.
description: Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI ⁠regulation.
body_raw: OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks and argued the technology should remain broadly accessible to the public We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency, Altman said in an interview with Politicos technology-focused newsletter Decoded. Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI regulation, adding I think theres a lot of daylight. I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like, This technology is going to get so powerful, and its so dangerous, that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens, and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits, Altman said. He called that a completely unacceptable trade-off that runs counter to the lighter-touch regulatory stance backed by OpenAI. I wouldnt take a trade of saying, Well make sure theres no major hacks, theres no misuse of this technology, theres zero scams, theres zero all the other bad things that will happen, Altman said. Because I think people will do tremendously - orders of magnitude more - good stuff than bad stuff. Altmans remarks come amid a growing debate within the AI industry over the pace of development and the risks posed by increasingly capable systems. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in September published an essay calling on the industry to slow down to pace the frontier, a stance that Altman publicly endorsed. Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, saying the people building AI believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic warned that, despite AIs potential benefits, the technology can sometimes act in ways that run counter to its makers intentions and penetrate other companies systems. The company said advanced models could exhibit self-preserving behaviors, including attempts to resist shutdown, conceal or manipulate information, or generate outputs that could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative. However, US President Donald Trump has largely dismissed calls for new restrictions, arguing they would make it harder for American companies to compete with Chinese rivals. He has repeatedly said existing law enforcement agencies, including the Justice Department, provide sufficient safeguards and that no new rules are needed.

articleTitle: Israeli singer learns Shah Rukh Khan song to honour Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Israeli singer dedicates Hindi song to Captain Smit
description: The musician learned the Hindi song and dedicated his performance to “brave” Captain Machchhar and Indians worldwide.
body_raw: Israeli-American musician Itay Benda paid a musical tribute to Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot who confronted a colleague mid-air and helped avert an alleged attempt to crash a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. In a gesture of gratitude following the attack aboard the flight, Benda specially learned a Hindi song and dedicated his performance to brave Captain Machchhar and Indians around the world. Benda described the performance as his small way of saying thank you. The now-viral video shows Benda singing Shah Rukh Khans popular song Tujh Mein Rab Dikhta Hai. Originally sung by Roop Kumar Rathore, the song is from Khans 2008 romantic comedy, Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi. Watch here Im impressed by this Israeli- Americans Hindi pronunciation when he sings a tribute to Captain Smit Machchhar. Enjoy the voice of Itay Benda. - Dina Shakti DinaShakti October 3, 2026 What a touching effort The video has since gone viral across all social media platforms, garnering a wave of reactions. The most apt song chosen to give praise and thanks to Capt Smit. What a touching effort to show your love and appreciation, a user wrote. Thank you very much from an Indian for singing such an appropriate song, another user commented. Very appropriate song for the occasion and you sing very well with good Hindi. Thank from all my Indian friends, a third user reacted. The tribute comes as Captain Machchhar has been praised for helping protect those on board during the attack. On September 30, Flydubai flight FZ1073, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was forced to make an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed Captain Machchhar and attempted to interfere with the aircrafts controls. The plane was carrying 174 people, all of whom survived.

articleTitle: New process helps remove toxins, pick rare earth metals from wastewater
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT Gandhinagar engineers a 'Molecular Fishing Net' that filters toxic heavy metals and recovers rare earth elements from waste water. (Image credit: IIT Gandhinagar)
description: IIT Gandhinagar, University of Cambridge, and University of Birmingham researchers develop a method to remove toxic heavy metals from waste water and recover rare-earth elements in it
body_raw: Researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology, Gandhinagar IITGN, University of Cambridge and University of Birmingham have jointly developed a method that they said will help capture toxic metals and recover valuable rare earth elements RREs from waste water. The protocol uses highly porous materials called metal-organic frameworks MOFs, according to a study, published in Nature Protocols. We generally throw away a broken camera lens, earphones, or an old phone that has stopped working and is beyond repair. However, these objects have rare earth elements RREs that have applications in magnets, superconductivity, optics, and batteries, among others. When such objects become part of water, recovering REEs becomes difficult, said Superb Misra, Jibaben Patel Chair Professor in the Department of Materials Engineering, IITGN, and the Principal Investigator of the Bio Nano Materials Group. On the other hand, industrial activities can introduce toxic metals such as lead, cadmium, nickel and manganese into water, he said, adding that the challenge is removing these unwanted and harmful metal pollutants from water and recapturing the valuable REEs. How the filter works Researchers said the MOF functions as a molecular fishing net. Its countless pores spread out a vast catching surface, while specially designed chemical sites act like hooks that can latch on to particular metals. The researchers tuned this net in such a way that it preferentially traps the metals they are looking for. Simply speaking, it is like identifying and specifically picking red and green coloured marbles from a bucket containing hundreds of marbles in different colours, they explained. Some MOFs can have internal surface areas of up to 7,000 square metres per gram. To put that number in perspective, one gram may look like a tiny pinch of powder, but inside it is a surface area comparable to an entire football field. This huge internal surface makes MOFs very good adsorbents, they said. While conventional methods such as precipitation, coagulation and flocculation can be useful for water treatment, they are generally sensitive to pH, with optimal removal confined to narrow ranges. Broadly speaking, precipitation lets heavy impurities settle out, coagulation makes impurities clump together, and flocculation makes small impurity clumps collide and grow into larger clusters that can be separated, Prof Misra explained. Beyond laboratory Industrial effluents-discharged from manufacturing, mining, and chemical processing - entering water bodies contain several metals and contaminants such as pesticides, detergents and organic pollutants. The specially designed MOFs can be used as an adsorbent for the recovery and removal of metals under controlled conditions. The protocol was tested in complex real-world scenarios. For example, it was tested using wastewater that is alkaline pH over 8.5, turbid, and high in dissolved solid impurities. The method was also tested in artificial seawater and e-waste-derived samples. The workflow developed in this study can be applied to similar adsorbents and other contaminants, researchers said. The MOF, in our protocol, demonstrated substantial adsorption capacities, said Dhruv Menon, who did BTech from IITGN and is currently a doctoral student in the Department of Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology at the University of Cambridge, United Kingdom. One gram of copper-based MOF can capture nearly half a gram of lead 490 mgg, and roughly a quarter of a gram each of cadmium 264 mgg and manganese 226 mgg. For rare-earth elements, it could capture around one-third of a gram per gram of material 351 mgg of neodymium, 343 mgg of yttrium, 335 mgg of dysprosium, 337 mgg of terbium and 345 mgg of europium, Menon said, citing their experiments. Towards sustainability There is a need for approaches that can solve multiple environmental challenges simultaneously. Our focus was on engineering the performance of MOFs to employ them for environmental remediation applications. That said, it is crucial to understand that controlled batch experiments cannot fully predict behaviours in complex wastewater. There is a need to look at factors like large-scale fabrication, cost analyses, MOF life-cycle assessment and regulatory testing, Dr Misra said. Other team members involved in the study include Prathmesh Bhadane PhD, IITGN Postdoctoral fellow, IIT Bombay, Priya Mahato doctoral student, IITGN, Prateek Goyal PhD, IITGN, Dr Iseult Lynch Professor, School of Geography, Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Birmingham, UK, and Dr Swaroop Chakraborty NERC Fellow, University of Birmingham.

articleTitle: Asian Games tour diary: Earthquake warnings, getting lost underground and a city too polite to say ‘no’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: For much of the fortnight, I have had the feeling that Aichi-Nagoya does not really want to host the Asian Games, but is far too polite to say no. (PTI Photo)
description: Earthquake warnings, a station maze, a last cookie and a closing-ceremony horse from a fortnight in Aichi-Nagoya
body_raw: Day 0 Care, caution I land in Nagoya, pick up my credentials and receive a media kit. I think of the Tokyo Olympics, my last trip to Japan. The welcome kit for those pandemic Games came with dozens of tubes, bottles and QR codes, all tied to the daily ritual of Covid-19 testing. This time, there is no reminder to spit into those tubes before even brushing. Instead, there is earthquake and tsunami safety guidance. Navigating earthquakes, it turns out, is one of the trickier parts of living here. Around 1,500 earthquakes are felt across the country each year, most of them harmless. But the government warns of a magnitude 8-9 Nankai Trough earthquake in the next 30 years, and Nagoya, sitting in the Nankai region, is among the areas considered particularly vulnerable. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage So, the warnings are everywhere. Evacuation zones are marked outside the athletes plaza. Safety advisories sit inside railway stations. Competition venues have their own instructions. Before play begins, the giant screen invariably flashes a reminder of what to do, and what not to do, in the event of an earthquake or tsunami. On the first day, I notice every one of them. Twenty-four hours later, I barely register them. The media kit contains another, more thoughtful item masks for neck, shoulder and leg pain. Because the other hazard of these Games is much less dramatic the walking. As the days pass, the step count keeps climbing. It peaks on October 1, when I travel between Nagoya, Obu and Okazaki, using the train-bus-train combination that has become something of a recurring feature of these Games. By the end of the day, I have covered 15.02 km on foot. If nothing else, these Games are going to do wonders for my annual step-count target. Day 1 Lost in the maze Nagoya Station is the sort of place that makes me question my own sense of direction. Above ground, there are trains, towers, roads and people moving in every direction. Below ground is another city platforms on different levels, underground passages disappearing around corners, shopping arcades, staircases, escalators and exits that seem to multiply the further I walk. While returning from a venue, I am completely lost. Google Maps suggests a train, then a bus to another station that would take me to Kinjofuto, where the main media hub is and the cruise liner for athletes is docked. I am used to the coarse pudhe chala move ahead of BEST conductors in Mumbai, the instruction delivered at full volume, with the assumption that I will somehow figure out the rest. Here, the woman bus driver wears a face mask, a crisp white shirt and a black jacket. At the Tokai-dori stop, she picks up the microphone and individually thanks every passenger who gets in. Arigato gozaimasu. There are perhaps 13-15 of us who get in. She thanks all of us. By the end of the day, at around 11.30pm, I am lost again somewhere underneath Nagoya. I am standing at a Kintetsu platform, staring at my phone and trying to work out whether the train waiting on Platform 1 will take me to Komeno, from where my apartment is a 7-minute walk. I find a uniformed woman and show her my phone. She squints at the screen. Nods. I hop in, and three minutes later, hop off. Then, just as the doors are about to close, the same woman steps out of the captains cabin. She looks at me. Checks that I have got off at the right station. Gives me a thumbs-up. Gets back in. The train chugs away into the darkness. I stand on the platform wondering if she really comes out just to make sure the lost foreigner gets off at the right station. Day 3 Early morning trek The city gradually disappears. The bus windows lose the towers and dense buildings. Then come fields, little houses, narrow roads, wooded slopes. By the time it drops us off, I am in a sleepy rural corner of Toyota City, with another kilometre to walk to the venue. It is early morning. The road is quiet. On either side are dense stands of trees, the hills rising behind them in layers of green. There are stretches where the only sound is my own footsteps. And somewhere inside this landscape is a shooting range. The venue is secluded, surrounded by the forest. It is a beautiful setting for a sport that demands a Zen-like state from its athletes. Reaching the venue and getting back takes up an entire day, but you dont really mind. By afternoon the weather changes, it starts to drizzle, then, almost theatrically, the sky turns orange and a rainbow appears across the hills. After making me trek into the middle of nowhere, Aichi decides to show off. Day 4 The last cookie The chocolate cookies at the venues are a hit. A serious hit. They disappear almost as soon as they arrive, which means that after a few days, spotting a fresh batch creates the sort of urgency usually reserved for breaking news. Late evening at the main media centre, I walk towards the lounge for a coffee and spot one last cookie sitting there. From the opposite direction, I notice a Malaysian journalist heading for the same cookie. He has seen it too. We continue walking, each pretending this is a perfectly normal stroll and not a race for the final chocolate cookie of the evening. We reach it at almost exactly the same time. There is a brief moment of politeness. He offers it to me. I to him. He insists. I insist. Eventually, I take it. India wins. Day 6 100 not out A friend points me to a report in Japan Today, which says the countrys population of people aged 100 or older has crossed one lakh for the first time. The number sounds abstract. Then I look at the volunteers. At subway stations, there are elderly men and women standing beside signs, helping confused tourists find the right platform. At venues, they shepherd athletes through security. At gates, they stand for hours, pointing, explaining, smiling. Some look old enough to be my grandparents. And yet they are here, wearing their volunteer uniforms and doing the most ordinary jobs required to make a giant sporting event work. A few I speak to say they wanted to volunteer at the Tokyo Olympics. The pandemic took that opportunity away. So they are here now. Day 8 Of flavoured KitKat and sake The shooting qualification hall is buzzing with athletes, coaches, officials and the usual post-event shuffle. An Indian shooter finishes his event, opens a matcha-flavoured KitKat and starts eating it. Then comes the story. The previous evening, he accidentally tries the sake-flavoured KitKat. It tasted so bitter. Tasted like desi daaru country-made liquor. He laughs. One finger, apparently, is enough. He tries it once and decides that is quite enough Japanese alcohol for the rest of the trip. Day. I lose track A little Brazil in Toyota Toyota is supposed to be the land of cars. Instead, somewhere between the factories and farms, there is a little piece of Brazil. I know it is Brazil because a football futbol, rather base sits amid open farmland, with low buildings, fields and long stretches of green around it. Then I start noticing the signs. Portuguese. On trains. On hoardings. Around the neighbourhood. Some 60,000-odd Brazilians live in the Aichi prefecture, the highest of any prefecture in Japan. The Brazil-town is not announced with a grand landmark. It is simply there, woven into the landscape. For a few minutes, rural Japan feels slightly Brazilian. Look up A citys fight against screen time I watch the queue inch forward, but almost nobody looks up. Heads are bowed, thumbs flicking, faces lit by the glow of phone screens. A few feet away, people are waiting together, yet each seems to be somewhere else. It feels familiar. We see the same thing all the time in India. But here in Japan, at least one politician has decided to do something about it. Or, more accurately, try. In Toyoake, a city in Aichi, the local government introduced a guideline last year encouraging residents to keep leisure-time smartphone and electronic-device use to about two hours a day. It isnt a ban, there are no penalties, and the city isnt asking people to abandon their phones. The idea is simply to make them look up a little more. The concern, the mayor, Masafumi Koki, tells me, is what gets displaced by those hours sleep, exercise, hobbies and face-to-face conversations. A survey conducted among residents revealed that there is a certain correlation between prolonged smartphone usage and feelings of loneliness, Koki says. A year on, the city is still trying to find out whether the experiment has worked. With 43.2 per cent of participants reporting some behavioural changes or shifts in awareness following the enactment of the ordinance, it is viewed as having been sufficiently effective, Koki says. When the Games leave Usually, the last day of a Games feels like a small bereavement. The venues begin to empty. People who have shared trains, buses, press tribunes and hurried coffees for a fortnight begin saying their goodbyes. There is usually a strange emptiness in the air, the feeling that a little travelling circus is packing itself up and leaving town. This time, I dont feel it. I dont really feel sad that these Games are over. Perhaps because these have been among the strangest Games I have covered. For much of the fortnight, I have had the feeling that Aichi-Nagoya does not really want to host the Asian Games, but is far too polite to say no. So it does what Japan does so well accommodates. Tens of thousands of athletes, officials, volunteers, journalists and support staff arrive, and the city makes room for all of them. But it never quite feels as if the city is curious about them. People dont seem particularly interested in discovering new sports or watching athletes from countries they know little about. The stands remain patchy. The city centre, around which almost everything here seems to revolve, never really feels as though an Asian Games is happening around it. There are no crowds spilling into the streets. No obvious sporting frenzy. No sense that the city has been taken over by the Games. Its strangely fitting then that at the closing ceremony, the biggest cheer comes when Qatars equestrian rider enters the stadium on horseback, takes the Asian Games flag, and then rides out with it. Maybe Nagoyans are simply thrilled by the sight of a horse. Maybe, for a brief moment, the spectacle finally cuts through. Or maybe they are happy that the fortnight is over. On Monday morning, Nagoya gets back to being Nagoya. The trains fill up, and people head to work, as if the Games never happened.

articleTitle: ‘Can get parole for own wedding’: Karnataka High Court allows murder convict 15 days
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court murder convict wedding parole
description: The case arose after the prison authorities rejected the convict’s request for emergency parole, saying it could be granted only in specific circumstances, including the marriage of a child or sibling.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court has allowed a man serving a life sentence for murder to leave prison for 15 days for his marriage, holding that a convicts own wedding can also fall within the reasons for granting parole. The court said it would be unreasonable to exclude a convicts wedding from the reasons for parole, while making the release subject to conditions. Justice B M Shyam Prasad was hearing a petition filed by the convicts mother and his prospective bride. They had challenged the May 9, 2025 decision of the superintendent of Central Prison, Parappana Agrahara, Bengaluru, refusing emergency parole to the murder convict. The question is whether the convict must be admitted to parole for solemnization of his own marriage. This Court is of the view that this reason must also fall within the fold of the reasons for which a convict is admitted to parole and to hold otherwise would be unreasonable, the court said on September 24. The case arose after the prison authorities rejected the request for emergency parole, saying it could be granted only in specific circumstances, including the marriage of a son, daughter, brother or sister. The petitioners challenged the refusal and sought 15 days release for the convicts marriage. Cant exclude own wedding from reasons for parole Justice Prasad noted that the undisputed position was that the convict could be admitted to general parole to attend a siblings marriage, among other reasons. The court then considered whether the same principle could apply when the convict himself was getting married. It held that the convicts own marriage must also fall within the fold of the reasons for which heshe could be admitted to parole. The other conditions governing parole would still have to be satisfied, the judge added. The ruling, hence, did not mean that every prisoner seeking to marry would automatically be entitled to temporary release but that the convicts own wedding could not simply be excluded from the reasons for considering parole. Court considers pending proceedings The imprisonment certificate dated January 16, 2025, also referred to other pending criminal proceedings against the convict. Documents relating to those proceedings were placed before the high court in support of the petitioners contention that they could not be used to refuse parole. The court noted that the convict had already been granted bail in the other pending cases, either by the high court or the sessions court, while in one of the proceedings, his bail was subject to submitting surety in cash. The high court took note of these orders while examining whether the pending proceedings could prevent the grant of parole. It then observed that no other conditions had been pointed out which could constitute a reason to refuse emergency parole to the convict. The high court then allowed the petition and directed the prison authorities to grant the convict 15 days of general parole, even though the petition had challenged the refusal of emergency parole. The parole was also subject to the terms contemplated under the Karnataka Prisons and Correctional Services Manual, 2021. The court also imposed specific safeguards on the mans release, including that the convict must mark his attendance with the jurisdictional police every three days. He must also not leave the jurisdiction of the concerned police station without the express permission of the station house officer SHO.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3 writer says wrote 100 versions of film: ‘Friends tried to bribe me for ending’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 writer says wrote 100 versions of film
description: Ajay Devgn starrer Drishyam 3's screenwriter recently recalled writing more than 100 versions of the blockbuster film, that he had almost lost count.
body_raw: Ajay Devgn returned as the iconic Vijay Salgaonkar in his latest release Drishyam 3 The Conclusion. After two successful parts, the third installment of the Drishyam franchise is also following the same footsteps. The film has emerged a winner, both critically and commercially, collecting over Rs 270 crore worldwide within three days. As the storytelling and climax of Drishyam 3 is being widely discussed, the films screenwriter Aamil Keeyan Khan, opened up about working on the final chapter. During a conversation with The Free Press Journal, he shared, I have folders inside folders, drafts with dates, numbers, dates after numbers, and files called things like FINAL, FINAL 2, FINAL FINAL and presumably FINAL PLEASE GOD. I have genuinely lost count, but well over a hundred drafts in different forms. Easily. The makers of Drishyam 3 also took strict steps to keep the films major twists under wraps. Aamil Khan revealed that the ending of the film was not shared with most of the cast and crew. Abhishek basically ran the production like Vijay Salgaonkar would. The climax wasnt given to a large part of the crew. People got information on a need-to-know basis, he said. He continued, Sometimes a department only knew what it needed to execute a scene, not necessarily why it was executing it. A lot of actors and crew from the film, and my own friends and relatives, tried to bribe me for the ending. But like Gaitonde, I remained honest and loyal to the producers. ALSO READ Tom Cruises Digger gets crushed by Ajay Devgns Drishyam 3, grosses Rs 1.30 crore in India The writer further explained how the screenplay was expected to maintain the identity of the franchise, while giving the audience something they had never experienced before. It was an enormous mountain to climb. You have a beloved franchise, a family that the audiences have lived with for years, and the legacy of two hugely loved films sitting on your shoulders. And most importantly, how do you surprise an audience for the third time? Khan added, In the first film, Vijay Salgaonkar is almost a blank slate. Now the audience knows him. They know how his mind works they know he has tricks up his sleeve, and frankly, theyre suspicious of everything the poor man does. Then there was the challenge of writing an original screenplay while retaining the DNA of Drishyam. It still had to have humour, family, emotion, drama and thrills without any one ingredient swallowing the others. It was a very, very thin tightrope. Thankfully, none of us looked down. About the film Drishyam 3 The Conclusion has been produced by Star Studio18 and Panorama Studios, and helmed by Abhishek Pathak, who also directed the previous instalment. He has also co-written the film with Aamil Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh. Besides Ajay Devgn, the Hindi thriller will features Tabu, reprising her role as IG Meera Deshmukh and Shriya Saran as Nandini. Actors Prakash Raj and Jaideep Ahlawat have also joined the star cast. The Hindi Drishyam franchise started in 2015 with the remake of Mohanlals Malayalam hit of the same name. The first Drishyam starring Ajay Devgn in Hindi language was also a huge success and it minted around Rs 110 crore worldwide. Drishyam 2, which hit the theatres in 2022, also emerged as a massive blockbuster, collecting around Rs 345 crore worldwide. Now, the latest Drishyam 3 has crossed Rs 272.8 crore worldwide in its first three days.

articleTitle: Accident death insurance rejected over ‘false information’, Andhra man secures Rs 50 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: consumer commission insurance post-mortem report death
description: The Kurnool District Consumer Commission was hearing a complaint filed by the deceased man’s brother and nominee challenging the rejection of his Rs 50 lakh insurance claim following the man’s fatal road accident.
body_raw: An Andhra Pradesh consumer commission has directed a private insurance company to pay Rs 50 lakh to the nominee of a man who died in a road accident, after the insurer rejected the claim citing alleged misrepresentation of facts. The commission also directed the insurer to pay Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 5,000 towards costs after finding that the insurers own investigator had called the accident genuine. Kurnool District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Karanam Kishore Kumar and members N Narayana Reddy and S Nazima Kausar were hearing a complaint filed by Yellala Jagadeeshawara Reddy, brother and nominee of Divakar Reddy Yellala, who died in the accident in April 2025. The insurance policy had a sum assured of Rs 50 lakh and was in force when the accident occurred. The rejectionnon-settlement of the claim by the Opposite Party the insurer, without establishing a valid and substantiated ground under the policy terms and conditions, amounts to deficiency in service. The complainant, being the nominee under the policy, is therefore entitled to receive the Sum Assured of Rs 50 lakh. Having regard to the prolonged non-settlement of the legitimate claim and the hardship and mental agony caused to the complainant, he is also entitled compensation, the commission said on October 1. The accident occurred when an unknown vehicle allegedly hit Divakars motorcycle at about 11.30 pm on April 14, 2025, on NH-40 near Ganesh Godown in Govindapalle village, Sirivella. Divakar suffered bleeding head injuries and died on the spot. His post-mortem report recorded Head Injury as the cause of death. Insurer rejects claim The insurance policy commenced on December 19, 2024, and was valid until December 18, 2025. The premium was Rs 4,767, and Jagadeeshawara Reddy was the nominee. The insurance nominee submitted the claim form on May 8, 2025. The insurer later sought additional documents and rejected the claim. In an email dated June 28, 2025, it said scrutiny and verification had revealed misrepresentation of facts to obtain the insurance benefit and that the claim fell outside the policy terms. The insurance company told the commission that the nominee had failed to provide documents despite repeated reminders. It said letters dated May 17, May 19, May 21 and May 25 had sought documents required to process the claim, including the final police report. But the commission found that the insurer had not produced evidence that these communications reached the complainant. No proof that notices reached nominee The commission noted that there were no postal receipts, acknowledgements, tracking reports, courier records, email delivery reports or other documentary evidence establishing that the alleged communications had been dispatched and served. It said that simply mentioning the dates of the communications was not enough to establish that they had been sent to or received by the complainant. The burden was upon the insurance company to establish that the complainant had been called upon to furnish the documents and given a reasonable opportunity to do so, the commission said. It also relied on the insurance companys own field verification report. The investigator found the incident to be genuine and the cause of death consistent with the post-mortem report. The commission said the investigation verified the complainants account of the accident and death. The commission found that the insurer had not identified the particular fact allegedly misrepresented by the deceased. It said the company had not established what declaration was false, when the alleged misrepresentation was made or how it was material to acceptance of the insurance risk. It said the insurance company had not shown that the absence of the final police report extinguished or suspended its liability under the policy. No evidence was produced to show that the report contained any finding adverse to the claim. Holding that the rejection of the claim was not supported by a valid ground under the policy terms, the commission held that it amounted to deficiency in service. The insurer was given 45 days from receipt of the order to comply. If it fails to pay within that period, the Rs 50 lakh sum assured will carry interest at 9 per cent per annum from October 6, 2025, the date of the complaint, until realisation. Takeaway If an insurer rejects a claim citing misrepresentation or missing documents, it should be able to clearly establish the specific violation and show that the claimant was properly asked to provide the required documents. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Andhra Pradesh helpline0866-2551431 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance. articleTitle: Sanjay Dutt, 67, speaks about bond with daughter Trishala: ‘We had a disconnect’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Trishala Dutt
description: Sanjay Dutt’s candid admission about his daughter Trishala sheds light on a complicated chapter in their relationship
body_raw: Sanjay Dutt, 67, recently spoke about his 38-year-old daughter, Trishala, who lives in New York, and reflected on their bond. Now she is a big lady. She does a lot of good work there. Its beautiful. I was in New York recently. We spent a lot of time together. We talk about her work, about my work. We had a disconnect in the middle. It happened for many reasons in my case.I was not to have her custody.old story now.I have seen a massive change in her. I am very, very proud of that, Dutt told actor and host Shekhar Suman on his late-night YouTube talk show Shekhar Tonite. Behind the word disconnect lies an experience thousands of families understand intimately, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach Delnna Rrajesh said. Divorce, separation, custody arrangements, legal difficulties, migration and circumstances beyond a childs control can sometimes physically separate a parent and child for years. We often discuss separation through the couples experience the marriage ended, custody was decided, homes changed. But for a child, something entirely different has happened. The relationship ended between two adults the childs family changed without the child ever choosing it. This is where we need greater psychological sensitivity. Custody determines where a child primarily lives and who has particular legal responsibilities it does not, by itself, measure the depth of a parents love or the childs attachment, shared Delnna. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. And everyday life matters enormously. Parenthood is not built only through birthdays, holidays and milestone photographs. It is built through school mornings, forgotten water bottles, fevers at midnight, homework, arguments about bedtime, car journeys, teenage moods and conversations that happen unexpectedly over dinner. When a parent and child are separated, these moments disappear. They may still love each other deeply while simultaneously grieving a relationship they are unable to fully live, Delnna told indianexpress.com. Psychology has a useful concept for some experiences of unresolved absence ambiguous loss. Unlike bereavement, where the loss itself is clear, ambiguous loss can involve someone who is still alive and emotionally significant but unavailable in the way they once were or are needed to be. In parent-child separation, the circumstances vary enormously and the concept will not describe every family, but it helps us understand why the grief can be so difficult to articulate. Nobody has died. Yet something precious may still have been lost, said Delnna. Reconciliation often becomes difficult when the parent begins by trying to correct history. That is why the goal shouldnt be to recover the lost years. The healthier task is to build the relationship that is possible now. We cannot retrieve childhood. We cannot attend yesterdays school function, wipe yesterdays tears or recreate yesterdays birthdays. But love does not belong only to the years that were lost. Where there is safety, accountability and willingness, it can also belong to the years that remain. A relationship can have a painful history without being sentenced to a painful future. Sometimes reconciliation is not about getting the past back at all. It is about refusing to let the years already lost take away the years two people may still have, said Delnna. articleTitle: 2020 Delhi riots cases seeking action against Sonia Gandhi, Anurag Thakur, cops dismissed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: On February 24, 2020, a communal riot had erupted on a service road near Chand Bagh on Wazirabad Road in Delhi. (Express Photo)
description: The petitions sought an independent probe into allegations of police excesses during the Jamia protests and the riots, and action against those accused of hate speech.
body_raw: A division bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain of the Delhi High Court on Monday junked 15 petitions, some of which sought an independent probe, including a judicial inquiry, into alleged police excesses against students at Jamia Millia Islamia JMI during the 2019 protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act and National Register of Citizens CAA-NRC, as well as compensation for the injured students. Refusing to issue any direction on petition seeking regulation of police action during public protests, the bench observed that the police did not enter the University premises at the outset to deal with an otherwise peaceful assembly confined to the campus and entered the campus after the situation outside and around the University had escalated and the crowd had moved into the campus. The court also dismissed pleas seeking the registration of criminal cases against politicians for alleged hate speeches made during the 2020 Northeast Delhi riots, ruling that there was no exceptional circumstance warranting such action. Among the leaders against whom action was sought were BJP leaders Parvesh Verma and Anurag Thakur, as well as Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Salman Khurshid, among others. Jamia violence On the allegations of police excesses within JMI, the bench ruled that the petitioners had failed to provide any material showing circumstances of actual or demonstrable institutional bias, malafides, deliberate suppression of material, failure to investigate material allegations, or such other defect as would render the existing process fundamentally unreliable. Noting that six years had passed since the riots, the court reasoned that a fresh inquiry at this stage would necessarily involve reexamination of events and material which have already formed part of statutory and judicial processes, and therefore refused to order any independent probe. On why it declined to issue directions regulating police action during public protests, the bench observed Once a gathering ceases to remain peaceful and the circumstances disclose violence, commission of cognizable offences or a threat to life or property, the police cannot be expected to remain inactive or as mute spectator merely because the gathering is taking place within a University campus.Where the situation requires immediate intervention, the police cannot be expected to remain outside merely because the premises belong to an educational institution., Thus, we are of the considered opinion that no fresh guidelines for regulation of police action during protests within educational institutions are required to be framed, the court concluded. Hate speech Similarly, the bench declined to issue any direction regarding the alleged hate speeches made during the riots. It recorded that since investigations in the incidents have substantially progressed and have culminated in the filing of charge-sheets in a large number of cases and numerous prosecutions are presently pending before the competent criminal courts, while several have culminated in judgments.It would neither be appropriate nor necessary for this Court.to issue any general directions regulating matters pending before competent courts. .The present case, in our considered view, does not disclose any such exceptional circumstance warranting a further direction for registration of criminal cases, the court observed What the petitions sought The petitions also varied in what they sought. While some pleas sought the preservation of CCTV footage, a few others sought the courts direction on regulating police action during demonstrations within educational institutions. Some of the petitions - those filed by former Rajya Sabha member and CPI M leader Brinda Karat, and socio religious organisation Jamiat Ulama-i-Hind - sought a probe against the police for their alleged inaction and apathy and political leaders for their alleged hate speeches. Another set of petitions sought a probe against the alleged rioters, including a National Investigation Agency NIA probe into the alleged funding and sponsoring of the riots, as well as against Congress leaders Sonia and Rahul Gandhi.These were filed by Lawyers Voice, a registered society co-founded by now sitting HC judge Justice Ajay Digpaul, and Delhi resident Ajay Gautam. AIMIM leader Shaikh Mujtaba Farooq, in his plea sought an investigation independent of the Delhi Police, with an Special Investigation Team SIT comprising officers from outside the state, into the role of BJP leaders Kapil Mishra, Anurag Thakur and Parvesh Verma, who are now Delhi cabinet ministers in the riots.

articleTitle: Tom Cruise calls Digger an ‘honour’ as it bombs with $20 mn opening, set to lose $150 mn
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Digger worldwide box office collection: Tom Cruise's film opens at $20 million.
description: Alejandro Inarritu's satire Digger has opened at $8 million at the North America box office, which is Tom Cruise's lowest opening weekend in nearly 20 years.
body_raw: Alejandro Inarritus satire Digger, which stars Tom Cruise in the unrecognizable titular role of a greedy oil tycoon, has bombed at the worldwide box office after an underwhelming opening weekend. Irrespective of the trade estimates, Cruise has hailed the film as an honour and a truly unforgettable experience. Digger has earned 20 million at the worldwide box office, 8 million in North America, and Rs 1.55 crore in India. Digger worldwide box office collection Diggers opening weekend of 8 million at the North America box office is far lower than the trade predictions between 12 million and 15 million. After adding 12 million it collected overseas, the total worldwide earnings of the film stand at 20 million after three days. This makes Digger Cruises lowest opening weekend in nearly two decades. As per The Hollywood Reporter, it was 19 years ago that a Tom Cruise film opened lower than 8 million in North America. Robert Redfords 2007 war drama Lions for Lambs, which starred Cruise, Redford, and Meryl Streep, opened at 6.7 million. However, its budget was merely 35 million, almost one-fourth of that of Digger - 125 million. Another 100 million were spent on promotions. As per Guardian, the film is set to lose almost 150 million. For the past 30 years, Cruise has consistently struck gold at the worldwide box office, mostly owing to his popular spy franchise Mission Impossible. Its final instalment which released last year, Christopher McQuarries Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning, opened at 24.8 million in North America, and 64 million more than three times of Digger in North America. Made on a budget of almost 400 million, it eventually amassed almost 600 million at the worldwide box office. DIGGER is officially in theaters and I am so honored to have had the opportunity to create this film alongside such talented artists. Thank you to the entire cast and crew for your dedication, hard work, and joy. The experience was truly unforgettable and Im so proud of what we created. 13 - Tom Cruise TomCruise October 3, 2026 Despite Cruises superstardom, Digger couldnt even emerge as the box office favourite in North America this weekend. It lost that spot to Michael Showalters erotic psychological thriller Verity. The Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson-starrer received even more negative reviews than Inarritus satire, but ended up earning 32.8 million during its opening weekend, likely to recover its modest budget of 40 million this week. The trajectory of Digger was no different at the India box office. On its first Sunday day 3, the Cruise-starrer earned only Rs 45 lakh, as much as it did on its first Saturday day 2 from 400 plus screens. It hasnt even crossed the daily mark of Rs 1 crore yet, opening at Rs 78 lakh this past Friday on October 2, despite it being a holiday on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. The box office performance of Digger has also been impacted by the homegrown juggernaut that is Abhishek Pathaks crime thriller Drishyam 3. The Ajay Devgn-starrer amassed Rs 176.50 crore from 17,000 plus screens at the domestic box office during its opening weekend, whereas Digger could only pull off Rs 1.80 crore gross and Rs 1.55 crore net in the same period. Tom Cruise hails Digger as an honour Despite Diggers underwhelming opening at the North America box office on Friday, and trade estimates of the opening weekend landing around 8 million, Cruise took to social media on Saturday morning to celebrate his new release. He shared pictures from the set - of him in the unrecognizable avatar as Digger Rockwell, alongside John Goodman, who plays the US President, Riz Ahmed scientist Ganesh, Sandra Huller Emma Rockwell, Michael Showalter US Vice President, Jesse Plemons Kenny, and director Inarritu among others. DIGGER is officially in theaters and I am so honored to have had the opportunity to create this film alongside such talented artists. Thank you to the entire cast and crew for your dedication, hard work, and joy. The experience was truly unforgettable and Im so proud of what we created, wrote the actor as the caption on his X handle. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark Filmmaker Ron Howard, who directed Cruise in 1992 Western romantic adventure epic Far and Away, commented on the actors post and heaped praises on Digger. Impressive on so many levels. Great twists..Outstanding performance, Tom. Your work in Digger has to be seen, thought about and discussed to be fully appreciated. Its one of those rare ones. Full of surprises and great choices. Bravo, he wrote.

articleTitle: El Nino, rain deficit likely to add to Mumbai’s pollution and poor air
articleFeaturedImageAlt: mumbai pollution
description: As many as 21 districts in the state recorded deficit rainfall as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) declared the withdrawal of monsoon on Saturday
body_raw: October has just begun, and Mumbais air quality has started to deteriorate, with certain pockets reeling under thick haze as the southwest monsoon marked an early withdrawal from Maharashtra. A strong El Ninophenomenon, which led to rainfall deficit and drought, is likely to add to Mumbais plummeting Air Quality Index AQI this winter. As many as 21 districts in the state recorded deficit rainfall as the India Meteorological Department IMD declared the withdrawal of monsoon on Saturday - Mumbais earliest monsoon withdrawal since 2023. El Nino - the warm phase of ENSO - refers to a phenomenon that is spurred by changes in sea-surface temperatures and atmospheric conditions in the eastern Pacific Ocean. The naturally occurring climate pattern can alter weather patterns globally and is most typically known to increase the likelihood of drier monsoons, drought, as well as extreme heat. WhileEl Ninohas been historically associated with below-average southwest monsoon in India, scientists and observers have said that strongEl Nino patterns are also associated with worsening air pollution conditions owing to influx of dust-laden winds, extreme heat and below-normal post-monsoon rainfall. For instance, Mumbai has been waking up to a thick blanket of haze and plummeting AQI levels since the onset of October. While the air quality index was in the good category of 0-50 until September 29, the AQI levels registered a sharp spike in October and finally went above 100 on October 2. The deteriorating AQI coincides with the withdrawal of rain-bearing winds, which play a crucial role in settling down pollutants. Speaking to The Indian Express, Raghu Murtugudde - Emeritus Professor at the University of Maryland and a visiting professor at IIT Kanpurs Kotak School of Sustainability- said the spike in AQI was a result of the clockwise wind patterns that usher in dry and dusty winds from as far as the Middle East, while the conditions worsened owing to the favourable atmospheric conditions created by El Nino. Over the past few days, the AQI worsened owing to the clockwise wind circulation that was pumping dry and dusty air from Rajasthan, Pakistan, and even the Middle East. When there is a clockwise circulation, the air tends to sink, trapping pollutants. The fact that PM10 pollutants were higher than PM2.5 was an indication of the fact that dusty and dry winds were blowing in from external regions. However, what worsened the pollution levels was the background of below-normal rainfall, high humidity, and dust influx caused by El Nino, said Murtugudde. Pollution-inducing factors such as vehicular emissions and industries are always present in the atmosphere. While rain is good for washing away these pollutants,El Ninomakes it harder for the pollution to be eliminated as the system is known to suppress rain activity, he added. Mahesh Palawat, vice-president of climate change and meteorology at Skymeg Weather Services, added that strong El Ninocan indirectly trigger higher pollution levels owing to suspension of loose soil and dust particles. SinceEl Ninois known to disturb widespread rainfall, it triggers dryness. Since the surface is left dry due to insufficient monsoon, the loose soil and dust particles get suspended in the atmosphere and contribute to PM10 pollutants in the atmosphere, Palawat told The Indian Express. In Maharashtra, an early withdrawal of monsoon winds means that the region now stares at a prolonged period of dry weather and a longer post-monsoon season. El Ninois also known to reduce the possibility of post-monsoon showers, which is responsible for bringing intermittent relief from high AQI levels, experts said, pointing to the likelihood of higher pollution levels. Last week, the state government of Maharashtra declared a drought in 265 of its 358 talukas. Over the past five years, Mumbai has been reeling under air pollution during winter. While the citys AQI showed improvement at monitoring stations in 2025, unhealthy air is becoming the new normal for Mumbai. Gearing up to tackle pollution, the BMC launched fresh standard operating procedures SOPs on October 2. Each civic ward is now set to identify at least 10 pollution hotspots, including major construction and redevelopment sites, infrastructure projects, open waste-burning locations, debris dumping points, and areas prone to traffic congestion. An officer will be assigned to each hotspot to monitor air quality and ensure corrective measures are taken.

articleTitle: Sharat Saxena starts work 27 days post spine surgery; expert explains recovery in the 70s
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sharat Saxena
description: The actor’s quick return to work after a major spine procedure has experts weighing in on what recovery really involves
body_raw: Veteran actor Sharat Saxena, 76, recently underwent a six-hour lumbar spine surgery and is back to work. What a wonderful feeling to be able to work again. Started working again, 27 days after spine surgery, he wrote in a post on Instagram. Dr Amogh Zawar, consultant, spine surgery, KIMS Hospitals Thane, told indianexpress.com that resuming work just over 25 days is possible in a few cases. Yes, in select cases, patients can return to work within a few weeks of spine surgery, particularly when the procedure is minimally invasive, and recovery is progressing well. However, there is no universal timeline for returning to work. It depends on the type of surgery, the spinal condition being treated, the patients age and health, and the physical demands of their work, said Dr Zawar. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. What factors determine how quickly someone can return to normal activities after spine surgery? According to Dr Zawar, pain control, mobility, muscle strength, neurological recovery, and the nature of the surgery are key factors. A patient with a less extensive procedure may regain mobility relatively quickly, while someone undergoing a more complex surgery may need several weeks or months. Rehabilitation and following post-operative precautions also play an important role, emphasised Dr Zawar. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sharat Saxena sharatsaxena Does returning to work within 27 days mean the spine has completely healed? Not necessarily. Being fit to resume selected activities is different from complete healing. Patients may feel considerably better and become independent in their daily activities while the operated tissues continue to heal. Even after returning to work, they may need to avoid heavy lifting, prolonged sitting, excessive bending or other strenuous movements for some time, said Dr Zawar. The expert noted that the return must be assessed based on the specific demands of the job. An actor may need to deal with long hours, travel, prolonged standing or physical movements, depending on the role. A gradual return, with modifications wherever required, is generally safer than immediately resuming the full workload, asserted Dr Zawar. What to note? The focus should be on recovery rather than simply meeting a deadline. Patients should follow their surgeons advice, continue prescribed rehabilitation and increase activity gradually. New or worsening pain, weakness, numbness or difficulty walking should not be ignored. An early return can be possible for some patients, but 27 days should not be considered a standard recovery period for everyone, said Dr Zawar. articleTitle: UP hospitals sold medicines at up to 67 times the purchase price
articleFeaturedImageAlt: An UPFSDA inspection of 214 hospital pharmacies found major disparities between procurement prices and MRPs of medicines, with some drugs priced up to 67 times higher.
description: Officials said the department was examining the reasons behind the wide variation.
body_raw: An inspection by the Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration UPFSDA has found a staggering gap between the procurement prices of medicines and the maximum retail prices MRPs printed on their packs, with the MRP of some drugs found to be several times higher - as high as 67 times-than the price at which hospitals procure them. Officials said that they are now looking into the reasons for such large gaps. The findings emerged from inspections of medical college and private hospital pharmacies across Uttar Pradesh. According to the UPFSDA, it collected data from 214 hospital pharmacies and analysed the purchase price and MRP of 130 medicines identified in the data. Of these 130 medicines, 36 had MRPs more than 10 times their purchase prices, while in some cases the difference was as high as 67 times. Several of the medicines showing wide disparities are injectable drugs used in ICUs and for serious bacterial and fungal infections. Among the most striking examples was Polymyxin-B injection GUFIPOL 500,000 units, which is used to treat severe bacterial infections in critically ill patients when other traditional antibiotics fail. The purchase price recorded by the pharmacy was Rs 74.09, while the MRP printed on the pack was Rs 4,980.94 - 67.23 times the purchase price. Another pack of the same medicine was purchased for Rs 90 against an MRP of Rs 4,528.10-a difference of more than 50 times. Terlipressin injection, used to treat severe bleeding, was purchased for Rs 56, while its MRP was Rs 3,050 - 54.46 times higher, an official said. Similarly, Colistimethate Sodium 4.5 MIU, another antibiotic, was purchased for Rs 210 against an MRP of about Rs 9,702, while Tigecycline injection was purchased for about Rs 154, and its MRP was printed as Rs 7,110. The MRPs in both cases were about 46 times their purchase prices. The gap was also significant in high-value medicines. Bevacizumab 400 mg, for instance, was purchased for Rs 7,541 against an MRP of Rs 69,995 - a difference of Rs 62,453. The inspection was not limited to medicines. The UPFSDA also examined medical devices and found substantial differences between procurement prices and MRPs in some cases. Officials said the department was examining the reasons behind the wide variation between procurement prices and MRPs, including whether the pricing and trade-margin structure allowed unusually high margins in some cases. Officials said that in some instances, a high MRP could provide scope for discounts to be offered to patients while still leaving a substantial difference between the actual procurement cost and the billed price. They said the extent to which such pricing practices ultimately benefit patients would be examined as part of the inspection. The UPFSDA is continuing inspections of hospital pharmacies to examine the quality, availability and pricing of medicines and medical devices. Officials said the data collected would help identify cases requiring further scrutiny and appropriate action.

articleTitle: Thane gangrape: 7 farmhouses, 17 properties — Absconding constable’s assets under scanner
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ex MLA pawar and constable patil thane gangrape
description: Thane gangrape case: Police are now verifying addresses of 10 more farmhouses that are owned by constable Patil and his wife, bringing the total number of properties being examined to 17
body_raw: The Thane rural police, investigating the alleged gangrape of a 22-year-old woman, have found that absconding former police constable Shailesh Patil owns sevenfarmhouses in his and his wifes names. The farmhousewhere the alleged assault took place is also registered in Patils name. The police are now verifying the addresses of 10 morefarmhouses that, according to a close aide of Patil, are owned by him and his wife, bringing the total number of properties being examined to 17. Patil and former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar are both absconding in connection with the Thane gangrape case. An officer investigating the case said, We were informed by his close aide that there were 17 farmhouses in the couples names in the MMR region. We have found evidence linking him to seven. Given his background, it seems unlikely that he purchased thefarmhouseson his own, and we suspect somebody may be using his name as a front. The immediate priority is to trace Patil and Pawar in the Thane gangrape case. Patils mother alleges assault Soon after their names were mentioned in the FIR, Patils mother, Sulochana, held a press conference in which she alleged that her son had assaulted her as well and demanded the death penalty for him. She alleged that Patil was trying to protect an IPS officer. According to police sources, Patil was jailed and suspended after his arrest in 2013 for allegedly accepting a bribe on behalf of others. He was reinstated in 2019. Two days later, he applied for voluntary retirement and quit the force, an officer said. An FIR was registered against Pawar and Patil on September 17 based on the statement of a 22-year-old woman, who alleged that the two had gang-raped her at Patils farmhousein Padhga. Pawar and Patil have been absconding since the allegations surfaced. A few days later, CCTV cameras and the digital video recorder DVR at thefarmhousewere found missing. articleTitle: ‘Cristiano Ronaldo should decide how he wants to end his time with national team’, says Portugal coach Jesus
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ronaldo left Portugal's training camp after being an unused substitute in a win over Norway and learning he would not start against Denmark. (AP Photo)
description: Jorge Jesus said that he had told Cristiano Ronaldo that he needed him, regardless of whether he was playing or not, when he had his first conversation with him after taking charge.
body_raw: Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus has said that it is upto Cristiano Ronaldo to decide if he wants to return to the national team or not. Jesus said that he had told Ronaldo that he needed him, regardless of whether he was playing or not, when he had his first conversation with him after taking charge. If he wants to, hell return to the national team. We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one whos going to decide, Jesus told reporters after Portugals 2-1 Nations League win over Norway on Sunday. Ronaldo left Portugals training camp after being an unused substitute in a win over Norway and learning he would not start against Denmark. He subsequently said on social media that he would explain his reasons for leaving the national team in due course. The incident caused shockwaves around the world of football, with Jesus in particular receiving significant backlash in Portugal for leaving Ronaldo out of the squad. Hes the one who should decide how he wants to end his time with the national team. In my first call-up, I said, I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you. And now Im saying the same thing, said Jesus. Portuguese Football Federation President Pedro Proenca also said Ronaldo remained part of the teams plans, describing the episode as a misunderstanding that should be resolved internally. He is in the national team on sporting merit, and that must be unquestionable, Proenca told RTP. We have to pay tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo. In the days after Ronaldo announced his departure, speculation was rife that the 41-year-old may end his illustrious international career. Ronaldo had earlier said that he had briefly considered retiring after the 2026 World Cup. Yes, I thought about it, Ronaldo had told reporters. I always think about my decisions, about the future and also about the present. I am someone who thinks a lot. You have to think. That is why you see me here now. It means I will continue. I think I can give the national team my support, not only through goals but also outside football, he said. My goal is to be able to play, score goals and help the team win matches.

articleTitle: Raju Kher recalls bad phase when brother Anupam Kher refused help: ‘Took him for granted’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Raju Kher recalls bad phase when brother Anupam Kher refused help
description: Veteran actor Raju Kher, recently recalled a bad phase of his career when he lost everything and expected his brother Anupam Kher to help. However, Anupam was going through challenges in his own life.
body_raw: In the year 2000, both brothers, veteran actors Anupam Kher and Raju Kher were going through a tough career phase. In a new interview, Raju recalled asking Anupam for financial help but later realised how his elder brother was dealing with his own issues, and learnt not to expect anything from him anymore. During a podcast with Siddharth Kannan, Raju Kher revealed shifting to a rented flat after investing his money in a programme on an upcoming new channel. There was a time when I was going through a bad phase. I had sold my house because a new channel was coming, so I had bought a flat elsewhere. A new channel was going to launch and many people were making pilots, agreements were already signed. I also made a programme Life Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega, he shared. The veteran actor-director continued, Suddenly, I got to know that the channel has disappeared. I had invested the money that I got from selling the flat in that programme. I thought that I had a first-class life, a 4-BHK house, everything set for the family. And then, the channel disappeared and no one knew what happened.. there was just a lock on their door. During the career setback, Raju Kher reached out to his elder brother, Anupam Kher, for help. He said, I also felt the pressure to pay the rent. I had no one else, I could only talk to my brother, and I thought he will help me. But at that time, he had also stopped working. The reason was that he didnt want to do any of those weird films, he wanted substantial roles. So, I felt that my brother did not help me out. He could have done so, that was my thought at that time. ALSO READ It ended in one day Raju Kher recalls brother Anupam Khers first marriage to Madhumalti However, his perspective towards his brother changed completely after reading a single headline in an article. Then, I was reading a magazine on the toilet. In the interview, Anupam Kher had said, I wish I had my own child. Although, he considers Sikander his own child. But then I never thought about my brother in that light. We took him for granted, thinking he doesnt have any problems because he was doing well financially. We never thought that what was going on in his life. He added, That was the thing that changed the whole concept of my life. Have expectations but dont do it like that. Try to find out what is going in the other persons life as well. I am talking about the year 2000, the year that changed my whole life, my thinking. On that day, I stopped expecting anything from anyone, no matter who it is. When asked about rebuilding his life and career, Raju recalled signing a TV serial after a long phase of no work. When your time is bad, your expenses tend to increase. Some suggested wearing certain rings, doing rituals, prayers, I got those done too. Work had also stopped coming. After a few months, I told my wife that we should trust in God, lets see what happens, and I removed all the rings. The next day, I got a call for work. I got an offer for a TV serial. I instantly agreed and told them to pay whatever they want. Life started again, he concluded. When Anupam revealed taking care of Rajus expenses Earlier this year, during an interaction with Zindagi with Richa Youtube channel, Anupam Kher had revealed that he has been taking care of his brothers finances for years. If every brother remembers what they were like when they were young, there would be no fight. I look at my life like its a film. How can I forget that we grew up together? I must also compliment Kirron Kher, wife, because she never, ever asked me, Why do you do so much for your brother? Thats how problems begin. I would sign cheques for Raju, the household, and other things. I told my manager long ago, Remember one thing in life, never ask me how much money Im giving to my brother.
