articleTitle: Pneumonic plague case in Russia raises questions: How it spreads and what Indians should know
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cough
description: A rare respiratory infection is drawing attention, but experts say the real differences may be more important to consider
body_raw: Hundreds have been quarantined after a 28-year-old laboratory technician reportedly died of pneumonic plague in the Siberian region of Irkutsk in Russia, according to Moscow Times report. Alexei Tsydenov, head of the neighboring republic of Buryatia, told the independent news outlet that the woman had died from an unspecified form of plague. Unverified X accounts also claim that pneumonic plague is about 100x deadlier than Covid-19. Given the threat, we spoke with experts to better understand the infectious disease and how it differs from Covid-19. Dr Amit Saraf, director, internal medicine, Jupiter Hospital, Thane, said that a pneumonic plague is a serious lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It is one of the three major forms of plague and is the one that can spread directly from person to person through respiratory droplets, particularly during close contact. The illness can develop rapidly, causing high fever, chills, weakness, cough, chest pain and difficulty breathing. In some cases, the patient may cough up blood-stained sputum. Unlike the plague of history books, this disease is not untreatable today. The important factor is recognising it early and starting the appropriate antibiotics without delay, said Dr Saraf. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. How is pneumonic plague different from Covid-19? The biggest difference is the organism responsible. Covid-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, whereas pneumonic plague is caused by bacteria. Their routes of transmission also differ. Covid-19 can spread quite efficiently through respiratory particles, including from people who may have mild or no symptoms. Pneumonic plague generally requires close exposure to respiratory droplets from an infected person, and person-to-person spread is much less common, said Dr Saraf. Both illnesses can cause fever, cough, weakness and breathing difficulty, so symptoms alone may not always distinguish them, mentioned Dr Samir Garde, director, Dept of Pulmonology and Lung Transplant, Gleneagles Hospital, Parel. However, pneumonic plague can progress rapidly and may cause severe pneumonia, chest pain and sometimes bloody or watery sputum. Covid-19 has a much broader range of presentations, from no symptoms to severe respiratory illness. For Indians, the key message is not to panic or assume every respiratory illness outbreak is plague. Plague is uncommon in India, and its occurrence is generally linked to specific epidemiological circumstances, said Dr Garde. Another important distinction is treatment. Antibiotics are effective against plague bacteria when given promptly they do not work against viruses such as SARS-CoV-2. Both illnesses can affect the lungs and cause pneumonia, so symptoms alone cannot establish the diagnosis. A proper clinical assessment and laboratory testing are essential, said Dr Saraf. Should Indians be worried about pneumonic plague? The general public has no reason to panic just because pneumonic plague is being discussed. Plague is rare today, although it has not disappeared completely. India has experienced plague outbreaks in the past, but that does not mean every respiratory infection or fever should be viewed as plague, Dr Sarf told indianexpress.com. Awareness rather than alarm helps. Those who have a relevant history of exposure to rodents, fleas, sick or dead animals, or a confirmed case of pneumonic plague should seek medical attention if they develop sudden fever and rapidly worsening respiratory symptoms, said Dr Saraf. The Pneumonic Plague that just escaped a lab in Russia is about 100x deadlier than COVID - Todd Hagopian Stagnation Assassin ToddHagopian October 5, 2026 What precautions should people take? Basic precautions remain important. Avoid handling sick or dead animals, particularly rodents, and maintain good hygiene. If someone has a suspected or confirmed pneumonic infection,minimise close contact and follow appropriaterespiratory precautions. Most importantly, do not self-medicate with antibiotics. If sudden fever is accompanied by breathlessness or a rapidly worsening cough, do not delay medical evaluation. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can make a significant difference in the outcome, said Dr Saraf. articleTitle: ‘16 years apart’: Telangana High Court grants man divorce over false criminal case, cruelty
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Telangana High Court divorce false case cruelty The bench also noted that the wife’s allegations of dowry harassment and possession of her jewellery were “vague or unsupported”.
description: The wife had approached the women’s protection cell and lodged a criminal complaint over cruelty and dowry demands, following which the husband filed the divorce petition.
body_raw: The Telangana High Court has granted divorce to a couple after 16 years of separation, holding that a false criminal complaint against the husband and his family, coupled with prolonged separation, amounted to mental cruelty. The court set aside the family courts earlier dismissal of his petition. Dealing with a plea of husband, a bench of Justices K Lakshman and B R Madhusudhan Raosaid that the conduct of the parties clearly indicates that there is no intention on either side to lead a marital life. It is apt to note that when the petition was filed, the appellant was 33 years old and the respondent was 27 years old. At present, they are 49 years old and 42 years old, respectively. They have been living separately for approximately 16 years. The appellant has categorically stated that he is not willing to resume cohabitation or take her back into his society, the September 18 order reads. The bench further noted that the couple had been living separately for around 16 years, neither had made a genuine effort to resume living together, and the husband had clearly stated that he was unwilling to take the wife back. The court held that continuation of the marriage would serve no meaningful purpose and would cause mental cruelty to both parties. Husband sought divorce over cruelty The petitioner-husband has filed a plea challenging the 2017 order of the family court which dismissed his petition seeking divorce on grounds of cruelty. The couple got married in 2007. The husband sought divorce, claiming that after three to four months of marriage, the wife started harassing and torturing him, and insisted that he should become a puppet husband. He stated that she stopped performing her matrimonial obligations. The petitioner alleged that when he refused to accede to her demands, she physically assaulted him. He further alleged that her parents assured him that they would counsel her and took her away for around 10 days, but when she returned, she resumed abusing and harassing him. According to the husband, the two started living separately in the same house in separate rooms from 2008. He claimed that in 2009, she left the matrimonial home and started residing at her parental home. The wife denied the allegations and, in turn, accused the husband and his family of harassment, physical abuse, and interference in their marital life. She alleged that her mother-in-law and other family members subjected her to harassment and that the husband had also physically assaulted her. The matrimonial dispute escalated in 2010 after the wife and her father approached the womens protection cell, following which a criminal complaint was lodged against the husband and his family for cruelty and under the provisions of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The husband then filed the divorce petition in 2010, alleging cruelty. The family court initially dismissed the husbands divorce petition, holding that he had failed to establish cruelty through clear evidence. He challenged that decision before the high court. On the other hand, the criminal case against the husband and his family ended in acquittal in 2020, and the acquittal was upheld in 2025 following a plea. Wifes dowry claims unsupported Order The high court observed that cruelty is not defined by statute and whether a particular act amounts to cruelty depends on the facts and circumstances of each case. It said the court must consider the parties background, social and economic circumstances, values and the overall conduct between them. The ruling stressed that the cumulative effect of the parties conduct has to be considered rather than examining individual incidents in isolation. Persistent quarrels, humiliating treatment, mental harassment, abusive language, disrespectful behaviour, unilateral desertion and false accusations may constitute cruelty, while ordinary disagreements or petty quarrels would not. The bench also noted that the wifes allegations of dowry harassment and possession of her jewellery were vague or unsupported. The dowry allegation was raised for the first time during cross-examination, without details of any specific demand, while her claim regarding jewellery was found inconsistent with her own statement about having the keys to her almirah. The court held that the criminal complaint lodged by the wife against the husband and his family, which ended in acquittal and was also upheld in appeal, could be considered as subsequent evidence of cruelty. It is a well-settled legal position that when a criminal case ends in acquittal, it can be considered as a ground for cruelty, it concluded. The court clarified that subsequent events and the conduct of parties can be considered while examining a claim of cruelty. In this case, although the husbands own testimony was alone not enough to establish cruelty, the later acquittal in the criminal case, coupled with the wifes contradictory statements, supported his case.

articleTitle: Employer can’t recover erroneous overpayment from retiree: Karnataka High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court salary recovery after retirement
description: The Karnataka High Court rules that an excess amount is recoverable only if it was paid on account of any misrepresentation or fraud by the employee.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court has held that an excess amount paid to an employee while in service cannot be recovered upon retirement if the payment resulted from the employers error. Justice M Nagaprasanna issued this ruling while directing Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited Bescom to refund a retired assistant lineman Rs 2,81,887. This amount had been recovered from his pension due to an erroneous increment granted 15 years ago. If the excess amount was not paid on account of any misrepresentation or fraud on the part of the employee, such excess payments of emoluments or allowances are not recoverable, the judge said in his order on September 25. The petitioner, Manjunath N, retired on April 30, 2025. His counsel, Devaraj N, argued that he did not receive the excess pay through fraud or misrepresentation but because of an alleged error by Bescom. Employer admits it cant recover the amount Bescom also admitted that money cannot be recovered from a retired employee unless fraud or misrepresentation on his part is involved. The court referred to a Supreme Court judgment in the case of Jogeswar Sahoo vs District Judge, Cuttack 2025. The judgment held that if the excess amount was not paid due to misrepresentation or fraud by the employee, or if the excess payment resulted from the employer applying a wrong principle for calculating payallowance or based on an interpretation of a ruleorder that was later found to be erroneous, such excess payments of emoluments or allowances are not recoverable. Holding that Manjunath was accused of neither fraud nor misrepresentation regarding the excess amount, the high court directed Bescom to refund it along with interest within eight weeks.

articleTitle: Baft-e-Hawa: Janhvi Kapoor turns heads in a 460-count Bengal muslin sari in Paris
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor in a Baft-e-Hawa muslin sari with an ornate embellished blouse in Paris
description: Janhvi Kapoor wore a 460-count Bengal muslin sari by Pankaj S Heritage to the Business of Fashion gala in Paris. Here’s what Baft-e-Hawa means and why the historic textile is so prized.
body_raw: Janhvi Kapoor took Bengal heritage to the Business of Fashion gala in Paris, wearing an ensemble by Pankaj S Heritage. Styled by cousin sister Rhea Kapoor, Janhvi wore a 460-count Bengal muslin in Khud - Rang, or unbleached, known for its exceptionally light, airy quality. Also referred to as Baft-e-Hawa, Shabnami or Chandani, the fabric represents one of the finest traditions of Indian handwoven textiles. The sari was paired with an ornate blouse featuring polkis, garnets and emeralds, along with saraafa tassels, kiran and resham fringing. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Talking about the look, Sneha Yadav, fashion consultant, brand image strategist, NIFT alumna, says that the design involves the tension between the simple muslin fabric and the bold blouse design. The sari possesses a near effortless feel whereas the decorated sleeves bring in formwork, workmanship and theatricality. This opposition prevents the ensemble from appearing too conventional or unduly flashy, she adds. What exactly is Baft-e-Hawa The name Baft-e-Hawa means woven air, a description that captures the fabrics extraordinary lightness. It wasnt a poetic exaggeration. It was a literal description of how the cloth felt in your hand. This was the finest Dhaka muslin we are talking about, spun exclusively from Phuti Karpas, a delicate cotton shrub that grew only along the silty banks of the Meghna River basin, in modern-day Bangladesh, says Nabanita Ghosh, Co-founder Director, Abritee. Making this fabric required extraordinary skill and precision. According to Ghosh, the spinning happened at the most unlikely hours.Young women with exceptional eyesight worked on boats during the humid hours of dawn and dusk, when the dew and humidity kept the micro-thin threads from snapping. The skill lay in their eyes, their fingertips and their timing, she says. The beauty lies not just in the fineness of the weave, but also in the expertise required to create it and the softness and fluidity that it brought to the garment. A khud-rang, or unbleached, cloth like this leaves the weaver nowhere a slight irregularity to hide, says Ghosh. There is no dye or finishing to cover an uneven thread, so every bit of its quality comes from the hands that made it. A count like 460 sounds technical, but what it really represents is patience. What legend says The most famous story about this cloth dates to the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Dhaka was then a Mughal hub, and its finest muslin, malmal khas, was made for the imperial court. The emperor is said to have scolded his daughter, Princess Zeb-un-Nissa, for appearing to wear nothing at all. Her reply was that she was wearing seven layers of it, says Ghosh. The story, however, has been retold and modified over generations. What gets lost in the retelling is that Baft-e-Hawa was never about transparency. It was about control, Ghosh says. Anyone can make a thin fabric. Making one that is fine, even, and still strong enough to be worn is what made it a global benchmark. The older names associated with the fabric describe it best. Shabnami, meaning dew, and Chandani, meaning moonlight, were given by people who handled this cloth and described exactly what they felt. Why the styling works With a fabric as delicate and visually distinctive as Baft-E-Hawa, adding too much ornamentation can easily overwhelm it. In Janhvis look, the relatively simple sari keeps the fabric visible, while the elaborate sleeves add structure and drama. When that delicacy is paired with a silhouette and intricate detailing, the result is a dialogue between softness and structure. That balance is what gives Janhvis look its character and makes the textile feel very relevant in a contemporary fashion context, she says. According to Yadav, this contrast helps bring a historical Indian textile into a contemporary fashion context. The sari stays closely linked with craft work, yet the styling imparts a contemporary, sculptural nature, proving that history may be read in a manner that feels present without needing to mask or recreate its roots, she says. articleTitle: ‘We get it, Gaitonde’: This Khakee scene justifies Drishyam 3 cop’s obsession with Ajay Devgn
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kamlesh Sawant and Ajay Devgn in Drishyam 3.
description: The internet has dug out a scene from Rajkumar Santoshi's 2004 cop thriller Khakee, which explains probably why Kamlesh Sawant's character of Gaitonde is obsessed with seeing Ajay Devgn's Vijay Salgaonkar behind the bars in Drishyam 3.
body_raw: As soon as the trailer of Abhishek Pathaks blockbuster crime thriller Drishyam 3 dropped last month, fans of the franchise have been churning out memes of Kamlesh Sawant, who plays Sub Inspector Gaitonde, on how relentlessly obsessed he is with seeing Ajay Devgns protagonist Vijay Salgaonkar behind the bars for murder. Now, the internet has dug out a 22-year-old scene from Devgn and Sawants maiden collaboration to justify their unending beef. Khakee scene justifies Gaitondes obsession with Vijay Salgaonkar The said scene is from Rajkumar Santoshis 2004 cop thriller Khakee, in which Devgn played the chief antagonist, ex inspector Yashwant Aangre. In a key scene, when a bunch of cops are escaping Devgns clutches by getting on to a moving train, Sawants character, also called Constable Kamlesh Sawant, is seen struggling to catch the train and chasing it with all his might. Come on, Kamlesh, Tusshar Kapoors character of Sub Inspector Ashwin Gupte screams as he extends his hand to Sawant from the moving train. However, before Sawant, whos running on the tracks, can get to the hand reaching out, Devgns antagonist shoots him down with a gun, leading to his death, much to the misery of Gupte and other members of the police force, including DCP Anant Kumar Srivastav Amitabh Bachchan. We get it, Gayatonde. We get it skull emoji, posted an X handle, along with the Khakee scene, justifying the Drishyam characters unrelenting beef with Devgn over the years. Drishyam 3 was in the making way before laughing with tears emoji, commented another X user. Finally, the prejudice is justified, wrote another. This is some bond level finding, said a third one. We get it, Gayatonde. We get it - The Cinprism TheCineprism October 3, 2026 Since Khakee, which was also Sawants acting debut, hes made a career out of playing a police officer. He also played a cop in late Drishyam director Bollywood directorial debut Mumbai Meri Jaan 2008 and 2011 hit action romance Force, 2012 action film Chakradhaar, Nitesh Tiwaris 2014 supernatural satire Bhoothnath Returns, Amin Hajees 2012 psychological thriller Koi Jaane Na, and Irshad Khans 2023 comedy Non Stop Dhamaal. Interestingly, his character was called Gaitonde in Non Stop Dhamaal, and addressed by his real name Kamlesh Sawant in Force and Bhoothnath Returns. He also played a cop in Marathi films like Santosh Ramdas Manjrekars 2009 vigilante film Mi Shivajiraje Bhosle Boltoy and Chandrakant Kanses 2o15 action thriller Dagadi Chawl. Ajay Devgn recognized Kamlesh Sawant on Drishyam set After working briefly with Devgn on Khakee, Gaitonde reunited with him 11 years later on the set of Drishyam in 2015. Much to his surprise, Devgn not only recognized him, but also walked up to him and gave a pep talk. I usually dont go up to superstars and disturb them on shoot days, and rather focus on my characters take, Sawant told Bollywood Hungama recently. One day, Ajay Devgn sir saw me and walked up to me, and said, Kamlesh, tu Khakee mein tha na, main tujhe goli marta hu you were in Khakee right, I shoot you down?. And then he said, Now, everyone around wanted to know who is playing Gaitonde. Lets make the best of his character, recalled Sawant, who also assured Devgn that hed do full justice to the key character. I replied, Nahi sir, iss character ko nibhane ki, nayay dene ki mein puri koshish karunga No sir, Ill try my best to stay true to and give justice to this character. So, that is the kind of legend Ajay Devgn is. He himself walked up to have a conversation with me, and it is a very big deal for a character actor like me, confessed Sawant. While the first two instalments of the Drishyam franchise were adapted from Jeetu Josephs original Malayalam films starring Mohanlal, the third instalment has been written as an original film by Pathak. The franchise revolves around the Goa police trying to prove Salgaonkar and his family guilty for the murder of Sam, the only son of Inspector General Meera Deshmukh Tabu. Drishyam 3 also stars Shriya Saran, Ishita Dutta, Rajat Kapoor, Jaideep Ahlawat, and Prakash Raj among others. Also Read - Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 3 Live Updates Ajay Devgn film sells 2.27 lakh tickets for Monday, eyes Rs 300 cr club Produced by Pathaks Panorama Studios, Drishyam 3 has already amassed Rs 177 crore at the domestic box office and Rs 272.80 crore worldwide over its opening weekend. Its thus become the sixth highest grossing Bollywood film of 2026 globally, eyeing the next target of Rs 293 crore, set by Priyadarshans horror comedy Bhooth Bangla, starring Akshay Kumar.

articleTitle: Election Commissioners’ SIR objections trigger court pleas: What they are seeking
articleFeaturedImageAlt: election commission of India EC commissioners ECI supreme court gyanesh kumar bombay high court
description: In response to 'growing concerns by citizens', the Lawyers Association for Constitution recently formed a panel of former apex court and high court judges, headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Madan B Lokur, to examine the SIR process.
body_raw: Following The Indian Expresss reports on objections raised by two Election Commissioners over decisions taken in connection with the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, multiple petitions have been filed in the Supreme Court and the Bombay High Court questioning the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar and seeking an SIT investigation into the matter, besides his removal from office. As decisions are awaited, heres a closer look at what has happened in these matters so far Before Supreme Court One of the petitions by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh referred to the alleged differences between CEC Kumar and ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi and the objections raised by the latter. Article 3241 of the Constitution does not vest the superintendence, direction and control of elections in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It vests those powers in a Commission, said the plea. The petitioner urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority. The petitioner argued that the SIR was undertaken without the necessary statutory or constitutional authority and without following the procedure required by law. The other petition by Delhi-based lawyer Shailendra Mani Tripathi has sought a probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or an SIT headed by a retired judge of the top court. The petition refers to unprecedented constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the ECI under the CEC as exposed by documentary records published on September 23, 2026. The plea said the alleged act of.CEC Kumar.falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability. The petitions were filed days after The Indian Express reported that ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR of electoral rolls. The two commissioners said some of the decisions were taken without their knowledge or recommendation. They separately wrote to the countrys top bureaucrat, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan, flagging concerns over the integrity of voter software. The ECI, however, said the letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation and were not related to policy or IT division matters. At Bombay High Court Two pleas were also filed in the Bombay High Court seeking several directions to the Election Commission of India ECI, including placing on record 14 decisions concerning the SIR, criteria for polling station rationalisation and ECINET specifications. ECINET is the ECIs comprehensive digital platform to facilitate citizen participation in the electoral process. The pleas also seek the restoration of every voter deleted during the SIR process in Maharashtra, or quashing of the SIR directions for the state and a stay on forthcoming Assembly elections until the electoral rolls are made legally compliant. One of the pleas seek the appointment of an independent judicial committee to investigate the data deletions and software blockages implemented during the current SIR process. A writ petition filed by four Maharashtra residents and registered voters through advocate Asim Sarode before the Kolhapur circuit bench cited The Indian Express investigation and claimed they were aggrieved by the systematic erosion of constitutional norms governing the management of electoral rolls, which they said directly affected their fundamental rights. The matter is likely to come up on October 22. At the High Courts Goa bench, a matter was heard relating to the deletion of names of six members of a family in Goa from the electoral rolls after their Form 8 applications for address change were rejected. It remarked that the ECI must endeavour to have as many voters who are eligible on the electoral rolls. The court said the poll body has to achieve the objective of not missing out on a voter, even when they come forward with a wrong form. We are asking the principle. The Election Commission must endeavour, and we see that is the endeavour.to have as many voters who are eligible on the rolls. Why should it reject the Form-8 if it comes during that enumeration period of SIR? Independent panel of former SC, HC judges In a related development, former Supreme Court and high court judges have formed a panel to examine the SIR exercise. In a press release dated October 2, the Lawyers Association for Constitution LAFC said that the constitution of the independent inquiry commission was in response to growing concerns raised by citizens regarding the design, implementation, and consequences of the SIR of electoral rolls by the ECI. The panel is stated to function with complete autonomy to examine the constitutional and statutory validity, methodology, and overall impact of the SIR exercise on eligible voters. It will be chaired by former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B Lokur and will comprise former Supreme Court judge Justice A K Patnaik, former Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice Badar Durrez Ahmad,former Delhi High Court judge Justice Rekha Sharma and former Patna High Court judge Justice Anjana Prakash. Senior legal practitioners, including Kapil Sibal, Prashant Bhushan, Chander Uday Singh, Prashanto Chandra Sen, Raju Ramachandran, Rebecca Mammen John, Warisha Farasat, Vrinda Grover, etc, will provide strategic legal advice, the release said. The panel seeks to travel across the country to hear testimony directly from affected citizens, civil society groups, and experts. At the same time, a dedicated research wing would collate and analyse the data regarding voter roll additionsdeletions across the country and present it before the panel. A legal support team will review relevant legislation, notifications, and verification processes to assess compliance with constitutional safeguards, the release added.

articleTitle: From TMC to BJP: Koel Mallick joins saffron party, eyes Rajya Sabha return
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Koel Mallick joins BJP, Koel Mallick BJP, Koel Mallick Rajya Sabha, Koel Mallick TMC, West Bengal Rajya Sabha bypoll, Koel Mallick BJP candidate, Rukmini Mallick, Koel Mallick political career, October 16 Rajya Sabha election, Bengal BJP, former TMC MP Koel Mallick, Indian Express, BJP news, Bengal news
description: Koel Mallick will submit her Rajya Sabha nomination later in the day in the presence of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
body_raw: Former Trinamool Congress MP and actor Koel Mullick formally joined the BJP Monday, a day after the ruling party named her as its nominee for the October 16 bypoll for Rajya Sabha in West Bengal. A popular face in the Bengali film industry, Mullick was elected as a TMC Rajya Sabha MP in April this year. However, she resigned from the Upper House in July after the Mamata Banerjee-led partys electoral setback in the West Bengal Assembly elections. She joined the ruling party in the presence of Sashi Agnihotri, state BJP general secretary. Mullick is scheduled to submit her nomination later in the day inthe presence of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Proud to be in such a party While speaking to reporters shortly after joining the BJP, shethanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari forgivingme this opportunity. In the last few months after BJP came to power in Bengal, there has been significant development in the state. It is inspiring. I am proud to be in such a party, Mullick said. People of Bengal want development and jobs. We have seen that after finishing their education, people leave Bengal for jobs outside because there is a dearth of jobs here. One should create more jobs here so these people can return, said Mullick. I am privileged. But many are not as privileged as I am. I will like to work for them. Since childhood, my family taught me to help people who are not as privileged as I am. During summer vacation, we used to go to the Missionaries of Charity. Even if I can contribute in a small way in helping people, I will be happy, she added. When asked about the TMC, Mullick said, Different parties work in their own ways. Each political party has its own way of working and trying to do good for people. I have never spoken against anyone, not during my film career or otherwise. BJP must also clarify the dilemma Koel is the fourth TMC Rajya Sabha MP to join the Bharatiya Janata Party after Sushmita Dev, Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, and Prakash Chik Baraik joined the BJP on July 9, 2026, after resigning from the TMC and the Upper House. They were also elected to the Rajya Sabha on BJP tickets. While West Bengal BJP leaders said they welcomed these leaders as untainted members to strengthen the party, the TMC labelled the moves as acts of betrayal. Our leaders Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee have already stated that our evaluation of some people was wrong. Our trust in some people was a mistake, Krishanu Mitra, TMC Mamata Banerjee spokesperson, said. The BJP must also clarify the dilemma within the party. First, they said no TMC men or women will be taken in the BJP. Then they said they picked good TMC leaders. They should evaluate who are their own party members and who are outsiders, Mitra added. Koel Mallick is the daughter of veteran Bengali film actor Ranjit Mallick and Deepa Mallick. She married film producer Nispal Singh in 2013. She has won several awards for her performances in movies, including a Filmfare Awards Bangla, two Bengali Film Journalists Association awards, and an Anandalok Puraskar. In 2023, the Bengal Government, under the TMC, honoured her with the Mahanayak Samman.

articleTitle: Can’t save ‘eroded’ marriage just by legally preserving it: Orissa High Court backs divorce
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Orissa High Court Marriage Divorce Cruelty
description: The Orissa High Court held that compelling a wife to resume a marriage marked by sustained mental anguish and eroded trust would be unrealistic.
body_raw: The Orissa High Court recently refused to reverse a divorce granted by a family court, observing that the sanctity of a marriage cant be saved by preserving only the legal form of the relationship when its foundation has been substantially eroded. Chief Justice Harish Tandon and Justice Chittaranjan Dash were hearing an appeal filed by a husband against a family court order by which a divorce was granted to his wife on the ground of cruelty. Marriage undoubtedly carries a sanctity which the court must ordinarily endeavour to preserve. But the sanctity of marriage is not served by preserving only the legal form of the relationship when the substantive foundation of that relationship has been substantially eroded. Mutual respect, trust, companionship and a willingness to make reasonable adjustments are not peripheral attributes of matrimonial life they constitute its very foundation, the October 1 order read. The high court added, Where those attributes have been progressively lost and the relationship has become a source of sustained mental pain and anguish, the court cannot shut its eyes to the reality of the relationship merely because its deterioration cannot be fitted into one isolated or neatly defined category of conduct. According to the husband, the couple got married on October 20, 2021, following which they initially resided at Visakhapatnam before shifting to Hyderabad, where they worked in the Information Technology sector. The husband alleged that the couple later developed differences and the wife left the matrimonial home in June 2023 and went to Rayagada along with her parents, after which she filed a case for divorce on the basis of cruelty before the family court. On January 27, 2024, the family court dissolved the marriage. The husband then moved the high court with the current appeal. Wrongly dissolved marriage Advocate S K Dwivedy, appearing for the husband, argued that the family court had wrongly dissolved the marriage on the basis of cruelty, as the allegations of the wife were neither proved by evidence and nor were they enough to be called cruelty under the Hindu Marriage Act. He further stated that the husband had also instituted a case for resuming the marriage, which reflected his intention to continue the relationship. Advocate T K Mishra, representing the wife, submitted that she had specifically named acts of physical and mental cruelty meted out to her during the marriage, along with evidence. He added that the husbands conduct had caused mental agony to the wife and rendered continuation of the matrimonial relationship impossible. Continuing discord The high court stated that ordinary wear and tear of married life, trivial irritations, occasional quarrels or differences arising in the course of matrimonial life cannot, by themselves, furnish a ground for dissolution of marriage. The conduct complained of must be of such a nature and degree as to cause a reasonable apprehension that it would not be possible for the parties to continue living together. According to the bench, Mental cruelty, by its very nature, may not always be capable of direct proof, and the effect of the conduct upon the mind of the spouse has to be assessed having regard to the circumstances, the status and background of the parties and the nature of the relationship. The high court observed that the evidence given by the wife could not be reduced to a case of a stray quarrel or an isolated matrimonial disagreement. As per the court, the allegations of physical assault and the specific incidents stated by the wife when seen as a whole, present a continuing course of discord. The court noted that the final separation of the couple was not an event occurring in isolation but the culmination of an already deteriorated matrimonial relationship and that according to the evidence there was not merely a difference in perception between two spouses, but a relationship in which the essential element of mutual confidence had substantially eroded. It further noticed that even when the parties were brought face to face before this court on March 20, the relationship could not be restored rather, both expressed their desire to bring the marital tie to an end. While granting divorce to the couple, the high court said that it did not grant a decree of divorce just because they were separated or wanted to end the marriage, but the foundation of the decree remains the cruelty established from the evidence. Accordingly, it refused to interfere with the family courts order and held that the matrimonial relationship has lost its essential character and that compelling the Respondent-Wife to resume such a relationship would be unrealistic.

articleTitle: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI to be ‘SpaceXSI’: Where does ‘super intelligence’ term come from?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence tool Grok was used to launch strikes against Iran
description: Musk is joining US President Trump’s push to replace ‘AI’ with ‘SI’. But what does super intelligence mean, what are its origins, and why is it a contested term?
body_raw: Elon Musk has said that he will rename SpaceXs AI unit to closely reflect the term US President Donald Trump has been pushing, super intelligence or SI, instead of artificial intelligence. The tech billionaire in a post on X on Sunday, October 4, said that the name of SpaceXAI will be changed to SpaceXSI. However, he did not provide any further details regarding the Grok-makers rebrand. Yes, we will make that change, Musk said in a reply to a user on X asking him about the possibility of renaming SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI. The SpaceX CEO is one of the first bold-faced names in Big Tech looking to embrace Trumps preferred term for AI. Earlier, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also said that data centres should now be referred to as superintelligence factories. These proposed name changes come days after tech CEOs and AI industry leaders met with Trump at the White House, and signed onto an agreement of voluntary safety standards that Trump said was morally binding. The voluntary pact primarily involves AI frontier companies teaming up with an independent external auditor to assess that models are operating as intended and implement internal controls to ensure that their AI agents do not hack systems. However, several critics have argued that AI is facing a crisis of public trust and a name change is unlikely to resolve mounting concerns over safety risks posed by the rapidly evolving technology. A look at Trumps super intelligence push Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Trump said, From this point forward, all of United States documents, and hopefully the worlds will be changed to use the much more accurate term super as opposed to artificial. So its super intelligence. The US president has even signed an executive order renaming artificial intelligence to super intelligence in order to better capture the fact that the technology does much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence. The executive order further requires US government agencies at the federal level to use the new term, or SI, when referring to the technology in public communications, websites, reports and policy documents. Michael Kratsios, director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, has reportedly been tasked with figuring out whether an official definition of the new term should be modified or expanded, as per the order. On one hand, AI industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have called for a deliberate slowdown of frontier AI progress and urged the government to implement federal guardrails on frontier AI models, Trump has so far opposed regulation. He has also repeatedly dismissed whistleblowers warnings of AI security risks as overblown and a hoax. The Trump administration has also set up a task force or Super Intelligence Force, which will be tasked with producing a report on the risks and opportunities of AI within 120. The group will be led by Trumps newly appointed AI czar, Jay Clayton, who also serves as the director of national intelligence. Meanwhile, California Governor Gavin Newsom has looked to counter Trumps super intelligence push by issuing an executive order of his own, requiring state agencies to refer to the technology only as artificial intelligence or AI. Super intelligence is clearly not coming from the White House - thats why California continues to lead, Newsom said in a statement. What does SI mean in the AI space? So far, super intelligence has been used by AI industry executives and researchers to refer to an AI system with cognitive capabilities that essentially outperform humans in all aspects of thinking. Currently, such an AI system is hypothetical and does not exist. The term is also a severely contested one. Proponents of AI often use it to describe systems that surpass human abilities and bring major benefits. On the other hand, AI safety advocates have warned that such systems could outpace human control and may lead to the extinction of human beings. There are several other terms in AI discourse that are closely related to super intelligence, but slightly vary in meaning. For instance, artificial super intelligence ASI, has its roots in a 2014 book titled Superintelligence Paths, Dangers, Strategies written by controversial philosopher Nick Bostrom. OpenAI has been pursuing artificial general intelligence AGI, which is an umbrella term used to refer to technology that outperforms humans in several tasks without specifically being trained to do so. However, in September 2024, Sam Altman outlined a heady vision of ASI and what it would be like to live in a world with such technology. It is possible that we will have superintelligence in a few thousand days it may take longer, but Im confident well get there, Altman wrote in his 2024 blog post titled The Intelligence Age. Another term popularised by a tech CEO is personal superintelligence. In August 2025, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a letter outlining his vision for personal superintelligence, which is rooted in the idea that people should use AI to achieve their personal goals. Metas vision is to bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We believe in putting this power in peoples hands to direct it toward what they value in their own lives. This is distinct from others in the industry who believe superintelligence should be directed centrally towards automating all valuable work, and then humanity will live on a dole of its output, he said.

articleTitle: Anti-CEC stir: Journalist detained 2 days after she alleged sexual harassment by cops
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police personnel detain All India Students' Association (AISA) National President Neha Bora during the ‘Citizens’ March’ from India Gate to Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Sunday. (ANI Photo)
description: The protesters had camped outside Parliament Street police station overnight, demanding against officers who allegedly sexually assaulted three women journalists
body_raw: The protest against the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls entered its fourth consecutive day on Monday, with the Delhi Police registering six FIRs and arresting 18 people in connection with the alleged instances of violence that broke out during a NSUI demonstration and for circulating AI generated poster of policemen, officers said on Monday. Among the six FIRs, four were related to violence, vandalism and rioting during the NSUI demonstration, one tied to an alleged attack on a CISF personnel and another related to circulating a fake poster that showed an officer allegedly sexually harassing a woman. Meanwhile, one of the three women journalists who had alleged sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel while covering the anti-CEC protest has been detained along with 16 others on Monday, for camping overnight outside Parliament Street police station, demanding action against the officers. The same day also saw a CISF constable allegedly getting attacked with a knife by a protester amid an NSUI demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The developments came amid continued demonstrations near Jantar Mantar and growing demands for a probe into the allegations made by three female journalists, who have accused police personnel of sexually assaulting them while they were reporting on the stir on October 3. A senior police officer said restrictions under prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS had been imposed across the New Delhi district. According to the officer, gatherings were not permitted at Parliament Street because it is not an authorised protest location. On Monday morning, around 17 people who had spent the night outside the Parliament Street police station were detained. The group, comprising freelance journalists, YouTubers and one of the alleged victims of sexual assault, had gathered to demand registration of an FIR and action against the officers accused in the alleged sexual harassment case. The protesters were detained individually and taken by bus to Delhi Cantonment Police Station, officers said. The woman who has alleged harassment told reporters that the group wanted to enter the police station and meet senior officers to find out the status of her complaint. The detainees were subsequently released in the evening. The police had on Sunday confirmed receiving three separate complaints from female journalists alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during the October 3 demonstration near Jantar Mantar. The complaints have been handed over to the Crime Branch. Meanwhile, a separate incident involving a CISF constable was reported during an NSUI demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Monday afternoon. The constable deployed for law-and-order duties was allegedly attacked with a knife by a protester, officers said. The constable, identified as Vikram Kumar, was reportedly moving a young man away from the barricades towards the designated protest area when the man allegedly pulled out a knife and attempted to strike him in the neck, police said. Kumar allegedly raised his hand to protect himself, suffering a cut and scratches on his right elbow, officers said. Kumar was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and was later discharged. Security personnel at the site detained the alleged attacker and handed him over to the police, officers said. In a purported video recorded after the incident, Kumar said he immediately informed his senior officers after the alleged attack. Police are questioning the accused to determine how he obtained the knife and what prompted the alleged assault. Around 50 NSUI protesters were also detained during the demonstration and later released. Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janta Party CJP expressed support for the women who have alleged sexual harassment and demanded action against the police personnel named in the complaints. CJP legal team head Ratna Singh alleged on X that the woman complainant and others demanding registration of an FIR were detained and claimed that some detainees were assaulted. Police, however, denied the allegation of manhandling, saying the protesters resisted detention while male and female personnel were escorting them to the bus.

articleTitle: Brazil election heads to runoff as Flavio Bolsonaro leads against Lula, second round of voting on Oct 25
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Brazil’s presidential election will go to a runoff on October 25 between Senator Flavio Bolsonaro (left) and incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (right) after neither won a majority in the first round. (AP Photo)
description: Brazil’s presidential election is headed for a runoff on October 25 after Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva failed to secure a majority in the first round.
body_raw: Millions of Brazilians voted in the first round of voting for the Presidential elections on Sunday, with right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro facing the incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. A second round of voting will be held later this month after Bolsonaros stronger-than-expected performance. Bolsonaro narrowly led the winning margin by 47 while Lula da Silva had 45 of the vote share. Bolsonaro lacked the outright majority needed to win the election. The runoff election will be held on October 25. Brazil wants change and I am very happy with the results, Bolsonaro told reporters in Brasilia after almost all votes were counted. He declared the result marked the end of the era of Lulas Workers Party. The election was focused on the cost of living, corruption and insecurity. Brazils currency and stock market have also risen. Flavio Bolsonaro is the son of right-wing former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted over a plot to overturn the 2022 election result. Lula da Silva, while speaking to supporters at a hotel in Sao Paulo, said he had expected to win in the first round. He said he would restart his campaign the next day and promised to highlight his record in office. Pre-election private surveys had projected Lula to lead by around three percentage points. Bolsonaro told Reuters before voting that he was counting on a protest vote from people opposed to Lula, even if they had initially planned to support other candidates. A voter and lawyer by profession, Thaise Lima, 41, said her priority was ending the Workers Partys rule, while a voter Fernando Tempel, 49, said he switched to Bolsonaro after initially backing former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, belonging to the New Party. As per a report by Reuters, economic concerns dominated the election, with Lula struggling to win over voters facing high living costs, household debt and rising gang activity despite falling inequality and unemployment. Flavio Bolsonaro sought to capitalise on cost-of-living pressures, while Lula moved to ban online gambling, expand welfare measures and propose debt relief for families. Rising spending and public debt above 82 of GDP have also raised fiscal concerns, with the government cutting its growth forecasts to 2 this year and 2.3 next year. The Banco Master case, involving an alleged multibillion-dollar fraud, drew in political figures including Bolsonaro, who is being investigated over suspected money laundering and has denied wrongdoing. Campaign debate was overshadowed by scandals and allegations of foreign interference in the elections. On the other hand, Lulas allies also warned that the Trump administration could refuse to recognise the election result if he wins. US President Donald Trump has not endorsed a candidate but hosted right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly. Brazilian intelligence officials also briefed French and German officials on alleged US and Russian interference in the elections. The United States has rejected these allegations.

articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | CAFE-III norms: What are the new rules and how will they work?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | CAFE-III norms: What are the new rules and how will they work?
description: The final Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE)-III norms are notified. What are new norms and how will they make passenger vehicles more fuel-efficient? Here’s what you need to know. Also, go "Beyond the Nugget" to know about the Bharat Stage norms.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on new Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE norms. Knowledge Nugget New Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE Norms Subject Environment and Economy Why in the news? Recently, the new Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE Norms for passenger vehicles were notified by the Ministry of Power. It will come into effect from 1 April 2027 and remain applicable up to 31 March 2032. The new norms will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. In this context, lets know what CAFE norms are and key highlights of CAFE-III norms. Key Takeaways 1. CAFE-III is a set of fleet-level fuel-efficiency standards for passenger vehicles. They were first introduced in 2017 under the Energy Conservation Act. 2. CAFE norms require manufacturers to keep the average fuel consumption - and therefore CO2 emissions - of all eligible passenger vehicles they sell within a prescribed limit, rather than requiring every individual model to meet the same number. Key Highlights of CAFE-III Norms 3. The CAFE norms will apply from April 1, 2027, to March 31, 2032. They cover M1 category passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. 4. The CAFE-III framework will drive progressive improvements in fuel economy through year-on-year tightening of targets across all five years. 5. At the heart of the system is a fleet-wide calculation a manufacturers permitted fuel consumption is determined by the weighted average unladen weight of the vehicles it sells. 6. The government has set an annual formula for calculating each manufacturers target Annual average fuel consumption a A- W a b c Here, W is the weighted average unladen mass of the manufacturers eligible vehicles. The reference weight, or b, has been fixed at 1,229 kg. The figure a determines how much the fuel-consumption target changes for every kilogram that a manufacturers average fleet weight is above or below the reference weight, and c is the baseline fuel-consumption target, expressed in litres per 100 kilometres. 7. The new norms provide flexibility to manufacturers to adopt cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and other innovative solutions. It promotes technological innovation in new technologies such as high efficiency air-conditioning for improved fuel efficiency and Solar reflective paints. 8. Through the introduction of the Carbon Neutrality Factor CNF, the CAFE-III framework recognises the contribution of renewable and low-carbon fuels, including ethanol-blended petrol, biofuels and CBG. 9. The list of recognised fuel-conservation technologies has been significantly expanded from four to twelve technologies. 10. Battery Electric Vehicles BEVs, Range-Extended Electric Vehicles REEVs, Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles PHEVs, Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles SHEVs, and Flex-Fuel Vehicles will receive super credits that are volume derogation factors in fleet-average calculations. 11. CAFE-III does not require manufacturers to balance their books completely every year. Manufacturers may opt to meet their obligations over specified two-yearthree-year compliance blocks.A This allows manufacturers greater flexibility in managing their technology transition and product portfolios over the compliance period. 12. Manufacturers that perform better than their prescribed targets will generate credits, which may be carried forward within the specified compliance blocks. 13. Manufacturers with a compliance gap may utilise eligible carry-forward provisions, enter into exchangetrade of credits with other manufacturers, or purchase credits through the buyout mechanism administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency. 14. Reporting will be done under both the Modified Indian Driving Cycle MIDC and the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure WLTP. What is WLTP ? The Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure WLTP, which the European Union adopted in 2018, ensures that emissions of carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides NOx, and particulate matter from vehicles on the road more closely reflect results recorded in laboratory conditions. BEYOND THE NUGGET Bharat Stage norms 1. Bharat Stage emission norms are Indias standards for regulating pollution from motor vehicles. They set legal limits on exhaust emissions of pollutants such as carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. Each successive BS tightens these limits, pushing manufacturers to adopt cleaner engine technologies, better exhaust treatment systems and cleaner fuel. 2. India introduced emission norms first in 1991, and tightened them in 1996, when most vehicle manufacturers had to incorporate technology upgrades like catalytic converters to cut exhaust emissions. Fuel specifications based on environmental considerations were notified first in April 1996 - to be implemented by 2000, and incorporated in BIS 2000 standards. 3. Following the landmark Supreme Court order of April 1999, the Centre notified Bharat Stage-I BIS 2000 and Bharat Stage-II norms, broadly equivalent to Euro I and Euro II, respectively. BS-II was for the National Capital Region and other metros BS-I for the rest of India. 4. From April 2005, in line with the Auto Fuel Policy of 2003, BS-III and BS-II fuel quality norms came into existence for 13 major cities, and for the rest of the country, respectively. From April 2010, BS-IV and BS-III norms were put in place in 13 major cities and the rest of India, respectively. 5. The BS IV norms had been enforced across the country since April 2017. In 2016, the Centre had announced that the country would skip the BS-V norms altogether and adopt BS-VI norms by 2020. 6. Major emissions governed under these norms are carbon monoxide emissions, hydrocarbon emission limits. Nitrogen Oxides and particulate matter are also significant metrics. Furthermore, for every step up in standards, an improved standard of fuel is required. For BS-IV compliant vehicles, BS-IV standard fuel is required. CAFE-III is a set of fleet-level fuel-efficiency standards for passenger vehicles. 2. The CAFE norms will apply from October 1, 2026, to September 30, 2035. 3. The CAFE norms were first introduced in 2017 under the Energy Conservation Act. articleTitle: Bengaluru techie drowns in abandoned quarry during Instagram trekking group’s outing
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru trekker drowning
description: Following an exhaustive two-day search, rescuers retrieved the body of techie Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay from a vast, waterlogged quarry pit near Yellammanadoddi.
body_raw: What began as a promising long-weekend getaway for a group of trekkers connected through Instagram ended in heartbreak near Jigani on the outskirts of Bengaluru. Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, 30, an IIT Delhi postgraduate and associate user experience UX designer living in Halasuru, drowned after taking a dip in an abandoned, water-filled stone quarry. Originally from Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, Vinay built his career in Bengaluru over the past four years. On October 2, he set out for a holiday trek with eight companions met through an Instagram trekking circle, including his fiance, a veterinary doctor. Midway through their journey, the group paused at a massive stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi. Decommissioned nearly 15 years ago, the pit had gradually become a deep rainwater reservoir, tempting the trekkers to step in for a swim. The group spent nearly an hour and a half playing in the water before the outing took a sudden, fatal turn around 5.30 pm, when his friends realised Vinay was missing. For some time, I think the group might not have noticed Vinay. It appeared that he knew swimming and are investigating under what circumstances he drowned, a police officer said. Challenging search operation His friends attempts to find him were unsuccessful, leading to an urgent distress call to the Jigani police. Local residents also joined in to help, though the vast quarry presented a significant challenge. It is an abandoned quarry. Not many go to that place. We got to know around 6 pm on the day of the incident, and it was a very vast place to search, said Kalappa, a local resident. A desparate search operation unfolded over the next two days. Initial efforts by local Fire and Emergency Services expanded to include teams from the State Disaster Response Force SDRF, the National Disaster Response Force NDRF, and local divers. Authorities also called renowned expert scuba diver Eshwar Malpe and his team from coastal Karnataka to join the rescue efforts. Following a non-stop effort, rescue crews retrieved Vinays body at around 9 am on Sunday. The Jigani police registered a case of unnatural death based on a complaint filed by his brother.

articleTitle: ‘Mere paternity dispute not enough’: Kerala High Court refuses to order child’s DNA test
articleFeaturedImageAlt: paternity DNA test father child domestic violence case kerala high court
description: The court held that DNA test cannot be sought simply because the child's paternity is disputed. Before directing such a test, there must be initial material establishing non-access between spouses during the period under consideration.
body_raw: The Kerala High Court has refused to order the DNA test of a minor child to determine paternity, holding that such testing cannot be sought routinely without preliminary proof that the spouses had no access to each other during the relevant period. Justice Jobin Sebastian was dealing with a plea in connection with a domestic violence proceeding in which the husband sought a direction for the couples minor child to undergo a DNA test to ascertain paternity. In the absence of specific pleadings and prima facie material demonstrating non-access between the spouses during the relevant period, a direction for DNA profiling cannot be sought as a matter of course merely on the basis of an allegation disputing paternity, the court said on September 26. The ruling held that a DNA test is not to be directed routinely and may be ordered only in appropriate and deserving cases where the court finds such examination necessary for the proper adjudication of the dispute. Unless non-access between the spouses during the relevant period is prima facie established, evidence cannot be permitted for the purpose of disproving the paternity of a child born during the subsistence of the marriage, it observed. Husband disputes childs paternity The case arose from proceedings under the provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, initiated by a woman and her minor child before the trial court. They sought maintenance and return of the womans gold ornaments. During the pendency of those proceedings, the husbandrespondent disputed that he was the minor childs biological father. He filed an application seeking a direction for the child to undergo a DNA test, claiming that it would establish that he was not the childs biological father. He also contended that the woman had agreed to undergo the DNA test during mediation. The trial court, however, dismissed the application. Aggrieved, the husband approached the high court challenging the order. Marriage raises presumption of childs legitimacy The court observed that proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act are meant to adjudicate allegations of domestic violence and provide legal reliefs, and not to determine the biological parentage of a child. It noted that the marital relationship between the parties was undisputed. Since there was no material showing that the husband had no access to the wife during the relevant period, the presumption under the Indian Evidence Act operates in favour of the childs legitimacy. The court explained that Section 112 of the Indian Evidence Act embodies a rule of public policy intended to protect the legitimacy of children born during a valid marriage. The ruling said that such legitimacy is conclusive unless it is shown that the spouses had no access to each other when the child could have been conceived. It further observed, A consensual understanding reached during mediation cannot, by itself, compel a court to order a DNA examination unless the court independently finds that such an examination is legally permissible, necessary, and justified in the facts and circumstances of the case. Parties cannot, by consent, require a court to pass an order contrary to law or public policy. Since there was no material establishing non-access, the presumption of legitimacy remained operative. The high court, hence, found that the magistrate was justified in refusing to direct the DNA examination and dismissed the petition.

articleTitle: Tribal student protesters arrested from Maharashtra Congress headquarters? What cops say
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress earlier alleged that Mumbai Police arrested tribal student protesters from its headquarters. (Express Photo by Soham Shah)
description: The protesters had called for a march to Lok Bhavan, and only those who attempted to proceed towards the Lok Bhavan were detained, police said
body_raw: The Mumbai Police has denied allegations that they entered the Congress headquarters at Tilak Bhavan and arrested tribal student protesters staying there. In a statement, the police said they detained Lok Bhavan march protesters from different locations and that legal action was being taken against them. Lok Bhavan is the official residence of the Governor of Maharashtra at Malabar Hill, Mumbai. The protesters had called for a march to Lok Bhavan, and only those who attempted to proceed towards the Lok Bhavan were detained, police said, without giving details on those arrested. Congress leaders, including Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal and senior leader Balasaheb Thorat, had earlier alleged that police entered the partys Tilak Bhavan headquarters during the night and detained tribal students, including women, who had arrived in Mumbai from Nashik after a foot march. Sapkal had alleged that police entered the office premises and threatened the students, while demanding their immediate release. He had also claimed that NSUI office-bearers were among those detained. Shame on the so-called double engine government in Maharashtra which is clearly Adivasi-virodhi, senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said. Balasaheb Thorat also criticised the alleged police action and asked, Is it a crime for tribal people to protest for their legitimate rights? Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe said, Women cannot be arrested at night. Who gave them this right? The party has meanwhile warned that party workers will gherao Varsha, the chief ministers residence, if the students arent released. Tribal students protest The students have been protesting over a range of demands concerning facilities in tribal schools and hostels, and an independent inquiry into deaths at tribal ashram schools. They have also submitted a 26-point demand charter to the Maharashtra government, also seeking the resignation of Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike. After their month-long agitation in Nashik, the students began marching towards Mumbai last week. A delegation had also sought a meeting with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

articleTitle: SBI credit card fee jumps from Rs 499 to Rs 2,999, woman wins Rs 50,000 compensation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Consumer Commission SBI Cards Woman Consumer News Credit Card Fee SBI
description: The commission was hearing a consumer complaint alleging deficiency in SBI credit card services and unfair trade practice over the issuance of the card with higher annual fees than the complainant said she had opted for.
body_raw: A Delhi Consumer Commission has held SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service and ordered to pay Rs 50,000 to a woman who alleged that she had opted for a credit card with an annual fee of Rs 499 but was issued one carrying a Rs 2,999 fee in 2023. She repeatedly asked the company to change the card, but her request was not resolved. Nearly three years after she filed the complaint, the commission ordered the card to be closed. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-II, Delhi president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Dr Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia, were hearing a complaint filed by one Neha Chaudhary against SBI Cards Payment Services Limited. It is difficult to comprehend as to the reason why the card was not closed if it could not be downgraded, the commission observed on September 18, finding SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service. According to Chaudharys complaint, she had opted for a Simply Click credit card carrying an annual fee of Rs 499 plus GST. She alleged that the companys agent instead obtained her biometric KYC for a Club Vistara card. A card was issued with a credit limit of Rs 73,000, but she found that it carried an annual fee of Rs 2,999 along with GST. Woman repeatedly asks for card change A bill dated August 3, 2023 showed annual fees of Rs 2,999 and GST of Rs 592.32. On August 4, she emailed SBI Cards stating that she had not used the card and requested that it be changed to a Simply Save card, with the applicable charges. SBI Cards replied on August 10, 2023 that its representatives had been unable to contact her on her registered mobile number. It said upgrading or downgrading a credit card required OTP validation and asked her to receive a representatives call or contact its helpline. Chaudhary then informed the company that she had contacted the helpline but the requested change had not been made. On August 11, she said she had called multiple times and was told that the card could not be changed and the fees could not be waived. She also informed the company that she had approached the RBI Ombudsman. On August 18, SBI Cards informed her that it was unable to process the downgrade request. She sent a legal notice through email the same day. The commission noted that Chaudhary had contacted the company through email and its helpline multiple times, but was eventually told that the downgrade could not be processed without any reason being assigned. Commission questions why card was not closed The commission recorded that SBI Cards neither appeared nor rebutted the complainants allegations. Its written statement was not taken on record because it was time-barred under an order dated October 24, 2024. The commission took note of an earlier February 2026 decision of the Karnataka State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, which referred to RBI directions dated April 21, 2022 on credit card closure. Those directions provide that a closure request should be honoured within seven working days, subject to payment of dues, and that issuers must provide multiple channels for such requests. Failure to complete closure within seven working days attracts a penalty of Rs 500 per calendar day where there is no outstanding amount. The commission said it was difficult to comprehend why the card was not closed if it could not be downgraded. The commission held SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service and directed it to close the credit card. It also directed the company to generate the bill as on August 4, 2023, the date of Chaudharys request for the change, provided the bill had not already been paid. The commission ordered SBI Cards to pay Rs 50,000 compensation. Takeaway If a credit card comes with a fee or charges different from what you agreed to, raise the issue immediately in writing and keep copies of all emails, bills and complaint records. If the issuer cannot make the requested change, ask for closure of the card and seek appropriate consumer redress rather than continuing to accept charges you dispute. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi1800-11-4000 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance. articleTitle: Vijay Deverakonda says Rashmika Mandanna tells him ‘I love you’ 10-15 times a day: ‘More mature’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna have opened up about the importance of expressing love in a relationship.
description: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna opened up about love, marriage and the importance of expressing feelings in their relationship during a podcast with Prakhar Gupta.
body_raw: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna recently opened up about their bond, their marriage and how their understanding of love has evolved over the years. The couple also shared how little efforts keep a relationship going. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. In a podcast with Prakhar Gupta, calling Rashmika the more mature one, Vijay says, Rashmika is more mature when it comes to relationships. Look at how shes talking. She makes sure she tells me I love you at least 10-15 times a day, and she tells me that its important for me to express it too. I constantly feel it, but I shouldnt think, Okay, she knows it, so I dont need to say it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rashmika Mandanna rashmikamandanna Why is it important to express love Most people assume the person they love already knows it. They have shown up, stayed, and handled the practical things, so surely the feeling is obvious. That assumption is where a lot of quiet distance begins, because as Dr Chandni Tugnait, MD A.M Psychotherapist, Life Alchemist, Coach Healer, Founder Director, Gateway of Healing says, love that is felt but never said often goes unnoticed by the very person it is meant for. She also explains why it is necessary to express feelings instead of assuming the other person already knows. Unsaid love gets misread A partner cannot see whats inside your head, and everyday acts of care are easy to read as habit or duty. Saying it plainly removes the guesswork and turns a feeling the other person had into something they can actually hold onto. It calms the background worry Many people carry a faint, constant question about whether they are still wanted. Hearing love expressed regularly answers that question before it grows, which tends to lower stress and make both people feel safer, including the one saying it, since voicing a feeling also strengthens it. It stops the relationship coasting In long relationships, affection is usually the first thing to be said less often, simply because life gets busy and the words start to feel unnecessary. Small, regular expressions work like maintenance, keeping two people connected instead of running on autopilot. It fills a quiet gap In many Indian households, love is shown through food, favours, and quiet sacrifice rather than words, and that language is real. Saying it aloud does not replace those acts, it simply makes sure the feeling behind them is actually heard. None of this means that the number of times matters most. Words work only when actions back them, and honesty counts more than frequency. But a feeling spoken at the right moment often does what months of silent effort cannot, which is to leave no room for doubt, she adds. The importance of physical touch As conversation flowed, Rashmika and Vijay kept brushing their feet against each other. That is when Vijay asks Rashmika what the most romantic thing that he has done for her is. Immediately, Prakhar Gupta replies, First of all, what youre doing right now. However, that was normal for the duo. This goes on 24x7, they say. Vijay later says, Some physical touch should always be there. That is one part of it. Rashmika also agrees with him. She says, I feel like we just live in a very romantic world, so. To this, Vijay adds, Maybe what is romantic for you is normal for us. Their upcoming movie Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna aregearing up for the release of their period dramaRanabaali, markinganother on-screen reunion for the actors. Directed by Rahul Sankrityan and produced by Naveen Yerneni and Y Ravi Shankar under the banner of Mythri Movie Makers, the period action drama is scheduled to release in theatres worldwide on October 16. articleTitle: RCB batting Coach says it is ‘Very hard’ for Kohli but Root has ‘good chance’ of breaking Tendulkar’s records
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kohli
description: Kohli became the second player after the great Sachin Tendulkar to reach 15,000 runs in the 50-over format during the 1st ODI against West Indies
body_raw: Virat Kohli and Joe Root have two of Sachin Tendulkars records in sight, records they can break. But they are different Kohli can reach 100 centuries, something only Tendulkar has done, and Root can surpass Tendulkars Test run tally of 15,921. Former Indian cricketer and batting coach of Royal Challengers Bengaluru Dinesh Karthik gave his view on the matter, saying it is tougher for Kohli to get to 100 centuries. I really wish he does, but I think it is very hard, Dinesh Karthik said of Kohlis chances on Cricbuzz. Good chance. They play a lot of Test cricket. He still looks quite fit. He is happily scoring runs every time he goes out to bat. So, I think it looks very possible for him, Karthik said on Root. Kohli became the second player after the great Sachin Tendulkar to reach 15,000 runs in the 50-over format during the 1st ODI against West Indies. Tendulkar took 377 innings to reach the milestone while Kohli did it in 303. With the talismanic India batter in hot form, Kohli will look to win his second ODI World Cup after clinching the trophy on home soil in 2011. He had a chance to repeat that feat on in 2023 but suffered a heartbreaking defeat in the final against Australia. The upcoming World Cup will be Kohlis fifth ODI World Cup and he has said that its going to be his last one. For me, its the last World Cup Im going to play for India. That is my motivation and like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup and whatever it takes, Im absolutely ready, Kohli told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday. The intensity of a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything. Because now, its about 10 games at a Twenty20 level of intensity. But you are playing 2.5 T20 games in one day. And to maintain that intensity for 10 games in a big tournament and World Cup is a big deal. Also now, its in foreign conditions. It takes a lot out of you, he had added.

articleTitle: ‘My father married around 20 people’: Sreelakshmi Arackal reveals traumatic childhood
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Evicted Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 contestant Sreelakshmi Arackal about her father.
description: As Sreelakshmi Arackal bid adieu to Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8, certain remarks she made about her father during her time in the house went viral on social media.
body_raw: In a first, Bigg Boss Malayalam saw a mass eviction this past weekend when as many as six contestants were shown the door from the ongoing Season 8 of the reality show. Among those evicted from the Mohanlal-hosted show was social activist Sreelakshmi Arackal.
