Opening up about the difficulties she has faced in her life, Sreelakshmi said that the reason she comes across as a man-hater, as many call her, is the intense hatred she holds for her father. Must Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr He married around 20 people Sreelakshmi on her father My father is a marriage fraudster. He has married around 10 to 20 people, including my mother. I am a child born out of such a relationship. The hatred towards my father is still there in my mind. That is what many people interpret as hatred for men misandry, Sreelakshmi said recently in the Bigg Boss house. Proudly naming her mother as her role model, she added, I was born through a Cesarean section C-section. Even before I turned six months old, my mother began going for daily wage labour. My grandmother wasnt very healthy and was mostly sick. So I did everything myself. Since the 6th or 7th grade, Id go to the ration shop alone and do everything men usually do. My mother was like that too. Shed go for painting and rubber tapping. Growing up watching her made me independent. Poverty was my motivation to study Sreelakshmi noted that for her mother - who thought her life was completely destroyed following childbirth - her brilliance in studies became the only hope. She continued, I was a rank-holder in BSc Physics. When I was born, my mother thought Id be a complete failure. But from first grade, I was always at the top of my class. Thats when my mother gained confidence in me. Poverty was my motivation to study, as there was no other way to succeed. My father is the reason Im standing here today because of the life he gave me. articleTitle: Does RAC guarantee a seat in Indian Railways? What Reservation Against Cancellation means for your train ticket
articleFeaturedImageAlt: An RAC ticket allows passengers to travel with reserved seating accommodation. (Image generated using AI)
description: Does an RAC ticket guarantee a seat on Indian Railways? Know what Reservation Against Cancellation means, whether you can board the train and when an RAC ticket can become confirmed.
body_raw: Indian Railways RAC rules seat guaranteeWhen booking a train ticket, passengers often come across the term RAC and wonder what it means for their journey. Does an RAC ticket allow them to board the train? Will they get a seat, or will they have to wait for a berth to become available?In Indian Railways, RAC stands for Reservation Against Cancellation. Here is how the RAC system works and what passengers can expect when travelling with an RAC ticket. What Reservation Against Cancellation means Speaking to Indianexpress.com, a senior railway official said that RAC is a reservation status used by Indian Railways when confirmed berths in a particular class have already been allotted but limited accommodation is still available for passengers. The official explained that a RAC passenger is permitted to board the train and is provided reserved seating accommodation. In classes with sleeping berths, two RAC passengers may initially be allotted seating on a berth designated for RAC passengers. This means that while the passengers journey is assured, a full sleeping berth is not necessarily assured at that stage, the official stated. Can RAC ticket become confirmed? According to the railway official, an RAC ticket can move to confirmed status if a berth becomes available.For example, if passengers holding confirmed reservations cancel their tickets before chart preparation, the available berths can be allotted to RAC passengers according to the applicable reservation system. So, a passenger whose status was RAC 25 at the time of booking may see it improve to RAC 10, RAC 2 or eventually CNF before the journey. Once the ticket becomes confirmed, the passenger is allotted a full berth, the official said. What happens if the ticket remains RAC after chart preparation? When asked about whether a passenger can travel with RAC ticket after chart preparation, the official replied that the passenger can still travel. If the ticket remains RAC after the final reservation chart is prepared, reserved seating accommodation remains available, but a full berth may have to be shared as per the RAC arrangement, the official added. The official further said that there is also a possibility of getting a full berth during the journey. If a confirmed passenger does not turn up, cancels at a stage permitted under the rules, or a berth otherwise becomes available, the vacant accommodation may be allotted to an RAC passenger by the travelling ticket checking staff as per applicable rules and priority. Why does Indian Railways have RAC system? As per the official, the RAC system helps Indian Railways make better use of available accommodation while giving more passengers certainty about their journey. Instead of keeping passengers entirely on the waiting list, RAC allows a limited number of passengers to travel with seating accommodation while keeping them in line for full berths that may become vacant due to cancellations, the official added.

articleTitle: Pneumonic plague in Russia? What we know about Siberian lab tech’s death
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sterile laboratory bench showing biohazard containment protocols (AI generated image). Russian health authority Rospotrebnadzor initiated plague quarantine procedures in Shelekhov near Irkutsk following the fatal laboratory-acquired infection of technician Daria Shipilova.
description: Plague outbreak in Russia: A lab technician at an Irkutsk anti-plague institute in Siberia died, and 197 contacts have been isolated amid reports of a pneumonic plague exposure but Rospotrebnadzor has not confirmed either a plague or a laboratory accident.
body_raw: It always begins with a broken test tube and a pathogen released, in every good or bad movie about plagues and epidemics. And one version of recent events in Russia sounds uncomfortably familiar. At least 197 people who may have had contact with a lab technician in Russias Irkutsk region have been placed under medical isolation. This was after reports the technician - Daria Shipilova - broke a test tube containing pneumonic plague bacteria while working at the anti-plague institute in Shelekhov, a small town roughly 20km from Irkutsk city. Shipilova was admitted to hospital with severe pneumonia on September 29. She died on October 2. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias federal public health body, diagnosed a pneumonia of unknown etiology but said it found no microorganisms associated with her work. It also said the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the region remains stable. But Alexei Tsydenov - the leader of Buryatia, a neighbouring republic Shipilova reportedly visited on work - first said she died of the plague. Hethen altered his post to add possibly. So is there really a plague in Russia? Not confirmed. Rospotrebnadzor has not confirmed a plague or that a laboratory accident occurred. Russian media has said 197 contacts have been identified and 189 are under observation. On October 2 Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said none of them are showing symptoms and their laboratory tests are negative. However, since then two have tested positive for COVID-19 and two others for rhinovirus, a viral infection behind the common cold. Gennady Onishchenko, a former head of Rospotrebnadzor, told state news agency TASS the onset of cold weather would likely prevent transmission. But that is one officials view and not a guarantee. How did Daria Shipilova fall ill? That is unclear, and there are two competing accounts. The first is the broken test tube. According to The New York Post, after that incident she was at places on Russias eastern border - near Mongolia - and fell ill on September 25. But Rospotrebnadzor contradicts this story. Its biosafety commission found no emergency involving pathogenic microorganisms at the institute. The second is that she fell ill after the work trip to Buryatia. But Tsydenov says she never visited the republic and that there is no outbreak there. What is pneumonic plague? It is a disease caused by the Yersinia pestis bacterium, the same one behind bubonic plague that ravaged Europe from 1346 to 1353 and was one of the most fatal pandemics in human history as much as 60 per cent of the European population of the time were killed. According to the US Centers for Disease Control, the pneumonic form spreads through infectious droplets when an infected person or animal coughs or sneezes. It can also develop when bubonic or septicaemic plague spreads to the lungs. Health officials consider it the most serious form. Symptoms usually appear between one and four days after exposure and can include fever, headache, weakness and a bloody or watery cough. The pneumonia rapidly worsens without treatment and can be fatal. But common antibiotics work, and recovery rates are high when treatment starts within 24 hours of the first symptoms. That is why close contacts are monitored. So what now? Three things to watch a laboratory report confirming the cause of Shipilovas death, a clearer account of how she was exposed, and the health of those under observation.

articleTitle: Rs 2.5 cr film Premada Ooralli beats Yash’s Toxic to emerge as most profitable Kannada movie
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Premada Ooralli
description: The financial constraints during the making of Premada Ooralli were so severe that, on one occasion, Kumar even asked his mother to pawn her mangalsutra, or thaali in Kannada, to help complete the shoot.
body_raw: Another small-budget film is becoming the talk of the town. This time, Kannada romantic drama Premada Ooralli has witnessed a remarkable jump at the box office. After opening at just Rs 9 lakh, the film earned Rs 3.5 crore on its tenth day, taking its total India net collection to Rs 16.96 crore. Made on a modest budget of just Rs 2.5 crore, Premada Ooralli is being touted as one of the most profitable films in Kannada cinema, alongside Love Mocktail 3 and Karavali. The film continues to draw audiences, with multiple shows in Bengaluru filling up even on a Monday, according to BookMyShow. From no shows to housefull According to industry tracker Sacnilk, the film opened to just Rs 9 lakh across 60 shows, partly because it did not feature a major Kannada star. However, word-of-mouth helped the film gain momentum almost immediately. On day two, Premada Ooralli saw its earnings rise by Rs 14 lakh, while the number of shows increased by 21. On day three, it earned Rs 55 lakh across 155 shows, recording a 55 occupancy. The film continued to grow even on weekdays, earning Rs 65 lakh on its first Monday and Rs 95 lakh on Tuesday. On its second Sunday, it collected Rs 3.85 crore, taking its India net total to Rs 14.57 crore at that point. Within 10 days, the film had crossed the one-million footfall mark in theatres. On its 11th day, Premada Ooralli had already crossed the Rs 1 crore mark, with the film running across 311 shows. Premada Ooralli to become the most profitable Kannada film While Toxic was one of the biggest Kannada releases of the year, the film failed to make an impact at the box office and reportedly could not recover its massive budget of over Rs 500 crore. Meanwhile, Love Mocktail 3, made on a reported budget of Rs 2 crore, earned Rs 18.55 crore at the box office, delivering nearly 10 times its investment. It was subsequently regarded as one of the most profitable Kannada films of the 21st century. Premada Ooralli, however, is now threatening to surpass that record, having already come close to its lifetime collection within just 10 days. Featuring a cast of relatively new faces, the film is directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Manoj Kumar. He won the National Award for Best Feature Film in Kannada for his debut film Akshi, which was made on a budget of just Rs 23 lakh and shot over 55 days. Produced by Vannila Entertainment, Janakamma Productions and Mukul Gowda Productions, the film stars Rangayana Raghu, Shree Raam, Thapaswini Poonacha and Ramika Shivu. The films trailer has garnered over 2.3 million views, while its songs have also found an audience online. Several tracks have clocked millions of views, with Eru Peru Hrudaya alone garnering 4.5 million views on YouTube. But the films journey to the big screen was far from easy. ALSO READ Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids No Benami property Begged people to give the film a chance By the time the shoot wrapped up, the makers had virtually no budget left for marketing. Their solution was unconventional they printed wedding-style invitation cards, boarded buses and trains, handed them to commuters and begged people to give the film a chance. Speaking to Cinema Express, Manoj Kumar recalled how the film initially struggled to find an audience. They plastered posters on autorickshaws we truly owe those drivers. At 1030 AM that Friday, not a whisper. By 130 PM, complete silence. Then came the 630 PM show, and word-of-mouth caught fire. What started across roughly 60 centres surged to 450 by Sunday. Jayanna Combines rolled in like a JCB to clear the path. Distributor Jayanna told us, Every single show through Sunday is houseful till October 4, even you wont get a ticket. Despite National Award win, director had no work Manoj Kumars return to filmmaking comes five years after his debut, but the gap was not by choice. Despite winning a National Award for Akshi, he struggled to find work. After winning the National Award for Akshi, I couldnt even find work people assumed backing an art-house director meant losing money. Devendra, our co-writer and producer, stepped up with his savings, he said. The financial constraints during the making of Premada Ooralli were so severe that, on one occasion, Kumar even asked his mother to pawn her mangalsutra, or thaali in Kannada, to help complete the shoot. When the director had to pawn his mothers mangalsutra Thapaswini Poonacha, one of the films leads, recalled the emotional incident. It was 630 PM, fading daylight, and our artificial rain water ran completely dry. Local villagers pumped water from their borewell to help us. Just then, Manoj sir stepped aside to call his mother, which Shree Ram and I overheard. Keep your thaali ready to pawn tomorrow todays budget is over, and if we dont get the shot now, we must extend the shoot. That broke us emotionally. Sir had told me Rukminis tears must never spill carelessly, they had to brim right in the eye. In that one single take, the rain, camera angles, and our emotions locked into place. When he yelled cut, hugged us, and told his mother, Keep your thaali, we finished in one take, I simply broke down. Premada Oorallis success is part of a larger trend in 2026, which has seen several small-budget films make an outsized impact at the box office across regional industries, including Hindis Hanuman Ansh, Marathis Deool Band 2 and Malayalams Bethlehem Kuduma Unit. In 2025, Gujarati film Laalo was all over the news for earning over Rs 120 crore after being made on a budget of just Rs 1.2 crore.

articleTitle: How a drug drop in Rohini led Delhi Police to heroin worth Rs 50 crores in Lucknow
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lucknow raid
description: Delhi Police crack an inter-state drug network and seize 6.25 kg of heroin from a drug manufacturing unit in Lucknow
body_raw: Heroin worth around Rs 50 crore was seized on Sunday from a drug manufacturing unit in Lucknow, which the supply chain led Delhi Police to after it intercepted a drug delivery in Delhis Rohini on September 16. On the night of September 16, a team of police from Rohinis Special Staff division had stopped a white SUV in Sector 32 of the Begumpur area. In the car was 58-year-old Laxman Hooda who was carrying 300 grams of heroin to deliver to a client, said police. Officers said that they had received a tip-off about this delivery and were waiting there for Hooda. 300 grams of Heroin and 3 lakh cash were recovered from his Grand Vitara car, which was also seized, said DCP Shashank Jaiswal. According to police, Hooda told them about his supplier, a resident of Delhis Raghubir Nagar named Anil, alias Bhola, who was on the run. Police traced him to Haryanas Sonipat and arrested him there, seizing yet another 500 gram package of heroin from him. Then, police said, Anil told them that he was getting his supply from a man he identified as Bablu from Lucknow. It took police another 15 days to zero in on the identity and location of this supplier. When they found him, they also found over 6 kg of heroin. On the basis of technical surveillance and human intelligence, on 04.10.2026, a raid was conducted at a heroin manufacturing facility in Sita Colony, Jankipuram, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, and Bablu, was apprehended. During the raid, 6.275 Kg of freshly manufactured heroin was recovered, said DCP Jaiswal. This quantity of heroin, police said, is valued at about Rs. 50 crores in the international market. Inside the Sita Colony house, a whole cache of drug mixing supplies was found 2.504 kg Sodium, 787 grams Acetic Anhydride, one tub, gas cylinder, mixer grinder, utensils, polythene, an electronic weighing machine, and a wooden basket. Police said that Bablu told them during interrogation that all the supplies had come from Bareilly, from a man he identified as Ruksar Ali. Ruksar Ali Raju, the main source supplierowner of the manufacturing facility, was traced and apprehended from Bareilly, UP after a prolonged and intensive pursuit of 120 km, said DCP Jaiswal. This was the second big heroin bust in Rohini this year. In April, the cops apprehended a family-run heroin operation in Rohini, which led them, again, to Bareilly and other parts of UP, leading to the recovery of a batch worth Rs. 16 crores. The source of this was traced to Manipur, where two men were allegedly procuring opium poppy-from which heroin is extracted-from a woman in the Indo-Myanmar border.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3 reminds us that more than family, the franchise is about movies
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn's Vijay Salgaonkar tells a story throughout the Drishyam trilogy.
description: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 concludes on a high, unlike the far more family-oriented Malayalam version, because it ties in neatly with what's always been the franchise's spiritual fulcrum -- the movies.
body_raw: More than a standalone movie, Abhishek Pathaks Drishyam 3 works best as the third act of Drishyam, if it were a consolidated crime thriller instead of a trilogy. The conflict gets set in Nishikant Kamats first part 2020 when Sam dies at the hands of Vijay Salganonkars Ajay Devgn family. The plot thickens in Pathaks Drishyam 2 2022 before the resolution comes in at a cinematic high in Drishyam The Conclusion, which released this past Friday on the befitting date of October 2. Like for the Goa police, pav bhaji, Maharaj ji ka satsang, and film watching in Panjim which film did they watch? Drishyam 3? were all distractions even for the audience. All this while, unreliable narrator Salgaonkar was doing what he does best - telling us a story through drishyam visuals. The movie-watching underdog In the first Drishyam, were introduced to Vijay Salgaonkar, a fourth class dropout whose only means to securing an education has been watching movies. Hes particularly on a steady diet of thrillers. Theyve edited it with fast cuts and taking the audience for a ride. On top of that is the pounding music So that it seems a lot is going on. But nothing is really happening. You need to feel the tension, he tells his subordinate, probably also referring to the Drishyam trilogy that takes its own sweet time to lure the audience in. At one point, Salgaonkar is also seen watching and weeping to Vipul Shahs 2005 family drama Waqt The Race Against Time. Though thats far from being a crime thriller, it does sound like a tagline to the Drishyam franchise itself. Because as the films unfold, we realize that every step of the way, Salgaonkar was far ahead of anyone else in the race against time. After his family panics following the murder of Sam, the only son of Goa Police Inspector General Meera Deshmukh Tabu, Salgaonkar devises a foolproof plan. He takes his family for an outing in Panjim the next day in order to crystallize the same chronology in granular detail when the police eventually interrogates them. Not just that, he even lives out that delayed reality for all the other eyewitnesses involved - the restaurant owner and the cinema projector operator among others - so that their testimonies sync with those of his family. Since Indians all across have grown up on movies, he uses that very device of visual memory as his weapon of choice. So, when the first part ends, Salgaonkar has an upper hand. But like most sequels, the conflict is brought back with a new lens. Enter Akshaye Khanna, who takes over the case from Tabu, capitalizing on his objective gaze sans personal prejudice. But to Salgaonkar, hes not the chief antagonist, but yet another actor just playing his part ironic, since thats what it turned out to be, given Khannas sudden exit from the franchise before Drishyam 3. To make the stakes more implausible yet interesting, he brings in Saurabh Shuklas character, an author who churns out a book out of the chain of events Salgaonkar has preempted. When the court dismisses the states case against Salgaonkar on the argument that the police is trying to frame a common man and his family by recreating events of a book, that twist seems far too convenient and far-fetched. But Shuklas author character is brought back again in Drishyam 3 to explain the rationale communicated to him by Salgaonkar - Films need not to be real. They just need to seem and feel real. That then becomes the spiritual fulcrum of not only the threequel, but also the trilogy. Suddenly, as Drishyam 3 draws to a close, the audience realize that Salgaonkar had been pulling the puppet strings all along. He uses the fame he gains from the events in the first part to rise the ranks and become a theatre owner from a DVD store owner. The events of the sequel allow him to further gain traction in his career, and become a film producer. But little do we know hes been producing a film all along - the film that weve been watching for the past 11 years. Through whats described as Salgaonkars three-part chakravyuh, the audience gradually uncovers that the sequel wasnt actually the second act, but the beginning of the second half of the film thats Drishyam. The climax of the first part boats of the cinematic high and narrative clencher of the interval block, and Drishyam 2 is merely a stepping stone to the rousing conclusion in Drishyam 3. Like every time, Salgaonkar was way ahead in the game, planning his course of action in Drishyam 2 itself, instead of saving it for the epic conclusion. A step above Mohanlals Drishyam 3 Spoiler alert Till the first two parts, Devgns Drishyam remained mostly faithful to its original source material, Jeetu Josephs films Drishyam and Drishyam 2 respectively, starring Mohanlal as Georgekutty, the Malayalam counterpart of Vijay Salgaonkar. But after the Malayalam Drishyam 3 didnt live up to the hype, Pathak and Devgn changed the course of their franchise, taking a completely new direction. However, this new direction neatly ties in with the spirit of the first part. It also weaves in the polarizing reaction towards Malayalam Drishyam 3 to tell a slightly deceptive story about family. Pathaks Drishyam 3 begins with Rajat Kapoors character Mahesh Deshmukh vowing to reopen the case and put Salgaonkar behind the bars, after his wife Meera tries to end her life out of depression. When Jaideep Ahlawats DCP hits back at Mahesh, asking him if hes a servant who reopens the case at his beck and call, its also a dig at the Malayalam Drishyam 3 which takes too many swings to take the story forward. In that version, Siddique who plays the Malayalam counterpart of Mahesh turns evil, a far cry from the fairly balanced sympathizer he is in the first two parts. Since SalgaonkarGeorgekuttys purported narrative throughout the franchise has been about protecting the family, it makes narrative sense to have another father determined to protect his family by avenging the death of his son. So, when Siddiques character steps up, it shouldve made for a riveting clash of the patriarchs. But what follows is a long-drawn, unwarranted climactic twist in which Georgekutty beats up his daughter in order to frame a troublesome cop. His argument was simple - beating up his daughter was in the larger interest of protecting his family from conviction. But it was not only problematic to watch, but also felt like a melodramatic copout. Surely, when the audience enter a theatre, they want to immerse themselves in the emotion and the drama. But not at the cost of the films own voice. So, when Pathaks Drishyam 3 avoids going down that path and instead pays a tribute to the movies, it all makes complete sense. When Salgaonkar pulls out his final trick from the hat, and the skeletons in his closet come tumbling out pun intended, he underlines what the Drishyam franchise has always been about - movies. Yes, family is at its heart too, but when his wife Nandini Shriya Saran breaks out of the character of the hapless wife, the film exposes family as just a visual decoy to make the police - and the audience - forget that Salgaonkars superhero power is watching movies. As the Malayalam Drishyam 3 revealed, family in fact turns out to be Georgekuttys Kryptonite. While he manages to get his family to dodge conviction yet again - paving the path ahead for another part - it comes at the cost of not only his daughters injuries, but also the audiences dissatisfaction. By making his Drishyam 3 all about the movies, Pathak underscores that while a family man may often have to sacrifice a part of his conscience for the sake of his family, a cinephiles win is written in the movie stars. Whether its a thriller like Drishyam or a family drama like Waqt, its always the sacrificial patriarch who pays a heavy price, while the underdog movie buff wins the race against time.

articleTitle: Vijay Deverakonda was ‘scared’ of speaking to women; Rashmika recalls attacks over accent
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda was 'scared' of speaking to women; Rashmika recalls attacks over accent
description: Actor couple Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna recently recalled the journeys of studying in their respective boarding schools during their formative years.
body_raw: Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda are busy promoting their upcoming film, Ranabaali. Ahead of its release, the actor couple recalled their respective boarding school experiences at a young age. In a recent interview, Vijay revealed that he was scared of talking to women after spending years in a strict boys hostel. On the other hand, his wife Rashmika shared that she was often cornered at school for her accent and language, something similar that happened with her in the film industry as well. During a candid interaction with Prakhar Gupta, Vijay Deverakonda shared, I was born in Hyderabad. When I was 6, I was put in a boarding school in Andhra Pradesh. It was a boarding school, boys hostel, and I grew up there from age 6-15. So, most of my life was in that boarding school. I came back to Hyderabad after passing 10th class. With no television, strict disciplinary rules, and almost no women in the hostel, the actor never developed a habit of talking to the opposite gender. I dont think it was to do with looks, but when you grow upin a boys hostel from age 6 to 15, and other than female teachers, you never seen a girl, this happens. Seeing girls from a distance felt like a concept, he said. ALSO READ Turn that music off Vijay Deverakondas blunt first words to Rashmika Mandanna on set He further added, Women are there and they walk like this, we werent allowed to look at each other. It was really strict. We used to spend 10 months in a year in boarding school. We came home only for two months to spend time with our families. There was no TV there and we were only shown one film every two weeks. When Vijay came back home, he did not speak to a girl for over two years. After spending 10 formative years there, when you come back as a teenager with hormones, you are attracted to the opposite gender but you dont know how they operate. You dont have the courage to talk to them. First two years of coming back, I didnt speak to a girl at all. I used to look outside the window in our school bus to avoid talking to the girls, he expressed. He continued, Girls thought it was cool or something so they would call me to sit with them and chat. Because I was scared of looking into their eye, I would look outside the window and talk. My heart would be pounding. But at some point, post my inter second year, I thought to myself that whats the point of all this fear. So when I went for my B.Com, I went and spoke to the first pretty girl I saw. When Rashmika Mandanna was asked about her experience of growing up in a completely different boarding school, she replied, I got into the boarding school at a very young age, at age 4. My boarding was co-ed, there was boys and girls hostel, you can have dinners together in different rows. After Class 5, the dining halls were separate. Ever since the beginning, there were interactions with boys. If the seniors said something, we had to listen to them. Thats how our hostel worked. ALSO READ Raju Kher recalls bad phase when brother Anupam Kher refused help Took him for granted The Animal actor recalled that she had to listen to her seniors to stay within the group. There were people from different parts of the world, and you had to live up to their traditions so that they dont call you uncool. Its not bullying, ragging, its actually cornering. The surviving skills I have today came from that time. In the industry today, I am doing the same thing I was doing at the hostel back then, she shared. The most challenging phase for Rashmika was speaking to people in English, because Tamil was the first language she learnt during early childhood. When I came to this hostel in Coorg. Suddenly, someone asked me something in English, and I went mum. I didnt know. It was terrible, I couldnt communicate in English. I went to the school in Class 4 and was there till Class 10, and by then people had already made their minds. No matter how much you speak in English, people already think You are lesser than us. I realised that it would be my survival instinct where I just smile to things, she recalled. Even after entering the film industry, she was always indifferent to comments over her language and accent. When I came to the industry, people commented that I have a different accent or that Im not a good actor. When something like this happens, and you feel that you have been dealing with such things since a long time. This is nothing new. Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakondas next film together is the period action drama Ranabaali. The film is set to hit the theatres on October 16, 2026. It has been directed by Rahul Sankrityan.

articleTitle: Dead drops in Punjab to godowns in MP, how drug kingpin’s syndicate operated
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, alias Navab Virk, sits inside an aircraft following his deportation from Turkiye to India. (Handout via PTI Photo)
description: A Delhi court has remanded the ‘drug kingpin’, who was deported from Turkey, to 10 days’ police custody.
body_raw: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, accused of running an international heroin syndicate, allegedly told investigators that drugs were delivered through dead drops - buried at multiple locations in Punjab and stored in godowns in Madhya Pradesh - according to the prosecution. A Delhi court on Saturday remanded the 34-year-old to 10 days custody of the Delhi Police Special Cell, which told the court it needed to recover the drugs, trace the syndicates supply chain, and identify other people involved in the alleged trafficking network. Navpreet, 34, was deported from Turkiye and arrested at Delhi airport on Saturday. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced his deportation in a post on X, saying Singh had obtained Turkish citizenship using the false identity of Navab Virk. The 2021 heroin case Navpreet was produced before Special Judge, Narcotic Drugs And Psychotropic Substances NDPS, Anuradha Shukla, at Rouse Avenue court on October 3 in a case dating back to July 2021. The Special Cell had then arrested a man in South Delhi and followed the trail to Faridabad, where a total of 358.08 kg of heroin was seized. During submissions, Special Public Prosecutor SPP Akhand Pratap Singh told the court, There is ample evidence against this accused Navpreet in form of his connection with co-accused Gurpreet and Gurjyot Singh, from whom huge quantity of heroin in total 358.08 kilogram was recovered. He also submitted that the co-accused had made disclosure statements against Navpreet. A cheque book recovered from the premises of co-accused Ramandeep belonged to the accused, the court order recorded. The court noted that Navpreet was declared a proclaimed offender on February 16, 2022. According to the prosecution, he had avoided investigation and court proceedings for more than four years. The court order also recorded the prosecutions submission that Navpreet had inflicted injuries on his hand and stomach when he was being handed over to the Special Cell. He was taken to Medanta Hospital at the Delhi Airport for medical treatment. Police seek to trace supply chain, identify associates According to the Special Cells remand papers, it sought Navpreets custody to question him about the alleged syndicates operations, his movements and the preparation of his passport in Delhi, as well as to confront him with statements made by other accused. It also sought to identify and apprehend other alleged suppliers, financiers, carriers and facilitators. The disclosure of the accused is on record wherein he has stated that he used to deliver drugs through dead drop, SPP Singh told the court. In a dead drop, a consignment is left at an agreed location for someone else to collect later. SPP Singh said Navpreet had told investigators that drugs had been buried at several places in Punjab and that he could identify the locations and help recover them. . the accused, in his disclosure, also stated that his associates, Labba and Manna, had taken godowns in MP where drugs were kept and there is a house in Punjab also which can be identified, the order reads. Judge Shukla said, The investigation necessitates police custody of the accused to recover the buried drugs which were dead dropped and other drugs which accused has stated that he has kept hidden to unearth the supply chain, source and transportation route for identification of other persons involved in procurement, transportation, storage and distribution and to establish complete financial trail connected with the illegal drug trade. The accused has to be taken to Punjab and MP for investigation purposes. For the needful to be done, 10 days police custody is being sought, which seems reasonable, the NDPS Judge said in the order. Navpreet is also an accused in a 2022 terror case lodged by the Special Cell. The case pertains to using funds allegedly obtained from selling narcotics to finance terror activities. A trail in Punjab Navpreet is from Wazir Bhulla village in the Beas area of Amritsar. He was first arrested in Punjab in a drug smuggling case in 2013 and was acquitted in 2017. Navpreets name re-surfaced in October 2024, when the Punjab Police counter-intelligence wing seized 105 kg of heroin at Baba Bakala. The two men arrested at that time were allegedly his associates. The India-based operations of the alleged drug syndicate were run by his cousin, Prabhdeep Singh alias Harry. Prabhdeep was extradited from Azerbaijan on May 13 by the Central Bureau of Investigation in coordination with the Special Cell.

articleTitle: ‘We were in love for 1.5 years’: Jason Sanjay on how his only relationship before Sigma ended
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Director Jason Sanjay, who has spoken publicly for the first time about his only romantic relationship
description: Director Jason Sanjay has revealed details about his only romantic relationship, a year-and-a-half-long college romance that ended in a mutual breakup while he was studying overseas.
body_raw: Jason Sanjay, director of Sigma and the son of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, has spoken publicly for the first time about his personal life, revealing that he has had only one romantic relationship, a college romance that lasted about a year and a half before ending in a mutual breakup. The period following the breakup was when he fully committed himself to making Sigma. There was only one love. It was a long time ago, when we were in college. We were in love for about a year and a half, Jason Sanjay said in a conversation with VJ Siddhu. It was a mutual breakup. We both talked to each other and broke up. Jason Sanjay, who studied filmmaking, said the breakup happened while he was overseas. The distance, he said, made the experience both isolating and clarifying. Also Read Sigma movie review Jason Sanjays debut has the vision but not the script to match Asked how he coped, Jason Sanjay answered, During the breakup, I used to listen to all the love songs of Yuvan Shankar Raja. The director later revealed that he deliberately stayed away from social media during and after the breakup.I didnt have any plans to post stories on Instagram. If we post stories after the breakup and then reconnect, we cant get out of it. So we kept a distance between us. I always control myself to not do things that I dont want to do, Jason Sanjay said. Jason Sanjay said he is at peace with the relationship and its ending. Im okay now. It was good at the time. We move on with our lives, he said. And then came the line that connects his personal life to his professional one After that, I got down to Sigmas business. About Sigma Sigma, an action-adventure heist comedy, stars Sundeep Kishan in the lead alongside Faria Abdullah, Raju Sundaram, Sampath Raj, Shiv Panditt, Anbu Thasan and Yog Japee. The music is composed by S Thaman, cinematography is by Krishnan Vasant, editing by Praveen KL and VFX by Hariharasuthan. The film is produced by Subaskaran under Lyca Productions. The film was originally scheduled to release on July 31, but was postponed to avoid clashing with Vijays final film Jana Nayagan. The movie was released worldwide on October 2.

articleTitle: In Maharashtra, everybody is protesting – From ‘cockroaches’ to tribals to women
articleFeaturedImageAlt: abhijeet dipke, cjp, mumbai protests
description: The triggers are many – farm loan waiver, student hostel facilities, better roads, noise pollution, irregularities in government recruitment exams, functioning of the Election Commission, among others.
body_raw: Protests in Maharashtra have reached a crescendo. In the past few weeks, different parts of Maharashtra have witnessed a string of agitations-from Gen-Z to tribal students to women, though only a few made the headlines. On Friday, October 2, the Cockroach Janata Party CJP held a protest in Mumbai, demanding the ouster of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, followed by a similar protest by the Thackeray cousins. As this was happening, another one walked into Mumbai from Nashik over the weekend-the tribal students. The triggers are many-farm loan waiver, student hostel facilities, better roads, noise pollution, irregularities in government recruitment exams, functioning of the Election Commission, among others. The Indian Express has listed what has kept the state government and the Maharashtra Police on their toes over the past few months. Farmers Farmers protested in June and July 2026, demanding eligibility relaxations in the Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar farm loan waiver scheme. In September 2026, the All India Kisan Sabha launched protests, demanding regular crop loan payees be given a Rs 2 lakh incentive In June 2026, onion farmers staged Rasta Roko on the Pune-Nashik national highway, demanding MSP for their produce. For the past year, farmers from western Maharashtra and Marathwada have protested against the Shaktipeeth road project, refusing to part ways with their lands. Students For over 2 years, students preparing for Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC examinations have protested against exam fees, online exams, delayed results and irregularities. The protests intensified after Vivek Bhimanwar was appointed the MPSC chairman. Students in Pune protested over hostel rules. What worked as a catalyst was the deaths of tribal students in Gadchiroli due to snake bites. In September 2026, resident doctors and interns across Maharashtras government medical colleges protested against allowing homoeopathy practitioners to be registered with the Maharashtra Medical Council MMC. Students have been protesting at IIT Bombay since the death of Sahil Wakode on September 18. CJP protests in Mumbai and surrounding areas in support of the Jantar Mantar agitation. Women Women excluded from Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme are protesting, alleging bias. Pune, Nagpur, and Mumbai witnessed citizens protesting in solidarity with the survivors of sexual assault across India. Social activist Manoj Jarange-Patil held a 20-day hunger strike, demanding Maratha quota To counter Jarange, OBC organisations held protests, alleging the government was diluting OBC reservation. Maharashtra is witnessing protests from Dhangar and Banjara communities, demanding Scheduled Tribe ST status. Mischellaneous A road blockade was held in August 2026 across Pune, Nashik and Ahilyanagar districts to demand restoration of the original direct railway alignment between Pune and Nashik. Citizens and environmentalists from across the state are protesting against the felling of trees in Nashik to make arrangements for the upcoming Sinhastha Kumbh Mela. Days before the Ganesh festival, Pune residents took to the streets, demanding a blanket ban on the use of DJs during festivals and religious events. Thanes Balkum, Majiwada and Dhokali saw protests against a hyperscale data centre, expected to consume 422 MW of power, 125 kilolitres of treated water daily and have 193 diesel generators on standby.

articleTitle: Supreme Court refuses to intervene in pleas challenging Great Nicobar Project
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Great Nicobar Project, Great Nicobar Project case, Supreme Court Great Nicobar Project, Calcutta High Court Great Nicobar Project PIL, Forest Rights Act violations, Great Nicobar PIL, Great Nicobar tribal rights, Great Nicobar environmental case, Meena Gupta Great Nicobar Project PIL, Great Nicobar infrastructure project, Supreme Court news, Calcutta High Court, Indian express news
description: The Centre had challenged the Calcutta High Court order rejecting its objection to petitions filed by retired IAS officer Meena Gupta against the Great Nicobar project.
body_raw: The Supreme Court Monday refused to intervene in a Calcutta High Court order, that allowed PILs challenging alleged Forest Rights Act violations in the Great Nicobar Project to proceed, saying the matter was already pending before the high court. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also pointed out that the main case is pending for final arguments and is listed for hearing on November 25 and 26. The Centre argued that the project was of great national importance and the maintainability of such Public Interest Litigations goes to the root of the matter. If I am able to place something more regarding maintainability, please allow us to place that submission. Do not close the door on maintainability because something very important turns on that, Attorney General of India R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, submitted before the court. Justice Bagchi observed that the high court had already ruled on maintainability and that the question now was on how far public interest survives, which would be considered there. Do they become integrated completely with the mainstream, or do we keep them with their unique identity and the identity of their culture? Preservation of culture is a constitutionally protected fundamental right, Justice Bagchi said, referring to the projects impact on indigenous communities. Let the high court take necessary steps to complete pleadings in the other matters and make an endeavour to hear the cases on the date fixed, the bench noted. What Calcutta High Court said The Centre had approached the top court challenging the Calcutta High Courts May 6 judgement, which rejected its objection to PILs filed by retired IAS officer Meena Gupta. Guptas petitions challenge decisions linked to the Great Nicobar Project, including alleged violations of the Forest Rights Act in obtaining consent from tribal communities and notifications reducing eco-sensitive buffer zones around Galathea and Campbell Bay National Parks. The Centre had argued that Gupta, a resident of Hyderabad, lacked legal standing and that a project involving a proposed port, airport, power plant, and defence infrastructure could not be challenged through a PIL. Rejecting the objection, the Calcutta High Court held, There is no thumb rule regarding the aspect of locus standi. It would not be expedient to lay down any general rule which would govern all cases under all circumstances. The high court also said that merely because a project involves substantial public expenditure, it is not insulated from judicial review, observing that a project involving huge expenditure must proceed in accordance with governing laws holding the field. What is the Great Nicobar Project The Great Nicobar Project is a proposed large-scale development programme that involves building a major transhipment port, airport, power plant, and other infrastructure, along with associated roads and development, at an estimated cost of around Rs 72,000 crore. The project has faced criticism over its potential impact on tribal communities and their rights alleged violations of the Forest Rights Act and environmental clearance norms changes to protections around ecologically sensitive areas such as Galathea Bay and Campbell Bay and the large-scale diversion of forest land and its impact on wildlife and biodiversity. The Centres position is that the project is of major strategic and national importance, including because of Great Nicobars location near major international shipping routes.

articleTitle: Gym trainer found dead in Bengaluru flat ‘after party’; 4 friends detained
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru gym trainer found dead
description: The 25-year-old man’s mother said she initially got information that her son was in critical condition in a hospital.
body_raw: A gym trainer was allegedly found dead in a North Bengaluru flat on Sunday, and the police have detained four men in connection with the incident. The police identified the man as Nandan, 25, a resident of Hebbal who worked at the Masiv Gym, located at Sahakaranagar. Nandans family members were informed around 3 pm on Sunday. His mother Manjula said, We reached the hospital after I received a call stating Nandan was in serious condition. But by the time we reached there, we came to know that he had already died. There were injury marks on his dead body. Nandan was Manjulas only son. The police have detained gym trainers Vishwanath, Sharath, and Nishanth and Anush Shetty, owner of the Smocky Docky restaurant. Mithun Kumar G K, Deputy Commissioner of Police Northeast, said on Monday, On Saturday evening, all four celebrated the first anniversary of the Masiv Gym and visited the Prestige Misty Water apartment located in Kempapura. Anush Shetty stays there. We came to know about the death around 7.30 am on Sunday. The body was shifted to Manipal Hospital for a postmortem. Later, Nandans family members filed a complaint with the Amruthahalli police. His mother said the family suspects that the four detained men killed him. We are waiting for the postmortem report. It appears that some personal rivalry could have led to the incident. But the prima facie information suggests that all four were thick friends and knew each other for nearly one year, Mithun added. A police officer said that Nandan might have been hacked to death that night. They may have consumed alcohol, and it appears that there was a fight among them, leading to his death, the officer added.

articleTitle: Why more Indian students are choosing Ireland over UK, Europe for education
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ireland Trinity college Dublin
description: Latest data shows Indian students now form the largest international cohort in Irish universities, driven by lower total costs, a thriving tech sector, and favourable post-study work norms.
body_raw: Written by Sameer Anasingaraju Ireland is increasingly emerging as a preferred destination for Indian students pursuing higher education abroad, with its English-speaking environment, shorter postgraduate courses and post-study work opportunities drawing students away from traditional destinations like the United Kingdom UK and other European countries. According to the Ireland Higher Education Authority HEA, 44,535 non-Irish-domiciled enrolments were recorded in higher education in 2024-25, a 10.2 per cent increase from the previous year. Indian students formed the largest international cohort, accounting for 20.6 per cent of these enrolments, around 9,175 students. While the numbers may be modest compared with the number of students who go abroad every year for studies, the uptick is unmistakable. From just over 2,000 students in 2017-18, the numbers rose steadily before the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted international student mobility. The recovery after the pandemic, however, was followed by a much sharper rise. Enrolments crossed 4,000 in 2021-22, then jumped to 7,070 in 2023-24. By 2024-25, the figure had climbed to 9,175, meaning Ireland was receiving more than four times as many Indian students as it did seven years earlier. The particularly steep increase in the last two years suggests that Irelands appeal is no longer limited to a small group of students, but is becoming a mainstream alternative for Indians considering education in the UK, US and other European countries. The English factor For many, Irelands use of English as the primary language of instruction is one of its biggest advantages over countries like Germany and the Netherlands, alongside shorter masters programmes, particularly when comparing overall costs. Tanishka Prabhu, 22, from Pune, studied at Griffith College Dublin from 2023-2025 and now works in Ireland. I came here for my bachelors. Mostly Indians come for masters here. When I came in January 2023, there were very few Indian students. But now they are here in huge numbers, Prabhu said. I chose Ireland because my elder sister also did her masters here, and while researching, we found out that expenses are lower than in Europe. It is an English-speaking country, and the weather is extremely nice too. Saanvi Gambhir, pursuing a masters in finance at University College Cork, had initially considered Germany. I chose Ireland as the post-study norms are much better than the UK. I was planning for Germany, but there is also the language barrier there. Here, theres no such issue. Aman Nanda, also pursuing finance at University College Cork, compared Ireland with the UK. I was initially planning for the UK, but I chose Ireland because the quality of life, education, and economy are much better than there, he said. My experience has been really amazing. Everyone is extremely nice and helpful here, with absolutely zero racism towards Indians. The course quality is excellent, and so are the teachers teaching it. Sadaf Sheikh, 28, is pursuing an LLM at Trinity College Dublin and initially considered the Netherlands. I wanted to go to the Netherlands, but it is much more costly than Ireland. Here the masters is only for one year, and we can work for two years after it is over. Sustainable career at affordable cost For Akheel Sisal, going abroad was a childhood dream, but the real question was where education could lead to a sustainable career without overwhelming costs. After his MBA in Pune and experience as a data analyst, he explored European colleges, but consultancies flagged his undergraduate record as a hurdle - until Ireland emerged unexpectedly. I started checking with friends studying in Ireland, and they told me the IT market was growing, there were job opportunities, and the process was relatively easy, Sisal recalls. Compared to the uncertainty of the United States - high tuition, heavy loans, visa concerns - Ireland seemed more manageable. The US was never an option because of the uncertainty, he says. Some of my friends had hefty loans and were still struggling to pay them back. Despite being warned his profile might not secure admission, Sisal received three acceptance letters and chose National College of Irelands one-year Masters in Data Analytics, with a E4,000 scholarship on a E15,000 fee. I asked if I would have to study from huge notebooks and prepare for written examinations. They told me the programme was much more practical and lab-focused. I knew then that this was where I wanted to go. Before graduating, he secured a full-time role and now works as a data and AI manager. Consultants see a pattern Education consultants in Pune also report rising interest. Digvijay Sawant of Imperial Overseas Educational Consultants said Ireland particularly attracts students in technology, pharma, and management. There is a rise in recent years of people going to Ireland. Ireland is known for three things IT, pharma, and management, noting the country is often called the Silicon Valley of Europe. In other European countries or the US, the masters programme is for two years. In Ireland, it is only for one year. After that, you can stay back for two years. Also, there is no language barrier. Costs are also down because youre only paying for 1 year of education instead of two, Sawant said. The seats for Ireland are getting filled very fast. Last year, we sent around 20-25 students to Ireland. We are currently on track to beat that number this year, he said. With inputs from Kalyani Lad. Sameer Anasingaraju is an intern with The Indian Express.

articleTitle: CJI Surya Kant: Any modified Form 6 not approved by Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Election Commission of India SIR Form 6 Gyanesh Kumar
description: Referring to The Indian Express report, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy argued that the Election Commission had made an 'unlawful alteration' to Form 6, targeting first-time voters.
body_raw: In response to an argument on the unlawful modifications made to Form 6, which new voters have to fill, Chief Justice of India CJI Surya Kant on Monday said that the Supreme Court hadnt approved any of the modifications to Form 6 and indicated that the court will examine who had modified it upon receiving a report from the Election Commission. The statement came when a three-judge bench headed by the CJI was hearing the petitions filed against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. For the first time, the Election Commissions online version of the electors registration form, known as Form 6, included a new section that seeks the status of the applicants parents vis-a-vis the last Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, even though the statutory form itself has not been amended. The Election Commission, however, removed the SIR declaration added to Form 6 from its ECINET application portal in states where the SIR has concluded. The poll body had on September 26 announced that for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Referring to The Indian Express report, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy argued, Let me give you an illustration.since it pertains to most recently, for instance, Delhi. Let us see how the SIR was conducted in Delhi. Form 6 has two new conditions added. Those Forms 6 were circulated. Neither the petitioner is now allowed to be on the roll. I got a notice also.based on this new Form 6, which cannot, under the schedule, be modified. Responding to Guruswamy, the CJI said, Lets be very clear. Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let us also be clear that when the report will be produced, we will like to see who has modified what. Form 6 coverage The Indian Express had reported on the Election Commissions September 26 press note on Form 6. The ECI had then said the form prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules will apply outside the SIR period. The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, it read. Guruswamy was arguing a petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, which stated, Defying this binding majority, respondent number 3 Gyanesh Kumar, acting in concert with respondent number 6 DG-IT, altered Form 6 digitally on the ECINet portal in July 2026. On August 13, 2026, Commissioner Sandhu formally recorded that this alteration was unauthorised and illegal and was causing arbitrary harassment to young, eligible first-time electors, ordering its immediate withdrawal. Despite this, the unauthorised form was kept live on the portal. The plea argues there was a unilateral and illegal alteration of statutory Form 6 for first-time young voters without legislative authority or amendment of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 which could be termed unauthorised and illegal by a majority of the Commission. The petition further alleged that the act of the Chief Election Commissioner of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bears no reasonable nexus or legal connection to his official duties. Such an act falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability, it added.

articleTitle: Batter who played vital role in Sydney draw during 20/21 BGT says: ‘Have to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar
description: "But it's not like I don't want to play for India. If I get a call, as simple as that," Bhuvneshwar said on his prospects of returning to India on the Jatin Sapru channel.
body_raw: In the third ODI during Indias game against West Indies in New Chandigarh, the hosts failed to defend 351 runs. In the 2nd ODI at Guwahati, they also conceded over 400 runs. Indian cricketer Hanuma Vihari noted that India should bring back Bhuvneshwar Kumar into the team. I think they have to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back. In my opinion, he is still one of the best bowlers in the country. He is proving in the IPL, Vihari said on his YouTube channel. Of course. I mean, Ive said before as well that Im not playing to prove anything right now. But its not like I dont want to play for India. If I get a call, as simple as that, Bhuvneshwar said on his prospects of returning to India on the Jatin Sapru channel. Bhuvneshwar also said he has moved past the phase of anxiety. I think Ive moved past that phase where I used to wait thinking, maybe this team, this series. Its been a few years now I dont get into that space anymore, he said. Vihari pointed at the injury records of both Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya and said if that happens, they cannot rely on bowlers without experience, suggesting its better to go for Bhuvneshwar and Shami. You cannot depend on Bumrah and Hardik. You have to have backup in case of such injuries. I will say go with experience. Get Bhuvneshwar and Shami back, he said. You will have some security with experience. When you need a breakthrough, you can go to them, and they will do the job for you. You need stability and experience will always count, Vihari said. We could not defend 350. Is this not a wake-up call? I think the team is going backwards. This is a big blow, he said. The West Indies exposed the Indian bowling attack. They are not even part of the World Cup. Imagine top teams like Australia, South Africa, England, Vihari added.

articleTitle: India’s HPV vaccine Cervavac gets WHO’s safety nod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: hpv
description: Previously approved for its use in India by the drug controller, Cervavac is administered for the prevention of diseases caused by the four HPV types
body_raw: Cervavac, Indias first indigenously developed gender-neutral quadrivalent Human Papillomavirus vaccine qHPV developed by Serum Institute of India has got the prequalification status by the World Health Organization WHO. This regulatory milestone marks the 32nd WHO prequalification for productsbiologicals received by Serum Institute of India. Inclusion on the WHO List of Prequalified Vaccines allows Cervavac to be procured by United Nations UN agencies. The vaccine targets HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18. It is indicated for girls and boys aged nine through 26 years. Adar Poonawalla, Chief Executive Officer, Serum Institute of India, said, WHO prequalification of CERVAVAC is an important step in strengthening the global response to HPV. This milestone reflects the effectiveness of the vaccine and creates the opportunity for countries to prevent HPV-related risks. We are pleased to see this indigenously developed vaccine reach this achievement, and look forward to contributing to immunisation coverage, advancing global healthcare Previously approved for its use in India by the Drugs Controller General of India DCGI, Cervavac is administered for the prevention of diseases caused by the four HPV types. This includes the prevention of anal cancer in boys and young men, and cervical, vulvar, vaginal, and anal cancers in girls and young women. It is also indicated in preventing genital warts, as applicable to the indicated population. Cervavac is indicated in girls and women between 9 through 26 years of age for the prevention of cervical, vulvar, vaginal and anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and genital warts caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Cervavac is indicated in boys and men 9 through 26 years of age for the prevention of anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and genital warts caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Those between 9 and 14 years of age receive Cervavac according to a two-dose schedule 0.5 mL at 0, 6 months, while individuals 15 to 26 years of age receive a three -dose 0.5 mL at 0, 2, 6 months schedule. The vaccine is administered intramuscularly. Cervavac is available in 1-dose vials of 0.5 ml and 2-dose vials of 1.0 ml presentations.

articleTitle: Woman’s Rs 20 lakh caught between two banks’ ‘ping-pong’, gets refund, payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission, deficiency in service, wrongly transferred money to closed account, bank transfer to closed loan account reversal, Consumer Protection Act 2019 45 days reply rule, refund of wrong bank transfer, National Consumer Helpline 1915, bank ping pong blame game consumer case, principle of non-traverse consumer court, Hemanshu Mishra consumer commission order, private bank transfer error refund rules
description: A woman mistakenly transferred Rs 20 lakh to her husband’s already-closed loan account and was caught between the two banks' blame game for over two months.
body_raw: A Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission has held two banks guilty of deficiency in service after a womans Rs 20 lakh remained blocked in an administrative loop for over two months after she mistakenly transferred it to her husbands already closed loan account, involving two banks blaming each other over who should reverse the transaction. Calling it a ping-pong blame game, the commission directed the banks to refund the amount and pay Rs 30,000 payout to the woman. President Hemanshu Mishra, members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur observed that the institutional apathy of both banks subjected the woman and her family to avoidable financial distress, severe mental agony, and forced litigation. The ping-pong blame game trapped the consumer in an administrative loop. Holding funds in a closed loan account despite clear, immediate written notices from both the remitter and the account holder constitutes a gross operational default and a clear deficiency in service, the September 11 order said. The order added that instead of executing a prompt reversal, standard protocol when funds were credited to a defunct or closed account, the bank engaged in bureaucratic delay, issuing automated responses before ultimately advising the wife to approach the remitting bank. 20 lakh transferred to a closed account The wife initiated a transaction of Rs. 20 lakh from her savings account held with a private bank, intending to transfer funds to her husband, and due to a clerical error, the funds were mistakenly directed to her husbands closed personal loan account maintained with another private bank. The loan account was fully settled and closed before the transaction date. Realising the error, the wife immediately notified her husbands bank on April 2, requesting reversal. The bank advised her on April 5 to approach her home branch from which the transaction was initiated. She then routed her complaint through her home branch on April 14. Subsequently, her bank put the blame back on the husbands bank, stating that reversal depends on the beneficiary bank. Caught in a cycle of blame-shifting between both banks, her funds remained blocked, forcing her husband to take an alternative loan by pledging shares on April 24 to manage liquidity. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of both the banks, she filed the present complaint, seeking refund along with compensation and litigation costs. Upon notice, both the banks appeared before the commission, but failed to file their reply within 45 days from the date of service. Hence, their right to reply was struck off and not legally recorded. Complaint allowed The commission observed that the documents adduced by the woman remain entirely unrebutted, unchallenged, and unimpeached, leaving no cogent reason to disbelieve the reliable and convincing evidence presented on record. The commission directed the two banks to pay Rs. 12,500 to the woman along with interest and also directed the husbands bank to pay Rs. 7,500 to her along with interest. It further added that both the banks jointly and severally pay Rs. 10,000 to the woman for litigation expenses. Takeaway The ruling highlights that if the banks fail to file their written versions within 45 days of notice, as mandated under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the principle of non-traverse would apply, and the complainants avermentswould stand legally admitted. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Himachal Pradesh 1800-180-8087 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: ‘He asked if I had AIDS’: Gayathri Suresh on her past toxic ‘situationship’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 alumna Gayathri Suresh about a toxic relationship.
description: Evicted Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 contestant Gayathri Suresh once opened up about a past toxic relationship in the house, revealing the shocking aftermath of her viral 2021 car accident.
body_raw: Although Bigg Boss Malayalam is known for delivering shocking surprises from time to time, even the shows biggest fans didnt expect to see actor Gayathri Suresh evicted from the ongoing edition of the Mohanlal-hosted show on its second day itself. Even more surprising was the way she re-entered the house on Day 9. Now, after about three weeks, Gayathri has bid farewell to the reality series once and for all. Gayathri was one of the eight contestants who were shown the door during the past weekends mass eviction. A few days before she stepped out the front door, she made certain remarks, revealing the darkest and most painful chapter of her personal life, which have caught peoples attention. Must Read My father married around 20 people Sreelakshmi Arackal reveals traumatic childhood Gayathri Suresh on the incident that traumatised her the most During one of the tasks, Bigg Boss asked her, If you got an opportunity to speak to the person who hurt you the most in life, what would you say? Gayathri then opened up about a past situationship that scarred her emotionally. Many people have hurt me in my life. but what hurt me the most, or rather what traumatised me the most, happened when I was embroiled in a controversy in 2021. At that time, I was in a situationship. I thought it was a relationship, but looking back now, I think it was just a situationship, she recalled. Although that person displayed major red flags from the beginning, the actor said she still gave him multiple chances to correct himself, as that was her nature. Im someone who notices everyones red flags quickly. Yet, I give people three chances, and then theyre out of my life. In the first week of our relationship, he asked me if I had AIDS. At that moment, I cut him off, she said. But then, you dont know if youre being too negative, always looking for red flags. Hence, I continued the relationship. Later, I found out that he was in a relationship with someone else. While I am based in Thrissur, he lives in Ernakulam, and there, he was in a relationship with another girl, the actor revealed. Gayathri Suresh on her viral 2021 car accident She continued, At that time, I was at rock bottom myself. Yes, I also have a lot of bad habits, so I wouldnt say I am a perfect person. But I have a good heart and dont want to hurt anyone. Then he started ignoring me completely. One day, I put my foot down and told him I had to see him, so he came. We were together in a car when the controversial accident happened. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr For the unversed, in October 2021, the car Gayathri Suresh was travelling in with a male friend, who was behind the wheel at the time of the incident, reportedly collided with another vehicle. Instead of stopping immediately, they allegedly drove away. The occupants of the second vehicle pursued them and eventually forced them to stop. Soon, a crowd gathered, and the matter escalated. Videos of the incident also went viral. During the Bigg Boss task, she further recalled, The police came and took him to the station following the accident. After coming back, he left me alone in a cafe and went to see his other girlfriend. That was the most traumatising thing for me. ICYMI Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner Avinash Mishra takes home trophy and Rs 20 lakh She added, So if I were to see him again, I would say, Thank you so much. I can clearly imagine what his girlfriend went through because it was a narcissistic relationship and there was narcissistic abuse. So if I see him now, Id say, Thank you so much for going after someone else. Otherwise, I would have had to suffer in that relationship. I grew because of that. I decided then that I would get better and grow. Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 mass eviction Jaseela Parveen, Sumesh Chandran, Sreelakshmi Arackal, Loletta, Rakesh, RJ Anjali and Mridula were the other seven contestants to exit Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 along with Gayathri Suresh. However, Anjali and Mridula have not been eliminated from the competition and are currently staying in a secret room. Meanwhile, a day after the mass eviction, four wildcard contestants - Nilina Elizabeth Joseph, Vedangi Cherukattu, Vipin Das Nair, and Suvarna Pulthukkiyil - entered the house.
