articleTitle: Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line commissioned, train operations to improve on Pune-Daund rail route
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line commissioned to improve train operations and ease congestion on the Pune-Daund rail route. (Image: Central Railway)
description: The Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line has been commissioned on the Pune-Daund rail route, improving train operations, freight movement and railway capacity while helping ease congestion at Pune station.
body_raw: Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd railway line commissioned The Central Railway CR has commissioned Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd railway line in Pune. The move is expected to improve train operations and increase capacity on the Pune-Daund rail route. This new railway line is also likely to improve the movement of both passenger and freight trains and provide greater operational flexibility in the Pune railway network. It will also help in reducing congestion and enable smoother movement of freight rakes. Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line to improve train movement The commissioning of the third Ghorpuri-Hadapsar line is expected to provide a dedicated transfer route between the rake maintenance depot and the proposed Hadapsar Satellite Terminal. This will allow such movements to take place without affecting operations on the UP and DOWN main lines. The arrangement is expected to facilitate the introduction of new train services from Hadapsar. New line to reduce congestion at Pune railway yard According to Dr Swapnil Nila, Chief Public Relations Officer CPRO of CR, the Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line will serve as an alternate shunting neck for rake formation, sorting, engine and brake-van reversal and other shunting activities.This will help reduce the detention of trains on the main line and improve punctuality. Overall, it will help in decongestion of Pune station by facilitating transfer and operational activities through the Hadapsar Satellite Terminal, the CPRO said in a statement. Major signalling and track works completed Several works were carried out as part of the project, including alterations to signalling and interlocking systems at Pune and Hadapsar. At Pune, 32 new or altered routes, six new or altered point machines, nine new or altered signals and 11 new or altered tracks were completed. At Hadapsar, the existing Kyosan K5D electronic interlocking was altered. The work also included 28 new or altered routes, one new or altered point machine and six new or altered signals. Other works included replacement of insulated overlaps and section insulators, installation of new portals, provision of AC brackets in turnout areas and four DC track circuits. 900 metres of contact wire replaced As part of the work, around 900 metres of damaged contact wire was replaced, restoring the speed potential on the affected section from 75 kmph to 130 kmph.Rail renewal, tamping, distressing, greasing, packing and welding works were also carried out. The works were completed over a span of 15 days using equipment including track relaying machines, Duomatic machines, Poclain machines, Hydra cranes, JCBs and gas-cutting equipment. A total of 745 personnel, including 485 contractual workers and 260 departmental staff, were deployed for the project.

articleTitle: ‘Defeating BJP more important’: DMK, Akhilesh Yadav’s UP poll message
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Akhilesh-Yadav
description: "The alliance should win and defeat the BJP. One party getting two or three seats more is not the question. Everybody should stand united to defeat the BJP," said DMK spokesperson.
body_raw: Amid speculation of tensions between INDIA bloc allies Samajwadi Party and Congress over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the DMK backed SP president Akhilesh Yadavs statement, emphasising that alliance victory is more important than seat-sharing, and urged parties to unitedly defeat the BJP. Following reports on the rift within the INDIA boc allies, Yadav took to the social media platform X on Sunday to assert that the primary focus should be on defeating the BJP and protecting democracy, the Constitution, and reservation. DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan said the party backs SPs stance. The alliance should win and defeat the BJP. One party getting two or three seats more is not the question. Everybody should stand united to defeat the BJP, he said. EC not neutral body The Election Commission is a neutral body. But after Gyanesh Kumar had come, it is not a neutral body, he claimed, alleging that Kumar was functioning under the influence of the ruling party at the Centre. Speculations over the rift between SP and Congress come amid Opposition parties clarion call to protest against the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls and the Election Commission. Key INDIA bloc leaders met last week to chalk out ways to organise a joint protest seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, halt the SIR process following Express Investigation revealing the rupture within the EC and Form 6 irregularities. Uttar Pradesh polls As Uttar Pradesh is headed for Assembly polls in February 2027, the Congress party has undergone a leadership revamp, reportedly drawing the ire of SP members. The appointment of Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president of its Uttar Pradesh Congress has been reportedly perceived as a pressure tactic to bargain for more seats in the polls. While SP spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary told The Indian Express that Masoods appointment would have no adverse impact on his partys seat-sharing talks with the Congress, some other SP leaders privately expressed discomfort over the development. I dont understand what is in the mind of the top Congress leadership. The new UP Congress president, Aradhana Misra Mona, and her father, Pramod Tiwari, have cordial relations with the SP. Her appointment will only help in smoothening dialogue between the two parties regarding the UP polls. But Masood, through his remarks on the SP, often creates uneasiness. Now, things will depend on how much authority senior Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra give Masood in seat-sharing talks, an SP insider told The Indian Express earlier. Masood, 56, a prominent face in western Uttar Pradesh politics, had rejoined Congress in 2023 following brief stints with BSP and SP. Masood, triggered row on September 21 as he told ANI that Akhileshs political activity was meaningless unless the alliance was finalised. Finalise the alliance if you have to have an alliance. If it the alliance is not to be done, we Congress are going ahead with our preparations. Akhilesh ji should finish this work alliance finalisation immediately. If you have to lead, the responsibility is on you. Dil bhi aapko bada karna padega You will have to have a large heart, Masood said. He said the SP should not think of moving ahead without the Congress. Because if you are going ahead without the Congress, defeating the BJP is not in your mind. Only the Congress can fight the BJP, he said. In June 2025, Masood had also stirred the alliance debate by saying the 62-17 formula would not work in the 2027 Assembly polls, referring to the seat-sharing arrangement between the two allies for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. articleTitle: India fined 20% of match fees, West Indies 10% as slow over rate in 3rd ODI draws ICC ire
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Indies' Shai Hope, left, and India's captain Shubman Gill after West Indies' won the third and final One Day International (ODI) cricket match of a series between India and West Indies, in Mullanpur, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. (PTI Photo)
description: The match went on for over nine hours and the length of the game was pointed out by notably by former India head coach Ravi Shastri from the commentary box and by former wicketkeeper-batter Dinesh Karthik on social media.
body_raw: India and West Indies were both fined by the International Cricket Council on Monday for maintaining a slow over-rates during the third ODI in New Chandigarh. The match went on for over nine hours and the length of the game was pointed out by notably by former India head coach Ravi Shastri from the commentary box and by former wicketkeeper-batter Dinesh Karthik on social media. While India have been fined 20 per cent of their match fee, the West Indies were docked 10 per cent of their earnings after being ruled four and two overs short of their required over-rates respectively, once time allowances were taken into consideration. Match referee Prakash Bhatt imposed the sanctions after the match on Saturday. Both captains pleaded guilty to the offences and accepted the proposed sanctions, meaning there was no need for formal hearings, the ICC said in a statement. The charges were levelled by on-field umpires Jayaraman Madanagopal and Sam Nogajski, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Virender Sharma. While India finished with a 2-1 win in the series, the West Indies recorded a famous win in the match itself, rewriting the record for their highest succesfull run chase in ODIs. Captain Shai Hope led the way with an unbeaten 162 as West Indies chased down 352. It was the first time since December 2019 that India had lost an ODI match at home against the West Indies. Earlier, India captain Shubman Gill fell after scoring just one run in his domestic home ground, after having scored centuries in the previous two matches. Virat Kohli was out for a golden duck after that, ending his streak of big scores as well. Rohit Sharma then scored a 92 and that was followed by KL Rahuls unbeaten 162 pushed India to a total of 351 The two sides will now turn their attention to the five-match T20I series, which begins on Tuesday in Lucknow.

articleTitle: Hanging from moving car, daredevil Gujarat cop recovers Rs 3.75 cr looted gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gujarat Police Ahmedabad
description: Robbers snatch gold from train passenger at Nadiad station; after dramatic chase and fake messages trap the robbers, Inspector S A Gadhvi finishes the job with Bollywood-style action
body_raw: A car full of alleged criminals rams into a police vehicle, bashing in a door. As they reverse in an attempt to get away, an officer emerges from his damaged vehicle and lunges at the criminals car. He gets a grip, but they keep going, dragging him along. A few hundred metres on, the officer opens a door, grabs the steering wheel and pulls the handbrake, bringing the car to a halt. This couldve been an action sequence from a film about a hero cop. Except it isnt. The chase was real, and at the end of it, Police Inspector S A Gadhvi of the Ahmedabad Rural Police emerged as a real-life hero. The incident took place outside Viramgam town on October 3. A Tata Tiago driven by an alleged gold robber, rammed into a car being driven by Inspector Gadhvi, jamming the door. Police personnel accompanying Gadhvi managed to prise open the door, but the accused had enough time to reverse their vehicle to attempt a getaway. As police swarmed the car, Gadhvi grabbed the door on the drivers side. The accused dragged the officer along with the moving vehicle for nearly 500 metres. Displaying extraordinary courage and determination, P I S A Gadhvi managed to open the door, gain control of the steering wheel, and pulled the handbrake, bringing an end to the chase, Om Prakash Jat, Superintendent of Ahmedabad Rural Police, said on Monday. The actions of Gadhvi and his team, taken in collaboration with Government Railway Police GRP, stopped four men who had snatched gold valued at Rs 3.75 crore a few hours earlier. The sequence of events had begun almost 110 km away-around 5 pm that evening. As the 12834 Howrah-Ahmedabad Superfast Express pulled into Nadiad station in Anand, Bharat Karsan Chaudhary alighted on the platform, clutching a green bag that contained 2.9 kg of gold jewellery worth Rs 3.75 crore. Suddenly, he felt the bag being snatched from his hand. He tried to pursue the snatcher, but the man was too fast for him. Chaudhary saw him jump into a car that seemed to have been waiting for him. As the car, a Tiago, sped away, Chaudhary managed to take a picture of its registration plate GJ-08-DJ-0311. He then went to the GRP. By 7.30 pm, the GRP had shared the information with the Gujarat Police State Control Room. From there it reached Ahmedabad Rural Police, who tracked the registration of the Tiago and its owner to Banaskantha district. Informants told police the vehicle was travelling through Rural Ahmedabad, and that it was being followed by another vehicle, a Suzuki Baleno without a registration number. Based on the intelligence inputs, we identified the possible movement routes, particularly towards Sachana and Viramgam. The Local Crime Branch LCB and Viramgam Town Police immediately activated naka points and deployed teams strategically on these roads, police said in a statement. Police officers Himanshu of the LCB and Siddhraj of Viramgam Town Police then displayed exceptional alertness and presence of mind and strategically blocked the road using trucks and other vehicles, police said. The Baleno was intercepted just before it entered Viramgam Town. Inside was one of the four accused. But the Tiago seemed to have got away. After the man in the Baleno was interrogated on the spot, it was revealed that the other accused, along with the stolen gold, had already crossed Viramgam Town in the Tiago, police said. Police then used the phone of the accused in the Baleno to send a text to the men in the Tiago, pretending that he was lost. They managed to persuade the men to share the live location of their car, and to meet the Baleno at a specific point. They then reached the spot and blocked the road. Soon, the Tiago arrived. Police flagged it down, but the driver rammed the car into a police vehicle, and Gadhvis heroics followed. Once Gadhvi had managed to stop the car, other police personnel rushed to assist him and successfully overpowered the three accused inside the vehicle, Ahmedabad Rural Police said in a statement. .One of the accused managed to escape from the scene into the adjoining fields, but a systematic search and cordon operation led to his apprehension as well, police said. The gold was found under the seat covers of the Tiago and both vehicles were seized. The four accused were handed over to the Nadiad GRP, who arrested them for robbery, police said.

articleTitle: Russian pneumonic plague scare: What it means for India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The woman reportedly worked at an anti-plague research institute and was said to have had a possible laboratory exposure.
description: Standard antibiotics (such as gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, or doxycycline) cure it very effectively, but timing is critical. Treatment must start within 24 hours of the first symptoms
body_raw: Reports from Russia about the death of a 28-year-old laboratory worker in Irkutsk have raised concerns about a possible case of pneumonic plague and prompted questions about whether the disease could pose a wider public health threat. The case has generated particular attention because the woman reportedly worked at an anti-plague research institute and was said to have had a possible laboratory exposure. Russias public health authorities have described the illness as pneumonia of unknown aetiology cause or origin and said testing did not identify micro-organisms associated with her professional activities. People considered potentially exposed have reportedly been placed under medical observation. Nevertheless, pneumonic plague is one of the most serious forms of plague because it affects the lungs and can spread between people through respiratory droplets. For India, the practical clinical message is therefore two-fold There is no reason for public alarm based on the Russian reports alone, but clinicians should recognise the disease quickly if a genuinely compatible case presents. Pneumonic plague is rare, but it is one of the infections in which early recognition and rapid public health action matter enormously, says Dr Jatin Ahuja, infectious disease specialist, Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, New Delhi, explains. What is pneumonic plague, and how does it differ from other forms? This is a severe lung infection caused by the bacteria Yersinia pestis. While bubonic plague attacks the lymph nodes causing swollen lumps called buboes and septicemic plague infects the bloodstream, pneumonic plague infects the lungs. It is the only form of plague that spreads directly from person to person through the air. How easily does it spread, and what poses the greatest risk? It does not linger in the air like measles or spread as easily as the flu. It spreads through heavy respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or spits blood. The greatest risk is being within 6 feet 2 meters of a coughing patient without a mask, caring for them directly, or performing medical procedures on their airway. What is the incubation period, and what are the warning symptoms? Symptoms appear quickly, usually within one to three days range one to seven days. It begins suddenly with high fever, chills, severe headache and extreme weakness, rapidly followed by shortness of breath, chest pain, and a cough that brings up watery, blood-tinged, or pinkish phlegm. How effective are modern antibiotics and how fast must they be started? Standard antibiotics such as gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, or doxycycline cure it very effectively, but timing is critical. Treatment must start within 24 hours of the first symptoms. Because lung damage progresses rapidly, delaying treatment beyond the first day dramatically raises the risk of death. What steps do health authorities take after a suspected case? Health officials immediately place the patient in isolated, negative-pressure rooms and wear protective gear N95 masks. They track down everyone who was in close contact, give them preventive antibiotic pills for 7 days, and monitor their temperature twice daily. Sputum and blood samples are rushed to reference labs for confirmation. Is there a risk for people in India right now? The risk is virtually zero. Because people only transmit it once they are visibly very sick, it is difficult for an infected person to travel undetected on long international journeys. For the risk to change, there would need to be widespread, uncontrolled outbreaks spreading through major international transport hubs. How would India detect and handle a symptomatic traveller from abroad? Indias Port Health Organisations screen incoming international travelers at airports. If an inbound passenger falls severely ill, the flight crew alerts air traffic control, and the plane is directed to an isolation bay. The passenger is transferred by a specialized biocontainment ambulance to designated infectious disease hospitals like AIIMS or Safdarjung, fellow passengers seated nearby are traced and given preventive antibiotics, and samples are tested at the National Centre for Disease Control NCDC. Are Indian hospitals prepared to identify it despite common symptoms? Initial symptoms look identical to standard viral flu or pneumonia, which is a diagnostic challenge. However, hospitals ask for recent international travel history for any rapidly deteriorating lung infection. Indian tertiary and government referral centers have standard stockpiles of effective antibiotics ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, gentamicin and established isolation protocols developed during the COVID-19 pandemic. What are the additional clinical points doctors should keep in mind? The most important clinical issue raised by the Russian episode is that pneumonic plague can initially look like much more common respiratory illnesses. Fever, cough, breathlessness and pneumonia are not, by themselves, specific for plague.The epidemiological history can, therefore, become critical. A rapidly deteriorating patient should be asked about recent international travel, residence in or travel to an area where plague occurs, contact with rodents or potentially infected animals, flea exposure, laboratory or occupational exposure, and close contact with a person suspected of having pneumonic plague. That history can change the differential diagnosis and determine whether urgent public-health notification and specialised testing are warranted. Why the Russia story should not be described as an outbreak The Russian reports have generated concern because of the laboratory workers occupation and the possibility of exposure. But unless Russian authorities confirm Yersinia pestis infection and evidence of transmission, describing the event as a pneumonic-plague outbreak would overstate what is currently known.The significance of pneumonic plague lies in its potential for rapid progression and person-to-person transmission - not in evidence that such transmission is currently occurring internationally. What would change the risk assessment for India? The risk assessment would change if there was credible evidence of confirmed pneumonic-plague cases accompanied by secondary transmission, particularly sustained community transmission or clusters across multiple locations.That is different from an isolated suspected case, including one involving a laboratory exposure. How fast does the bacteria mutate? Unlike rapidly evolving RNA viruses, Yersinia pestis does not typically undergo dramatic genetic change over days or weeks. In a suspected pneumonic-plague event, the immediate concern is, therefore, not rapid mutation but whether the bacterium is actually present, whether it is transmitting between people, and whether it remains susceptible to effective antibiotics.

articleTitle: How JEE Advanced AIR 1 toppers’ scores have shifted over 10 years: From Aman to Shubham
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iit delhi placement
description: JEE Advanced 2026 topper Shubham Kumar leads ten years of AIR 1 rankers, showcasing mark variations from 314 to 355 and popular choices like IIT Bombay Computer Science.
body_raw: Every year, over a million students compete for a place in the JEE Advanced merit list, but only a fraction qualify for admission to the IITs. In 2026, a total of 1,79,694 candidates appeared in both papers and 56,880 qualified. At the top was Shubham Kumar, who scored 330 out of 360. Kumar was followed by Kabeer Chhillar at AIR 2 with 329 marks, a one-mark difference between the two. Chhillar had also secured a 100 percentile in JEE Main and had been among the six candidates who scored a perfect percentile in the exam. The two were also hostel-mates in Kota and had prepared together for the IIT entrance exam. From Aman Bansal in 2016 to Shubham Kumar in 2026, these are the students who have topped JEE Advanced over the past 10 exam seasons. JEE Advanced 2016 topper Aman Bansal Aman Bansal from Jaipur topped JEE Advanced 2016 with 320 marks out of 372. He scored 113 in Physics, 105 in Chemistry and 102 in Mathematics. At the time, Bansal said he wanted to pursue Computer Science at IIT Bombay. The official JEE Advanced report lists him as AIR 1 and the IIT Bombay zone topper. JEE Advanced 2017 topper Sarvesh Mehtani Sarvesh Mehtani from Panchkula topped JEE Advanced 2017 with 339 out of 366 marks. He scored 104 in Physics, 115 in Chemistry and 120 in Mathematics. Mehtani subsequently studied Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bombay, where he was part of the 201721 BTech batch. JEE Advanced 2018 topper Pranav Goyal Pranav Goyal from Panchkula secured AIR 1 in JEE Advanced 2018 with 337 out of 360. His subject scores were 117 in Physics, 114 in Chemistry and 106 in Mathematics. Goyal chose Computer Science at IIT Bombay after topping the examination he had also scored 97.2 per cent in his Class 12 CBSE examination. JEE Advanced 2019 topper Kartikey Gupta Kartikey Gupta from Ballarpur, Maharashtra, topped JEE Advanced 2019 with 346 out of 372 marks. He scored 113 in Physics, 112 in Chemistry and 121 in Mathematics. Gupta had studied at Allens residential programme in Mumbai and said after the result that he wanted to pursue Computer Science at IIT Bombay. JEE Advanced 2020 topper Chirag Falor Chirag Falor topped JEE Advanced 2020 with 352 out of 396 marks, scoring 110 in Physics, 118 in Chemistry and 124 in Mathematics. Unlike most JEE toppers, Falor had already secured admission to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and appeared for JEE Advanced primarily for the experience. He subsequently chose MIT over the IITs. JEE Advanced 2021 topper Mridul Agarwal Mridul Agarwal of Jaipur topped JEE Advanced 2021 with 348 out of 360 marks. He scored 120 in Physics, 112 in Chemistry and 116 in Mathematics. Agarwal appeared from the IIT Delhi zone and had also been among the candidates who secured a 100 percentile in JEE Main that year. JEE Advanced 2022 topper R K Shishir R K Shishir of the IIT Bombay zone secured AIR 1 in JEE Advanced 2022 with 314 out of 360 marks. His scores were 96 in Physics, 109 in Chemistry and 109 in Mathematics. The result year saw a substantial gap from the previous editions topper score Shishirs 314 was 34 marks below Agarwals 348 in 2021. JEE Advanced 2023 topper Vavilala Chidvilas Reddy Vavilala Chidvilas Reddy topped JEE Advanced 2023 with 341 out of 360 marks, emerging as the AIR 1 from the IIT Hyderabad zone. He later enrolled at IIT Bombay the institutes academic records list him among its 2023 undergraduate students. JEE Advanced 2024 topper Ved Lahoti Ved Lahoti from the IIT Delhi zone produced the highest JEE Advanced score recorded up to that point, with 355 out of 360 marks. He scored 118 in Physics, 120 in Chemistry and 117 in Mathematics. Lahoti subsequently chose Computer Science at IIT Bombay, according to reports following the result. JEE Advanced 2025 topper Rajit Gupta Rajit Gupta topped JEE Advanced 2025 with 332 out of 360 marks, after also securing a 100 percentile in both sessions of JEE Main. He emerged as AIR 1 from the IIT Delhi zone and was reported to be aiming for Computer Science at IIT Bombay. His 332 was also tied with AIR 2 Saksham Jindal, with Gupta taking the top position on the tie-breaking criteria. JEE Advanced 2026 topper Shubham Kumar Shubham Kumar from Gaya, Bihar, became the 2026 AIR 1 with 330 out of 360 marks. He had already secured the 100th percentile in JEE Main, where he ranked sixth nationally. Kumar has said he hopes to join IIT Bombay for Computer Science. articleTitle: Insurer rejects accident claim over ‘alcohol intake history’, widow secures Rs 60 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: chandigarh police salary bank life insurance claim alcohol head constable widow consumer news
description: The consumer commission noted that the deceased was covered under a personal accidental death insurance policy and his death following the 2022 accident was also undisputed.
body_raw: The Chandigarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed an insurance company and a bank to pay Rs 60 lakh to the widow of a deceased head constable, after holding that a hospital record mentioning a history of alcohol consumption did not establish that he was under its influence when the accident occurred. Holding a private insurance company liable for wrongly rejecting an accidental death insurance claim of a deceased, a bench of president Pawanjit Singh and member Mohan Sharma also ordered Rs 20,000 to the widow as compensation for causing mental agony and harassment as well as costs of litigation. The insurer was unjustified in repudiating the claim of the complainant on the ground of the deceasedinsured being under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident, and the same certainly amounts to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on their part, and the present consumer complaint deserves to succeed, the September 22 order read. The commission noted that the hospitals summary report mentioned the deceaseds history of alcohol consumption but it did not say that he was under the influence of liquor at the relevant time. Needless to mention here that history of alcohol consumption and being under the influence of liquor are not akin to each other, the ruling held. Widow sought accidental death benefit The womans husband was working as a head constable with the Chandigarh Police and maintained his salary account with a leading private bank. Under a Memorandum of Understanding MoU dated October 30, 2021, Chandigarh Police personnel holding salary accounts with the bank were covered by a personal accidental death insurance policy. On July 2, 2022, he met with a road accident while travelling on his scooter and sustained serious injuries. He was initially admitted to SPS Hospital, Ludhiana, and was later referred to GMCH-32, Chandigarh, where he died from his injuries on July 18, 2022. His widow then sought the accidental death insurance benefit under the MoU. However, the insurance company rejected the claim in October 2022, stating that hospital records indicated that he was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident. The woman then approached the district consumer commission, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. Fell within policy exclusion Insurer The insurer opposed the complaint, raising objections regarding its maintainability, locus standi, concealment of facts and cause of action. It admitted that the head constable was insured but argued that the policy was subject to its terms and conditions. It maintained that he was not on duty when the accident occurred and that the claim was rejected because he was drunk, which fell within the policy exclusion. The bank argued that its role under the MoU was limited to facilitating and forwarding the relevant documents to the insurer. It stated that the insurer was responsible for deciding the claim and that the claim had already been repudiated by the insurance company. Couldnt prove intoxication The commission noted that the MoU between Chandigarh Police and the bank covered the deceased under a personal accidental death insurance policy. His death following the July 2, 2022 accident was also undisputed. Regarding the mention of history of alcohol consumption in the hospital summary, the order, relying on national consumer commission precedents, held that simply recording alcohol consumption, without scientific or medical evidence such as a blood-alcohol or breathalyser test, was insufficient to establish intoxication. The commission concluded that the insurer was unjustified in rejecting the claim which amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. Takeaway The ruling made it clear that insurers cannot reject accidental death claims solely on a hospital record mentioning alcohol consumption. It reinforces that intoxication at the time of an accident must be established through credible medical or scientific evidence before applying policy exclusions. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Chandigarh 0172-2700 183 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: ‘So much more at peace’: Aishwarya Lekshmi on life after quitting social media
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Aishwarya Lekshmi spoke about attaining peace after quitting social media
description: Actress Aishwarya Lekshmi has spoken about her decision to quit social media, saying she is 'in a better place in life' since stepping away.
body_raw: Actress Aishwarya Lekshmi has said she is so much more at peace since stepping away from social media, while acknowledging that the reasons that drove her off the platforms still exist. On the other hand, producer Soundarya Rajinikanth defended the platforms as a necessary professional tool that crosses a line when criticism turns personal. Aishwarya, who deactivated her social media accounts earlier this year, said the decision has given her a sense of calm she did not have before. Its falling in place. Im happy with my life as it is right now. So much more at peace than I was while I was on social media, she said in a conversation with Puja Talwar. She added, I do see that the things that were the reason I made the decision to get out of social media still prevail in certain quantities. But at least Im not there always watching it and getting affected by things like that. Im generally in a better place in life. Soundarya Rajinikanth, who sat along Aishwarya Lekshmi and Arjun Das during the promotional interaction for their Netlfix series Love, offered a producers perspective on the same issue. I think you cant deny the fact that social media does play a part. But where it crosses the line is when professional stops and personal attacks or comments start, Soundarya Rajinikanth said, adding, Even for us as producers, we do look into Instagram forecasting. We do want to know the comments. We do want to know how a trailer is received. Thats not something Im going to deny. Also Read Felt exposed to viciousness Why Aishwarya Lekshmi has no plans to return to social media She then drew a distinction between the experience of people behind the camera and those in front of it. Its different for our artistes because theyre in front of the camera. Its different for makers, storytellers because were behind the camera. Maybe we dont get targeted as insensitively as they do. It is difficult for them, so I understand why Aishwarya took the step that she did. Soundarya Rajinikanth said social media could work for the industry if the culture around it improved. If people have a little bit more sensitivity when they come on social media, itll make everything pleasant. We do need social media today. But I still feel it can be a lot cleaner than what it is, she said. Aishwarya Lekshmi was careful not to dismiss social media entirely. She acknowledged the power the platforms have given to independent creators and cited the example of Hashir, the Kerala-based Instagram influencer and content creator whose popularity on the platform led to him being cast as the lead in Vaazha 2, which went on to become one of the highest-grossing Malayalam films in history. The powers also with them content creators now. Earlier, you could say the industry didnt choose you. But now you also have a way to showcase your talent or build yourself up in a way that you cannot be ignored. In Kerala, one of the highest-grossing films recently was Vaazha 2, which was led by one of the most popular Instagram influencers, Hashir. Wonderful actor. People love him, Aishwarya said. But for Aishwarya Lekshmi, the professional benefits of being on social media were no longer worth the personal cost of what it was doing to her mental health. I do see that side. But personally, I was done.

articleTitle: Pneumonic plague: What to know about the disease after suspected case in Siberia
articleFeaturedImageAlt: plague
description: A lab worker in Siberia died after developing severe pneumonia, prompting medical observation of nearly 200 people. Here’s what to know about pneumonic plague, how it spreads, its symptoms and how it is treated.
body_raw: Around 200 people have been placed under medical observation in Irkutsk in eastern Siberia, Russia, after an employee of an anti-plague institute there died of suspected plague on October 2. According to local reports, Darya Shipilova had broken a test tube containing the plague pathogen. She fell ill with suspected pneumonic plague after returning from a work trip to Buryatia, where an outbreak had been reported near the border with Mongolia. A special set of measures was organized and carried out following a case involving an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, who was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown etiology, Russias consumer watchdog Rospotrebnadzor told the state agency Tass. The watchdog said expanded testing of samples from the patient found no microorganisms linked to her work at the lab. According to its website, the Anti-Plague Institute is a major research and public health facility responsible for monitoring and preventing outbreaks of high-risk bacterial and viral infections across Siberia and Russias Far East. First, what is the plague? Plague is an infectious disease caused by Yersinia pestis, a zoonotic bacteria that can spread between animals and people. Y. pestis is usually found in small animals and their fleas. According to the World Health Organisation WHO, humans can be infected in one of three ways - the bite of infected vector fleas, unprotected contact with infectious bodily fluids or contaminated materials like being bitten by an infected rat, and the inhalation of respiratory dropletssmall particles from a patient with pneumonic plague. Types of plague BUBONIC PLAGUE Bubonic plague is caused by the bite of a flea infected with Y. pestis. The disease travels through the lymphatic system to the nearest lymph node where it replicates itself. Of the three variants, bubonic plague has proven to be especially deadly in the past The Black Death, the 14th-century plague pandemic, killed more than 50 million people in Europe, according to the WHO - up to one-third of the continents population. Symptoms typically include sudden onset fever, chills, head and body aches and weakness, vomiting and nausea. The lymph node becomes inflamed and painful as a result, and is called a bubo. SEPTICAEMIC PLAGUE In this variant, the Y. pestis bacteria multiply rapidly in the bloodstream and can develop from any other form of plague. Primary septicaemic plague can also occur. Symptoms can range from bleeding under the skin to severe complications, including organ failure, tissue damage, respiratory distress and bleeding under the skin. If left untreated, it could turn fatal. PNEUMONIC PLAGUE Pneumonic plague, which Shipilova was suspected to have, is the most virulent form of plague with an incubation period as brief as 24 hours. Pneumonic plague is the most dangerous, and according to the WHO, invariably fatal if untreated. As the name suggests, it happens when the bacteria enter the lungs and causes rapidly developing pneumonia and other symptoms. According to the CDC, it is the only form of plague that can be spread from person to person by inhaling infectious droplets - also making it the most contagious. However, this disease also enjoys high recovery rates if detected and treated within 24 hours of onset of symptoms. What you should know With the advent of modern antibiotics, which can treat Y. pestis, and improved hygiene and understanding of the disease, plague is now relatively uncommon. However, it remains endemic in several countries. Today, plague is concentrated largely in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar. Between 2019 and 2025, WHO recorded 3,860 suspected cases worldwide, including 2,646 confirmed cases and 423 deaths among the countries reporting confirmed cases. Plague is treatable with antibiotics, and early treatment greatly improves the chances of survival. Untreated pneumonic and septicaemic plague are invariably fatal.

articleTitle: Telangana CEO orders action against Form 7 misuse to delete eligible voters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Telangana: BLOs are conducting door-to-door distribution of Enumeration Forms for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. (Express File Photo)
description: A Telangana poll official has warned of action against those misusing Form-7 to seek deletion of voters from electoral rolls.
body_raw: The Chief Electoral Officer of Telangana, C Sudarshan Reddy, has issued an order to the Commissioner of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, the District Education Officer, Hyderabad, and all collectors and DEOs of districts across the state, asking them to take appropriate action against individuals who submitted Form 7s to falsely delete eligible voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The CEOs memo, issued on Monday, reads, It has come to the notice of this office that there have been instances of filing bulk applications in Form 7 before the EROs electoral registration officers and it is also alleged that such forms are not genuine. The memo added that officials, including collectors, DEOs and EROs, should take action against the applicants, who have made knowingly false statement or declaration in writing in form 6, 6A, 7 and 8 as per the provisions of section 31 of the Representation of People Act 1950. The memo further states that such action shall be preceded by an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The CEOs instructions come against the backdrop of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committees TPCC electoral office filing a complaint with the Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad, seeking FIRs over alleged Form 7 misuse. The first alleged instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency. Pre-printed applications were allegedly filed by a booth-level agent BLA of the BJP, seeking the deletion of 31 electors, including a Congress BLA and his family members, the Congress claimed. In another case, a pre-printed Form 7 surfaced in Bahadurpura constituency. This, too, was flagged by the TPCC. The third instance brought to the notice of the commissioner was from Goshamahal assembly constituencys booth number 173. In the Goshamahal case, the BLO booth-level officer refused to accept the bulk pre-printed forms, a TPCC leader claimed. The Congress is in power in the state. Speaking to The Indian Express, a BLO who refused to take in pre-printed Form 7s said, I was only doing my duty. I brought it to the notice of the ERO. What is Section 31 Section 31 of Representation of People Act -1950 refers to making false declarations. It reads, If any person makes in connection with-a the preparation, revision or correction of an electoral roll, or b the inclusion or exclusion of any entry in or from an electoral roll,a statement or declaration in writing which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 pertains to inquiry into claims and objections. As per the rule, The registration officer shall hold a summary inquiry into every claim or objection in respect of which notice has been given under Rule 19 and shall record his decision thereon. The rule further states, At the hearing, the claimant or, as the case may be, the objector and the person objected to and any other person who, in the opinion of the registration officer, is likely to be of assistance to him, shall be entitled to appear and be heard. The registration officer may in his discretion-require any claimant, objector or person objected to, to appear in person before him b require that the evidence tendered by any person shall be given on oath and administer an oath for the purpose.

articleTitle: Problem with school History books isn’t just the facts. It’s what they aren’t teaching
articleFeaturedImageAlt: history
description: The real issue lies in shifting the emphasis increasingly to lionised accounts of certain periods in history and presenting the past as a set of acts by a variety of actors engaged in religious antagonism. The interrogative character of historical studies is less frequently seen in these textbooks
body_raw: In recent decades, the periodic revisions of Indian school History textbooks have become increasingly tenuous and worrying. From the invention of fictitious narratives to the erasure or inappropriate abridgement of important periods in history, revisions have assumed several questionable forms. The new textbooks tend to present pieces of information that are sometimes contrary to facts, besides contradicting their own statements in some instances. The larger purpose of these textbook revisions is to present a communally informed account of Indias past that conceives of history as a story of antagonistic groups forced to share a geopolitical territory. History is the discipline that tells us how we reached the present and what it meant to live in times when human lives were organised differently. Human lives were transformed by deep-seated processes involving the introduction and increased use of metals, tools and weapons, fire, agriculture, livestock farming, the wheel, alphabets and numbers, money, monumental architecture and more. Ideas, ranging from god, value, valour and hierarchy to justice, equality, democracy and peace, have shaped human lives in profound ways. A lesson in History involves a nuanced understanding of this journey. Do the new History textbooks in our schools live up to this mandate? No, they do not. NCERTs new Social Science textbook for Grade IX, Understanding Society India and Beyond - Part 2, is the latest in a series of contestable textbook revisions. Released last Tuesday, the book putatively aims to equip students with the skills that are needed to grow. and to enhance their analytical, descriptive, and narrative capabilities. As it turns out, there is much to be desired in the book on these counts. Consider the chapter, Indias Long Road to Independence, which is meant to be an account of a decisive phase in Indian history. The chapter turns out to be an assorted set of events presented chronologically. Little is said in it of historical processes that might encourage critical thinking. Colonialism and nationalism are not defined or discussed in conceptual terms, and processes such as the growth of literature, the development of capitalism and the course of constitutional reforms are nowhere seen. There isnt a word on Ripons local self-governance initiative or the Morley-Minto or the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. The chapter begins with a big question How did a land of diverse geographies, languages and religions come together to challenge and finally end nearly two centuries of British rule? This is precisely the kind of question that encourages critical thinking, but the chapter ends without touching upon any of the issues that the big question flags. Another chapter, Cultural Currents 13th to 17th Centuries, puts off a conscientious reader with its embarrassing big question How did Indian culture endure and continue to grow richer during this period despite invasions and an unstable political context? The chapter states that religious differences between the Islamic invaders and the local population were so striking that there wasnt really a meeting ground in sight for a time. The power of the Bhakti tradition, along with Sufism, allegedly helped India overcome this crisis. The chapter posits that monotheistic Islam and a religion with several schools of thought were marked by a stark difference. A few pages later, it argues that Islams idea of the oneness of god was already present in the Upanishads. One is left wondering what the stark difference was all about This chapter holds that Islamic invasions led to the imprisonment of women and their sale as slaves. As a natural consequence, women began to make their public appearances less frequent. The use of purdah, ghunghat and other forms of veiling are presented in the chapter as an attempt to protect women from the invaders. The 10th-century traveller Abu Zayds words are cited as evidence to the effect that Indian women wore no veil before the advent of Islam. It is, then, mighty uncertain what Rama was referring to in the Pratima, a play attributed to Bhasa, when he told Sita, apaniyataam avagunthanam, remove your veil. And what was Sudraka speaking of in the Mricchakatika when he said that Sarvilaka covered Vasantasena with a veil vasantasenaam avagunthya after she relinquished her life as a courtesan? These arent the only factual inaccuracies in the book. There are several more. But the challenge that such textbooks pose is not with deliberate misrepresentation of facts or contradictory information. A learned class teacher can address these inadequacies in the classroom effortlessly. The real issue lies in shifting the emphasis increasingly to lionised accounts of certain periods in history and presenting the past as a set of acts by a variety of actors engaged in religious antagonism. The interrogative character of historical studies is less frequently seen in these textbooks. Students are told of thousands of soldiers marching, but not how the soldiers were fed or from where they sourced their weapons. Students are told of high-quality steel produced in ancient India but not how the furnaces worked. Students are told of fire sacrifices by the Vedic people, but not told what it took to produce and maintain fire in an age when lighters and matchsticks did not exist. Students are given a checklist of great advances in astronomy but not told what an armillary sphere is and how it worked. Students are told that Bankim Chandra wrote the Anandamath but not told how the schools of the day equipped children to be literate enough to read Bankim. The schools that made Indians literate in the past 200 years have contributed in no small measure to the making of India as we have known it in our lifetime. This important lesson from the past should inform every line that a textbook committee decides to include in a book meant for our schoolchildren. The writer is associate professor of History at IIT Mandi, Himachal Pradesh

articleTitle: This actor became Trinamool MP in April. Now she is BJP Rajya Sabha pick
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Koel Mallick Rajya Sabha
description: Asked why she cut ties with the Trinamool, Koel Mallick avoided a direct response. “I have no anger towards them. Perhaps being a student of psychology has made me empathetic."
body_raw: On April 6 this year, popular Bengali actor Koel Mallick took the oath as a Rajya Sabha MP from the Trinamool Congress. In an Instagram post sharing photographs of her in Parliament, Mallick wrote that she is honoured to get the opportunity to serve the people of Bengal and called it the beginning of a new journey. The journey proved to be short. Less than a month later, the Trinamool Congress lost the Assembly polls in Bengal, and the BJP came to power. The poll setback triggered an implosion in the Trinamool Congress ranks, with leader after leader deserting the partys firebrand chief Mamata Banerjee. Amid the Trinamool meltdown, Mallick resigned as a Rajya Sabha MP on July 16. Shortly after, she met Union Minister Bhupender Yadav at his Delhi residence. And in less than three months, she is on the list of BJP candidates for the Rajya Sabha. Earlier, the BJP sent former Trinamool MPs Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, Sushmita Dev and Prakash Chik Baraik to the Rajya Sabha, shortly after they quit as Trinamool MPs. Who is Koel Mallick A popular actor in Bengali films, Mallick has received multiple awards, including the Bengal governments Mahanayak Samman in 2023. An alumna of Modern High School and Gokhale Memorial Girls College, she holds a degree in psychology. She is the daughter of veteran Bengali actor Ranjit Mallick and is married to film producer Nispal Singh. aaaoeaa aaaoeaaaa aaaaaa aaaaaaaaa, a aaaaaaa aaa aaaa aaaoeaa aaaoeaaaa aaaaaa aaaaaaaaa aaaaEaaa shashikisoch aaaaaaaa aaa aaa aaaoeaaa aaaaaaa aaa- aaaaa aaaaaaaY aaaaaaaaaE aaaaaa aaaaaaaY aaaoeaaa aaaaaaa aaaaa aaaaa-a - BJP West Bengal BJP4Bengal October 5, 2026 Koel Mallicks BJP entry Mallick joined the BJP on Monday, a day after the party announced that it has chosen her for a Rajya Sabha seat. She filed the nomination in the presence of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and the partys state president Samik Bhattacharya. Speaking to the media, Mallick said, I am honoured. I have been given a great responsibility. Serving people is a duty, and that is what I will do happily. I am overwhelmed to see the development work that has begun in Bengal over the past few months. This is what Bengal needs the most. she said. I have always heard my father at home saying, Why is this happening? Why is that not happening in the state? As an ordinary person, there are so many things we want and so many thoughts we keep to ourselves. This time, I will speak about those issues. It is easy to read a newspaper and say, Oh, this was not done, but the real thing is to come to the field and work on those issues, she said. Asked why she cut ties with the Trinamool, she avoided a direct response. I have no anger towards them. Perhaps being a student of psychology has made me empathetic. Those who derive satisfaction from putting others down may themselves be facing problems. I wish them mental well-being, she said. The ideologies of the two parties are different. Every party tries to do good in its own way. I am proud to have joined this party. They are working for the development of the people. I will also try to do the same, she said. A tale of 2 meetings On January 15, a month before Trinamool chose Koel Mallick for the Rajya Sabha seat, the partys national general secretary, Lok Sabha MP and Mamata Banerjees nephew Abhishek Banerjee met Ranjit Mallick at his Kolkata home and presented him with Unnayaner Panchali, a report card of 15 years of the Trinamool governments achievements. Both spoke highly of each other. Cut to September 4, Bengal Chief Minister Adhikari greeted Ranjit Mallick by touching his feet and holding his hand to lead him onto the stage during the centenary celebrations of legendary actor Uttam Kumar in Tollygunge. And a month later, his daughter is BJPs Rajya Sabha choice.

articleTitle: Woman goes under knife for ‘pointed’ nose, left with ‘crooked’ one, wins Rs 65,000 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cosmetic surgery nose job delhi woman hospital refund medical negligence consumer news
description: The doctor claimed that the complainant approached him with problem of bulbous nose and wanted refinement of her tip. It was stated that she specifically wanted cosmetic rhinoplasty for a well-defined and sharper nose.
body_raw: A Delhi District Consumer Commission has directed a doctor to pay Rs 65,000 to a woman who underwent cosmetic nose surgery, observing that while aesthetic dissatisfaction and medical negligence are distinct, the cosmetic outcome cannot be ignored, as the primary objective of cosmetic surgery is to make individuals appear beautiful. A bench of president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia said the procedures purpose is to improve appearance and found shortcomings in service. The primary objective of cosmetic surgery is to make individuals appear beautiful. Aesthetics is frequently the focal point of the procedure. However, dissatisfaction with the aesthetic outcome and proof of medical negligence are two distinct matters and cannot be treated as synonymous, the bench observed on September 25. At the same time, it held that the aesthetic outcome cannot be completely disregarded in a cosmetic-surgery case because the very purpose of such a procedure is to improve the patients appearance. The ruling noted that the complainant has filed photographs which indicate that the tip of the nose has been turned a little up and the nose appears to be a little crooked. It added that the complainant also underwent a revision surgery by another doctor. Woman challenged nose job outcome The matter concerned a woman who approached the consumer commission alleging deficiency in service against a doctor and the hospital over the outcome of a cosmetic rhinoplasty surgery. Rhinoplasty surgery, commonly called a nose job, is a plastic surgery procedure that changes the size, shape, or proportions of the nose. The complainant had approached the doctor with concerns relating to the shape of her nose. A CT scan showed deviation of the nasal septum towards the right, following which she was advised open rhinoplasty with functional tip plasty and septoplasty. Septoplasty is a surgical procedure to straighten a deviated nasal septum, the wall of bone and cartilage that divides your nostrils. She underwent the surgery in January 2023, after paying Rs 1.30 lakh. After the surgery, she alleged that the nose tip had been positioned upwards, that the nose remained crooked, and that she continued to face breathing problems. She also alleged that the nasal packs were not properly fixed and that she had to undergo a revision procedure. The complainant later underwent a revision rhinoplasty with septal reconstruction by another doctor, incurring an expense of Rs 4.60 lakh. She wanted sharper nose Doctor The doctor, on the other hand, maintained that the complainant had been informed about the risks, had given informed consent, and had been told that the shape of the nose could change during the healing process. It was stated that the complainant approached him with a problem of a bulbous nose tip and wanted refinement of her nose tip. It was stated that she specifically wanted cosmetic rhinoplasty for a well-defined and sharper nose. Nose appeared crooked Order The commission noted that the complainant had undergone rhinoplasty after paying Rs 1.30 lakh, and the medical records confirmed that she had a deviated nasal septum and was advised open rhinoplasty with functional tip plasty and septoplasty. It was found from the photographs that the tip of the complainants nose had turned slightly upwards and appeared somewhat crooked, forcing her to undergo a revision surgery by another doctor. Considering the shortcomings in the service, the commission directed the doctor to pay 50 per cent of the Rs 1.30 lakh paid for the surgery. Takeaway The judgment clarified that while aesthetic dissatisfaction alone does not establish medical negligence, cosmetic outcomes remain relevant. It recognises shortcomings in cosmetic surgery as deficient service and provides consumers a remedy where the intended aesthetic outcome is not achieved. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi helpline 011-23379146 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
