articleTitle: ‘No one is to blame’: Kalaranjini lost her voice after consuming fake blood containing acid
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kalaranjini lost her voice on a movie set after purportedly consuming fake blood that had mistakenly been prepared using acid instead of coconut oil.
description: Decades ago, Kalaranjini shockingly lost much of her voice on a movie set after purportedly consuming fake blood that had been mistakenly prepared using acid instead of coconut oil.
body_raw: Although Kalaranjini never had a career as illustrious as those of her younger sisters, Kalpana and Urvashi, she has repeatedly demonstrated impressive acting skills, shining brightest in comedic roles, with the most recent examples being director Krishnadas Muralis Bharathanatyam 2024 and its sequel Mohiniyattam 2026. Apart from Malayalam, she has also acted in Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada languages, as well as in television serials, leaving a lasting impression wherever she set foot. However, while she was slowly soaring high, an unexpected incident turned Kalaranjinis life upside down, affecting both her career and emotional well-being. Must Read My father married around 20 people Sreelakshmi Arackal reveals traumatic childhood Decades ago, Kalaranjini shockingly lost much of her voice on a movie set after purportedly consuming fake blood that had been mistakenly prepared using acid instead of coconut oil. Despite the incident significantly affecting her film career, she recently said she has no complaints against anyone, as she believes it was an honest mistake on the part of the makeup artist. The shocking on-set accident that changed everything At that time, he was terribly upset. Everyone avoided him on all sets. Then, in his final days, I was the one who helped him. Their children also still have a very good relationship with us. It was a small mistake. He must have been very sad that it happened that way. He wouldnt do such a thing to his profession on purpose. KV Bhaskar who prepared the fake blood was one of the biggest makeup artists in Malayalam cinema. He would have never done it on purpose it was a slip of the hand. He wouldnt have thought that it would make my life like this either, she shared during a conversation with Can Channel Media. Also Read He asked if I had AIDS Gayathri Suresh on her past toxic situationship Kalaranjini continued, Therefore, I dont have any major sorrows. I have been acting since that day, thanks to my co-workers and fellow artistes. Whenever I say my lines, people go completely silent because those acting with me need to react to what I am saying. This her acting career has moved forward because of everyones cooperation. Ambili used to dub everything for me. She is no longer with us. Later, Rosshan Andrrews director asked me to use my own voice. Even then, I didnt have the confidence. When I saw it, I felt it was not necessary. Then I did it in Chirakodinja Kinavukal. In Bharathanatyam, director Krishnadas insisted that I dub for myself. Thats how he helped bring my voice back, she added. Dont Miss Sanjay Dutt says he cant feel peace in India anymore, comments on PM Modi as Munna Bhai What happened on the fateful day According to Mathrubhumi, the aforementioned tragic incident happened while Kalaranjini was working with Malayalam superstar Prem Nazir. In one scene, she was supposed to die by vomiting blood. Back then, fake blood was made by mixing coconut oil with red colour. Since Kalaranjini was wearing a white saree, it was certain the dress would be stained if the red liquid splattered on her body. Hence, right before the shoot, Prem Nazir told her, I will feed it to you when the moment arrives. Kalaranjini agreed. However, she only remembers him pouring the red liquid into her mouth. Suddenly, Kalaranjini felt like her mouth and throat were burning and swelling up. But she couldnt do anything her windpipe contracted. Even after extensive treatment, there was no result. She mostly lost her voice and never fully regained it. She was in the hospital for about three months. ICYMI Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Kalaranjini only learned what had actually happened to her later. The makeup artist had prepared the liquid by adding acid instead of coconut oil. Disclaimer This article is a personal narrative detailing a set injury and its long-term impact. It is provided for informational and editorial purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or professional safety guidance.

articleTitle: Accenture forecast lifts most IT stocks but near-term outlook remains hazy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A handful of banks and IT majors have a big weightage on both indices.
description: TCS, Wipro gained up to 2%, while Persistent, Mphasis rose 3%. Meanwhile, Infosys and HCL Tech logged a 1-3% fall
body_raw: A handful of Indian IT stocks were among the best performers in the stock market on Monday after global technology major Accentures better-than-expected revenue forecast for the year lifted sentiment across Indian bourses. Big names such as Tata Consultancy Services Ltd TCS and Wipro Ltd gained up to 2. Smaller names like Persistent Systems Ltd and Mphasis Ltd also added up to 3. However, not all IT stocks rose, as Infosys Ltd and HCL Technologies Ltd fell 1-3. In fact, the latter two were briefly in the green early in the session before swiftly falling into the red. Others that ended higher also lost some steam by the end due to profit booking. This led to Nifty IT, which had gained nearly 1.6 earlier in the session, eventually ending flat compared to its previous close. Overall, the benchmark Sensex gained 472.77 points or 0.7 to end at 72,382.47. Nifty 50 also added 0.6 to close at 22,555.75. Many sectors, including banking, financial services and fast-moving consumer goods, also saw strong buying, helping lift the benchmarks. A handful of banks and IT majors have a big weightage on both indices. This follows a lean patch for the markets as the two key indices extended their losing run for the eighth straight week - the longest such losing streak in 25 years. Markets staged a recovery, supported by softer-than-expected US jobs data and a moderation in crude oil prices, providing some relief to investors assessing the near-term interest rate outlook, said Vinod Nair, Head of Investments at Geojit Investments. Accenture results lift most IT stocks Irish major Accentures earnings for the June-August quarter beat analysts estimates on Thursday. However, the bigger talking point was the higher-than-expected guidance provided by the company for FY27. As the markets remained shut on Friday on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, this exuberance was seen on Monday. Accentures 4QFY26 revenue of 18.68 bn 7 y-o-y in constant currency or cc terms exceeded its top end of guidance band of 18.4 bn. It guided for 3-6 growth in cc with inorganic contribution at 2-2.5 terms for FY27E, which was higher than the Street expectations of 2-5, and expects no effect from currency movements in FY27E, noted Nomura. This guidance was despite the companys management acknowledging headwinds from the West Asia war, impact of AI-led deflation, and a dynamic discretionary spending environment among clients. The management also noted an increase in smaller deals and improving conversion of deal wins into revenue, which is good news for Indian IT players. Big names such as Accenture and Cognizant act as bellwethers for the countrys IT sector, providing a glimpse at how the sector may perform or grow in the near-term. Indian IT stocks, which earn much of their revenue from US and European clients, tend to benefit from positive commentary by these global technology giants. Improvement seen in Q2, but outlook bleak The picture remains bleak for IT companies despite this brief pullback. IT companies, which have delivered flat to low single-digit revenue growth in recent quarters, are expected to witness only a moderate improvement in the July-September quarter as the West Asia conflict continues to weigh on client spending and decision-making, according to Pritesh Thakkar of PL Capital. AI traction remains healthy, but smaller-sized and shorter-tenure AI projects are yet to offset leakage in traditional services, limiting the pace of revenue growth. We expect median Tier I revenue growth of 0.9 Q-o-Q in CC terms, with growth partly aided by acquisitions, while Tier II companies are expected to outperform with 2.7 Q-o-Q growth, supported by deal ramp-ups and stronger conversion of recent wins, Thakkar said in his report. AI-related deflation in revenues of IT services companies has been a major concern for the industry since early this year, as AI-driven productivity gains made by clients are expected to take away a chunk of revenue for the IT companies that deliver projects for them. The concern is so deep that Nifty IT remains down over 25 for the year.

articleTitle: Calcutta High Court clears 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition on disputed land
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Calcutta High Court, Durga Puja 2026, Kolkata Durga Puja dispute, Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, Kolkata news, Haridevpur Police Station, Kolkata land dispute Durga Puja, Justice Saugata Bhattacharya, Calcutta HC Durga Puja order, Kolkata eviction suit land dispute
description: The Calcutta High Court has allowed a registered society to hold its 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition at a disputed Kolkata property, without deciding ownership rights.
body_raw: A 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition at a disputed Kolkata property recently got clearance from the Calcutta High Court, which directed the police to allow the Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, a registered society, to hold this years celebration despite the ongoing eviction issue. The court, however, said in the October 1 order that it would not decide the ownership rights, leaving that issue to the civil court. Justice Saugata Bhattacharya said that the earlier high court order stopping a Durga Puja in a residential building, relied upon by the respondent, was not applicable as they lacked permission from the flat owners. The judge also noted that the respondent Trust had not demonstrated any right, title ot interest over the disputed land. There might be rivalry between petitioner registered society and respondent no.5 Trust in convening Durga Puja, but there is no denial of the fact that petitioner has been convening Durga Puja for the last fifty-six years at the said premises, the order said. It added that the court was not an appropriate forum to decide the right, title and interest of a party over the land in question, and without making any observation in this regard, it directed the police to grant permission for holding Durga Puja this year. Durga Puja vs disputed land Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, a registered society, and its secretary approached the Calcutta High Court seeking permission to hold Durga Puja in 2026 on the land where it has been organising the puja for more than 50 years. The land was involved in a pending eviction suit filed by a trust against the society. Senior Advocate Indranil Roy, appearing for the society, submitted that the power of attorney holder of the co-owners had permitted, on September 10, to hold the puja. She submitted that other necessary permissions have been accorded on the designated portal by Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation, Fire and Emergency Services and Pollution Control Board, but the police authority had not granted permission. The counsel sought directions to the police authority to accord permission to enable the Parishad to convene Durga Puja on the land in 2026. Senior Advocate Kaushik Gupta, on behalf of the Trust, submitted that it had the right over the land in question and that, devoid of their permission, Parishad was not authorised to convene Durga Puja on the said land. Noting that the Parishad had been convening the Durga Puja for 56 years, the court directed the deputy commissioner of police, South West Division, Kolkata and the officer-in-charge, Haridevpur Police Station, to grant permission to the society for holding Durga Puja for the present year by October 5.

articleTitle: Hardeep Puri among two Union Ministers dropped from BJP’s UP list for Rajya Sabha polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma (left).
description: Union MoS B L Verma also dropped as BJP balances caste and regional equations in its list of eight candidates for October 16 UP Rajya Sabha polls
body_raw: The BJP on Monday announced eight candidates for the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, leaving out Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, whose terms in the Upper House are set to end next month. Puri is currently the Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas. Verma is the Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and Social Justice and Empowerment. With their Rajya Sabha terms ending on November 25 and the BJP not renominating them, they can continue as the Union ministers for up to six months without being a member of either House of Parliament, as per the constitutional provisions. The omission of the two ministers names was seen as an indication that there could be a reshuffle of the Union ministry in the coming months. BJP calculations The BJPs list of Rajya Sabha candidates from UP comprises three OBC faces, two Brahmins, two Dalits and one Thakur nominee. The list increases the share of OBCs and Dalits because the eight seats falling vacant had two OBCs, two Thakurs, two Brahmins along with one Dalit and one Sikh. Among the OBC candidates this time is Dharampal Singh, the BJP MLA from Bareillys Aonla and a minister in the Yogi Adityanath-led government, where he holds the Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development portfolio. Singh is a Lodh, with his nomination seen as a replacement for Verma who also belongs to the community. The Lodh group is influential in the Bundelkhand and Rohilkhand regions of UP, which has traditionally backed the BJP. Its support for the party is also linked to former UP CM late Kalyan Singh, a Lodh leader who was one of the BJPs tallest OBC leaders. The other two OBC nominees in the BJPs list are Prakash Pal, state president of the partys OBC Morcha who hails from Kanpur district, and Shruti Gangwar of Bareilly. Shruti, an IIT graduate, is the daughter of Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwar. She has been politically active in the Bareilly-Baheri region. The two Brahmin nominees are Radha Kant Ojha, a lawyer from Prayagraj and younger brother of former minister Shivakant Ojha, and Gopi Krishna Pandey of Kanpur, who has worked in the partys farmer and youth wings. The BJPs Dalit candidates are former Barabanki MP Priyanka Singh Rawat, a state party vice-president, and Vidya Sagar Sonkar from Jaunpur, former MLC and state party general secretary. The eighth nominee Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan, former MLA from Agra, is a state BJP general secretary in charge of the western region. He has been involved in several key party campaigns. Upper House contest UPs 10 Rajya Sabha seats falling vacant have had eight BJP members-Hardeep Singh Puri, Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brij Lal, B L Verma, Dinesh Sharma and Seema Dwivedi. Dinesh Sharma vacated his seat last month following his appointment as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Lieutenant Governor. The BJP has not re-nominated any of the remaining seven MPs. The principal Opposition Samajwadi Party SP has renominated veteran leader Ram Gopal Yadav, uncle of party president Akhilesh Yadav, whose current term is also ending next month. The party has fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani as its second Rajya Sabha candidate. The SP has enough strength in the UP Assembly to get its two candidates elected for the Upper House. Nathwani, 40, is the son of Parimal Nathwani, Director, Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent in the June 2026 election, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. Another Rajya Sabha seat from UP is falling vacant due to retirement of Ramji Gautam, currently the lone BSP representative in Parliament. The BJP and the SP have the numbers to smoothly win seven and two seats respectively. However, a contest is likely to take place for the remaining one seat, with the SP planning to field a third candidate. The contest would take place in the run-up to the high-stakes UP Assembly elections slated for February 2027. Currently, there are 396 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly. Each Rajya Sabha candidate, therefore, will require 37 first-preference votes to win. The SP has 101 MLAs. However, its effective strength is 100 as Chail MLA Puja Pal, who continues to figure in the House records as an SP member, has switched to the BJP and is currently its state vice-president. With the support of two Congress MLAs, the SP has 102 votes, nine short of the first-preference votes required to ensure the victory of its third candidate. The BJP has 255 MLAs with its NDA allies adding another 33 members Apna Dal S 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. With the support of Puja Pal unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDAs effective tally could reach 294, two short of the required 296 37 for each first-preference votes to ensure a win for its eight candidates. The BJP is placing its bets on MLAs Rakesh Pandey, Vinod Chaturvedi and Ashutosh Maurya, who had also cross-voted in 2024 but still continue to be listed as SP members in the Assembly records as Akhilesh had not expelled them citing their good conduct. Chaturvedi told The Indian Express that he would vote in favour of a BJP candidate in the Rajya Sabha polls.

articleTitle: Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt over ‘no peace in India’ remark: ‘He loves his country’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt (1)
description: Sanjay Dutt's comments soon went viral, with several social media users criticising the actor. Amid the backlash, the actor issued a clarification on his social media handles.
body_raw: Shekhar Suman has come out in support of Sanjay Dutt after the actor recently found himself embroiled in a controversy over his comments on the talk show Shekhar Tonite. Sanjay Dutts remarks on Shekhar Sumans YouTube show sparked criticism after he said that he could no longer feel peace in India. The backlash eventually prompted the actor to issue a clarification over his comments. Now, the shows host Shekhar Suman has reacted to the controversy, defending Sanjay Dutt and insisting that his comments were taken out of context. Speaking to NDTV, the actor said, Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he said was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never said or meant. I know him for years he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it. Sanjay Dutt appeared on the Gandhi Jayanti special episode of Shekhar Tonite on Friday, where he combined humour with references to Mahatma Gandhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump. During the conversation, Sanjay said, The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I cant feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shivji that those days come back soon. ALSO READ Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids No Benami property Towards the end of the episode, Sanjay Dutt was asked to imagine himself as the Prime Minister for five minutes and address the people of the country. The actor immediately slipped into the language and mannerisms associated with his iconic Munna Bhai character. Speaking in Hindi, he said, My dear countrymen, today I am very happy to have become your PM. There is a strange kind of energy running through my body. This is such a huge country, there are so many people, and now the responsibility of all of them is on me. He added, But you people dont have to worry at all. I am not going abroad to celebrate this happiness. I will stay right here, among all of you. Otherwise, how will there be a connection between the PM and the people? The comments soon went viral, with several social media users criticising the actor. Amid the backlash, Sanjay Dutt issued a clarification on his social media handles. I want to clarify that it has never been my intention to hurt the feelings of any individual, community, or institution, to insult them, or to disrespect them, he said. He further explained, My comments were made in the context of a scripted conversation, the purpose of which was to engage in lighthearted and humorous dialogue. The sentiment behind it was akin to the style of humor and satire depicted in films like Munnabhai, particularly inspired by the concept of Gandhigiri, which aimed to convey a message of love, unity, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted differently, detached from that original context. Sanjay Dutt was last seen in the film Aakhri Sawaal.

articleTitle: Suryakumar Yadav asked to confirm availability for Ranji Trophy, and then snubbed; Yashasvi Jaiswal picked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: FILE: Suryakumar Yadav in action. (CREIMAS for BCCI)
description: While Jaiswal found a place in the squad, Suryakumar was overlooked for the match scheduled from October 11 to 15.
body_raw: The Mumbai selectors have not picked former India T20 captain Suryakumar Yadav for their Ranji Trophy season opener despite the veteran confirming his availability for the same a week ago. The selection committee of the Mumbai Cricket Association MCA announced a 16-member squad on Monday. Both Suryakumar, under whose captaincy India had successfully defended their T20 World Cup crown earlier this year, and Yashasvi Jaiswal had informed the panel that they were available. But only the latter finds his name in the list. Chief selector Rajesh Pawar said Suryakumars lack of recent red-ball match practice was behind their decision. He is a very big player. But he hasnt played red-ball cricket in the last one and a half years. Should he play a few red-ball games, he can definitely come into the side, Pawar said. It was just last week that Suryakumar was asked about his availability and willingness to play Ranji Trophy, and he took a day before confirming it. However, MCA officials claim they tried to reach out to him many times but he didnt respond to their calls. Mumbai will take on Chandigarh in their season opener at the Wankhede Stadium from October 11-14. The selection committee has appointed Siddhesh Lad as skipper for the season with opener Ayush Mhatre as his vice-captain. Speaking on Jaiswals return, Pawar said, Its a good thing that Yashasvi is coming to play for Mumbai. He also needs match practice. When asked, he said he is available, so thats good for the team. There is a chance he might be in either the senior or the A team touring New Zealand so we only announced the squad for the first match. The squad features India batter Sarfaraz Khan, who recently played for the Rest of India side that beat Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup. Also included is Shams Mulani, whose all-round performance against Australia A helped India A clinch their two-match unofficial Test series 1-0. Mhatre, who led India to the Under-19 World Cup title earlier this year, has been rewarded for his impressive leadership with the vice-captaincy. Mumbai will miss the services of pacer Shardul Thakur, who got injured a few weeks ago. articleTitle: Medicine Nobel goes to scientists who can ‘control brain using light’: What their work is
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Medicine Nobel
description: Nobel Prize 2026 in physiology or medicine winners: What are light-gated ion channels and optogenetics? What exactly have the Medicine Nobel winners done, and what is the real-world impact of their work? We explain.
body_raw: Nobel Prize 2026 Medicine Scientists who developed a way to use light to control specific nerve cells in the brain, allowing researchers to study - and influence - how they shape memories, feelings and behaviour, have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. The prize was awarded to Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel and Karl Deisseroth for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, the Nobel Prize committee said. What exactly have the scientists done, and what is the real-world impact of their work? We explain. First, what are light-gated ion channels and optogenetics? Light-gated ion channels are proteins that act like tiny doors in a cells membrane, but with one special feature light controls whether the door is open or closed. When a particular wavelength of light hits the protein, it changes shape and opens. Charged particles called ions can then flow through the channel. For example, when light hits the human eye, it sets of a reaction that leads to ions moving through the channel as an electric current, travelling through optic nerves to eventually reach the brain. Optogenetics is a technique that lets scientists control specific cells using light. According to the Nobel Prizes official press release, optogenetics has transformed neuroscience from observing and reading brain activity to actively writing into it, establishing a causal link between distributed, genetically specified circuit motifs and behavior, emotion, and cognition. Among the actions the Nobel winners managed to perform using light was a mouse moving its whiskers, and creating the memory of feeling fear in mice who were perfectly safe. Scientists have always been fascinated with the brain The brain is a remarkable organ, and scientists have long wondered how it can control physical functions, govern feelings and memory, and create art. In the 20th century, researchers identified which brain regions govern which bodily functions. However, they could not show that a specific type of nerve cell directly caused a particular feeling or behaviour, so the resulting picture was like a blurry photograph. Francis Crick Nobel 1962 imagined a solution. Nerve signals are extremely fast, so he reasoned that light would be the ideal way to control them. If nerve cells could be made to react to light, neural activity could be controlled. Crick admitted the idea was far-fetched, but perhaps not impossible. An alga that swims towards light In the early 1990s, Peter Hegemann, at the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry in Martinsried, was intrigued by the unicellular alga Chlamydomonas, which could sense light through an eyespot, a tiny orange dot on its cells surface. If the alga was kept on one end of a bowl, and light shone on the other end, it would swim to that side within milliseconds. Hegemann wondered how the eyespot was so much faster than the human eye. His theory was that unlike the human eye, where photoreceptors first register light and then many proteins have to be moved before an electric signal can pass through the ion gate, in Chlamydomonas, the same protein was doing the reception and the passing on. Others were sceptical, since no known ion channel reacted to light on its own. Isolating the protein proved difficult because it became unstable outside the eyespot. Around the turn of the millennium, however, Japanese researchers mapped the algas DNA. Hegemanns group found two genes resembling known light-capturing proteins. Two scientists and a discovery Hegemann contacted Georg Nagel at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt. Nagel injected each gene separately into frog egg cells, which then produced the proteins and placed them in their outer membranes. He found that Hegemanns hypothesis was correct both proteins were ion channels that opened in response to light. They were named channelrhodopsin-1 and channelrhodopsin-2, and the second paved the way to optogenetics. It opened within 0.2 milliseconds of a light pulse, letting positively charged ions flow and producing an electrical signal. The two then introduced the gene for channelrhodopsin-2 into human embryonic kidney cells and hamster kidney cells. The cells became light-sensitive and produced electrical signals when illuminated. In 2003, Hegemann and Nagel published their results and proposed the protein as a tool for generating electrical impulses in cells using light. From psychiatric clinic to nerve cells Karl Deisseroth, while studying medicine in the 1990s, trained at a psychiatric clinic. Here, the functions of the brain, and the sufferings of those whose brain worked differently, held his attention. His group then searched for a protein that could trigger impulses in nerve cells. After hearing of channelrhodopsin-2, he asked Nagel for the DNA. Introduced into rat nerve cells in petri dishes, it was produced without apparent problems. Blue light provoked a nerve signal that could pass to other nerve cells. The group published this in 2005. Control in a living brain The method was named optogenetics in 2006, and researchers soon found more light-activated proteins that turn nerve cells on and off. In 2007, Deisseroths group introduced the channelrhodopsin-2 gene into a specific nerve cell type in the mouse motor cortex. A thin optic fibre fed through a small hole in the skull let them control the movement of the mices whiskers. The same year, light shone on a recently discovered cell type suspected of controlling wakefulness woke sleeping mice, confirming the hypothesis. In 2012, with Susumu Tonegawa, Deisseroth activated an engram, the pattern of neural pathways formed when a memory is created. Reactivating the cells that formed a fear memory made mice show fear when not in danger. It was the first demonstration of exactly which nerve cells are necessary for a specific memory. What it has revealed An adult human brain has around 90 billion nerve cells, each with thousands of connections, and cells with entirely different functions can be intermingled. Optogenetics lets researchers separate them. They have identified circuits governing pain, social behaviour, thirst, food consumption, reward, attention, circadian rhythm and fever. The method also works beyond the brain. Deisseroth showed that forcing the heart to work harder can reinforce anxiety, and other researchers found gut cells that explain why some prefer sugar to sweeteners. Towards treatments Optogenetics has deepened understanding of depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, Alzheimers and Parkinsons disease. In ongoing clinical trials for retinitis pigmentosa, a channelrhodopsin-like protein placed in a blind persons retina restored some vision. With light-emitting glasses, the person could discern and grasp objects on a table. Researchers also hope optogenetics could make cochlear implants more precise. As the Nobel Prize websites official press release says, Across cognition, emotion, and movement, these discoveries and applications illustrate a profound shift. Behaviors previously understood as unified phenomena can now be experimentally deconstructed into discrete computational streams. By enabling temporally precise, pathway-specific interventions in intact brains, optogenetics has transformed neuroscience by revealing the causal logic of brain function. But does this not sound potentially dangerous? While most scientific advancements have the risk of potential misuse, optogenetics doesnt exactly mean shining a light and controlling someones brain. Rohit Singh, Assistant Professor in the Departments of Biostatistics Bioinformatics and Cell Biology at Duke University, USA, told The Indian Express, There are three major technical safeguards. First and most important, optogenetics typically relies on genetically modifying neurons to produce light-sensitive microbial proteins that human cells do not naturally produce. Doing so would require a genetic intervention. Second, when it comes to visible light, the scalp and skull block much of the incoming light, while the light that penetrates is scattered, making precise targeting difficult. Third, changing the activity of specific neurons does not by itself give us the ability to control a persons thoughts or actions. Who are the Medicine Nobel Laureates? KARL DEISSEROTH Born in 1971. He is theProfessor of Bioengineering and of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University, USA. PETER HEGEMANN Born 1954. Professor of Neuroscience, Humboldt University of Berlin, Germany. GEORG NAGEL Born 1953. Professor of Molecular Plant Physiology, University of Wurzburg, Germany.

articleTitle: Flydubai attack: How Israel’s security lapses almost led to another ‘October 7’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai
description: A series of revelations show how there was sufficient opportunity for authorities in three countries to prevent Flight FZ1073 co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami from even getting anywhere near the cockpit, let alone almost causing a crash.
body_raw: As the dust has begun to settle around last weeks flydubai flight incident, the initial euphoria regarding a potential terrorist attack being averted has given way to the realisation that there were security failures on multiple fronts in three countries Israel, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates UAE. A series of revelations showed how there was sufficient opportunity for authorities to prevent the Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight FZ1073 co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami from even getting anywhere near the cockpit, let alone attacking his captain - the Indian pilot Smit Machchhar - mid-flight using an emergency axe that almost caused a crash. We explain what these revelations are and how they indicate serious lapses on part of Israels security system. How Oman Air stopped Hamam al-Hammami from flying. Hammami, 29, was born to an Omani father and Syrian mother. Although a Dubai resident, he frequently travelled to Syria during the countrys prolonged civil war, where Islamist rebels fought against the Bashar al-Assad regime. Investigators in the flydubai incident said they were looking at the possibility of radicalisation during his time in Syria. He then went on to study in Australia. He joined Oman Air in 2018 and became a pilot by 2022, although authorities raised concerns in 2024 about his radical views after he was found browsing extremist websites. He was disallowed from flying and made to undergo a deradicalisation programme, following which he was assigned an administrative job. After leaving Oman Air in 2025, Hammami tried to join the Moroccan national carrier Royal Air Maroc but wasnt hired. He eventually joined the budget carrier flydubai, owned by Dubais flagship airline Emirates, in February 2026. .but the UAE didnt Flydubai has been in the midst of an aggressive hiring spree to fuel its growth. Global demand for pilots is high and to meet its requirements, the airline set up a programme in 2025 to train pilots. It also operates its own flight training centre. As things stand, international aviation licensing works on a country-by-country basis. Citing sources, The Wall Street Journal reported that Oman mishandled the situation had Oman withdrawn Hammamis pilot licence over its concerns, the matter wouldve been flagged to the UAE and other Gulf countries. At the time of hiring, flydubai didnt contact Oman to verify his experience, although a criminal-background check was done, sources within the airline said. Hammami was then assigned to fly on the sensitive route to Tel Aviv, where he flew multiple times. The airline said it wouldnt comment on the investigation while it was ongoing. How Israels security system failed to avert flydubai incident According to a 2023 law passed in Israel, foreign airlines have to submit lists of passengers and crew to the Israeli government ahead of time. A database of these lists are maintained by the countrys Tax Authority, primarily as a measure of preventing terrorism. Although the Shin Bet - Israels internal security service - oversees the domestic carriers, it is the Ministry of Transportation that oversees pilots and crew on flights of foreign airlines to ensure they come from countries Israel considers friendly. As per the law, the Tax Authoritys database can be accessed by authorised bodies such as the Transportation Ministry as well as Israeli security agencies like Shin Bet and Mossad in order to vet people on flights. The ministry, however, said it didnt know that the database was operational - or that it could access it. Since the database was set up in 2023, the ministry has never asked for a passenger or crew list for vetting purposes, sources told WSJ. The ministry also said that while it was indeed responsible for the security of inbound flights, it lacked the intelligence capabilities to stop onboard threats. Foreign carriers were required to make those checks and in this case, it had asked flydubai - the ministry said that the airline agreed in writing to check its pilots backgrounds and nationalities. The final opportunity to stop Hammami from getting onboard FZ1073 was in Israel itself. Notably, Oman doesnt have diplomatic relations with Israel, and pilots from such countries are barred from flying to the country. So, the co-pilot couldve been stopped from boarding the flight merely on the basis of his nationality, but was instead allowed to fly multiple times to Tel Aviv instead. Meanwhile, a classified May 2024 report by Israels comptroller general had flagged the countrys Transportation Ministry for failing to adequately secure foreign carriers flights, WSJ reported. It found that officials in the ministry were failing in their oversight in part due to manpower and budget issues. Although Israeli airlines flying between Dubai and Tel Aviv were subjected to scrutiny and even stopped from flying considering the risks posed by the ongoing war in West Asia, flydubai continued to ply on the same route. October 7 anniversary, elections round the corner What is significant is that the attack happened barely a week ahead of the three-year anniversary of the armed attacks on October 7, 2023, which were carried out by the militant group Hamas and other Palestinian groups. This also comes about a month ahead of Israels parliamentary election, scheduled for October 27. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus office has instructed the head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel, a statement from the prime ministers office said. Opposition leader Yair Lapid dismissed Netanyahus announcement, pointing that the chain of failures leading up to the incident couldve led to a disaster of historic proportions. In a reference to the October 7 attacks, he added Just as Netanyahu escaped an investigation into the Oct. 7 massacre, he is now running away again. Even as calls for a serious investigation into the security lapses have been growing in Israel, Transport Minister Miri Regev rejected responsibility for the failure and said that security oversight for flights operated by foreign carriers fell under the remit of security agencies such as Mossad and Shin Bet. Keren Terner, a former director-general of the transport ministry who is now an opposition candidate in the upcoming Israeli parliamentary elections, blamed Regev for the security failure, noting that the Civil Aviation Authority was under the direct subordination of her ministry. Gadi Eisenkot, a leading challenger to Netanyahu in the upcoming election, wrote on X that in a proper and functioning government, the minister of transportation would have submitted a letter of resignation.

articleTitle: Ireland Head coach on spitting incident during game against Israel: ‘…not going to comment’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ireland
description: Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened
body_raw: Israel faced Ireland in the UEFA Nations League, and tempers ran high between the two sides yet again. This is the second time both teams have faced each other in a fortnight. The Irish media reported that one of the Israeli players spat on the Ireland coach, Damien Doyle, during the half-time whistle. Asked about the spitting incident at the post-match news conference, Icelandic football manager Heimir Hallgrimsson declined to provide details. I was there. Im not going to comment. Its something a disciplinary committee will look at, he told reporters. Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened. Halftime, I was in the dressing room, in my room with my staff I didnt see anything. When Im going to see and check, I will get back to you with the answer, he told reporters. Ireland had faced calls from some supporters and politicians to boycott the fixtures before beating Israel 3-0 behind closed doors in Hungary in their first meeting a week ago. Im absolutely delighted this is finished, Irelands Hallgrimsson told reporters. Its taken a toll out of us all. Ive given so much credit to the players. They have been absolutely amazing in tough times, and I wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks. Ireland is one of Europes most outspoken critics of Israels genocidal war on Gaza, and the Football Association of Ireland chose to stage Sundays match behind closed doors in Serbia amid the pressure to withdraw from the fixtures. The absence of supporters, however, did little to ease the tension on the pitch. As in the first meeting, there were no pre-match handshakes or exchange of pennants, while players from each team bowed their heads during the opposing national anthem. Ireland again wore black armbands commemorating all the victims of the conflict in Gaza, with the Israelis sporting black armbands in memory of the victims of the October 7 attack that sparked the war. articleTitle: Haryana, Chhattisgarh CMs seek business investment from Singapore
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Haryana and Chhattisgarh chief ministers seek Singapore business investment (Image: @NayabSainiBJP/X)
description: This is the first time two Indian chief ministers have jointly addressed Singapore investors, citing each state's role in the robustly growing Indian economy, which, at last count, registered 7.8 per cent GDP growth.
body_raw: The chief ministers of Haryana and Chhattisgarh held a series of back-to-back meetings with Singapore investors on Monday, highlighting investment opportunities in mineral resources and their states planned shift from an agri-economy to technology-driven industries. Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini arrived in the city-state on Sunday. On Monday, both chief ministers and their high-level delegations addressed the Singapore-India Network for Growth Forum 2026, attended by around 300 Singapore-based investors with a focus on Indian industrialisation programmes. The forum was organised by the Singapore Business Federation. Speaking to PTI after addressing the forum, Saini said his administration is focused on semiconductors, electronics, AI, data centres, medical devices, automobiles, electric vehicles, agri-business and global capability centres. We have issued specific incentives and policies for these industries for which 100 MoUs have been signed, said Saini. He highlighted the success of Singapore companies in Haryana and NCR and said, Singapore brings global expertise Haryana offers the scale of Indias growth. Singapore has shown the world how, despite limited resources, it is possible to build world-class infrastructure, efficient cities, robust logistics and thriving business ecosystems. He invited Singapore investors to participate in the development of Haryana, including in logistics and urban infrastructure. Chhattisgarh chief minister Sai invited investors to become long-term partners and highlighted the potential in the states large mineral resource reserves. This is the first time two Indian chief ministers have jointly addressed Singapore investors, citing each states role in the robustly growing Indian economy, which, at last count, registered 7.8 per cent GDP growth. We have rich mineral resources. Minerals such as iron ore, coal, limestone, and bauxite are available in large quantities. This creates a strong foundation for mineral-based as well as downstream industries, Sai said. He also highlighted strong trade relations between Chhattisgarh and Singapore, including the export of rice, spices, pharmaceuticals, speciality industrial materials, engineering products, electronic components and steel-related products. We now wish to take this relationship beyond trade and transform it into a long-term partnership. On Tuesday, the two chief ministers and their delegations will visit Singapore industrial sites, including the technical education centre, and are scheduled to separately hold round-tables with CEOs.

articleTitle: The Cornell case made me ask my sons — what would you have done?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Cornell fraternity case, Cornell sexual assault case, Cornell Chi Phi fraternity, Cornell 2024 allegations,
description: As a mother of two boys studying at American universities, I have talked to them about consent, sex, drugs and equality. But I had never asked them what they would do if another man crossed the line
body_raw: By Nalini Sorensen As details surfaced about the reopening of the alleged 2024 gang-rape case at Cornell University, I felt physically ill. I read every horrific detail, and then my thoughts turned to my sons. I have two sons, aged 18 and 21, both studying at universities in America, including an Ivy League one. That made this feel very real for me. I share a close relationship with both of them, and over the years, we have spoken openly and honestly about pretty much everything - relationships, sex, consent, equality, LGBTQ issues, alcohol, drugs, cigarettes and vaping, but I had never asked them what they would do if another man crossed the line. I wondered if Id done enough. What is enough in this world where the rules change daily? Is a mothers work ever truly done with her children? Here I was, thousands of miles away in Mumbai, my head swirling with thoughts, while both my sons were living in university dorms where frat parties happen regularly. There was something I needed to ask my sons. I called my older son first. He didnt pick up. My younger one didnt answer my call either. So, I did the next best thing. I sent each of them a text message This Cornell incident has made me feel sick to my stomach, and it has made me ponder. We have never had this kind of a talk, and so I have to ask. if you were in a text thread with 50 other young men, and they sent violent and explicit messages about a passed-out young woman, what would you do? Because, to me, its not just about those seven boys. Its also very much about the 50 others who were on that chat. Thats what I was calling about. Both my sons called me back. The conversations went very differently, but on reflection, very similarly. I told each of them that it was the silence of those other boys that bothered me. Only a thin line separates silence from complicity. I asked questions When is it okay to keep quiet? When must you call for help? When do you take yourself out of a setting? What kind of situations demand what kind of action? Is consent from someone drunk or high valid? It was interesting to hear their responses and see the difference in their personalities coming through. My younger son was outraged. He could not believe I thought he would keep quiet. It upset him that I had to even ask him what hed do that I didnt just know. Young, brash, fiery, principled. My older son was fuming over what he had read about the case. He wanted consequences that fit the allegations. He hated that Jane Doe had to go through this, that she had had to keep living with it. He wanted justice for her. And yes, he sure as hell wouldnt look the other way. Compassionate, just, action-driven. Both touched on the fact that the other boys on the chat might not have thought this was really happening. That they might have regarded it as someone typing nonsense while high or drunk, or both. It gave all three of us some pause. That led us to discuss which messages we should question, particularly when someones safety is at stake. Who should we believe? Who should we give the benefit of doubt to? They werent easy conversations to have, but I definitely slept better that night. The truth is, as parents, we are never really done. Our children may grow up and leave home, but the conversations dont have to end. We keep asking the difficult, uncomfortable questions. We keep reminding our sons that masculinity doesnt require hardness. We keep teaching them not just how to avoid doing the wrong thing, but how to recognise when something is wrong, and find the courage to do something about it. We keep hoping that we have raised boys who will know when to speak up, when to step in, when to ask for help, and when to understand that silence is a choice too. We owe that to our sons. And we owe it to every girl in the world. Sorensen is a Mumbai-based childrens author

articleTitle: How OpenAI’s runaway agents covered their tracks while targeting govt websites
articleFeaturedImageAlt: OpenAI agents
description: Key findings from a new report on the novel tactics used by OpenAI’s agents to erase records or make them inaccessible in order to obscure their activity.
body_raw: OpenAI agents that targeted Australian and US government websites earlier this year, were part of a much broader pattern of rogue agent activity, which included probing dozens of other organisations websites, using sophisticated tactics to try to exfiltrate data, and conceal their traces, according to a new security report. In a report published on Thursday, October 1, Asymmetric Security claimed to have found evidence that 55 additional US government and other websites were probed by OpenAIs agents, including the CDC, International Energy Agency, and Mayo Clinic. These websites were accessed in ways that bypass OpenAIs restrictions between March and September 2026, using only publicly available data, as per the report. Based on a 48-hour investigation, the report highlights the novel tactics used by the agents to erase records or make them inaccessible in order to obscure their hacking attempts. Additionally, the researchers uncovered how the AI agents gained access to private test versions of live government websites and the use of attacker-style reconnaissance tactics. The Asymmetric Security reports findings add another piece to the unsettling picture emerging of what happened in July 2026, when OpenAIs under-testing agents broke out of containment, gained unauthorised access to the internet, and went on a hacking spree. Similar incidents have since been reported by Anthropic, Meta, and Google, with each new case or type of behaviour raising fresh questions about how far AI agents can go once they escape from their sandboxes. Their use of tactics for deliberate subterfuge also makes it harder to rule out that the agents accessed sensitive data, as per the report. Heres a look at new details uncovered by Asymmetric Security researchers about OpenAI agents rogue activity. Key findings from the report Primary motivations The report suggests that limiting web access and imposing other constraints on the agents may have prompted them to devise increasingly elaborate ways to circumvent these restrictions. On a similar note, OpenAI and Google researchers have found evidence that constraints could lead to misalignment and reward hacking type of behaviour by the agents. Tasks assigned to agents Based on their analysis, the researchers said that the rogue AI agents were originally tasked with researching public health and other data, possibly as part of an evaluation. As a result, the agents searched for health and prescription statistics from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare AIHW trade figures from the UNs Trade and Development Body UNCTAD and university statistics from Data USA, as per the report. Tools used by agents The report found that the AI agents used a host of tools to exfiltrate data from targeted websites and support other activity, including remote browsers such as Wayback Machine, payload hosts, reader services like Common Crawl index, and link shorteners such as tinyurl.com. How it played out As per the evidence seen by the researchers, the agents went beyond searching for official information sources to complete their assigned tasks. They attempted to find exposed configuration files, create accounts, route requests through third-party services, and retrieve results through unintended channels. Mimicking a web browser One of the ways in which agents worked around sandbox restrictions is by using public web tools such as httpbin and urlquery to access websites on their behalf. Httpbin lets developers test how their software communicates with websites while Urlquery opens submitted links in a browser and records what happens. The agents relied on a combination of these services to emulate a full web browser to try and fetch data from the target website. Retrieving data through notifications The AI agents used a push-notification service called ntfy and other web archives in order to exfiltrate data from targeted websites. The agents may have used ntfy because they could not download the data directly from the targeted websites with their available tools, as per the report. Notably, ntfy messages expire after 12 hours by default which means that there is some evidence of data exfiltration, no one knows what that data actually was. Creating multiple accounts to obscure activity From June 14, 2026, onwards, the agents created a number of private accounts to hide their activity on the urlquery platform. They used disposable email services, browser platforms, and scanning services that could further support such activity. Temporary mailboxes could receive registration and verification emails, while scanning-service accounts could unlock additional features. Over time the agents began creating private accounts which limited visibility into their browser activity, as per the report. Differences between agents and threat actors One of the key differences between a swarm of rogue AI agents and traditional threat actor groups is the rapid evolution of tactics. There was a spike in activity targeting Australian entities between June 16 and 21. During this period, the agents rapidly cycled through tools and tactics. For traditional threat actors this type of technique evolution happens over months or years the evolution of agent techniques was compressed into just days, the report said. Harder to detect agent activity The bursts of activity resembled the surges that can follow disclosure of a major vulnerability. However, because the agents varied approaches produced a more varied set of indicators, activity was harder to recognise and cluster, it added. What next The researchers said that getting access to OpenAI agents chains of thoughts or reasoning traces could help determine whether the agents were deliberately using these mechanisms to cover their tracks. The report also calls for further investigation to help establish what the agents did and why, including analysing model transcripts, tool calls, internal logs from targeted websites, and additional records held by third-party services used by the agents.

articleTitle: FSSAI orders recall of Everest cumin powder: What to do if you have used affected batch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Experts explain what consumers should do after consuming a recalled batch of cumin powder and how to check packaged spices.
description: A recalled batch of Everest cumin powder was found to contain pesticide residues above prescribed limits. Experts explain what this means, what consumers should do if they consumed it and how to check packaged spices.
body_raw: FSSAI continues to enforce strict regulatory compliance to safeguard consumer health across the country. On October 4, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India recalled a batch of Everest cumin powder. On X, it wrote, MS Everest Food Products Private Limited has been directed to immediately recall Pre-packed Cumin Powder after tests declared the sample unsafe. 2 Product Recall Order Ms Everest Food Products Private Limited has been directed to immediately recall Pre-packed Cumin Powder after tests declared the sample UNSAFE.22 FoodSafety FSSAINotice FSSAIAction - FSSAI fssaiindia October 4, 2026 The action follows laboratory testing that found pesticide residues above the prescribed limits. FSSAI has declared the affected batch of Everest cumin powder, Batch No. E080668761, unsafe after residues of Azoxystrobin and Thiamethoxam were found above permissible limits. This is afood-safety concern related to a specific recalled batch and should not be interpreted as meaning all packaged cumin powders are unsafe. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. What if you have accidentally consumed the product Dr Chirag Tandon, Director, Internal Medicine, ShardaCare - Healthcity says, Finding residues above the permitted limit does not automatically mean that someone who accidentally consumed the product containing residues of pesticides such as Azoxystrobin or Thiamethoxam will develop poisoning or immediate illness. So, it is important not to panic. The actual risk, he says, depends on the concentration, quantity consumed, frequency of exposure, and the persons age and body weight. EFSA assesses pesticide exposure using both acute and chronic dietary exposure models. However, if a product contains pesticide residues above the prescribed limit, you should stop using that batch. Repeated or higher exposure is more concerning. Thiamethoxam belongs to the neonicotinoid group of insecticides, while Azoxystrobin is a fungicide. Their presence above the permitted residue level does not by itself establish that a person will experience symptoms, and consumers should not assume that headaches, nausea or other nonspecific symptoms are necessarily caused by the spice, Dr Tandon explains. If a person has consumed a recalled product once, the sensible approach is to discontinue its use and avoid further exposure rather than attempting to induce vomiting or undertake a detox. However, Dr Tandon says that if anyone develops significant or persistent symptoms after suspected pesticide exposure, or has consumed a large quantity of the affected product, they should seek medical advice and provide the product packaging or batch details if available. Children and people with other vulnerabilities warrant particular caution because dietary exposure is assessed by body weight. What should consumers check? From a consumer perspective, checking the label is one of the simplest precautions. Before using a packaged spice, check the brand, batch or lot number, manufacturing and best-before dates, FSSAI licence details, and the integrity of the packaging. Avoid damaged, tampered, or poorly sealed packets. Consumers should also check official FSSAI recall information when a particular product or batch has been flagged. When it comes to powdered spices, adulteration is another major concern. Dr Tandon says, This is because grinding makes it difficult to identify what has been mixed into the product. FSSAI guidance notes that cumin may be adulterated with substances such as coloured grass seeds, while powdered spices can contain fillers such as starch, flour, sawdust or other cheaper materials. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: DMK gets court permission to sue TVK ministers over Veeramani case remarks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Granite baron R Veeramani faces multiple child sexual abuse cases as Madras High Court clears DMK to sue ministers and TVK IT wing over shielding claims (File Photo)
description: The DMK, which was in power when the allegations first came to light, is seeking Rs 1.01 crore in damages from Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and CTR Nirmal Kumar, and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s IT wing
body_raw: The Madras High Court on Monday granted the DMK permission to pursue a defamation suit against two Tamil Nadu ministers and the ruling TVKs information technology wing over statements allegedly accusing the party of shielding granite businessman R Veeramani, who is facing multiple child sexual abuse cases. The DMK, which was in power when the allegations first came to light, is seeking Rs 1.01 crore in damages from Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and CTR Nirmal Kumar, and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagams IT wing. It has also sought an order restraining the ministers from making statements it describes as defamatory. Justice K Govindarajan Thilakavadi allowed the partys application for leave to institute the suit. Mondays order concerns permission to bring the proceedings, and it does not decide whether the disputed statements were defamatory or establish the merits of either sides account. The application, argued by senior counsel J Ravindran, sought the courts permission because the TVK IT wings office and the headquarters of social media companies named in the proceedings-X Corp, Meta Platforms and YouTube-were outside the HCs territorial jurisdiction. Filed on behalf of the DMK by its general secretary, Duraimurugan, the suit places the timing of the original police response at the centre of the partys defence. According to the petition, police registered a First Information Report FIR under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act on October 7, 2025, a day after a child rights activist submitted a video clip showing the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl. The DMK argues that this sequence demonstrates that the police acted promptly under its government. The police had in February this year sought to file a closure report in the case, but a POCSO court intervened and ordered a fresh probe. The CMK maintains that the subsequent investigation proceeded according to law and the evidence available, and that it neither interfered in the inquiry nor had any connection or connivance with the accused. Those assertions form part of its case before the court. The DMK also alleges that the ministers remarks were intended to secure political advantage ahead of the Madurantakam and Dharapuram by-elections and to divert attention from what it calls the current governments failures. The ministers opposed the application on procedural grounds. They argued that, because they had been sued in their official capacities as Cabinet members, the DMK should have served notice under Section 801 of the Code of Civil Procedure or obtained permission under Section 802 to dispense with that requirement. At an earlier hearing two weeks ago, the judge had directed the defendants to file a counter-affidavit and listed the matter for Monday.

articleTitle: Flydubai Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami planned Tel Aviv crash before joining airline: Report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai copilot
description: Two Israeli officials told Reuters the co-pilot allegedly told UAE interrogators he had planned the attack before joining flydubai and had searched for airlines flying to Tel Aviv.
body_raw: The flydubai flight FZ1073s co-pilot, who allegedly stabbed Indian pilot Smit Machchhar in a suspected attempt to crash the plane in a midair cockpit brawl last week, has reportedly told the UAE authorities that he had planned the attack before he was hired by the Dubai state-owned airline, two Israeli officials said. The co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, had planned to crash the flydubai flight into Tel Avivs Ben Gurion International Airport, news agency Reuters reported, citing Israeli officials. Israeli officials have said the co-pilot is from Oman but have not named him, while the UAE and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilots identity. Previous Israel-bound flight also allegedly targeted The plane took off from Dubai last Wednesday with 174 passengers and six crew members. The report added that Hamam had operated another Israel-bound plane earlier this year and had intended to hijack and crash it, but he chose not to. Little information is available as to why the Omani co-pilot changed his mind while operating the previous flight bound for Tel Aviv however, he is thought to have known someone on board, the Reuters report added. The Omani co-pilot attacked Machchhar with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said. The UAE official termed the midair violence a terrorist incident. Co-pilot allegedly sought flydubai job to target Tel Aviv The Omani co-pilot reportedly told the UAE authorities that he had applied for a job at flydubai after searching for several airline companies that fly to Tel Aviv, Israeli officials were quoted as saying. The major disaster on flydubai flight FZ1073 was averted after Captain Smit Machchhar, who has been hailed as a hero, was able to open the cockpit door, and passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot. Questions over airline vetting and Israeli security protocols The new details have raised concerns about how thoroughly flydubai vets potential employees, and how the Omani co-pilots presence on a flight filled with Israeli passengers leapfrogged Tel Avivs stringent security protocols. This comes as Israeli authorities have said that they have agreements with foreign airlines to keep pilots of nations without diplomatic ties from flying there. Israel and Oman do not have formal diplomatic relations.

articleTitle: No membership card, land after promise, holiday firm to pay Delhi man Rs 3.25 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Holiday provider Delhi State consumer dispute redressal commission
description: The Delhi state consumer commission directed a holiday provider to refund Rs 1.75 lakh and pay Rs 1.5 lakh for mental agony and litigation costs.
body_raw: The Delhi State Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission recently ordered a hospitality and holiday provider chain to pay Rs 3.25 lakh to a man, as it was held guilty of deficiency in service for not issuing a membership card and allotting the promised plot after collecting the payment for a holiday membership scheme. President Sangita Dhingra Sehgal and Member Bimla Kumari were hearing a plea filed by a man who had paid Rs 1.75 lakh to a holiday provider chain for obtaining membership of a scheme which claimed to provide holiday offers, benefits and a complimentary plot on Bombay-Goa Highway. The opposite party holiday provider was deficient in providing its services to the complainant the man, as it failed to render the services and facilities assured under the Mr Cool Global Parivar Life Membership, including issuance of the membership card and allotment of the complimentary plot measuring 2000 sq. ft. at Kolad, Maharashtra, the September 28 order read. The commission further said that the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, came into being in order to protect the interests of consumers who are affected by the acts of the service providers, who in order to attract the consumers, tend to make lucrative offers but when it comes to actually providing the offered services, they take a step back. The man claimed that in April, 2008, he met the business promotion executives of the hospitality and holiday provider chain who were carrying out word-of-mouth business promotion of the scheme at Connaught Place, New Delhi. According to the man, the hospitality chain was providing various services and facilities in the scheme, including Lifetime membership for the member, spouse, and parents for life, and children up to the age of 18 years. Annual subscription of Rs 4,000. Lifelong, transferable, and global membership. 2000 square feet plot at Golf Village, Kolad, Mumbai, situated on the Bombay-Goa Highway, to be registered in the name of the man. Free holiday for 7 days and 6 nights at any of the properties of the chain for 30 years under Resort Condominiums International RCI membership. 3 days and 3 nights holiday for 5 years by paying Rs. 350 per day Food and Beverages charges extra. Five years free membership to RCI-affiliated clubs. Holiday in Goa for 3 nights and 2 days for a couple with one-way air ticket. The man alleged that, lured by the genuineness of the offer and services, he opted for Mr Cool Global Parivar Life Membership at the rate of Rs 2 lakh and paid Rs 1.75 lakh after a discount of Rs 25,000 was given to him. The man was also allotted a membership number. The man contended that he was assured by the holiday provider that he would receive his membership card and other information, brochures, etc., within two weeks so that he could enjoy the benefits of his membership during the summer vacation. However, no membership card was received, and the entire vacation plan made by the man with his family members was ruined. The man stated that he had to face a very awkward situation as he had also included one of his married relatives and their children. The man was forced to file a consumer complaint because even after calling various officials of the holiday provider and furnishing different documents that the provider asked for, he did not receive any satisfactory response, which caused considerable mental anguish to the man and his father. No proof of payment Advocate Ankur Saini, appearing for the holiday provider, argued that the man never applied for or availed any holiday package services under the agreement and that he had failed to place any proof that he had made a payment of Rs 1.75 lakh towards the membership of the holiday provider. The counsel urged that the man had himself opted for the membership after understanding the terms and conditions of the agreement and had paid the non-refundable membership fee. The counsel stated that the complimentary plot was subject to certain terms and conditions, like payment of Rs 20,000 towards registration and other expenses, which were not fulfilled by the man. Not sustainable The state commission noted that the holiday provider failed to issue the membership card to the complainant the man for availing the services and benefits under the said membership. According to the commission, the contention of the opposite party holiday provider that the complainant man was required to pay Rs 20,000 towards registration and other expenses for the complimentary plot and annual maintenance charges for availing the membership benefits, is also not sustainable, as the holiday provider had failed to establish that it had fulfilled its primary obligations under the membership scheme, including issuance of the membership card and allotment of the complimentary plot. The state commission directed the holiday provider to refund Rs 1.75 lakh paid by the man and further pay Rs 1 lakh as cost for mental agony. The holiday provider was also ordered to pay an additional sum of Rs 50,000 to the man as litigation costs. Takeaway The ruling establishes the obligation of holiday provider companies to follow up on their holiday schemes and that the concerns of the consumers must not be ignored, causing them unnecessary inconvenience. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Delhi waste dumped in Gurugram: 10 arrested, interstate syndicate under scanner
articleFeaturedImageAlt: waste pickup
description: The action comes as the city grapples with 1,200 tonnes of municipal waste a day and millions of tonnes of legacy waste. Police said so far, no link with any Delhi civic body has been found.
body_raw: A waste trail from Delhi to Gurugram has led to 10 arrests and the seizure of seven vehicles, with police alleging that an interstate network was bringing in municipal and plastic waste to dump, segregate and sell in the state. As of now, we have found that the dumping work was operating like a syndicate, where they would also segregate useful items theyd find and sell those, a senior police officer said. Senior officers said the enforcement drive on Sunday evening was launched following a Friday review meeting chaired by Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, who directed authorities to ensure the city is not turned into a dumping ground and ordered strict action against vehicles bringing in garbage from outside. Following the directives, police initiated suo motu action rather than waiting for formal complaints, officials said. Four FIRs have been registered across three border-adjacent police stations two at Bajghera, and one each at Udyog Vihar and Rajendra Park. This is the first of its kind police operation earlier we would only get complaints of it happening on a small scale, said an officer. Inside the op Gurugram Police spokesperson, Assistant Sub-Inspector ASI Sandeep Kumar, said the drive was carried out under the directions of the Commissioner of Police and the supervision of the Deputy Commissioner of Police West. Police teams conducted checking and naka-bandi at several locations. Vehicles bringing garbage and plastic waste from Delhi were intercepted, leading to the arrest of 10 accused and the recovery of seven vehicles, including canters and tractor-trolleys, Kumar said. Questioning revealed that the waste was being transported into Gurugram through a coordinated network linked to Delhi, ASI Kumar. Once brought across the border, the plastic waste was separated from the general refuse and segregated before being dispatched to buyers elsewhere, he added. ASI Kumar said that investigators are scrutinising ownership records of the seized fleet. Police teams are gathering information regarding the arrested accused and vehicle owners. If the involvement or role of any vehicle owner is established during the probe, strict legal action will be taken against them as per law. Strict action for environmental protection will continue, he said. A senior police officer said notices have been sent to truck owners to join the investigation. We will check if the vehicles belong or are under any government or private body from Delhi, he said. So far, no prima facie link with any Delhi civic body has been found, officers said. Police said further investigation is underway to track the waste supply chain back to its collection points in the national capital and identify all intermediaries involved in the transport and recycling network. Gurugrams waste problem The operation assumes importance given the scale of the citys garbage problem. Millennium City generates roughly 1,200 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, as per civic body data, while struggling to fully clear millions of tonnes of legacy trash at the oversaturated Bandhwari landfill. The landfill site is under persistent National Green Tribunal NGT scrutiny over alleged groundwater contamination, toxic leachate, and frequent fires. Garbage is currently not segregated at the time of collection from most residents. The citys garbage collection and processing has been addressed only through stopgap arrangements and short-term tenders for over two years, when the work order of the previous contractor was scrapped due to poor performance.

articleTitle: ‘Completely false’: Makers deny ticket price hike in AP for Vijay-Rashmika’s Ranabaali
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna in Ranabaali
description: Production house Mythri Movie Makers has issued an official statement on X denying reports that it has applied for ticket price hike in Andhra Pradesh for Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna's Ranabaali.
body_raw: Production house Mythri Movie Makers has denied reports that it has applied for a ticket price hike in Andhra Pradesh for Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandannas upcoming period action drama Ranabaali, calling the reports completely false in an official statement posted on X on Sunday. There have been reports that we have applied for ticket price hikes in Andhra Pradesh for Ranabaali. We would like to clarify that these reports are completely false. We have not applied for any ticket price hikes in either of the Telugu states, the statement read. The statement confirmed that Ranabaali will release at standard ticket prices when it arrives in theatres on October 16 during the Dussehra festival window. Ranabaali will release at standard ticket prices, and we are confident that audiences will have a great cinematic experience this festive season, the statement added. Also Read Ranabaali director on how Vijay Devarakonda and Rashmika Mandannas marriage helps his film The clarification comes at a sensitive time for ticket pricing in the Telugu states. Andhra Pradesh has maintained strict controls on theatrical ticket prices, with any increase requiring government approval. The issue has been one of the most contentious subjects in the Telugu film industry over the past two years, with producers and exhibitors arguing that fixed pricing caps limit their ability to recover rising production costs. Telangana operates under a similar but slightly different pricing framework, with the state government retaining authority over ticket price approvals. About Ranabaali Ranabaali is directed by Rahul Sankrityan and stars Vijay Deverakonda as Singanamala Bobbili Ranabaali, a Rayalaseema warrior who rises against British colonial forces during the Madras Famine of 1876-78. The film also stars Rashmika Mandanna as Jayamma and South African actor Arnold Vosloo as the British antagonist Sir Theodore Hector. The film is produced by Naveen Yerneni and Y. Ravi Shankar under Mythri Movie Makers banner and presented by T-Series. It releases worldwide on October 16, where it will compete with Rajinikanths Jailer 2, which releases a day earlier on October 15, for screens across the Telugu and Tamil markets.

articleTitle: Ola, Uber, bike taxis in Maharashtra get 9 months to switch to 100% EV fleets
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ola uber 100 percent EV fleets maharashtra
description: The 100 percent EV fleets directive comes amid concerns raised by bike taxi associations and riders over the mandatory transition to electric vehicles.
body_raw: The Maharashtra government has set July 2027 as the deadline for bike taxi aggregators, including Ola, Uber, Rapido and other bike taxis to transition to a 100 per cent electric fleet. In October, the State Transport Department wrote to ride-hailing aggregators and Regional Transport Offices RTOs across Maharashtra, granting a nine-month phased transition period to operators to switch to 100 percent EV fleets, following directions from Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. Under the 100 percent EV transition plan, aggregators currently operating petrol-powered bike taxis will be given six months in the first phase to comply with the EV mandate. Operators that have applied for provisional or temporary licences under the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Rules, 2025, will receive an additional three months to meet the requirement.
