The directive comes amid concerns raised by bike taxi associations and riders over the mandatory transition to electric vehicles. What did the bike taxi aggregators seek? In September, the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Welfare Association had written to CM Fadnavis and other officials, including the State Transport Minister and Transport Commissioner, requesting one-and-a-half years to fully switch to EVs given several considerations. Most bike taxi riders hail from middle or lower-middle-class backgrounds, making it difficult for them to undertake a significant investment to purchase an EV bike at once. The lack of EV charging infrastructure and the smaller life of an electric vehicle also makes this decision more difficult, Amit Gawde, President of the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Welfare Association, said. Aggregators had also sought an extension until 2030, citing the Maharashtra Electric Vehicle Policy and the need for more time to transition their fleets, according to a state government official. The government has, however, granted them only nine months to switch to 100 percent EV fleets. Aggregators had also sought an extension until 2030, citing the Maharashtra Electric Vehicle Policy and the need for more time to transition their fleets, according to a state government official. The government, however, has granted only a nine-month transition period. The move comes as the state has stepped up enforcement against unauthorised and non-compliant bike taxi operations. State Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik had earlier told The Indian Express that the government had initially considered allowing a 5050 mix of petrol and electric motorcycles. However, the Cabinet rejected the proposal amid concerns that companies could choose not to procure electric vehicles despite having the capacity to do so, as they are more expensive.

articleTitle: CJI says Supreme Court did not approve Form 6 changes: What the form is, why it matters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Form 6 mess: People served SIR (Special Intensive Revision) notices arrive at Appasaheb Kulkarni Primary School in Gokhalenagar on Monday with their documents. (Express Photo - Arul Horizon)
description: The voter enrolment form was changed to include questions linked to the special intensive revision, prompting objections over the legal process followed.
body_raw: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday October 5 said that the Supreme Court had not approved any of the modifications to Form 6 in response to an argument on the unlawful modifications made to Form 6. While hearing petitions against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a three-judge bench headed by the CJI said the Supreme Court will examine who modified the form after receiving a report from the Election Commission. The latest development comes two weeks after The Indian Express investigation on September 23 that revealed that two Election Commissioners had flagged the illegal and unauthorised changes to Form 6. One petition accused the Chief Election Commissioner of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bears no reasonable nexus or legal connection to his official duties. Such an act falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability, it added. What is Form 6? Form 6 is the statutory form for applicants who have newly become eligible voters after turning 18 years of age or acquiring Indian citizenship or deleted voters who want to apply afresh. The existing Form 6, which is published in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, asks the applicant to provide the name and EPIC number of those family members with whom they currently reside. The Indian Express reported on July 12 that the online version of the form on ECINET had a new declaration inserted between the above two sections. The change introduced questions related to the Special Intensive Revision SIR into Form 6. It asked applicants to choose one of three statements whether their name appeared in the electoral roll during the last SIR held in the early 2000s, whether a parents or grandparents name appeared in that roll, or whether neither their name nor that of their parents appeared in it. If their name appeared in the 2000s SIR, applicants were asked to provide the Assembly constituency number, the polling booth number known as part number and the serial number at which their father or mother was registered in the last SIR. Interestingly, the Form 6 available for download on the EC portal did not have this declaration. Why was the change disputed? The Indian Express investigation revealed that Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected to decisions taken and orders issued without their knowledge at least 14 times over 10 months. The changes under scrutiny concerned the national rollout of the SIR. After The Indian Express reported on the updated Form 6 on ECINET in July, Sandhu put on record on August 13 that it was unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately. Since the move was without amendment, the two Election Commissioners had objected to the same. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, only the central government can amend the voter enrolment, deletion and correction forms. On September 26, the Election Commission announced it had removed the SIR declaration in Form 6 on the ECINET application portal in states where the SIR has concluded. However, the declaration was still there for those states where the SIR is still ongoing. The EC said, For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Interestingly, the ECs press note did not mention the online form, or the question, or say whether it has been removed. However, it said that the Supreme Court upheld the declaration, which the courts May 27 order on the SIR does not appear to do in terms. And it does not say who put the question there in July, or why it stayed after Sandhu called it unauthorisedillegal on August 13. What does the law say? Article 326 of the Constitution guarantees the right to enrol as an elector to all adult citizens who are ordinarily resident in a particular Assembly constituency, unless otherwise disqualified by law. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Union government to make rules for the conduct of elections and the registration of electors. Section 28 of the Act, titled Power to make rules, says The Central Government may, after consulting the Election Commission by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. It also says that every rule made under the Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament. Form 6 is a part of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which emerges from the Act. Therefore, any change to the form would require an amendment and gazette notification by the Law and Justice Ministry. However, the ministry did not notify any change to Form 6, as seen in the notifications available on the e-Gazette website from June 24, 2025 - when the EC first announced the SIR - to date.

articleTitle: Minimum 10% water cut in Maharashtra from October 16 amid drought, El Nino concerns
articleFeaturedImageAlt: maharashtra drought water cut
description: Amid drought-like conditions, the Maharashtra government has ordered a minimum of 10 percent water cut.
body_raw: The Maharashtra government has directed all municipal corporations, municipalities, and gram panchayats to impose a minimum 10 percent water cut from October 16, citing water storage, drought-like conditions, and the possibility of El Nino-related water stress extending into next year. Local bodies have also been asked to undertake special drives to identify and stop water leakage. Besides, sewage treatment plants have to be operated at full capacity. The government has local bodies to ensure that instead of fresh water, treated wastewater should be used for gardening, construction and washing. Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan said the department had prepared a reservoir-wise and use-wise water management plan up to August 31, 2027, with drinking water given the highest priority. The government has asked all agencies to use water carefully and take measures to conserve available supplies. Under the plan, water needed for drinking purposes will first be reserved in dams and reservoirs up to August 31 next year. The department said it would take into account evaporation, siltation and unauthorised water extraction while calculating the available supply. A 10 percent emergency buffer stock will be maintained in every reservoir to deal with uncertain rainfall and water situation. In an extreme situation, water from the dead storage of a reservoir may also be used after a technical assessment, the government said. Irrigation only after drinking water, livestock needs The department has also laid down a priority order for agricultural use. Water will be released for agriculture only after meeting the drinking water, livestock and fodder requirements. For irrigation, the priority will be rabi foodgrain and fodder crops, followed by other rabi crops. Water will be made available to perennial crops only if supplies remain after meeting these requirements. The government has also said it will encourage water-saving irrigation methods. Industries must reuse 30 of water For the industrial sector, the government has made reuse or recycling of at least 30 per cent of the consumed water mandatory. The move is part of the departments efforts to reduce freshwater demand as reservoir levels remain limited, according to the government. Illegal extraction under scanner As two-thirds of Maharashtra is reeling under drought-like conditions, the government will form joint squads to patrol dams, rivers and canals and prevent unauthorised water extraction. The squads will take action against those drawing water illegally. The water availability will be reviewed regularly through guardian ministers and canal advisory committees, Girish Mahajan said. Every department and citizen must use every drop of water carefully to avoid a water crisis in the coming year, Mahajan said. The government also referred to 265 talukas where drought had been declared, saying that the possibility of El Nino conditions continuing into the following year had prompted the detailed planning.

articleTitle: Suvendu Adhikari signs UDAN airport pact, blames delay on TMC ‘attitude’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UDAN scheme West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari
description: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari said land had become the main obstacle for aviation infrastructure development under Trinamool Congress rule.
body_raw: The West Bengal government has finally joined the Union civil aviation ministrys UDAN scheme by signing a memorandum of understanding to set up four new airports in the state-at Chharra in Purulia, Balurghat, Hasimara, and Kalaikunda. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, and senior officials from both the state and the Centre attended the event at Nabanna where the agreement under the Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik UDAN scheme was signed on Monday. At a press conference held afterwards, Adhikari sharply criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government, accusing it of delaying the states airport and infrastructure development. Even though the central government asked for land, the previous government did not provide it. The signing of the agreement was stalled for so long because of this negative attitude. The previous government had refused to provide land for a second airport in Kolkata. Not only the airport, but due to the failure to provide land, several important national highway and railway projects remained stuck for years, the chief minister said. Adhikari further said, Land had become the main obstacle in the path of development. Once the new airports are built, trade and economic activity in the state will surge. As per the MoU, the state government will provide required land and basic infrastructure, while the Centre and the Airports Authority of India will oversee the airport development. The chief minister said the government planned to set up a modern pilot training centre at Behala in southwestern Kolkata. The four new airports are expected not only to reduce pressure on Kolkata airport but also to create direct air connectivity between the states districts and other parts of the country.

articleTitle: NCERT launches 40-week online science teaching diploma; register from October 12
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ncert course
description: Registration for the fresh batch will begin on October 12, 2026, and candidates can enrol until November 12, 2026 through the NCERTX learning platform at ncertx.in.
body_raw: NCERT has announced a 40-week online Diploma Course in Teaching of Science at Middle Stage Classes 6-8 for the 2026-27 session. The programme is aimed at in-service and pre-service teachers and others involved in science education, with a focus on improving subject knowledge as well as pedagogical skills needed to teach Science at the middle stage. Registration for the new batch will begin on October 12, 2026, and candidates can enrol until November 12, 2026 through the NCERTX learning platform at ncertx.in. The course is designed as a MOOC for Science teachers dealing with Classes 6 to 8. It uses multimedia-based interactive learning material and is structured to take learners from basic concepts to greater conceptual depth. NCERT says the material can also support classroom teaching, including lesson planning and explaining concepts to students. Also Read Ram Rajya, NEP, Sengol What students will learn in NCERT in Governance and Public Policy chapter The programme is intended for professional development and is available online, allowing enrolled participants to access the course through their registered accounts. Who can enrol? Candidates with a Bachelor of Science BSc degree, in-service teachers teaching Science in Classes 6 to 8, candidates with a diploma or degree in education, and pre-service teachers pursuing a diploma or degree in education can apply. Other individuals directly involved in Science education can also enrol. The course is not, however, a teacher-appointment qualification. NCERT specifically states that it is an academic course and cannot be treated as equivalent to another qualification required for teacher appointment or claimed for exemption. The programme carries a one-time enrolment fee of Rs 2,000, with no other fee specified. Payment has to be made online. After making the payment, candidates will receive an invitation email from NCERTX, generally within a week, with instructions to complete enrolment. Candidates have been advised to use the same email ID throughout the payment and enrolment process. Also Read Resisting invaders to swords of goddesses NCERT revises book on medieval history for Class 9 The course is scheduled to begin on November 16, 2026, and tentatively conclude on August 31, 2027. It will have 40 modules, with a new module opening every Monday and each module expected to require around six to eight hours. What after the course Assessment and certification Each of the 40 modules will have an objective end-of-module test. The tests will remain open for 15 days, allowing learners to complete them at their convenience. Participants who complete all modules and appear for all 40 tests will be eligible for the final examination, which will be a timed test with its date announced separately. Also Read No topics dropped from class 9 math syllabus NCERT On successful completion, NCERT will award an e-certificate for Teaching of Science at Middle Stage. The course can be accessed online throughout the course period using a laptop or desktop with an internet connection.

articleTitle: Supreme Court gets 3 new judges, including its second woman Justice
articleFeaturedImageAlt: President Droupadi Murmu appoints High Court Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh as Supreme Court judges
description: High Court Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh elevated to Supreme Court
body_raw: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed three High Court chief justices - Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh as judges of the Supreme Court. The appointments were made in exercise of the powers conferred on the President by the Constitution of India, Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said in a post on X on Monday. In exercise of the powers conferred by the Constitution of India, the President of India is pleased to appoint the following Chief Justices of High Courts as Judges of the Supreme Court of India - Arjun Ram Meghwal arjunrammeghwal October 5, 2026 Justice Sunita Agarwal is the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, while Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya is the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. Both have the Allahabad High Court as their parent High Court. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh is the Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court and has the Jharkhand High Court as his parent High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended the names on September 28. While the current working strength of the apex court is 34, once the three new judges formally take the oath, its effective strength will go up to 37. The top courts sanctioned strength is 38 judges, including the chief justice of India. It was recently increased from 34 following the Supreme Court Amendment Act, 2026. -With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Do we really need affidavits?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: affidavit
description: If identity can be authenticated, false statements can be punished and facts can be verified, what does the act of swearing actually add?
body_raw: By Preeti Kumari The Act XIV of 1848 empowered the Supreme Court at Fort William to commission persons to take affidavits and solemn affirmations. An affidavit so taken was deemed to have been taken in Court. The purpose was practical It let a sworn statement be treated as made in court without the maker appearing in person. Nearly two centuries later, we must ask whether a device intended to save a journey has itself become the reason for another journey? Affidavits are routinely used for caste, income declaration, residence, and eligibility for benefits, etc. But this does not answer a fundamental question Why must the statement be sworn at all? Suppose an applicant states in an affidavit that her annual family income is below Rs 2 lakh. The notary neither verifies ITRs, employment records or bank accounts nor bears responsibility if the statement later proves false. The affidavit establishes the makers belief in its truth under oath, not the truth of the assertion. The government may still require documentary evidence or administrative enquiry before deciding the claim. We are dealing with four separate questions Who made the statement? Can the authority or court legally receive it? What happens if the maker deliberately lies? Is the underlying fact true? If identity, admissibility and consequences for deliberate falsehood can all be provided by law, why must I go before another person and swear that I am telling the truth? During my time in public administration, I have seen the huge cost that the procedural requirement of affidavit imposes on citizens, particularly in smaller towns and remote areas. The line Affidavit to be enclosed creates an entire journey. She finds the format, gets it drafted, procures stamp paper, locates a notary or magistrate, pays, and returns to the government office or court carrying substantially the same statement she could have made directly. A few thousand rupees fee, and a days lost work mean something very different to a poor person seeking a caste certificate or welfare benefit than they do to the system imposing the requirement. But the argument cannot stop at the government counter. There is another citizen whom affidavit reform often forgets The person caught in a legal proceeding - a witness, an accident victim, a maintenance claimant, a spouse in a matrimonial dispute or a person defending her home in a property case too is a citizen. Some inconvenience is unavoidable in administering justice but inconvenience should serve a clear purpose. If the statement needs to be challenged, challenge it. If the maker needs to be cross-examined, summon her. If records contradict her, examine the records. If the underlying fact needs verification, verify it. If she deliberately lies, punish her. Which of those protections disappear merely because she did not submit a sworn affidavit? To dispense with affidavit is not an untested idea. In the United States, 28 U.S.C. 1746, Unsworn declarations under penalty of perjury, separates truthfulness and legal liability from the necessity of swearing. Irelands Civil Law and Criminal Law Act 2020 has removed the need for making statements through sworn affidavits with electronically signed self-declarations - Statement of truth. Crucially, it has replaced, in the proceedings covered by the reform, the sworn form with a statement carrying direct legal responsibility. Affidavit reform in India has generally asked In which cases can we dispense with the affidavit and accept a self-declaration?. That is, it starts with the affidavit as the default and the declaration as an exception. Perhaps the presumption should now be reversed. The reform can begin with the principle Preserve the legal consequence, dispense with the ritual. For government services, an authenticated self-declaration carrying clear legal consequences for deliberate falsehood should suffice. The courts could recognise an electronically authenticated statement of truth, with Aadhaar-based authentication as one possible means of establishing identity, give it the evidentiary status by law, preserve the ability to challenge it and cross-examine its maker, and attach serious consequences to deliberate falsehood. In Swear Not At All 1817, Jeremy Bentham asks If these safeguards can be built into the process, and falsehood punished, what does swearing add? Perhaps it is time the affidavit itself proved its necessity. The writer is district commissioner, West Karbi Anglong, Assam

articleTitle: Jailer 2 trailer: Rajinikanth returns with a bigger cast and an even bigger battle. Watch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajinikanth movie Jailer 2 trailer
description: Jailer 2 trailer: Jailer 2 brings back Rajinikanth as the retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, alongside an expanded ensemble featuring SJ Suryah, Vidya Balan, Mithun Chakraborty and Suraj Venjaramoodu.
body_raw: Jailer 2 trailer Sun Pictures released trailer for Jailer 2 on Monday, October 5, offering audiences their first detailed glimpse of the sequel to the 2023 blockbuster Jailer. The trailer arrives ten days before the release, following a promotional campaign that has included four singles from Anirudh Ravichanders 12-track album, including the Nora Fatehi special number Bindaas. What the Jailer 2 trailer shows The Jailer 2 trailer picks up from where Jailer left off. Rajinikanth reprises his role as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, the retired jailer who dismantled an idol smuggling network in the first film. The sequel finds the entire racketeering network turning against him, with former allies and new enemies converging on the retired officer who thought his fight was over. While his enemies try to track him, Tiger is seen working as a driver in a remote village. The trailer establishes a darker, more expansive conflict than the first film. While Jailer was primarily a cat-and-mouse game between Tiger and Vinayakans idol smuggler, Jailer 2 appears to involve multiple antagonists and a broader criminal conspiracy. SJ Suryah features prominently in the trailer in what appears to be a pivotal antagonist role, bringing his trademark unpredictability to a character whose motives are deliberately kept under wraps. Vidya Balan makes her Tamil cinema debut in a role whose details have been kept under wraps. The trailer offers glimpses of her character without revealing her connection to Tiger Muthuvel Pandian or the central conflict. The trailer also shows glimpses of Jackie Shroff, Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar. Vijay Sethupathi, who had earlier confirmed his involvement in the film, is not seen in the trailer. The trailer showcases action sequences that appear to be significantly larger in scale than the first film. Nelson Dilipkumar, who established a distinctive visual style in Jailer that blended dark comedy with bursts of violence, appears to have amplified both elements for the sequel. The comedy, particularly between Rajinikanth and Yogi Babu, is prominently featured, suggesting the sequel will maintain the irreverent, crowd-pleasing tone that made the first film a phenomenon. Also Read If I do a cameo in Rajinikanths film, people wont even notice me Vijay Sethupathi Jailer, released on 2023, was a turning point for Rajinikanths commercial trajectory. After a string of underperforming films and a decade of inconsistent box office results, Jailer collected over Rs 600 crore worldwide and became the second-highest-grossing Tamil film of all time after 2.0 at the time of its release. Jailer 2 releases worldwide on October 15.

articleTitle: Gujarat courts at standstill as lawyers protest proposed Rent Bill
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lawyers take part in a protest rally against the Gujarat Rent Bill 2026, in Ahmedabad, Monday. (PTI Photo)
description: Change amounts to shifting judicial functions to executive, advocates say; Bar associations across state back protest called by Bar Council of Gujarat
body_raw: Courts across Gujarat were brought to a virtual standstill on Monday as lawyers launched an indefinite statewide strike against the proposed Gujarat Rent Bill-2026. The protest, led by the Bar Council of Gujarat BCG and supported by the bar associations across the state, followed three days of demonstrations that failed to produce a resolution. The Gujarat Bar Association subsequently called for an indefinite boycott of court work, while the Gujarat High Court Advocates Association GHCAA urged lawyers to stay away from court proceedings in support of the BCG. At the heart of the protest is a proposed change in the mechanism for deciding rental disputes. Under the proposed legislation, disputes arising from rent agreements would no longer be dealt with primarily by civil courts or Small Causes Courts. Instead, administrative authorities- including Mamlatdars, Deputy Collectors and Assistant Municipal Commissioners- would be empowered to adjudicate such disputes. Lawyers argue that the change amounts to shifting judicial functions to the executive. Hearings adjourned, litigants turned way The impact of the protest was felt immediately across the district courts as well as the Gujarat High Court. Private lawyers and advocates remained absent from every courtroom and hearings were adjourned. Lawyers gathered outside the respective courts, chanting slogans and demanding that the Bill be withdrawn. In Ahmedabad, lawyers took out a motorcycle rally from the City Civil and Sessions Court through the Metro Court and Gheekanta area while in Surat, thousands of lawyers continued their boycott, bringing court work to a halt for the fourth consecutive day. Litigants and parties arriving at the court were turned away from the main gate, causing considerable inconvenience. Lawyers know law better than MLAs Outside the Vadodara District Court, Baroda Bar Association President Hasmukh Bhatt said, We are Dharashastri Lawyers, and the elected representatives are Dharasabhya members of the Legislative Assembly. Lawyers know the law better than the members of the Legislative Assembly. the clear demand of all the lawyers of the Bar Associations is that the draft which has been sent to the state government for signature should first be taken back and amended. Only after that should the agitation be withdrawn. The Bill was drafted without discussing the matter with the Bar Council and the GHCAA. Gujarat High Court Advocates Association GHCAA president Senior Advocate Yatin Oza said that the association had abstained from work in support of the protest by the BCG. If lawyers are united, then no law can shake us, no action can shake us. We are standing with the Bar Council of Gujarat today. The public will also see what kind of action the government takes, because of which they are compelled to extend their support. Our support will certainly continue for two days, Oza said. Bhatt said moving a substantial category of litigation out of the civil courts could result in administrative delays. Our objection is not merely about jurisdiction, but about the nature of the forum in which citizens property and tenancy rights would be decided. revenue and municipal officials are not equipped in the same manner as judicial officers to assess complicated property documents, evidence and testimony. Moving a substantial category of litigation out of the civil courts could result in administrative delays rather than the speedy disposal promised by the proposed system, Bhatt argued. Fear of loss of livelihood There is a fear of loss of livelihood for lawyers as rental and tenancy disputes constitute a significant part of the work handled by lawyers in civil courts. The proposed transfer of rental disputes to executive authorities, bar associations contend, would substantially reduce the scope of civil litigation and affect the practice and income of advocates, particularly juniors.

articleTitle: ‘No.1 finish at Asian Games shows we are on the right track,’ says boxing coach Santiago Nieva
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Santiago
description: Indian women's boxing Head coach confident that India's boxers have the level to get Olympic qualifications in the World Championships
body_raw: With two gold and a bronze at the Asian Games, after five gold and a silver at the Commonwealth Games, womens boxing is on an upswing. The Asian Games haul was their best in the continental tournament, where India topped the medal table in womens boxing as well as the overall boxing pile three gold and as many bronze medals, edging out powerhouses like Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and China. Indian womens boxing Head coach Santiago Nieva talks to The Indian Express about the lessons from Japan, the gains and the challenges ahead. Excerpts How do you rate this Asian Games campaign? Obviously, we are super happy. We always want more, and we won two gold medals. Beforehand, there were very, very tough fights. We would end the year as the Asian Championship winner, and the number one in the CWG and Asian Games. Yes, we lost some of our top performers early, but overall we have never achieved results like this before. We have scored wins over stronger countries in Asia, like China, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. What was the biggest lesson from Japan? For me, the main thing is to control the bout for nine minutes, not only two good rounds and then lose our shape. We need to look at how we can achieve this as efficiently as possible. We have seen clear improvements. A boxer has to try, and have different variations and become a universal boxer. You should be able to handle different styles and types of opponents. If you are winning, you have more options and, if you are down in the score, you have fewer options. You need to increase the pace, box at a higher pace and need to slow it down when necessary as well. All these things sound easy in theory, but as you can see, sometimes emotions take over, and you dont make the best decisions. Thats what we aim to teach them. The biggest lesson is that we see that anything is possible. India ending up number one shows we are on the right track. On Parveen and Lovlina. Parveen was not part of the Asian Championships and then lost in the first bout in CWG. She had some doubts, and we had a relook at the way she boxed. She had a very tough draw with three very difficult bouts. But she stepped up every time. The main focus was to manage the distance and not to rush in attacks. Basically, her footwork improved, and she managed the bouts much better. For Lovlina, this gold is a confidence booster. She has achieved a lot in her career, but after the Paris Olympics and World Championships, there was some pressure. In Glasgow, she had been close to winning before she lost 2-3 in the final. We knew Lovlina had it in her to win the title, and she had to beat two world-class opponents, Natalya Bogdanova and Ziyi Bao. Preeti and Sakshi exited early, and Priya lost in the semis. How do you assess that? I am not worried about them. They had been consistent the whole year. They lost close bouts against world-class opponents. But they will definitely be back. In Sakshis case, her offensive boxing and medium-distance boxing need a bit of upgrading, so that she doesnt rely too much on her long-distance boxing. Its difficult to say about Preeti. She is an all-round boxer, and she is at a very good level. But usually, she can start a little faster, and thats something we need to work on. Priya is very young, and this is her first major competition year. So she has gained a lot of experience. She had been in many tough bouts, which she has come through. The only bout she has lost this year was in the semi-finals against Yang Chengyu, who she had beaten in Asian Championships. Sometimes, she loses her balance, and a little bit of concentration. With more experience, she will improve. What was the best bout, according to you? It has to be Parveens semi-final win against Navbakhor Khamidova. If we look at the Uzbeks record, she has beaten all other boxers, including Parveen. So you have some doubts. But when we trained, we had the belief that we could win. Then Parveen went into the bout and outclassed her. She managed the distance, she prepared her attacks and did not rush in. She kept a long distance when she attacked and did not fall in. The Uzbek ran out of ideas about how to attack Parveen. Thats the way we want to box. The World Championships next year will be the first competition offering LA Olympics quotas. How do you see the challenge? It will be a super tough competition, obviously. But I am confident we have the level to get qualifications at the World Championships. It will be a rehearsal for the Olympics too. Obviously, we have done well at the Asian level and the last Worlds too. We need to be able to control the different situations in our offensive and defensive boxing, when we are winning and when we are down. But the most important thing is understanding how to box in different distances, how to slow down and how to increase the pace, how to be effective in offensive boxing as well as defensive counterpunching boxing.

articleTitle: Ex-Bengaluru jail chief held for releasing lifer on fake Supreme Court order
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru prison official fake Supreme Court order
description: Shankar A Aradhya, who was serving a life sentence in a kidnapping case, was released from Bengaluru Central Prisons on November, 13, 2018.
body_raw: The police have arrested a former chief superintendent of Bengaluru Central Prisons for allegedly assisting in the release of a life convict by forging a Supreme Court order. M Narayana, Deputy Commissioner of Police Electronic City, announced the arrest of M Somashekar, who is now Deputy Inspector General Prisons, North Zone, Gulbarga, on Monday. In May, the current superintendent in-charge of the prison discovered that the release order submitted for the convict Shankar A Aradhya was fake and filed a police complaint. The police later found that Srikanth S, who was then a second-division assistant and is now a first-division assistant in the prisons Convict Prisoner Section, had forged a Supreme Court order dated November 2, 2018, to release Shankar. Based on the order, Shankar was released from the prison on November, 13, 2018. During the investigation, Shankars wife stated that Somashekar had also assisted in securing her husbands release. The police arrested both Srikanth and Shankars wife and they were remanded to judicial custody. However, Somashekar allegedly failed to cooperate with the investigation. He was produced before court and sent to police custody for further investigation till October 9. Who is Shankar A Aradhya? Shankar had been serving a life sentence in a 2001 kidnapping case registered by the Chickpet police. His appeals before the Karnataka High Court and later the Supreme Court were unsuccessful, with the sentence being upheld. Shankars wife, who had come in contact with Srikanth, allegedly managed to strike a deal to get her husband out. While Srikanth had sought Rs 12 lakh, she paid Rs 6 lakh and then Shankar came out of the prison using the forged Supreme Court order, a police officer said. Shankar was engaged in construction contracting, a business his father had also been involved in.

articleTitle: AC short circuit sparks Surat factory fire, firefighters recover diamonds worth lakhs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Within minutes, the flames intensified and the office was engulfed in dense black smoke, making it difficult to see or move inside the unit. (Express Photo)
description: According to officials of the Surat Municipal Corporation's Fire and Emergency Services Department, the fire broke out after a short circuit in the air conditioner in one of the polishing units of a diamond manufacturing factory.
body_raw: A fire that could have caused a loss running into lakhs was contained in time after Surat firefighters entered a smoke-filled diamond factory in Katargam and recovered diamonds worth more than Rs 50 lakh. The blaze, triggered by a short circuit in an air-conditioner, rapidly filled the unit with thick black smoke, forcing firefighters to enter wearing breathing apparatus to bring the flames under control and locate the valuables. According to officials of the Surat Municipal Corporations Fire and Emergency Services Department, the fire broke out after a short circuit in the air conditioner in one of the polishing units of a diamond manufacturing factory at Gangotri Tower near Kesar Ba Market in the Gotalawadi area of Katargam, one of Surats major diamond hubs. The sudden blaze sent panic through the premises as smoke quickly spread through the office. Within minutes, the flames intensified and the office was engulfed in dense black smoke, making it difficult to see or move inside the unit. Hitesh Thakur, Regional Fire Officer, Surat, told The Indian Express that the fire team reached the building soon after receiving the emergency call around 7.45 am on Monday. Five fire tenders from three fire stations were deployed for the operation. Thakur said that the smoke inside the office was so dense that the fire personnel equipped themselves with breathing apparatus sets before going inside. There had been a short circuit in the air conditioner and almost the entire room was charred. The workers vacated in a timely manner so no casualties occurred. Once the fire had been doused, the owner of the factory and the police accompanied fire personnel in order to recover the diamonds, Thakur said. He added that although an official value of the diamonds had not been calculated, with the help of the owner, the fire officials were able to retrieve gemstones from some of the work stations. The unit has partitions and since this fire was contained in one room, we were able to minimise the damage. There may have been gemstones misplaced while we were dousing the flames with water but we managed to retrieve several pieces from the work tables, Thakur said. The intensive firefighting and rescue operation, Thakur said, lasted around 45 minutes. The Katargam-Gotalawadi belt is densely populated with diamond-cutting, polishing and manufacturing units, making fire safety a recurring concern in the area. For the unit involved in Mondays incident, however, the rapid intervention of fire officials meant some of the assets inside were safely secured.

articleTitle: In dry Gujarat, traffic cop booked for drunk driving, suspended
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gujarat Police Sub-Inspector Bharat Venishankar Pandya suspended after being booked for drunk driving and crashing into Ahmedabad garbage heap
description: The 46-year-old S-I was booked after the incident happened around 11:45 pm on Sunday.
body_raw: A SUB-INSPECTOR S-I of the Gujarat Police was on Monday suspended from service after he was booked for allegedly driving while drunk and slammed into a garbage heap in Ahmedabad city. S-I Bharat Venishankar Pandya, who was posted as in-charge of the Vishala beat under M Division Traffic police station, was placed under suspension by the Assistant Commissioner ACP Traffic in connection with the FIR filed against him at Sabarmati police station, said a statement from Inspector U B Dhakhada. The 46-year-old S-I was booked after the incident happened around 1145 pm on Sunday. According to the FIR filed based on a complaint by a Head Constable of Sabarmati Police Station on behalf of the state, a personnel posted to a 112 patrolling vehicle informed about the incident. According to residents of Rabari vaas in Tragad Gam area, a white coloured Hyundai Creta veered into the garbage heap at the end of the lane. A crowd gathered at the spot where they noticed that the driver was allegedly in an inebriated condition. Upon checking the boot of the vehicle, they also found several sealed bottles of liquor there, after which they informed the police. When police checked the vehicle, they found nine sealed bottles of Indian Made Foreign Liquor IMFL. S-I Pandya was booked under section 661b of the Liquor Prohibition Act as well as under section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

articleTitle: Odds back Can Xue, pattern a woman: All about 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nobel Prize in Literature 2026: Composite portrait of three women writers on a dark background: a woman with grey hair in a topknot and dark-rimmed glasses resting her chin on her hand; an older woman with curly grey hair, a pink beaded necklace and a headset microphone; and a woman with shoulder-length dark hair, glasses and a maroon scarf over a white top.
description: Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 will be announced on October 8 at 4.30 pm IST. Can Xue leads the odds; Rushdie at 25/1. Prize money, process and more.
body_raw: Will it be Can Xue, the Chinese writer known for her experimental fiction, perennial favourite Haruki Murakami, or a writer of Indian or South Asian descent? The question, which has occupied literary circles for months, will be answered on October 8, when the Swedish Academy announces the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. When and where to watch The Swedish Academy will announce the prize on Thursday, October 8, at 4.30 pm IST 1 pm in Stockholm at the earliest. The announcement will be streamed live on the Nobel Prizes official website and social media channels. Who are the frontrunners According to the British betting site Ladbrokes, Can Xue is the favourite at 101, followed by Haruki Murakami Japan at 141, Gerald Murnane Australia and Thomas Pynchon US at 161, and Cristina Rivera Garza Mexico, Enrique Vila-Matas Spain, Lidia Jorge Portugal, Ludmila Ulitskaya Russia, Margaret Atwood Canada and Michel Houellebecq France at 20 Bookmakers have no inside information, but they are not always wrong. Last years winner, Lszlo Krasznahorkai, fluctuated between 61 and 101 across various betting markets. Who is Can Xue? Deng Xiaohua, who goes by the pen name Can Xue, has appeared on bookmakers lists for years. She was tied with Lszlo Krasznahorkai, who won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature, at 101 on Ladbrokes. The 73-year-old author is known for experimental fiction, including dreamlike, stream-of-consciousness prose that defies conventional plot. Her writing has been likened to Franz Kafka and Jorge Luis Borges. Her best-known books in English areThe Last Lover, which won the US Best Translated Book Award in 2015 Love in the New Millennium, which was longlisted for the International Booker in 2019 and I Live in the Slums,which was longlisted in 2021. Is this her year? Since 2018, the prize has alternated between women and men, ending with Krasznahorkai. If that pattern holds, which the Academy is under no obligation to keep, the 2026 winner would be a woman. Patterns over the last decade Over the past decade four of the 10 laureates were women six wrote in a language other than English six were European one was from Asia South Koreas Han Kang, in 2024 none from South Asia Is there an Indian or South Asian contender? This year, the best-placed writers of South Asian origin are Salman Rushdie, 251 One of the worlds most famous writers, Rushdie was the target of a fatwa issued by Irans Ayatollah Khomeini in 1989 over his book, The Satanic Verses. Thirty-three years later, in August 2022, he was stabbed during a speaking engagement in New York. He won the 1981 Booker for Midnights Children, and is credited with bringing magic realism into Indian writing in English. His latest book is The Eleventh Hour 2025, and a documentary on the attack, which left him blind in one eye, was released this year. Michael Ondaatje, 251 With the same odds as Rushdie, Ondaatje was born in Colombo in 1943 and shared the 1992 Booker for The English Patient. He is known for lyrical, fragmented narratives that blend poetry with history. His latest book is a poetry anthology, The Distance of a Shout 2026. Ananda Devi, 401 A Mauritian writer of Indian descent who writes in French. Devi is known for her unsparing portraits of women confined within tradition and her depiction of fractured identities. She won the 2024 Neustadt Prize her latest book is Chronicle of a Lost Kingdom 2026. Amitav Ghosh, 501 Of late, the Kolkata-born author is known for his writings on climate change. He is the author of the Ibis trilogy, beginning with Sea of Poppies, and The Great Derangement. His latest book is Ghost-Eye 2026. Has an Indian ever won? Only once. Rabindranath Tagore won in 1913 and was the first Asian laureate. Two other winners have Indian links Rudyard Kipling, born in Bombay, won in 1907, and V S Naipaul, a Trinidad-born British writer of Indian descent, won in 2001. Does a Booker help? While the Nobel Prize honours a writers whole body of work, the Booker rewards a single novel written in English, and the International Booker rewards a single book translated into English. Even so, the two lists overlap. Five authors-V S Naipaul, Nadine Gordimer, William Golding, J M Coetzee, and Kazuo Ishiguro - who won the Booker Prize, and four who won the International Booker Prize-Alice Munro, Lszlo Krasznahorkai, Han Kang, and Olga Tokarczuk- have won the Nobel Prize. Abdulrazak Gurnah, the 2021 laureate, was shortlisted for the Booker in 1994 for Paradise. Interestingly, Rushdies Midnights Children won the prize in 1981. It was later named the Booker of Bookers in 1993 and the Best of the Booker in 2008 Ondaatjes The English Patient shared the 1992 prize and won the Golden Man Booker in 2018. A Booker is not a guarantee. For instance, Doris Lessing was shortlisted several times without winning, and won the Nobel in 2007. The favourite, Can Xue, was longlisted for the International Booker in 2019 and 2021, while Amitav Ghosh was shortlisted in 2008 for Sea of Poppies. How is the winner chosen? Each September, the Academy invites qualified people to nominate. They include members of the Swedish Academy and similar academies professors of literature and linguistics former laureates heads of national writers organisations Writers cannot nominate themselves. In April, the Nobel Committee picks 1520 preliminary candidates, then narrows them to five in May. The Academys 18 members vote, and whoever gets more than half the votes wins. Will we ever know who was nominated? The Academy publishes no longlist or shortlist, and it doesnt tell nominees they are under consideration. Nomination records are sealed for 50 years, so this years nominations will only open in 2076. Several Indians have been nominated, according to the Nobel archive, including philosopher Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, repeatedly from 1933 to 1962 Sri Aurobindo, in 1943 Bengali novelist Tarashankar Bandyopadhyay, from 1971 to 1973 R K Narayan, from 1974 How much does the winner get? This year, the winner will receive SEK 12 million, about 12 crore, up from SEK 11 million in 2025. The prize will be presented in Stockholm on December 10.

articleTitle: Maharashtra SIR in Bombay HC: Hearing deferred by 3 weeks over Supreme Court proceedings
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Maharashtra SIR bombay high court
description: The High Court said it could not hold a parallel hearing to decide whether to pass an interim order to the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding the Maharashtra voters list and the SIR process
body_raw: The Bombay High Court has deferred the hearing on a writ petition over the Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise in Maharashtra by three weeks after it was told that the Supreme Court SC will hear a plea on the issue on October 8. During the hearing on Monday, the High Court said it could not hold a parallel hearing to decide whether to pass an interim order to the Election Commission of India ECI regarding the Maharashtra voters list and the SIR process. A bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna was hearing a writ petition by two Mumbai residents, including Sagar Ramesh Gawai, youth president of the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi VBA, that raised concerns over the collection of documents during enumeration and voter exclusion based on uncollectible status. The plea also sought direction to specify criteria for polling station rationalisation and ECINET specifications. Senior advocate Ashutosh Kumbhakoni, representing the EC, told the High Court bench that the Supreme Court was already dealing with legal challenges to the SIR and had requested the High Courts not to decide on these issues for the time being, as per its November 2025 order. The next Supreme Court hearing in the matter has been scheduled for October 8. Advocate Prakash Ambedkar, representing the petitioners, has, however, argued that the Supreme Court ruling was limited to the SIR and citizenship in Bihar and that the present plea was totally different. Ambedkar argued that until the final decision on the present plea, Maharashtras electoral roll should not be disturbed, as nearly 2 crore voters would be deleted from the list It is true that Maharashtra is not listed there the SC ruling, so you can argue on a limited aspect, but as far as the broader issue is concerned, if the SC is hearing it, then there is no need for a parallel hearing. October 8 is not far., CJ Tripathi remarked orally. Ambedkar has sought an interim direction that no voters be deleted in Maharashtra in the meantime. We are not hearing a PIL. This is a writ petition. A request has been made by the SC, and how can the HC proceed despite that? How can we stop it, and how can this interim direction be done? the bench orally responded, and, on a request by the ECI lawyer, posted the hearing after three weeks.

articleTitle: Legislative privileges vs free speech: The question before Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court
description: At the heart of the case is whether legislative privileges, special powers and immunities enjoyed by Parliament and state legislatures, under Articles 105 and 194, can override fundamental rights under Article 19.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Tuesday October 6 will begin hearing a long-pending reference on the scope of legislative privileges, special powers and immunities enjoyed by Parliament and state legislatures to protect their functioning, and whether they can be invoked against citizens, journalists and others on breaching the privileges of the House. At the heart of the case is whether these privileges, under Articles 105 and 194 of the Constitution, can override fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and expression under Article 19. A seven-judge Constitution Bench comprising the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Chandrashekhar and V Mohana will hear the matter. Legal framework Article 1943 of the Constitution grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. Article 191a guarantees freedom of speech and expression, including press freedom. The case turns on the interplay between these two rights and whether legislative privilege can override the right to free speech. The petitioners contend that such a privilege exists to protect the functioning of the House, not to shield it from scrutiny. Articles 14 and 21 provide for the right to equality and the right to life. The petitioners argue that when legislatures order arrests or imprisonment for alleged breaches of privilege, they affect personal liberty. According to them, any action affecting liberty must satisfy constitutional guarantees of fairness, due process and protection against arbitrariness. History of the challenge to legislative privileges In 2003, The Hindu reported on sharp exchanges between Tamil Nadu Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa and the Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly. Speaker K Kalimuthu objected to those reports and referred them to a Privileges Committee, saying the descriptions were contrary to truth and had affected the privileges of the legislature. The controversy widened after The Hindu published an editorial titled Rising Intolerance, which criticised the crude use of state power against various sections including political opponents and the independent media shows a contempt for the democratic spirit that is deeply disturbing. It further stated that legislative privilege exists to protect its free and independent functioning and not to protect the reputation of the government or of individual members. A Tamil translation published by Murasoli was also referred to the Committee. The Assembly ultimately held five journalists of The Hindu and Murasoli editor S Selvam guilty of gross contempt and breach of privilege, sentencing them to 15 days imprisonment and issuing arrest warrants. Police teams were deployed across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Delhi to execute the warrants. The journalists approached the Supreme Court, which immediately intervened and stayed the warrants. The court, however, referred the matter to a Constitution Bench, observing that substantial questions of law as to the interpretation of Articles 1943 and 191a, the interplay between these two articles.are involved. Supreme Court precedents The reference came about because of two conflicting Constitution Bench decisions. In 1959, the Supreme Court, in a 41 majority, in Pandit M.S.M. Sharma v. Sri Krishna Sinha also known as the Searchlight case held that Assembly privileges under Article 1943 included the power to prohibit publication. It said that because Article 191a is a general provision and Article 1943 is a special provision, free speech must yield to legislative privilege. If, therefore, the Legislative Assembly has the powers, privileges and immunities of the House of Commons and if the petitioner is eventually deprived of his personal liberty as a result of the proceedings before the Committee of Privileges, such deprivation will be in accordance with procedure established by law and the petitioner cannot complain of the breach, actual or threatened, of his Fundamental Right under Art. 21. However, in 1964, in the Special Reference No. 1 of 1964 Keshav Singhs case, the Uttar Pradesh Assembly jailed a citizen, Keshav Singh, distributing pamphlets accusing an MLA of corruption. When the Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail, the Assembly ordered that the two judges who passed the order, the lawyer and Keshav Singh himself, be brought before the House in custody. While a Full Bench of the High Court stayed those arrest warrants, the President referred the dispute to the Supreme Court. The seven-judge bench held that Constitutional courts could examine the legality of detention ordered in privilege proceedings, and that legislatures could not proceed against judges and lawyers for performing their duties. The court said that the Searchlight case did not lay down a universal rule that Part III fundamental rights a reference to Part III of the Constitution - Articles 12-35 - guaranteeing the fundamental rights of citizens and individuals always yield to legislative privileges. It said Therefore, we do not think it would be right to read the majority decision as laying down a general proposition that whenever there is a conflict between the provisions of the latter part of Article 1943 and any of the provisions of the fundamental rights guaranteed by Part III, the latter must always yield to the former. The Supreme Courts approach to legislative privilege has evolved over the years. In 1954, it ordered the release of the editor of the news weekly Blitz, who had been detained under the Uttar Pradesh Assembly Speakers warrant, after finding that he had not been produced before the magistrate within 24 hours. In Raja Ram Pal 2007, arising from the cash-for-query sting, the court upheld Parliaments expulsion of 11 MPs but held that the exercise of parliamentary privilege is subject to judicial review. In Amarinder Singh 2010, the court quashed the Punjab Assemblys expulsion of the former Chief Minister, saying that privilege cannot be used to punish conduct unrelated to the functioning of the House. Most recently, in the 2024 Sita Soren case, a seven-judge bench overruled P V Narasimha Rao 1998, in which the court had granted immunity to MPs accused of taking bribes to vote, holding that bribery is not protected by the Constitution. What the petitioners are arguing The petitioners argue that the Assemblys action violated free speech, personal liberty, and basic principles of natural justice. They contend that honest and courageous reporting by the press is the bedrock of parliamentary democracy and that journalists cannot perform their role in an atmosphere of fear and terror. They further argue that legislative privileges are subject to Article 21 and that permitting a legislature to deprive a person of liberty by mere passing of a resolution would be an anathema to the Constitution. The petitioners also argue that privileges exist to protect the functioning of the House, not the government, stating that there is no concept of any parliamentary privilege being applicable to a Chief Minister. or to a government and that privileges are not intended to protect the fame and reputation of the ruling party. Multiple intervenors have filed applications in the matter, including the stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra, the journalist Ajit Anjum, and former CPIM MP Subhashini Ali. In her application, Ali argues that parliamentary privilege is functional in character and exists to protect legislative deliberation, not to insulate legislators from scrutiny by citizens or the press. Criticism of a legislature, she says, even where stringent, severe, disputed or inconvenient cannot by itself amount to contempt unless it directly obstructs the Houses functioning. Journalist Ajit Anjum, meanwhile, argues that Indias constitution is based on constitutional supremacy, not British-style parliamentary sovereignty therefore, legislative privilege remains subject to constitutional limitations. He has also urged the court to reconsider the 1959 Searchlight ruling, arguing that restrictions on accurate reporting can have a chilling effect on the freedom of the press in an era of live broadcasts, digital publishing and social media.

articleTitle: Mayawati’s flip-flop: Nephew Akash Anand back a month after being sacked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mayawati announced reinduction of Akash four days after he apologised to BSP supremo seeking another chance to serve the party. (File Photo)
description: Three days ago, Akash had publicly apologised to Mayawati, calling her Bua Maa
body_raw: A month after Mayawati removed nephew Akash Anand from BSPs national convener post, saying he needs to be more mature for significant responsibilities, the party supremo on Monday reinstated him, replacing his younger brother Ishan. The BSP chiefs latest flip-flop comes days after Akash apologised to Mayawati in a social media post on October 2, calling her Bua Maa and seeking a second chance to serve the party. In a long post in Hindi on X, Mayawati on Monday said there have been some reasons concerning Akash in recent days due to which necessary changes in the party organization had to be made several times and ultimately, his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, was also compelled to retire from politics. Since then, people have been observing changes in Akashs personality, work style, and so on-evidence of which was a post he recently wrote on X regarding his return to the party, Mayawati stated, referring to her nephews public apology. The BSP chief added that most people in the party believed that Akash should be given the opportunity to resume work in the party along with his previously assigned responsibilities, for which his father, as well as his younger brother Ishan, have also expressed their consent. According to Mayawati, Akashs brother, Ishan, has expressed his wish to continue working as a worker. She said that Ishan, demonstrating his missionary spirit, stated that he would carry out any work assigned to him, without holding any party post, with complete honesty and devotion. In such a situation, after much deliberation, the party is now giving Akash Anand the opportunity to work in the party once again by reappointing him as the National Coordinator National Convener of the BSP in the interest of the party and the movement. It is hoped that, following Ashok Siddharths retirement from politics, everything in the party will now proceed smoothly and properly, and repeated changes in the party organization will not be necessary, although this will depend considerably on Akash Anand as well, Mayawati said, cautioning Akash once again. On September 3, Mayawati had removed Akash from the party posts, saying he needs to be more mature and that it would be inappropriate to assign him significant responsibilities at this point. A week later, Mayawati asked Akashs father-in-law Ashok Siddharth to retire from politics in the interest of the political future of his son-in-law as well as the BSP. A day later, she also completely freed Akash from the party. Later, Mayawati on September 12 announced her antim faisla final decision that neither of her two nephews, Akash and Ishan, will engage in politics by holding any party position. But soon took another U-turn, announcing Ishan as the new national convener of the party. On October 2, Akash, in a post on X, referred to Mayawati as Buaa Maa and described her as his political guru and inspiration. He backed her decision to expel his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, and sought an apology, explaining that his past silence on the issue was misunderstood. At that time, I had distanced myself from social media, so I was unable to repost your post. My silence at that time was misunderstood, and it gave space to rumours. If this has hurt you, I apologise for that, he wrote. Sources said that Akash met Mayawati in Lucknow on September 29 to apologise and then publicly apologised with a post on social media on October 2. The ongoing development marks the latest chapter in Akashs eventful relationship with his aunt over the past two years. He was projected as her political heir ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. However, in May 2024, after being booked for allegedly promoting enmity during a public rally in Sitapur ahead of the Lok Sabha election, Mayawati removed her nephew as BSPs national coordinator and withdrew her earlier declaration naming him as political heir. He was also barred from campaigning. Giving him a second chance, Mayawati in June 2024 reinstated Akash as national coordinator and again named him her successor. In March 2025, however, Akash was expelled from the party. Two months later, the decision was reversed. The party appointed him chief national coordinator and, in August 2025, elevated him to the post of national convenor.

articleTitle: India-US trade deal stuck? Sitharaman says give-and-take ‘very difficult’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nirmala Sitharaman said that the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US is that the trade balance is in India’s favour. (PTI Photo)
description: A few days ago, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that signing the deal is not “imminent” as both countries have identified a “universe of items that are sticking points”.
body_raw: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said that the India-US trade deal talks have hit a plateau, beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. This comes days after United States Trade Representative USTR Jamieson Greer said that signing the deal is not imminent as both countries have identified a universe of items that are sticking points. India-US trade relations are undergoing a fresh challenge ever since US President Donald Trump signed into law the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, giving him the authority to impose tariffs up to 100 on countries, including India and China, that continue buying Russian oil and gas. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has been in the US since September 29 for the G20 Trade ministers meet and bilateral trade deal negotiations. One thing about the US agreement, which is yet to be finalised, is that its been a hard and very rigorously negotiated agreement. The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although wed like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are room to operate from, both sides could do it, Sitharaman said at the Munich Security Conference MSC here. Sitharaman said that the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US is that the trade balance is in Indias favour, adding that India is facing a steep imbalance in its trade with China. Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies.now, the imbalance has been sought to be addressed through other means, where .. tariff has become weaponised. Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, Sitharaman said. The Finance Ministry in its latest Monthly Economic Review had noted that trade relations with the United States remain unsettled with the passage of the Graham Bill through the Congress and its Presidential assent. A day after meeting Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, Greer had said the talks were constructive and that India and the US were in their final phase. At the same time, I dont think theres something imminent, but we truly have identified the universe of items that are sticking points. Were working diligently toward them. My sense is that the president, the Prime Minister, may have another call, very soon on this, just to assess progress in where we are, Greer said at a press briefing Friday. Apart from the Russia-related tariffs, India is also awaiting a decision on an investigation launched by the US under yet another tariff mechanism - Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The investigation is expected to establish if India has excess industrial capacity and is hurting American companies with its output. The first set of Section 301 tariffs resulted in 10 tariffs. With the new set of Section 301 tariffs expected to come in, Indian exporters have said that the uncertainty is changing the nature of orders coming from the US. US buyers are no longer placing bulk orders and are diversifying imports. This could mean lower export orders for Indian businesses in the long term till the deal is not signed.

articleTitle: India vs Uruguay: Can the Blue Tigers build on lessons from Brazil match?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India's players pose for a group photo before the international friendly soccer match against Brazil in Kolkata, India, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Bikas Das)
description: India will look to build on the lessons from their Brazil clash when they take on two-time world champions Uruguay in Kolkata, with Khalid Jamil’s side facing another stern South American test.
body_raw: A few fans were loitering around the Salt Lake Stadium ticket counters on Monday, a day ahead of Indias match against Uruguay. The scene was markedly different from before the Brazil match, when the same counters had been largely empty. The much-anticipated Brazil game also failed to sell out, with swathes of empty seats visible during the match. With ticket sales for the Uruguay match also struggling, the All India Football Federation appeared to have taken note. A couple of days before the match, the federation announced that tickets for some blocks had been slashed by 90, with seats that once cost Rs 1,999 coming down to Rs 199. In addition, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that people who had bought tickets for the Lionel Messi GOAT Tour last December but were deprived of seeing their star because of the events organisational chaos would receive free tickets for the India-Uruguay international. Kolkata giants Mohun Bagan, East Bengal as well as Mohammedan FC also announced complimentary tickets for their members and supporters. Since these measures were taken, a lot of stands showed as sold out in the matchs official ticketing app. The Uruguay match was always going to be a harder sell than Brazil. The South American team does not have a so-called superstar in its squad who commands the same recognition among casual Indian football fans. One big name who could perhaps have helped ticket sales was Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde, but he was ruled out ahead of the tour due to injury. That left Uruguay with names such as Darwin Nunez and Ronald Araujo, world-class players in their own right, but not quite as familiar to Indian fans. Their coach, Diego Forln, though, is a much more familiar name to Indians, having played for Mumbai City in the Indian Super League. The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner took over this Uruguay side after their disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, where they failed to win a single match and were eliminated in the group stage under Marcelo Bielsa. Since then, they have lost to Japan but thrashed South Korea 4-1, with Nunez bagging a brace. Next up is 138th-ranked India, a relatively straightforward match on paper. Forlan, however, did not agree. Theres never an easy game in football. We will try to do our best and enjoy our game tomorrow, he said at the pre-match press conference on Monday. He also had praise for the Blue Tigers, lauding them for their performance against Brazil. You could see some combinations, some long balls, some good players. If you give them time and space, they can damage you, and they can play well. So, you have to respect everybody, he said. While Uruguay are not as unfamiliar an opponent as Brazil, with the two sides having met twice, their last meeting came way back in 2001 and was not an official FIFA friendly. Uruguay remain two-time World Cup winners and the 20th-ranked team in the world. The heady days of Luis Suarez, Forlan and Edinson Cavani may be behind them, but this side in transition still has enough quality to hurt any opposition. Former Liverpool striker Nunez is in good form, while former Barcelona defender Araujo and former Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira remain more than capable of holding their own in defence and midfield, respectively. India, meanwhile, want to take lessons from the Brazil game forward and use them against Uruguay. Not conceding an early goal is important. We have to go with the flow, but we are going to play against a good team. One mistake can cost us really badly, so we have to be very careful and not take this match lightly at all. They are a good team, attacking-wise and defensively. They have experienced players and their coach is also one of the best. We have to be careful in all aspects, coach Khalid Jamil said.

articleTitle: British Airways BA295 drops 28,000 feet over Ireland, declares emergency
articleFeaturedImageAlt: british airways flight BA 295 emergency landing
description: British Airways London-Chicago flight BA295 Emergency Landing: A British Airways flight from London to Chicago declared a midair emergency after reportedly dropping 28,000 feet, forcing the aircraft to return to Heathrow.
body_raw: British Airways BA Flight BA295 made a U-turn back to the UK just an hour into its journey from London to Chicago on Monday, according to flight tracking data. BA said the flight made a safe landing back at London Heathrow following a technical issue, with passengers disembarking the aircraft. The safety of our customers and crew is always our top priority, and the aircraft landed safely after our highly-trained pilots returned to Heathrow following a technical issue, said a BA spokesperson. Customers disembarked the aircraft normally and our teams are working to get their travel plans back on track as quickly as possible, the spokesperson said. Earlier, the flight BA 295 was diverted back to Heathrow International Airport, cancelling its planned journey to the United States after plunging 28,000 feet and declaring an emergency, data from flight-tracking website Flightradar24 showed. British Airways declared the emergency midair following a sudden and steep descent while flying over Ireland. The British Airways flight, operated by a Boeing 777-200ER and registered as G-VIIA, departed from Heathrow Airports Terminal 5 at 1150 am on Monday local time with a scheduled flight time of 8 hours and 40 minutes and was heading to Chicago OHare International Airport ORD. BA295 from London to Chicago squawking 7700 and descended down to 9000 feet above Ireland. - Flightradar24 flightradar24 October 5, 2026 Nearly an hour after takeoff, the plane had reached a cruising altitude of 37,000 feet when the BA 295 started facing an unexpected operational issue, UK news outlets reported. It added that the plane witnessed a steep descent when it was flying over Ireland, and flight tracking data show the aircraft plunging rapidly to around 9,000 feet.

articleTitle: Nobel Medicine Prize 2026: How three scientists discovered a way to control brain cells with light
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel are shown on the screen as they are awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (AP/PTI)
description: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries that laid the foundation of optogenetics — a technique that lets scientists switch specific cells on and off using light.
body_raw: The Nobel Prize in Physiology and Medicine for 2026 was jointly awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their discovery of an algae protein that react to light and its use as a switch to study the functions of nerve cells. Their explorations led to the creation of a new field of study called optogenetic, which may finally help scientists understand how the brain forms memories, feelings and behaviours. We were able to precisely pace the heart and look at the effects that different heart rates have on brain states. Communication across the body, from the body to the brain, but with the precision of a gain of function in a peripheral organ allowing us to see the effects on brain and behavioural state . this ability to execute a precision intervention in one organ and read out the effects in complex behaviours - this is something that people have wanted for a long time to be able to do, said Deisseroth. In simple terms, they found a way to control cells with light. Imagine that the brain is a vast electrical network containing billions of tiny cells called neurons. These neurons communicate by sending electrical signals, allowing us to move, see, remember, feel pain and experience emotions. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel helped scientists develop a remarkable way of controlling these electrical signals using light. Their research led to the discovery and development of light-sensitive proteins, called opsins, that can be placed in specific cells. When light is shone on those cells, the proteins act like tiny switches, turning the cells activity on or off. This technology is known as optogenetics - essentially, using light to control genetically modified cells. What is optogenetics? It is basically a field of research that uses light to manipulate the activity of neurons or other types of cells and study the resulting effects. This is done by expressing the light-sensitive protein in the targeted cells. Within the brain, it has contributed towards identifying neural circuits responsible for sense of pain, social behaviours, thirst, food consumption, reward and attention or the understanding of how memories are created. How did the discipline evolve? Interestingly, the field rests on a theory proposed by Francis Crick, the molecular biologist who was behind the discovery of and was awarded the Nobel prize for the double helix structure of DNA. He envisioned activating individual nerve cells in a brain to investigate the mechanisms that underlie human consciousness. With nerve signals being extremely rapid, he realised it would only be possible if scientists were somehow able to manipulate the nerve cells with light. He himself admitted that the idea sounded far-fetched. But it was made possible by the work of Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel on the alga Chlamydomonas. These are famous for their ability to quickly swim towards a light. Hegemann found that it reacted extremely quickly, within half a millisecond after the light reached a tiny orange dot called eyespot that the alga used to detect light. To compare, it takes 10 milliseconds for the human eye to react to light. Hegemann wondered how could the response to light be more than twenty times faster in Chlamydomonas? He hypothesised that a single protein complex both captured light and acted on it in the alga as opposed to the multi-step process in the human eye. Yet, finding this protein was a challenge because when the proteins in the algal eyespot were removed from their natural setting, they became unstable and easily damaged. This is when he discovered that Japanese researchers had mapped the DNA of Chlamydomonas, among which were the codes for two genes that had similarities to light-capturing proteins. Enter Nagel. He used egg cells of frogs to express the two proteins and confirm that Hegemanns hypothesis was actually correct. The alga detected and reacted to light using the protein channelrhodopsin-2 ChR-2. They then introduced the cells in different types of cells and found that they all became light sensitive. Karl Deisseroth found that ChR-2 could control the activity of specific nerve cells in the manner proposed by Francis Crick. He used it to control rat nerve cells in a petri dish and later in the rats. With Deisseroths lab at the forefront, researchers soon found more proteins that can turn nerve cells on and off, and which are activated by different wavelengths of light.
