How does it help to study the brain? Imagine the brain to be a building with lots and lots of rooms - now there was no way for us to know what happens if the light is switched on in just one room. Optogenetics has given us an extremely powerful way to switch on and off the neurons and see what happens. It has allowed us to manipulate nerve cells and study its effects with unprecedented level of precision. It has completely changed the scale at which discoveries are happening in neurosciences, said Vidita Vaidya, senior professor at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. While optogenetics is still largely used in the laboratories to see which set of neurons regulate what type of behaviour in animals - it helps us look into the black box, she says - it is still ways away from therapies to help those with spinal cord paralysis. Dr Sanjeev Kumar Mahto, professor at IIT BHU, said it has allowed scientists to see the functions of the brain and enhance the understanding of what causes certain conditions. Deisseroths research group introduced the gene for ChR-2 in 2006 and successfully used a light to activate neurons to control movements of the mouse whiskers.The same year he used the technique to wake sleeping mice by manipulating a recently discovered type of nerve cell that was suspected to control wakefulness. His team also studied the brains of mice as they experienced fear, and noted which nerve cells appeared to form the memory. When they later reactivated these nerve cells, the mice showed signs of fear, despite not being in danger at the time. What kind of therapies are being developed based on this field? There are ongoing clinical trials on restoring vision in people who have become blind due to retinitis pigmentosa, a disease that destroys the eyes rods and cones. Using special glasses emitting light, the person was able to discern and grasp objects on a table. There are also hopes that optogenetics could improve cochlea implants. Currently, these implants stimulate the auditory nerve using electricity.

articleTitle: Beyond Mughal monuments & ghats: UP putting lesser-known sites on tourism map
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tulsidas birthplace, Chitrakoot
description: 97 such projects worth Rs 1,425 crore taken up in 35 districts of the state from 2021 to 2026, say officials
body_raw: Uttar Pradesh is increasingly expanding its tourism map beyond established destinations. From the temple town of Bateshwar in Agra district and Munshi Premchands birthplace, Lamhi near Varanasi to the Buddhist sites in Maharajganj and Gorakhgiri Parvat in Mahoba, the state government is turning its attention to lesser-known tourism sites - places with religious, historical, literary, cultural or natural significance but limited presence on the mainstream tourist itineraries. Between 2021 and 2026, at least 97 such projects worth around Rs 1,425 crore were taken up across 35 districts of the state, officials said. The focus is on developing these sites and linking them with existing tourist circuits, rather than concentrating the tourism activity around a handful of established destinations, in an attempt to encourage longer stays and greater local economic activity, they added. They maintained that since Agras tourism identity has long been dominated by its Mughal monuments, Bateshwar offers another aspect - a temple settlement along the Yamuna river which is also associated with the ancestral roots of former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The effort is aimed at giving the visitors to Agra another reason to travel beyond the established Mughal circuit and explore a part of the district with a distinct religious and cultural identity. For this, more than Rs 200 crore is being invested in nine projects there, covering the temple complex, heritage conservation, kunds, ghats, lighting and visitor facilities, it is learnt. Varanasi adds literary and Jain heritage In Varanasi, the tourism focus is being extended beyond the Ganga river and major temples. At Lamhi, the ancestral house of Munshi Premchand is being developed as a museum, bringing the citys literary heritage into its tourism circuit. At Chandravati, a project worth more than Rs 17 crore is being developed at the birthplace of the eighth Jain Tirthankar, Chandraprabhu. In Amethi, around Rs 35 crore is being spent to develop the sites associated with Jains, and Guru Gorakhnaths Taposthali and the literary legacy of Malik Mohammad Jayasi. In Chitrakoot, projects at Maharishi Valmiki Ashram in Lalapur, Tulsidass birthplace in Rajapur and Sri Ram Vatika Eco Park near Ganesh Bagh are intended to expand the tourism circuit beyond Ramghat and Kamadgiri. In Prayagraj, Nishadraj Park at Shringverpur is being developed around the traditional association of Lord Ram with Nishadraj. In Maharajganj district, development at Ramgram and Devdah is aimed at bringing attention to sites associated with Buddhism. Officials said such destinations require not only infrastructure but also better interpretation, connectivity and digital information to explain their significance and link them with established Buddhist circuits such as Sarnath, Kushinagar and Shravasti. Chyavan Rishi to Vedic traditions At Gugrapur in Kannauj district, Rs 81.35 lakh Chyavan Rishi Ashram project is being developed around the traditions associated with Sage Chyavan. At Naimisharanya in Sitapur, the Rs 14.09 crore Vedaranyam project will have zones inspired by the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda, along with medicinal planting, yoga, contemplation, music and traditional learning. In Mahoba district, the Gorakhgiri Parvat is being developed around its association with Guru Gorakhnath, while the Sun Temple Interpretation Centre has been planned to bring together heritage, archaeology, yogic traditions and astronomy. A proposed planetarium is expected to add an educational component to the project. In Gorakhpur, two projects worth nearly Rs 47 crore have been taken up at the birthplace of Paramhansa Yogananda, whose writings helped popularise yoga and Indian spirituality internationally. Local suggestions drive development The state is also using local suggestions to identify sites for tourism development. Under the Chief Minister Tourism Development Partnership Scheme, MPs, MLAs, local bodies, trusts, institutions and other eligible participants can propose religious, historical, cultural and natural sites. Projects costing between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 5 crore can receive the Tourism Departments support for up to half of the eligible cost. Tourism and Culture Minister Jaiveer Singh said the states tourism identity should reflect the breadth of its history and traditions. Every district has places closely connected with its people, traditions and history, but many of them remained outside organised tourism because their stories were not presented and essential visitor facilities were missing, Singh said. The expansion of tourism to lesser-known destinations also brings a challenge infrastructure does not automatically create sustained visitor demand. Connectivity, accommodation, trained guides, local businesses, cleanliness, safety and credible interpretation would be important for these destinations to develop as sustainable tourism centres, the officials said. The government is also looking at digital tools to make such places easier to discover. Additional Chief Secretary, Tourism, Culture and Religious Affairs, Amrit Abhijat, said verified digital information, mapping, thematic itineraries, QR-based interpretation and multilingual content could help travellers discover lesser-known destinations. The larger test for the governments plan will be whether visitors coming to established destinations begin adding these lesser-known sites to their itineraries - turning them from individual development projects into functioning tourism circuits.

articleTitle: Karnataka SIR chief vows probe into bulk voter-deletion pleas, silent on FIRs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka SIR Form 7 row
description: The police have booked booth-level agents for allegedly filing Form-7 applications fraudulently to delete voters from electoral rolls.
body_raw: Following multiple complaints of bulk Form-7 application submissions allegedly intended to disenfranchise voters mostly from the Muslim community, Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer CEO V Anbukumar said Monday that action would be taken as per the law. The Electoral Registration Officer ERO will take action after an inquiry. Action will be taken as per law. ERO has to take action at his level, the CEO said, adding that a discussion was held with district election officers about bulk filing of Form-7 applications. The exact number of Form-7 applications submitted by the September 24 deadline is unavailable because it appears on the dashboard only after data entry is done, Anbukumar added. Anbukumar refused to comment on FIRs registered against the Opposition BJPs booth-level agents BLAs for allegedly filing fraudulent Form-7 applications. The police have filed multiple FIRs since September 30 against BLAs who filed Form-7 applications in constituencies such as Bhalki, Bableshwar, Belgaum Uttar, Ballari and other places. Incidents of mass submission of Form-7 applications, which appear to have been auto-populated, were also reported in various places across the state. On Monday, former Jayanagar MLA Sowmya Reddy filed a police complaint alleging that over 4,300 names were deleted in her constituency. She alleged that one Lokesh did this at the behest of BJP MLA C K Ramamurthy. Also on Monday, BJP leader Dr Ravi Patil, who was booked by the Belagavi police for allegedly filing false Form-7 applications, secured anticipatory bail. He had appeared for questioning before the police a day earlier.

articleTitle: Fire breaks out at Goregaon Film City; AICWA says Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set affected
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AICWA claims Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set affected in Goregaon Film City fire
description: The blaze erupted in the structure behind Prime Focus Studio around 4 pm, following which Mumbai Fire Brigade and other agencies were immediately mobilised.
body_raw: A temporary structure at Film City in Goregaon area of Mumbai was gutted in a blaze on Monday, officials said, adding that nobody was injured. The blaze erupted in the structure behind Prime Focus Studio around 4 pm, following which Mumbai Fire Brigade and other agencies were immediately mobilised. The fire was doused after more than an hours efforts at 4.55 pm. There is no report of any injury to anyone, the official said, adding that the blaze was confined to electric wiring, electric installations, cables, doors, wooden plank, AC units, bamboo and plastic materials, sound system, and shooting material at the temporary structure. Watch - Jailer 2 trailer Rajinikanth returns with a bigger cast and an even bigger battle Meanwhile, the All Indian Cine Workers Association AICWA claimed that the fire broke out on the set of Colors reality show Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 at Prime Focus Studio in Film City. The association claimed that a large number of workers and artistes were present on the set when the fire broke out. AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta alleged that adequate fire-safety measures were not in place on the set. He demanded a time-bound inquiry into the incident and an FIR for alleged negligence against the channel, producer and production house. The association also sought the resignation of the Managing Director of Film City. Mumbais Film City Burns Again, and No One Is Held Accountable Mumbais Film City is burning again, and as always, no one is being held accountable. Fire after fire, year after year, thousands of workers and artists are pushed into danger by channels, producers and production houses that refuse to spend on basic fire safety to save a few rupees. The sets go up in flames, the poor workers pay the price, and those who profit walk away without a single consequence. Fires in Film City are not accidents. They are the result of greed, negligence and a system that has never punished the guilty. Unless accountability is fixed at the top, these fires will keep coming, and so will the loss of innocent lives. DevFadnavis ShelarAshish advakash Ashishjaisw3Adv ritutawde KishoriPednekar ANI PTINews iansindia sureshsgupta - All Indian Cine Workers Association aicwaofficial October 5, 2026 This is not an accident, it is criminal negligence. Every day thousands of workers and artists put their lives at risk on these sets. When a fire breaks out, the people who suffer are the poor workers, not the channels and producers who profit. This cannot go on. Accountability must be fixed at the top, and those responsible must face the law, Gupta said. Suresh Shyamlal Gupta has also written to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis regarding the incident. AICWA urged the government to make fire audits, on-set fire-safety staff and firefighting equipment mandatory for every shoot in Film City. It also demanded that licences of productions that fail to comply with fire-safety norms be cancelled. With inputs from PTI

articleTitle: Himachal High Court halts operation of anti-hail guns in Himachal apple belt: ‘affects rain pattern’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anti-hail guns are shock-wave generating machines used by some horticulturists with the objective of preventing crop damage by disrupting the formation of hailstones in clouds.
description: Directs state to examine if anti-hail system pushes out cloud from apple orchards leading to excessive rainfall in adjoining areas.
body_raw: The Himachal Pradesh High Court on Monday directed the state government put an immediate halt on the operation of anti-hail guns across the state for at least one year, while observing that concerns raised by orchardists over excessive rainfall and damage to adjoining apple-growing areas appear to stand substantiated. A Division Bench of Chief Justice G S Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin Chander Negi issued the directions while hearing a Public Interest Litigation PIL, initiated suo motu by the court, following representations from apple growers who have complained that anti-hail guns were impacting the rainfall and hail patterns. Anti-hail guns are shock-wave generating machines used by some horticulturists with the objective of preventing crop damage by disrupting the formation of hailstones in clouds. The Court took note of an affidavit filed by the Director of Horticulture, which stated that heavy and prolonged rainfall was observed when the hail-control system was operational for more than an hour. It is apparent.the concerns raised in the representation, that operation of anti-hail guns could push clouds towards adjoining orchard areas, resulting in excessive rainfall and hail in neighbouring locations, stand substantiated in the circumstances, the bench observed. It directed that two anti-hail guns installed by the government at Deorighat and Bareonghat in the Jubbal-Kotkhai area of Shimla district is not operated till further orders. It also directed the government to issue instructions prohibiting the operation of privately owned anti-hail guns anywhere in the state. The system should remain non-operational for at least one year, the Bench said, while directing the authorities to examine whether surrounding areas benefit after the guns are stopped. Earlier, appearing for the State, Additional Advocate General Gobind Korla, submitted in the court that Dr Y S Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, Solan, was conducting a study to assess the efficacy and impact of anti-hail guns. It was submitted that the study would require at least another four years before reaching a definitive conclusion. In view of the duration required for the study, the Court impleaded the university through its Registrar as a respondent and issued notice to it, returnable within four weeks. The Bench further directed the State to file a response specifically addressing whether stopping the operation of the anti-hail guns results in any benefit to areas in the neighbourhood or vicinity of Deorighat and Bareonghat. The Court also noted that the representation before it referred to alleged adverse effects associated with anti-hail guns in Mexico, Romania and other countries. It directed the Himachal Pradesh government to file a comprehensive response dealing with the available global studies as well as the impact of anti-hail guns in the state. The matter has been listed for further hearing on December 8, 2026.

articleTitle: Indian Railways identifies 11 trains with journeys over 40 hours for special cleanliness monitoring
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian Railways will step up cleanliness monitoring on 11 long-distance trains that remain on the tracks for more than 40 hours. (Image: Southern Railway)
description: Indian Railways has identified 11 long-distance trains with journeys of more than 40 hours for enhanced cleanliness monitoring, including Vivek Express, Avadh Assam Express and Jhelum Express.
body_raw: Indian Railways has identified 11 long-distance trains with journey durations of more than 40 hours for enhanced cleanliness. The move is aimed at ensuring that passengers get better housekeeping, cleaner toilets and improved onboard services throughout the journey, rather than only at the originating station. According to a Railway Board letter dated October 3, the identified trains will receive special attention for cleanliness and serviceability during their journeys. Why are these trains being monitored? Long-distance trains remain on the tracks for several days. During such extended journeys, issues related to coach cleanliness, toilets, garbage disposal and minor repairs can affect the passenger experience if they are not addressed on time. The Railway Board RB has asked the concerned zones to closely monitor these trains while they are en route. The focus will be on maintaining cleanliness throughout the journey until the train reaches its destination. The list includes some of the countrys longest-running trains, including the Vivek Express, Avadh Assam Express, Amrapali Express and Jhelum Express. The Vivek Express has the longest journey among the identified trains, covering about 4,158 km, while its rake turnaround time is 170 hours. What will Indian Railways do? The Railway Board has directed the zones to take several measures to improve cleanliness and upkeep. The identified trains will be closely monitored by the owning depots during their journeys. Officers will also review cleanliness levels and passenger complaints on a regular basis. Special attention will be given to Clean Train Station CTS points, where cleaning teams will be expected to have adequate manpower, equipment and consumables. The RBhas also asked for small repairs to be attended to during the journey, while bio-toilets will be checked at maintenance depots and designated en-route locations. Garbage collection to be monitored Under the onboard housekeeping arrangements, garbage collection is carried out every two hours in coaches. The RB has directed that the collected waste should be handed over at designated disposal points instead of being thrown along the railway track. Photographic monitoring Time-stamped photographs of coaches and toilets will also be taken at selected inspection points, as well as at originating and destination stations, to help monitor the condition of the trains. Focus on passenger experience The Railway Board has stressed that the objective is not simply to improve cleanliness when a train starts its journey. In the new OBHS scheme emphasis has been given on the passenger awareness and regular training of OBHS staffs. This need to be emulated in all depots on OBHS trains. The OBHS staffs to be regularly trained for task assigned and proper etiquettes and behavior, the letter reads.

articleTitle: 150 Bangladeshi immigrants flown out of J&K on IAF aircraft for deportation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jammu and Kashmir: Police sources said a batch of people described as "illegal immigrants" was sent in an Indian Air Force plane to Bagdogra airport in West Bengal. (File Photo)
description: This comes two months after a high-level committee on demographic changes, set up by the Union Home Ministry in May this year, visited Jammu and Kashmir for its first field visit.
body_raw: As many as 150 Bangladeshi nationals who were allegedly living illegally in Jammu and Kashmir were airlifted on Monday to West Bengals Bagdogra, from where they will be deported. The 150 are among 500 people who were detained from different parts of the Union Territory during a survey to identify illegal immigrants and kept in a facility manned by the police. From Bagdogra, the 150 will be deported to Bangladesh, officials said. This comes two months after a high-level committee on demographic changes, set up by the Union Home Ministry in May this year, visited Jammu and Kashmir for its first field visit. Police sources said that the batch of 150 immigrants was sent in an Indian Air Force aircraft. They would be handed over to the Border Security Force BSF and deported on October 7, sources said. JK police have conducted a special exercise over the last few days to identify illegal immigrants in the Union Territory, sources said, adding that around 500 people-mostly from Bangladesh-were detained and shifted to the facility on the outskirts of Srinagar city. Most of these people have been settled in different parts of the Kashmir Valley for many years now, said a police officer. They were mostly doing menial jobs like ragpicking, etc. Sources said some of those detained are Rohingya from Myanmar. Others will also be sent out in batches in the coming days and deported, sources said. The high-level committee, during its visit to Jammu and Kashmir, was informed that there are 7,656 Rohingya and 504 Bangladeshi nationals in Jammu and Kashmir-6,737 Rohingya and 46 Bangladeshi immigrants in Jammu, and the rest in Kashmir. The committee was also informed that 117 cases are registered against them-101 in Jammu and 16 in Kashmir. The committees mandate is to study demographic changes arising from illegal immigration and other factors and to recommend measures to address them. It has been asked to submit its report within one year. It had sought details from states and Union Territories regarding visible changes in religious demography across districts, industrial clusters and border districts over the last 15 years. In a letter dispatched to states and UTs over the last two months, the Committee sought time-series data indicating changes over the years, alongside other administrative datasets, an assessment by state governments of major trends in demographics, and data on the religious composition of tribal populations since 2011. -With PTI

articleTitle: ‘I don’t call myself a rockstar anymore’: Rhiti Tiwari on being schooled by Salman Khan
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rhiti Tiwari Bigg Boss 20 eviction interview
description: In an exclusive interview, evicted Bigg Boss 20 contestant Rhiti Tiwari recalled Salman Khan schooling her for two hours after she misbehaved with Qazi Touqeer.
body_raw: Manoj Tiwaris daughter, singer Rhiti Tiwari exited Bigg Boss 20 last week following a mid-week eviction. Since leaving the house, Rhiti has been reflecting on her journey on the Salman Khan-hosted reality show. In an exclusive conversation with SCREEN, she opened up about her time on Bigg Boss Season 20, being schooled by Salman over her behaviour, dealing with the nepo kid tag on the show, and the trauma she has faced in her personal life. Rhiti Tiwari on the nepo-kid tag Ever since Rhiti Tiwari entered Bigg Boss 20, a section of the internet has claimed that she landed a spot on the show because of her father Manoj Tiwaris recommendation. Even inside the house, Rhiti had to deal with the nepo kid tag. Reacting to it, Rhiti said, What is really funny is that my dad didnt even know I was going on the show until 1-2 days before. He sent me a news link asking if I was going. If people think I was on the show because of him, thats not true. Sharing her take on nepotism, Rhiti added, I can defend the nepo kid tag, but nepotism holds a different value for me. Before all of this happened and I entered a room, they would know whose daughter I am. There was already love, admiration, and some respect coming to me. Whatever he has earned in his life comes to me as a blessing in terms of respect. If I were truly a nepo-kid, what have I been doing for 5 years? Why didnt I reach the place I aspire to be at? Why is all this happening now? Using his name, I could have done a lot of things, but I wanted to do things myself. I was told you have to do it yourself, so where is the nepotism? Rhiti Tiwari on her equation and fight with Qazi Touqeer Rhiti Tiwari also opened up about her equation with Qazi Touqeer, revealing that she had initially formed a strong emotional bond with the singer. However, after learning that Qazi had faked his illness on the show, Rhiti admitted that she felt deceived and took it personally. She also expressed regret over losing her temper and lashing out at him. I genuinely connected with Qaziji in the beginning. Our artiste-to-artiste energy matched. I doubted if he acted, then we had a deep conversation where I cried. I felt bad about what he was going through. I have built a very strong connection with him. Due to my personal experiences, when I see someone go through something, I get really affected. When I found out it was all for entertainment, I took it personally. He fooled me and hurt my ego. In that fit, I did and said things I wholeheartedly regret. I dont wish to be that person ever again. However, Rhitis anger did not end there. During another task, she used derogatory language against Qazi and even threatened him. Following the incident, Salman Khan schooled Rhiti over her behaviour and told her that she appeared insecure about Qazi. Talking about it, Rhiti said, I wanted the earth to swallow me. I was called insecure, jealous, desperate, and whatnot. I dont call myself a rockstar anymore. I would like the world to call me that one day if they see fit. It was the most ashamed I ever felt. I always thought love and anger were two very strong emotions, but that day I realised what strong emotions like shame, guilt, and embarrassment are. I was weighed down by it. I told myself, What have you done. I was disappointed in myself this was not the Rhiti I came to be. I broke down. I was destroyed. The only way was to rebuild stronger and harder. I took it all. Somewhere, a part of me has not healed from the things I have been through. It came out in all the wrong ways. That house has healed in me, what could have taken 10 years and countless therapy sessions. Everything that happened was my worst fear. Also Read Salman Khan schools Rhiti Tiwari You are Manoj Tiwaris daughter, not Dolly Bindras Asked whether she felt Salman Khan had been a little too harsh on her, Rhiti added, If Salman sir took 2 hours to explain something to me, so that I can be a better human being, I think its my greatest privilege. The whole episode was about me thats insane. I dont think I would have wanted to be called Dolly Bindras daughter. But my actions were such that, obviously, people will comment. Rhiti on parents divorce and trauma During her stint on Bigg Boss 20, Rhiti Tiwari spoke several times about her parents divorce and how the experience continues to affect her. Opening up about growing up in a broken home, Rhiti said, Being from a broken home does affect me. A lot of people from broken homes exist in this world. The things I have seen in life have shaped me. There are things that have not made sense to me yet. A lot of what I did, the way I acted, came from the lack of dealing with and learning about myself. I believe I have been learning, trying to be better, grow, but when you come from these things, they stay in your brain a certain way. When all of this happened to me on Bigg Boss, it healed a very big part of me. Rhiti also spoke about her equation with father Manoj Tiwari today. She said, I am always cheering for my father. If he calls me for support on his show Pati Patni Aur Panga 2, Rhiti Tiwari shall be there for Manoj Tiwari. Today our equation is very loving. We were not able to be around each other a lot I have not lived with him. Whatever happened, he is a proud father I am a proud daughter, and whenever I need him, he is there. On the work front, Rhiti Tiwari is gearing up to release her music album Rejected, which will reflect on her journey on Bigg Boss, her actions and her path to redemption. Explaining the idea behind the album, Rhiti said, I was always someone who felt the most likeable in a room all delusions about myself were shattered on Bigg Boss 20. I was rejected in that house, and I own it.

articleTitle: JSA, working group seek cap on hospital charges, medicine margins
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jan Swasthya Abhiyan and health rights groups urge government intervention to regulate private hospital rates amid soaring treatment and medicine costs
description: While the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 (CEA) provides a legal framework for regulating clinical establishments and envisages government-determined ranges of charges, it has not been implemented, they said.
body_raw: The Jan Swasthya Abhiyan JSA and the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment Working Group have called for urgent government intervention to regulate healthcare by private hospitals, warning that patients continue to face excessive and arbitrary charges for treatment, medicines and medical consumables with little effective protection or recourse. The demand comes amid renewed scrutiny of private hospital pricing. The Supreme Court recently questioned steep mark-ups on medicines sold through hospital pharmacies, including a case in which a cancer medicine supplied at around Rs 2,700 carried an MRP of around Rs 27,000. The SC also questioned practices that require patients to purchase medicines from hospital-linked pharmacies and has asked the government to examine regulation of trade margins. At a virtual media conference, Dr Abhay Shukla, co-convener, JSA, said private healthcare has expanded enormously in India, but regulation has simply not kept pace, adding there is no regulation of rates and the patient has virtually no bargaining power over what they are charged. Leading corporate hospital chains have been earning huge surpluses estimated in the range of Rs 22 lakh to Rs 55 lakh per year from each bed in the last few years, Dr Shukla observed. Experts said there is a need for an effective nationwide system to regulate what private hospitals can charge patients for procedures, services, medicines and consumables. Leading corporate hospital chains charge on average Rs 60,000 to Rs 78,000 per day of treatment. This is an unacceptably high level of profiteering that is paid for by ordinary patients through exorbitant hospital bills, Dr Shukla said. While the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 CEA provides a legal framework for regulating clinical establishments and envisages government-determined ranges of charges, it has not been implemented, they said. Regarding fixing margins on medicines and medical consumables, concerns have also been raised with Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. Dr Shukla said at the state level, the FDA Commissioners office can issue orders requiring hospitals that supply medical consumables above a specified unit price to disclose their procurement price alongside the selling price. This will lead to a huge amount of transparency, so that patients are aware of the actual cost of what they are buying and the cost incurred by the hospital, Dr Shukla said. Maharashtra is in the process of drafting a Clinical Establishments Act CEA. Since pricing is a subject in the Concurrent List, there is a possibility that the state could introduce a provision in the CEA requiring hospitals to limit the markup on medicines and consumables they supply to no more than 30 per cent over the procurement price. Such a provision could potentially be introduced and implemented at the state level itself, the experts said. The CEA was passed more than a decade ago, but its non-implementation has produced zero results on the ground. It is high time the government starts to regulate the procedures in private hospitals. A patient should know how much they will they be charged before agreeing to a treatment, according to K M Gopakumar, co-convener, Working Group. The MRP cannot become a licence to charge patients many times the procurement price. The government must urgently fix the trade margins on all medical products and ensure that patients are free to purchase medicines and consumables from outside wherever clinically possible, said Jyotsna Singh, Co-Convenor, Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments.

articleTitle: How a sports psychologist helped Pranavi Urs win Asian Games gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pranavi Urs became the first Indian women to win a gold in golf at Asian Games. (Reuters)
description: A session before the final round trained her brain for every scenario, including the triple bogey that came on the third hole
body_raw: If sports psychology looks like a luxury at the elite level, Pranavi Urs has an answer. It could be the difference between an Asian Games gold medal and nothing. The 23-year-old had little sleep the night before the final round at the Kasugai Country Club East Course, and her anxiety wasnt helped by a triple-bogey 7 on the third hole, which wiped out her three-shot lead going into the last day and handed the edge to World No. 6 Yin Ruoning of China. That is where her work with her sports psychologist paid off. Going into the final round of any big event, you are bound to be nervous because you care so much, Pranavi told The Indian Express on Monday. I had a session with my psychologist before the final round, where we trained my brain for all the possible scenarios and focused on having fun out on the golf course. Preparing for Murphys Law anything that can go wrong will go wrong worked to her benefit.It triple bogey was the worst thing that could have happened. I told myself that I had hit rock bottom and the only way from there was upwards. I just had to stick to the gameplan. The preparation did its job. Pranavi caught Yin with a birdie on the 10th, went ahead with another on the 13th, and did not give up the lead after that. Not that Pranavi suffered from a lack of confidence going into the competition. ALSO READ How Pranavi Urs shrugged off a triple bogey to win golf gold Whenever you enter a tournament, you want to win, not just participate, she said. But to go ahead and actually do it was surreal. The psychologists contribution was vital to the biggest title of her career so far. She is in her third season on the Ladies European Tour LET and, despite contending several times, has not quite taken the final step. Whats more, her teammate Aditi Ashok had an unenviable history at big events. At the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, she held a seven-shot lead going into the final round before a 5-over 77 relegated her to the silver medal. At the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, she was second going into the final 18 holes, but finished just outside the medal positions. No negative vibes Pranavi said the topic remained off-limits during team discussions. Ive known both Aditi and Diksha Dagar for a long time. Ive always looked up to Aditi. Ive played together with Diksha. All three of us are good friends and in good form. When we came together at the start of the week, we were confident that we will definitely win a medal, she said, preparing to board a flight out of Japan. I didnt ask for any advice from Aditi, and certainly didnt bring up those two final rounds in our chats. Were friends, why would I do that? We talked about everything other than that during our dinners together. Though Aditi 14th at two-over and Diksha tied 23rd at 12-over didnt do as well individually as they would have liked, the Indian womens team did clinch a silver medal behind China. Indias first womens individual golf gold at the Asian Games is likely to give the game a shot in the arm, and could help the golfer from Mysuru in her own development. Im in a better headspace now and feel more confident now. This gold medal is definitely a boost for me. The next step is to win on the LET, she said. That she beat some of the top players in the womens game augurs well for her growth. Apart from Yin World No. 6, bronze medallist Shannon Xuan Yin Tan of Singapore is the 2025 LET Order of Merit winner. Its great to win an event beating such players and a good sign that my career is going in the right direction. Now I have complete clarity that my game is in great shape and good enough to win big events, said Pranavi, who will play the Womens India Open at the DLF Golf Country Club in Gurgaon later this month.

articleTitle: Diego Forlan on Indian football: ‘Talented young players, need stronger academies & league’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uruguay coach Diego Forlan in action. (AP)
description: The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner said that playing international friendlies against stronger opposition like Brazil and Uruguay would benefit the Blue Tigers in the long run.
body_raw: After Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti caused quite a stir last month when he said India did not have a footballing culture, Uruguay coach Diego Forlan said that while the main sport in the country was cricket, India still had a lot of young talented football players. Your main sport is cricket, so its different. Football has been here for many years, of course, but its not the main sport. But you have a lot of young talented players, Forlan said, speaking on the eve of the India vs Uruguay match. The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner said that playing international friendlies against stronger opposition like Brazil and Uruguay would benefit the Blue Tigers in the long run. I think this kind of game, playing against Brazil, Uruguay, and also having a strong league, would improve the development of young players. In the near future, India could be playing important and crucial games, he said. ALSO READ India vs Uruguay Can the Blue Tigers build on Brazil lessons? You need to build from the roots - academies, young players, kids to start playing a lot. If you build more academies, the league gets stronger and stronger, you will achieve getting more players and getting better players, thats for sure, added Forlan. Before the Uruguay fixture, India have played Panama against whom they drew 1-1 and then taken on Brazil, where they showed some spark in the beginning before getting trounced 4-0. Uruguay, meanwhile, landed in Kolkata on September 30 and have been taking time to acclimatise to the Indian conditions. We know its not going to be easy. Playing here, the weather is humid. You also need to adapt. Thats why all these days that we came here were good for us to adapt. The weather is different from Japan and Korea, so we know its going to be a difficult game, Forlan said. Before talking on India, Uruguay had toured Japan and Korea, losing to the former 1-3 and defeating the latter 4-1.

articleTitle: ‘Won’t be able to step out of house’: Bengal CM warns Mamata Banerjee
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, former CM and TMC leader Mamata Banerjee. (PTI, ANI Photos)
description: Suvendu Adhikari's statement came after Banerjee sought that her 2021 leg injury medical records be made public
body_raw: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday warned his predecessor Mamata Banerjee against digging too deep into the disclosure of her 2021 leg injury medical records, stating that more such documents could be made public if required. The remarks came hours after Banerjee served a legal notice on SSKM Hospital and Bangur Institute of Neurosciences seeking an explanation over how her medical records relating to the 2021 Nandigram incident were disclosed publicly without permission. Addressing the media, Adhikari said, Do not poke around too much. If I start showing the X-ray plates and MRI reports, you will not be able to step out of your house. If necessary, I will say where I got the records from. The papers were not at SSKM. It was not supposed to be at SSKM. I will tell her lawyer not to dig too deep into this issue. She had thought she would become chief minister for a fourth term. So, she had left all the documents in her drawer in her chamber at the Chief Ministers Office at Nabanna, Adhikari said. He did not, however, specify whether the medical records had been obtained from Banerjees office or residence. This comes a few days after Adhikari claimed that Mamata had faked her leg injury during campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. At a press conference a few days ago, he had held up a document saying it was the March 11, 2021, report of the Department of Radio Diagnosis of Bangur Institute of Neurosciences, which showed no evidence of a fracture. The state government would launch a fresh inquiry into her false claims of leg injury during the 2021 assembly poll campaign, Adhikari had said. Following this, Banerjees lawyer Arka Nag sent the notice through email to the director and medical superintendent of SSKM and the head of the neurology department at Bangur Institute of Neurosciences, seeking an explanation on how his clients medical records reached Adhikari and were subsequently made public.

articleTitle: Seven-year-old died in Andhra after anti-malaria dose. Now top court asks High Court to monitor probe
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court took cognizance of the matter and directed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to closely monitor the investigation into the girl's death.
description: The girl was among 70 people, including 15 children, from her village who were hospitalised early September. Taking suo motu cognizance of the death, CJI Surya Kant has asked the HC to monitor the probe ordered by the state government
body_raw: In the last week of August, a seven-year-old girl was handed out an anti-malaria tablet in Andhra Pradeshs Polavaram district during a drive against the mosquito-borne illness in her village. A few days later, along with 70 people in her village, she was hospitalised. While the rest of them recovered, the girl, Madivi Jamuna, died during treatment. A month later, the Supreme Court took cognizance of the matter and directed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to closely monitor the investigation into the girls death. Several villagers of Gollaguppa village in Yetapaka mandal in Polavaram fell ill after consuming chloroquine tablets during a drive that was carried out after reports of malaria cases. The girl, a Class 2 student, developed complications on August 31 and died on September 2. Taking suo motu cognisance of her death, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has asked the HC to monitor the probe ordered by the state government. Meanwhile, an investigation team is awaiting detailed reports from different laboratories, including the Andhra Pradesh Forensic Science Laboratory in Amaravati, to check if the batch of anti-malarial tablets was contaminated. On September 1 and 2, at least 70 people, including many children, were hospitalised at primary health centres in Polavaram. They were later moved to Bhadrachalam Area Hospital in neighbouring Telangana where all of them recovered and were discharged the next day. The girl, however, died at the hospital. The village is located on the Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border. CM ordered probe Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu had ordered a probe into the matter. District Collector K Dinesh Kumar said two villagers had tested positive for malaria, following which officials conducted the drive. As per the FIR, Jamuna fell ill and lost consciousness a day after taking the tablet. She was among the 15 children from the village who fell ill. Health officials said that the chloroquine tablets had been distributed in age-appropriate doses in accordance with medical and health department protocols and that quality-control tests conducted on the medication had given satisfactory results. articleTitle: BJP’s Smita Jadhav files nomination for Pune Graduates’ constituency
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jadhav is the daughter of P D Patil, founder of Dr D Y Patil Vidyapeeth, Pimpri-Chinchwad, and the wife of Yogesh Jadhav, director of “Pudhari”.
description: Speaking on the occasion, Gorkhe said in Jadhav, the Mahayuti has a cultured, studious and highly educated candidate who represents a confluence of education, media, and social sectors.
body_raw: Smita Yogesh Jadhav, the official candidate of BJP-led Mahayuti for the Pune Graduates constituency, filed her nomination papers at the Returning Officers office on Monday. Besides Jadhav, BJPs Kaustubh Gawade from the Teachers constituency also filed nomination papers on Monday at the Pune Vidhan Bhavan. On the occasion, Union Minister of State Muralidhar Mohol, Maharashtras Minister for Higher and Technical Education Chandrakant-Patil, Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Minister Jaykumar Gore, MLA Amit Gorkhe, MLA M Mahesh Landge, MLC Uma Khapre, BJP state general secretary Rajesh Pande, along with a large number of BJP office-bearers and activists were present. Speaking on the occasion, Gorkhe said in Jadhav, the Mahayuti has a cultured, studious and highly educated candidate who represents a confluence of education, media, and social sectors. Backed by the educational and social legacy of the D Y Patil family, she is fully capable of effectively addressing the pending issues of the Graduates constituency, such as unemployment, skill development, higher education, and new job opportunities. Every worker of the Mahayuti stands firmly behind her, Gorkhe said. Jadhav is the daughter of P D Patil, founder of Dr D Y Patil Vidyapeeth, Pimpri-Chinchwad, and the wife of Yogesh Jadhav, director of Pudhari. She is currently serving as the Pro-Chancellor and Secretary of Dr D Y Patil Vidyapeeth. Her long and rich experience across education, media, and social sectors will prove invaluable in voicing the pending concerns of graduates, Gorkhe said. Speaking on the occasion, Jadhav said education, youth power and knowledge-based development hold the highest priority in Prime Minister Narendra Modi jis vision of Viksit Bharat. The BJP and Mahayuti have given me the opportunity to work for youth and graduates. For the past two decades, I have been working in the education sector, striving for the goals and future of young people. Through this platform, I have now received an opportunity to work on a much broader scale, and I will make the best use of it. For graduates, Jadhav said her primary focus will be on employment and skill development. It is essential to boost youth startups, develop incubation centres, and provide maximum opportunities for skill enhancement.

articleTitle: A judge must be impartial, never indifferent: Justice Vikram Nath
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Justice Nath is also the executive chairman of the National Legal Services Authority. (Image Enhanced using AI)
description: Justice Nath also said courts must pay attention to how those who pass through the system experience justice.
body_raw: Judges are not appointed to be charitable, and compassion in adjudication is not favour and it is not leniency, Justice Vikram Nath said while delivering the second Prof. Dr N R Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture in New Delhi on Monday. He said, Impartiality and indifference are not the same thing. The blind fold on Lady Justice does not mean she cannot see. It means she does not look at who stands before her before deciding what is right. She still weighs and weighs with care. A judge must be impartial but never indifferent. Justice Nath, who is also the executive chairman of the National Legal Services Authority, delivered the annual lecture on the topic Judging with Compassion Human Understanding in the Practice of Law. Chief Justice of India CJI Surya Kant inaugurated the session. Justice Nath also said courts must pay attention to how those who pass through the system experience justice. For the survivor made to relive her trauma in the witness box, or the litigant who cannot follow the language of the proceedings, the process is what justice actually feels like, he said. We must ask whether, for too many, it has itself become a trauma, he said. The Supreme Court judge also highlighted that courts must see the gap between formal equality and experienced equality. He gave the example of undertrials granted bail on identical conditions, where one walks out and another stays in prison because he cannot furnish sureties. On paper the law treated them equally. In life, it did not. During his address, CJI Kant underlined the importance of legal scholarship saying that while courts hear individual disputes, research helps show how judicial decisions affect peoples lives long after a case is over. The scholar who follows the victim beyond the courtroom, asking whether the compensation is actually paid, whether a brief family receives the support it needs, and whether victims are truly hurt.it is scholarship that gathers those 10,000 orders into one picture. and shows us whom our well-meant judgments may have left behind, CJI Kant said. On cases involving survivors of sexual violence and child witnesses, Justice Nath said that a trauma-informed courtroom is not a softer courtroom. Compassion, he added, does not tell us who should win. It tells us how carefully we must understand what winning and losing mean.

articleTitle: When did India begin latest round of talks with Russia, Ukraine? Jaishankar reveals
articleFeaturedImageAlt: **EDS: THIRD PARTY IMAGE** In this image posted on Oct. 5, 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar along with Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) President NK Singh, left, and former Singapore Foreign Minister George Yeo, right, during the concluding session of the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) on ‘India and the World: Adaptive by Design’, in New Delhi. (@DrSJaishankar/X via PTI Photo)
description: Jaishankar said New Delhi started the latest round of conversations with both sides in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea.
body_raw: A day after stating that India is in touch with both Ukraine and Russia over the ongoing conflict, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday spelt out the kind of conversations India was having with the two sides amid evolving dynamics. However, he emphasised that while its not an easy situation, it would be a big positive even if Kyiv and Moscow were to agree on something of a limited nature. The minister said that from the very beginning, India has held that this conflict is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. Therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties. There were actually negotiations in the early stages of the conflict. Though we have been maintaining for some time that both parties should come to the table, and there were a number of conferences where countries gathered to express their support for peace, but often they would gather in the absence of Russia, he said, in reference to initiatives like the Swiss peace conference. However, he added that New Delhi has always believed that there was no point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there. He said New Delhi started the latest round of conversations with both sides in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea. In fact, after losing Indian sailors in such attacks, New Delhi had strongly conveyed its condemnation to both sides and also summoned envoys to register protest. In July, there were attacks on civilian shipping by both Russia and Ukraine. And in the course of those attacks, some Indian sailors were killed, some were injured. We regard these attacks as completely unacceptable, whether it is in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, or the Gulf. So, we protested very strongly to the Russians, to the Ukrainians. I myself took it up with the foreign ministers of both countries. We started getting active initially to secure the maritime shipping and the mariners involved in that, he said. Jaishankar added that those conversations brought out the nature of the cargo which was being shipped. And there was the concern expressed about the grain exports which had come to a halt in the Black Sea. So the conversation developed into whether non-attack on shipping is good, but is there a possibility of facilitating the shipment of grain. it got linked to energy. So, it became a somewhat broader conversation, added the minister. The conversations started with Prime Minister Narendra Modis meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek in August. After that, Jaishankar went to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, which was followed by another discussion between Modi and Putin in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. We still keep in touch with both sides. Its not obviously an easy situation. Its not something which anybody can say with a high degree of confidence that something is going to come out. But it seems definitely an effort worth making, he says, adding that resolving concerns about grain, fertiliser and fuel are in Indias as well as the Global Souths interest. We have the interests of the parties themselves that if they can even agree on something of a limited nature, we feel that in the given circumstance thats a big positive, he said. He also spoke about the need to fix the United Nations, not work around it, and how this was going to be an age of flux for the world, with conflicts and tariff volatility making it turbulent, underlining that responding to the challenges emerging out of the choppy waters is the task at hand. Im very confident that we will rise to the challenges, Jaishankar said during an interactive session at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, where he shared the dais with former foreign minister of Singapore, George Yong Boon Yeo, during the closing session. The minister, however, said that as Indias record shows, we have been able to rise to the challenges, whether it was Covid, or the challenge of a double conflict today. The challenges of energy, food, fertilisers - we need to factor them into our thinking, plan and respond. That in a sense is the task before us. And Im very confident that we will rise to the challenge, he said. Jaishankar also spoke about championing the voice of the Global South. The Global South expects India to articulate on the world stage, he said. On reforms needed for the United Nations and other multilateral institutions, Jaishankar said, The UN is gridlocked, adding that a few countries were resisting its reforms. However, he said that the US is one of Indias principal strategic partners - our largest economic account, our biggest trade account, it is a very major critical defence partner.

articleTitle: Sentence tossed after AI video of victim ‘forgiving’ his killer is played
articleFeaturedImageAlt: stacey wales, ai
description: The three-judge panel reaffirmed the conviction of Gabriel Horcasitas, 55, who had been sentenced to 10 1/2 years in prison, but said that he must be resentenced in the 2021 road-rage shooting death of Christopher Pelkey, 37.
body_raw: An appeals court in Arizona on Wednesday threw out the prison sentence of a man convicted of manslaughter after a video created by artificial intelligence depicting the victim forgiving his killer was played in court. The three-judge panel reaffirmed the conviction of Gabriel Horcasitas, 55, who had been sentenced to 10 12 years in prison, but said that he must be resentenced in the 2021 road-rage shooting death of Christopher Pelkey, 37. The judges concluded that the sentencing judge committed a fundamental error by allowing and relying on an AI video that generated a likeness of Pelkeys voice and appearance. The appeals court found the video did not reflect actual events while presenting statements in the footage as if they were coming directly from the victim. The appeals court noted the use of the AI-generated video posed a novel legal issue and that no prior Arizona case had addressed the admissibility of such a depiction of a victim during sentencing. The video was used with victim-impact statements made by members of Pelkeys family and friends in the courtroom during the sentencing of Horcasitas last year. At the sentencing, Pelkeys older sister, Stacey Wales, presented the AI video depicting Pelkey addressing Horcasitas. I believe in forgiveness and in God who forgives, the video said. The video also portrayed Pelkey as addressing the court, saying, This here is a true representation of who I was. The sentencing judge, Todd F. Lang of Maricopa County Superior Court, praised the video, saying, I loved that AI. He called it genuine and noted that the victim was allowed to speak from his heart. He then imposed the maximum sentence, which was more than the nine years that prosecutors had sought. Critics have argued that the introduction of AI in legal proceedings can open the door to manipulation and deception, compounding the already emotional process of giving victim-impact statements. The appeals court held that a victims right to speak cannot trample a defendants right to be sentenced based on accurate and reliable information. The video erases the interpretive distance between the familys belief about what the victim would have said and the victims own voice and opinions, the judges wrote. They decided that the reliance on the video made the sentencing procedure fundamentally unfair. Lawyers for Pelkey and Horcasitas did not immediately respond to requests for comment Sunday. Wales was preparing her own victim-impact statement for two years, she told The New York Times last year, but believed that it was missing a critical element. I kept hearing what Chris would say, she told the Times. Wales said that her husband and the couples longtime business partner had used AI to help corporate clients with presentations, including one featuring the likeness of a companys CEO who had died years ago. With the help of her husband and business partner, she took Pelkeys voice from a YouTube video of him speaking after completing treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder at a facility for veterans, she said. For his face and torso, they used a poster of Pelkey from a funeral service, digitally trimming his thick beard, removing his glasses and editing out a logo from his cap, she said. Wales said that she had written the script that was read by her brothers AI likeness. I know that AI can be used nefariously, and its uncomfortable for some, Wales said last year. But this was just another tool to use to tell Chris story. Wales was not immediately available for comment Sunday. On Nov. 13, 2021, Pelkey was stopped at a red light in Chandler, a Phoenix suburb, when Horcasitas pulled up behind him and honked. That caused Pelkey to leave his vehicle and approach Horcasitas car and gesture with his arms as if to say, What the heck? according to a probable cause statement. Horcasitas then fatally shot Pelkey in the chest. The case will be returned to Maricopa County Superior Court for a new sentencing hearing, without the AI-generated video of Pelkey giving his statement.

articleTitle: Darya Shipilova: Who was Russian anti-plague lab worker who died? Moscow accused of covering up leak
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Darya Shipilova, russia,
description: Darya Shipilova, 28, worked at Siberia’s Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute and died after developing pneumonia of unknown origin, triggering quarantines and fears of pneumonic plague.
body_raw: Darya Shipilova worked in a place devoted to studying one of the worlds most feared infectious diseases. The 28-year-old laboratory worker was employed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, a specialist facility in eastern Russia. She died on October 2 after developing severe pneumonia, according to reports. Russian health authorities have described the illness as pneumonia of unknown aetiology, meaning its cause has not been established, news agency Reuters reported. Her death has since become the centre of a public-health scare in Siberia, after reports circulated that she may have contracted pneumonic plague, the respiratory form of a disease caused by Yersinia pestis. But there is currently no confirmed evidence that Shipilova died from plague or that she contracted an infection through her work. What happened to Darya Shipilova? Shipilovas condition deteriorated rapidly before she was taken to a hospital in Shelekhov, a town near Irkutsk. She died there on October 2, according to Reuters. Unconfirmed reports circulating in Russian media have suggested that she may have been exposed to plague bacteria following an accident involving a test tube at the laboratory. But Russian authorities have not confirmed that account. The Guardian reported that another account linked the onset of her illness to a work trip to Buryatia. Neither explanation has been publicly confirmed by Russian health authorities. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias public-health watchdog, said extensive testing found no microorganisms associated with the patients professional activities. It also said investigators found no incidents at the institute involving pathogenic microorganisms. The institute where she worked The Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute is a specialist facility with a long history of studying dangerous infectious diseases.The Washington Post reported that the institute was established in the 1930s as an anti-plague organisation and later expanded its work to diseases including cholera, brucellosis, tularemia and anthrax. She was working at an institute dedicated to researching plague when she developed severe pneumonia and died. Yet authorities say there is no evidence so far linking her illness to the pathogens handled at her workplace. Did she die from pneumonic plague? It has not been confirmed as yet. Rospotrebnadzor said Shipilova was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown aetiology and that extensive testing found no microorganisms associated with her professional activities. The Independent and local media have raised the possibility that she died from pneumonic plague, but those reports remain unconfirmed. Why were people quarantined? Authorities placed the hospital in Shelekhov, where Shipilova was treated under quarantine and began monitoring people who had been in contact with her. Anna Popova, head of Rospotrebnadzor, travelled to the Irkutsk region and met regional officials as authorities coordinated their response. Governor Igor Kobzev said identified contacts had been placed under medical observation and that they were showing no signs of illness, with laboratory tests returning negative results. News agency Associated Press reported that two contacts tested positive for a virus that causes a common cold and two others for Covid-19. Other people who were tested were negative, according to the agency. Why are there accusations of a cover-up? The Telegraph reported that local pro-Kremlin websites and some local officials deleted posts referring to the suspected plague case. One local authority reportedly advised residents against travelling to Shelekhov after unofficial information about a possible plague infection emerged, before the post was removed. The Guardian reported that Alexey Tsydenov, head of neighbouring Buryatia, initially wrote that Shipilova had died of plague before editing his post to say she had possibly died of the disease. Authorities in Baikalsk also briefly advised residents not to travel to Shelekhov, citing unofficial information about a possible plague infection, before deleting the post. Hamish de Bretton Gordon, a former commanding officer of the UKs Joint Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Regiment, told The Telegraph that Russian authorities had clammed up over the incident. We should be worried about whats happened in Russia because plague has a long history of causing mayhem, he said.For a lab technician working with plague to die from plague is extraordinary. She should have been vaccinated, there should have been medical countermeasures, he said. What do Russian authorities say? Russian authorities have repeatedly rejected speculation that there is a confirmed plague outbreak. Rospotrebnadzor said Shipilova died from pneumonia of unknown aetiology and that tests found no microorganisms linked to her professional work. The agency also said it had found no incidents involving pathogenic microorganisms at the institute, Reuters reported. Kobzev said there had been no new cases of anti-plague institute staff seeking medical attention and described the situation as stable, according to Reuters. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged the public and media to rely on Rospotrebnadzors official statements rather than rumours and speculation. Former Rospotrebnadzor chief Gennady Onishchenko also said the infection was most likely not the plague, CNN reported, while cautioning that even if plague were confirmed, he did not expect it to spread. What happened to people who came into contact with her? AP reported that two people who had been in contact with Shipilova tested positive for a virus that causes a common cold and two others tested positive for Covid-19. Other people tested were negative, according to the agency. Kobzev said those identified as contacts were under medical observation and had shown no symptoms, with laboratory testing returning negative results. What is pneumonic plague? Pneumonic plague is one of the three main forms of plague caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It affects the lungs and can be transmitted from person to person through respiratory droplets. It is the most serious form of plague and can become fatal quickly if untreated, but it can be treated with antibiotics when detected early. The disease is associated with the same bacterium that caused historic outbreaks of bubonic plague, including the Black Death. Plague remains endemic in parts of Siberia and the Russian Far East, where Yersinia pestis occurs naturally among small wild mammals and their fleas. Human cases in Russia are rare. Why is the US monitoring the case? US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was monitoring the situation but did not believe there was cause for alarm.Were watching and monitoring it closely. I dont think its cause for alarm, Rubio said. He added that if an infection were to spread, it could spread quickly. The Financial Times reported that US officials were closely monitoring the suspected case, while The Guardian reported that the US was watching developments because of the potential for a respiratory infection to spread. With inputs from agencies

articleTitle: Keralam to install Rs 10 sanitary napkin vending machines at public places
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Women and Child Development, Labour, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development Minister Bindu Krishna will inaugurate the project at the Thampanoor KSRTC Bus Terminal in Thiruvananthapuram at 5 pm on Tuesday.
description: As part of the pilot project, sanitary napkin vending machines and incinerators will be installed at 14 KSRTC terminals and depots across the state, the release said.
body_raw: Sanitary napkins will soon be available through vending machines at select public places in Keralam, with the Women and Child Development Department launching an initiative aimed at improving access to menstrual hygiene products for women and girls during travel. The initiative, called WOMN - Women on the Move Menstrual Need-s, will begin on Tuesday as part of the state governments 100-day action programme, according to an official press release. As part of the pilot project, sanitary napkin vending machines and incinerators will be installed at 14 KSRTC terminals and depots across the state, the release said. Each packet will contain three sanitary napkins and will cost Rs 10. Incinerators will be provided at the locations to facilitate the disposal of used sanitary napkins, it said. The project will subsequently target major tourist destinations, KSRTC terminals and depots and other public places across the state, according to the department. Women and Child Development Minister Bindu Krishna will inaugurate the project at the Thampanoor KSRTC Bus Terminal in Thiruvananthapuram on Tuesday. With PTI inputs
