articleTitle: ‘If citizens being removed, what is purpose of SIR?’ Bombay High Court asks Election Commission
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay High Court questions purpose of Special Intensive Revision exercise if citizens face exclusion from voters list, flags voter Catch-22 over rejected address change forms
description: Hearing a petition where names of six members of a Goa family had been deleted from the electoral rolls after their Form 8 applications for a change of address were rejected, the High Court of Bombay at Goa said the voter is facing “a Catch-22 situation” in this matter
body_raw: Stating that the Election Commission has an obligation to ensure all citizens are on the electoral rolls, the High Court of Bombay at Goa on Monday asked what the purpose of this entire SIR process if citizens are being removed from the voters list. If citizens are excluded, what will we do with SIR? the HC asked. Hearing a petition where names of six members of a family had been deleted from the electoral rolls after their Form 8 applications for a change of address were rejected, the HC said the voter is facing a Catch-22 situation in this matter. A division bench of Justices Amit S Jamsandekar and Valmiki Menezes said, If a gentleman comes and says I have shifted, I am giving you ECI Form 8 for change of address. You cannot tell him I will not hear you.You cant do that. because the roll that is being referred to in Rule 21 Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 is the existing roll, not the draft roll. It said, Everything must be seen qua the existing roll, otherwise the voter has absolutely no way out of this. look at this complete Catch-22 situation before him. If he gives Form 6, it is a false declaration. He gives Form 8.you say I cannot accept it and you must give the enumeration. He says I dont want to give the enumeration. But Rule 21 says you have to hear him before removing his name. not from the draft, from the original roll. The bench said the ECI has an obligation to ensure all the citizens are on the list. If citizens are excluded, what will we do with SIR? If citizens are being removed from the list, then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process?, it asked. The petitioners-Paresh Salgaoncar and five members of his family-had moved to a new house in the same Santa Cruz Assembly constituency eight years ago and were instructed by the booth-level officer BLO to submit Form 8 for change of address. The petitioners submitted that the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer informed them that their EPICs Electors Photo Identity Cards had been deleted from the rolls and consequently, their Form 8 applications could not be processed. The only recourse available was to submit Form 6 which is for new voters since there was no option in ERONET for reviewing or restoring the deleted EPICs. No voter should sign a false declaration .in the enumeration form, the declarations are such that I have to declare in a pre-filled form for a ward, where I used to reside.I have to make a declaration that please include me in that same place, and I state that I am not there in any other place. How will a person make such a declaration when he knows he is in another place? The moment he makes such a declaration, he is open to prosecution, the court said. We are asking this. Why will he sign this? This is a false statement.Why should he give a false declaration? No voter should sign this, the bench said. The Election Commission of India ECI told the court that the guidelines clearly state that if someone has not submitted the enumeration form, their name is liable to be deleted from the roll. In case an elector is unable to submit their filled-in enumeration form within the specified time, they may fill Form 6 along with declaration for inclusion during the claims and objection period.Ordinarily, Form 8 is by a person whose name is there in the draft roll, but says I am no longer residing here and I have shifted. He submits his Form 8 because it refers to an existing residence on the roll. So, if you are not there on the draft roll only, what entry am I transferring under Form 8? I cant transfer a non-existent entry, the counsel for ECI said.

articleTitle: Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 4 Highlights: Ajay Devgn film grosses Rs 303 cr, set for further drop on Tuesday
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 4
description: The worldwide gross of Ajay Devgn-starrer Drishyam The Conclusion currently stands at Rs 303 crore.
body_raw: After a record-breaking opening weekend, Ajay Devgns Drishyam The Conclusion witnessed a sharp drop at the box office on its first Monday. On Day 4, the film earned Rs 21 crore net from 16,274 shows, marking a 65.6 per cent drop from its Sunday collection of Rs 61 crore. This took the films India net collection to Rs 197 crore and domestic gross to Rs 237 crore. Its worldwide gross currently stands at Rs 303 crore. On Day 4, Drishyam The Conclusion recorded an overall Hindi occupancy of 24.71 per cent. The film saw its highest occupancy during the night shows at 38.38 per cent, followed by evening shows at 26.85 per cent, afternoon shows at 20.69 per cent and morning shows at 12.92 per cent. Also Read - Ajay Devgns Drishyam 3 writer says wrote 100 versions of film Friends tried to bribe me for ending Drishyam 3 has already delivered the biggest opening day and opening weekend of Ajay Devgns career, while also emerging as the second-highest opening weekend grosser of 2026, behind only Dhurandhar 2. It has also surpassed the entire lifetime theatrical gross of the Malayalam original. Jeethu Josephs Drishyam 3, starring Mohanlal and released on May 21, collected Rs 237.70 crore worldwide across its full theatrical run. Drishyam The Conclusion, directed by Abhishek Pathak, stars Ajay as Vijay Salgaonkar, reprising his role as the cable operator whose elaborate cover-up of a crime forms the backbone of the franchise. Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor and Ishita Dutta return in their respective roles, while Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj join the cast.

articleTitle: Pakistan appoint Sahibzada Farhan as new T20I captain, drop Salman Ali Agha from squad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pakistan appointed Sahibzada Farhan as the new T20I captain in place of Salman Ali Agha. (AP)
description: Farhan, the top run-scorer at the 2026 T20 World Cup, takes over for the Sri Lanka series; Shaheen Shah Afridi retains ODI captaincy
body_raw: Pakistan have named top-order batter Sahibzada Farhan as their new T20I captain, with the 30-year-old taking over from Salman Ali Agha starting with the upcoming series against Sri Lanka. Agha, who led the side at the 2026 T20 World Cup, has been dropped from the 15-member squad for the shortest format. Agha is set to remain part of the ODI setup, where Shaheen Shah Afridi retains the captaincy for the tri-nation series against England and Sri Lanka. Former captain Babar Azam has also been included in the ODI squad. Pakistans three-match T20 series against Sri Lanka begins on Friday, October 9 in Rawalpindi, while the ODI tri-series will begin on October 18 and feature a double round-robin format, with the top two teams facing off in the final on October 31 at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. Farhan, who top-scored at the T20 World Cup earlier this year, led Pakistan to a silver medal at the recently concluded 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. He scored 383 runs at a strike rate of 160 to become the player with the most runs in a single edition of a T20 World Cup. The right-handed opener is among several players from that squad retained for the senior side, with Abdul Samad, Saim Ayub, Hasan Nawaz, Arafat Minhas, Maaz Sadaqat, Abrar Ahmed, Sufiyan Moqim and Mohammad Salman Mirza also included. While Farhan has been named captain the shortest format, he is not part of a 16-member ODI squad. From the squad that last played the format and beat Australia 2-1 in January this year, Abdul Samad, Rohail Nazir, Shamyl Hussain, Maaz Sadaqat and Ahmed Daniyal have also been left out. Fakhar Zaman, Faheem Ashraf, Razaullah, Saad Baig and Saim Ayub have been called up alongside Hasan Nawaz, who scored a fine 96 in the Asian Games final against India. Pakistans T20I squad Sahibzada Farhan c, Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Khawaja Nafay wk, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim. Pakistans ODI squad for tri-series Shaheen Shah Afridi c, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Babar Azam, Faheem Ashraf, Fakhar Zaman, Haris Rauf, Hasan Nawaz, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori wk, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saad Baig wk, Saim Ayub, Salman Ali Agha, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim.

articleTitle: Family member held for murder of two elderly women in Baramati, robbing gold jewellery
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police detained Vikas Ladkat after finding his movements suspicious.
description: Pune rural police Superintendent Sandeep Singh Gill formed eight teams to crack the murders.
body_raw: Pune rural police have arrested a family member in connection with the murder of two elderly women at their house in Baramati. Police identified the accused as Vikas alias Appa Rajendra Ladkat 25, a resident of Sherechiwadi village in Baramati taluka of Pune district. Indumati Maruti Ladkat 75 and Krushnabai Kundalik Ladkat 60 were found dead, with their throats slit, in an open space near their house in Sherechiwadi on September 29. About 50 grams of gold ornaments on their bodies were missing. Indumatis son Ganesh Ladkat 45 lodged the FIR at the Supa police station in Pune rural. Initial probe revealed that the two elderly women were murdered while they were sleeping, robbery being the motive. Pune rural police Superintendent Sandeep Singh Gill formed eight teams to crack the murders. Police teams checked about 200 history sheeters in Ahilyanagar, Solapur, Satara, Kolhapur, Pune and Beed districts in Maharashtra and Nipani in Karnataka. Police also checked CCTV cameras installed at various locations for leads. Simultaneously, the police also kept watch on the movements of people in Sherechiwadi village, especially those residing near the deceased women. Police detained Vikas Ladkat after finding his movements suspicious. During interrogation, Vikas admitted that he murdered the two women, who were his relatives, by attacking them with an axe and then looted their gold ornaments, a press release issued on Monday stated. Police arrested Vikas under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS sections 103 1 murder, 309 4, 332 c, on October 4. Police also recovered the robbed ornaments from his possession. Assistant police inspector Shashikant Shelke of Supa police station said, A court has remanded the accused in police custody for five days. He is a distant family member of the deceased woman. Probe so far has revealed that he was debt-ridden. So he killed the elderly women when they were alone and robbed their gold jewellery. In the past he was booked in a criminal case when he was a minor. Further investigation is on.

articleTitle: From calling for peace in Russia-Ukraine and beyond, Delhi is now working for it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: From calling for peace, Delhi is now working for it
description: Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has said that, among the proposals Kyiv has received, India’s is the “most comprehensive”; President Putin has said PM Modi “constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict” and has “very good ideas”.
body_raw: By all accounts, India has stepped into a more proactive role vis-a-vis the Russia-Ukraine war. Since the conflict began in February 2022, New Delhi has consistently urged restraint, with PM Narendra Modi saying to Russian President Vladimir Putin in September that year that this is not an era of war. Now, Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has said that, among the proposals Kyiv has received, Indias is the most comprehensive President Putin has said PM Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has acknowledged that India has gone beyond advocacy and is talking to both sides. The shift from calling for peace to working for it is welcome. Delhi must build on it. On this front, Indias interests align with those of the world. Strikes on ports and vessels by both Russia and Ukraine, two major grain exporters, have left farmers in both countries vulnerable and increased the risk of a global food shock. Minister Jaishankar referred to this a few days ago when he warned of a major food crisis in the coming months, in addition to the already significant fertiliser shortages caused by conflicts in Eastern Europe and West Asia. The Ukraine war has also disrupted European energy markets, while Indias purchases of Russian oil have strained ties with the US. An end to the war, or even a de-escalation, would ease such pressures. Going forward, Delhi would do well to focus on specific issues such as grain and energy, rather than sweeping questions involving territory or security guarantees. Both sides have immediate and shared interests in these areas, which means something can be agreed upon without first resolving the harder questions. Even if it does not exert as much leverage over Ukraine or Russia as the US and China, respectively, India can demonstrate that it is actively working towards getting the warring parties to talk. A record of even-handed diplomacy would also answer critics who see India as too close to Russia, a relationship that has drawn scrutiny, not least over oil purchases, for nearly five years.

articleTitle: In Nobel Prize for medicine, a single cell, a flash of light, a breakthrough
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A single cell, a flash of light, a breakthrough
description: In awarding the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Hegemann, American neuroscientist Karl Deisseroth and German biophysicist Georg Nagel, the Nobel Assembly has recognised what is effectively a new era in neuroscience.
body_raw: In the beginning was a single cell, instinctively moving towards light so that the business of living may continue. For German photobiologist Peter Hegemann, studying the microscopic alga known as Chlamydomonas in the 1990s, the question was straightforward How did this simple organism respond to light in one-twentieth of the time that it took the human eye to see? The simplicity of the algas biology, it turned out, was the key needed to unlock the complexities of the human brain, from how different organs are controlled to where feelings, memory, even consciousness itself, reside. In awarding the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Hegemann, American neuroscientist Karl Deisseroth and German biophysicist Georg Nagel, the Nobel Assembly has recognised what is effectively a new era in neuroscience. Hegemann, along with Nagel, discovered channelrhodopsin, a protein that enables Chlamydomonas to react to light in half a millisecond - compared to the 10 milliseconds that it takes the human eye to process information. Deisseroth then used it to develop a light switch that can control nerve cells, thus inaugurating the field of optogenetics. The pinprick of illumination that was made by Hegemanns curiosity has since expanded to shed light on neural pathways that could once only be guessed at. Researchers have been able to identify the precise circuits that control functions and behaviours, from why some people develop a greater preference for sugar to how the rhythms of the heart can affect emotions and how the brain stores information about fear, anxiety and depression. It offers hope for a greater understanding of psychiatric and neurological disorders - areas of darkness that could soon become less intimidating.

articleTitle: Brazil elections: Why a jailed ex-president’s son is leading race, and the Trump factor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Opposition presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro in Brasilia, Brazil, Oct. 4. (AP Photo/Eraldo Peres)
description: Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for an attempted 2023 coup in Brazil. How did his son become the frontrunner to lead the country? And what has been Trump’s role in the elections for South America’s biggest country and economy?
body_raw: Brazil voted in the first round of its presidential elections on Sunday October 4, with incumbent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva and Flvio Bolsonaro receiving 45 and 47 of the vote, respectively. Since neither won over 50 of the vote but still secured the most votes among all candidates, they will go head-to-head in another round of voting on October 25. Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who won the 2018 elections and rejected the 2022 poll results after losing to Lula. His supporters stormed government offices in the capital, Brasilia, evoking visuals of US President Donald Trumps supporters attacking the US Capitol building in 2021. This is only one of many ways Bolsonaro and Trump are linked, with Trump backing him strongly over the years and expressing solidarity with him over supposed witch hunts for not accepting the results. Today, Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence in relation to the attempted 2023 coup. How did his son become the frontrunner to lead Brazil? And what has been Trumps role in the elections for the continents biggest country and economy? Who is Flvio Bolsonaro? Flvio, 45, is a lawyer by training and Jair Bolsonaros eldest son. A senator from Rio de Janeiro, he bears a striking physical resemblance to his father, which may or may not lend him a political advantage given Bolsonaro Sr.s reputation as a polarising figure. Take the 2022 election, the closest in Brazils history, where Lula received 50.9 of the votes against Bolsonaros 49.1. When Jair first came to power as the leader of Brazils Liberal Party LP, his supporters saw him as a conservative, pro-business politician who would tell it like it is, similar to other populist right-wing leaders globally. Among his key policies was relaxing protections for the Amazon rainforest to encourage commercial activities. He vowed to combat corruption, which was noteworthy since his own political rise was fuelled by mainstream political figures in Brazil getting implicated in major corruption scandals. Bolsonaro is also known to make homophobic and misogynistic statements, telling a woman legislator who accused him of being a rapist I wouldnt rape you because you dont deserve it. He was also criticised for his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic, with Brazil having the second-highest death toll among countries, after the United States. As the Financial Times put it in a profile of the Bolsonaro family, Flvio is the self-styled moderate of the family a vaccinated Bolsonaro, in his own words. In the constant shadow of his father, he treads a difficult line. He all but acknowledges being an inferior substitute. How can you compare Pels son to Pel himself? Flvio asked the FT in an interview earlier this year during which he refused to sit behind his fathers desk in the party HQ. The Bolsonaros have enjoyed voter support among more well-off groups, the more conservative Evangelical Christians, and the countrys southern regions. On the other hand, Lula, 80, is a veteran socialist leader now contesting for a fourth term with supporters such as Catholics, progressives and poorer groups. Flvio has criticised Lula for not being tough enough on crime and drug gangs. Lula was also president when the first BRIC meeting comprising Brazil, Russia, India and China was held in 2009 South Africa was not a member of the grouping then. And what is Trumps role in the Brazilian elections? Since Jair Bolsonaros first term, which partly overlapped with the first Trump administration, Trump has publicly supported him owing to their similar ideology and disdain for critics. He met Flvio earlier this year, calling him a smart young man, who loves his country, Brazil, very much. Within months of his second term, Trump announced 50 tariffs on imports from Brazil in July 2025 for threats to the US. The executive order also noted that Brazilian officials were persecuting Bolsonaro and that this contributes to the deliberate breakdown in the rule of law in Brazil. Trump has earlier warmed up to other strongman leaders globally, with vocal support for those from South America. Another prominent example is Argentinas Javier Milei. This approach is also in line with the US National Security Strategy, released in November 2025. It laid out intentions for the US to be dominant in the Western Hemisphere, and its effects were seen in the military capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January this year. As The New York Times said of South America in a recent report, Candidates aligned with President Trump on issues like fighting drug gangs and woke ideology have won the last seven elections in the region, with Brazil the biggest remaining prize. This period of rightward political shift comes not too long after a pink tide around 2022. The term was first used around the early 21st century, with the election of Hugo Chavez in Venezuela, followed by a roughly decade-long period that saw many countries reject neo-liberalism in favour of socialism hence pink, rather than Communisms red. Oliver Stuenkel, Visiting Scholar at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington, wrote back in 2022 for Americas Quarterly that this wave would be more short-lived. His reasons ranged from greater geopolitical instability translating into tougher economic circumstances for governments to their declining interest in maintaining a sense of regional unity and convergence. Todays leftist presidents are less likely to prioritize ties to their neighbors because they are less relevant from an economic point of view. Intraregional trade amounted to over 20 of Latin Americas total exports in 2008, but this share has declined by a third and is set to fall further as commodity exports to China are on the rise, he wrote.

articleTitle: SEBI’s ‘Jagrook’ call: Don’t follow tips, understand before you invest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SEBI’s ‘Jagrook’ call: Don’t follow tips, understand before you invest
description: SEBI urges investors to avoid tips and finfluencers, understand products and risks and make informed investment decisions
body_raw: Launching its nationwide investor-awareness initiative, Project Jagrook, from Chandigarh on Monday, SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey urged investors to beware of investment frauds and use regulated products, channels and entities instead of relying on anonymous tips, finfluencers or exaggerated claims about returns. Pandey advised investors to follow five basic habits - invest only in products they understand, start early and stay invested to allow compounding to work, diversify their investments and not mistake fixed returns for risk-free investments. Instead of asking, Which product gives the highest return?, first ask, What am I investing for? he said. Stating that more savers are becoming investors, Pandey said mutual fund assets have grown sharply from 12 lakh crore in 2015-16 to around 87 lakh crore today, at an average annual growth rate of about 21 per cent over the past 10 years. Our message is simple Do not invest because someone told you to. Do not invest because everyone else is investing. Invest, because you understand, he said. Referring to a large-scale survey on awareness of securities-market products and actual market participation, Pandey said only 36 per cent of investors had high or moderate knowledge of the securities market. The survey found that awareness was far wider than actual participation. While 63 per cent of households were aware of at least one securities-market product, only about 9.5 per cent actually participated in the market, he said. It also highlighted a clear urban-rural divide, with securities-market participation standing at 15 per cent in urban India compared with only 6 per cent in rural India. Fewer than one per cent of those surveyed had attended an investor-awareness programme. Yet, 91 per cent of those who attended found it useful. The challenge, therefore, is not only content but also reach, Pandey said. He added that people wanted to learn in Hindi as well as regional languages, with social media, mobile apps and television or digital advertising emerging as the preferred channels. Awareness of SEBIs investor-centric initiatives also remained low. Only 6 per cent of the respondents knew about SEBIs grievance-redressal mechanisms, although 88 per cent of those who had used them were satisfied with the outcome, he said. Speaking about Project Jagrook, Pandey, an alumnus of Panjab University, said, The success of the project will not be measured by the number of people who view it, but by the number of informed investors it creates. He emphasised that the initiative aims to make investing simple and understandable by stripping away complex financial jargon. Sandip Pradhan, Whole-Time Member, SEBI Kamlesh Chandra Varshney, Whole-Time Member, SEBI Sundeep Sikka, Chairman, Association of Mutual Funds in India AMFI and PU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Meenakshi Goyal and UBS Chairperson Prof. Meena Sharma were present at the pan-India launch hosted by the University Business School UBS. Addressing the launch of SEBIs regional office in Chandigarh, SEBI Whole-Time Member Sandip Pradhan highlighted Real Estate Investment Trusts REITs and Infrastructure Investment Trusts InvITs as opportunities for retail investors to participate in the real estate sector. PU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Meenakshi Goyal highlighted the universitys commitment to academic excellence and interdisciplinary collaboration, and said the university was focused on transforming knowledge into life skills beyond the classroom.

articleTitle: Sonos Play review: A premium portable speaker that sounds superb
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sonos Play review
description: A premium portable speaker with excellent sound and smart software, the Sonos Play suits buyers already invested in the ecosystem.
body_raw: If actors have their entourage, I have a backpack full of gadgets that I may or may not use on a work trip, but I like to lug them around anyway. These days, even security staff ask me what I would do with so many devices, and I simply smile. In fact, when I was returning from San Francisco last week, a security staff member noticed the Sonos Play I had with me and asked me to play the late Dolly Partons I Will Always Love You on the speaker. I think the staff liked the Sonos Play. I am sure you may be wondering why I carry a portable speaker with me. Well, I start my day listening to music and end it with music. Hotel rooms can get lonely at times, and music helps me feel happy and comforted. The Sonos Play is portable, but depending on where you put it, the sound it produces comes close to what you hear from home speakers. But of course, Sonos Play is a very different beast designed to be mobile, but at the same time it can be part of your home entertainment system if you live within Sonos ecosystem. With a brand-new Sonos 27 operating system, a redone app and the Play portable speaker, they complement each other, and I tested them over several weeks. Heres my review of the Sonos Play. What Sonos Play Price Rs 35,999 Differentiated design Ive been a Sonos fan since the brands inception. The way it designs its speakers and audio products reminds me of Apple in the 2000s. Sonos avoids cheaply designed products and instead uses a design language that is part Japanese and part American, with fine detailing that also has a touch of European finesse. The Play follows the design of a compact bookshelf speaker. I could see how Sonos has taken bits and pieces from the Move 2 and the Era 100 and incorporated them into the Play. What I liked about the Sonos Play is that it has a rugged feel, but you wouldnt immediately notice it. The speaker has heft its dense, and you get the sense its built with premium internals. At 1.3 kg, the Play isnt featherlight, but I had no trouble travelling with it. However, after using the Play for weeks, I feel the speaker is designed for home use, an apartment balcony, or a friends place. The speaker has a minimalist design and clean looks, and it blends effortlessly wherever you put it, whether thats a hotel room, bedroom, kitchen or living space. Its like a luxury T-shirt with no visible logos understated and a premium bespoke experience. The oval-shaped speaker, which came in black for my review unit, is also available in white. It has a rubberised top with playback buttons, volume controls, and a button to activate a voice assistant. You can choose between Sonos own voice assistant and Amazon Alexa. It also has a dedicated Bluetooth button and a hardware microphone switch to turn the microphone on or off. A small LED cluster on top indicates the connection, battery, microphone, and mute status. The Play is primarily a Wi-Fi-based speaker, but it also supports Bluetooth 5.3 for use away from home, allowing you to stream music from your phone or another device. The speaker has a large 35Wh battery that you can easily replace at home. It offers up to 24 hours of Bluetooth playback and easily lasts a full day of Wi-Fi listening at 65 per cent volume. The portable speaker sits on its wireless charging base, but can be easily lifted and carried outdoors. No cables or setup hassles needed. Sadly, the USB-C power adapter isnt, so you need to buy an 18W charger separately or greater USB-C power adaptor, which needs to be 45W to support fast charging. I used my iPhone charger, and it works, but you still need a dedicated charger just for the Play. Ecosystem advantage and the brand new Sonos 27 OS Perhaps the biggest advantage of getting the Play is its integration with the Sonos ecosystem. If you buy the Play, you can easily integrate it with the rest of your Sonos speakers and products. In my case, Sonos provided two Play units, which I grouped together just like other Sonos speakers for multi-room audio. With support for virtually any music streaming service, you can stream music over the internet and control playback through the Sonos app, Spotify Connect, or Apple AirPlay 2. You can also link two Play speakers together to create a stereo pair. And thats exactly what I did. Everything changed the moment the second Play was up and running. It took me less than 10 minutes to set up the second Play and pair the speakers. More on the audio experience later. Beyond reviewing the Play, I was keen to test the new Sonos 27 operating system and the redesigned app. The app recently received a major redesign alongside the launch of the Sonos 27 audio operating system. Adding a speaker from the get-go is easy, with the app automatically detecting it. You can also add surround speakers and subwoofers through the app with just a few taps. The app shows your entire Sonos system and, separately, your rooms. You can go into each room to add or remove speakers, and you can easily switch audio from one room to another, as long as the speakers support Sonos 27. Whats great about Sonos 27 is that it brings together your music services and controls, including Spotify, Apple Music, Bluetooth, AirPlay, voice commands, and AI assistance, under one operating system. It features Sonos Voice, which lets you ask Sonos for what you want using natural voice conversations. It also supports AI assistants such as Claude and Gemini to help you play music around your home and interact with your Sonos system. In the future, the new operating system will allow users to create their own AI agents. Sonos 27 is an interesting proposition if you already live within the Sonos ecosystem, much like many of us do within Apples ecosystem. It all comes down to how much you are willing to invest in Sonos products, because the more you add, the more youll see the advantages of Sonos 27. Exceptional audio quality The Sonos Play features three Class-H digital amplifiers, two angled tweeters, and a single mid-woofer for a balanced sound. It also supports automatic Trueplay tuning, which adjusts the EQ based on the room, while the Sonos app lets you manually tweak the bass, treble, and loudness. I spent most of my time testing the single unit of the Play, listening to music. It has that signature Sonos sound that I am familiar with, having reviewed almost every Sonos product over the past few years. But, frankly, there is no real sweet spot when it comes to the Play. What I think Sonos has nailed is that, no matter where you put the speaker in a room, you get the same sound everywhere. I cant explain how good music sounds on the Play, since its also very subjective. That said, the Play offers excellent tonal separation, well-defined mids, detailed highs, and punchy bass. Vocals sound impressive too, although I felt the speaker lacks deep bass. When I set up two Plays as a stereo pair bringing the total cost to Rs 71,998, I was immediately impressed. Using two speakers in stereo is wonderful, and the improvement in sound quality was immediately noticeable. The Play already does a great job delivering clear sound from anywhere in the room, but two speakers in stereo added a ton of detail and depth that was missing from the mono output of a single Play. Final verdict The Sonos Play sounds remarkably good for its compact size, and it looks great on a shelf or countertop. But it certainly isnt cheap. Sure, it may be one of the best-sounding portable speakers on the market, but its also smart and easy to use. With Sonos 27, the new app, long software support and a replaceable battery, Sonos is certainly moving in the right direction. The Play comes close to being the perfect portable speaker, but it still lacks spatial audio support and Dolby Atmos.

articleTitle: India vs West Indies 1st T20I Live Streaming: When, where to watch IND vs WI match?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India vs West Indies 1st T20I Live Streaming: IND take on WI in Lucknow. (CREIMAS)
description: India take West Indies in the first of a five-match series at the Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow on Tuesday.
body_raw: Fresh from their 2026 Asian Games gold, India will look to carry the momentum into the T20I leg when they face West Indies in the first of a five-match series at the Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow on Tuesday. articleTitle: Campus polls return in Odisha after 8 years. Why all 3 parties are hopeful
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Campus polls return in Odisha after 8 years. Why all 3 parties are hopeful
description: The Mohan Majhi government announced the revival of student body polls in the state’s universities and colleges, signalling the return of student politics after an eight-year hiatus.
body_raw: Campuses across Odisha are bracing for a fresh bout of political activities after the state government announced the return of students union polls in degree colleges and universities after an eight-year gap on Monday. Student wings of major political parties such as the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ABVP, Biju Chhatra Janata Dal BCJD and National Students Union of India NSUI swung into action, reviving their campus networks and stepping up outreach activities. The students union polls are also being closely watched by all three major political parties, which see the event as an opportunity to connect with the Gen Z voters, understand their concerns and cultivate their support. For political parties, success in the campus polls could also be viewed as a measure of their acceptance among young voters and an indication of the extent of support they enjoy among the student community. According to a notification issued by the state higher education department on Monday, students union elections will be held in all colleges on October 15. The states higher education minister, Suryabanshi Suraj, announced the decision following a meeting with chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi. The decision to hold campus polls is a key step towards nurturing youth leadership in our state. Reviving campus polls was also one of our major promises in the election manifesto. After our party formed the government, it took us some time to review the situation on campuses. This year, the poll will be held across campuses, said the higher education minister. The decision to complete the entire process within 10 days has been taken to prevent violence on the campuses, said officials. Campus polls in Odisha were last held in 2017. The students wings of various political parties were also demanding the revival of student body polls, with the National Student Union of India - the students wing of the Congress-meeting the higher education minister to demand student body polls. Euphoria swept campuses following the announcement of the students union polls the ABVP, the student wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS, launched marches across campuses to thank the state government for the decision. The decision has also triggered a political slugfest, with BJP spokesperson Anil Biswal criticising the former BJD government for not holding campus polls for a long period. He said the previous BJD government didnt want to encourage youth leadership. BCJD president Ipsita Sahoo said the campus poll was suspended during the BJD regime due to various reasons such as COVID-19 and that it had always supported student body polls.

articleTitle: He stood beside his mahout’s body. Five years later, Kerala bids him farewell
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 'Gentle giant', fixture of temple festivals: Keralam bids adieu to elephant Brahmadathan
description: Pallatt Brahmadathan was brought to Kerala 28 years ago from Arunachal Pradesh. His owner said the elephant had never attacked any person in its almost three decades in the state.
body_raw: For decades, Pallatt Brahmadathan was a constant presence in temple festivals across Kerala. Only last year, the tusker had carried the thidambu or sacred replica of presiding deity Paramekkavu Devi during the Thrissur Pooram last year. On Monday, scores of people gathered at the premises of its owner, Pallattu Rajesh, at Erattupetta in Kottayam to pay their last tributes to the gentle giant known for its calm demeanour. Brahmadathan, the 54-year-old male elephant, died after being struck by lightning on Sunday evening. As Brahamadathan lay motionless at the Pallatt family compound, flowers and wreaths piled up and sandalwood sticks burned as grieving admirers stood around. Brahmadathans owner Rajesh, his family members, and mahout Sarath grieved inconsolably near the carcass when a crane lifted it for post-mortem examination. Brahmadathan was brought to Kerala 28 years ago from Arunachal Pradesh. His first owner in the state was Pappalaparambil Pothen Varghese of Puthuppally in Kottayam. At that time, it was known as Puthuppally Brahmadathan. Sixteen years ago, the Pallatts, another family of traditional elephant owners in the city, took over its guardianship. Ever since, Brahmadathan had been carrying their family name. Brahamadathans imposing presence at many annual festivals in Keralam had made him a social media star of sorts with a number of its reels being shared widely. Like a family member Recalling his relationship with the elephant, owner Rajesh said, My three brothers and I were managing Brahmadathan. After the festival season, we used to tether him at our house compound. Each time, before he left for a festival procession, Brahmadathan used to greet my aged mother. He had become a member of our family over the years. Rajesh said Brahmadathan was loved by both young and the old alike. I can proudly say that Brahmadathan had never attacked any person in his 28 years of life in Keralam, he said. As Brahmadathan passes into the lore of Keralas domestic elephants, its bond with its mahouts was fondly recalled by elephant lovers. In 2021, when his previous mahout Damodaran Nair alias Omanachettan died, Brahmadathan had stood beside his body. It was seen raising its trunk towards Omanachettan, giving a final farewell to the man who had been his shadow for 25 years.

articleTitle: ‘No land for burial’: Chhattisgarh village resolution raises concerns for Christians
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 'No land for Christian burials': In Chhattisgarh, gram sabha resolution raises concerns
description: Of 2,000 residents of this village in Sukma district, only 21 families with 75 members in total follow Christianity. Community members say some groups have been misusing the split verdict by the Supreme Court in a burial rights case earlier this year to trouble them
body_raw: At Punpalli, a village in Chhattisgarhs Sukma district, a new banner has come up prohibiting the entry of pastors for religious activities. The notice further states that the village will not allow any event being held for the purpose of conversions or any other religious activity. The development follows a list of 12 resolutions taken recently by the village panchayat. However, it is the resolution not written in the banner that has become a source of greater worry for people from the Christian community in this village of 2,000 residents. It one of the resolutions says that the village will not give any land for burials to tribals, who follow Christianity, Madkam Bhima, a Janpat member elected from Punpalli village, said. Bhima said that till now, a total of four villages have made such resolutions in Sukma, including Punpalli. It started from Errabore a few months ago followed by my village Polampalli. It will be done gradually in all villages, he said. This village has only 21 families with 75 members in total who follow Christianity. If the resolution holds, the families will have to travel over 13 kilometers to Dhornapal for burials or to Sukma headquarters, which is over 40 kilometers away. When asked if the diktat had a legal basis, Bhima said, Yes, we are adhering to the PESA law. We are not violating any law. During the October 2 meeting, the Punpalli Gram Sabha cited the Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, 1996 PESA, as the village is covered under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, as it passed the resolution. The board that was put up soon after read According to PESA, the Gram Sabha has the right to protect its cultural identity, traditions, customs and social heritage. The villagers believe that activities related to religious conversion through inducement, pressure or any other means affect our traditional tribal culture, social unity and cultural identity. Therefore, it has been decided that any event related to religious conversion by outsiders, religious preaching whose objective is to convert people to another religion will not be acceptable. However, advocate Sudeep Shrivastava, who has been raising such issues in the region, said, The entry of any Indian citizen in a village cannot be prohibited. A person can profess his religion in any village. As far as others joining his prayers is concerned, the villagers have the right to voluntarily do so. If there is a resolution that says land will not be given for any person living in the village, who professes Christianity, for burials, it is unconstitutional. Nukesh Baghel, vice president of Bastar District Rural Christian Service Committee, said, This is at least the 10th village in Bastar region which is doing this. Top courts split verdict being misused Nukesh said some groups have been misusing the split verdict by the Supreme Court in a burial rights case earlier this year. The Supreme Court, in February, had ordered an interim stay on forcible exhumation of tribal Christians. Following this, villagers are not allowing us to bury the bodies in the first place, Nukesh added. In January 2025, a two-bench judge was deciding a case wherein Ramesh Baghel, son of a deceased Christian pastor from Chhattisgarh, was seeking to bury his fathers body in his native village in Bastar district. While Justice B V Nagarathna pulled up the gram panchayat authorities for denying the man a burial in the tribal-majority village, and allowed Ramesh to do so in his private agricultural land, Justice S C Sharma was of the view that the statutory rules did not permit this and said the burial should be conducted at a common designated burial ground designated for Christians of three-four villages in Karkapal. Baghel had to carry out the burial rites in Karkapal under heavy security. The right-wing workers have made a team, which is going to villages where tribes and tribal Christians are living in peace. They provoke the tribals and get them to pass such resolutions, misusing the split verdict, said Nukesh. Soon after the SCs interim relief in February, we wrote to the Chhattisgarh DGP, requesting implementation of the top court order that forcible exhumation of bodies should not happen but it still takes place. We are documenting all these instances and will approach the court in the matter again, said advocate Degree Prasad Chouhan, convenor of Chhattisgarh Association for Justice and Equality. When contacted about the resolution, Mukund Thakur, CEO Zilla Panchayat, Sukma District, said, It was not in the agenda. If I receive a written complaint, I will take appropriate action after checking the legality of the matter as per the applicable rule.

articleTitle: Who modified what?: Supreme Court seeks ECI records on Form 6 change
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Will like to see who has modified what in records: Top court
description: The court’s observation comes after the ECI issued a statement on September 26 that the Form 6 would revert to the original version as per Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
body_raw: The Supreme Court said on Monday that it had not approved any modified version of Form 6, which is used to enroll new voters, and will examine Election Commission of India ECI records to know whether any change had been made and, if so, by who. The apex court was responding to a petition, which argued that a modified Form 6 was used for the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. The matter is being heard by a three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. The courts observation comes after the ECI issued a statement on September 26 that the Form 6 would revert to the original version as per Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, the ECI had said in its statement. The ECI was responding to the findings of an investigation by The Indian Express published on September 23 that two Election Commissioners in the three-member ECI objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar - from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. The Indian Express had first reported in July that the online Form 6 on the ECIs ECINet portal has started asking applicants whether they, or their parents or grandparents, were on the electoral roll of the last SIR - and that the form could not be submitted without an answer. On September 23, this newspaper reported that Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi had recorded on May 16 that the form cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and his colleague Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19 - the change in the portal went ahead regardless. On Monday, appearing for petitioner Shailendra Mani Tripathi, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy told the bench Let me give you an illustration.since it pertains to most recently, for instance, Delhi. Let us see how the SIR was conducted in Delhi. Form 6 has two new conditions added. Those Forms 6 were circulated. Neither the petitioner is now allowed to be on the roll. I got a notice also.based on this new Form 6, which cannot, under the schedule, be modified. The CJI said Lets be very clear. The modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let us also be clear that when the record will be produced, we will like to see who has modified what. The reference was to a related plea by Patna-resident Rakesh Kumar Singh who sought the summoning of original records of the ECI in this regard. Referring to The Indian Express investigation, Tripathis plea raised unprecedented Constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the Election Commission of India under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as exposed by documentary records published. The plea sought probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or a special investigation team headed by a retired judge of the Supreme Court into the CECs actions. These illegal acts include Unilateral Illegal Alteration of Statutory Form 6. Centralisation and Usurpation of Statutory Powers Depriving decentralised Electoral Registration Officers EROs of their statutory authority under Section 13B, 22, and 23 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and centralizing electoral roll management under the Director General of IT DG-IT in Delhi, the petition said. The plea also listed disenfranchisement due to software failures unauthorised subversion in West Bengal by filing over 16.10 lakh unauthorised appeals in the name of the ECI to purge citizens restored by 700 Judicial Officers, without the knowledge, authorization, or sanction of the other two Election Commissioners or the Chief Electoral Officer CEO of West Bengal. It raised the issues of bureaucratic usurpation and subversion of oversight and subversion of multi-member decision making. The plea contended that defying this binding majority, respondent number 3 CEC Gyanesh Kumar, acting in concert with respondent number 6 DG-IT, altered Form 6 digitally on the ECINet portal in July 2026. Referencing The Indian Express investigation, the plea said that on August 13, 2026, Commissioner Sandhu formally recorded that this alteration was unauthorised and illegal and was causing arbitrary harassment to young, eligible first-time electors, ordering its immediate withdrawal. Despite this, the unauthorised form was kept live on the portal. In May, in its judgement upholding the Bihar SIR, the Supreme Court had said that the ECI had residual powers to formulate appropriate documentation work regarding Form 6 to meet the needs of a special revision of electoral rolls, provided it was not arbitrary. Such authority, however, is not unbounded, the court had said then.

articleTitle: Karnataka CID probe puts forest dept in the dock over killing of three ‘poachers’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka CID probe puts forest dept in the dock over killing of three ‘poachers’
description: Cites autopsy reports, red-flags absence of weapon at site, removal of bodies
body_raw: A CID investigation into the killing of three alleged poachers in Karnatakas Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, bordering Tamil Nadu, by forest officials in the early hours of August 15 this year, has raised several questions autopsy reports indicate shots were fired at close range videography of crime scene does not show weapon alleged to have been found with the victims bodies were removed and crime scene not preserved. The CID has cited some of these findings, based on forensic and field evidence, in its plea to the Karnataka High Court for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the three forest officials - Shivaraja Sasalavada 29, beat forester to whom the shotgun used in the killings was issued by the forestdepartment Shivalinga Nayaka 51, anti-poaching forest watcher and Girisha R 29, anti-poaching camp watcher. The HC registered the CIDs plea on September 24, and the first hearing was held on September 30, when the court issued notice to the accused. The state forest department had said the three who were killed - Anthony Swamy 50, John Rose Peter 43 and Sebastian David Kumar 35, residents of villages on the fringes of a forest in Hanur in Karnataka - were poachers. It had said the men were armed and had first opened fire on the forest team, leading to retaliatory firing. A fourth person, Joseph Mahima Das alias Benjamin 45, had managed to escape. Based on his account, a police complaint was filed by Anthony Swamys wife, Lourde Mary. The police complaint had said the four men had gone to find lost cattle and were sleeping in the forest when forest officials opened fire on them. A CID investigation was ordered on August 24, after post-mortem reports found the shooting happened at close range, and, contrary to the forest departments claims, indicated that the victims were probably on the ground facing upwards when they were shot. On September 10, a local court in Hanur granted anticipatory bail to the forest officials, saying that the prosecutions case was based on circumstantial evidence. Opposing the bail, the CID, in its plea before the HC, has raised the following points It has cited the post-mortem report which said the cause of death was shotgun injuries, and the range of fire of shotgun injury was at close range. Citing the crime scene video recording by the forest department, the CID has said it does not disclose the existence of a weapon alleged to have been found with the deceased at the crime scene. The very fact that the dead bodies have been removed from the scene of the offence, that the crime scene was not preserved, and that the accused did not inform the nearest police as early as possible discloses that the officers have breached, the norms prescribed in a 1991 notification for incidents of firing by armed forest personnel, it has said. There is no material to indicate the deceased caused a threat or danger to the forest personnel to justify the action of killing three people at close range, the CID has said What autopsy reports said According to the autopsy report, Sebastian David Kumar, had two shotgun bullet entry wounds on his body. A shot on the left side of his chest revealed burningscorching and singeing of chest hair, indicative of a close range gunshot. The shot was fired front to back, above downwards and left to right, the report said. A second shot on his right thigh found burning scorching present and charring singeing and soot deposition. within and around the wound margins, indicating it was also fired at close range and in a below upwards direction, it said. Antony Swamy had a gunshot wound on the right side of his lower rib cage from a close range, the report said. The direction of the gunshot was above downwards, front to back and right to left. John Rose Peter had a single shotgun wound on his neck above the collar bone, fired at close range, with a top down direction. At the time of the incident, the hunters were at a higher point than the department staff at the Karadikalu rocks. Since the hunters were not visible to the department staff they were shot in the upper part of the waist when the staff retaliated. The staff did not act with any malicious intent, Karnataka Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy had said on August 17. The forest department had said the firing incident was the culmination of a night-long search to find poachers on the basis of actionable intelligence. They were conducting searches and when they chanced upon the persons who had come with the intent of poaching, both groups became alert. They have fired and we have fired, Hanur Assistant Conservator of Forest Mariswamy had said. Around 75 metres from the place where they were found, two bags of deer meat were found. It was the meat of the animal they hunted in the night, the Hanur ACF had said. Based on the evidence, it is certain that those who entered the forest were poachers, the Chief Conservator of Forests for Chamarajanagar district, Dr Malathi Priya, had said. A September 20, 1991, order grants immunity to forest personnel whenever they open fire to protect government property and life, but the immunity is subject to conditional use of firearms and reporting norms for shooting incidents.

articleTitle: Ukraine or West Asia, India backs all meaningful peace efforts: PM Modi
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ukraine or West Asia, India backs all meaningful peace efforts: PM
description: His statement came a day after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that India has got a “little more involved beyond advocacy” and is having conversations with both Russia and Ukraine.
body_raw: In his first remarks since India initiated a proposal to end the war between Russia and Ukraine, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Monday that India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace. In his statement after the bilateral meeting with visiting Swiss President Guy Parmelin, Modi said Both India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. We will continue to work together for global peace and stability. Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace. His statement came a day after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that India has got a little more involved beyond advocacy and is having conversations with both Russia and Ukraine, trying to be helpful on the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports and on non-attack possibilities. Last week, Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha had said that India has put forward a comprehensive and broad proposal to end the war, for the first time since the war began in February 2022. Elaborating on the context and rationale behind Indias move, Jaishankar said on Monday that Delhi started the latest round of conversations with Russia and Ukraine in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea. Speaking at an interactive session at the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, Jaishankar said In the month of July, there were attacks on civilian shipping by both Russia and Ukraine. And in the course of those attacks, some Indian sailors were killed, some were injured. We regard these attacks as completely unacceptable, whether it is in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, or the Gulf. So we protested very strongly to the Russians, to the Ukrainians. I myself took it up with the foreign ministers of both countries. And we started getting active initially to secure the maritime shipping and the mariners involved in that. Jaishankar said those conversations brought out the nature of the cargo being carried. And there was concern over grain exports which had come to a halt in the Black Sea. So the conversation developed into whether non-attack on shipping is good, but is there a possibility of facilitating the shipment of grain. So it got linked to energy. So it became a somewhat broader conversation, he said. He said those conversations are ongoing - including during Modis meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek on August 31, after which Jaishankar went to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Vlodymyr Zelenskyy in early September, followed by another discussion between Modi and Putin in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit on September 11-12. We still keep in touch with both sides. Its obviously not an easy situation. Its not something which anybody can say with a high degree of confidence that something is going to come out. But it seems definitely an effort worth making, Jaishankar said, adding that resolving concerns pertaining to grain, fertiliser and fuel are in the interest of India, as well as the Global South. We have the interests of the parties themselves, that if they can even agree on something of a limited nature, we feel that in the given circumstance thats a big positive, he said. From the very beginning, he said, India has held the view that this conflict is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. Therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties. there were actually negotiations in the early stages of the conflict. Though we have been maintaining for some time that both parties should come to the table, and there were a number of conferences where countries gathered to express their support for peace, but often they would gather in the absence of Russia, he said, in a reference to initiatives like the Swiss peace conference. However, he said, India has always believed that there wasnt any point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there. On October 1, Putin had said that Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas. Later that day, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Ukraines Foreign Minister Sybiha had said, We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is Indias proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role. He had said Ukraine was prepared to agree to an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, and was also considering an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Besides India, Ukraine has received proposals for a possible ceasefire from Turkey, Egypt and the United States. According to Sybiha, Ukraine will agree to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations, but also an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea. Modi has been raising the issue with Putin since 2022, when he first said this is not the era of war. In a meeting with Putin in Moscow in July 2024, Modi said peace talks do not succeed amid bombs, guns and bullets, and a solution cannot be found on the battlefield. On August 31 this year, Modi had urged Putin to move from endless war to end of war, when they met in Bishkek on the sidelines of the summit of SCO leaders.

articleTitle: Did not clear Form 6 change… can annul unilateral decisions: Supreme Court sends notice to Election Commission
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Did not clear Form 6 change... can annul unilateral decisions: SC sends notice to EC
description: The CJI assured that the court would examine the records and ensure that any decision taken without unanimity will have to go. “We can always annul any decision,” the CJI said.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India ECI on a petition accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting in violation of the law that governs his terms of office by functioning in a unilateral manner and seeking his removal. The notice issued by a three-judge bench, presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, was also directed at the CEC, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI Director General Information Technology Seema Khanna. The petition, filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh, is based on the findings of an investigation by The Indian Express published on September 23 that Sandhu and Joshi had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under the CEC - from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. The plea urged the bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, to seek the complete original and primary records relating to the matter from the Election Commission. It also prayed that the ongoing exercise be declared illegal. The CJI assured that the court would examine the records and ensure that any decision taken without unanimity will have to go. We can always annul any decision, the CJI said. Justice Bagchi said that after examining the records, if the court finds that some decisions were taken neither by unanimity nor by majority, we will injunct those decisions.we will say these decisions are ultra vires.. The bench, however, declined to pass any interim order to suspend CEC Kumar or direct that the poll body should take decisions unanimously till it finally decided the matter. Appearing for the petitioner, Senior Advocate Vikas Singh said some interim directions are necessary. I am wanting an interim order today to suspend the CEC immediately.Today there are elections happening.or divest him of the authority to act as CEC, he said. Justice Bagchi, however, asked who will conduct the election in such a scenario. Singh responded that the two Election Commissioners can, and added that in the interim, the court should also restore the position of the ECI as it had made the CJI a member of the selection committee for CEC. We are dealing with a very grave situation today. A grave situation which can undermine the very basis of our democracy. Today, our democracy is vibrant and known all over the world because of the way we are able to conduct the elections. This election.. has been conducted for 76 years, with the ECI having a certain amount of respect, Singh said. He said that while there have been earlier occasions where one or two decisions of the ECI may be questioned, today we are having a situation where the very CEC as a constitutional body is acting in a manner which is completely contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Pressing for interim relief, Singh said .today Your Lordships will pass some orders. Otherwise this country will burn today. The elections were conducted with the ECI having some respect. But today we are having a situation where the CEC is acting in a manner which is completely contrary to the statutory framework. Your Lordships have to take some interim measures here. Because otherwise the very credibility of the electoral process is so undermined that every citizen of this country is feeling unsafe. When the court expressed its disinclination to issue any order to suspend the CEC, Singh sought a direction that the ECI will decide things unanimously till the court hears the matter next. Referring to The Indian Express investigation, Singh pointed out that the ECI had not denied the report. There is a press release on September 26 by the Election Commission, which has not denied the newspaper report. The press release is in the vaguest of language. The CJI said The newspaper report may be 100 percent correct, it may be partially correct, it may be partially incorrect. We cannot really pass an order today on that basis. But we would definitely like to have their response. And then whatever correctional requirements are needed, will issue them. When Singh insisted that the court pass an interim order directing that the ECI act unanimously till the next date of hearing, the CJI said .going by the law, they are expected to take firstly a decision by unanimity and if there is no unanimity, by majority. Now if there is a decision which is neither unanimous nor by majority, then that is subject matter of challenge.. The CJI said, There is a mandatory law. We will accept that they follow it. And if ultimately we find there are instances it has not been followed, you know the consequences. Accusing the CEC of violating the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office Act, 2023, the petition said If the power constitutionally vested in the Election Commission as a multi-member body can, in fact or in substance, be exercised by one office within it without the participation the Constitution and the 2023 Act. then decisions that determine who is on the electoral roll, and therefore who may vote, raise a serious constitutional question as to whether such decisions are being taken by the constitutional authority the Constitution created for that purpose.

articleTitle: Dozen Bengal tribunal judges flag EC portal: ‘Can’t restore deleted voters’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dozen Bengal Tribunal judges flag their EC portal: ‘Can’t serve notices, hold hearings or restore deleted voters’
description: 3 months after polls, on Aug 11, Tribunals put on record challenges in SIR appeal process; sent to EC, Calcutta High Court Chief Justice.
body_raw: Judges of more than a dozen Tribunals appointed in West Bengal on the orders of the Supreme Court to process SIR appeals, including of 27 lakh deleted electors, have highlighted glaring gaps in a digital portal set up for them by the Election Commission of Indias IT division. Official records show they complained that the portal did not allow them to serve notices to parties, slowing down the disposal of appeals. It did not allow the Tribunals to upload additional documents from voters who filed appeals, or hold virtual hearings, or restore a deleted voter. It didnt even let the appellants download Tribunal orders, the judges said. These concerns form the minutes of a meeting of over a dozen Tribunal judges on August 11 - there are 19 in all - and were conveyed to the Election Commission of India and the Chief Justice of the High Court of Calcutta, The Indian Express has learnt. An investigation by The Indian Express last month had revealed that two Election Commissioners had put on record 14 objections in 10 months to a string of decisions taken that pertain to who gets to vote and who doesnt. One of the key concerns they raised was that ECINET, the ECs principal digital system for citizens and officials, restricted access for the officers on the ground responsible for finalising the electoral rolls. Subsequently, the EC announced it would set up a committee with an independent expert to review ECINET and double-check its compliance with the law. Similarly, the hurdles highlighted by the Tribunal judges, they said, were, in effect, getting in the way of ensuring due process for deleted voters. On October 1, The Indian Express sent emails to the Election Commission of India and the Registrar General of the High Court of Calcutta for their response to the judges concerns and whether these were addressed. There was no response. The key challenges judges put on record The August 11 minutes put on record the challenges the judges face. The excerpts from the minutes are telling Cant serve notices There is no mechanism.till date in spite of several requests and reminders to develop a common and proper mechanism on the portal to serve notice to the parties directly or through proper channel. Sometime in the month of May 2026 some of us even approved a format of notice to be issued to the parties but it has not seen the light of the day till date. Cant store documents .when the Tribunal finds uploaded documents are not in terms of enumeration form or whenever the Tribunal needs additional documents, there is no mechanism how the same are to be secured. In the absence of such a mechanism on the portal, each Tribunal is trying to serve the notices through e-emails, that is, through DMDEO concerned but the response is very poor. Cant hold virtual hearings There is no mechanism to hold virtual hearings in case the Tribunal intends to hear the parties.Once the appeal is disposed of either by way of deletion or inclusion of the voter, it cannot be restored on the portal if the restoration is needed on account of direction of the judicial order or otherwise. Cant give an order copy to appellant There is no procedure for the parties to get certified copy or download copy of the order of the Tribunal from the designated portal to know the reasons why their name is deleted or included. This is significant because the Supreme Court, in its order on April 1, had asked the tribunals to communicate the reasons and to revisit the records before they decide on the appeals. Cant digitise physical records The judges flagged the uncertainty over the appeals filed physically with the District MagistrateDistrict Election Officers. .there is no proper mechanism for maintenance of record of these appeals since they are not digitized. If their appeals are not brought to the proper channel, injustice will be done to such citizens, they said. Incidentally, as early as April 6, the Supreme Court had acknowledged this same issue which had then been raised during the hearing in the petition of Mostari Banu, a West Bengal voter. The ECI has already notified on 20.03.2026 that appeals can be filed either online through the ECI NET platform or physically at the office of the DMSDMSDO, who shall ensure digitisation and uploading of the appeal on the ECI NET platform at the earliest, the SC had said in its April 6 order. Another judge complained in May There was an earlier alert, too. On May 22, one of the tribunal judges, wrote to the Calcutta High Court Chief highlighting how the issue of setting up a mechanism to send a notice was raised but went unheeded. Absence of such a mechanism to notify the parties to the appeal is adversely affecting the pace of disposal of appeals, said the judge in the letter to the CJ. The judge also underlined the lack of accurate data on the number of appeals disposed of being shared by the EC. Unfortunately through EC source incorrect data is being catered to the press regarding number of disposal, suppressing the fact ECI has not been able to set up proper mechanism for issuance of notice to the parties for hearing of the appeal, the judge said in the letter. Shadow over appeal process All these concerns raised by Tribunal judges cast a shadow on the Supreme Court-ordered unique appellate process meant to give the 27 lakh deleted voters a chance to appeal their exclusion from the rolls. The Tribunals are a unique aspect of the contested West Bengal SIR process. As many as 27 lakh voters deleted had been identified by the Election Commission using algorithms for logical discrepancies and unmapped as per the documents they submitted during the SIR. After invoking its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution while hearing a challenge to the SIR in West Bengal, the Supreme Court had on February 20 ordered appointment of judicial officers to decide on the eligibility of electors in the state. The Commission, using its centralised software, had drawn up a list of 60.06 lakh such electors, based on logical discrepancies flagged in their documents. Hundreds of judicial officers from Bengal, Odisha and Jharkhand, appointed by the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, following the Supreme Court directions, went through these cases, finally deleting 27.16 lakh electors just weeks ahead of polling in the Assembly elections in the state in April. To give those affected a chance to appeal, the Supreme Court had on March 10 ordered appellate Tribunals of retired High Court judges to be established, which the EC did on March 20 by notifying 19 single-member tribunals. Since then, two judges have resigned citing personal reasons. They have been replaced with other former judges, it is learnt. TMC, BJP evenly shared gains in seats with heavy deletions The two-phase elections in West Bengal last April led to a landslide win for the BJP. The incumbent Trinamool Congress claimed voter deletions played a role in its defeat but thats an allegation more political than empirical. SIR deletions exceeded the victory margin in 49 seats of the 293 that went to polls. In these, the spoils were almost evenly shared - 26 were won by the BJP and 21 by the TMC. The EC had not released any data of the appellate process until a submission in the Supreme Court in another related matter on September 18, when it said 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed, of which only 1.26 lakh had been disposed of till September 10. Of the total appeals, it said, 22.21 lakh were filed by voters who had been deleted and 16.10 lakh were filed against inclusions i.e., seeking deletion. Before the elections, problems with another portal used by judicial officers to adjudicate 60 lakh names were also raised during Supreme Court hearings. In fact, the court noted this in its order on March 10. The judicial officers, through the Honble Chief Justice, have expressed an urgent concern, which seems to have been created due to some mistake at the level of the Election Commission of India. Learned senior counsel for the Election Commission of India assures that the same shall be rectified immediately without any delay. We strongly recommend that the Election Commission of India provide full logistic support to the High Court at Calcutta and all the judicial officers in the completion of the responsibilities which we have assigned to them through our order dated 24.02.2026, the March 10 order said.
