articleTitle: Great Nicobar project: Supreme Court dismisses Centre’s objection to maintainability of PILs in Calcutta High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Great Nicobar project: SC dismisses Centre’s objection to PILs’ maintainability in HC
description: A Chief Justice of India Surya Kant-led three-judge bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked the HC to make an endeavour to decide the matter on the dates (November 25-26) fixed.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to entertain the Centres objections regarding the maintainability of a PIL filed before the Calcutta High Court against the clearance for the ambitious Great Nicobar project. A Chief Justice of India Surya Kant-led three-judge bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked the HC to make an endeavour to decide the matter on the dates November 25-26 fixed. The National Green Tribunal NGT had in February this year cleared the way for the governments Rs 81,000-crore Great Nicobar mega infrastructure project, noting its strategic importance and observing that there were adequate safeguards in the projects environmental clearance. This was challenged before the HC on the ground that it violates the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers Act, 2006. Before the HC, the Centre raised objections to its maintainability, but they were rejected. Following this, the Centre approached the Supreme Court. Appearing for the Centre, Attorney General R Venkataramani told the SC, .this is such an important matter on which somebody comes and files a petition years later, and then three different petitions try to challenge it in three different ways. Then they say the tribals are affected, and they are not before the court. Now they have got impleaded. Therefore, this petition should not be there before the High Court at all. This question of maintainability goes to the root of the matter. He urged the bench to allow him to make submissions on the point of maintainability. Do not close the door on maintainability because something very important turns on that. I just want to keep the door open, he said. Appearing for respondent original petitioner before HC Meena Gupta, Senior Advocate S Muralidhar said the Centres counsel had himself urged the HC to list it for final hearing. He contended that the PIL was maintainable as it involved the issue of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups. Justice Bagchi said the preservation of culture is a constitutionally protected fundamental right. He added that the Great Andamanese had by now become integrated with the mainstream population, adding, Do they become integrated completely with the mainstream, or do we keep them with their unique identity and the identity of their culture? The court ultimately left it to the HC, noting that other similar matters were also pending there.

articleTitle: India, Switzerland to strengthen ties in defence, nuclear energy sectors
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India, Switzerland to strengthen ties in defence, nuclear energy sectors
description: After the bilateral meeting with the visiting Swiss President, PM Modi said, “Today, we identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. We also reached a consensus on further deepening our collaboration in the field of nuclear energy.”
body_raw: India and Switzerland signed pacts on mobility that will ease granting longer-duration visas and the exchange of young professionals and agreed to strengthen cooperation in defence and nuclear energy sectors, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Swiss President Guy Parmelin on Monday. After the bilateral meeting with the visiting Swiss President, PM Modi said, Today, we identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. We also reached a consensus on further deepening our collaboration in the field of nuclear energy. On people-to-people ties, he said that the Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement and the Young Professionals Agreement signed today will open up numerous new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals, and the youth. According to Ministry of External Affairs, the MoU aims to develop migration and mobility cooperation under equal treatment principles, and to prevent and combat irregular migrationhuman exploitationtrafficking in accordance with national laws. It provides for multiple-entry visas for up to 5 years, including stays of up to 6 months on each visit, and renewable 1-year student permits, it said. On the agreement for exchange of young professionals, MEA said that the pact incorporates an exchange of 300 persons annually per country, which may increase to 500, and a timeline of 30 to 90 days for verification of nationalityresidency status, among other provisions. Lauding Swiss President Parmelin, Modi said, I appreciate his commitment to India-Switzerland relations. Last October, with his personal support, we operationalised a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association EFTA countries. This is Indias first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe. It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to realise the goals of attracting 100 billion in investment and creating one million direct jobs in India over the next 15 years. Swiss President Parmelin said, Trade was a key aspect, as my visit marks the first anniversary of the entry into force of the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association. This partnership benefits both sides India gains access to capital, technology transfers, and easier access to markets for high-value-added goods. Switzerland, for its part, benefits from trade with a massive partner experiencing sustained growth-at a time when global trade has become more vulnerable and unpredictable. He said, I am accompanied by a large delegation of high-ranking business leaders, underscoring our commitment to capitalising on the opportunities offered by this trade and economic partnership agreement. To further boost investment, Switzerland hopes to conclude an investment protection agreement soon. In this context, achieving results in discussions on intellectual property protection is equally important, the Swiss President said. In October last year, the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement TEPA between India and the European Free Trade Association EFTA States of Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, came into force. Modi said, We have taken several important decisions to expand market access for Indian exports to Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries. This will increase Indias exports of agriculture, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract new Swiss investment in key sectors like biotech, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability, he said. Through these initiatives, we will jointly develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the entire world, he added. Modi said, The ropeway in Varanasi, the Jewar Airport in Noida, and railways and tunnelling projects in hilly areas are shining examples of our infrastructure cooperation. An agreement was also inked for collaboration on transport and infrastructure. We invite Swiss infrastructure companies to invest in India on a large scale, and to participate in capacity building, design, and manufacturing, Modi said. The PM said new joint research projects in priority areas such as health, clean energy, and space will be launched soon. He said India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on Wednesday will be an important platform to translate the promise of our trade and investment partnership into concrete outcomes, he said. PM Modi also extended his best wishes to Switzerland for hosting the next edition of the AI Summit next year.

articleTitle: Plaque in tribute to Indian Express group founder Ramnath Goenka unveiled at Nariman Point in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Plaque in tribute to Express group founder Ramnath Goenka unveiled at Nariman Point in Mumbai
description: The plaque commemorates the memory of Ramnath Goenka who launched The Indian Express in 1932 and ensured it became a fearless, credible and fiercely independent newspaper.
body_raw: A marble plaque built in tribute to the founder of The Indian Express Group of newspapers, Ramnath Goenka, was inaugurated on Monday by Bombay High Court judge Somasekhar Sundaresan at Mumbais Nariman Point, where the newspapers office is located. The plaque commemorates the memory of Ramnath Goenka who ensured that The Indian Express, founded in 1932, became a fearless, credible and fiercely independent newspaper. The Executive Director of The Indian Express Group, Anant Goenka, was present at the event organised on the founders 35th death anniversary. Built in Makrana marble, the plaque is installed on Ramnath Goenka Marg, a street that links Maharashtra Vidhan Bhavan to the Vinay K Shah Road in Nariman Point. The road was named after The Indian Express founder after former Mumbai mayor and senior Congress leader from Mulund, Ramcharitra Rambhajan Singh, on September 13, 1993, cleared a request submitted by former corporator Vijaya Kanti Dhulla. Two years after the BMCs decision, the road was officially named as Freedom Fighter Ramnath Goenka Marg on November 25, 1995. It was inaugurated by then Vice-President K R Narayanan, with then Chief Minister Manohar Joshi and municipal commissioner JD Jadhav. The name of the lane has now been engraved upon the new plaque along with Goenkas portrait and his words that define the newspapers motto of Journalism of Courage. Remembering our founder Ramnath Goenka On his 35th death anniversary, a plaque was unveiled on the corner of Ramnath Goenka Marg, Nariman Point, Mumbai in the presence of Justice Somasekhar Sundaresan of the Bombay High Court and Anant Goenka, Executive Director, Indian Express Group. Express Photo by Sankhadeep Banerjee - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 5, 2026 The plaque of 8.5 feet width and 12.5 feet height, was constructed over four months. While the plaque was constructed in four months, the intricate engravings were executed over a period of 25 days. The plaque rests on a platform, which takes the total height of the structure to 14 feet, said urban planner Hardik Sankhe, who worked on its design. The project work was executed by the contractor, Aditya Interiors. The final nod for constructing the commemorative plaque was granted by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporations A ward office in July 2025, following which permissions from traffic police, BEST and the Mumbai Heritage Conservation Committee were obtained.

articleTitle: Hours after rescue, lioness that attacked 5 persons in Gujarat dies; rabies suspected
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hours after rescue, lioness that attacked 5 persons in Gujarat dies; rabies suspected
description: Tissue samples sent to agricultural university for tests, forest dept says 'no cause for worry'.
body_raw: A LIONESS has died of suspected rabies in Amreli district after it was rescued last week following separate attacks on five persons. Samples of its brain tissues have been sent to Anand Agriculture University for confirmation, a senior forest department officer said on Monday. Meanwhile, all the five persons injured after being attacked by the lioness earlier have been administered anti-rabies vaccine as per standard medical protocol, officers said. The lioness - aged 2-3 years - was rescued on October 2 from Arjunsukh village in Amreli after it injured five persons in separate incidents Four villagers and a forest department officer. The lioness was later shifted to Krankach Animal Care Centre, where it showed unusual behaviour, such as biting and unusual vocalisations. Within around 20 hours of its rescue, the lioness died at the centre on October 3, forest officers said. Deputy Conservator of Forests, Shetrunji Wildlife Division, Chirag Amin said that primary symptoms indicated that the cause of death may have been rabies, but added that this could be confirmed only after scientific tests. Amin added that the samples of the lionesss brain tissues have been sent to Anand Agricultural University. Amin said there was no cause for worry so far, as the lioness was solitary and there were no other instances of any other lion showing similar symptoms. Forest department officers also checked the surrounding areas near the spot from which the lioness was rescued. Another senior forest officer said a lion can get infected with rabies if it consumes or bites an animal infected by the virus. Similarly, if an infected animal drinks water from a waterbody and then the lion also drinks water from the same waterbody that has rabies infection through the saliva of the infected animal, it can cause transmission of the virus to the big cat. It can also happen that a lion has made a kill and temporarily abandoned the carcass after partially consuming it. It then comes back after some time and again consumes the meat. During this gap period, if some other infected animals such as dogs, hyena etc consume meat from the same carcass, it can lead to transmission of rabies to the lion. The chances of transmission of rabies is more in revenue areas which are not in so much of control and which have the presence of dogs and cattle. and they share the habitat with lions, the officer said.

articleTitle: Rahul Gandhi says abuse of position by CEC Gyanesh Kumar proven, BJP calls remarks ‘full of lies’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rahul says abuse of position by CEC proven, BJP calls claims ‘full of lies’
description: Election Commission says Form 6 not changed, says Rahul Gandhi’s post ‘misleading’.
body_raw: As Chief Justice of India CJI Surya Kant on Monday said that the Supreme Court didnt approve any of the modifications to Form 6, the Opposition hit out at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, saying that the courts observation was proof that he was abusing his position to help the BJP. In response, the ruling party stated that the top courts notice to the poll panel and the Centre was democracy in action. The Election Commission had included a new section in Form 6 that seeks the status of the applicants parents vis-a-vis the last Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, even though the statutory form itself has not been amended. Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi said it is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP, he said. In a post on X, Rahul said that Kumar and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable. Taking on Rahul Gandhi, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra termed Rahuls post on X full of lies, an attempt to spread anarchy in the country by propagating lies. The CJI did not say that the Form 6 was illegal. Rahul Gandhi is lying that the Supreme Court said so. There is punishment for lying, he said. Patra alleged that Rahul is trying to mislead the country on what transpired during the Supreme Court hearing and on the statement issued by the Election Commission on September 26. On both the issues, Rahul Gandhi is trying to create anarchy in the country by misleading people so that is political rallies gain some strength, he said. The fact that this entire matter was taken to the Supreme Court and the apex court issued notices is also democracy in action, Patra said. Responding to Rahuls post on X, the Election Commission of India called his remarks misleading. The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026, said the ECI. In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1iii, ECI has stated that, the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court, the ECI said on X. Congress general secretary organisation K C Venugopal said it was yet another instance where Gyanesh Kumar overruled other ECs to perpetuate illegality for the BJP. During the Modi-Shah regime, the Election Commission has truly become a cheating commission which deprives the ordinary citizen of their inalienable right of franchise. Based on todays proceedings, we reiterate our core demand - Gyanesh must go, he said. TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee said that the contradiction is glaring. The ECs own press note of 26 September says Form 6 was upheld by the SC, while the Supreme Courts statement now says otherwise. Who is misleading the country? These contradictions go to the heart of our democracy. If the institutions meant to protect our vote contradict each other, who protects the voter? This is how elections are stolen, he wrote on X. Samajwadi Party MP Rajeev Rai told The Indian Express that the top court is now realising the seriousness of the issue of SIR. The people of the country are hitting the streets. The courts are realising the seriousness now, even though it is late. CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the SC categorically stated that it never approved the modified Form 6. How many lies will Gyanesh Kumar tell. The ECI, under Gyanesh Kumar, claimed in its September 26 press release that the top court had approved the changes. Now that press release has mysteriously disappeared from the ECI website. This is not a minor discrepancy - it is a grave assault on institutional credibility, said Kumar. CPIM MP John Brittas said I had written to the EC months ago pointing out that the modifications to Form 6 are illegal and unconstitutional. I am glad that the Supreme Court, after an inordinate delay, has finally clarified that these changes never had its sanction or clearance. Citizens were deeply anguished by the Courts prolonged reluctance to step in and protect their most fundamental right - the right to belong to and participate in the electoral process.

articleTitle: No Dussehra or Diwali here: Yavatmal’s dry fields leave farmers counting losses
articleFeaturedImageAlt: No Dussehra or Diwali here: Yavatmal’s dry fields leave farmers counting losses
description: ‘Four chief ministers have come from Vidarbha, yet they could not resolve water crisis here’.
body_raw: Last year, by the time Dussehra arrived, cotton had already reached the homes of farmers in Narsapur. This year, with the festival only days away, Ashok Dasreji Landge, 63, is still waiting for the bolls in his fields to open. Dussehra is on 20th and nothing yet, he says. All 16 talukas of Yavatmal district in Maharashtra are experiencing severe drought conditions, all are under the Trigger-1 drought category, issuing orders for 12 key concessions. Kalamb being one of these. Prolonged dry spells and deficient rainfall have left farmers facing severe drought. Fields that could produce 25-50 quintals of cotton in a normal season are yielding estimates of five to eight quintals, while some farmers expect barely 10-25 per cent of normal crop. Landge is part of a 10-member household comprising him and his wife, their two sons, daughters-in-law and grandchildren. He owns seven acres, with the remaining land divided between two sons. His son Swaroop, 36, cultivates six acres. Landge spent around Rs 21,000 per acre and would normally expect five to six quintals of cotton. But this year there is no production, he said. The family has already been forced to sell their livestock. Four cows and two buffaloes were sold for about Rs 60,000 because the animals could no longer be maintained. Landge said insurance policies taken in earlier years have not yielded payments. His crop loan of Rs 2.10 lakh has remained overdue, while his son has an outstanding loan of about Rs 1.10 lakh. The family pledged household utensils to keep the cultivation going. Diwali and Dussehra will come, but we will have to continue according to whatever the situation is, he said. At Dhanodi, 49-year-old Chitaman Vitthal Bhoyar is facing a similar crisis on his 3.16-hectare holding - one hectare under soybean, two hectares under cotton and 16 gunthas under tur. The soybean crop did not develop because of lack of water. In a good year, I would have got about 25 quintals of soybean. This year, I may get only five, Bhoyar said. For cotton, I would have got around 35 quintals. This year, just seven to eight. His cultivation expenditure has reached about Rs 2.75 lakh, while total crop income may be only around Rs 90,000. Pulling out a plant and showing the sparse pods, he said, Look at this. What will come out of this? His elder daughter is pursuing BSc Nursing in Yavatmal. Her fees for two years being Rs 1.25 lakh, of which he has paid about Rs 25,000. He is now considering withdrawing her. I will have to work somewhere, he said. Bhoyar has also had to sell his bullocks. He bought them for about Rs 70,000 but sold them for around Rs 40,000 after fodder became unavailable. Nitin Gangadhar Nagose 34 of Ichora owns five acres and grows only cotton. Last year, he harvested around 25 quintals this year, he expects seven to eight. Even if it rains now, losses wont be covered, he said. With the farm unlikely to provide income through the year, Nagose expects to take up daily wage work. Construction work in a nearby city may be the only possibility. Nagose lives with his wife, two sons and parents. The children do not understand what is happening. they will demand new clothes for Diwali, he said. Behind Nagoses field, Subhash Meshram, 52, and his wife Sumanbai, 48, face another failed cotton crop. Meshram cultivates five acres of cotton and tur. He dug a 35-foot well but there is no water in it. He expects only four to five quintals of cotton this year against about 50 quintals in a normal year. His wife Sumanbai says, Dussehra and Diwali will not be celebrated this time. They have two bullocks and a cow, but managing fodder and water is difficult. Meshram has a crop loan of Rs 1.30 lakh and does not know how he will repay it. At Ichora, Arun Balkrishna Deotale, 55, cultivates 3.5 acres under tur and cotton and expects only about 10 per cent of the expected crop. I can die, I can hang myself from this tree, but what will that achieve? Ramchandra Warhade, 34, who cultivates four acres of vegetables and cotton, fears farmer suicides could increase this year. Vidarbhas condition is very bad. Four chief ministers have come from Vidarbha, yet they could not resolve water crisis here, he said. Sandeep Thakre, 45, of Ichora, whose cotton, soybean and tur have all suffered, has already spent more than Rs 2.5 lakh. Even if we recover what we have invested, that would be enough, he said. How much will the government give us? Rs 8,000 or Rs 15,000? he asked. Warhade added Fertiliser prices have increased. They say subsidy has been given, but prices have gone up by Rs 200-300 per bag, except urea. The Indian Express spotted panchanamas being done on the fields of Kalamb. We have started conducting panchnamas across the area and will complete them as soon as possible and submit the report to the government, tehsildar Abhay Deshpande said. The decision on relief, he said, would be taken by the state government. Sub-divisional magistrate SDM Vikas Kardile said 15-20 water-conservation works were under way in Kalamb. Our priority going forward is water conservation, Kardile said. The administration is planning recharge pits on farm lands and repairs to deteriorated bunds and gates. March and April will be challenging here. This area largely depends on kharif farming, and that itself is lost, he said.

articleTitle: By-Elections 2026 Highlights: TN’s Madurantakam tops bypoll turnout at 83.86%, Bengal’s Nandigram records 79.39% until 5 PM
articleFeaturedImageAlt: By Election 2026
description: Tamil Nadu's Madurantakam Assembly byelection recorded the highest turnout of 83.86% by 5 pm.
body_raw: By Elections 2026 Voting Live Updates Polling in the Madurantakam Assembly byelection in Tamil Nadu recorded the highest voter turnout among the constituencies reporting figures by 5 pm, with 83.86 of voters casting their ballots, according to the Election Commission. In West Bengal, the Nandigram Assembly constituency saw 79.39 voter turnout till 5 PM.In Puducherry, the Thattanchavady Assembly bypoll recorded 78.83 turnout, while the Nagaon Lok Sabha byelection in Assam saw nearly 76 of voters exercise their franchise. In Tamil Nadus Dharapuram, the figure stood at 78.53. Both Dharapuram and Madurantakam are reserved for Scheduled Caste candidates. Polling in Bengal will continue till 6 pm, while voting in Assam will end at 5 pm. Counting of votes in all the constituencies will take place on October 9. Tamil Nadu The bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram were necessitated by the resignation of then AIADMK MLAs K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Satyabama, who later joined the ruling TVK. Both have been re-nominated from their respective seats. The DMK and AIADMK are also contesting both constituencies. In West Bengal Nandigram is the more closely watched contest, with BJP candidate Hasirani Rath facing Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, rival TMC faction candidate Mohammad Eteshamul Haque and CPIs Santigopal Giri. Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari who was killed in May. In Rejinagar, the candidates include Golam Nabi Azad of the Aam Janata Unnayan Party, BJPs Sakharav Sarkar, TMCs Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, rival TMC candidate Safiuzzaman Sheikh, Congress Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi and CPIMs Syed Asad Ali. In Assam The Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll is an important contest for the BJP, Congress and AIUDF. The BJP is trying to increase its support in the Muslim-majority seat, while the Congress is working to hold on to its minority voters. AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal is also trying to regain the partys influence after it won only two Assembly seats in April, down from 16 earlier. Fifteen candidates are contesting, but the main fight is expected to be between BJPs Devashish Sharma, former Congress MLA Sibamoni Bora and Ajmal In Puducherry Bypoll is being seen as a test of the four-month-old NDA government led by Chief Minister N Rangasamy. The election was necessitated by Rangasamys resignation from the seat. While 11 candidates are in the fray, the main contest is expected to be between the ruling AINRC-led NDA, the Congress and former ally DMK.

articleTitle: Trump approves firing squad execution for 2009 Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Donald Trump, firing Squad, Nidal Hasan
description: Nidal Hasan had opened fire on unarmed troops at Fort Hood, Texas, while shouting "Allahu Akbar", resulting in 13 deaths and 32 injuries
body_raw: The Pentagon announced late on Monday that President Donald Trump has approved death by firing squad for Nidal Hasan, who was convicted for his role in the fatal 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood in Texas. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell posted on X that the recommendation came directly from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who will set the timeline and venue for the execution. Recalling the event, Parnell noted that Hasan opened fire on unarmed troops while shouting Allahu Akbar, resulting in 13 deaths and 32 injuries. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come, Parnell stated. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has recommended - and President Donald J. Trump has approved - death by U.S. Army firing squad for convicted terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan, the jihadist who opened fire on unarmed American soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009. He killed 13 people and wounded 32 others while shouting Allahu Akbar during the attack. The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come. - Sean Parnell SeanParnellASW October 5, 2026 In a follow-up post, Hegseth echoed the sentiment, writing Justice. FROM THE ARCHIVES Fort Hood Muslims voice outrage at rampage Is firing squad legal in the US? Execution by firing squad is authorised in five US states - Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Utah. Three executions by firing squad were carried out by South Carolina after the inmates chose the method in 2025. Before that, a firing squad execution was carried out in 2010 in Utah. In the United States, a firing squad execution involves strapping the condemned inmate to a specialised chair with protective restraints and placing a dark hood over their head. A medical examiner or official locates the inmates heart and pins a target often a white cloth target with a red bullseye directly over it. The execution takes place behind a wall equipped with small ports or a black curtain, says the Death Penalty Information Center in the US. A team of designated executioners - typically five trained law enforcement or correctional officers - stand roughly 20 feet away armed with identical high-powered rifles. To spare the officers from individual guilt, one of the rifles is randomly loaded with a blank or dummy cartridge so no shooter knows who fired the lethal rounds. Upon command, the shooters fire simultaneously at the chest target, causing rapid fatal internal injuries. Apart from the US, execution by firing squad remains legally authorised as a primary or secondary form of capital punishment in several nations, including Indonesia, North Korea, Taiwan, Cuba, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Yemen, Somalia, and Saudi Arabia. Some countries, like Brazil and El Salvador, authorise firing squad executions during times of military conflict. Firing squad executions in the five states require the Presidents authorisation, as in the Nidal Hasan case. From the archives OPINION What should we make of Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan,who apparently killed 13 innocent people at Fort Hood? The Nidal Hasan Case On November 5, 2009, US. Army Major Nidal Hasan, an American citizen of Jordanian descent, carried out a deadly mass shooting at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center inside the Fort Hood military post near Killeen, Texas. Hasan was a military psychiatrist there. Armed with an FN Five-seven semi-automatic handgun, Hasan opened fire on unarmed troops preparing for deployment, killing 13 people-including a pregnant soldier-and wounding 32 others while shouting Allahu Akbar. The rampage ended when civilian responders engaged him in a gunfight, shooting him multiple times and leaving him paralysed from the waist down. Prior investigations revealed Hasan had been radicalised after getting in touch with extremist Islamic figures, including radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki. Hasan was charged under the Uniform Code of Military Justice and faced a court-martial in August 2013, where he represented himself and admitted to have carried out the attack. He claimed his motive was to protect Taliban leaders abroad. A military jury convicted him on 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted premeditated murder, subsequently sentencing him to death. Since his conviction, Hasan has remained incarcerated on military death row at the United States Disciplinary Barracks in Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

articleTitle: Only 9% of Indians take public transport to work, buses key for women
articleFeaturedImageAlt: free bus travel
description: More than a fifth of urban women travel to work by bus, three times as high as their male counterparts.
body_raw: The statistics ministrys first-ever household travel survey has found that only 9 of Indians primarily use public transport to go to work, with 43 using two-wheelers. A mere 3 use cars. The surveys results also seemingly back the decision by several states to offer free bus travel to women, with more than a fifth of urban women using this mode of transport to go to work, three times as high as urban men. Further, people in urban areas spend as much as Rs 1,044 per month to commute to work, 71 more than the Rs 612 spent by people in rural areas. Nationally, the average monthly expenditure to go to work is Rs 785. As per the survey, buses are the primary mode of transport for 6.7 of people who reported travelling more than 1 kilometre to reach their place of work. Another 2.1 said they used monorail or tram, while 0.2 said they travel by rail. While monorail, metro, suburban rail, and trams account for 5 of urban worker commutes nationally, usage surges in Maharashtra 20.7, West Bengal 16.5, and Delhi 14.4, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation MoSPI said on Monday. Train, monorail, and tram includes metro rail and local trains. The findings of the National Household Travel Survey NHTS, conducted from July 2025 to June 2026, are based on responses from 20 lakh people across 14,274 villages and 10,377 urban blocks. MoSPI said the surveys main objective is to generate data-driven insights that can be used in regional transport planning and infrastructure developments as well as identify gaps, optimise transport routes, and improve service frequency and scheduling. Free bus travel for women The surveys results back the decision made by several states to offer free bus travel for women, with 21.7 of urban women who travel more than 1 km for work primarily using a bus. For urban males, this figure is just 6.9. In certain states, the fraction of urban women commuting to work by bus was significantly higher than the national average 46.8 in Keralam, 41.1 in Tamil Nadu, 34.9 in Karnataka, and 28.9 in Telangana. The bus category includes public, private, company, and inter-city buses. According to an April 2026 IIT Bombay paper titled Ticket to Ride Impact of free public transport on womens workforce participation in India, participation of women in the labour force is closely linked to access to affordable public transport. In areas where regressive social norms serve as a binding constraint against womens mobility and their workforce participation, the free bus scheme for all women encourages higher ridership which provides a social cover for even more women to travel, thereby starting a virtuous cycle, the paper said, adding that its findings showed that states can leverage the free bus scheme for women as a tool for inclusive economic growth and development. Criticised by some as a freebie, schemes offering free bus travel to women are becoming increasingly popular, with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay last week expanding the scheme in the state by removing the limit on daily trips. The expansion is expected to benefit over 84 lakh women. Some of the other states that offer free bus rides to women include Delhi, Punjab, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, West Bengal and Keralam. MoSPIs survey report released on Monday also showed that the monthly expenditure commuting to work for urban women in many of these states was much lower than in others Rs 564 in Tamil Nadu, Rs 577 in Karnataka, Rs 716 in Andhra Pradesh, Rs 746 in Telangana, and Rs 820 in Punjab. The all-India average for urban women was Rs 884.

articleTitle: India’s bullet train not delayed, even Japan can’t do it in 10 yrs: High-speed rail body head
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India bullet train
description: The official said even though Japan has 62 years of experience in building and operating bullet trains, it cannot complete a 500-km long stretch in 10 years
body_raw: Amid allegations over delays in Indias first bullet train project between Mumbai and Ahmedabad, the head of the international high speed rail body said it should not be said that the project is delayed given the many unforeseen problems India encountered, such as the Covid-19 pandemic and land acquisition. Speaking to The Indian Express on the sidelines of the Kautilya Economic Conclave, Masafumi Shukuri, Chairman of the Japan Transport and Tourism Research Institute JTTRI and International High-Speed Rail Association IHRA, defended the Indian government, saying that even though Japan has 62 years of experience in building and operating bullet trains, it cannot complete a 500-km long stretch in 10 years. The first high-speed rail project in Japan was launched in 1964, which means Japan has 62 years of experience of constructing and operating the high-speed train. Now, lets just say today Japan decides to make a high-speed rail track of 500 km. It is not possible to complete it in 10 years. Even todays Japan cannot do it. I think from this perspective, given the different conditions, building a high-speed rail of 500 km long in India is a big deal, Shukuri said. We also have to remember that initially when any project starts, there are many unforeseen problems. I know that there was a delay in land acquisition and many other things which have to be factored in, the IHRA Chairman added. Shukuris comments come after Hideki Makihara, a former justice minister and a member of Japans ruling Liberal Democratic Party, who alleged in July that India had displayed sheer recklessness in its bullet train project that stalled its progress. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail MAHSR, Indias first ever bullet train project, was initially expected to be completed in 2022. I do not think there is a delay really, because you have to look at the size of this project. It is a 500 km long alignment. It is being done for the first time in India. With all of this together, it is a humongous, massive project. It is not a project which is expected to be wrapped up and completed in a matter of just a few years. It is just not possible, Shukuri said. Another thing is that we also had to deal with the Covid-19 pandemic, which came with disruption that it took time to get back on track. I feel that despite all of that this project is proceeding very strongly, he further said, adding that IHRA has been involved with the project since 2014, even before it was officially announced. The first section from Surat to Vapi in Gujarat of the 508-km project is scheduled to begin operation by the end of 2027. The entire project is expected to be completed by 2029. The priority section will begin the operation with India-made bullet trains, since the Japanese E10 Shinkansen wont arrive before 2034 and is still under design in Japan. India is currently developing its own bullet train set B28. The design speed of the train is 280 kmph and two sets are being developed by BEML in Bengaluru. It will operate at a maximum speed of 250 kmph. The manufacturing of the train is scheduled to be completed by April 2027, with testing to be done between May-July 2027. The commercial operation of the train will begin by December 2027. Shukuri also said that while it is absolutely fine that India has decided to use its own rolling stock, or India-made bullet train, for the project, it has to ensure the operation is not only stable, but safe and reliable. I think it is not only about procurement of rolling stock and signalling systems. It is also about making sure that training of the people is in place on time, they have the requisite skill-set, they have the technical know-how, as well as enough trials are done to really get a full performance of the final commissioning of the train, said Shukuri. In the Mumbai-Ahmedabad project, three systems were to be taken from the Japanese the Shinkansen bullet train, the Signalling System, and the Operation Control Centre OCC. However, this is yet to be finalised between both countries. The civil construction work is to be done by India.

articleTitle: Extreme heat puts pregnant women, newborns at greater risk: Survey
articleFeaturedImageAlt: heat, pregnant women
description: Global survey includes 200 Indian maternal healthcare professionals; separate India research examines heat exposure and pregnancy outcomes
body_raw: Extreme heat is increasingly affecting pregnant women and newborns, with maternal healthcare professionals reporting a rise in heat-related complications and growing concerns over health-system preparedness, according to a new international survey commissioned by Wellcome, a global charitable foundation that funds health and scientific research. The survey of 1,000 healthcare professionals across India, Australia, Brazil, the UK and Zimbabwe found that 73 per cent reported an increase in heat-related cases or complications affecting pregnant women over the past five years, while 76 per cent reported an increase affecting foetal or newborn health. Nearly all respondents said they had personally cared for a pregnant woman 98 per cent or baby 99 per cent whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat. India accounted for 200 respondents in the survey, which included obstetricians, gynaecologists, doctors, midwives, nurses and other frontline healthcare workers involved in pregnancy, childbirth, postnatal or newborn care. The survey was conducted online between September 17 and October 1. Separate India-specific research has highlighted the potential consequences of heat exposure during pregnancy. In a July 2026 overview of heat and maternal health, researchers in India had found that working in high heat can double the risk of miscarriage and stillbirth. A separate research is examining the effects of extreme heat on maternal, placental, foetal and newborn health across different climatic regions of India. The study is examining heat exposure during pregnancy and its potential impact on outcomes for mothers and babies, including through research involving 600 pregnant women across three climate zones. Pregnant and postpartum women face particular risks from extreme heat. The study has linked heat exposure with preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth and maternal complications. For every 1C rise in heat exposure, the odds of preterm birth increase by around 5 per cent, while exposure to heatwaves has been associated with a 25 per cent higher risk of obstetric complications. Among healthcare professionals surveyed, 23 per cent said they had seen pregnancy complications requiring additional monitoring or treatment that they believed were linked to extreme heat. They also reported low birth weight or restricted growth 34 per cent, dehydration and heat-related illness in newborns 36 per cent, and difficulties with feeding, breathing and temperature regulation 33 per cent. Heat is also affecting access to healthcare. Twenty-seven per cent of respondents said extreme heat was making it harder for pregnant women and families to travel to or access care, while 29 per cent reported an increase in urgent or emergency presentations. Midwives and doctors from countries across five continents are telling us that extreme heat is affecting the health of pregnant women and newborn babies, said Julia Gillard, Chair of Wellcome and former Prime Minister of Australia. As the planet continues to heat-up because of anthropogenic climate change more mothers and babies will be put at risk. More than four in five respondents 81 per cent were concerned that extreme heat would pose a growing risk to maternal, foetal and newborn health over the next five years unless further action is taken. Another 82 per cent said policymakers and health-system leaders should give greater priority to protecting pregnant women and babies from extreme heat. The survey also highlighted a preparedness gap among health workers. Ninety-two per cent of respondents said they wanted more training and resources to protect pregnant women during extreme heat, while 55 per cent said clearer national or international guidance would help them provide better care. Extreme heat, fuelled by climate change is impacting our way of life and our health - and yet many countries are not prepared, said Dr Madeleine Thomson, Head of Climate Impacts and Adaptation at Wellcome. She said measures such as early warning systems and cooler buildings could help protect vulnerable groups, including pregnant women and newborns. The researchers called for pregnant women, new mothers and babies to be specifically included in national climate and health plans, along with clinical guidance on heat during pregnancy and the postpartum period. They have also called for stronger surveillance systems to track the impact of heat exposure on maternal and newborn health. The survey has been released ahead of COP31, as climate and health researchers push for maternal and newborn health to be given greater prominence in climate adaptation and health planning.

articleTitle: 5 injured in accident on Pune-Mumbai Expressway’s Missing Link; traffic diverted briefly
articleFeaturedImageAlt: pune mumbai accident
description: According to the State Highway Police, the injured have been provided with necessary medical assistance.
body_raw: At least five people were injured after a private bus collided with a container on the Pune-Mumbai Expressways Missing Link Connecting Link on Tuesday morning. The injured have been provided with necessary medical assistance, State Highway Police said. The incident led to the closure of the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway, with traffic being briefly diverted through the Ghat section of the expressway. Traffic movement towards Mumbai remained closed on the carriageway for four to five hours before being restored by afternoon as the damaged vehicles were removed from the spot. The State Highway Police confirmed that the situation was under control. The accident also brought into focus the restrictions on and violations by the vehicles on the Connecting Link. Containers are not permitted on the Missing Link, while buses are allowed to use the corridor. The container involved in the accident was therefore in violation of the restrictions applicable to the route. The Highway Police said official, detailed information about the circumstances of the accident will be shared after an initial probe. Motorists travelling from Pune towards Mumbai have been advised to follow the directions of the traffic police and use the Ghat section until the affected carriageway is cleared and reopened.

articleTitle: How Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is challenged by Morne Morkel when he is left out of playing XI
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sooryavanshi is yet to play a senior international match in India. (BCCI Photo)
description: Morne Morkel said that being with the team is good for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's development, regardless of whether he is in the playing eleven or not.
body_raw: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have captured the imagination of the cricket world with his big-hitting prowess at the age of 15 in last years IPL but the Indian team management is being cautious with the teenager. There have been moments in his fledgling international career when it has looked clear that he remains in early stages of his development despite his immense talent and India bowling coach Morne Morkel has said that he likes to challenge Sooryavanshi regardless of whether he is playing or not. Morkel said that being with the team is good for Sooryavanshis development, regardless of whether he is in the playing eleven or not. If he is not getting that game time, he is still on a bus, in the dugout, in the hotel with guys with a lot of experience, Morkel told reporters ahead of Indias first T20I against the West Indies. I think, with him, sharing that dressing room and talking to guys, just actually watching how the guys go through their processes and how they set up will be key. So I always challenge him. I say, watch what this guy is doing in training. How does he face his first 15 balls when the wicket is tough? What sort of game plan has he come up with? For any young player, if he gets game time or if that game time is a little bit limited, it is still our job to make sure that these guys learn, they grow and they ask questions. I always ask him on the bus, What is the one thing you have learned today? Tell me what you think about that guys batting. That makes him think, and I think next time he comes to the nets, the sort of things he will observe, he will adapt to his game. Morkel said that he cant say for sure if Sooryavanshi will open for India in all five of their upcoming T20Is against the West Indies. Head coach Gautam Gambhir had said that the teenager will have to wait for his chances. Sooryavanshi has played eight T20Is thus far and has a strike rate of 186.16 but an average of only 30.75 in the 246 runs he has scored. He is yet to play an international match in India, having been left on the bench during the T20I series against Afghanistan earlier this year while Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma opened. I am pretty sure Gautam will look to rotate them, Morkel said about Indias openers. The guys just came back from the Asian Games, so we want to see how everybody is feeling after jet lag, after travelling, and then from there make the plan.

articleTitle: India News Highlights, 6 October 2026 | Delhi Police release Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi from detention hours after Opposition’s anti-CEC protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra are detained by police during a protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls at Akashvani Bhawan in Delhi on Tuesday. (Express Photo by Gajendra Yadav)
description: INDIA bloc MPs were demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls.
body_raw: Delhi Police on Tuesday night released Opposition leaders, including Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, after a nearly nine-hour protest at Akashvani Bhavan in Delhi. The INDIA bloc leaders had been detained after staging a protest inside the All India Radio premises next to the Election Commission office. They were taken away in buses before being released later in the evening. The Opposition leaders, who had earlier climbed atop barricades during the protest, had vowed to continue their demonstration until they were allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and tell him that he had committed vote theft. The protest was held over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. Earlier several opposition MPs were detained by Delhi police and taken away in buses to different police stations. These detainees included Akhilesh Yadav, Abhishek Banerjee, Kalyan Banerjee, Derek OBrien, Imran Masood, P Santosh and A Rahim. As the protest escalated, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with some supporters, entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises while attempting to reach the Election Commission headquarters. Congress leaders Pawan Khera and other party workers also remained at the premises. Rahul Gandhi, speaking to media persons from inside Akashvani Bhawan, said the opposition was fighting to save democracy. We are not only countering them. I have no interest in what the BJP is saying. Im standing here to save democracy. Other MPs are also trying the same, Gandhi said. He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had finished democracy in the country. Youth of our country have understood this. Even the police officers were also telling me the same thing. They have done vote chori and hijacked the elections, Gandhi alleged. articleTitle: World News Updates: UK Police arrest British national over security incident at US-run air base
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Britain US Air Base
description: The latest arrest is the seventh linked to the RAF Fairford security scare, a US military-run base previously used by American bombers during the Iran war.
body_raw: The UK Police on Tuesday arrested a 22-year-old British national on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in connection with a security incident at a US military-run air base, RAF Fairford. It is the seventh arrest by the counter-terror police related to the security scare at the base, which is located 100 miles 160 kilometres west of London. The base has been used by American bombers to strike Iran during the war that started earlier this year. Trump confirms B-1 bombers moved from UK base amid threats US President Donald Trump said that Washington moved its B-1 bombers out of RAF Fairford due to some threats. Speaking to the reporters on Monday, Trump said that the United States had known of potential threats and decided to move the aircraft rather than tempting the enemy. Why should we leave them there? Trump said, adding that the bombers had been moved around a little bit but not very far. Houthis claim strikes on Riyadh airport, Aramco refinery The Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen claimed that they struck the international airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery and military sites across southern Saudi Arabia. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree, according to news agency AFP, said that the attacks, which included drones, ballistic and cruise missiles, targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. He added that the Aramco refinery in Rabigh was also hit along with other military sites and smaller airports in the south. Tanker hit by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations UKMTO said a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire in the engine room. No casualties or environmental impact were reported in the incident, the agency said. UKMTO has received a report of an incident within the Strait of Hormuz. The Master of a tanker reports being struck by an unknown projectile, causing a fire in the engine room, which the crew are fighting. There are no reported casualties or environmental impact at the time of this warning. Authorities are investigating. Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, the agency said in a post on X. articleTitle: Don’t interfere with ‘right to azaan’ at mosque if noise norms followed: Allahabad HC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Saharanpur
description: Petitioners claim authorities were not allowing them to use loudspeakers for azaan despite court orders allowed it
body_raw: The Allahabad High Court has directed the authorities concerned to not interfere with the right to five-time azaan Islamic call for a prayer at a mosque in Saharanpur district, provided the noise pollution rules are complied with strictly. A writ petition was filed in the court in July requesting to direct the district administration and police to permit the mosque management to perform azaan five times at Ayesha Masjid in Pathed village of Gagalhedi area and permit the use of loudspeakers for the purpose. According to the petitioners, despite there being court judgments permitting the use of loudspeakers for azaan, the authorities were not allowing them to do so. The state governments counsel, however, submitted before the bench that the petitioners were not restrained from performing azaan as such but were only asked to use loudspeaker according to the Noise Pollution Regulation and Control Rules, 2000, which provide for certain level of sound in terms of decibel units. Citing a May 2020 Allahabad High Court judgment, the counsel maintained that certain timings have also been prescribed for the use of loudspeakers for the purpose of azaan. The 2020 judgment stated that azaan may be an integral part of Islam but the call through loudspeakers or other sound amplifying devices cannot be an essential part of the religion, warranting protection of the fundamental right under Article 25 of the Constitution. Therefore, under no circumstances sound amplifying devices can be permitted to be used between 10 pm and 6 am by the district administrations, it was stated. The 2020 order also maintained that in case any such application is filed before the authorities concerned, it may be dealt with in accordance with law, including noise pollution norms. The petitioners submitted that there was no question of violating any rule or the court order on the use of loudspeakers and their use during azaan will be followed strictly. After hearing the submissions, the division bench of Justices Ajit Kumar and Garima Prashad in its October 1 order directed the petitioners to file an affidavit to comply with the Noise Pollution Regulation and Control Rules, 2000, as well as the HCs 2020 order. It will however, be the duty of the police as well as district administration to ensure that the petitioners do abide by their own undertaking given in the affidavit, failing which it will remain open for them to take appropriate action in accordance with law, the bench stated.

articleTitle: ‘Not my personal views’: Sanjay Dutt’s new clarification for ‘don’t feel peace in India’ remark
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt issues another clarification regarding his remarks on Shekhar Tonite.
description: A day after issuing a clarification about his remarks on Shekhar Tonite, Sanjay Dutt shared yet another explanation, this time on camera and in Hindi.
body_raw: A day after issuing a clarification for his dont feel peace in India comment on Shekhar Sumans talk show Shekhar Tonite, Sanjay Dutt has now shared yet another explanation. This time, his clarification comes in a video, where hes speaking in Hindi, and underlining a key point the remarks he made on the show, which was part of a scripted conversation, are not his personal views. Sanjay Dutts second clarification A paparazzo handle shared a video recorded by Dutt, where hes addressing the audience by looking into the camera. A lot of people contacted me on social media regarding my recent expression on Shekhar Sumans show. Some people said theyre quite shocked by my words, while the others expressed strong disagreement with them, said the actor. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Pallav Paliwal pallavpaliwal I completely understand their feelings. I want to make one thing very clear. Whatever I said on the show was part of a scripted segment, like it often happens in television shows of this kind. We were acting as per a script. A lot of the things I said were part of that performance and that context. Theyre not, by any stretch, my personal views, thinking or feelings, he added. I deeply respect the love and trust showered by my friends and well-wishers. Id never want a scripted performance to create a misunderstanding about my personal views. I hope this will clarify the right thing in the right context, concluded Dutt, signing off with Jai Hind Jai Bharat What did Sanjay Dutt say on Shekhar Tonite? Dutt said on Shekhar Tonite that he doesnt feel peace in India anymore. The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I cant feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shiva ji that those days come back soon, he said on the show. After that, he went on to deliver a monologue as the new hypothetical prime minister of the country. Harking back to his iconic role of gangster with Gandhigiri as his weapon of choice, Munna Bhai, he took digs at Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his foreign trips and indulgence in getting his pictures clicked everywhere. Dutt didnt even spare US President Donald Trump, claiming that the next time the leader wants to send missiles to another country, he should be sending bouquets instead. Referring to him as mamu, Dutt said that Trump needed a jadoo ki jhappi. In Rajkumar Hiranis 2006 blockbuster sequel comedy Lage Raho Munna Bhai, Dutts gangster goes on Mahatma Gandhis path of non-violence, which he also advocated for during his satirical monologue on Shekhar Tonite. Dutt and Shekhar Sumans clarifications A day after his monologue drew divisive reactions, Dutt took to his X handle to issue a clarification. I want to clarify that it has never been my intention to hurt the feelings of any individual, community, or institution, to insult them, or to disrespect them. I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution, he wrote. My remarks were made in the context of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous. The spirit behind them was similar to the humour and satire seen in films like Munna Bhai, particularly the concept of Gandhigiri, which was intended to convey a message of love, warmth, togetherness, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted outside of that intended context, added Dutt. Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he said was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never said or meant. I know him for years he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it, Shekhar told NDTV.
