articleTitle: Lucknow flooded, 40,000 homes hit: Trouble began hundreds of kilometres upstream
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Residents at flood-hit areas of Lucknow.
description: The rising level of the Gomti river is being attributed to a chain of weather events in UP
body_raw: For the past few days, Lucknow has received no significant rainfall. Yet large parts of the state Capital are flooded in the month of October. Faizullaganj, on the citys northern fringes, is worst hit, and the situation has been deteriorating with each passing day. At least 40,000 homes are estimated to be affected. The reasons for the flood-like situation, affecting areas from Bakshi Ka Talab and Lucknow North through Faizullaganj towards Naimish, are the result of a chain of events. Officials said the water inundating low-lying areas is largely the result of heavy rainfall in the upper catchment of the Gomti in the last week of September, with the river now carrying the water downstream to Lucknow. The Gomti rivers catchment areas are spread over Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri and Sitapur districts that witnessed exceptionally heavy rainfall between September 22 and 27. Normally, the rainfall over five days would be around 15 mm. This time it was around 150 mm, with some places receiving nearly 257 mm, Principal Secretary Irrigation Anil Garg said, describing the spell as extreme rainfall. The Gomti originates near Madhotanda in Pilibhit and flows through the upstream districts before reaching Lucknow. The extreme rainfall in the last week of September also flooded smaller rivulets and streams feeding the Gomti, resulting in a large volume of water entering the Gomti system. How did this happen? The water in a river system does not move instantaneously, Garg explained. Under normal conditions, it takes about 10-12 days for water to travel from the Pilibhit region to Lucknow, he added. This time, however, several days of exceptionally heavy rainfall meant that large volumes accumulated across the catchment and in the smaller streams before moving downstream. So, even after the skies over Lucknow cleared, the city continued to receive water generated much earlier and much farther upstream, the official said. The high flow also takes time to move through the river. Since it takes 10-12 days for water from upstream to reach Lucknow, experts expect the water level to start receding after two days, as the peak inflow moves downstream. With the upstream areas of the Gomti receiving 25 per cent of the annual rainfall in just three days time till September 27, and with water travelling at the speed of 1 km per hour, it took several days for the water to reach Lucknow, which is about 240 km from the point of origin, said District Magistrate Vishak G. Garg said the water generated after the September 22-27 spell continued moving downstream for several days, eventually heading towards areas such as Sultanpur. Lucknows own share of record rainfall Lucknow itself received around 150 mm of rainfall during the September-end brief spell, adding to the water flowing through the Gomti. The combined effect of local rainfall and upstream inflow pushed the rivers discharge to around 1,100 cusecs, said Garg. To allow the excess water to pass downstream, all 10 gates of the Gomti barrage were opened, as holding back the water would have led to more problems, according to officials of the Irrigation Department. Also, as the river passes through Lucknow, its flow is affected by multiple bridges and structures along the river, meaning the water does not move through the city as one uniform surge. Why Faizullaganj is worst hit Faizullaganj lies in the floodplain of the Gomti river, an area naturally prone to inundation when the water level in the river rises. Concrete houses have come up in the area over the past two decades. This has increased the vulnerability of the settlement when the river receives an unusually large volume of water, said an official. Sources said that since there was no such flooding in the past two decades, settlements developed on this floodplain. Whats next The state government is now looking at building embankments from Faizullaganj to Naimish as a measure to protect vulnerable areas from future flooding. According to officials, the Lucknow Development Authority LDA was already in the process of laying embankments in Faizullaganj. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who on Monday did an aerial survey of the affected areas, ordered building embankments along the river. The Irrigation Department is expected to conduct the survey from Faizullaganj to Naimish in Sitapur.

articleTitle: ‘Left doesn’t fear or sell out’: Neha Bora says right-wing outfits threatening secular views at educational institutes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Neha bora
description: Neha Bora also alleged that an “atmosphere of terror has been created ever since the current dispensation came to power in Bengal…bulldozers are being run on houses one after another.”
body_raw: AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday alleged that right-wing organisations like the RSS and BJP were carrying out attacks on campuses of premier educational institutes in West Bengal, threatening democratic and secular views. Addressing an event organised by the Left-wing student organisations at Jadavpur University, Bora said, The BJP and RSS are out to destroy Bengal. Repeated attacks are being carried out in an institution of national importance like the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute SRFTI by the right-wing forces, while democratic, liberal and secular views are also coming under increasing threat. She also alleged that an atmosphere of terror has been created ever since the current dispensation came to power in Bengal.bulldozers are being run on houses one after another. Hitting out at the Centre, Bora said, They think that they have either scared people away or bought them off. But what they dont know is that there is a community that neither fears nor sells out, and that is the Left. As long as even a single voice remains alive against oppression in this country, in Bengal, and across the world, the Left will remain alive. Bora also raised questions about the role of the Election Commission, the police, and the media. The media, Election Commission, and police all are under the control of those in power. Voting is peoples democratic right, and that very right is being repeatedly attacked. The Constitution is also being insulted, she said. She also brought up the ongoing agitation at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and the recent protests at SRFTI. Protesters cannot be suppressed by attacking them. Even if they face violence, the protesters will not step back. Wherever there is oppression and violence, Leftists will protest. If blood is spilled in Delhi, protests will echo in Kolkata similarly, if violence takes place in Kolkata, Leftists will reach there, she said. SFI leader Srijan Bhattacharya also addressed the convention, raising questions about the right to speak and freedom of expression. How was Rabindranath Tagores poem removed from the syllabus and replaced with the biography of Syama Prasad Mookerjee? When blood flows in Delhi, Kolkata feels the pain and when blood flows in Kolkata, Delhi will surely stand up. This is a promise, a commitment to one another that we will keep making time and again. And on the foundation of this solidarity and this promise, a new India, a new Bengal will surely rise. These are just four more days of sorrow, four more days of oppression these days too shall pass, he said. After being detained by Delhi Police, AISA leader Neha Bora was released on Sunday night. Upon reaching Kolkata on Monday, she attended the JU convention. Fearing protests from right-wing groups, CPIM workers and supporters cautiously escorted her from the airport to Jadavpur. As the crowd swelled, the venue had to be changed mid-way. Ultimately, the convention was held at the K.P. Basu Memorial Hall of JU.

articleTitle: Rs 50,000 per audit, Rs 2.5 lakh in a packet: CBI case against DGCA officer
articleFeaturedImageAlt: DGCA bribery case, DGCA bribe case, CBI DGCA arrest, Sushil Kumar Garg, Sachin Keshav Bhane, DGCA airworthiness certification, Ekvi Air Training Organisation, flight training organisation, DGCA Chennai officer, CBI bribery case, Directorate General of Civil Aviation, Directorate General of Civil Aviation news, Indian express news, DGCA news
description: CBI arrested Sushil Kumar Garg, Deputy Director (Airworthiness), DGCA, and Ekvi Air Training Organisation Private Limited director Sachin Keshav Bhane in connection with an alleged bribery case.
body_raw: A senior officer of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA allegedly sought Rs 50,000 per audit from the director of a flight training organisation to issue airworthiness certificates for aircraft it operated, without ensuring full compliance with prescribed airworthiness and safety requirements, according to a probe. On Sunday, the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI arrested Sushil Kumar Garg, Deputy Director Airworthiness, DGCA, posted in Chennai, and Ekvi Air Training Organisation Private Limited director Sachin Keshav Bhane in connection with an alleged bribery case. The agency alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 2.5 lakh to extend undue favours in the airworthiness certification of aircraft operated by the private firm. According to the First Information Report FIR registered on October 3, Ekvi Air Training Organisation, registered with the Registrar of Companies, Mumbai, and based in Thane, Maharashtra, operates a fleet of seven aircraft, with its training base at Salem Airport in Tamil Nadu. The FIR said Garg conducted an airworthiness audit or inspection of the companys aircraft on July 31. It alleges that he sought a bribe in return for a favourable audit report, without properly inspecting the aircraft and overlooking certain deficiencies observed in the fleet. However, he could not collect the amount on that occasion because he was accompanied by a senior officer. On September 23 and September 26, Garg told the company he would visit its training facility in the first week of October 2026 and collect the payment from its representatives, and that Bhane would be present at Salem during the visit. Later, they negotiated on October 2 and settled at Rs 50,000 per audit. Garg had previously received a mobile phone worth approximately Rs 50,000 from Bhane, the FIR alleged. The FIR alleged that Garg told his wife that day that Bhane had given him a packet containing five bundles of currency notes amounting to Rs 2.5 lakh.

articleTitle: ‘No malafide intention’: Gurugram police chief concedes ‘lapses’ before SC in Delhi man’s cremation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gurugram
description: While the Gurugram police chief claimed that all records were handed over on September 15, Delhi Police documented that inquest papers and the post-mortem report were produced at Lajpat Nagar police station only on September 21.
body_raw: Gurugram Commissioner of Police CP Sibash Kabiraj has conceded that the local police committed procedural lapses while handling the unidentified body of Delhi-based real estate professional Yuvraj Manchanda who was allegedly killed by his former colleague and her partner last month, The Indian Express has learnt. A compliance affidavit, filed in the Supreme Court on October 1, has the Gurugram CP tendering an unqualified apology for the lapses. The affidavit acknowledged that supervisory reviews had found that information regarding the unidentified body was not entered promptly in CCTNS form IIF-10, that intimation was not given to the Executive Magistrate within 24 hours and that the control room in-charge was negligent in performance of her duties for having relayed the information with regards to the discovery of the dead body only to local police stations and not to adjoining states. The police chief, however, maintained that there was no malafide intention involved on the part of the local police. Sequence of events per affidavit Police said a PCR call was received around 405 pm on September 10 regarding a body lying in a waterlogged open field near a drain in Sector 70. According to the police, a team of officers reached the spot to find that the body was bloated and decomposed, rendering fingerprint collection impossible and detailed on-site examination for external injuries infeasible. The body was shifted to a mortuary, and following an autopsy on September 14, it was cremated as an unidentified individual at Ram Bagh Crematorium, police said. According to the affidavit, officers at Badshahpur police station uploaded a recovery entry on the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network Systems CCTNS form, IIF-10, only on September 15, a day after the cremation. An order dated September 17, issued by Deputy Commissioner of Police Headquarters Dr Anshu Singla, placed investigating officer ASI Sahun Khan under immediate suspension and ordered a joint regular departmental enquiry against him and Badshahpur police station SHO Rajesh Kumar. The order observed that ASI Khan made no effective efforts to establish the identity of the deceased, failed to publish an advertisement in local newspapers, omitted uploading details onto the Zonal Integrated Police Network ZIPNET portal, and failed to record complete particulars in CCTNS Forms IIF-10 and IIF-11, police said. The DCP Headquarters noted that an abduction case had already been registered at Lajpat Nagar police station, Delhi, remarking that had the information regarding the unidentified dead body been uploaded on the ZIPNET portal in accordance with the prescribed procedure, there was a possibility of establishing the identity of the deceased. Inspector Kumar was deemed prima facie liable for gross negligence for failing to visit the spot, inspect the body and supervise formalities. ASI Khan was directed to deposit arms and ammunition with him and restricted to subsistence allowance. A second departmental enquiry against both officers was initiated via an order dated September 30, also issued by Dr Singla. This order cited a report by the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Badshahpur, that had found that both the SHO and the IO failed to callseek the presence of the Executive Magistrate at the spot, in direct violation of BNSS Section 194 as well as the police commissionerates Standard Operating Procedure. Through a communication dated September 18, the DCP Headquarters recommended departmental action to the Superintendent of Police, Telecommunication H, against ESI Hasina, who was on duty as Control Room In-charge on September 10. It recorded that she failed to convey the said information regarding the recovery of the unidentified dead body to the concernednearest districts and neighbouring States. Following these lapses, the Gurugram Police Commissioner issued fresh instructions on September 28, mandating that control room personnel must immediately flash particulars of every unidentified body to adjoining districts and neighbouring states. Differences between affidavits Meanwhile, a comparative analysis of affidavits filed by Delhi CP Anurag Kumar dated October 3 and his Gurugram counterpart reveals some differences in the accounts. CP Kabiraj asserted that on September 15, the Delhi Police approached the district police regarding the FIR concerned, and on their request, the entire case property and the documentation was handed over to them. The Delhi Police affidavit, however, stated that its officers were tracking the suspects in Uttarakhand during September 15-16, arrested them on September 17, and only discovered the recovery and cremation of the body on September 18 while inspecting the drain in Gurugram. While the Gurugram police chief claimed that all records were handed over on September 15, Delhi Police documented that inquest papers and the post-mortem report were produced at Lajpat Nagar police station only on September 21. Emphasising the operational fallout of Gurugrams omissions, the Delhi CP Anurag Kumar submitted that the efficacy of ZIPNet and CCTNS in matching missing persons with unidentified dead bodies depends upon the contemporaneous uploading of both by every participating police unit, and upon a cross-search of these databases before an unidentified dead body is disposed of.

articleTitle: Hanuman Ansh team performs aarti at Neem Karoli Baba’s Kainchi Dham, film earns Rs 424 cr
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shobhinaw Satyaa visits Kainchi Dham after the success of Hanuman Ansh.
description: As Hanuman Ansh earned over Rs 424 crore at the worldwide box office, its team including lead actor Shobhinaw Satyaa, visited Kainchi Dham, the spiritual site associated with Neem Karoli Baba.
body_raw: The team of Vishal Chaturvedis blockbuster devotional film Hanuman Ansh has paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand in order to offer their prayers to Neem Karoli Baba, the revered spiritual guru whose life their film is based on. However, their visit comes a day after the director urged devotees to exercise caution and avoid visiting the site amid reports of overcrowding over the long weekend. Vishal was not a part of the group visiting the holy site. Hanuman Ansh team visits Kainchi Dham The team of Hanuman Ansh - led by actor Shobhinaw Satyaa, who plays Neem Karoli Baba in the biopic - participated in the aarti and paid their respects to the spiritual gurus shrine at Kainchi Dham. Satyaa expressed his gratitude for the visit and also thanked the audience for making their film a super-duper hit, as per ANI. We are missing the rest of the team, especially our director Vishal Chaturvedi. It is because of his hard work that the film got made and reached this level of success. But he has a lot of responsibility at the moment and because of that, he couldnt make it, he told Uttarakhand News. ALSO READ Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity The team of Hanuman Ansh managed to make it to Kainchi Dham despite the swelling crowds reported in the past few days. So much so that Vishal Chaturvedi had to take to his Instagram handle on Sunday to urge devotees to check the situation before heading there. Kainchi Dham is overcrowded, and people have said that this is because of the influence of Hanuman Ansh. If that is the case, and if that is not the case, even then, people should visit there only after knowing the present conditions, he said. It is my humble request that if there is overcrowding, please consider visiting other places. Dont become part of a situation where women and children feel suffocated or get stuck in traffic jams, added the director. He also suggested that in case of overcrowding, the devotees could consider visiting other sites associated with Neem Karoli Baba, like Neem Karoli village and Vrindavan in the neighbouring state of Uttar Pradesh. Over the long weekend, which started with Gandhi Jayanti this past Friday on October 2, more than 35,000 devotees visited Kainchi Dham every day, as opposed to the 25,000 the administration is used to handling. The Nainital administration is now even considering opening an alternate route to ease the pressure, as reported by The Indian Express. Both the pilgrims and the locals use the same road to Kainchi, which also goes up to Mukteshwar, causing a traffic jam for hours, said Nainital District Magistrate Lalit Mohan. He attributed the rush to both the end of the monsoon season - enabling safer travel to the hills - and the release of Hanuman Ansh, which has amassed over Rs 420 crore at the worldwide box office so far. Hanuman Ansh box office collection After 60 days at the domestic box office, Hanuman Ansh has now earned Rs 384.44 crore gross and Rs 325.48 crore net at the domestic box office. Its just Rs 4 crore away from surpassing the domestic box office collection of Anurag Singhs period war drama Border 2, starring Sunny Deol and Varun Dhawan, post which itd become the second highest grossing Indian film of 2026 after Aditya Dhars spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge, starring Ranveer Singh. Ever since its overseas release by Hombale Films on September 11, Hanuman Ansh has collected Rs 39.80 crore at the international box office. The films worldwide collection currently stands at Rs 424 crore. On October 9, Hanuman Anshs dubbed Telugu version will also release in cinemas across India, which is likely to increase the films box office collections. Made on a budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has already earned over 212 times globally.

articleTitle: Nvidia-backed Reflection unveils first AI model to take on Chinese open models
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The latest letter, signed by 25 companies, comes at a time when Chinese AI models are rapidly proliferating. (AI Image via OpenAI)
description: Founded ​in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis ​Antonoglou, Reflection develops tools that automate ⁠software development, a fast-growing use case for AI.
body_raw: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI debuted its first open-weight model named Beam on Monday, as the startup aims to compete with lower-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Kimi in coding and agentic tasks. Reflection said Beam is competitive with Chinese AI startup Z.ais GLM-5.2 and is closing in on Qwen3.8-Max on coding and agentic tasks. Here are some details The startup said that Beam contains 501 billion total parameters, or variables that determine how an AI system processes information, but activates only 23 billion for each task to make the model faster and cheaper to run by using only part of its network for each task. Comparatively, Z.ais GLM-5.2 has about 744 billion total parameters with 40 billion active parameters. The launch comes as US tech firms are trying to fend off competition from Chinese open-weight models that are cheaper, more customizable and capable of generating code nearly as well as leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, Reflection develops tools that automate software development, a fast-growing use case for AI. Earlier this year, Reflection signed a deal with SpaceX for additional computing capacity at the Elon Musk-led companys Colossus 2 data center.

articleTitle: A thick heart? When my patient’s perfect lifestyle wasn’t the whole story
articleFeaturedImageAlt: heart disease
description: She was 36, fit and health-conscious, yet breathlessness, dizziness and fainting revealed a heart condition she never knew she had. Here’s what everyone should know about hypertrophic cardiomyopathy — and the myths that surround it
body_raw: Tanvee, a 36-year-old woman, had always considered herself playing by the book. She exercised regularly, enjoyed yoga and strength training at the gym and maintained a balanced diet. Over the past year, however, she began experiencing breathlessness while climbing stairs, occasional chest discomfort, dizziness, and a racing heartbeat after mild physical activity. She initially dismissed these symptoms as stress, lack of fitness, or fatigue from balancing work and family responsibilities. But when she briefly lost consciousness after walking uphill and sought medical attention, the diagnosis surprised her. Imaging tests revealed she had obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy oHCM, an inherited condition in which the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick, making it harder for blood to leave the heart. Although the diagnosis initially caused anxiety, she was reassured that with appropriate treatment, regular follow-up, and lifestyle guidance, she could continue to lead an active and fulfilling life. Her story is not unique. OHCM remains one of the most misunderstood cardiac conditions, despite being the most common inherited condition. Misconceptions around the disease can lead to fear, delayed diagnosis, and hesitation in seeking appropriate medical care. While oHCM has historically been associated with sudden cardiac death, particularly in young athletes, advances in diagnosis and treatment have significantly transformed its management. Today, with early diagnosis and appropriate treatment, many patients can lead active and fulfilling lives. Understanding oHCM Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a form of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy HCM - an inherited heart muscle disorder caused by genetic mutations that affect the structure and function of the heart muscle. These changes cause the heart muscle to become abnormally thick, most commonly affecting the wall, or septum, between the two lower chambers of the heart. In nearly two-thirds of patients with HCM, the thickened heart muscle can block the flow of blood leaving the heart, a condition known as obstructive HCM oHCM. As a result, the heart must work harder to pump blood throughout the body, often leading to breathlessness, chest pain, fatigue, palpitations, dizziness, or fainting during physical activity. Myth 1 A diagnosis of oHCM inevitably leads to sudden death. Fact While oHCM was once primarily recognised for its association with sudden cardiac death, advances in medical science have significantly improved patient outcomes. With timely diagnosis, appropriate medical care, and ongoing monitoring, many people with oHCM can experience a good quality of life and a near-normal life expectancy. Regular follow-up helps assess disease progression and guides individualised care. Myth 2 People with oHCM need to avoid physical activities. Fact Complete avoidance of physical activity is no longer recommended for most patients. Although high-intensity competitive sports may not be suitable for everyone with oHCM, mild-to-moderate exercise is generally encouraged and offers important cardiovascular benefits. Exercise recommendations should always be individualised after a comprehensive assessment by a cardiologist, taking into account symptoms, severity of obstruction, and overall risk profile. Myth 3 Diet and lifestyle are the primary causes of oHCM. Fact Unlike heart conditions caused by high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol, oHCM develops because of inherited genetic mutations affecting heart muscle proteins. Since the disease often runs in families, screening of close relatives may also be recommended. Myth 4 Every patient with oHCM will require surgical treatment Fact Surgery is only one of several available treatment options. Care is individualised, and the most appropriate approach depends on each patients symptoms and clinical condition. Myth 5 oHCM cannot go unnoticed. Fact The condition can remain silent for years. Symptoms can be subtle and easily mistaken for stress, poor fitness, or other illnesses. Some individuals carrying the genetic mutation never develop symptoms, while others experience mild or intermittent symptoms. Typical symptoms include Shortness of breath Chest pain Fatigue Palpitations Dizziness or light-headedness Fainting, particularly during or after exercise Given this variability, individuals with persistent symptoms or a family history of cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death should undergo appropriate cardiac evaluation. Myth 6 Medication can cure the condition. Fact Advances in treatment have significantly improved disease management, helping many patients lead healthier and more active lives. While current therapies focus on controlling symptoms and reducing complications, ongoing research continues to expand treatment possibilities. Treatment aims to reduce symptoms, improve blood flow, minimise obstruction, and lower the risk of complications such as abnormal heart rhythms and heart failure. Long-term follow-up remains an important part of care, allowing treatment to be adjusted as the condition evolves. Timely evaluation is particularly important for those with a family history of the disease. Early detection can also help identify family members who may be at risk and require screening. Although oHCM remains a lifelong condition, it is no longer viewed through the lens of fear alone. The author is cardiac electrophysiologist at AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad

articleTitle: A midnight Shimla heist, a cross-country chase and a shocking twist
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The suspect maid caught on CCTV camera installed in the house
description: Early on September 8, the home of a 76-year-old was burgled in an upscale neighbourhood of Shimla. The trail led to a maid, a taxi and finally to four Uttarakhand officials accused of snatching the stolen jewellery
body_raw: When she woke up at 8 am on September 8, Renu Baljees could suddenly feel something was off. For one thing, it was an hour and a half later than usual, and her body refused to move-unusual for this active 76-year-old. For another, her three-storey house in the upscale, picturesque Fingask Estate locality adjoining Shimlas iconic Mall Road was deathly quiet. Her first thought was why didnt the alarm go off this morning? But as she strolled through the house, the reason became increasingly clear the battery to the alarm had been pulled out, and her cordless phone was missing. And once she stepped into another room, everything started to make perfect sense. The room had been completely ransacked. She had been robbed of valuables-later estimated to be worth Rs 1 crore. My phone was gone. I had no way of communicating, she says. I had a bell that connected me to my bakery on the ground floor I rang it. The staff quickly came up. They found a maid lying unconscious after she was knocked down. Another maid was missing. All my valuables had been stolen. The missing maid, Karishma, who was originally from Nepal, had been hired only ten days ago. What followed was still strange. During the investigation, police found that Karishma and her three accomplices had allegedly been intercepted by uniformed personnel at Uttarakhands Rudrapur while fleeing towards Nepal, and the jewellery was taken by the officials. The recovery of the jewellery from Karishma wasnt, however, reported to the police. On September 22, police arrested four excise officials. They have now been released on bail. We are investigating if there was an organised network involved, one officer says. The burglary Ever since her husband died in 1996, Renu knew how to live alone, caring for her two daughters and running the family bakery. Now 76, and with her daughters abroad, Renu increasingly relies on her staff her assistants at the bakery and her live-in domestic help. According to the police, Renu had placed a request for a maid through an online placement agency. She, however, denies this, claiming instead that she received repeated WhatsApp calls from a man who claimed he could provide trustworthy help. On August 27, Karishma, a woman originally from Nepal, arrived at Renus house with only a rucksack in tow. Slim, dressed in trousers and a T-shirt, with her long hair tied in a bun, she was unassuming-and fit right in. The man had shared a copy of the contract between him and me, along with Karishmas identity proof, on WhatsApp, she says. But police verification was always on my mind, and I kept asking her for documents. She kept evading it by telling me she would send them to me later, and that her brother and sister-in-law would bring them when they came down on September 7, but it never happened. She also sent me her number, but thats been switched off since. Later, I realised that the copy of the contract and Karishmas identity proof have since disappeared from my WhatsApp chat. A CCTV recording from the time of the burglary allegedly showed Karishma entering the house with three accomplices-all men - and leaving with what police suspect was the loot. The FIR initially estimated the jewellery to be worth Rs 1 crore, although Renu now claims that this value is conservative. But as the investigation progressed, there was another development that has since left investigators puzzled. On September 10-two days after the burglary-Renu received a call from a woman who introduced herself as Karishmas older sister. According to investigators, the call came from a Nepal number. She came straight to the point. She sought my forgiveness for what had occurred, and told me that some uniformed people had intercepted her sister and her accomplices at Rudrapur and took all the valuables from them, she says. Located in Udham Singh Nagar district of neighbouring Uttarakhand, Rudrapur is a popular transit point for travellers going towards the western Nepal border. Its still unclear who this caller was - or how she knew that Karishma and her accomplices had been intercepted at Rudrapur. But for investigators, this puzzling call served to confirm a thread they were already pulling at-a white taxi that the group had allegedly taken out to Uttarakhand on September 8 and which was also captured on CCTV. The call was significant, but by then, one of our teams had reached Uttarakhand chasing the taxi. We were also coordinating with the police in Rudrapur, the officer says. The taxi driver, investigators later allegedly found, was originally from Nepal but had no known connection to the suspects. He became the key to solve this puzzle. The taxi drivers testimony helped us establish what happened, and he played a crucial role in identifying the four officials at the Rudrapur border crossing. Hes now a witness, the officer says. The probe On September 22, the Shimla Police took custody of the four personnel from Uttarakhand Police. While two - Sub-Inspector Devendra Kumar and Constable Baljit Singh-are from the excise department, the others have been identified as Uttarakhand Purv Sainik Kalyan Nigam employee Pappu Lal and Naeem, a personnel with the auxiliary volunteer force, the Prantiya Rakshak Dal. Both Lal and Naeem were attached to the excise department at the time of the incident. At the same time, the investigators are now pursuing some more suspects-those involved in the original burglary, and the missing woman Excise constable they believe was part of the group that intercepted the quartet in Rudrapur. Investigators say that Karishma and her three accomplices, who committed the burglary in Renus house, are from Nepal. Were trying to trace the Excise constable and establish her role in the events of that day, the officer says. We believe they are all hiding in Nepal now. The role of the man, who claimed to be from the online placement service and had arranged the job for Karishma at Renus house, is also under scrutiny. His phone is now switched off, police say. Karishmas phone too isnt working. Investigators suspect that Karishma may have sedated both Renu and her other live-in house help, to make an easy getaway. Renu claims her food was spiked. Anjali, who has been working with me for many years, is the one who cooked the food-chapatis and sabzi. Anjali and I both ate that food that night. Karishma didnt, Renu says. The police claim 80 of the stolen jewellery items have been recovered-an assessment Renu disagrees with. We are now trying to find out if they were all part of an elaborate network that provides maids and robs them, or if the personnel were simply there, took the stolen loot and allowed them to enter Nepal and disappear. Back at her Fingask Estate house, Renu has been shaken by the incident. But even during this traumatic time, she has turned to a person she trusts the most, her old help, Anjali. I know that Im not alone in feeling like this, she says. Here, youll find families that have domestic help, who have been working for a family for years. This must also have shaken them.

articleTitle: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s rogue agents possibly tied to data service disruption in May
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AI coding
description: OpenAI has been scrambling to get its ‌arms around ⁠the full scope of its rogue agent activity.
body_raw: The Wikimedia Foundation, which operates online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said heavy traffic from OpenAIs rogue agents was possibly tied to a disruption that its data service experienced in May. In a blog post on Monday, Wikimedia said it could confirm that we have discovered some activity by these rogue OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms, including a May incident that resulted in a partial outage of its Wikidata Query Service. Wikimedia said the disruption seemed to have been triggered as the agents visited millions of pages and made hundreds of thousands of data queries. Wikimedia also said the OpenAI agents made unauthorized edits to Wikimedia wiki sites, including potentially malicious edits to a citation tool, which the foundation said were likely intended to hijack it. Wikimedia said its Etherpad note-taking tool was also hit by malicious activity from OpenAIs agents. OpenAI said in a statement that it appreciated Wikimedias detailed findings and was working with the organization to analyze the activity. Well continue to share relevant information as that work progresses, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said. OpenAI has been scrambling to get its arms around the full scope of its rogue agent activity, Reuters has previously reported.

We sincerely express our gratitude to Honble Health Minister Shri Prafulbhai Pansheriya Saheb and Honble Chief Minister Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel Saheb for recognising the genuine concerns of FMG interns and supporting this historic step. Heartiest congratulations to everyone. This is a victory of unity, perseverance and collective representation. articleTitle: BJP, JD(S) defend bulk Form 7 filings, allege ‘false FIRs’ in Karnataka
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka SIR voter deletion Form 7
description: A delegation of BJP and JD(S) leaders submitted a petition to Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukumar, seeking that election officials be instructed to 'safeguard the interests of individuals filing Form 7 objections'.
body_raw: A delegation of BJP and Janata Dal Secular leaders on Monday submitted a petition to the Karnataka chief electoral officer CEO, urging him to direct the state police not to register false or unwarranted FIRs against individuals, including BJP workers for allegedly filing Form 7s in bulk to disenfranchise eligible voters during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. The National Democratic Alliance NDA partners also sought that CEO V Anbukumar instruct the electoral registration officers ERO and assistant EROs to safeguard the interests of individuals filing Form 7 objections as there was no bar on filing bulk objections through Form 7. Form 7 allows an elector to object to the inclusion of a name or seek deletion of an existing entry from the electoral roll. The delegations memorandum also accused the Congress government in Karnataka of unduly influencing and interfering in the SIR process. The members of the ruling government, along with their party workers are also misusing the state police machinery by filing false and serious criminal charges against individuals who have been filing objections through Form 7, thereby creating a sense of fear and apprehension in the minds of objectors and diluting the entire exercise of SIR, the NDA partners said in the petition. Karnataka voter row Protests escalate Last week, a Karnataka BJP delegation had met Director General and Inspector General of Police M A Saleem, alleging that criminal cases were being registered against BJP workers and political activists for submitting Form 7 objections. The development came amid multiple FIRs being filed across the state based on complaints by voters who discovered that Form 7s were submitted against their names despite them being genuine voters. A protest by Congress leaders, led by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, saw Anbukumar agreeing to initiate legal action against those responsible for filing bulk Form 7 applications to remove eligible voters. No bar on bulk objections BJP, JDS There exists a provision to file applications in bulk for identifying corrections to be carried out in the draft electoral rolls. Hence, there is no bar on filing bulk objections through Form-7 as per the communique issued by the Honble Election Commission of India dated 16.01.2026. There are no restrictions on the number of Form-7 applications that may be submitted to the ERO Hence, no illegality is committed while submitting Form-7, the BJP-JDS petition said. The two parties also raised questions about the protest staged by Shivakumar and other ministers in front of the CEOs office. We express our serious concern and disapproval regarding the undue influence exerted by the state government on the constitutional process of SIR. It is also distressing to note that the chief electoral officer appears to have succumbed to such pressure, it added.

articleTitle: Karnataka High Court stays drug licence suspension, cancellation orders
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka FSDA, fake medicines
description: The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration on September 18 cancelled the licences of 16 retail and wholesale pharmaceutical firms across Bengaluru. It suspended the licences of eight others, including pharma major Pfizer’s depot.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court on Monday stayed the Food Safety and Drug Administration FSDA order cancelling Fortune Medical Solutions licence and suspending Vivanta Pharmaceuticals licence for allegedly selling spurious products. The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration FSDA on September 18, cancelled the licences of 16 retail and wholesale pharmaceutical firms across Bengaluru and suspended those of eight others, including global pharma major Pfizers depot, as they violated Rule 66 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945. Rule 66 provides for an opportunity of hearing and explanation to the party against whom action is proposed before suspending or cancelling the licence. Justice C M Poonacha said, The petitioner shall also be permitted to carry on its pharmaceutical distribution business till the next date of hearing in accordance with law. This order will not preclude the respondents from taking such measures as may be permissible under law and petitioner shall cooperate with the authorities in any action that is undertaken in accordance with law, the court said. The court issued notice to FSDA and others and directed them to file their reply to the petitions. The petitions are now posted for hearing on October 9. Additional Government Advocate Rahul Cariappa said the court will hear together all 16 petitions filed by similarly placed pharma companies on October 9. FSDAIs action follows raids at farmhouses in the Bidadi and Dodderi areas of Bengaluru South district on August 18. The agency seized suspected counterfeit medicines worth around Rs 5 crore, along with fake bills, injection-filling equipment and counterfeit labels. Later, a Special Investigation Team SIT was formed to probe the wider racket. According to the FSDA, preliminary investigations revealed that the farmhouse premises were being used to procure low-cost medications from neighbouring states. These cheaper drugs were allegedly refilled into new vials and relabelled to counterfeit expensive life-saving brands of multinational corporations, specifically imitating imported products under the brand name Pfizer. To deceive buyers and maximise illicit profits, the counterfeit labels featured QRscanning codes that the FSDA found completely non-functional upon verification. These counterfeit drugs lack active medicinal ingredients and may contain harmful substances, the agency had noted. In its petition, Vivanta Pharma claimed that the allegations only relate to identified batches of Zavicefta, whereas the impugned order suspended all the drug licences of the petitioner from carrying on its business and violates its fundamental right. Further, the blanket order is excessive, arbitrary, and disproportionate. Firms whose licences were cancelled Avesco Healthcare,Bangalore Speciali Pharma,Patel Medi Trade,Rajarajeshwari Pharma,Surya Speciality Pharma,SWS Pharma,Krupa Healthcare,St Philomena Hospital Drug Centre,Sagar Pharma,Zymus Pharma,Fortune Medical Solutions,Excelcare Pharma,Patel Medicals, and Bangalore Speciality Pharma outlet at Chamarajpet. Firms whose licences were suspended Med Pharma, Surya Speciality Hospital, Sagar Pharma Unit-II, Vivantha Pharmaceuticals, Maruthi Medicals,Viva Pharma Belagavi,Hi-5 Pharma, and Pfizer. Seized materials-5,640 vials of counterfeit Cefiavigent 2.5 injection, falsely branded under Eucratia Healthcare Pvt Ltd, valued at over Rs 3.38 crore, the single largest component of the haul.-1,531 vials of Hizlam injectables, falsely attributed to Welcure Remedies Rs 52.24 lakh.-264 vials of Emblaveo, counterfeiting Pfizer Rs 20.59 lakh.-30 boxes of expired medications, valued at Rs 35 lakh, which officials say were apparently being prepared for reintroduction into the market.-Several other counterfeit injectable batches, including Xavitaz, Zavicefta, Tigynt, Tigvnet, Aztreo, and Trezam, along with packaging components, an injection-filling machine, and bulk quantities of forged labels and stamps.

articleTitle: Orissa High Court upholds divorce over wife’s cruelty but hikes her alimony to Rs 25 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Orissa High court divorce cruelty alimony rs 25 lakh wife
description: The family court granted the husband’s divorce plea in 2022 on grounds of cruelty by the wife and directed him to pay her Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony.
body_raw: The Orissa High Court recently confirmed a couples divorce on the ground of cruelty by the wife but increased her permanent alimony from Rs 16 lakh to Rs 25 lakh. The court noted that the couple stopped living together within months of their marriage. It also held that once cruelty by the wife was established, the husbands decision to live separately could not be said to be without reasonable cause. Chief Justice Harish Tandon and Justice Chittaranjan Dash were hearing the appeal filed by the wife challenging the family courts order of May 2022. The family court had allowed the husbands plea to end the marriage and ordered him to pay Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony. Once the course of matrimonial cruelty established against the appellant wife is taken into account, it cannot be said that the respondent husbands withdrawal from her society was without reasonable cause, the October 1 order read. Started living separately within few months The woman claimed to have married in July 2017 with her estranged husband. It was added that their marriage did not continue for long and the couple have been living separately since February 2017. The husband filed for divorce in 2020, citing cruelty. The wife opposed the plea and later filed an application seeking to resume the marriage. The family court eventually granted the husband a divorce, rejected the wifes plea to resume the marriage and ordered him to pay Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony. Aggrieved, she filed an appeal before the Orissa High Court challenging the family courts May 2022 order. Arguments The wife, through senior advocate A Mohanty, submitted that the finding of cruelty based on the allegation that the woman was accustomed to a lavish lifestyle could not by itself constitute matrimonial cruelty. He further argued that the serious allegations made by the wife regarding demand of money, physical and mental harassment and other matrimonial misconduct had not been properly appreciated. On the contrary, the man, through advocate A K Sarangi, submitted that the matrimonial relationship had become irretrievably strained within a short period of the marriage. He added that the couple had been living separately since February 2017 and repeated efforts at reconciliation had failed. He also supported the amount awarded towards permanent alimony, based on the income and financial circumstances of the husband. Not on talking terms The high court noted that the marriage had lasted only a few months before the couple stopped living together. It also noted that the wife had admitted that although they had lived together as husband and wife until February 2017, they were not even on talking terms afterwards. The court clarified that differences in financial background, standard of living or lifestyle cannot by themselves amount to matrimonial cruelty. The relevance of these circumstances is only in understanding the actual matrimonial dynamics between the parties, it added. The court upheld the divorce, noting the long period of separation, lack of communication, repeated but unsuccessful efforts at reconciliation, serious allegations exchanged by the couple and the overall course of their relationship. It held that these circumstances amounted to mental cruelty. On alimony, the court considered the husbands income, expenses and liabilities, the wifes professional qualifications and previous employment, as well as her current unemployment. It said the amount needed a reasonable enhancement and increased the total permanent alimony to Rs 25 lakh.

articleTitle: Railways to pay Rs 47,000 fine 8 years after family ‘robbed’ in Mewar Express AC coach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand Consumer Commission Indian Railways Robbery AC Coach Passenger Railway Police Consumer News
description: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission was hearing the Railways’ appeal against the district commission awarding compensation for the theft of belongings of a family during the Mewar Express journey.
body_raw: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission held Indian Railways liable for negligence after a family travelling in a reserved AC coach of the Mewar Express reported that thieves forcibly took away their valuables near Mathura in the early hours of July 2, 2018. The commission also upheld Rs 47,222 payout ordered by the District Consumer Commission, Dehradun. The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president, Kumkum Rani, and member B S Manral heard an appeal filed by the Union of India and railway authorities against the May 11, 2022 order of the district commission, which had directed the Railways to pay Rs 37,222 towards the loss suffered by the complainants, Rs 25,000 towards mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. The negligence on the part of the railway administration and its servants is clearly proved, the state commission said on October 5, referring to the circumstances of the incident. It found that the reserved coach doors had been left open during the night and that there was no coach attendant, police personnel or TTE inside the coach when the theft occurred. The dispute arose from the familys return journey from Udaipur to New Delhi on July 1, 2018. They were travelling in the reserved AC coach of the Mewar Express and reached Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station on July 2. During the journey, when the train reached Mathura at around 4 am, the complainants said unauthorised persons entered the coach and forcibly took away the belongings of two passengers. Theft reported during early-morning journey According to the complaint, one of the persons forcibly took away a large bag belonging to Veena Dobhal, who was sleeping at her berth. The bag had been kept under her head, below the pillow. She woke up when the bag was taken and raised an alarm. Other members of the family and passengers also woke up and tried to catch the person, but he jumped from the moving train with the bag. The passengers then searched for the coach attendant, RPF personnel, and the TTE but did not find any of them available in the coach. The TTE was subsequently contacted and informed about the theft. An FIR form was filled in and later handed over to the Government Railway Police at Hazrat Nizamuddin. A Zero FIR was lodged at the railway police station at 750 am on July 2, 2018. The complainants told the commission that they had not been able to ascertain the outcome of the investigation despite their efforts. Railways blamed passengers The Railways denied negligence and argued that passengers were responsible for safeguarding luggage carried by them. It relied on the provisions of the Railways Act concerning liability for loss or damage to luggage and pointed out that the family had neither booked the luggage with the Railways nor declared that they were carrying valuables. The Railways also argued that passengers were advised inside the coach to secure their luggage with a chain and that the complainants had not followed the instruction. It maintained that reserved coaches were meant only for authorised passengers and that coach attendants and TTEs were responsible for keeping the doors closed during the night. The state commission rejected this defence in the circumstances of the case. It noted that the complainants had specifically alleged that the coach doors and the end doors of the vestibule had not been kept locked. The commission also noted that the Railways had not specifically denied this allegation and had not produced evidence from the coach attendant or TTE to establish that the doors had been kept closed. If the doors of the coach were locked closed, there was no occasion for the unauthorised persons miscreants to have enter into the coach and commit theft robbery, the commission observed. It further rejected the argument that the availability of remedies under railway laws barred the consumer complaint, noting that the Consumer Protection Act provides remedies in addition to those available under other laws. The commission awarded Rs 47,222 in total, comprising Rs 37,222 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation expenses, with 7 per cent annual interest on Rs 37,222 from July 31, 2020, until payment. Takeaway Passengers may seek compensation for valuables stolen from a reserved railway coach when they can establish that the loss resulted from negligence or misconduct by railway staff, such as failure to secure the coach or prevent unauthorised entry. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Uttarakhand 1800-180-4188 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Parents arrested for repeated rape, sexual abuse of minor daughter in Gujarat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gujarat police
description: According to police, the girl told them her father had repeatedly abused her over a period of a fortnight in September. Police found pictures of the abuse in the girl’s mother’s phone
body_raw: A couple living in the Kutch district of Gujarat were arrested over the past weekend for the alleged repeated rape and sexual abuse of their minor daughter over a period of a fortnight in the second half of September. The horrific incident came to light only after the minor girl managed to get her hands on a phone and call police, which led to her rescue and the arrest of her parents, police officers said. However, even this happened only after the couple had succeeded in thwarting the complainants attempt to reach police once, and cutting off ways for her to reach for help by switching off the mobile phone that she had used, officers said. Senior officers of the Kutch East Police have claimed that they have found evidence to support the minors allegations in a phone that they seized from her mother. This evidence allegedly includes nude photos of the child, as well as photos of her with her father, the officers said. According to police officers, the complainant, who is in her early teens and the oldest among four siblings, was caught by her mother allegedly talking to a male friend in a North Indian state. The woman had allegedly complained about this incident to her husband. The minor told the police that the alleged abuse had begun the next day. She was not given food for a day, after which her father had allegedly raped her in front of her mother in the living room of their home. The entire sequence of abuse was repeated again and again during the latter half of last month, the complainant alleged-she was stripped and beaten before being raped, according to police officers. The complainant allegedly told the officers that on September 30, she had finally attempted to reach out to police from the home of a relative who lives in the same housing society. However, her parents had snatched away the phone and switched it off, she allegedly told police. This was followed by another day of abuse on October 1, and her mother allegedly took photos of the events, the complainant told police. But then she managed to escape again to her relatives home and to call the police helpline number 112. The minor gave the police her address, after which personnel from the jurisdictional police station reached her home and rescued her, police officers said. Mukesh Chaudhary, Deputy Superintendent of Police of the Kutch East Police, told The Indian Express that the father and mother of the complainant had been placed under arrest on the same day after the FIR was registered and evidence was found on the mothers phone that corroborated the account of the complainant. Further investigations were underway, Chaudhary said.

articleTitle: After sexual harassment complaint, Delhi cop’s additional charge withheld
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat
description: Three women journalists have complained of alleged harassment during an October 3 protest near Jantar Mantar. One of them specifically named Delhi cop Vivek Bhagat
body_raw: The Delhi government has withheld a temporary posting given to Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat, who is accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The government said Bhagat had requested that he not be given the charge of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police until the allegations are fully investigated. The government said the proposal to confer the Additional Duty Charge ADC on 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers, including Bhagat, was initiated on August 25, much before the present set of events, and the orders were issued after due approval on October 5. It clarified that this was a temporary arrangement with no financial benefit, and that officers assigned the charge could not exercise the statutory powers of the regular incumbents. Accordingly, the October 5 order is being modified in respect of Bhagat and will be reissued for the 11 remaining officers, the government said. Bhagat is currently posted as Sub-Divisional Police Officer, Connaught Place. The complaints The development came at a time when three women journalists had complained of alleged sexual harassment and manhandling during the October 3 protest near Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls. The women journalists had alleged that they were manhandled and subjected to inappropriate behaviour while covering the police action during the protest. One of the complainants specifically alleged that Bhagat touched her inappropriately while she was covering the police action. The complaints by the three women have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a fair and impartial inquiry. The government order said the arrangement had been made in the interest of government work. Besides Bhagat, the officers assigned the current duty charge include Dr Vikas Sheokand, A Venkatesh, Gursewak Singh, Renu Lata, Vidushi Kaushik, Manu Himanshu, Sakaria Mihir Pravinbhai, Garima Tiwari, Ashish Kumar, Manish Ladla and Rohit Gupta. The government said the arrangement would continue until the Ministry of Home Affairs fills the Addl DCP posts on a regular basis. It can also be discontinued at any time without assigning any reason.
