articleTitle: Sonakshi Sinha, Shahid Kapoor’s driver opened a momo shop, Tukaram Mundhe shut it down
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Suraj Lama, whose momos shop was suspended by the FDA, was once a Bollywood celebrity driver.
description: Suraj Lama Momos, a popular dumpling eatery in Versova, Mumbai, had its eatery suspended by Tukaram Mundhe-led Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration.
body_raw: Tukaram Mundhe-led Maharashtra Food Drug Administration FDA suspended the licenses of eight more eateries on Monday, as part of its intense festival season encroachment drive. These outlets included the original Andheri West branch of Suraj Lama Momos, one of the most popular momo shops of Mumbai, the eponymous owner of which has an interesting Bollywood connection. Suraj Lama was Shahid Kapoor, Sonakshi Sinhas driver Suraj Lama relocated to Mumbai at the age of 14, leaving behind his village Mirik in Darjeeling, in order to seek employment. After doing a few odd jobs, Suraj became a celebrity driver. He worked in that capacity for 25 years, including with actors Sonakshi Sinha and Shahid Kapoor, and also drove the car for leading banners like Karan Johars Dharma Productions. I worked with a lot of dedication, and saw people I worked with as my own family, but sometimes I wasnt seen as equal. It bothered me, Suraj confessed in an interview with The Indian Express a couple of years ago. He recalled an incident as the final nail in the coffin - I drove an actor to the set. There was a child who wanted to take a photo with the actor, and had been waiting for a long time. I thought of helping that child, but when I conveyed his wish to the actor, they refused. I didnt feel good, he recounted. When Suraj quit driving to sell momos The subsequent rise in app-based cab services like Ola and Uber was also a factor in Suraj going for a pivot to selling momos in 2017. He even made Sonakshi and her family taste his momos, and they approved of his skills. So, he decided to quit his job, sell his motorbike and buy a cycle, with which he started a pop-up shop. He also convinced his wife Vijayata to join him, so she also quit her job of a cook at singer KKs household. In hindsight, it was a big risk. We both were earning around Rs 30,000 each, spending half of it running our home, and saving the rest. The gamble paid off, but it could have gone in another direction as well, admitted Suraj. Since momos werent as easily available in Mumbai back then as they were in North India, Suraj got a pretty good start. Hed cycle across parts of Andheri West to sell both vegetarian and non-vegetarian momos. The demand swelled up fast, which prompted him to open a roadside eatery in Versova. In fact, when I first asked the owner of our current store to lease the space to me, he said, You wont be able to afford it, and later, he himself reached out to me, said Suraj. Even though Suraj and his wife earned Rs 30,000 each from their previous jobs, once they began selling momos, they quickly began earnings Rs 700 in a day alone. He spelled out the secret to his recipe, claiming that the momos reminded him of home. My momos are just like my mothers. I follow her recipe. I dont use preservatives or artificial colouring, he told Mid-Day in 2017. He also claims his wife, a great cook, makes delectable momos. Even though he expanded with more outlets in Malad and Kandivali, he hadnt reached other far-flung areas of high demand, including Pune, Nashik, and Gujarat. It is important to maintain quality. Today, we have a central kitchen in Mumbai, overseen entirely by my wife, with a staff of 25, preparing about 16,000 momos daily across various options. It is these momos, cooked till about 90 per cent, that go to each store, whether run by us or a franchise. Until I can do that in another city, I wont expand, said Suraj in 2024. The authority flagged lapses in the way the food was handled and stored, in sanitation, cleanliness and safeguards intended to prevent contamination. It said the violations were serious enough to take swift action against the establishment under the applicable food safety guidelines.

articleTitle: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026: How Uruguay beat Spain and Portugal to top spot

description: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026 list: Know more about the world's 10 best countries for retirees seeking financial security, superior healthcare, and an exceptional lifestyle.
body_raw: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026 Uruguay has been named the best country in the world for retirees, taking the No. 1 spot in the annual Global Retirement Report and Index 2026 published by Global Citizen Solutions. The overall rankings are derived from a composite score calculated across five weighted pillars quality of life, mobility and citizenship, tax, cost and investment, and administrative procedure, including processing speed and family inclusion. With a near-perfect score of 99.90, Uruguay emerged as the worlds premier retirement destination and was one of only two top-10 nations to score at least 75 in every evaluation category. Mauritius, Spain, and Costa Rica were ranked at No. 2, 3, and 4, respectively. Portugal, Paraguay, and Latvia were ranked at No. 5, 6, and 7, respectively. Andorra and Italy were ranked 8th and 9th, respectively, while Greece closed out the top 10 list. A primary driver behind Uruguays top ranking is its streamlined immigration and naturalisation pathway. Eligible applicants can apply directly for citizenship without completing a prior temporary residency period. The index also highlights Uruguays manageable monthly income requirement of 1,700, along with short routes to naturalisation three years for married applicants and five years for single applicants. According to the report, the modern concept of retirement has shifted away from simply withdrawing from active life. Patricia Casaburi, CEO of Global Citizen Solutions, noted that the concept of retirement has changed over the years. Earlier, retirement was closely tied to withdrawing from active life. But lately, retirement has become a deliberate new chapter. Casaburi added that retirement involves more than safety. Quality of life after retirement also has to be healthier, lighter in taxes, and richer in possibility than the life left behind, Casaburi said. Rank Country 1. Uruguay 2. Mauritius 3. Spain 4. articleTitle: 70s AI photo trend: 6 Gemini prompts to give your photos a retro Indian look
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 70s retro AI Gemini trend prompts
description: To create a photo, users can upload a photograph to Gemini and describe the period, setting, mood, lighting, and photographic style they want.
body_raw: The AI photo trend is once again taking social media users back several decades. Instead of adding a vintage filter to their pictures, users are turning ordinary photographs into detailed 1970s-style scenes using AI image-generation tools such as Google Gemini. From old department stores and optical shops to rooftop photography, the trend focuses on recreating specific moments that look as though they were captured decades ago. These photos feature muted colours, film grain, imperfect exposure, faded textures, period clothing, and everyday Indian surroundings. To create one, users can upload a photograph to Gemini and describe the period, setting, mood, lighting, and photographic style they want. More detailed prompts can help create a more specific and believable result. Here are some prompts to try 1. 1973 department-store escalator Turn your photograph into a scene from the opening day of a newly installed escalator in an Indian department store. Prompt Transform my uploaded image into an entirely original Indian department-store photograph captured in 1973, on a day when a newly installed escalator has become a point of public curiosity. Preserve the persons facial identity and natural features. Place them among mirrored columns, patterned flooring, period interiors and curious shoppers. Use authentic 1970s Indian clothing, muted analogue colours, subtle film grain, slight exposure imperfections and the look of a photograph taken on a vintage film camera. 2. 1974 optical shop Give your photograph the feel of an old optical-shop picture without relying on stereotypical oversized 70s glasses. Prompt Create an entirely original Indian optical-shop photograph from 1974 using my uploaded image as the exact human reference. Preserve the persons facial identity and features. Place them inside a modest Indian optical shop surrounded by loose trial lenses, glass reflections, wooden displays and a rotating lens tray. Use realistic 1970s interiors, natural indoor lighting, faded colours, analogue film grain and subtle imperfections associated with an old printed photograph. 3. 1972 civic-wall photograph This prompt recreates the visual character of an Indian public wall from the early 1970s. Prompt Transform my uploaded image into an entirely original Indian civic-wall photograph captured in 1972. Preserve the persons identity and facial features. Place them beside a limewashed public wall featuring hand-painted lettering, uneven brush strokes, chipped paint and a drying paint edge. Recreate the atmosphere of an ordinary Indian street from the early 1970s, with period-appropriate clothing and surroundings. Make it look like an authentic analogue photograph with muted colours, natural shadows and subtle film grain. 4. 1977 rooftop photography class For something more cinematic, imagine the subject attending a photography lesson on an Indian rooftop. Prompt Create an entirely original Indian rooftop photography-learning photograph from 1977 using my uploaded image as the exact human reference. Preserve the persons facial identity and natural appearance. Place them in a small rooftop photography class with a vintage camera, grey card and basic photographic equipment. Include strong afternoon shadows, weathered terraces and authentic 1970s Indian surroundings. Give the photograph a documentary feel with muted colours, realistic analogue film grain and slight imperfections. 5. 1970s railway platform For a quintessentially Indian retro setting, transform the photograph into a railway-platform scene. Prompt Transform my uploaded image into an entirely original Indian railway-platform photograph from 1975. Preserve the persons exact facial identity and natural features. Place them on a busy Indian railway platform with period luggage, old railway signage, metal benches and passengers dressed in authentic 1970s clothing. Use warm natural light, faded colours, realistic analogue film grain, slight motion blur and the imperfect texture of a photograph printed from 35mm film. 6. 1970s neighbourhood photo Users can also recreate the feeling of an ordinary family photograph taken in an Indian neighbourhood. Prompt Create an entirely original Indian neighbourhood photograph from 1976 using my uploaded image as the exact human reference. Preserve the persons identity, facial features and natural expression. Place them outside a modest Indian home with scooters, balconies, potted plants, textured walls and everyday neighbourhood activity typical of the 1970s. Make the photograph feel candid and unstaged, as though taken by a family member on a 35mm film camera. Use slightly faded colours, subtle grain, natural lighting and authentic period details. Rather than simply asking Gemini to make this photo vintage, users can describe a particular year, location, objects, clothing, lighting and photographic style. They can then refine the generated image by asking the AI to change specific elements while retaining the subjects appearance.

articleTitle: Karnataka job scam: Flat purchased near Bengaluru airport by IAS officer’s kin under lens
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar
description: Arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, the then KPSC's controller of examinations, allegedly received around Rs 1.30 crore of the Rs 1.52 crore from candidates as bribes for leaking the entrance examination for veterinary doctors.
body_raw: An apartment purchased in the name of a family member of arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in Karnataka has come under scrutiny of the Enforcement Directorate in connection with a job recruitment fraud at the Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC, sources in Karnataka Police said. During interrogation, Basavaraj Kannale, a middleman involved in the fraud, revealed that Gangwar, the then KPSCs controller of examinations, allegedly received around Rs 1.30 crore of the Rs 1.52 crore from candidates as bribes for leaking the entrance examination of veterinary doctors conducted on January 8 and 9. Around 20 candidates allegedly paid Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh through Kannale, a close associate of Gangwar. Gangwar, 41, served as KPSCs controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026. The Criminal Investigation Department CID and the ED arrested Gangwar on August 29 and September 18, respectively. It was found that Gangwar used some of the proceeds of the crime to purchase an apartment in the name of the brother of the IAS officer at the Godrej Royal Woods complex near the Bengaluru International Airport at Devanahalli. The IAS officers brother and family are unaware of the flat purchased in their name in Bengaluru, and they never visited or used the property. It was used by the officer for hosting parties and other activities since it provided privacy, said police sources familiar with the probe. Gangwar has also stated before the ED that a portion of the amount he received from Kannale was used to purchase a flat in the name of his brother, apart from using the funds for buying gold jewellery for his fiance. While the investigations have tracked Rs 52 lakh in bribe amounts being funneled back to the IAS officer - through bank accounts of associates of the middleman - for the purchase of expensive pieces of gold and diamond jewellery at the Bhima Jewellery showroom in Bengaluru for the IAS officers girlfriend, the remaining amount of bribes is untraced. The ED has earlier told the court that the apartment at Devanahalli was bought with proceeds of the crimes at the KPSC. The proceeds of the recruitment frauds at the KPSC were routed through the middleman Kannale and his associates for the purchase of immovable property in the name of his brother, purchase of gold jewellery in the name of his fiance, and payment of personal expenses, a special court for PMLA cases noted last week after an ED submission. The ED has reported that an unexplained amount of Rs 26 lakh was deposited in cash between January 2025 and August 2025 in the bank accounts of a brother and sister-in-law of the IAS officer. The ED is also probing immovable assets acquired by the IAS officer - such as a semi-constructed house in Bareilly in 2025 for Rs 25 lakh, and a real estate construction business launched by his older brothers in 2025 in Uttar Pradesh for possible links to illegal gratifications at the KPSC. Gold jewellery purchases Unlike the property purchases linked to the IAS officer, the CID and ED probes have mapped the flow of Rs 52 lakh of funds from the KPSC veterinary officers recruitment fraud to Kannale and associates, and to Gangwar for jewellery purchases by his fiance. According to the investigations, gold jewellery worth Rs 29.94 lakh was purchased for Gangwars girlfriendin March 2026 at Bhima Jewellery in Bengaluru, and gold jewellery worth Rs 23 lakh was purchased again in July 2026. In both cases, the funds were provided by Kannale. The CID probe has revealed that Rs 15 lakh for the jewellery purchase in March 2026 came from a Kotak Mahindra Bank account of Balu Reddy, an associate of Kannale, and another Rs 15 lakh from the Om Lakshmi Souharda Sahakari Bank in Bidar, operated by Kannales friend Onkar Kamshetti, where aspirants transferred bribes from bank accounts. Gangwar has reportedly told investigators that he asked Kannale to buy the jewellery in July for his fiance through money transfers of Rs 8 lakh from Kannales accountant Umesh and Rs 15 lakh by Onkar Kamshetti, the vice president of the Om Lakshmi Souharda Sahakari Bank in Bidar. Gangwar has made contradictory claims that his fiance issued cheques for repayment of the cost of the gold purchases and that the jewellery purchases were a birthday gift to her. The ED is continuing investigations against the IAS officer to look at whether similar scams were also perpetrated in 12 other KPSC examinations carried out during Gangwars tenure from January 2024 to March 2026. The Karnataka High Court has ordered a SIT probe into two cases of KPSC recruitment frauds, which has been challenged by the Karnataka government in the Supreme Court on the grounds that there were no adverse remarks by the court on the CID probe into the alleged KPSC job frauds. Former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar is also under investigation in the veterinary officers recruitment fraud as well as the recruitment of his daughter through illegal means to the post of an industrial extension officer.

articleTitle: He hacked into medical body’s records to help unqualified people practice in Maharashtra
articleFeaturedImageAlt: maharashtra MMC unqualified doctors fraud
description: These applicants, whose details were changed, were students who obtained an MBBS degree abroad without clearing qualifying exams in India – necessary to practise as doctors in India.
body_raw: Maharashtra Cyber has busted an inter-state network in which a medical representative, acting as a link between pharmaceutical companies and doctors, hacked into the Maharashtra Medical Council MMC website and changed records of certain applicants to enable them to practise as doctors. Investigators also suspect that exam websites of other states may have been targeted similarly. The applicants, whose details were changed, were students who obtained MBBS degrees abroad but had not cleared the qualifying exams - the screening test conducted by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences NBEMS - required to practise as doctors in India. Investigators suspect the applicants paid lakhs to the accused to manipulate the MMC records into showing that they had passed the examination. How was the MMC fraud detected? The MMC approached the Maharashtra Cyber police station after detecting unauthorised access to their systems and database. During the investigation, Maharashtra Cyber found that certain foreign medical graduates who had not qualified the mandatory FMGE Screening Test also had medical registration certificates, as the MMC site showed they had cleared it. The agency then identified three accused allegedly involved in the fraudulent activity. The two accused have been identified as Varun Akhade 28 and Sanket Unhale 26, who studied in the Philippines after allegedly failing to qualify in the required local examination, Maharashtra Cyber SP Ajay Kumar Bansal said. Further investigation led Maharashtra Cyber to apprehend another person, identified as Rahul Patil, suspected to be a key operative of the inter-state gang involved in the generation and procurement of the forged documents. He charged anywhere between Rs 15-25 lakhs per applicant. An official said, We are checking if the records of any more accused have been manipulated in the MMC database. We are also checking if the accused had manipulated the database of other state medical council exams, as we have found some data of persons from other states who had paid him money. More arrests are likely in the case.

articleTitle: Tamil Nadu bypolls are an early test for Vijay’s young government
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay
description: Both constituencies in the state are reserved seats, won in April by AIADMK candidates who subsequently resigned, joined Vijay’s TVK, and are now seeking election again under their new party’s symbol
body_raw: Five months after Tamil Nadu voters elected a new government, some of them returned to polling booths on Tuesday to answer a narrower question Whether the political movement that brought C Joseph Vijay to power has endured through its first months of governing. Voting was brisk by late morning in the two Assembly by-elections in Tamil Nadu. At 11 am, Madurantakam recorded 35.55 per cent turnout and Dharapuram 37.28 per cent. Both constituencies are reserved seats and were won in April by AIADMK candidates who resigned to join Vijays Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK, and are now seeking re-election with this party. In neighbouring Puducherry, meanwhile, Thattanchavady was voting in a separate by-election necessitated by Chief Minister N Rangasamys decision to vacate the constituency after winning two seats in April. Turnout there was 19.2 per cent by 9 am, slightly above the 18.32 per cent recorded during the same first two hours in the April Assembly election. ALSO READ Vijays river of obscenity barb to slam DMK, Udhayanidhis reels counter The Tamil Nadu contests carry a different political weight. TVK won 108 seats in April but fell short of an outright majority and formed the government with support from smaller parties. Since then, defections from the AIADMK have altered the political landscape. Madurantakams Maragatham Kumaravel and Dharapurams P Sathyabama were among the AIADMK legislators who resigned and moved to TVK. Voters are now being asked, in effect, whether their representatives moved alone. That question explains the unusual intensity of the campaign. Vijay spent four days personally campaigning in the two constituencies - two days of public rallies and two of roadshows - a substantial commitment for two by-elections from a Chief Minister whose own appearances during the April statewide campaign had been comparatively limited. For TVK, winning both seats would validate not only its candidates but the continuing movement of politicians and local organisations towards the ruling party. Losing one would give the AIADMK and DMK an opening to argue that the post-April political realignment has limits. CHECK THE LIVE UPDATES ON THE BYELECTIONS HERE. The first hours of voting offered few reliable clues. Madurantakam began sluggishly, reaching 15.99 per cent turnout around 9.30 am, before the pace accelerated. When reporters asked Kumaravel about the initially lower turnout compared with the general election, she offered a distinctly local explanation Tuesday, she said, was a day when many women visited temples. They would pray for a TVK victory and then come to vote, she said. People have the same enthusiasm as during the general election, Kumaravel said. They are coming to vote with smiling faces. The gender question has occupied TVKs calculations throughout the campaign. Women outnumber men among registered voters in both constituencies Madurantakam has 108,797 women and 104,926 men among its 213,788 voters, while Dharapuram has 116,013 women and 107,285 men among 223,306 electors. Earlier, Kumaravel said voters retained confidence in Vijay and argued that the four-month-old government needed more time to demonstrate change. Polling hitches Polling itself encountered some interruptions. In Madurantakam, electronic voting machines EVMs developed technical problems at two polling stations. At booth 26 in Sithandi, the control unit had to be replaced twice. At booth 55 in L Endathur, the ballot unit was changed after polling agents objected to a visible mark on the name of a candidate. In Dharapuram, voting at a booth in Kottapulipalayam was interrupted by an EVM malfunction, while another machine problem delayed polling at Kundadam-Manurpalayam. There were political disputes as well. At Kolinjivadi, agents objected to a polling official whom they accused of acting in favour of TVK, leading to an interruption in voting. At Veerachimangalam, AIADMK members stopped a vehicle carrying TVK functionaries from outside the constituency, alleging that they had come to distribute tokens to households. DMK and AIADMK members then argued with TVK workers. The allegations come after a campaign in which opposition parties repeatedly accused the ruling party of using money and government machinery to influence voters. TVK has denied accusations of cash distribution. Sathyabama, the TVK candidate in Dharapuram, also entered polling day dealing with a video circulating on social media that purported to show her discussing election expenditure and other matters. After voting at a school in Madukkampalayam, she said the video had been fabricated and that those responsible for releasing it had been identified. The people are clear, she said, insisting that the video would not affect the result. For the AIADMK, the identity of the TVK candidates has been central to the election. Both were elected on AIADMK tickets only months ago. Edappadi K Palaniswami has accused them of betraying the voters who elected them, while AIADMK workers have repeatedly used the word traitor during the campaign. The DMK has made much the same event into a broader democratic argument. Former CM M K Stalin described the by-elections as having been imposed on voters because elected representatives resigned and returned to seek their votes under another party. The DMK has its own stake in Tuesdays numbers. It is contesting without most of the alliance that accompanied it into the April election. Even without winning, an improvement on its previous performance would allow the party to point to the size of its independent vote after its loss of power. The Left parties, despite supporting the TVK government from outside, are contesting against it CPIMs Suganthi is in the race in Madurantakam and CPIs P Lakshmanan in Dharapuram. Naam Tamilar Katchi is also contesting both seats, making the elections five-cornered. In Puducherry, the political geometry is different. Eleven candidates are contesting in Thattanchavady, but the principal contest is among the ruling AINRC-led NDA, Congress and the DMK. Rangasamys AINRC has fielded Ashok Anand, while Congress candidate E Vinayagam has TVKs support. The DMK has fielded K Sethuselvam. For Rangasamy, the election provides an early measure of support for his four-month-old NDA government. For Vijay, the Puducherry contest places TVK in the less exposed position of supporting an ally rather than defending its own government and two defectors. The distinction is important. A general election asks voters who should govern. A by-election held five months later may be asking what they make of what has happened since. In Madurantakam and Dharapuram, even that question has an unusually literal form. Voters elected two candidates in April. The candidates changed parties. On Tuesday, the voters get to decide whether they have changed with them. Polling continues until 6 pm. Counting will take place on October 9.

articleTitle: Harmanpreet Kaur’s real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur's last act as India captain was leading the side to their second consecutive Asian Games gold medal. (BCCI Photo)
description: Before her, India reached two ODI World Cup finals. Under her, semifinals and finals became regular, and the 2025 title came at home
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaur ran back to complete the catch that sealed Indias 2025 ODI World Cup triumph. The captain who had carried Indian womens cricket through expectation was there at the finish. But her legacy is bigger than that trophy. Harmanpreet leaves captaincy having changed what India expects from itself. Before her, India had reached the ODI World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 under Mithali Raj. Under Harmanpreet, India became regulars at the business end of tournaments the 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, the 2020 T20 World Cup final, the 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal and, eventually, the 2025 ODI World Cup title at home. Her biggest contribution was renewed belief. Semifinals and finals were no longer a flash-in-the-pan moment. India started to feel like they belonged there. She took over when Indian womens cricket was growing, but was still searching for consistency and belief. At the 2018 T20 World Cup, her first major tournament as captain, she announced herself with a 103 against New Zealand. It was a statement of the captain she would be aggressive, unafraid of the big stage. That intensity stayed with her. Harmanpreet was emotional, vocal and sometimes combative. Players were coming in with bigger ambitions, and her job was to build a team that believed it could compete at the highest level. Her batting, however, became less consistent as the years went by. Her strike rate was a concern. The Harmanpreet who could win a match from anywhere showed up less often. But she still produced when India needed her. In the 2025 World Cup semifinal against Australia, with India chasing a record total, Harmanpreet made 89 and helped keep the chase alive alongside Jemimah Rodrigues. A year later, in a must-win T20 World Cup game against Australia, she made 56 off 27, hitting three sixes in the final over to take India to a competitive total. Those innings offered reminders of the player India will want to see more often. In her farewell post, Harmanpreet acknowledged the cost of captaincy herself. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first, she wrote. There were difficult days too defeats, criticism, questions over her decisions. She faced them as openly as she celebrated the wins. I gave this team everything I had, she wrote. I carried the responsibility with pride. She said every difficult decision was made with one intention to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves. She leaves behind a team in which Smriti Mandhana has become the batting leader, Deepti Sharma a central figure, and younger players such as N Sree Charani have emerged with confidence. It is a team that has won a World Cup and now knows what it feels like to be there. Harmanpreet wrote that she leaves captaincy with a heart full of emotions, but also with PEACE because she believes the team is in a good place. It is a team with talent, character, belief and a future that she is excited to be part of. Her post ends Now, Im ready to play for the love of the game again. That is what Indian cricket will hope for. Without the burden of captaincy, Harmanpreet can focus on being the batter who can change a game. At 37, the hope is that giving up the captaincy brings back more of her best batting. India have a home global event, the Womens Champions Trophy, in February next year, before bigger challenges in 2028 and 2029. She says she has done her duty. She leaves the next captain with more than a World Cup trophy a team that believes it can compete on the biggest stages. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, Harmanpreet wrote. For Indian cricket, the hope is that the next chapter brings back the player who made everyone believe.

articleTitle: Too much screen time? Try the 20-20-20 rule to protect your eyes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: eyes
description: Prolonged screen exposure is increasingly becoming a lifestyle challenge for eye health, with digital eye strain, dry eyes and rising concerns around myopia, especially among children
body_raw: Written by By Dr Mahipal Singh Sachdev A 12-year-old boy was recently brought to our hospital by his parents after he began complaining that he could no longer see the writing clearly on his classroom board. At home, he was spending several hours on a tablet for online classes, gaming and videos, often without taking breaks. His parents initially assumed that the frequent eye rubbing and headaches were simply because he was using the screen too much. An eye examination, however, revealed myopia or short-sightedness that required correction. The case is a reminder that what may appear to be ordinary screen fatigue can sometimes signal an underlying vision problem-particularly in children. His prolonged close-up work on devices, combined with very low outdoor activity and exposure to natural light had affected vision. This may cause the eyeball to grow longer than normal, causing light to focus in front of the retina instead of directly on it. As a result, distant objects appear blurry. From the moment we wake up to check our phones to hours spent on laptops at work and evenings scrolling through social media, screens have become an inseparable part of modern life. While digital devices have transformed the way we work, learn and communicate, prolonged and uninterrupted screen use is also putting increasing demands on our eyes. One of the most common consequences of prolonged screen use is digital eye strain. People may experience dryness, burning or irritation in the eyes, blurred vision, headaches, tired eyes and difficulty focusing after spending long periods looking at a screen. A major reason is that we tend to blink less while concentrating on digital content, allowing the surface of the eye to become dry. Simply looking at a screen does not mean that our eyes are being permanently damaged. However, prolonged, uninterrupted near work can cause significant discomfort and fatigue. The solution is not necessarily to abandon technology, but to use it more responsibly. The 20-20-20 rule can make a difference One of the simplest habits is the 20-20-20 rule after every 20 minutes of screen use, look at something around 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. Regular breaks allow the eyes to relax and can reduce symptoms of digital eye strain. Blinking consciously and frequently is equally important. Screen users should also maintain an appropriate viewing distance, reduce glare and ensure that the screen is positioned slightly below eye level. If dryness persists, an eye specialist can advise whether lubricating eye drops are appropriate. Children need special attention The concern becomes particularly important in children. Increasing time spent on near-vision activities, combined with insufficient outdoor exposure, has been associated with the growing concern around myopia, or short-sightedness. WHO guidance recommends regular breaks during near work and encouraging children to spend adequate time outdoors in daylight. Parents should therefore avoid allowing children to spend long, uninterrupted periods on phones, tablets or gaming devices. Outdoor play should be made a regular part of a childs daily routine rather than treating it as an occasional activity. Dont blame everything on blue light There is also considerable confusion around blue light. While excessive exposure to bright screens in the evening can interfere with the bodys sleep-wake cycle, current evidence does not establish that the blue light emitted by ordinary digital screens causes retinal damage or age-related macular degeneration. Digital eye discomfort is more closely associated with prolonged or improper screen use. Therefore, rather than relying solely on blue-light-blocking glasses, people should focus on the fundamentals - regular breaks, adequate blinking, appropriate screen distance, good lighting and reduced screen use before bedtime. When should you see an eye specialist? Occasional tiredness after a long day on screens is usually not a cause for alarm. However, persistent blurred vision, frequent headaches, recurrent eye pain, redness, double vision, difficulty seeing distant objects or continuing dryness should not simply be attributed to screen use. A comprehensive eye examination can identify an underlying refractive error or other eye condition that may be contributing to the symptoms. Regular eye examinations are particularly important for children, as early detection of vision problems can help prevent them from affecting learning and daily activities. Screens are here to stay, but unhealthy screen habits dont have to be. Small behavioural changes - taking regular breaks, blinking more, spending time outdoors and getting periodic eye examinations - can go a long way towards keeping our eyes comfortable and our vision healthy in an increasingly digital world. The author is Chairman Managing Director, Centre for Sight Group of Eye Hospitals

articleTitle: TV damaged ‘during shifting’, Delhi man wins Rs 50,000 payout from packers and movers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Consumer Commission TV Packers and Movers Delhi TV Gurgaon Consumer News
description: A Delhi consumer commission was hearing the complaint alleging deficiency in service after household goods, including a TV and shoe rack, were damaged during shifting.
body_raw: A Delhi consumer commission has ordered a packers and movers company to pay Rs 50,000 after a customers TV was allegedly damaged when its box fell during packing, and a shoe rack was also found damaged on delivery. It held that the companys own records and the consumers documents supported the claim. President Suresh Kumar Gupta and member Harshali Kaur of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-West Delhi were hearing a complaint filed by one Rajnish Kumar Ahuja, who had paid Rs 18,050 to the company for packing and transporting his household goods from Naraina Vihar to Gurgaon. We have no reason to disbelieve the complainants averments, the commission said in the September 16 order, considering the documentary evidence produced by him, and added that the evidence had remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. The dispute began on October 16, 2023, when four employees of the company arrived at Ahujas residence to pack his household goods. The company prepared a list of 50 items, including their values, as informed by the consumer. The goods were delivered the next day. TV box fell during packing According to Ahuja, the Sony LED TV was checked and found to be working before it was packed. He said the box containing the TV fell while the employees were making space to place it with the other goods. The delivery acknowledgement carried his handwritten note, stating that the TV box had fallen during packing and the screen was damaged, while the TV had been found in working condition before packing. The note also recorded that the shoe rack was damaged during unpacking. Photographs of the damaged items were placed before the commission. Ahuja then approached the companys customer care and shared photographs of the damaged TV. The authorised Sony service centre initially estimated the repair cost at Rs 29,618. It later informed him that it could not arrange the display panel and offered an exchange model for Rs 44,788. Ahuja forwarded the communication to the company. The company initially closed the claim as No Claim, stating that its scrutiny showed the TV had not been damaged by its employees. It later offered Rs 10,000. After Ahuja wrote to the companys chairman, its legal department offered Rs 15,000 through a letter dated February 6, 2024. He rejected the offer and pursued the consumer complaint, seeking Rs 90,000. Commission rejects valuation argument Before the commission, the company described the complaint as false and baseless. It argued that the TV had not been declared or valued and that its liability was restricted under the Carriage by Road Act. The commission rejected the valuation argument, pointing out that the companys own document listed the value of the LED TV as Rs 30,000. It also found that the consumers documentary evidence supporting his allegations had remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. The commission also noted that the companys defence had been struck off after it failed to file its reply within the legal period despite appearing before it. The commission did not accept Ahujas separate allegation that the company delayed delivery. He claimed that delivery had been promised on October 16 and that the delay caused inconvenience. However, the commission found no mention of the alleged delay in his handwritten delivery acknowledgement, the emails exchanged with the company or his National Consumer Helpline complaint dated December 2, 2023. It therefore declined to rely on the allegation. The commission allowed the complaint and held the company deficient in service. It directed the company to pay Rs 50,000 towards the damaged TV and shoe rack, inclusive of litigation costs. Takeaway Document the condition and value of your belongings before shifting, and record any damage on the delivery receipt itself. Keep photographs, emails, repair estimates and other supporting documents, as these can be crucial when seeking compensation for damage during transportation. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi1800-11-4000 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance. articleTitle: Alcohol shop charges Rs 75 extra for beer bottle, Himachal man wins Rs 12,500 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: consumer court beer case
description: The commission observed that selling any packaged commodity or excisable product above its printed MRP constitutes a flagrant violation of laws.
body_raw: A consumer commission in Himachal Pradesh has directed a liquor shop and its salesman to refund Rs 75 and pay 12,500 to a customer after he was allegedly charged Rs 230 for a beer bottle carrying a maximum retail price MRP of Rs 155. President Hemanshu Mishra and members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur observed that selling any packaged commodity or excisable product above its printed MRP constitutes a flagrant violation of the Legal Metrology Act, Consumer Protection Act, and state excise regulations. Charging above the MRP amounts to an unfair trade practice under Section 247 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, as well as a severe deficiency in service. The refusal to issue a receipt further demonstrates an intent to conceal illegal trade practices, the order read. Illegal trade practices According to the complaint, the complainant visited a liquor shop in Kangra on April 27, 2026, and purchased a bottle of beer. It was stated that the bottle carried an MRP of Rs 155, but the salesman charged him Rs 230, resulting in an overcharge of Rs 75. When the customer objected, the salesman allegedly told him that he was charging the amount on the instructions of the shop owner. The salesman also allegedly refused to issue a purchase receipt. Alleging gross deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, the complainant moved consumer commission seeking a refund and compensation. The liquor shop and its salesman did not appear before the commission after being served with notices and were proceeded against ex-parte. The commission noted that the complainants evidence therefore remained unrebutted and unchallenged. The opposite parties, despite valid service of notice, chose not to contest the complaint and opted to remain ex-parte. Consequently, the evidence adduced by the complainant remains entirely unrebutted, unchallenged, and uncontroverted. There is no legal or factual reason to disbelieve the cogent, trustworthy, and convincing evidence adduced by the complainant, it said. The commission found that the complainant had established that he was charged Rs 230 for a product bearing an MRP of Rs 155. It also noted that refusal to issue a receipt further showed an intent to conceal illegal trade practices. The commission thus allowed the complaint and directed the opposite parties to jointly and severally refund Rs 75 and awarded Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 7,500 litigation costs. Taking note of what it described as the gravity of the illegal overcharging and the alleged defiance of excise norms by a licensed liquor vend, the commission directed that a copy of its order be sent to the Additional Commissioner, Excise and Taxation Department, Dharamshala, for strict departmental and penal action as per rules. Takeaway Sellers cannot charge consumers more than the printed MRP. Overcharging above the MRP can amount to an unfair trade practice and deficiency in service, attracting refund, compensation and litigation costs. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Himachal Pradesh helpline 18001808087 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Ban defied: Karnataka IAS officer seeks police explanation over idol immersion
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Hassan Ganesh idol immersion row
description: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K S Lathakumari issued a notice to SP Shubhanwita for failing to prevent Ganesh idol immersions in Devigere Tank despite prohibitory orders.
body_raw: The deputy commissioner of Hassan district in Karnataka issued a notice to the superintendent of police Sunday, seeking an explanation for why Ganesh and Gowri idols were allowed to be immersed in Devigere Tank, a prominent water body, despite a district administration ban. Acting on requests from the Hassan Municipal Corporation commissioner and the tahsildar, Deputy Commissioner K S Lathakumari, an IAS officer, Saturday banned immersions in the tank, which falls under the Muzrai Department that manages temples in the state, to prevent water contamination from chemical paints, flowers, fruits, and puja materials. The prohibition order was issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS and Section 24 of the Water Prevention and Control of Pollution Act. Despite the ban, major public Ganesh festival organisers held massive processions led by the main town pandal. They immersed the idols in Devigere Tank near the Neerubagilu Anjaneya temple Saturday. DC Lathakumari asked SP Shubhanwita why the matter should not be referred to the competent authority for disciplinary action over alleged dereliction of duty and negligence unbecoming of a government servant. The notice highlighted that although police were empowered to book violators, no FIRs were registered and no action was taken against the organisers. The notice asked SP Shubhanwita to respond in writing immediately, failing which it will be presumed she has no explanation to offer. Copies of the notice were forwarded to the minister-in-charge of the district, the chief secretary, the regional commissioner Mysuru, and the inspector general of police southern range. Addressing the issue on Tuesday, DC Lathakumari said, There is nothing personal in the issue. Since Devigere Tank was polluted, such prohibitory orders were issued after consulting the SP as well. If some untoward incident had taken place, the district administration would have been held responsible. I was also unhappy that plaster of Paris PoP and non-eco-friendly Ganesh idols were also immersed in Devigere. JDS MLA back police officer While SP Shubhanwita was unavailable for comment, a police officer attributed the lapse to the last-minute arrival of the prohibition order. The orders were issued on Saturday morning when the massive procession had already begun. The organisers had obtained permission providing their route map and immersion place. At the last minute, it was impossible to change it, the police officer said. Hassan MLA H P Swaroop Prakash of the Janata Dal Secular backed the SP, pointing out that the pandal committee has immersed its idols in Devigere Tank for six to seven decades. The DC has threatened to initiate legal action against those who have immersed Ganesh idols in Devigere. We will have to stage a protest against the DC. We learned of the order only after the procession had begun. If the district administration is not coordinating with district agencies properly, it will be a problem, Prakash told reporters. The dispute comes weeks before the annual Hasanamba temple fair, scheduled between October 30 and November 10, which is expected to draw at least 20 lakh devotees to the district.

articleTitle: What happened when the lone municipality fire truck went to ‘wash’ a BJP MLA’s house in Gujarat’s Dahod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: dahod MLA
description: The MLA's house is nearly 25 kms from the fire station which has just one fire tender.
body_raw: A BJP MLA allegedly summoning a fire tender from the Devgadh Baria municipality in Dahod district to wash his house has kicked up a controversy, at a time when the states water reserves are under pressure after a deficit monsoon. The MLAs house is nearly 25 kms from the fire station which has just one fire tender. Videos of firemen spraying water on his house in absence of any fire, went viral after which the municipality took a charge from the MLA. BJP leader and President of Devgadh Baria Municipality Dharmesh Kalal confirmed that Khabad had summoned the fire tender for cleaning purpose. He clarified that the cleaning was stopped within 15 seconds as soon as officials informed the fire officer about the deployment. He also added that the municipality recovered Rs 2700 as charges from the MLA after controversy. Sources said, Khabad, a former minister was recuperating in hospital from a major surgery when the truck was summoned allegedly to wash his house in Dhanpur-Pipero area of Devgadhbaria town ahead of Diwali. Most Gujaratis take up deep cleaning of their homes during Diwali, sometimes washing them. However, the timing makes the episode harder to dismiss as Gujarat is dealing with uneven and deficient rainfall, leaving water storage in several reservoirs under pressure. Sources within the BJP say that Khabad, a four-time MLA, who recently underwent a kidney transplant surgery has been advised to observe meticulous hygiene and since he had been away for over two months for treatment, the house was locked and needed cleaning. The incident, however, has made for another awkward moment for the BJP, which has already witnessed a defeat during the recent bypolls of the Municipality following a rebellion against Kalal. eom

articleTitle: 25 years, three times the cost: Versova-Yari Road bridge gets a December 2027 deadline
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Versova-Yari Road bridge
description: The 206-metre bridge over Kavthe creek, conceptualised in 2002 at Rs 16 crore and now pegged at Rs 48 crore, will cut a 30-minute detour between Lokhandwala and Andheri back road to under 10
body_raw: The Versova-Yari road bridge - one of suburban Mumbais much-awaited infrastructure projects is set to see the light of day in December 2027, 25 years after it was conceptualized. The 206-meter-long bridge is set to connect Lokhandwala with Andheri back road, passing over the Kavthe creek at Andheri West. At present, there is no direct connectivity between these two places, and the travel time between these two places takes 30 minutes. Meanwhile, once operational, the travel time is set to drop below 10 mins. Earlier on Monday, a team of Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC officials led by Abhijit Bangar - additional municipal commissioner Projects carried out a site inspection. Following this, the private agency executing the work was told to complete the work by December next year. At present the work of erecting the pillars and columns is underway. The bridge will pass above the creek establishing a direct east-west connection between Yari Road, Panch Marg and Versova in Andheri West, an official told the Indian Express. The bridge will be Y-shaped, while the main structure will feature a 110-metre-long single-span steel basket handle arch structure. Tension rods will connect the steel arch to the bridge deck slab. The cost of this bridge has been pegged at Rs 48 crore. Initially the cost of this project was pegged at round Rs 16 crore. However, with the delay, the project saw a massive cost escalation. In 2019, members from a local housing society filed a petition with the Supreme Court stating that this project would affect mangroves therefore, it needs to be scrapped. They have also stated that the proposed alignment of this bridge was flawed. Later in August 2022, the SC quashed the stay. Following this, the project came back on track. Civic officials said that they had to acquire a slew of permissions from the forest and mangrove departments before they could go ahead with the work. As a result, the issuance of permission took more than three years, and the work could have begun last year.

articleTitle: C Raja Mohan: In Iran war, US midterm elections are the new front
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iran war, us midterms
description: For both Tehran and the White House, managing the home front can matter as much as gaining on the battlefield
body_raw: Irans Revolutionary Guards have found a new audience for their war with Donald Trump The American voter. The history of warfare tells us that weakening the adversarys domestic support can be as important as defeating its armed forces on the battlefield. In a 25-page letter last week, the Guards appealed to the honourable people of the United States to reject Trumps policies and consider peaceful coexistence with Iran. Trump, in turn, hopes that escalating military and economic pressure will force the Islamic Republic to fall in line. Coming just weeks before the midterm elections, the letter brings Tehran directly into Americas domestic political contest. With Republicans vulnerable in November, the political consequences of the Iran war are becoming harder to separate from its military course. In Tehran, too, internal struggles between advocates of negotiation and hardliners favouring confrontation are shaping the wars conduct. That brings us to the idea of the October surprise in American politics - a major event or political move that changes the national mood before the traditional voting in the first week of November. Iran helped make the phrase part of American political language during the 1980 presidential election. The Iranian Revolution of February 1979 overthrew the Shah, a close American ally. In November, militants seized the US embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage. The crisis haunted President Jimmy Carters re-election campaign. His Republican challenger, Ronald Reagan, feared that freeing the hostages before November would rescue Carters political fortunes. Allegations that Reagans team secretly worked to delay the release remain disputed. The hostages came home as Reagan took office in January 1981. Irans upheaval had become entangled with the struggle for power in Washington. Today, Tehran hopes to exploit another American electoral moment. Trump insists the midterms do not determine his Iran policy. But the electoral calendar is now visibly intertwined with the military debate. In an interview last week, Trump said it was possible that US bombing of Iran could intensify after the November 3 elections. He has also said the war could be won right after the election - or perhaps before it. The military preparations reinforce the message. The unfolding deployment gives Trump more options if diplomacy fails - and gives Tehran reason to take his threats seriously. Setting aside the Islamic Revolutions enduring slogan, Death to America, the IRGC letter claims to have no quarrel with ordinary Americans. Its immediate target is Trump. It hopes public anxiety over the war and rising prices will weaken Republicans and create space for a more accommodating policy in Washington. The appeal could easily backfire as Republicans accuse Democrats of serving Tehrans interests. Iran is not alone in trying to exploit domestic divisions. Trump has hoped that military and economic pressure would encourage Iranians to challenge their rulers. That expectation has produced little so far. Tehrans appeal to American voters may prove equally ineffective. Both sides nevertheless see the adversarys home front as a battlefield. Meanwhile, Trump has secured an important gain at Hormuz. The recovery in Gulf oil flows has accelerated. New data show Gulf crude exports averaged about 16.3 million barrels a day in September - roughly 91 per cent of pre-war levels. This does not establish Trumps claim of total control. Iran never enjoyed uncontested sovereignty over the international waterway. Its leverage lay in making passage dangerous and expensive. Tanker attacks, higher insurance costs and uncertainty forced its adversaries to spend heavily on keeping commerce moving. Nor has the energy crisis disappeared. The problem has shifted from crude supply towards logistics and refining. Refined-product exports from the Gulf recovered to only about 60 per cent of pre-war levels in September. That distinction matters politically. More crude moving through Hormuz does not automatically mean cheaper diesel at American pumps. Crude must be transported, refined and distributed. Diesel prices have a direct effect on inflation and cost of living, a major issue in US domestic politics right now. The G7s decision, under Trumps pressure, to release 100 million barrels of crude and fuel products from emergency reserves is meant to ease this pressure. But Trumps dilemma remains. Convincing Tehran that it cannot wait him out requires a credible threat of escalation. Reassuring American voters requires avoiding an escalation that sends fuel prices soaring again. Irans letter seeks to exploit precisely that tension. Tehran faces pressures of its own. Washingtons Operation Economic Outcast is tightening the financial noose. The US has expanded sanctions from military procurement networks to Irans automotive, rail, manufacturing and steel sectors. Washington has now warned foreign financial institutions that doing business with Iran could bring sanctions without prior notice. Neither side can assume the other will crack first. The October surprise could be another military blow, a diplomatic opening, or another fuel-price shock. For India, there is a larger lesson from the US and Iranian efforts to influence each others domestic politics. Americas hopes of political change in Iran and Tehrans appeal to American voters underline an old truth Wars are fought within societies as much as between states. Managing the home front can matter as much as gaining military ground on the battlefield. The principle applies in peacetime too, especially to democracies such as India. Effective engagement with a turbulent world demands cohesion at home. Political differences are inevitable in a democracy. But a politics of winner takes all can turn those differences into debilitating domestic conflicts. That inevitably weakens the nations capacity to deal with mounting challenges abroad and the growing prospects for external meddling in its domestic affairs. The writer is contributing editor on international affairs for The Indian Express. He is professor and director at the Motwani Jadeja Institute of American Studies, Jindal Global University, Delhi

articleTitle: More wait for Sewri-Worli connector as deadline pushed to May 2027
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sewri-worli connector
description: The Sewri Worli is a 4.5km connector between the Coastal Road at Worli and the Atal Setu at Sewri, improving east-west connectivity in the city
body_raw: The wait for the east-west Sewri-Worli connector, linking Coastal Road and Atal Setu, is getting longer as the Maharashtra government has pushed the completion deadline to May 31, 2027, informed Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis during a meeting on various infrastructure projects. An MMRDA senior official confirmed the development, adding that the height of the bridge piers and the double-decker corridor have added to the construction challenges in launching girders, with traffic flowing on the road below. The Sewri Worli is a 4.5km connector between the Coastal Road at Worli and the Atal Setu at Sewri, improving east-west connectivity in the city. Over the railway tracks at Prabhadevi and Parel stations, the bridge doubles to replace the local Elphinstone bridge for traffic going over the railway tracks. Shut since September 2025, the project was supposed to be completed by September 2026. But the deadline was extended because a lot of work on the connector still remains. Currently, officials of MahaRail - which is constructing the portion of the bridge over the railway tracks - are preparing for the launch of girders over the tracks in November. This involves the assembly of the prefabricated girders on site before they can fit into place. Each of the xx girders is 132 meters long. MRIDC dismantled the 112-year-old bridge in April, a month later than scheduled. The authority plans to complete its portions by the year-end, following which the rest of the bridge will rest on the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority MMRDAs work. A senior official from the MMRDA said, Due to the height of the bridge, there are challenges in launching girders particularly towards Parel and Sewri, as the contractor also has to maneuver around busy traffic on the road below. After MRIDCs completion, the MMRDA will have to complete the connecting portions between the railway bridge and other portions. This will extend the work until May 2027, said the senior official.

articleTitle: NYC Council hearing on AI risks: What Jacob Coxon, others told policymakers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NYC Council hearing
description: The hearing comes at a time when the New York City Council is examining legislative proposals to require companies to disclose information about AI tools.
body_raw: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who quit his job last month over concerns that AI could lead to human extinction by the end of the decade, reiterated those warnings in a hearing by the New York City Council on Monday, October 5. The hearing was held to discuss the risks that AI poses to humanity. Officials from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta also appeared before the Council, but Elon Musks SpaceX was a no-show. In their testimonies, AI safety researchers who recently exited Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind, laid out a reckless culture at the firms. They said that the biggest tech companies are racing to create technology they do not understand how to control. Meanwhile, the tech industry representatives called for greater oversight by local governments in response to mounting concerns that advanced AI systems could endanger humanity. The hearing comes at a time when the Council is examining legislative proposals to require companies to disclose information about AI tools, require third-party approval for AI systems in the city, and allow whistleblowers to receive a portion of fines from AI companies that violate laws. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has also moved to impose reporting and transparency standards around AI. Policymakers elsewhere in the US and the rest of the world are also exploring measures to strengthen AI safety. These moves have been driven by the growing fear of AI systems causing catastrophic harm, coupled with a string of hacking incidents involving AI agents behaving unexpectedly. Last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an intentional slowdown of frontier AI efforts across the world to let safety research catch up. The titans of the AI industry, including OpenAIs Sam Altman, SpaceXAIs Elon Musk, and Googles Demis Hassabis, were in rare agreement. But others like Nvidias Jensen Huang and US President Donald Trump dismissed these concerns as trivial and a hoax. What happened at the NYC Council hearing? The companies run on a startup mindset Move fast, break things, fix them later. That works for a photo sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built, Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic former engineer who has become a leading voice for regulation, was quoted as saying by Associated Press at the Council hearing. On the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control to these AIs and it could end in human extinction, Coxon said. A panel of AI company staffers representing tech giants OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, also testified at the hearing. They told officials that their systems are already improving peoples daily lives and emphasised that safety was the top-most priority. Anthropic and OpenAI representatives said their advanced AI products need to be regulated. I share your commitment to ensuring that technology is developed safely and that its benefits are widely shared, said OpenAIs Morgan Dwyer. On whether the risk posed by AI could be quantified, Dwyer replied, I dont know - I also dont think it matters whether its 1 or 10 or 20 chance that something catastrophic will go wrong. None of these levels is remotely acceptable. We should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that we can keep under human control. I would say that the percentage chance doesnt matter. What matters is the commitment to safety, and that is what OpenAI is committed to doing, he added. Anthropics Logan Graham told the Council that the company welcomes smart regulation and that state and local governments have a role to play in developing frameworks. AI is powerful enough that getting this wrong has real consequences, for individuals, institutions, public trust. We have to work relentlessly to do the science of mitigating the risks, he said.

body_raw: The Bengaluru traffic police have restricted vehicle movement on Race Course Road and nearby stretches as white-topping and civic infrastructure work is underway and is expected to run until December. According to the traffic police, the Greater Bengaluru Authority began white-topping work on Race Course Road from Maurya Junction to Hare Krishna Road Junction on October 5. The movement of all vehicles on Race Course Road, from Trilight Junction to Maurya Junction and from Shivananda Junction to Maurya Junction, will be restricted, a traffic police officer said. What are the traffic restrictions All vehicles are prohibited from moving from Shivananda Junction to Maurya Junction. All vehicles are prohibited from moving from Trilight Junction on Race Course Road towards Maurya Junction. articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | How should you read Maharashtra’s drought?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | How should you read Maharashtra's drought UPSC IAS, UPSC CSE, UPSC 2027
description: Maharashtra has declared drought in 265 of its 358 talukas amid an 18% rainfall deficit and prolonged dry spells across large parts of the state. What is drought, and how is it classified in India? Which parts of Maharashtra are most drought prone? Also go beyond the nugget to understand how a drought is declared in India.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on Drought. Knowledge Nugget Drought Subject Geography, Disaster Management Why in the news? On September 26, the Maharashtra government declared a drought in 265 out of the states 358 talukas, across its 36 districts, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis terming the crisis the worst the state has endured since 1972. Key takeaways 1. With no rainfall in over 20 days during the crucial kharif crop season and the Southwest monsoon receding, the crisis is expected to worsen in the summer months next year. 2. The Maharashtra government has directed all municipal corporations, municipalities, and gram panchayats to impose a minimum 10 percent water cut from October 16, citing water storage, drought-like conditions, and the possibility of El Nino-related water stress extending into next year. 3. From June 1 to September 26, Maharashtra has received 798.2 mm of rainfall against a normal 970.9 mm, a deficit of 18. 4. According to the India Meteorological Department IMD, 31 of 36 districts in Maharashtra are rain-deficient, with 20 of these facing a deficit of 25 to 58 per cent. 5. Beyond the deficit, shifting rain patterns have added to the damage in more than 100 of the states 355 drought-hit talukas, gaps between rain spells have stretched to 4060 days. 6. As a result, the main kharif crop, sown across 147 lakh hectares, has withered. Maharashtras agriculture is largely rain-fed its irrigation potential, at under 20 per cent, is much lower than in states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. What is drought? -Drought is a rainfall scarce period, affecting the availability of water for irrigation, drinking etc. -Ministry of Agriculture is the nodal Ministry in respect of monitoring and managing drought conditions. It classifies droughts into meteorological droughts, hydrological droughts and agricultural droughts. -Meteorological drought is classified based on rainfall deficiency w.r.t. long term average-25 or less is normal, 26-50 is moderate and more than 50 is severe. It is usually the starting point of drought conditions, indicated by prolonged dry spells. -Hydrological drought is best defined as deficiencies in surface and sub-surface water supplies leading to a lack of water for normal and specific needs. -Such conditions arise even in times of average or above average precipitation when increased usage of water diminishes the reserves. It can develop after prolonged rainfall deficiency or excessive withdrawals. -Agricultural drought is identified by 4 consecutive weeks of meteorological drought. Scarcity of water and inadequate soil moisture for normal crop growth starts affecting agricultural production. Which regions in Maharashtra are prone to drought and why? 7. Marathwada and Vidarbha, the two rain-shadow regions of the state which traditionally are drought-prone, have received very little rainfall. 8. Marathwada is particularly affected, having received 38 less rainfall than normal, while Vidarbha has a 27 deficiency. 9. The big deficit is in seven districts - Solapur, Dharashiv, Latur, Hingoli, Jalna, Beed and parts of Nanded, which are away from Godavari river - where rainfall has been just around 50 of normal. Except Solapur, all these districts fall in Marathwada region. 10. Vidarbha region is a little less affected, while western Maharashtra, which is the sugarcane and onion producing zone, is in a relatively comfortable position. Nashik district, known for onion production, has received 37 excess rainfall till now. 11. In Vidarbha, the average deficit across 11 districts is 27, with the shortfall ranging from 26 in Yavatmal to 42 in Amravati. Did you know? - A drought year is especially hard on the women. While most of them work on fields along with the men of the household, their days start much before daybreak, usually around 4 am - a relentless cycle of cooking, cleaning, tending to the children and livestock, besides spending backbreaking hours on the land they till but dont own. What are the relief measures undertaken by the Maharashtra government? 12. The declaration, under the Drought Management Code, 2016, will trigger crop-loss surveys and a package of immediate concessions, including waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans, a stay on recovery of agriculture-related loans and relaxation of Viksit BharatGuarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin VBG RAM G norms. 13. The government has also provided for concessions on electricity bills for agricultural pumps, with bills for pumps up to 7.5 HP already waived and concessions to apply to pumps above that capacity. 14. Financial assistance for crop losses will be decided separately after the assessment is completed, government officials said. 15. For farmers and rural households, the immediate relief measures announced with the drought declaration include a waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans and a stay on recovery of agriculture-related loans. 16. Other measures include a waiver of examination fees for school and college students, deployment of tankers for drinking water wherever required, no disconnection of electricity supply to agricultural pumps in villages declared to be facing shortages, and arrangements for foodgrains and fodder. 17. The government has also directed authorities to plan drinking water and livestock water supply and undertake water conservation works in affected areas. The measures are intended to provide immediate relief while the crop-loss assessment is carried out. 18. The extent of compensation to individual farmers will depend on the findings of the surveys and the separate government order to be issued on crop damage assistance. BEYOND THE NUGGET How is a drought declared? 1. Under the National Disaster Response Fund NDRF rules, drought declaration for kharif the monsoon cropping season, which runs from June to October requires an assessment that can begin from October 5, once the monsoon starts to withdraw. 2. For rabi, the winter cropping season from October to April, assessment can be held in March 2027. 3. There is no single definition of drought accepted across India. States have the authority to declare a drought based on local conditions. 4. But the state governments report should conform to parameters specified under NDRF norms, and disaster relief funds can be unlocked by the Centre. 5. Under NDRF rules, drought declaration is based on crop loss, the moisture adequacy index used to assess soil health, and rainfall deficit, along with decline in food production and labour migration in search of work. 6. Sowing must fall below 50 per cent of total cultivable kharifrabi area, drinking water shortage must be severe, groundwater tables must be shrinking, there must be fodder shortage, and rainfall deficit must be up to 70 per cent. Post Read Question With reference to drought in India, consider the following statements 1. The State Government is the final authority for declaring an area drought-affected. 2. Rainfall deficiency is the sole criterion for declaring drought. 3. Crop conditions, soil moisture and socio-economic indicators can also be considered in drought assessment. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 and 3 only b 1 only c 2 and 3 only d 1, 2 and 3 Answer a Sources Maharashtra is parched, but heres why drought cant be declared before October, Maharashtra declares drought in 75 of state amid rainfall deficit,Three kinds of drought, Behind Maharashtra drought crisis, sharp regional variation in rainfall Click here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026.
