articleTitle: Archana Puran Singh supported son’s love with a 6-year-older girlfriend: ‘The perfect couple’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: archana puran singh son love story
description: Archana Puran Singh described her younger son Ayushmaan and his girlfriend Samiksha as the 'perfect couple'. Archana also encouraged her son to be serious about Samiksha as she found her to be a 'really nice girl'.
body_raw: Archana Puran Singh and her family have been sharing chapters from their personal lives on YouTube for nearly two years now. Archana, whose channel has nearly 1.3 million subscribers, is all about family vlogs, food challenges, and home tours. Her older son, Aaryamann Sethis channel, Aary Vlogs, has nearly 370K subscribers and often puts up daily vlogs. Recently, her younger son, Ayushmaan Sethi, also started his channel, which already has around 50K subscribers, and in his latest video, he opened up about his love story with his girlfriend, yoga instructor Samiksha Shetty, who moved into their family home a few months ago. In the video, Ayushmaan, who is six years younger than Samiksha, shared that they met through actor Yogita Bihani, who is Aaryamanns fiance. Archana, while sharing her thoughts about their nearly one-and-a-half-year-long relationship, said, I think you guys are the perfect couple. You dont fight much. You are calm, she is calm. You both have such positive vibes. Everyone thinks that they are just made for each other. Archana shared that when she felt that their relationship was getting to the next level, she gave him some motherly advice. I told you, Ayush, you are getting serious about her. Finding a nice girl is all about destiny, and if you have found a nice girl, then dont think about timing, or I am not ready, because she is a really nice girl. You have found such a good girl, so you should just recognise that goodness and then hold it forever, she said. Parmeet Sethi also praised their relationship and said, You complete each other. Its a solid, beautiful, positive relationship. ALSO READ Not my personal views Sanjay Dutts new clarification for dont feel peace in India remark In the video, as Ayushmaan and Samiksha spoke about their relationship, she shared that she thought of him as a kid when she met him initially. At that time, she was in her Devdas era and both of them had just gotten out of bad relationships. She eventually found him to be sweet, mature as they started getting fond of each other. When Samiksha went through a medical crisis, Ayushmaan was by her side, and they eventually took their first international holiday to France and Portugal. She later joined the Sethi family on a trip to London. Until this time, Samiksha was living with a flatmate in Mumbai, but when the flatmate moved out, she started looking for new accommodation, as the couple started talking about their plans of living together in the near future. Ayushmann then brought up the idea of her moving into his family home, with his parents, his brother and his fiance, and his grandparents, and Samiksha immediately agreed. The couple recently started sharing their life on YouTube via Aary Vlogs and Archana Puran Singhs channel, and with Ayushmaans new channel, they plan to share more about their life with the viewers.

articleTitle: Rahul’s impromptu move, Priyanka’s negotiation skills: The INDIA march twist
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi climbs atop the barricades during the INDIA bloc MPs' march from Parliament to the ECI, demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)
description: Congress leaders have credited the Gandhis with derailing the police plan to end the protest.
body_raw: The INDIA bloc protest against the Election Commission took a surprise turn on Tuesday, thanks to Rahul Gandhi and his sister and Wayanad MP, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.Opposition MPs were detained and pushed into buses to different police stations in Delhi. The protest was all but over when the siblings pulled off an impromptu move that even left Congress leaders confused. India News Live UpdatesRahul Gandhi, Priyankas sit-in at Doordarshan office in face-off with cops Priyanka was already seated in one of the buses, parked outside the Akashvani Bhavan, the headquarters of All India Radio, and Rahul was about to get in. Suddenly, the siblings looked at each other, and then walked past the cops and into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. The move was off the script and the police personnel initially did not know how to react. Once the Gandhis went inside, Congress leaders KC Venugopal and Pawan Khera climbed the boundary wall of Akashvani Bhavan and started raising slogans. Congress leaders Imran Pratapgarhi and Srinivas BV joined them. Most Congress leaders said they had thought the protest was over. We dont know what happened. This was not part of the plan, one of them said. According to sources in the Congress, Rahul Gandhi planned to enter the Akashvani Bhavan premises and then exit through the back gate, located opposite the Election Commission. All the other routes to the poll panels office were blocked for the rally, so the Leader of the Opposition made this plan on the go, the sources said. Once he entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises, police officers shut the back gate. So he sat here in protest, said a source. Only the two of them know what they had in mind when they walked in, said a Congress MP outside Akashvani Bhawan. At this point, the Congress leaders are still camping on the premises as top security officers talk to them. Personnel from Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force are now stationed outside the Akashvani Bhavan. A police officer said the force inside the premises was to ensure the leaders safety. Congress leaders have credited the Gandhis with derailing the police plan to end the protest. The protest would have been over if they didnt do this. Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera said in a post on X, In the morning, the India Alliance attempted to walk towards the election commission. The police forcibly stopped the MPs. Currently, Leader of Opposition Shri Rahul Gandhi and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra along with several leaders, are sitting on a dharna inside the All India Radio premises which is next to ECI office. The Congress leaders are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of disenfranchising voters through the Special Intensive Revision exercise to give advantage to the ruling BJP. According to highly placed sources in the Congress, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is leading negotiations with the top police officers. Following The Indian Express investigation on the rift within the poll panel, underlining how two Election Commissioners objected on record at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken without their knowledge, the Election Commission acknowledged these notes, but described them as part of the panels decision-making process. However, it did not respond to any of the concerns raised by the two Commissioners, nor did it state whether or how these concerns had been addressed. Opposition leaders detained Earlier, top Opposition leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, were detained as police stopped the march to the Election Commission office. The protesting MPs were taken away in buses. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said the opposition would continue its protest to protect voting rights and democracy. This protest will continue. We are doing this to protect your vote and your freedom. The people of the country are saying that many of their votes have been deleted and vote theft is taking place, and we are fighting and will continue to fight for their protection, he said. BJP takes a swipe Criticising the Opposition march to the Election Commission to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation, the BJP said this was yet another attempt by the Congress and its allies to create anarchy and relaunch Rahul Gandhi. Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the Opposition leaders are venting their frustration over electoral defeats by levelling baseless allegations. Friends in the opposition, the very system you are questioning is the one under which you won in Kerala. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Karnataka. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Himachal. Was that victory illegitimate? Opposition governments were formed in Punjab and Jharkhand were those victories illegitimate? the senior BJP leader asked. If you question constitutional institutions, you will commit the sin of plunging the country into the fires of anarchy. Do not commit the sin of plunging the nation into unrest and anarchy. The country and its people will never forgive you, he added. Addressing the media at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said, The Congress has been repeatedly trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary. When, despite numerous attempts, he failed to gain traction, the Congress and some of its allies decided that even if it meant resorting to anarchy and undermining the nations democracy, they would launch Rahul Gandhi politically at any cost. As part of these efforts, they attacked the Indian army from time to time, the Supreme Court, Hindus, and EVMs Electronic Voting Machines. And for the last few weeks, they have been attacking the Election Commission, Patra said.

articleTitle: RBI repo rate news HIGHLIGHTS: RBI raises GDP growth forecast to 7.1 per cent for FY27
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, RBI MPC meeting
description: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has announced that the MPC had voted to increase the repo rate to 5.5%, a hike of 25 basis points amid West Asia tensions and inflation concerns.
body_raw: RBI Repo Rate News The Reserve Bank of Indias Monetary Policy Committee MPC kicked off its three-day bi-monthly review meeting in Mumbai on October 5. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has announced that the RBI will hike the interest rate by 25 basis points and change stance to tightening amid rising global energy supply concerns and inflation. This is likely to translate into hiked EMIs for retail consumers. Financial markets were bracing for the hike in interest rates amid mounting global and domestic headwinds. A hike in the short-term lending rate repo by the RBI in its upcoming monetary policy would mark a stance reversal, following four rate cuts totalling 125 basis points in 2025 and a prolonged pause thereafter, the agency reported. The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 25 basis points to 6.50 per cent. Markets fall ahead of MPC decision, rise later Equity benchmarks began Wednesdays trading session on a weak note as investors remained cautious in anticipation of a rate hike. Sentiments remained cautious as investors sought clarity on the central banks review on economic growth and inflation. The BSE Sensex slipped 102.43 points, or 0.14 percent, to open at 72,965.38, while the Nifty 50 shed 85.65 points, or 0.38 percent, to start at 22,690.45. Selling pressure intensified shortly after the bell across both benchmark indices. However, soon after the repo rate announcement, markets marginally picked up. Global instability, rising CPI big concerns The central banks MPC review comes at a time when the economic policy faces fresh pressures from geopolitical instability and rising prices. Key drivers influencing the committees stance include geopolitical tensions, rising Consumer Price Index CPI, and increasing domestic food price pressure, among other factors. The prolongedconflict in West Asia and higher crude oil costs are stoking broader macroeconomic concerns with microeconomic consequences they are pinching the common mans pocket every day. Moreover, concerns over persistent food inflation have kept retail price growth volatile.

articleTitle: IIT Ropar launches app to help children learn about plants, crops and agriculture
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The app is designed to introduce agricultural knowledge before children formally study agriculture as a subject
description: The platform is described as free, ad-free and privacy-focused, with a child-focused design aimed at keeping the digital learning environment safe and age-appropriate.
body_raw: IIT Ropars Centre of Excellence in AI for Digital Agriculture, ANNAM.AI, has launched AVNI-Grow with Nature digital learning platform designed to help children learn about plants, crops, food and agriculture through their surroundings. The web and mobile app uses artificial intelligence AI along with hands-on activities to help children identify and understand what they see around them. The platform allows children to explore crops, fruits, vegetables, spices, cereals and millets. For example, a child can use the app while looking at a plant, fruit or crop and learn more about it through AI-powered identification. The idea is to connect what children see in everyday life with basic knowledge about agriculture and food. AVNI developed by the team at IIT Ropar, is available in Hindi and English and also provides audio content for younger children. It includes daily challenges, a digital Nature Book, a Nature Gallery and a Crop Compare feature. These tools allow children to record what they learn, explore different plants and compare crops as part of their learning. The app is designed to introduce agricultural knowledge before children formally study agriculture as a subject, IIT-R said in a statement. A plant in a school garden, a fruit at home or a crop in a nearby field can become a starting point for learning about how food is grown and where it comes from. Also Read IIT Ropar announces scholarship for underprivileged students, lays foundation stone of yogic sciences centre The platform also places emphasis on learning through observation rather than only reading information. Children can explore their surroundings, identify plants and crops and gradually build a basic understanding of agriculture and nature. AVNI has been developed by Dr Mukesh Saini, Co-project Director of ANNAM.AI, IIT Ropar. The initiative is part of ANNAM.AIs work on the use of AI in agriculture and education. The platform, as per the institute is free to access, ad-free and privacy-focused, with a child-focused design aimed at keeping the digital learning environment safe and age-appropriate. ANNAM.AI is working on AI-based digital public infrastructure for Indian agriculture. AVNI extends this work into education by using AI not just to provide information but to help children learn about agriculture through direct observation and exploration. The initiative is aimed at building agricultural awareness among children at an early age, including an understanding of the plants they see, the food they eat and the role agriculture plays in producing it.

articleTitle: The aloo posto burger is not as innocent as it looks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: now the potato patty sits inside a bun where the rice ought to be. There may be lettuce, perhaps cheese, some sauce or mayonnaise or commercial mustard paste, a toasted surface where there was once steam rising from rice.
description: Fast food will keep borrowing from home kitchens, and home kitchens will keep changing without much ado. For now, the burger can have its moment under the festive lights, and the aloo posto is not going to be displaced from its place with the rice, mustard oil and chillies
body_raw: A cafe chain has put an aloo posto burger on its Durga Puja menu. And a section of Bengalis is incensed - perhaps understandably. The potato mashed, its edges crisped and browned, will presumably be folded into the nutty texture of poppy seed paste, pressed into a patty and tucked into a toasted bun. The umbrage, very likely, is not about the burger itself, but about seeing something intimate, pocket-friendly and comforting being recast in the language of fast food. When a dish has lived in ones home for generations, giving it a new form does risk making innovation feel like intrusion. One of the oft-repeated accounts of eastern Indias culinary history is about how posto became a part of the everyday meal. It is the story of a food born, in part, of the human instinct to make do with what is available. Cultivated in enormous quantities to supply the East India Companys extractive colonial trade, the opium poppy left its tiny white seeds behind for use in local kitchens. Soaked and ground on the shil-nora, the grainy texture of the seeds gives way to a thick, pale paste, almost creamy. The residue of an imperial cash crop was absorbed into the frugal economy of homes. It found a companion in the aloo, a traveller so completely naturalised that its foreignness now seems an affront to the spud. The potato becomes tender and absorbs the posto paste, while mustard oil gives everything a sharp nasal fragrance that softens as it meets the heat of the pan. But now the potato patty sits inside a bun where the rice ought to be. There may be lettuce, perhaps cheese, some sauce or mayonnaise or commercial mustard paste, a toasted surface where there was once steam rising from rice. The ensemble appears to belong to another vocabulary Fast, portable, assembled, engineered for eating with one hand - not licking the fingers. A caveat, however Culinary cultures can become a small place when authenticity becomes a regular test. Posto itself has never been particularly monogamous. There is jhinge posto, with ridge gourd turning soft and almost silky beneath the poppy paste dhyarosh posto, with okra imparting a slippery texture posto with broad beans and other vegetables. There are posto boras, little fritters in which the poppy seed paste crisps around the edges and stays soft within. There are preparations in which posto thickens, coats and binds. Khosha bhaja - salted strips of potato skin embedded with posto and fried until they crackle between the teeth - belongs to a culinary instinct that sees possibility in what might otherwise be thrown away. It is difficult to build a very convincing case for culinary purity in a cuisine that has spent generations finding new things to do with the same small bowl of poppy paste. Is it fair, then, to call the aloo posto in a bun a great culinary transgression? The irritation could have less to do with the burger than with what it seems to say about the food. The faint bitterness of posto rubbing against the starch of the potato, the sharp green chilli, the mustard oil opening up in the heat, the first morsel mixed into rice until everything becomes soft, pale and fragrant - they are memories of meals shared with loved ones. Comfort food has a strange relationship with innovation. We like innovation when it happens to somebody elses food - a paneer makhani or butter chicken pizza, is acceptable to us Indians, Italians balk at the pineapple pizza. We become more cautious when it reaches the foods we recognise by smell before we recognise them by sight. Perhaps that is the paradox that makes the aloo posto burger less innocent than it looks. Home food has never been a museum of fixed objects it has always been about the twists taken by every cook - described with great felicity in the Hindi phrase, haat ka khana - the liberties taken by every generation. But a restaurant changes the transaction. What is unsettling is that the posto whose flavours unfurled bite by bite on the palette is now being announced as an innovation on a festive menu. Dishes are known to wander, and yet they are never quite the prodigal child. Fast food will keep borrowing from home kitchens, and home kitchens will keep changing without much ado. For now, the burger can have its moment under the festive lights and the aloo posto is not going to be displaced from its place with the rice, mustard oil and chillies. I confess I am not averse to tasting the burger. But when the posto meets the aloo, I know I will still reach for the rice. In the years to come, though, the question may well be Will the aloo posto burger be an homage to the East Indian home? Or will it become a marker of that grandiloquent and frequent, but rarely convincing, claim that innovation arrived only yesterday at the chefs kitchen? The writer is senior associate editor, The Indian Express. kaushik.dasguptaexpressindia.com

articleTitle: Swatantra Bhardwaj gets regular bail in Jantar Mantar assault case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: self-styled influencer Swatantra Bharadwaj
description: A Delhi court had earlier granted the self-styled influencer interim bail for three weeks
body_raw: A Delhi court Tuesday granted self-styled influencer Swatantra Bharadwaj regular bail in a case where he allegedly attacked the father of a student protester who had participated in the Cockroach Janta Party CJP protest in July. Additional Sessions Judge ASJ Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler of the Patiala House Court had earlier granted Bharadwaj interim bail for three weeks. ASJ Laler had then said that it would observe his conduct before considering his plea for regular bail. A detailed regular bail order is awaited. In its order granting Bharadwaj interim bail, ASJ Laler had said, Weighing all circumstances, the Court takes into account that the applicant has been in custody for a little over 10 days. a period that should have afforded him time for reflection. The case Bharadwaj had purportedly admitted to attacking the father of the student protester at Jantar Mantar in a video. He was picked up by the Crime Branch officers from his house in Bulandshahr on September 4 and brought to Delhi after securing a transit remand. On September 4, relevant sections pertaining to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 SCST Act, were added to an earlier FIR registered against Bharadwaj over the alleged attack, amid a protest by CJP supporters and the Indian Youth Congress, as well as Lok Sabha MPs Chandra Shekhar alias Azad and Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav. The same day, another FIR was also registered under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences POCSO Act, 2012, and for criminal intimidation based on the protesters complaint alleging she had received rape threats from Bhardwajs supporters. Bharadwaj had been in judicial custody since September 5 till he was granted interim bail on September 15. While granting interim bail to the accused, the court had also pulled up the police for leaving significant ground uncovered in the investigation. The investigation, as disclosed in the reply, leaves significant ground uncovered. The podcast forms the central basis of the States opposition, and its authenticity is disputed. Yet the reply does not state whether the person who manages the channel has been examined, whether the original footage has been requisitioned, or whether the electronic material has been sent for forensic examination, ASJ Laler had said in the interim bail order.

articleTitle: Retired Delhi High Court judge, family lost Rs 3.2 crore in real estate scam
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ML Varma
description: After years of delays, bounced cheques and assurances, retired Delhi High Court judge M L Varma has now approached the police. An FIR has been filed on his complaint
body_raw: Sixteen years ago, Justice M L Varma was going through his morning ritual of reading the newspaper when his eyes fell on an advertisement in a corner. The advertisement carried striking pictures of an upcoming project in Noida Sector 15, said the 84-year-old, who retired in 1991 from the Delhi High Court. It promised a high rental commercial unit. The pictures were so attractive and appealing, it looked like it was absolutely out of the world. They showed a metro station nearby, a very good sector, he added. Interested, he quickly dialled the contact number mentioned in the advertisement. He also nudged a relative to book another unit in the same project. The papers were signed at his office in Delhis Neeti Bagh, and he and his brother-in-law, Naveen Sawhney, paid Rs 3 crore. It is now 2026 and not a single brick has been laid, he said. We have been cheated out of the money. Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen years, and not a brick has been laid there, Justice Varma said. Last month, he filed a complaint at the Hauz Khas police station in Delhi against Aims Sanya Developers Private Limited, and its directors Roop Kishore Madan, Sanjay Thukral and other unknown persons. Police lodged the FIR on September 18 against unknown persons under sections of criminal conspiracy and criminal intent. A senior police officer said the investigation is underway and no arrests have been made till now. There was no response to emails sent to the builder seeking comment. The phone number registered for this project on the RERA website was not reachable. Five years of assurances and delays Varma initially had no plans to take the legal route, hoping instead that the builders would honour their commitments. It seemed like a good investment to make, to be able to earn some money later., said Varma. who enrolled as a lawyer in 1964 and is quasi-retired - he still practises and does arbitrations. The location was good and they had shown such a good picture, the brochure had made it very attractive. It would also have fetched rent, so that would have been a source of income. According to the complaint, the commercial project was to be completed within 36 months, with a grace period of six months, and was to yield high returns on investment for the investors and purchasers. As per the assurances and public advertisements, the construction of the commercial project was to commence in September 2010 and conclude by March 2014, the complaint stated, alleging that the complainants have been cheated of over Rs 3,22,34,640. After the deadline passed, Varma said he made multiple trips to the builders office in Defence Colony. He would be made to wait for hours, he said, while the builder did not show up. A few years ago, they eventually entered into a Memorandum of Understanding MoU. If there was a delay, he was supposed to give assured returns based on what the property would have fetched if it had been rented. He did not. Eventually, some years ago, we entered into an MoU. He gave advance cheques, but the cheques would bounce. That went on for five years, Varma claimed, adding that the accused paid the monthly assured returns intermittently. Eventually, when the builder stopped picking up calls in October 2025, the family decided to approach the police. He the builder induced and tricked us into buying a property which he had no intention, from day zero, of building, claimed Varmas son Satvik, a senior advocate in the Delhi High Court. Property not even demarcated Satvik said he could have understood the delay if construction had at least begun. If he had dug up the land, there could have been reasons such as a National Green Tribunal order or a ban on construction. But. the property is not even demarcated. We dont even know if it has a name now. Earlier, it was called Landmark Towers, then they changed it to Tempean Towers, he said. Varma and his wife, Nita, had persuaded Naveen to invest in the project. Naveen died two years ago after suffering from cancer for a year and a half. We could have used those resources. My father always felt that because of his mistake, my uncle lost his money as well. There was guilt and a moral dilemma, said Satvik. Varma still has the brochure of the property, which runs into multiple pages and contains elaborate maps. He asked in disbelief What could be more dishonest than this? If it can happen to someone who has been a part of the legal system for over 50 years, then what is likely to be the plight of the common man about whose misery one reads every day, who is deprived of their life savings?

articleTitle: Allies turned foes? Bombay HC steps into BJP vs Shiv Sena in Ulhasnagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay HC ulhasnagar BJP vs Shiv Sena
description: The Mayor, a Sena Corporator, allegedly altered the UMC Commissioner's recommendations, excluding the names of S B Singh and Pradeep Ramchandani – the other BJP nominees.
body_raw: In a setback for the ruling Shiv Sena in the Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation UMC in Thane district, the Bombay High Court on Monday halted further steps on Mayor Ashwini Kamlesh Nikams decision to recommend only two of four BJP candidates as co-opted or nominated corporators. The Mayor, a Sena Corporator, allegedly altered the UMC Commissioners recommendations, excluding the names of S B Singh and Pradeep Ramchandani-the other BJP nominees. Ramchandani, along with BJP district president Rajesh Vadhrya, had approached the court with pleas challenging the proposed nomination of councillors in the Special General Body Meeting SGBM of the UMC held on October 1, which recommended the names of only two of four BJP candidates while recommending five candidates of the Ulhasnagar Shahar Vikas Aghadi USVA - alliance dominated by the Shiv Sena. Prima facie, there appears to be substance in the contentions of the counsel for the Petitioners on whether the Mayor at all had any authorityjurisdiction under the Maharashtra Municipal Corporations Qualifications and Appointment of Nominated Councillors Rules, 2012, to reject the nominations as made, and place the names of only two candidates out of four as recommended by the Commissioner, a bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale noted. In the meantime, till the adjourned date of hearing, the Municipal Secretary is restrained from taking any steps to notify andor undertake any publication of the nominated councillors as per the provisions of Rule 6 of the 2012 Rules, the HC noted. Senior advocates Birendra Saraf and Anil Y Sakhare, appearing for the petitioners, argued that while the Municipal Commissioner, under Rule 5 1 of the 2012 Rules, had recommended three USVA candidates, the Mayor placed the names of five USVA candidates before the house and thereafter, hurriedly closed the meeting with the national anthem. The long-standing BJP-Shiv Sena dispute over UMC-nominated corporators had earlier reached the High Court and Supreme Court, which ordered the convening of SGBM for the issue by October 1, after which the Mayor took a decision in question in the present pleas. It should be noted that BJP and Shiv Sena are allies in the state, but not the civic body. On October 5, the petitioners sought urgent ad-interim relief and argued that as per 2012 rules, the Mayor had no power to reject the Commissioners recommended candidates. Finding prima facie substance in petitioners contentions, the bench issued notices to the respondents, directing them to file reply affidavits by October 12.

articleTitle: Gift coupon fraud: Police bust suspected Dubai-linked fake BPO in Bengaluru
articleFeaturedImageAlt: gift coupon fraud
description: The Bengaluru police initially suspected that employees were being trained to commit fraud and that SIM cards registered in other persons’ names were being used to contact and threaten potential victims.
body_raw: The Bengaluru police have detained and questioned six people after a suspected gift coupon fraud operation targeting overseas victims was uncovered on Hennur Main Road, officials said on Tuesday. The police have not identified any victims in India so far. Investigators suspect that the operation was linked to a network being run from Dubai, though the alleged Dubai connection is yet to be established. The Central Crime Branch CCB registered a case on September 26 following a tip-off that an alleged fraudulent operation was being run from a building. The police initially suspected that employees were being trained to commit fraud and that SIM cards registered in other persons names were being used to contact and threaten potential victims. Around 60 to 70 young men and women were working from the premises, which initially led investigators to suspect that it was being used as a call centre to facilitate online fraud. However, the subsequent investigation indicated that the suspected operation was linked to a gift coupon fraud targeting people outside India, the police said. Not everyone was involved. As per our interrogation, only a few people appear to have known about the activity. We have served notices to everyone and are questioning them to ascertain their roles, a senior CCB officer said. The police have also served notices on more than 60 employees who were working at the premises. Investigators have seized laptops and mobile phones and are examining the devices to determine how the suspected operation functioned and which employees were aware of the alleged fraud. The CCB is yet to establish a financial trail linking the premises to the suspected fraud, as they have not found transaction IDs or other financial details so far. The police said the investigation is continuing to establish the complete modus operandi, the roles played by the employees, and the alleged link to the Dubai-based operation.

articleTitle: Colonial legacy of India’s policing system must end: Andhra Pradesh High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Andhra Pradesh High Court police policing colonial
description: Hearing six pleas alleging police interference in land or property disputes, the Andhra Pradesh High Court barred the police from adjudicating civil rights.
body_raw: The Andhra Pradesh High Court has invoked the colonial legacy of Indias policing system while calling for a shift towards people-centric and democratic policing. Referring to legal scholar Upendra Baxis observation that the colonial police survived decolonization it simply changed masters, the court said the police structure, methods and legal framework largely continued to reflect the colonial model even after Independence. Justice Maheswara Rao Kuncheam was hearing a batch of six petitions alleging police interference in civil disputes involving land, houses and other properties. The petitioners alleged that police personnel had called them to police stations, pressured them to settle disputes and interfered in matters pending before competent courts or legal forums. The common order in the six petitions was passed on October 5,restraining the police from interfering in civil disputes. Police are entrusted with the responsibility of protecting life, liberty, rights and public order, but they are not an authority above the people. Police powers are conferred by law and must be exercised fairly, reasonably and proportionately. Thus, the police must act as guardians of the constitutional principles, rather than as rulers exercising unchecked authority over citizens., the court said. The police structure, methods and legal framework largely continued to reflect the colonial model, mainly based on the Police Act, 1861, which was primarily designed to maintain order, control the population and protect the interests of the ruling authority, rather than to function as a citizen-oriented service, it added. The court said that though the British rulers were replaced by an elected Indian government, the basic institutional character of the police remained substantially unchanged. Hence, all the stakeholders contribute their respective support to change the overall existing police structures from the colonial phase to people-centric policing in the larger interest of modern Indian and turns into Democratic policing, which means a system of policing in which the police exercise their powers within the limits of law, remain accountable to constitutional and democratic institutions, and respond to the legitimate needs and rights of the people, it added. 6 pleas raised common concern The six petitions involved different disputes but raised the common issue of police allegedly interfering in civil matters already pending before competent forums. In one petition, the petitioner alleged police interference in a dispute concerning his house and pressure to vacate it. Another alleged that police had locked her house and prevented her from entering. Other petitions involved allegations that police repeatedly called parties to stations to settle disputes concerning land or property. One petitioner alleged that police threatened her to withdraw a civil suit, while another alleged that he was detained for hours and pressured to compromise in a property dispute. These were allegations made in the petitions. The State disputed them and told the court that police had not called the petitioners to the respective stations and would not interfere in civil disputes unless a cognizable offence was registered. The high court also highlighted the limited police strength in Andhra Pradesh. It noted that the state has approximately 166.18 police personnel per one lakh population, against the United Nations recommendation of 222 personnel per lakh. The court said that, given these limitations, deploying police resources in areas where they have no jurisdiction could become a futile exercise. It referred to the possibility of unjust enrichment of some police personnel through such intervention and described such conduct as illegal and unconstitutional. Police cant decide civil rights The court made it clear that the police retain their legal duty to maintain law and order, prevent crime, protect life and property, and take lawful preventive measures where there is a threat to public peace. However, those powers do not extend to deciding civil rights between private parties. The court said that once a competent judicial or quasi-judicial forum has seized a dispute, an executive authority without adjudicatory powers cannot assume the role of that forum and determine the rights of the parties. Such action would amount to acting without jurisdiction. The duty to resolve civil disputes is entrusted to the judiciary. No such power is empowered to the Police, the court said, adding that interference in pending or potential civil disputes is not within their province. DGPs guidelines draw the line The court took note of instructions issued by the Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police on October 24, 2025 concerning land disputes. The guidelines say police should not take sides or interfere in civil ownership or title disputes, while providing for preventive action where a dispute threatens public peace. The guidelines also provide for criminal cases where criminal intent or violence is evident, including trespass, cheating, forgery, assault or criminal conspiracy. The high court ultimately held that police have no jurisdiction to adjudicate upon or determine civil rights between parties. It directed the police not to interfere, adjudicate, determine or settle such rights without legal cause and ordered strict compliance with the DGPs guidelines. The parties were left free to pursue remedies before appropriate civil courts or competent forums. The court clarified that if a cognisable offence is made out, police remain free to proceed according to law. There was no order as to costs, and pending interlocutory applications were closed.

articleTitle: Movers and packers ‘unload’ goods on highway, man wins Rs 73,000 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: packers and movers AC highway man puducherry consumer court
description: The man claimed that his 7-year-old AC went missing after the movers and packers company delivered the rest of the household articles on a highway in 2025.
body_raw: A Puducherry consumer commission has directed a movers and packers company to pay nearly Rs 73,000 to a man after it allegedly unloaded his household goods on a highway, failed to deliver his air conditioner and demanded extra money for its release. President S Mouttouvel, along with members A S Suvitha and G Arumugam, was hearing the complaint filed by a man who, following his employment transfer, was shifting his residence from Gujarat to Puducherry when the AC went missing after the rest of his household articles were delivered. Between the place of move from and place of move to as shown in Exhibit C1 Bill, the opposite party company staff had done some foul play, and thereby they have not delivered the air conditioner. It is the duty of the packers and movers to deliver all the items that were packed, the August 31 order read. AC missing, extra money demanded The man claimed that he was residing in Puducherry and required the relocation of his household essentials, including an air conditioner, from Gujarat to Puducherry due to his employment. He added that the company contacted him and offered an all-inclusive quote of Rs 25,000 for the consignment, presenting itself as a cost-effective option. The man claimed that he was impressed by the company, which had represented that it had provided services to the Air Force, Military, BSF, ITBP, Navy, all major banks, ONGC and Indian Oil, and portrayed itself as a reliable service provider. He submitted that the company, through a series of payments, collected Rs 43,000 from him, despite the agreed amount of Rs 25,000, and, during the delivery process in June 2025, refused to deliver the consignment at the specified address in Puducherry. He added that the company insisted on unloading the goods on the highway, citing reasons including that it was not allowed to enter the state, forcing him to arrange transportation of the goods from the highway to his residence. Later, he claimed that an inspection of the delivered consignment showed that his AC worth about Rs 39,999 was found missing. The man added that when he approached the company representative, they initially denied knowledge of it but later admitted that the AC was in their possession. However, the company allegedly demanded Rs 5,000 initially and later Rs 13,000 for its release. Aggrieved, he moved the commission with this complaint. No return of same AC The commission found that the company did not appear to contest the case despite receiving notice. It declined to direct the return of the same AC, noting that the AC had been purchased in 2019 and nearly seven years had passed. It held that its present condition was unknown and that returning the same AC would be of No use to the complainant. The commission also took depreciation into account and directed the company to pay 50 of the ACs value instead. It found that the complainant had established that he suffered mental agony, adding that the wrongful retention of the AC and repeated demands for additional money added to his distress. In addition to that, demanding a higher amount and repeated demanding of money, quoting some reason or the other, would have caused mental agony to the complainant, it mentioned. The commission directed the company to pay Rs 18,000 as the excess amount collected, Rs 20,000 50 of the ACs value, Rs 25,000 for mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards litigation costs. Takeaway This ruling highlights that a packers and movers company cannot demand an amount higher than what was agreed and that failure to deliver a consigned item amounts to deficiency in service. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Puducherry 180-0425-1082 or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Jonathan Bailey as Dracula: Mary Lambert talks casting the ‘Sexiest Man Alive’ as vampire
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jonathan Bailey voices Dracula in Mary Lambert's Audible adaptation.
description: In an exclusive interview with SCREEN, Dracula director Mary Lambert talks about casting Jonathan Bailey as Dracula in Audible's adaptation, and using her experience on Pet Sematary and Madonna's "Like A Prayer" to tell the horror tale.
body_raw: There couldnt have been a more apt name than Mary Lambert to helm the new Audible Original adaptation of Bram Stokers 1897 seminal Gothic novel Dracula. Shes no stranger to horror, having helmed films like Pet Sematary 1989, an adaptation of Stephen Kings 1983 bestseller. Shes also been an aficionado of sound, music, and aural effects, having directed trailblazing music videos of pop stars like Madonna and Janet Jackson. And shes certainly not new to the cocktail of spirituality and sex that is Dracula, having collaborated with Madonna in the highly controversial 1989 video Like A Prayer. Mary Lambert on the cocktail of sex, religion, and horror Why not a Black Jesus?, Lambert recalls suggesting to Madonna when the Grammy winner pitched making out with a Black guy at the altar in the music video of Like A Prayer. It invited the ire of a lot of fundamentalist Christians and other people who want to use religion to control people, instead of connecting people, claims the director in an exclusive interview with SCREEN. She believes that unlike the extremely conservative Americans, Indians have historically been far more open to the idea of embracing sex, a la the Kamasutra. Indians deal with sexuality much better. They acknowledge that sex and sexual desire are religious experiences. Religious ecstasy is very close to what people experience as sexual ecstasy. And I dont mean that in a religious way, but as something like being consumed by desire to a point that youre not limited to your body, argues Lambert. So, when she had Peoples Sexiest Man Alive of last year - Jonathan Bailey - cast as Dracula, she could use his magnetic persona to make the audiences imagination run wild, despite the obvious setback of them not being able to watch Bailey in all his glory as the mythical vampire on screen. Jonathan is an extremely attractive man, and not just physically. Hes so charming. Sexiness is much more than that. It definitely helps to have a gorgeous face, beautiful hair, and lovely skin, but theres something else that makes someone sexy - its their personality and humanity. You really feel theres a lovely, thoughtful, and funny person inside there. He really responds to you in that moment, says Lambert. Beyond not projecting Baileys visual as the sinister, otherworldly aristocrat, directing an audio show was a challenge for Lambert because as a painter, shes also a very visual person. Thats what I enjoy most about movies - making paintings that move, she says, adding, But with sound, you can leave people to their own imagination. When you listen and visualize, the sunlight feels more real and the castle more frightening, instead of watching a movie, where the castle just looks like a hotel On learning horror storytelling from Stephen King Lambert is an advocate for whipping out of imagination than consumption on a platter also because shes a book nerd. Thats also what led to her helming Pet Sematary, which she confesses was difficult to adapt. Stephen King uses the characters voice as the singular point of view, and the readers read their thoughts. For instance, when you read Pet Sematary, you know what Louis Creed is thinking. He wants to kill the cat. He hates his daughter. These are things people dont share. But we understand thats what drives him in order to bring his son back to life, says the filmmaker. Dracula, starring Jonathan Bailey, is now available on Audible - best of jonathan bailey badpostjbailey October 1, 2026 But with Dracula, the job was made slightly easier by multiple characters points of view. They write diaries and letters, and they tear them off sometimes. More often than not, the first letters they write are what they actually think. Its a difficult thing to visualize what someone is saying to themselves. Sometimes, its conveyed through narration, but I feel its best done through performance. Its easier in an audio drama because there are no visuals to distract from it. Sometimes, wed do a sequence over and over again until we were on the same page. Because there are no cameras, sets, hair, and makeup to take care of after every shot, adds Lambert, heaving a sigh of relief. Fallout star Ella Purnell, who voices Mina Murray in Dracula, is not designed as his hapless victim, as has been the trope in several previous iterations. Lambert feels she was able to achieve that because of two key changes in the three decades since Pet Sematary. Studios and financiers realized that women were making up a large percentage of the audience for certain horror movies. Also, more young women began directing horror movies, pointed out the director. Also Read When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood bunch of thieves for stealing his bestseller plots As a result, female characters began to have more agency in the plots of horror films. The female nature - and men can have a female nature - is more in touch with instinct, spirituality, and the invisible world. So, this worked well in movies like The Others 2001, The Ring 2002, Insidious 2010, The Conjuring 2013, A Girl Walks Home Alone At Night, and The Babadook 2014, says Lambert, adding, Women could even be villains Like Amy Madigan, who totally changed the face of horror in Weapons, my favorite movie of 2025, largely because of her performance and its implications.

articleTitle: Tata feud widens, key Trust on edge as Charity Commissioner steps in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Venu Srinivasan (left) and Vijay Singh. (File Photo/ Facebook Tata Trusts)
description: Charity Commissioner has sought a response from the trust by October 12, adding urgency to a dispute that has moved beyond differences behind closed doors.
body_raw: Pressure is mounting on the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust SDTT as the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner has sought a response to the complaints filed by Tata Sons Director and SDTT Trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, even as a separate order on the Sir Ratan Tata Trust SRTT is expected in the coming weeks. The latest move adds another layer to the increasingly bitter internal dispute within the Tata Trusts, with questions over the governance of the two principal trusts that together hold more than half of Tata Sons. The Charity Commissioners proceedings have already had a direct impact on Tata Sons, with the holding companys annual general meeting AGM adjourned after the regulators restraining order prevented SRTT from conducting its board proceedings. The Charity Commissioner had earlier issued an ex-parte order restraining SRTT from holding meetings and taking decisions while an inquiry into the composition of its board was pending. The order has effectively frozen the trusts functioning and created a procedural hurdle for Tata Sons. The SDTT now faces scrutiny on a separate front following complaints by Srinivasan and Singh. Srinivasan had sought an immediate inquiry into the administration and governance of SDTT, including the appointment and continued status of its perpetual trustees and the basis on which Noel Tata assumed and continues to hold the chairmanship of Tata Trusts. The Charity Commissioner has sought a response from the trust by October 12, adding urgency to a dispute that has moved well beyond differences behind closed doors. Trusts charitable objectives SDTT resolution targets Srinivasan Srinivasan and Singh also alleged that SDTT trustees exposed the trust and its charitable corpus to potentially significant fiscal consequences by involving the trust directly in commercial activities that, according to him, may not be incidental to its charitable objectives. He described such conduct as mismanagement of the affairs and property of SDTT and a breach of trustees duties. The dispute intensified after SDTT circulated a resolution seeking to restrain Srinivasan, in his capacity as a nominee director on the Tata Sons board, from participating in or voting on the proposed listing of Tata Sons. They termed the move an extraordinary attempt to prevent him from exercising his independent judgment and vote. He alleged that it was an attempt to neutralise his position as a trustee because his views differed from those of other trustees. He further described it as an attempt to effect a power grab within SDTT and influence the course of Tata Sons. The developments have opened a new front in the Tata Trusts internal battle at a time when the issue of Tata Sons listing has become the central fault line among trustees. The Reserve Bank of India RBI rejected Tata Sons application to remain an unregistered core investment company CIC on September 11 and directed it to comply with applicable regulations, effectively putting the company on the path towards listing. Pending decision on SRTT Meanwhile, the Charity Commissioners pending decision on SRTT remains crucial for Tata Sons. The SRTT holds a 23.56 stake in Tata Sons and its inability to convene a board meeting has prevented it from jointly nominating an authorised representative with SDTT. That nomination is critical under Tata Sons Articles of Association, which require at least five members to be personally present for quorum at the AGM, including an authorised representative jointly nominated by SDTT and SRTT. This was precisely why the Tata Sons AGM scheduled for August 18 was adjourned for want of quorum. The freeze on SRTT meant that the trust could not complete the process required to nominate its representative jointly with SDTT. The consequences extend beyond the immediate AGM. The meeting has to consider key corporate matters, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as a director. His current five-year term as Tata Sons chairman ends on February 20, 2027. With the Charity Commissioner now seeking a response from SDTT on the Srinivasan and Singh complaints, and an order on the SRTT proceedings expected in the coming weeks, the regulators decisions could have significant implications for the governance of the Tata Trusts as well as the functioning of Tata Sons, sources tracking the developments said.

articleTitle: Maharashtra police told CJP volunteers to skip Delhi protest, asked who’s paying: Dipke
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Abhijeet Dipke CJP mumbai protest
description: Ahead of the October 10 Jantar Mantar protest, the CJP founder called the Chandrapur police notices "dictatorship." The district's SP says they are routine before any protest.
body_raw: Cockroach Janta Party CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday accused the Maharashtra Police of trying to intimidate protesters, after police in Chandrapur issued notices to volunteers planning to join a protest at Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 10. He called the action dictatorship. A notice issued by Chandrapurs Ballarpur Police on October 5 under Section 168 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS to a CJP supporter, which Dipke shared on X, states that police had learnt he was planning to travel to New Delhi to support Dipke in the proposed march. The notice asks why he was joining the CJP agitation, who was funding his participation and what his objective was. It directs him not to take part in the Delhi protest or any agitation without permission, not to associate with violent protesters, not to post violent content on social media and not to make provocative speeches. It also directs him to follow police instructions and not obstruct public peace or law and order, and warns of preventive or criminal action if a violation leads to, or could lead to, a cognisable offence. The notice further states that Section 3713 of the Maharashtra Police Act is in force in Chandrapur district by order of the district collector to maintain law and order, and warns of legal action if he violates it and a law-and-order situation arises from his actions. At a press conference, Dipke said several volunteers had received similar notices, asking them not to join the protest and seeking details of their travel to Delhi, including who was paying for it. Somewhere or the other, the Maharashtra Police have broken our hearts. Yesterday, some of our volunteers received notices from the Chandrapur Police. They have been told not to go to the protest at Jantar Mantar. They have also been asked where the funds for their travel to Delhi are coming from, he said. If a person from Maharashtra wants to go to Delhi for a protest, what business is it of the Chandrapur Police to ask where his travel expenses are coming from? Cant a person himself buy a railway ticket worth Rs 1,000 or Rs 1,500? he asked. Chandrapur Superintendent of Police Ayush Nopany said the notices were routine. Issuing such notices before any protest or event is a routine activity. This is a prohibitory provision, and the police noticed that some people from Chandrapur were likely to travel to Delhi for the protest. We wanted to caution them against violence and provocative speeches, and remind them that they need to obtain permission from the concerned police station - in this case, the police station in Delhi and not Chandrapur, he told The Indian Express. He stressed that the notices were a preventive measure and not aimed specifically at the protesters. Dipke questioned the polices suggestion that the protest could turn violent. The notice says the protesters could become violent. How does the Chandrapur Police already know that the protest will turn violent? Has it already been planned that it will become violent? On the warning against social media posts, he said, I want to ask the Maharashtra Police to show me one video where anyone from our side has said anything that could lead to violence. I keep speaking about Gandhi and Ambedkar. Does that appear violent? Why is the Maharashtra Police behaving like the Delhi Police? When did Jantar Mantar come under the Chandrapur Police? Who are the Chandrapur Police to tell people not to participate in a protest at Jantar Mantar? he asked. Who told these officials to issue these notices? No police officer would send such notices on his own. One or two police officers should not end up bringing disrepute to the Maharashtra Police. Dipke also criticised the Mumbai Police over action against tribal students marching in Mumbai. He alleged that some students in the agitation, which he said was led by tribal activist Rahul Pawra, were detained and beaten. Criminals have reduced so much that you have started laying hands on students? he asked, questioning whether police would treat the children of influential politicians and businessmen the same way. He accused the BJP of assuming that protesters are paid to take part, and repeated his demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation, citing allegations of voter deletions and the Supreme Courts observations on Form 6 applications. Every Indian should demand Gyanesh Kumars resignation because our right to vote is being taken away, he said. The Form 6 row follows The Indian Express investigation that revealed objections by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to a declaration added to the online version of Form 6, the form used to enrol new voters. The ECI has said the Supreme Court upheld the declaration, a claim legal experts have disputed, arguing the court never directly examined its validity. He said he was ready to face arrest. If you want to arrest me, arrest me. I am sitting here. Impose NSA, impose UAPA if you think that threatening us with arrest will make us remain silent. That will not happen. If you want to put me in jail, put me there. We will continue to fight to save democracy.

articleTitle: ‘Seen him shouting at stars’: Raza Murad compares ‘perfectionists’ Bhansali, Raj Kapoor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Raj Kapoor, Sanjay Leela Bhansali
description: Raza Murad recalled working with Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali, saying both filmmakers are perfectionists who know how to get the best out of sensitive actors.
body_raw: Veteran actor Raza Murad, known for speaking his mind, recently took a sharp dig at the big stars of the film industry for skipping the last rites of Welcome actor Mushtaq Khan. And now, in a recent interview with Vickey Lalwani, the seasoned actor also opened up about the similarities between filmmakers Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali, and why he considers both of them perfectionists. Raza Murad says Sanjay Leela Bhansali is a perfectionist Sanjay Leela Bhansali is a perfectionist, said Raza Murad. The host then asked him about reports of the filmmaker being moody and losing his temper. Responding to this, the actor said, See, about the anger, when you are consistently unable to understand what hes trying to say, then he loses his cool. Its not like he is angry right from the start. And, of course, every person has their own temperament, and that anger isnt personal, its related to work because it isnt happening properly. So, its fine, if hes getting angry. And, its not like he only loses his temper at his assistants. I have seen him shouting at bigger stars as well. When asked if he had seen Bhansali shout at Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone or Priyanka Chopra, Raza said, Yes, he wants what he wants, and of course, I have seen him getting angry at stars as well. Both of them are perfectionists Drawing a parallel between Bhansali and Raj Kapoor, Raza said both filmmakers wouldnt compromise when it came to their work. Speaking about how he would rate the two filmmakers, the Padmaavat actor stated, Both of them are perfectionists. They want what they want. Time, shift, money, set, dates were of least importance to them. Its okay, if it takes eight days instead of four days. And, when they are on set, they mean business. Hum kaam karne ke liye aaye hain We have come here to work. And, this has happened twice with me. Raza then recalled his first experience of working with Raj Kapoor in Prem Rog 1982. When I was working for the first time with Raj saab in Prem Rog. It was my first day, and meri kya aukaat thi unke saamne What was my status in front of him?. Despite stiff opposition from his sons stating that I wouldnt suit the role. and I was a small time actor, Raj saab said, Ye role karenge toh Raza saahab hi karenge If theres someone, who can do this role, its only Raza sir. He made me meet everyone on the set like I was some head of the state. Also Read Staff touched Bollywood stars feet Sabeer Bhatia says celeb worship shocked American guests Raza recalls similar experience with Sanjay Leela Bhansali Raza said he experienced a similar gesture from the Devdas filmmaker when he first worked with him. And the same thing happened with Sanjay Leela Bhansali, the first day when I went on his set, he also called his entire unit and introduced me to them saying, Raza saab is working with us. So, this was common in both filmmakers Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali. They gave me a lot of respect and importance. He would get angry at heroines The host then asked Raza if Raj Kapoor would get angry at stars in the same way Sanjay Leela Bhansali does. The Prem Rog actor recalled, Actors are extremely sensitive but they directors know how to get work done from them. He would get angry at heroines, Kya kar rahi hai tu? Ye kya kar rahi hai? Aise mat kar What are you doing? What is this that you are doing? Dont do it. Youre not listening to me. Leave, Ill do and show it to you. He would shout the way elderly people do. And, I have never seen any heroine take offence at his anger. They used to listen to those harsh words and deliver, this was his working style. Raza also revealed that he had seen Raj Kapoor lose his temper with Padmini Kolhapure on the sets of Prem Rog and with Mandakini while shooting Ram Teri Ganga Maili 1985. Raj Kapoor would fall ill before film releases Raza further recalled how Raj Kapoor would become unwell before the release of his films. I saw Raj Kapoor saab fall ill twice, I have seen those pink lips and cheeks turn pale before any of his films release, and the moment the film would be declared a hit, he would recover. He was very concerned about RK Banner, Raj Kapoor ki film hai. Aise hi Raj Kapoor, Raj Kapoor nahi hue hai, Its a Raj Kapoor film. He didnt become Raj Kapoor by fluke, he had many qualities, shared the actor. On the debacle of Mera Naam Joker He was very upset about it. He couldnt come to terms with the reality that the film had flopped at the box office, because Sangam was also a very lengthy film, there were two intervals. But, because the times had changes, peoples mindsets had also changed, and he felt that maybe he made his autobiography. That film is a masterpiece but it happens, said Raza Murad on Raj Kapoors condition post the release of Mera Naam Joker.

articleTitle: Rewilding great Indian bustards: The project and the challenges ahead
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Two male great Indian bustards (GIB) are released in Rajasthan’s Desert National Park on Sunday. (X: Bhupender Yadav)
description: For the first time, two captive-bred great Indian bustards have been released into the wild. While this experiment is indeed important, the recovery of their population still remains a long-term challenge.
body_raw: October 4 marked a significant milestone in the efforts to conserve the critically endangered great Indian bustard GIB. Two captive-bred male GIBs were released into the wild for the first time in Rajasthans Desert National Park near Jaisalmer town. The pilot release marks the first step in rewilding bustards that have been bred and raised in captivity. This is part of Project GIB which the Centre is running along with the Wildlife Institute of India and the governments of Rajasthan and Gujarat. What is the great Indian bustard and why is its population being revived? The great Indian bustard is a large, ground-dwelling bird found in savannahs, grasslands and deserts in India. Till the late 19th and early 20th century, it was spread across 11 states - from Haryana in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, and from Rajasthan in the west to Odisha in the east. But a range of issues resulted in its decline - hunting, poaching of eggs, gradual conversion of open habitats into croplands and mining areas and, more recently, deaths due to collisions with renewable energy power lines. GIBs poor frontal vision, combined with their heavy body, makes it difficult for them to detect or avoid such infrastructure. From an estimated 1,260-1,400 in the early 1970s, the wild GIB population has now plummeted to only around 150, of which around 130 -20 are in Rajasthan. The rest are in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh - facing the risk of local extinction. To counter their decline, the Centre and the Rajasthan government launched a long-term bustard and lesser florican project in 2012-13. This project was expanded from 2014 with funding support to start a conservation breeding program. Beginning 2019, wild GIB eggs were collected from Desert National Park and surrounding areas, incubated artificially at two centres in Rajasthans Sam and Ramdevra and hand-reared. These hand-reared birds mated at these centres, giving birth to 98 birds as of now. Of these, two were released Sunday and 11 more have been earmarked for wild release. The others remain at the centres for captive reproduction. What does rewilding entail? Before initiating the rewilding process, a rewilding aviary was set up at the Ramdevra Center while a soft release facility was developed by the Wildlife Institute of India inside Desert National Park. Unlike the hand-reared birds that were used to humans, chicks aged between three and four months were released in these facilities so that they could move freely and adapt to the natural environment without human imprinting. Scientists associated with the project said the birds have been fitted with transmitters. These devices will send alerts thrice a day on their coordinates and movement pattern. Teams will also monitor them from afar. Challenges in long-term recovery The beginning of the rewilding phase, while crucial, is a challenging experiment. The released birds will face a challenge to their survival. Enclosures within Desert National Park were picked because they comprised grasslands as well as stretches free of either human or technological interruptions. While this is an experiment in Rajasthan, similar experiments would have to be carried out in range states such as Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, albeit only after habitat improvements. We can learn from the Rajasthan experience, and if this is successful, then Gujarat may do a similar pilot. However, restoration and protection of grasslands is crucial for the revival of bustards outside Rajasthan, said Gobind Sagar Bhardwaj, Director, Wildlife Institute of India. Unlike forested areas across Indias states, grassland protection has always been challenging as they are not traditionally considered protected areas in public perception. Bharadwaj said this makes them vulnerable to land-use conversion and degradation, which consequently affects the livelihoods of pastoralists and those who rear livestock. The afforestation of grasslands was red-flagged by Asad Rahmani, one of Indias foremost bustard experts and former director of Bombay Natural History Society, in the NGOs famous Hornbill magazine back in 2008. Rahmani wrote Ironically, one of the biggest threats to grasslands is not from the graziers, but from the forest department. To live up to their name, officials of the forest department consider their solemn duty to convert every grassland and even wetlands into a forest. He noted that from Gujarat to Andhra Pradesh, it was seen that forest officers decided to improve habitats by planting trees or creating waterholes in bustard habitats. Threats to GIB revival At the conclusion of a landmark case seeking protection of GIBs, the Supreme Court had, accepting the recommendations of an expert panel, ordered some broad protection measures for GIBs and their habitats in Rajasthan and Gujarat. It demarcated priority areas for the bird 14,013 sq km in Rajasthan and 740 sq km in Gujarat and ordered that 80 km of power lines in Rajasthan should be buried underground. This has to be completed between 2027 and 2028. It also ordered the creation of powerline corridors that will accommodate re-routed overhead lines. Experts have warned that rewilding will not be sustainable if these power lines cannot be buried underground soon. Limestone mining is yet another issue that threatens to affect the open and flat areas that Bustards need. The Supreme Court did not order specific measures against mining, and mine operations are proposed in the northern side of DNP, where the birds were released.

articleTitle: IIM Lucknow, TeamLease launch 11-month executive programme in Brand Management
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iim lucknow medusa campus image
description: The curriculum covers consumer insights, brand strategy and integrated communications, along with digital marketing, e-commerce, performance marketing and customer lifecycle management.
body_raw: The Indian Institute of Management IIM Lucknow has launched an 11-month Executive Programme in Brand Management in partnership with TeamLease EdTech, for working professionals seeking to build skills in brand strategy, consumer understanding, digital marketing and business decision-making. The programme comprises 132 learning hours, including 114 hours of live online learning and 18 hours through a three-day campus immersion at IIM Lucknow. The course uses case studies, business simulations, projects, assignments, faculty-led live sessions, practitioner-led masterclasses and peer learning to connect classroom concepts with business situations. Read JEE scores can get you into these IIMs undergraduate programmes after Class 12 The curriculum covers consumer insights, brand strategy and integrated communications, along with digital marketing, e-commerce, performance marketing and customer lifecycle management. Participants will also study digital consumer psychology, brand storytelling, social media and influencer branding, marketplace and quick-commerce strategy, and omnichannel growth. A key component of the programme is the use of emerging technologies in marketing. The curriculum covers AI-driven marketing and advertising and examines how AI can be used to understand consumers and support engagement with them. The programme also looks at how changing digital consumer journeys affect brand building and customer experience. The programme links marketing decisions with the financial and commercial aspects of running a brand. Participants will learn about unit economics, profitability, financial planning, valuation and governance, along with cross-functional leadership. This is intended to help professionals assess brand decisions not only from a consumer or marketing perspective but also in terms of their wider business impact. Also Read From buckets to hangers Why No-Bag Day is becoming a campus trend at IITs, IIMs The programme is designed for brand and marketing professionals, digital and growth professionals, product and business leaders, entrepreneurs, sales professionals and those aspiring to marketing leadership roles. The curriculum is structured around the changing role of brand managers, where consumer insight, digital execution, data, technology and business economics increasingly overlap. Learning is primarily delivered online, with the campus component providing an opportunity for in-person learning at IIM Lucknow. The application-oriented format includes business simulations and projects alongside academic sessions, allowing participants to apply concepts such as positioning, customer experience, digital growth and marketing economics to business situations. The programme is open to graduates, diploma holders and postgraduates. Selection will be based on the candidates academic and professional background and experience. Participants who meet the prescribed academic and attendance requirements will receive a Certificate of Successful Completion from IIM Lucknow. Admissions for the upcoming cohort are open. Details on the programme curriculum, eligibility, fee and application process are available on the programme website.
