articleTitle: Denied pension over schizophrenia, Orissa High Court restores it for retired CRPF man
articleFeaturedImageAlt: crpf man disability pension rules orissa high court (1)
description: The petitioner was a CRPF employee who retired on medical invalidation grounds in 1999 after he was found to have schizophrenia. The authorities later rejected his disability pension saying that it was a 'non-classified' disease.
body_raw: Holding that the petitioners claim could not be rejected merely because schizophrenia was not a classified disease, the Orissa High Court has quashed a 2011 order rejecting a former CRPF personnels claim for disability pension, directing the authorities to allow the pension and release the arrears. Justice Biraja Prasanna Satapathy was dealing with a plea of a former personnel with the Central Reserve Police Force CRPF, who retired on medical grounds in 1999 due to schizophrenia with an approved 50 per cent disability pension. However, the authorities later revoked the benefit, claiming schizophrenia was non-classified and he lacked 10 years of service. Taking into account the nature of the order passed and the grounds of rejection issued, this court is of the view that since the petitioner was allowed to take retirement on the ground of invalidation because of his.schizophrenia, on the ground that such a disease is not a classified disease, the petitioners claim could not have been rejected, the court said on October 1. The ruling held that since it was clearly indicated in the order that the petitioner is entitled to get the disability pension of 50 per cent and the said order since was never modified or recalled, this court is of the view that the ground on which the petitioners claim was rejected is not sustainable in the eyes of the law. Retired due to schizophrenia The petitioner was a CRPF employee who was allowed to retire on medical invalidation in 1999 after he was found to have schizophrenia. The medical board had found him completely and permanently incapacitated for future service and recommended disability pension of 50 per cent. The CRPFs order allowing his invalidation retirement also specifically stated that he would be entitled to the pension from the date of invalidation. However, his claim for disability pension was later rejected in 2011. The authorities said schizophrenia was not a classified disease for the purpose of Extraordinary Disability Pension EOP under the CCS Pension Rules, 1972, and that he had not completed the required 10 years of qualifying service. He was told he was only entitled to service gratuity, which had already been paid. The petitioner challenged the rejection before the high court, seeking quashing of the 2011 order and release of his disability pension. Original order never recalled Order The court noted that the petitioner was allowed to retire on medical invalidation because of schizophrenia, based on the medical boards assessment that he was permanently incapacitated for further service. The 1999 retirement order specifically stated that he was entitled to 50 per cent disability pension from the date of invalidation. The high court observed that the pension claim was later rejected on the grounds that schizophrenia was not a classified disease and that the petitioner had not completed 10 years of qualifying service. It further noted that the original retirement order had never been modified or recalled. Therefore, the subsequent rejection of the pension claim was not sustainable in law and was also hit by the principle of promissory estoppel, a legal principle that allows a court to enforce a promise even when there is no formal, written contract.

articleTitle: Rs 5,000 per student: Gujarat doctor caught accepting bribe for ‘not harassing’ students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bribery
description: Dr Rahim Ibrahim Memon, medical superintendent of the J S Chauhan Civil Hospital for allegedly seeking bribe of Rs 40,000 from 8 students.
body_raw: A government medical superintendent in Gujarat was arrested on Monday by the state Anti-Corruption Bureau ACB for seeking and receiving a bribe from medical students who were deputed to his hospital for rural service. The ACB, on Monday, booked and arrested Dr Rahim Ibrahim Memon, 59, Medical Superintendent Class-1 of the J S Chauhan Civil Hospital in Devgadh Baria, Dahod, for allegedly seeking the bribe under the pretext of not harassing the medical students during their time at the institution headed by him. A statement from the ACB on Tuesday stated, A total of eight students were appointed to J S Chauhan Government Civil Hospital, Devgadh Baria, Dahod, under the District Residency Programme DRP. The accused demanded a bribe of Rs 40,000 in total, calculated at Rs 5,000 per student, from the eight students in exchange for assigning favourable duties and ensuring they would not be harassed during their service. The incident came to light after one of the students who refused to pay the bribe approached the Gandhinagar ACB, said officials who set a trap to nab him. A team of the anti-corruption agency set a trap at the government staff quarters of the officer, who was caught red-handed while accepting a bribe of Rs 40,000 from the complainant, said the ACB. He was placed under arrest, and further investigation is underway.

articleTitle: King Charles warns Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor not to use royal funds in battle against police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor legal challenge
description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor receives an annual stipend from King Charles’ private funds, although the amount has not been disclosed.
body_raw: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has reportedly been warned not to use money provided to him by King Charles from the monarchs private funds to finance his legal challenge against Thames Valley police in England. This comes in the backdrop of the former Duke of York seeking to quash search warrants that led to his arrest earlier this year for his alleged role in sharing sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein. The Guardian report, which cited palace sources, comes just days ahead of a private high court hearing on Thursday over his legal claim. Mountbatten-Windsor receives an annual stipend from King Charles private funds, although the amount has not been disclosed. However, it has been made clear that the money should not be used to fund the judicial review, the report said. The report further said that Mountbatten-Windsors legal defence was a matter for him and his lawyers, while Buckingham Palace had no role in deciding the strategy or actions being taken in the case. Andrew Mountbatten-Windsors arrest and charges The legal challenge relates to searches carried out by Thames Valley police following Mountbatten-Windsors arrest on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office. The former duke was arrested on his 66th birthday over allegations that he had shared sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the UKs trade envoy. Police searched his residence on the Sandringham estate and his former home, Royal Lodge, after warrants were issued by a judge at the Old Bailey. The searches ended on February 24, according to Thames Valley police. Mountbatten-Windsor was interviewed under caution and later released under investigation. The arrest came as scrutiny continued over allegations concerning his links with Epstein and the handling of information during his time as a trade envoy. The former duke, who now lives on King Charles private Sandringham estate in Norfolk, was previously granted permission to challenge whether Thames Valley police acted lawfully in obtaining and executing the search warrants. What is expected in the Thursday hearing The Guardian cited a judicial spokesperson who confirmed on Monday that a hearing in the legal claim would take place at 2 pm on Thursday before Justice Hilliard at the High Court. The hearing will concern an attempt by Thames Valley police to restrict access to court documents and will begin in private. It remains unclear whether Mountbatten-Windsor will attend the hearing. The king had maintained that the legal process should proceed independently. Following Mountbatten-Windsors arrest, Charles issued a written statement saying the law must take its course. Thames Valley police said its investigation into alleged misconduct in public office remained ongoing and confirmed that it was involved in legal proceedings concerning warrants previously obtained from the central criminal court. As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further, the Guardian report quoted a police spokesperson as saying.

articleTitle: Denied boarding on Kochi-Abu Dhabi flight, mother and child wins Rs 70,287 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Airlines boarding consumer flight
description: The commission held that the airline's failure to transport the complainants to the destination without any reason amounted to a shortcoming and inadequacy in the service.
body_raw: A Kerala consumer commission has directed an airline to pay Rs 70,287 to a mother and her minor son after they were allegedly denied boarding on a confirmed Kochi-Abu Dhabi flight and had to purchase fresh tickets. President CT Sabu and member Ram Mohan R observed that the complainant had to manage the minor child, rearrange their travel at short notice, undertake an additional journey and were constrained to pay a higher amount for the second ticket. The fact that the 2nd complainant was a child of approximately three years at the time makes the inconvenience and hardship more significant. The 1st complainant had to manage the minor child, rearrange their travel at short notice and undertake an additional journey between Sharjah and Abu Dhabi. Also constrained to pay a higher amount for the second ticket to Sharjah, the order read. Boarding denied The complainant said that she had booked flight tickets to travel from Kochi to Abu Dhabi on 11 February 2021, paying Rs 20,287. It was alleged that they had valid travel documents and were eligible to travel to Abu Dhabi under the travel guidelines applicable at the time, but were denied permission to board the flight. The complainant alleged that they were then compelled to purchase fresh tickets from Kochi to Sharjah for which they paid Rs 29,510. It was further stated that since Abu Dhabi was their intended destination, the mother and child had to undertake an additional journey from Sharjah to Abu Dhabi after landing there. The complainant said that the airline neither provided a satisfactory justification for denying boarding nor refunded the original KochiAbu Dhabi airfare. The airline did not appear before the commission despite being served notice and was proceeded against ex-parte. The commission said that if boarding had been denied because of any lawful restriction, failure to meet mandatory travel requirements or any other valid reason attributable to the complainants, the airline was required to disclose and establish the same. However, no such explanation or evidence was placed before it. The commission held that the airlines failure to transport the complainants to the contracted destination, without establishing a legally sustainable reason, followed by collection of a further amount for travel to a different destination, amounted to a shortcoming and inadequacy in the service. The commission thus directed the airline to refund the original airfare of Rs 20,287. It also awarded Rs 40,000 as compensation for deficiency in service, mental agony, inconvenience and hardship, and Rs 10,000 towards proceedings costs. Takeaway An airline that denies boarding on a confirmed ticket must have a legally sustainable reason and cannot retain the fare for a journey it failed to provide. Passengers can seek a refund and compensation for the resulting hardship. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Kerala 1800-425-1550 or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 for assistance.

articleTitle: 7 die as SUV crashes into parked truck in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The police officer said all seven men worked in the shipbreaking yard and commuted daily from Bhavnagar to Alang, a 50-km distance.
description: The incident took place around 9.45 am near Trapaj village at the trijunction of roads leading to Bhavnagar, Talaja and Alang.
body_raw: Seven people died after an SUV travelling from Bhavnagar to Alang in Gujarat crashed into a stationary truck on Tuesday morning. All the victims worked at the Alang shipbreaking yard and were headed there when the accident took place. The incident took place around 9.45 am near Trapaj village at the trijunction of roads leading to Bhavnagar, Talaja and Alang. Manish Nakum, Deputy Superintendent of Police, told The Indian Express that six people died on the spot and one was rushed to a nearby hospital. The survivor succumbed to injuries later, said Inspector PM Desai of Alang police station. The police officer said all seven men worked in the shipbreaking yard and commuted daily from Bhavnagar to Alang, a 50-km distance. The truck driver had parked the vehicle on the service road and had gone to have snacks when the SUV hit the truck from behind, the Inspector added. The front part of the SUV was completely damaged, indicating the intensity of the crash. CCTV videos of the crash show that the impact caused the parked heavy vehicle to move forward. Visuals showed the SUVs windshield shattered and its roof damaged. The doors of the vehicle had to be forced open with iron bars to recover the victims bodies. Inspector Desai said the bodies had been sent for post-mortem and the identities of the victims would be revealed shortly after.

articleTitle: Gujarat couple died by suicide live on Instagram, family was among viewers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dahod couple live suicide, Dahod couple suicide case, Gujarat couple live suicide, Gujarat Instagram live suicide, Dahod Instagram live, young couple death Dahod, Dahod news, Gujarat suicide case, social media live tragedy, Dahod police investigation, Gujarat news, Indian Express news
description: Family members alerted the Dahod police after watching the livestream, but poor connectivity hampered efforts to locate the couple.
body_raw: At least 57 people watched a young man and a teenage girl in Gujarats Dahod as they went live on a social media platform from a forested area and allegedly took their own lives, turning a family dispute into a tragedy that unfolded in real time. Senior police officers said the incident occurred on October 4 on the outskirts of Hirapur village in Singwad, where a teenage girl, below 18, and a young man, in his early 20s, travelled roughly 20 km from their respective villages in a neighbouring taluka before starting the Instagram live. The live stream has since emerged as a crucial part of the police investigation. Poor connectivity Among those watching the couple were members of their families, who alerted the police after seeing what was unfolding. The families contacted a police station in the district, under whose jurisdiction their respective villages fall, prompting the police to mobilise teams to locate the couple. The police rushed to find them, but poor network connectivity and the challenge of pinpointing the exact location turned the response into a race they could not win. The police team was immediately dispatched, but due to network issues as well as the challenge of identifying the exact location, the two had already taken the extreme step by the time the police reached the spot, a senior officer said. A spontaneous act Karan Panna, Assistant Deputy Superintendent of Police, Limkheda division, told The Indian Express that the circumstances pointed towards family opposition to the relationship. A probe is on. Prima facie, it was a spontaneous act, and the circumstances suggest their families opposed the relationship. We are conducting an investigation after an accidental death case has been lodged. The further steps will be decided accordingly, Panna said. A team from the police station reached the spot and recovered the bodies, beginning the investigation. The bodies of the couple were sent for post-mortem examination and handed over to their families Monday for the final rites, Panna said.

articleTitle: Navratri 2026: Start and End Date, Navratri Colours With Calendar, Significance and Importance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: navratri
description: Navratri 2026 Start and End Date: Know the significance of Navratri 2026, its start and end dates, nine-day colour calendar, and the traditions associated with each day.
body_raw: Sharad Navratri 2026The term Navratri or Navaratri is a combination of two distinct words-nava, which stands for nine, and ratri, which signifies night. When brought together, the name literally translates to nine nights. Spanning nine consecutive nights and ten days, Navratri ranks among the most sacred and widely observed festivals in the Hindu tradition, typically taking place during the autumn months. At its core, the celebration emphasizes devotion to Goddess Durga, also revered as Shakti, the embodiment of universal cosmic power honouring her through her nine distinct manifestations. While four different Navaratris are observed across India over the course of the year specifically Chaitra Navratri, Paush Navratri, Magha Navratri, and Sharad Navratri, it is Maha Navratri, also known as Sharad Navratri, that is held as the most sacred and significant of them all. According to the Hindu calendar, the festival is celebrated in the month of Ashvin, which typically falls in September and October as per the Gregorian calendar. This year, Navratri will be observed from October 11 to October 20, 2026, and the 10th and last day will be celebrated as Dussehra. Importance and Significance of Navratri Regarding the significance of Navratri, it shares the fundamental theme central to all major Indian festivals, the ultimate triumph of good over evil though the underlying legends and mythologies vary significantly. Across Indias diverse regions, the festival manifests in unique ways eastern and northeastern states observe these dates as Durga Puja, whereas communities across the northern and western regions celebrate the nine-night festival to commemorate Lord Ramas victory over the demon king Ravana. According to tradition, Goddess Durga engaged in a fierce battle against the demon Mahishasura, ultimately emerging victorious over him. The festival is observed to honor and worship the Goddess in celebration of this triumph of divine light over darkness. The festivities officially commence on Mahalaya, the first day of the festival, which is dedicated to invoking and remembering Goddess Durga while signifying the conclusion of Pitru Paksha, the sacred fortnight of Shradhh honored by ancestors. On the sixth day of the festival, Goddess Durga is formally welcomed into family homes and elaborate public pandals. These festive observances stretch across the subsequent days until the tenth day, known as Vijayadashami, when the deitys idol is immersed in a body of water. Throughout this period, communities gather to go pandal-hopping, partake in sanctified feast meals called bhog, and distribute food to those in need-an act that celebrates and honors the spirit of goodwill in everyone. Across Northern India, the nine-day occasion centers on commemorating Lord Ramas historic triumph over the demon king Ravana. Over the course of nine nights, theatrical stage plays known as Ramlila perform dramatic adaptations of the ancient Hindu epic Ramayana. On the tenth and concluding day, which depicts Lord Rama slaying Ravana with a bow and arrow, the celebrations culminate in the ceremonial burning of massive effigies representing Ravana alongside his brothers, Meghnad and Kumbhakaran. Observers throughout the region dress in traditional attire, keep ritual fasts, and gather for group prayers. Intricate stage decorations, storytelling recitals, dramatic reenactments of ancient legends, scripture chanting, devotional prayers, and vibrant folk dances like dandiya and garba are performed to embody the energetic spirit of the festivities. Friends and families unite to explore pandals and participate in local gatherings. On the ultimate day, the festivities conclude either with the immersion of the Goddesss idol in water-as practiced during Durga Puja-or through the dramatic burning of effigies during Dussehra. body_raw: UP Scholarship 2026-27 at scholarship.up.gov.in The Uttar Pradesh governments Scholarship Scheme for 2026-27 provides financial assistance to students studying in Classes 9 to 12 as well as those pursuing graduation, postgraduate, diploma, ITI and other post-matric courses. The scheme covers students from General, SC, ST, OBC and minority communities, subject to the eligibility conditions prescribed for each category. For the 2026-27 academic year, applications for Classes 9 to 12 opened on August 11. While the Class 9-12 application deadlines have passed, students pursuing courses beyond Class 12 under the Dashmottar category can apply until October 31, 2026. The scholarship amount varies according to the students category, course and whether they are a day scholar or hosteller. UP Scholarship 2026-27 Important dates Application stage Date Class 9-12 fresh applications August 11 to September 21, 2026 Class 1012 renewal applications August 11 to August 25, 2026 Post-matric fresh applications Dashmottar September 15 to October 31, 2026 Post-matric renewal applications September 15 to October 15, 2026 Fresh Class 9-12 scholarship disbursal January 25-31, 2027 Renewal Class 9-12 scholarship disbursal October 25-31, 2026 What are the benefits? The UP Scholarship provides financial assistance towards education-related expenses. For pre-matric students, the amount differs by category. articleTitle: Drishyam 3: Ajay Devgn’s Vijay is like any political leader who uses religion to get his way
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn plays Vijay Salgaonkar in Drishyam 3
description: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 is the representation of the moral decay of our society because here, good does not win over evil, and justice is never served.
body_raw: Drishyam 3 The Conclusion released in the theatres this past weekend and if you, like many others, were waiting for the promised conclusion at the end of Vijay Salgaonkars story, this must have been a disappointment, for the story never really ends. The loose ends still exist, the decade-old crime is still unsolved, and those who committed the accidental killing are still walking around, scot-free. In the first film, back in 2015, the chain of events begins after Vijays daughter Anju and wife Nandini accidentally kill a boy named Sam, who sexually harassed Anju and is now blackmailing her. Vijay then makes it his lifes mission to save his family from getting imprisoned. He forges evidence, coaches the family to lie, and befriends any potential pawn who could help him in his scheme. He succeeds. The film projects Vijay as the family man, the hero, who will do anything for his family, while completely dismissing the fact that, in this attempt, they are villainising those who are trying to seek justice for the dead son. Vijay lies like a sociopath and trains his family like he is running a sleeper cell so no one gets caught for a crime that was indeed committed by them. Of course, the man was killed in an accidental altercation, but he did end up dead, and someone was responsible, but the film is not interested in that conversation. There is no concept of justice in the Drishyam universe. The film only cares about worshipping the family man Vijay Salganokars family values, and not examining how those values come across as completely hollow. Vijay incites religious hatred, and believes its completely okay In many ways, Vijay is the exact representation of the political leaders of our times, which also explains his popularity amongst the masses. He claims to be an uneducated man who has supposedly become street smart from working at a cable TV shop and watching a bunch of movies. This somehow explains his warped idea of morality, as its entirely derived from fictional films, but it also explains why he lives his regular life like a main character where everyone else is just background noise. ALSO READ Is Chris Hansen a hero or villain? Primetime explores his god complex to get to the answer In the new film, Vijay even uses religion as a weapon to save his family because his political smarts tell him that this tactic, if used correctly, cannot fail. This has worked for many political leaders, and it works perfectly for him as well. The authorities watch his plans unfold while being fully aware of how he is manipulating a mob, and just end up being mute spectators. There is even a scene where Prakash Raj lists the qualifications of those trying to put Vijay behind bars. He points out that a chauthi-fail Vijay has left even Harvard graduates scratching their heads but the film fails to acknowledge that a conniving, sly man doesnt really need a degree to fool the world. Fooling the system for ten long years is not a cause for celebration. For over a decade, Vijay has spent hours and days befriending those who are in a weaker position than him so he can take advantage of their situation and save his family. And all this while, the film has never bothered to actually reflect that his morally corrupt practices have turned him into a hate-inciting criminal. Daughters scarred for life but Vijay believes he has saved them Amid all the damage that he has been inflicting on those around him, there has never been even the slightest pause to actually ponder over how deeply he has damaged his own daughters, whom he is supposedly trying to save. In this film, when he pushes his older daughter to get married, he simply talks about moving on, as if she is not still scarred by the act of killing a man with her bare hands. The woman has been living a nightmare that led to seizures, and Vijays solution is just to get an arranged marriage match so she can move on. Its almost as if he truly believes that he saved his family, and did not create a monster that would never be tamed. The family is constantly looking over their shoulder and cant even breathe peacefully without Vijays nod, for they dont know what awaits at the next corner. The younger daughter, who must have been just 7-8 years old when Sam was killed, has lived with the burden of this case all her life. Vijay has coached her into believing that he is her saviour but the poor girl doesnt know that normal families arent hiding bodies and murders for family time. He has created an elaborate scheme for everything, and the family is playing along. Do they think they are saved? Because it definitely doesnt look like they are living a good life. Drishyam 3 is the representation of the moral decay of our society because here, good does not win over evil, and justice is never served. Vijays family faces no consequences for taking the life of a young man but Vijay is celebrated for being a mastermind criminal who can fool the masses by manipulating them.

articleTitle: Three drivers suspected of taking minor girls to granite baron Veeramani arrested
articleFeaturedImageAlt: veeramani-granite
description: This takes total number of arrests to 7 as probe against granite baron continues to widen
body_raw: The Central Crime Branch has arrested three longtime drivers of Gem Granites founder R Veeramani, accusing them of bringing minor girls to him and helping facilitate sexual offences that are now the subject of five separate cases, police said. The three men-Lazar, Parthiban and Babu-were arrested on Monday after the Anti-Vice Squad and the Special Investigation Team questioned them earlier. Their arrests bring the number of people held in connection with the widening investigation to seven. Police alleged that the drivers had been assigned to escort minor girls from their homes to a guest house used by Veeramani in Teynampet, where some of the alleged offences took place. Police said Lazar worked for Veeramani for 23 years and Babu for eight years. Parthiban was also employed as his driver, though the duration of his employment is unclear. Investigators searched the residences of the three men and seized eight mobile phones and 55 documents, which are being examined. The trio were arrested in connection with the five cases already filed so far. So no fresh FIR has been registered, an officer part of the investigation said. Five cases involving allegations of sexual abuse of minors have now been registered against Veeramani and other accused. The latest was registered on October 2, and investigations are continuing in all five. Veeramani, 84, was arrested on August 29 along with M Shanthi, 60, and her husband, Mahendra Simhan, 63. Police accuse Veeramani of sexually assaulting minor girls and allege that Shanthi and Simhan abetted him. The three were initially remanded in judicial custody at Puzhal Central Prison and were detained under the Goondas Act on October 1. A fourth accused, Ganesan, a former employee of Veeramani, was subsequently arrested after investigators allegedly found video clips involving a minor girl in his possession. The investigation began after a child rights activist approached Chennai police on October 6, 2025, with a pen drive containing footage purportedly showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a minor. Police registered an FIR the following day. But in February this year, police filed a further action dropped report seeking to close the case after saying they had been unable to identify the girl. A Special POCSO Court rejected that report and ordered further investigation. The probe gathered pace again after a woman came forward identifying herself as the girl in the video and Veeramani as the alleged perpetrator.

articleTitle: Anupam Kher ‘almost slapped me’ over hospital costs: Raju Kher on battling bladder cancer
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anupam Kher, Raju Kher
description: Anupam Kher's older brother, Raju Kher recalled being diagnosed with bladder cancer in 2004 and revealed how the former left his shoot abroad and returned to Mumbai to support him.
body_raw: Raju Kher, 69, the younger brother of Anupam Kher has opened up about one of the most difficult phases of his life, recalling how his brother Anupam stood by him when he was diagnosed with bladder cancer in 2004. From leaving a shoot abroad to rushing back to Mumbai, to quietly taking care of his medical expenses, Anupam was there for Raju through his treatment. Looking back at that time, Raju said his brother is not just family but a father figure to him. In an interview with Siddharth Kannan, Raju Kher recalled the time when he broke the news to Anupam, Raju said his brother immediately left his work abroad and returned to Mumbai to be with him. In 2004, I got to know that I have cancer in my bladder. This is that time when I was going through a bad phase. He Anupam Kher was shooting abroad, and he left his work and came to Bombay. I told him everything, and he said, Lets go to Lilavati Hospital, and I said, Lilavati is expensive. He almost slapped me, and said, Who are you to speak about in this matter? Stay quiet, and do as I say. Raju shared that Anupam quietly took care of the financial aspect of his treatment. And, without my knowledge, he bore all the expenses, and there are many such things that he has done for me. Hes a father figure to me, he said. Raju Kher further opened up about the seriousness of his condition and explained that doctors had to remove his urinary bladder to save him. I had tumour in my urinary bladder, and the doctors removed my urinary bladder. I was lucky to have a big intestine, which was converted into a urinary bladder, and attached to the kidneys and the urinary tract, he said. Also Read Sonakshi Sinha, Shahid Kapoors driver opened a momo shop, Tukaram Mundhe shut it down He explained that there are five levels of the tumour and that his was detected at the first level. There are 5 levels of tumour, and we found out through the original bladder that the tumour was at the first level, it was growing fast. This operation lasted for 17 hours, Raju recalled. The actor also spoke about how his relationship with Anupam Kher has given him a sense of security. In todays times, I am not scared about anything because somewhere I know that my brother is there, who can take care of everybody here. So, Im not worried, he said. Raju also emphasised, At the same time, I am also very conscious about not taking him for granted. Raju Kher also shared an update about his sister-in-law and actor-politician Kirron Khers health who earlier battled cancer. He said that she is alright and only needs an injection as part of her treatment.

articleTitle: Protests against Gyanesh Kumar: What was the 2006 Keralam corruption probe that led to his removal from post?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
description: At a time when CEC Gyanesh Kumar is under fire over the SIR process, the Keralam government has reopened an earlier graft case that was followed by his resignation as PWD Secretary.
body_raw: Keralams Congress-led government on Sunday October 4 directed the states Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to re-open a 2006 probe into an alleged claim of bribery against Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar. It comes as Congress leaders, including Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, have demanded the CECs resignation over allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision SIR process. At the time, Kumar, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Keralam cadre, served as Secretary of the state Public Works Department PWD. The bribery claim stemmed from the suicide note of a Malaysian engineer, who was part of a World Bank-aided road work project executed by a Malaysian and Indian joint venture called PATI-BEL. What was the project? The Kerala State Transport Project KSTP has been a flagship project of the state PWD. Costing Rs 1,600 crore, it was envisaged to modernise and renovate select major roads of 1,600 km under the PWD with a World Bank loan. Initial discussions were completed during the last lap of the CPIM-led government from 1996 to 2001. P J Joseph, the leader of the breakaway faction Kerala Congress Joseph, was then the PWD minister. Joseph, then part of the Left Democratic Front LDF alliance, is now with the ruling United Democratic Front UDF alliance. What went wrong? KSTP was the first project in the state to be associated with an overseas contractor firm, with the Keralam-based Bhageeratha Engineering and Malaysian firm PATI joining hands for the bidding. The joint venture took up works worth Rs 216 crore, mainly involving the modernisation of the main central road from the state capital of Thiruvananthapuram in the south to Angamaly in Central Keralam. The project would build the states first road designed with novel surfacing techniques. PATI-BEL began their work in December 2002 after entering into a final agreement with the then Congress-led government. IUML leader M K Muneer was the PWD minister. However, the government had handed over the project to the contractor without acquiring the land for road development. The notification for land acquisition was issued only in 2004. In October 2006, the contractor informed the government that they could not complete the work within the original deadline, citing the delay in land acquisition. As construction costs escalated, PATI-BEL demanded a 30 increase in the contract amount. The finance department, led by Thomas Isaac under the CPIM government, refused the demand and sought the World Banks permission to re-tender the work. What was the suicide case? Lee See Been, 54, was the chief project manager of the works executed by PATI-BEL. In 2006, the company submitted bills worth Rs 18 crore for payment. According to Legislative Assembly documents from 2007, PATI-BEL officials visited the ministers several times to seek payment. As the chief project manager, Lee was reportedly under pressure from subcontractors and construction material vendors who sought their dues. As the work got delayed, the Congress-led Opposition also put pressure on the CPIM government. It was the former alliance that had awarded the work to the venture. Assembly documents show Congress had demanded the company be blacklisted, following the CPIM government conceding to PATI-BELs demand for a 30 increase in project cost. It also alleged that the CPIM government had an understanding with PATI-BEL. As pressure mounted from various quarters in Keralam, Lee, who had by then returned to Malaysia, died by suicide on November 11, 2006, in Kuala Lumpur. It was reported that he had left a suicide note addressed to the company director and his wife, alleging that PWD officials had sought bribes for clearing the bills. It was also reported that the suicide note had included the name of then PWD secretary Gyanesh Kumar. The note was never made public. What did the vigilance probe find? The death spotlighted issues including bureaucratic hurdles, corruption and delays in executing public works. A month after Lees death, the CPIM government removed Kumar from his post. The government also ordered a probe by the Vigilance Bureau to examine the allegations. In a related development, the government decided to cancel the contract with PATI-BEL, as the work could not be completed within the deadline. Subsequently, the government re-tendered the work. In March 2010, then Home Minister Kodiyeri Balakrishnan, a CPIM leader, informed the Legislative Assembly that two Vigilance probes concerning the KSTP were ongoing. One was about hiring foreign consultants during 2003-04 when Congress was in power, and another probe was ordered in December 2006 a month after Beens death about lapses in KSTP work. However, the probe did not proceed. According to Congress leader Malayinkeezhu Venugopal, on whose petition Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered reopening the probe last week, the earlier investigation was torpedoed midway. Kumar, who was removed as the PWD secretary in December 2006, was not given any fresh posting in the state. He then went on central deputation to New Delhi, when the Congress-led UPA was in power. CPIM had also supported the UPA-I. What happened to the road work? In early 2007, the CPIM government cancelled the contract with PATI-BEL on the grounds that the delay in completion would invite action from the World Bank, which had funded the KSTP. Despite re-tendering, no entity came forward to bid for it. A year later, the government agreed to renew the contract with PATI-BEL itself. PATI-BEL took over the project again after the government allotted an additional Rs 72 crore apart from the original Rs 216 crore. Congress, then in Opposition, had asked the CPIM government to explain why the work was awarded to PATI-BEL when a probe was ongoing. Opposition leader Oommen Chandy had then demanded Finance Minister Thomas Isaac clarify the circumstances of the renewal, given that Isaac had demanded blacklisting of PATI-BEL when the work was delayed.

articleTitle: Centre may look at reviving jet fuel price stabilisation fund scheme amid surge in fuel costs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jet fuel prices for international flights have been reduced by 27%, bringing aviation turbine fuel (ATF) rates closer to domestic levels. (File Photo)
description: However, jet fuel prices have surged again as the conflict drags on, leading to major disruptions in global energy flows.
body_raw: With a surge in jet fuel prices in recent months hitting airlines, the government could consider a revival of the Price Stabilisation Fund PSF scheme to provide stable fuel pricing to airlines amid extreme price volatility in the international market, a senior government official said Tuesday. The Rs 10,000-crore PSF scheme was first announced in June amid soaring jet fuel prices, but lapsed after it failed to attract any airline at the time as prices moderated shortly afterwards on hopes of truce in the West Asia conflict. However, jet fuel prices have surged again as the conflict drags on, leading to major disruptions in global energy flows. Separately, Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu told reporters that the government is in discussion with airlines as well as the public sector oil marketing companies OMCs on jet fuel prices, but didnt elaborate further. The recent hike in jet fuel prices has prompted Indias largest airline IndiGo to hike fuel surcharge on flight tickets after six months, and other airlines might follow suit. Recently, the Federation of International Airlines FIA, which has IndiGo, Air India, and SpiceJet members, also urged the government to review jet fuel pricing in India and implement a cost-plus pricing model instead of the current model of international benchmark pricing. It also said that if timely relief was not made available, the airlines could be forced to withdraw from a number of unsustainable routes. It also said that jet fuel now accounts for 55-60 of airlines operational expenses, versus 30-40 earlier. Under the PSF scheme, which didnt find any takers among airlines at the time, the OMCs were to sell jet fuel to participating Indian airlines for their domestic as well as international flights at a fixed price irrespective of the price fluctuations in the international market. The OMCs were to be compensated from the Rs 10,000-crore price stabilisation fund when they incurred losses on ATF sales. When international prices fell, the OMCs gains were be used to offset the financial support that was provided to them. The government expected this arrangement, which was to be in place for up to three years, to ease the pain for the OMCs as well as Indian airlines, and rein in runaway airfares due to fuel price pressure. It was a voluntary facility only available to Indian airlines, and was to be implemented through an agreement between the airlines and the OMCs, under which the carriers had to commit to procure fuel exclusively from the OMCs for up to three years. The stable jet fuel price level under the scheme was set at Rs 115 per litre in Delhi, with price levels varying at different airports due to differences in state taxes. However, soon after the scheme was announced, prices fell below the fixed price level as global prices eased amid hopes of a resolution in the West Asia conflict. As none of the Indian carriers signed up for the scheme within the prescribed timeline, it was allowed to lapse. But with the revival and escalation of the conflict in subsequent weeks, jet fuel prices again jumped. In the latest revision on October 1, the price of jet fuel was hiked by about Rs 16 per litre to Rs 137 per litre.

articleTitle: Karnataka Asian Games gold medalists to get Rs 1 crore, 2% sports quota
articleFeaturedImageAlt: karnataka asian games
description: The hike in prize money comes amid sprinter M R Poovamma, a gold medallist in the 4x400 relay and silver medallist in the mixed relay at the Asian Games, expressing disappointment over the negligence from her home state.
body_raw: Karnataka has raised cash rewards for Asian Games 2026 medalists and announced a 2 per cent reservation for sportspersons in state government recruitment. While declaring rewards worth Rs 8 crore to Asian Games medalists, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Tuesday said that gold medalists would now receive Rs 1 crore instead of Rs 35 lakh, silver medalists Rs 75 lakh instead of Rs 25 lakh, and bronze medalists Rs 50 lakh earlier Rs 15 lakh. The announcement came during a felicitation ceremony held at Vidhana Soudha to honour the Karnataka athletes who brought laurels at the Asian Games 2026. The hike in prize money comes amid sprinter M R Poovamma, a gold medal winner in the 4x400 relay and silver medallist in the mixed relay at the Asian Games, expressing disappointment over the negligence from her home state. While other states had congratulated their Asian Games athletes for bringing glory to the country, Poovamma had stated that there was not even a single congratulatory message or call from the Karnataka government. She had also said while other states were paying medal winners in crores, Karnataka continued to pay Rs 35 lakh, which could hardly support the sportspersons to focus. Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara, who was also present at the function, said, In addition to cash rewards, each of the eight medallists will receive Rs 5 lakh as a participation incentive for competing at the Asia Games 2026. There were 20 Karnataka athletes who qualified for the Asian Games. They will be rewarded with Rs 5 lakh each. Qualifying to compete at the international level is itself a major achievement. The decision has therefore been taken to encourage not only medal winners but every Karnataka athlete who represented the state at the Games. Direct recruitment for medallists The government also announced direct recruitment to Group B posts for Asian Games and Commonwealth Games medallists. Parameshwara, who is also the Minister for Youth Empowerment and Sports, said the objective is to provide career security to athletes who bring honour to the state and the country through sporting excellence. While a 2 per cent reservation has been introduced in direct recruitment, a notification in this regard was issued on October 3, providing direct recruitment to Group-A, Group-B, Group-C and Group-D posts across all levels of the state government. Parameshwara said sportspersons should not have to worry about employment after achieving success in sports. The measure is intended not only to honour their sporting achievements but also to provide security for their future.

articleTitle: Kid in arms, man dangling from window: Tribal students say forcibly being sent home
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tribal students mumbai tilak bhavan
description: The students have alleged that since they refused to leave Mumbai, the police officials tried to push them into the buses and take them to their homes
body_raw: Hundreds of tribal students who marched into Mumbai from Nashik two days ago to press for their demands were allegedly thrown into the police bus-some with a kid in their arms, some dangling from the bus windows, and some with their legs upside down, their clothes torn in the scuffle. Pushing them inside the bus, the cops stood there, smiling. These were the visuals The Indian Express witnessed outside the Tilak Bhavan in Mumbai today on October 6. The tribal students have refused to leave Mumbai without meeting Governor Jishnu Dev Varma. The students have alleged that since they refused to leave Mumbai, the police officials tried to push them into the buses and take them to their homes, prompting an altercation between the students and the police. We have been protesting for so long in Nashik. And we began our journey to Mumbai on September 29. After walking for so many days, we are denied to meet the governor with our demands, one of the protesting students said. The police have denied detaining anyone. A bus was arranged, and the students have been taken back to their hometown. No one was detained, a senior official said. The students had earlier planned to march to the Lok Bhavan, but permission was denied. On Tuesday, there was a heavy police deployment outside the Tilak Bhavan, which is headquarters of the Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee. The students were not allowed to move out of the Tilak Bhavan. On Sunday, October 4, the Congress had alleged that the Mumbai Police entered the Congress headquarters and detained some tribal students, including women. The cops have rejected the allegations. Now the students are planning a protest at a later date. The plan is now to come back to Mumbai for a protest on October 25. All students will go back to their respective home districts in buses arranged by the Congress. Each bus will have a Congress member to ensure safety of all students, said Dhananjay Shinde from Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee.

articleTitle: For India’s ’80s kids, Jeffrey Archer was a window to the grown-up world of power and greed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jeffrey archer
description: Archer’s characters had ambition, greed, villainy, rivalries, deviousness, and love for the good life, with his stories often ending on a satisfying twist
body_raw: Before Hollywood came to our neighbourhoods, before Santa Barbara flummoxed our crammed living rooms, there was Jeffrey Archer. Accessible and dependable, churning out thrillers in book after book, putting us right there next to people in positions of power beyond our budding teenage comprehension. White House to Westminster, FBI to Mossad, within our reach, occupying pride of place on the mats of enthusiastic sellers of pirated books in Connaught Places colonnaded, post-imperialist corridors an irony to please any writers heart held aloft by indefatigable hawkers at traffic lights or jostling for space with Manohar Kahaniyan and Readers Digest at railway platform bookstalls. Pop-up libraries, functioning from crummy, dimly lit garages in DDA colonies, stocked them, friends swapped them, and us of the 80s generation got a new vocabulary that didnt seem handed or drummed down, even as parents beamed in approval at our love for reading English. This was unlike other parent-approved reading material-a big bulk of it Soviet-discounted literature-that one way or the other turned out to be a lesson in abstinence or discipline or being better. Archers characters had ambition, greed, villainy, rivalries, deviousness, and love for the good life, with his stories often ending on a satisfying twist. His women could be politicians and, yes, even the US President, run corporations and rock families, with Archer attributing it to the strong women in his own life. One of them was late British prime minister Margaret Thatcher, who was behind Archers own short-lived political career. It worked, earning Archer 14 years and five months on Britains Sunday Times bestseller lists, over five years on The New York Times bestseller lists, and sales of 300 million books worldwide. When Archer served time for perjury, for lying in a libel case against a tabloid that said he had paid a woman for sex-years after the event-it seemed just the kind of scandal that would animate one of his novels. Unsurprisingly, wife Mary Archer, a scientist in her own right, earned herself some unforgettable lines too, with the judge remarking after her testimony Has she elegance? Has she fragrance? Would she have, without the strain of this trial, radiance? Archer probably would have kept it simpler, not sound as laboured as a judge in a wig. And yet for us non-native-English speakers, he was our introduction to terms such as First Among Equals, Honour Among Thieves, and a personal favourite, A Quiver Full of Arrows. It was a cosy, warm summer when we waited for that one, the quiver holding a promise as much in its title as how our lips and teeth met over the word. And, has there ever been a title that sounded as intimate and as ambitious as Shall We Tell The President? Archer reaffirmed his position as the author whose books we took into beds, and raced through over one night, with his professed love for India. He often came to the country, had friends here, and released books in India before they premiered abroad. One reason for this was to beat the book pirates. But would he have minded the boy hawker peddling the latest Jeffrey Archer, while balancing countless other knockoffs, tapping on his car window at a traffic light? It would be a twist he would enjoy. As much as the fact that death came to him a day before the release of what would be his final book. Its title? Adam Eve. The writer is editor planning and projects, The Indian Express. shalini.langerexpressindia.com

articleTitle: At least 12 Indian sailors injured in attacks in Black Sea, Hormuz; MEA condemns
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MEA: A motorboat travels past commercial vessels appear anchored in the Strait of Hormuz
description: The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, the MEA reiterated, and urged for the earliest restoration of navigation and commerce through international waterways.
body_raw: With Indian seafarers being injured in two separate attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea, the Ministry of External Affairs MEA on Tuesday condemned the incidents and expressed deep concern over the targeting of commercial shipping. Eleven Indian crew members were injured after a Panama-flagged vessel was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. In the other incident, at least two foreign crew members were killed and some others, including an Indian, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire on a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Monday. We condemn the attack earlier today on a Panama-flagged commercial vessel, MT On Peace, off the coast of Oman, where it was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the MEA said in a statement. Of the total crew of 19, 17 are Indian nationals. It is learnt that 12 crew members have been injured, including 11 Indian nationals, it said. With the assistance of Omani authorities, the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Khasab, Oman. We thank the Omani authorities for their valuable support, it said. The MEA said the continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region remain a cause of deep concern for India. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of such attacks in the interests of peace and stability in the region, it said. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest, the MEA said. In the other incident, the Indian Embassy in Romania reported that there were three Indian nationals among the crew members and one of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties foreign nationals while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members, the mission posted on X. It said all three Indians are safe and in good health. We condemn the attack on MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea in which two foreign seafarers were killed and some members of the crew, including Indian nationals, injured. The injured have been rescued by Romanian authorities and are receiving medical attention. The three Indian nationals, who were part of the crew, are safe. We thank Romanian authorities for their swift action in this incident, the MEA said. India views these attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers with grave concern, it said. The targeting of traffic in international waterways is severely undermining global commerce and welfare of people across the world. We continue to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts. Indian seafarers account for almost 12 per cent of the global maritime community. According to sources, at least nine Indian seafarers have died, one is presumed dead, and seven have been injured since the start of the West Asia crisis, until July this year. There have been at least 29 incidents of attacks on vessels carrying Indian seafarers - four involving Indian-flagged vessels and the rest involving foreign-flagged vessels. In the Black Sea, too, Indian seafarers have been victims of attacks from both Russia and Ukraine. In fact, India started actively pushing for Russia-Ukraine peace after Indian seafarers were hit by such attacks. In September 2026, India and Liberia launched a 25-nation Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers during the UN General Assembly to ensure safety and security of merchant crews and commercial shipping against targeted attacks, the MEA said. With PTI, London

articleTitle: What the 2026 Physics Nobel winner has done: Capturing messengers from space in ice
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Physics Nobel
description: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026: What exactly are neutrinos, why do we need ice to observe them, and why observe them at all? We explain.
body_raw: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 After the Medicine Nobel went to scientists who discovered a way to control the brain using light, the Physics Nobel, announced on Tuesday October 6, also involves light. Francis Halzen has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Born on March 23, 1944 in Belgium, Halzen is affiliated with the University of WisconsinMadison, Madison, USA. What exactly are neutrinos, why do we need ice to observe them, and why observe them at all? We explain. What is a neutrino? A neutrino is a subatomic particle with no electric charge and almost no mass. The Nobel Prize official release calls it the shyest particle in the universe, because it passes through matter almost without a trace. Every second, 65 billion neutrinos from the Sun pass through our bodies, and we do not notice. Neutrinos are produced in enormous numbers by the Sun, exploding stars, nuclear reactions and radioactive decay. The same processes also produce protons, but because protons carry electric charge, their paths change by the time scientists can study them. Neutrinos interact so little with the world around them that studying the particles can give scientists a window into the processes that created them. Neutrinos also come from other regions of space, carrying clues to some of the mysteries of the cosmos. Researchers that succeed in capturing these rarer cosmic neutrinos can then extract information about the extreme environments in the universe where they originated, as the Nobel release says. However, the same reason that makes neutrinos important to study also makes them difficult to detect - they pass through matter leaving almost no trace. Enter Francis Halzen. Francis Halzens idea use the Antarctic ice In the 1980s, Francis Halzen realised that glacial ice at the South Pole could serve as a giant detector of neutrinos. On the rare occasion that a neutrino collides with an atomic nucleus, it can produce a charged particle that emits a faint blue light as it travels through the ice. If the material is transparent, sensors can detect that light and, from the pattern of light, infer the direction from which the neutrino came. What matters most is having a large enough volume of the interceptor material, to catch many collisions. Ice has several advantages at depth, the darkness is constant, so it is easy to see flashes of light unlike the ocean, there is no interference from living creatures. In the Antarctic, radioactivity is low, the ice is stable, and the area has no earthquakes. Also, when Halzen first floated the idea, a research station with regular transport already existed there. The drawback was that practical work was only possible in the brief Antarctic summer, between November and February. Halzen first presented the concept with John G Learned in 1988. Interest in the idea kept growing, and researchers from various institutions gathered around Halzen to build such an observatory. Building the IceCube observatory Glaciologists showed the team that hot water, delivered through a sophisticated shower head, can melt kilometre-deep holes. Strings of light sensors, which Halzen describes as a lightbulb in reverse, were then lowered into them. The sensors capture light and turn it into an electrical signal. The first attempts were disappointing, because bubbles in the upper ice scattered the light. Below 1,400 metres, however, the ice proved extremely pure and transparent, and light could travel 300 metres before being absorbed. The first observatory, AMANDA, worked as intended but was not big enough. Its successor, IceCube, is a cubic kilometre of ice with 5,160 light sensors on 86 cables, completed in 2011. Halzen carried both projects from idea to results as principal investigator. What has IceCube since done? IceCube must pick out cosmic neutrinos from an enormous background. Over a hundred million particles from the atmosphere above Antarctica register every day, and a few hundred atmospheric neutrinos a day reach IceCube after travelling through the Earth. The team looks at selected events and checks whether, taken together, their properties match cosmic neutrinos rather than atmospheric ones. In 2013, they reported the first evidence of high-energy neutrinos from astrophysical sources subsequent data strengthened the result. The neutrino has thus helped physicists confirm their models of the processes inside the Sun and what happens inside a supernova. The idea behind IceCube is to take neutrino astronomy to a new level, the hope being that neutrinos will provide information about phenomena that are hidden behind dust clouds, or objects that are so distant that other forms of radiation have disappeared along the way. The aim is to gain knowledge that cannot be obtained in any other way, the Nobel release says. What comes next Scientists hope to establish sources of neutrinos that come towards the Earth. A few potential sources have been found by IceCube, of which one is the active galaxy NGC 1068 also called M77. Of the neutrinos registered in IceCube, 79 appear to come from the direction of this galaxy. However, this evidence is not robust enough to definitively identify NGC 1068 as a neutrino source the more neutrinos that are captured by the sensors, the greater the chance of being able to find their origin, the release says. Put very simply, IceCube gives us a better idea of our universe. As the observatorys website says, IceCube is fundamental research, and pure exploratory research usually leads to other astounding discoveries. As IceCube gives us new ways to study the mysteries of our universe, it is likely to uncover or lead to the discovery of things we couldnt have anticipated. For example, roughly 4 of our universe is made up of regular matter like atoms and molecules. The other 96 of our universe is made of a material we cant see and that we barely understand. It is composed of dark matter 23 and dark energy 73. Neutrinos may give us a better understanding of dark matter and dark energy.

articleTitle: Christa Pike case exposes the myth of ‘humane’ execution
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This photo provided by the Tennessee Department of Correction shows Christa Pike
description: Surely, there comes a time when even the constitutional state, having attempted and failed to end human life lawfully, acknowledges the boundaries of its authority
body_raw: It is hard to find a more surreal turn of events than what befell Christa Pike in Tennessee. The state prepared to execute her and gave her two doses of pentobarbital, but she survived. She was then taken from the prison to a hospital by ambulance, where doctors immediately began working to preserve her life, contrary to the states recent actions. Pikes attorneys stated that medical personnel were attempting to remove the drug from her body. The woman found guilty of the horrific 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer was reported to be unconscious, critically ill, and on a ventilator. This represents a troubling confrontation between the two sides of the contemporary state. In one place, authorities apply chemicals intended to cause death, whereas in another, medical professionals employ their expertise and technology to preserve that same life. If Pike recovers, an even stranger question emerges Can the state then prepare to execute someone its medical system has just fought to save? To make this an issue of sympathy for Pike would miss the point. Her crime was appalling. No serious discussion of capital punishment should diminish Colleen Slemmers suffering or disregard the claims of victims and their families. The moral challenge of the death penalty stems exactly from the fact that the crimes are often so horrific. The question, however, is What can a constitutional state do once guilt is confirmed? American law has faced this dilemma before, if not under these circumstances. Willie Francis survived an attempt to execute him in the electric chair by the state of Louisiana, because there was a malfunction of equipment in 1946. The US Supreme Court in Francis vs Resweber 1947 held that a botched execution was accidental and not a separate punishment, thus permitting a second attempt. However, Justice Felix Frankfurter added a crucial caveat A series of abortive attempts might create what he called an altogether different constitutional problem. That warning deserves renewed attention. However, the question is not simply whether Tennessee could still go forward and put Pike to death. By this I mean If a life is extinguished multiple times, does that change the very nature of what punishment means? A court has the authority to impose the death penalty. The state does not automatically gain an unlimited licence to keep trying to cause death until it succeeds. Punishment involves not only its intended outcome but also the actual suffering imposed on the condemned person. Expose someone to the fear of death, invasive treatments, deadly chemicals, severe medical outcomes, and emergency care, then force her to endure the whole ordeal again, and the experience takes on a different character from the initial punishment declared. Now that the condemned has reached deaths door and been gravely injured again, what purpose does it serve to bring her there a second time? One might ask When does administering justice become a demand for a deed to be performed? Foucault identified another paradox. Discipline and Punish laid out how punishment moved away from the public spectacle of bodily suffering - it became bureaucratic, regulated, and increasingly invisible. The transformation could end in a lethal injection Sovereign violence erased once more, disguised as clinical peace delivered through limp plastic tubing. Pikes survival shreds that clean, polished facade. That also hints at the more profound contradiction of contemporary capital punishment. Lethal injection owes its acceptance, in part, to medicalisation. A prisoner is positioned on what appears to be a hospital gurney. Death looks like the evisceration of a grotesque tumour. However, medicine and execution have utterly opposite moral foundations. Medicine interposes itself to preserve life or ease suffering, while execution is an intervention that can only remove a life. The Pike case also unsettles the reassuring language of humane or painless executions. The US Supreme Court ruled that the Eighth Amendment does not ensure a painless death. To put it another way, prisoners face a tough standard when contesting execution protocols. Nevertheless, Pikes situation is not just about faulty needles or incorrect dosing. The question is whether any institution deliberately created to kill can genuinely attain the moral standing of a routine medical procedure. By the close of 2025, 113 countries had completely abolished capital punishment for all offences. In contrast, the US carried out 47 executions that year, marking its highest yearly total since 2009. In a nutshell, wherever it is found in constitutional democracies, the continued use of capital punishment is becoming increasingly unusual. The reason the state holds a monopoly on legitimate violence is to substitute personal revenge for impartial justice. Yet, by intentionally ending that life, the state risks mirroring that inflexibility, preventing any chance for remorse, restoration, or remedy. As you read this, Tennessee faces the question of whether to pursue Pikes execution again. In the end, the law will probably permit this. Nonetheless, legality is not the only form of justice. Surely, there comes a time when even the constitutional state, having attempted and failed to end human life lawfully, acknowledges the boundaries of its authority, as sovereignty can also be demonstrated through restraint - the ability not only to wield its immense power but also to understand when and how to stop. The writer is professor, Jadavpur University

description: The Board has also stated that candidates must have 75 per cent attendance for appearing in the written and practical examinations.
body_raw: The Punjab School Education Board PSEB has released the schedule for filling examination forms and depositing examination fees for the Punjab Board Class 10 and 12 board exams 2027. The examinations are scheduled to be conducted in February-March 2027. The schedule applies to regular students of government, recognised, affiliated and associated schools. Schools can begin generating examination forms and paying fees from October 5, 2026. The examination fee for a regular Class 10 candidate is Rs 2,000, including Rs 1,650 examination fee and Rs 350 towards the hard copy and digitised soft copy. An additional subject fee of Rs 550 per subject will apply where applicable. For Class 12, the examination fee is Rs 2,450, comprising Rs 2,050 examination fee and Rs 400 for the hard copy and digitised soft copy. The additional subject fee is Rs 550 per subject. Particulars Class 10 Class 12 Examination fee Rs 1,650 Rs 2,050 Hard copy digitised soft copy Rs 350 Rs 400 Total examination fee Rs 2,000 Rs 2,450 Additional subject fee Rs 550 per subject Rs 550 per subject Punjab Board 10th, 12th registration dates 2027 Schools can submit examination forms and fees online or generate a bank challan for offline payment. The last date to submit forms and pay the fee without a late fee is October 23, 2026. Thereafter, candidates will have to pay a late fee of Rs 500, Rs 1,000, Rs 1,500 or Rs 2,000 depending on the date of submission. articleTitle: ‘Bulli Bai’ auction app case: Engineering student discharged; court says ‘no evidence’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: bulli bai student discharged
description: 'Bulli Bai' was allegedly a mock auction app made to upload photos of Muslim women with objectionable comments.
body_raw: A magistrate court has discharged a 25-year-old engineering student who was arrested in 2022 in connection with the Bulli Bai auction app case. While discharging the student, the court observed that there is no evidence that he was involved in the creation of the Bulli Bai app or shared photographs of the women. Bulli Bai was allegedly a mock auction app made to upload photos of Muslim women with objectionable comments. Vishal Jha, who was then an engineering student at a Bengaluru institute, was the first person to be arrested in the case by the Mumbai Police. It is, however, not known if Jha is still a student. Seeking to be cleared in the case, Jhas lawyer said that the only allegation against him in the chargesheet is that he had shared and followed the app. On this, the court said this in itself is not an offence. .admittedly, the role of the present applicant is that he followed the..App and he was in contact with the co-accused. In the case cited. the Honble Allahabad High Court held that following the page on the website is not an offence. In the present case, the applicant followed.the App. There is no further role attributed by the prosecution against him. So, following the App in view of the above-mentioned judgment is not an offence, Judicial Magistrate Court R T Ingle said. In April, the court had rejected the discharge plea of another accused, Mayank Rawat, noting that prima facie there is proof that he had outraged the modesty of women by downloading the photographs of the Muslim women from their social media accounts and posting them on the app. The cyber cell unit of the Bandra Kurla Complex had filed a complaint under sections including 153 a promoting enmity between two groups, 295 a deliberate acts to outrage religious feelings, 354 d stalking, 500 defamation, and 509 insulting modesty of a woman of the Indian Penal Code and relevant sections of the Information Technology Act. Discharging Jha, the court said that while there is evidence that he was in touch with some of the co-accused, that in itself is not evidence of his involvement. But, in entire charge-sheet, there is no further role of the present applicant which would show that, he either created said App or the help co-accused in creating it. Even there is no allegation that he shared photographs of Muslim women, the court said.

articleTitle: As Rahul protests in Delhi, criticism from Telangana: KTR calls him coward and bully
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Manne Krishank arrest
description: Attacks Congress leader over arrest of BRS leader who had criticised Telangana CM Revanth Reddy.
body_raw: Bharat Rashtra Samithis working president KT Rama Rao has lashed out at Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi in connection with the arrest of BRS leader Manne Krishank. Telangana police have arrested Krishank in connection with his posts and press conference against Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy. Krishank had accused Reddy of amassing disproportionate wealth after he became CM of the Congress-led government in 2023. Mr Rahul Gandhi wants to be Prime Minister, but acts like a coward, a bully and an undemocratic human. He preaches the Constitution, yet runs anarchy in Telangana through his puppet Revanth Reddy and encourages defections. He shouts vote chori on the streets, but made Telanganas biggest vote-chor, the original vote-for-note peddler, the Chief Minister. He can make baseless allegations against anyone. But when BRS leader Krishank Manne questioned the Anumula familys corruption with proof, he gets arrested, Rao claimed on X. Rein in your puppet, Rahul. Stop making a mockery of the Indian Constitution. KTRs attack on Rahul Gandhi and Reddy comes after the latter visited KTRs Assembly constituency, Sircilla, on October 1 and accused TRS national president and KTRs father, K Chandrashekar Rao or KCR, of amassing disproportionate wealth during the BRS regime between 2014 and 2023. In Sircilla, Reddy said that the KCR family looted Telangana at the expense of its people. Soon after this, a series of BRS leaders issued statements against Reddy and his family, accusing them of amassing ill-gotten wealth. BRS leader Krishank on October 3 claimed that the CMs daughter, Naimisha Reddy, is linked to pharmaceutical companies, which is why Reddy is pushing for a pharma city at the expense of the people. He also said an Enforcement Directorate probe should be ordered into the alleged business interests, assets, investments and financial transactions of the CM and his family members.

After completing the practice, Vidyut explained that he had used a technique from the Patanjali Yoga Sutras. He also revealed that the practice has helped him achieve several milestones in his life and that he teaches the technique to youngsters.
