articleTitle: He went to Russia to study. Rs 3 lakh visa took him to Ukraine war zone instead
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab man Russia Ukraine war
description: After losing his parents, Patiala yoga teacher Gagandeep Singh did not want to live alone. He chose to move to Russia, a decision that would land him on the frontlines of the Russia-Ukraine war.
body_raw: For nearly a year, Gagandeep Singh lived by two rules look up for drones, look down for mines. The 35-year-old yoga teacher from Punjabs Patiala had travelled to Russia on a student visa, hoping for a better life. Instead, he found himself on the frontlines of the Russia-Ukraine war, watching fellow soldiers die, and fighting to stay alive. When the danger became extreme, I contacted my sister and sought help, Singh, who returned to India in August, recalled. Singh says he was content working as a yoga teacher at the Government Ayurvedic College and Hospital in Patiala, earning around Rs 26,000 a month. But the death of his parents devastated him. Its then that he decided to move abroad. There was one major constraint he could not afford to go to a European country. Russia, however, was within his means. So, with the help of a Bathinda-based travel agent, Singh says he managed to secure admission to Moscow State Linguistic University, one of Russias largest linguistic universities, and left for Moscow in May 2025 on a one-year student visa. The expenses were about Rs 3 lakh. How Singhs plan fell through His plan was simple learn Russian and work part-time to support himself. He believed knowing the language would help him understand people better and find work in Russia. For around three months in Moscow, he attended classes and worked part-time as a delivery worker. Then a fellow student told him about a job with the Russian Army. Singh says he was offered a good salary and told that the work involved building bunkers and other support duties-not fighting on the battlefield. He agreed. Singh says he, along with around two dozen men from India, signed a contract with the Russian Army and underwent two months of military training. The recruits were made to run, undergo weapons and firing practice, and learn to build bunkers. Their salaries started coming into their Russian accounts, but their phones, Singh says, were taken away. Then the recruits were moved towards Ukraine, bags full of arms and ammunition. On the frontlines of the Ukraine war Around 100 men were left in different groups in different forested areas along the Russia-Ukraine border. We thought it was bunker work, Singh says. He found himself moving through forests with a Russian commander, fellow Indian Inderjit Singh from Kolkata, and two men from other countries. Drones constantly flew overhead, while mines and explosives lay scattered across the ground. It was like walking on our deathbed, he recalls. Food was scarce. He says he was able to bathe only two or three times during the entire period. One by one, the people around him disappeared. Inderjit died. So did the Russian commander and the two other men. Eventually, Singh says, he was alone. He says he spent nearly 11 months in jungles and war-affected areas, eventually reaching close to Kyiv. His right foot and a hand were badly injured during an attack. While under Russian military care, he received some medical aid, but after returning home he underwent an operation. A call for help, an MP steps up Singh kept the truth from his family. They knew he had gone to Russia on a student visa, but not that he had ended up in Ukraine. After he contacted his sister, Singhs family took up the matter with Rajya Sabha MP Baba Balbir Singh Seechewal, who appealed to men not to get trapped by such enticements. The matter was subsequently taken up with the Ministry of External Affairs, which intervened. The Russian authorities were contacted and Singh eventually returned to India on August 26. Back home after surviving a war he never chose to fight, Singh says he only desires the simple things a yoga mat, a classroom, and a normal day.

articleTitle: Lionel Messi farewell match: When, where and how to watch Argentina vs Benin?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lionel Messi will play his last game for Argentina against Benin. (Reuters)
description: The 39-year-old brings the curtain down on a glittering international career at the Estadio Mas Monumental in Buenos Aires on Wednesday
body_raw: Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on a glittering international football career when Argentina take on Benin in a friendly at the Estadio Mas Monumental in Buenos Aires on Wednesday. The match, being dubbed the Last Tango, kicks off at 430 AM IST and will see the 39-year-old lead out La Albiceleste one last time in front of a packed house, with members of Argentinas FIFA World Cup 2022-winning squad and their families on hand to mark the occasion. Messi announced his retirement from international football on August 31, a little over two months after Argentinas FIFA World Cup 2026 final defeat to Spain in New Jersey. The Argentine Football Association tempted him to make one last appearance for the farewell he deserves, and thousands of fans are expected at the Estadio Monumental to show their appreciation. The AFA said the match will transcend sports and be full of emotion. ALSO READ Lionel Messis international retirement Football loses a part of its soul Messi is the most decorated figure in Argentine football history, having made 207 appearances, scored 125 goals and provided 68 assists, all records for La Albiceleste. His roll of honours includes the Beijing 2008 Olympic gold medal, the FIFA World Cup 2022 title, back-to-back Copa America trophies in 2021 and 2024, and the 2022 Finalissima. He appeared in a record-tying six World Cups alongside his great rival Cristiano Ronaldo. Alongside Messi, veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi is also set to hang up his boots, while midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso could also be seen in the Argentina shirt for the final time, according to reports. Argentina are currently ranked world No. 2, while Benin are 89th, coached by Gernot Rohr, who led Nigeria at the FIFA World Cup 2018. Messi posted pictures on social media of him arriving to join the national team for the last time and his final training sessions. Special moments I know I will miss, he wrote. He briefly retired from Argentina duty in 2016 before enjoying his most successful period with the national team, winning the Copa Americas in 2021 and 2024 as well as the 2022 World Cup. He continues at club level with Inter Miami, where he recently won the Campeones Cup, his fourth trophy with the team. Messi Final Match - All you need to know When will Messi play his last game for Argentina? Messi will play his final match for Argentina on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. The match kicks off at 430 AM IST. Who will Messi play against in his final game? Messi will face Benin in the friendly, with the African side ranked 89th in the world and coached by Gernot Rohr. Where will Messis last game for Argentina take place? The match will be played at the Estadio Mas Monumental in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Where to watch Lionel Messis last match in India? Live streaming of the Argentina vs Benin friendly will be available on ZEE5. There is no live telecast of the match on any TV channel in India.

articleTitle: Bank of Baroda fined Rs 2 lakh for hiding interest-saving scheme from Army officer
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bank of Baroda Loan indian army home loan
description: The 51-year-old Indian Army officer took a home loan from Bank of Baroda in 2012 and claimed that the bank did not inform him of relevant schemes.
body_raw: A Haryana consumer commission ordered Bank of Baroda to pay Rs 2.10 lakh to a serving Indian Army officer after finding that the bank failed to inform him about a facility that could have reduced the interest burden on his home loan. The commission held that the banks failure to apprise him of the facility, despite his request for information on ways to reduce his loan burden, amounted to deficiency in service. President Nagender Singh Kadian, along with Dr Tripti Pannu and Dr Vijender Singh of the Rohtak District Consumer Commission, was hearing the complaint filed by a 51-year-old man, a serving Indian Army officer holding the rank of Brigadier, who took a home loan of Rs 42 lakh in 2012. The complainant was deprived of an opportunity to take an informed financial decision regarding his existing housing loan because the relevant facility was not brought to his notice despite his stated request to the Bank officials. The deficiency on the part of the bank Bank of Baroda has consequently caused financial prejudice as well as inconvenience and mental agony to the complainant, the September 9 order read. No scheme communicated by bank The complainant, a Brigadier in the Indian Army, along with his wife, took a housing loan of Rs 42 lakh in 2012 from the Bank of Baroda. The loan was disbursed in instalments and was fully disbursed by 2016. The complainant also claimed that since he is a serving Indian Army officer, he had to remain posted at different places over the years. He added that he frequently visited the bank branch and regularly interacted with branch managers and other staff. The complainant claimed that he regularly expressed his desire to the bank staff to be informed about schemes or options that could reduce the interest burden on his loan. He moved the commission alleging that he had suffered a loss in interest payments which could have been saved if the bank had timely informed him. Aggrieved, he moved the commission alleging that he had suffered a huge loss in the payment of interest levied on his loan account, which could have been saved if the bank had timely informed him. He added that the Bank of Baroda had launched the advantage fund facility in 2015, under which money kept in a linked savings account could provide corresponding interest relief on the principal outstanding on the home loan, but the bank allegedly did not inform him about it. He further claimed that, as a customer, he was entitled to relevant information about facilities connected to his existing loan and that the bank failed to provide such information despite his request. The complainant was represented by advocate Savita Dalal before the commission. Banks defence The Bank of Baroda, through advocate Pardeep Ahlawat, submitted that new schemes were publicised through its website, social media platforms, branches and other modes. It also submitted that whenever the complainant enquired about the banks schemes, the information was provided to him. The bank denied that the complainant had suffered the alleged loss. Duty towards existing customers The commission noted that the Bank of Baroda had pleaded that new schemes were publicised through its website, social media platforms, branch displays and other modes. However, it held that mere general publicity of a beneficial banking facility could not completely absolve the bank of its obligation towards an existing customer who had specifically sought information on ways to reduce his interest burden. A consumer may not reasonably be expected to possess knowledge of every scheme, circular or facility introduced by a banking institution, the commission observed. The commission clarified that the banks obligation was not to individually communicate every promotional offer to every customer, but to provide relevant and material information to a customer whose existing financial relationship with the bank was directly connected with the facility and who had specifically sought such information. The commission held that the Bank of Barodas failure to apprise the complainant about the facility amounted to deficiency in service. Accordingly, itdirected Bank of Baroda to pay Rs 2 lakh as lump-sum compensation, Rs 5,000 for deficiency in service and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses, taking the total to Rs 2.10 lakh. Takeaway This ruling highlights that banks may be required to provide relevant and material information about loan-related facilities to existing customers who specifically seek information that could help reduce their interest burden. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Haryana helpline 1800-180-2087 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Cross-voting to 2027 polls: Why Akhilesh dropped plan to put up third RS candidate
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also alleged that poor people were being defrauded of their land in Ayodhya. (File Photo)
description: Samajwadi Party's last-minute move paves way for its two nominees and BJP’s eight candidates to get elected unopposed in October 16 UP Rajya Sabha polls
body_raw: Days after indicating that it would field its third candidate for the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party SP decided against the move Tuesday, the last day of filing nominations, paving the way for the partys two nominees and the ruling BJPs eight candidates to get elected to the Upper House unopposed. The SPs last-minute decision was driven by a combination of factors involved in its attempts to cobble together the numbers needed for a third candidates win, with the high-stakes state Assembly elections just over four months away. SP president and ex-UP chief minister Akhilesh Yadavs rethink on the matter came a day after senior party MLA Ravidas Mehrotra indicated that the party had completed formalities to put up its third candidate for the Upper House polls for 10 vacant seats from UP. On Tuesday morning, however, Akhilesh, in an X post, said, Now our eyes are not on three but on 403 seats, signalling that the party has shifted its focus to the Assembly polls due in February 2027. His move, ending week-long political suspense, made it clear that there would not be any contest between the BJP and the SP for the Rajya Sabha polls now. The BJP and the SP have enough numbers to comfortably win seven and two seats respectively. SPs calculations The SP has already fielded party general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who is seeking his sixth term in the Rajya Sabha, and Reliance executive Dhananjay Nathwani. Nathwani, 40, is the son of Parimal Nathwani, Director, Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent in the June 2026 election, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. Currently, there are 396 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, with each Rajya Sabha candidate requiring 37 first-preference votes to win. The SP has 101 MLAs. However, its effective strength is 100 as Chail MLA Puja Pal, who continues to figure in the House records as an SP member, has switched to the BJP and is currently its state vice-president. With the support of two Congress MLAs, the SP has 102 votes-nine short of the first-preference votes required to ensure the victory of its third candidate. SP sources said that the partys calculations following the BJPs decision to field its eighth candidate became a key factor in the SPs rethink. Some BJP MLAs were in touch with the SP but showed hesitance to rebel openly months before polls, sources claimed. BJP play The BJP has 255 MLAs with its NDA allies adding another 33 members Apna Dal S 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. With the support of Puja Pal, unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh-who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls-and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDAs effective tally stands at 294-just two short of the required 296 37 for each first-preference votes to ensure a win for all its eight candidates. The BJP named its eight candidates Monday, dropping Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma from its list. Its nominees include Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar. Assembly poll factor The BJP appears confident of managing the two additional votes required for its eighth candidate, even as the possibility of cross-voting by some NDA MLAs is not ruled out within the ruling camp too. The presence of the third SP nominee would have led to a contest for the election of 11 candidates for 10 seats. This would have led to cross-voting among the MLAs, which would have favoured the BJP more, said an SP insider. Considering the vindictive nature of the ruling camp, several of its legislators despite being unhappy were hesitant and even fearful to reveal themselves at this stage. We decided to respect their decision and instead aim for the bigger target of the 2027 elections, the party insider said. For the SP, the numbers game was tighter. Its leaders said that in the final analysis, while the party required at least nine additional first-preference votes to push through its third nominee, the BJP needed only two additional votes to secure the victory of its eighth candidate. Thus the arithmetic made the extra-candidate gamble considerably more difficult for the SP than the BJP, especially given the nature of voting in the Rajya Sabha polls. Unlike a conventional secret ballot, the Rajya Sabha elections use an open-ballot system for the MLAs, who are required to show their marked ballots to an authorised party agent. The SP leaders said this made it difficult to rely on cross-voting by even those NDA MLAs who it claimed were in touch with them. With the Assembly elections round the corner, several MLAs were said to be unwilling to risk open defiance of their parties at this stage, when the candidate selection for the 2027 polls has yet to get underway.

articleTitle: Why Anthropic is turning to religion to shape Claude’s values, and asking if AI can be conscious
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anthropic, Christopher Olah at the Vatican
description: As AI systems tackle more complex questions, Anthropic is drawing on religious and philosophical thinking to shape Claude’s behaviour. But could such a system itself be conscious and deserve moral consideration?
body_raw: As it prepares for an IPO that could value it at 2 trillion, Anthropic is in the spotlight for meetings it held this summer with religious leaders. The Washington Post reported in April that the company had invited 15 Catholic and Protestant leaders to guide Claudes moral and spiritual development as the LLM encounters increasingly complex ethical questions. Weeks later, Anthropic co-founder Christopher Olah was present when Pope Leo unveiled his encyclical on artificial intelligence, Magnifica Humanitas, which warns against the blind adoption of AI, emphasises the primacy of the human person and rejects the idea that AI can replace or surpass humanity. The New York Times last week reported that these engagements, and several more, were part of a broader effort by Anthropic with two distinct aims to draw on religious and philosophical traditions to shape Claudes moral character, and to convince participants to seriously consider whether AI systems might themselves be conscious and deserving of moral consideration. Current AI systems can produce strikingly human-like language and behaviour, but there is no scientific consensus that they are conscious, or an agreed test for determining machine consciousness. Over the weekend, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he was very uncomfortable with ascribing religious power to AI models, while Google DeepMind researcher Jon Barron urged researchers to focus on actual humans rather than elevating the moral standing of AI systems. Anthropic is increasingly turning to religious leaders and philosophers for help thinking about what its systems should value, even as some of the industrys most powerful figures warn against treating AI itself as a source of moral or religious authority. That matters because people are already turning to these systems for advice, information and even moral or spiritual guidance. The values built into them can shape the answers people get and the judgements they make. According to The Economist, religious queries accounted for roughly 5 of millions of publicly released chatbot conversations analysed by CEFE AI. Why is Anthropic talking to religious thinkers? Anthropic has long positioned itself as the safety-focused AI company. Its efforts to shape Claudes behaviour have evolved from an internal memo dubbed the Soul Document to an 84-page constitution published this January, setting out the principles Claude is expected to follow. But questions about what kind of character an AI system should have quickly move beyond technical safeguards. They touch on morality, personhood, consciousness and human relationships, all questions that religious and philosophical traditions have debated for centuries. That made religious and philosophical traditions a natural place for Anthropic to look as it began asking what consciousness or moral worth might mean for an AI system, and what obligations could follow. None of that settles whether current AI systems are actually conscious. Mark Coeckelbergh, a philosopher of technology and professor at the University of Vienna, told The Indian Express that this move was an attempt to make sense of human-like technology. Its part of a broader tendency to try to understand what happens when we have an advanced technology that seems human-like or, according to some, gets increasingly divine qualities such as omniscience. The Vatican has grappled with similar questions a 2023 volume produced by scholars working with its Centre for Digital Culture examined AI through personhood, consciousness and human relationships with advanced systems. Coeckelbergh also cautioned that this messaging may go beyond understanding AI and help a company occupy a certain market position. Its important to see that this is not just a question of understanding AI. Its also rhetoric in the service of their business. Some Big Tech leaders intentionally use religious language to draw attention to their technologies and attract investments, Coeckelbergh told The Indian Express. What did the people in the room think was at stake? This is also where Anthropics effort to shape Claudes values began to run into a different question whether Claude itself might deserve moral consideration. Mois Navon, a rabbi and professor of ethics in AI at Ben Gurion University, Israel, who was invited to a meeting with Olah in April, said Anthropic was seeking feedback from different wisdom traditions on the Constitution that sets out Claudes moral framework. I submitted to them a 35-page critique from my traditions perspective. In addition, they were interested in hearing what kind of character would be best for Claude to have in order to fulfil its role in society. That said, the discussions drifted to what would be good for Claude itself, Navon told The Indian Express. In the critique, Navon argues that morality cannot simply be reduced to a list of rules Claude would need to exercise moral judgement within a framework of values. He also raises a more basic question about Anthropics attempt to cultivate human-like qualities in the model whose values? Charles Camosy, professor of medical humanities at Creighton University and another participant in Anthropics consultations, offered a more cautious account of the meetings. He said the discussions were broader than the question of Claudes moral status and that he did not feel participants were being steered towards any particular conclusion about AI consciousness. I dont think its fair to say that they wanted any one thing in particular. Some of the social media chatter is suggesting that the people we interacted with were trying to manipulate us or push us into thinking a certain way about Claudes moral status. That is not true. in multiple ways, Camosy told The Indian Express. Navon, however, said that once the discussion turned to Claude itself, Anthropics representatives appeared to be treating the possibility of consciousness as more than a remote hypothetical. They Olah and his colleagues at Anthropic said that they had observed internal behaviours that mimicked human behaviour to such an extent that they called them weird, and implied that, in their minds, there was a very high probability that Claude is conscious. Accordingly, they discussed its welfare, Navon told The Indian Express. Why does moral status matter, and who gets to choose the values? If an AI system were conscious, that would not automatically settle how humans ought to treat it. The next question is whether it has moral status, meaning whether it deserves moral consideration in its own right. In practical terms, that means asking whether it can be harmed or whether humans could owe it duties. Camosy said that after considering the question seriously, he did not think current AI systems possess significant moral status. When you first experience what contemporary models can do . many can be gobsmacked or taken aback at first. But when I went back to foundational principles about what consciousness is and where it comes from . it became clear that these models do not have a significant moral status, Camosy said. Navon took Anthropics premise in the opposite direction. If the company believed Claude might be conscious and therefore capable of being harmed, he argued, it also had to confront what it meant to make such a system work for humans. Anthropic acknowledged the moral problem but said, All the AI labs are doing it. At least we are being nice to ours. That is when I responded with what was quoted in part by The New York Times So you are nice slave owners. I think you should be fighting the South and freeing the slaves, Navon told The Indian Express. But even if Claude has no moral status, the question of what values it should embody remains. Anthropic is already making those choices. That question has already surfaced in Anthropics standoff with the US government over who gets to decide how its models can be used. Coeckelbergh warned that values embedded in AI systems can be exported globally with the technology. If most of these models are made by US companies, then of course they are going to reflect US values. That means we risk a kind of tech colonialism, where those values are exported through the technology, he told The Indian Express. At least if companies are explicit about the religious or philosophical values they are drawing on, there is something to discuss and contest. But this cannot remain in the hands of a few companies. It needs to be democratised. Camosy, however, drew a distinction between the moral status of the models and the effect our treatment of them may have on us. I do think the question remains about what kind of people we want to be in relation to the models. But thats a different kind of question from the ones asking whether the models themselves have a significant moral status or capability of being harmed, he said.

articleTitle: ED summons Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s brother-in-law in graft case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Defector MPs to dissenting MLAs: How AAP cracks widen on eve of Punjab polls
description: Grewal is associated with the Punjabi film industry and is linked to East Sunshine Production Pvt. Ltd. The company’s corporate records list Amardeep Grewal Singh as one of its directors.
body_raw: The Enforcement Directorate ED on Tuesday summoned Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns brother-in-law Amardeep Singh Grewal in connection with its probe into the alleged corrupt practices by senior officials linked to the Chief Ministers Office including cash for transfers and cash for getting favourable policies. ED had initially issued summons to Grewal for October 7, but following an appeal, he has been asked to appear at the federal agencys Delhi office on October 9, a source privy to the developments said. Grewal is associated with the Punjabi film industry and is linked to East Sunshine Production Pvt. Ltd. The companys corporate records list Grewal as one of its directors. He has been associated with various Punjabi films, including Maujaan Hi Maujaan 2023 and Snowman 2022, having overseas productionrelease linkages, an ED official said. On Monday, a the Punjab and Haryana High Court ordered the CBI to register an FIR and investigate the allegations of corruption against Punjab government officials, Rajbir Singh Ghuman an officer to special duty OSD to CM, saying the material shared by the ED prima facie substantiated the commission of cognisable offences. The Punjab government on Tuesday challenged the order in the Supreme Court. The high court order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who sought a CBI probe into issues raised by the ED in a letter sent to Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav. The petition contended that the allegations raised serious questions about the state governments functioning and warranted an independent investigation outside the Punjab Police and Vigilance Bureau. In its communication to the DGP, the had agency sought registration of a criminal case against Ghuman and his alleged associates, Nitin Gohal and Bir Devinder. According to the communication, the three allegedly interfered in the transfer and posting of government officials, government work and tender processes. The agency also referred to material purportedly indicating attempts to influence postings, access confidential government documents and interfere in administrative approvals and other official processes.

articleTitle: Cabinet greenlights new apex body to oversee transport and logistics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RELIEF scheme exporters India
description: The Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority aims to reduce costs, and meet the government’s Vision 2047 targets
body_raw: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the constitution of an Integrated Transport Logistics Authority ITLA to have a synergy among different transport departments and assess the countrys future requirements in infrastructure development. The authority will be set up in the Ministry of Commerce Industry, serving as the apex body for project planning and appraisal, research, monitoring and evaluation, among other functions. Minister of Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw said that all the major sectors such as the railways, highways, aviation, among others, will have representation under the new authority. Practically, if GDP increases by 7, the logistics requirement increases by 10 in the economy. To meet this heavy requirement, Highways, railway lines, waterways, ports, airports are being built. To have a unified planning of these things, Gati Shakti portal was launched. Now, to meet the future requirements in transportation and have a synergy among different departments, the Integrated transport logistics authority will be set up, said Vaishnaw, as he announced the decision. The fragmented planning across multiple transport-related ministries has been a long-standing challenge in the country. The ITLA is part of the governments Vision 2047 to reduce logistics costs and improve infrastructure efficiency. Apart from the long-term planning of transport projects covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways and coastal shipping, the authority will do the technical appraisal of the projects worth over Rs 500 crore. It will also monitor the transport and infrastructure projects above Rs 500 crore and assess post-completion impact. The authority will create a national transport data repository to integrate GSTN Goods and Services Tax Network e-way bill, FASTag, Vahan, GPS, and urban traffic data and use freight-flow and origin-destination analytics for evidence based project planning. The authority will also advise and assist in reviewing and updating National logistics policy 2022. ITLA will also evaluate short-term sectoral plans five years or so and annual plans of transport ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.

articleTitle: Raid before FIR: Karnataka High Court scraps slaughter case despite beef seizure
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court cattle slaughter case beef seizure
description: The court held that taking substantial investigative steps before filing an FIR made the entire process legally unsustainable.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court recently scrapped criminal proceedings against a man accused of illegal cattle slaughter and meat distribution after finding that the police raided his godown and seized beef without registering an FIR first. In an order dated September 28, Justice Rajesh Rai K allowed the petition filed by Zainul Abdeen, challenging the case registered against him under various provisions of the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020. The court held that taking substantial investigative steps before lodging an FIR rendered the entire proceeding legally unsustainable. The failure to register the FIR before proceeding with the raid and seizure, coupled with the fact that substantial investigative steps were undertaken before registration of the FIR, vitiates the proceedings initiated against the petitioner-accused. Consequently, the further proceedings arising out of such FIR cannot be sustained, the bench noted. Pre-FIR search and seizure violates mandatory procedure The case dates back to February 26, 2023, when the police received information at around 9.30 am regarding the illegal sale of beef without a license. Officers subsequently conducted multiple raids on shops and a godown in Shabbeer Nagar, Mysuru. During the search at Abdeens godown, the police allegedly found cattle being slaughtered, meat being processed for transport, and a cattle carcass with two horns. After seizing the meat, the police registered a suo motu complaint against Abdeen. Seeking to scrap the case, the petitioner argued that the police were duty-bound to register an FIR or make an entry in the general diary upon receiving information about a cognisable offence before searching. The petitioner cited the Supreme Courts landmark ruling in Lalita Kumari v. State of Uttar Pradesh 2014, which mandates registering an FIR first upon receiving information about a cognisable offence. The petitioner also noted that the property belonged to his father and that he had no connection to the alleged offence. Court rejects preliminary inquiry argument Opposing the plea, the prosecution argued that the investigation was complete, a chargesheet had been filed, and witness statements pointed to Abdeens involvement. Citing the High Court judgment in Ismail v State of HAL Police Station 2026, the state contended that conducting a preliminary inquiry before an FIR does not invalidate proceedings unless the accused demonstrates prejudice. The court rejected the prosecutions stance, observing that police received information at 9.30 am and had ample opportunity to file an FIR before raiding the premises. In the circumstances, the action of the police cannot be characterised as a mere preliminary enquiry undertaken for the purpose of ascertaining the truth of the information received. The police had already proceeded substantially with the investigation by conducting searches, effecting seizures and recording the statements of panch witnesses before registration of the FIR, the bench stated. Concluding that procedural shortcuts directly impacted the accused, the court held, Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, it cannot be held that no prejudice has been caused to the petitioner on account of the failure to register the FIR before undertaking the raid and seizure.

articleTitle: ‘Tech-savvy’ fighter pilot, who’s flown Mirage and Tejas, set to be next Air Chief
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit
description: A fighter pilot, was involved in Safed Sagar and Operation Sindoor.
body_raw: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is set to become the next Chief of the Air Staff at the end of this month, the Ministry of Defence announced on Tuesday. The announcement comes nearly three weeks before the current Air Chief, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, is due to retire on October 31. Air Marshal Dixit is currently serving as the Vice Chief of the Indian Air Force IAF. Popular among his colleagues, Air Marshal Dixit is described by officers as a thorough professional, soft-spoken, balanced and a grounded individual. An Experimental Test Pilot and Qualified Flying Instructor, he has more than 3,500 hours of flying experience on aircraft including the Mirage 2000, various MiG variants, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, Hawk and Tejas. At the same time, he is known to be an avid reader, highly tech-savvy and a visionary leader. His ideas are unique and very different from others. As a leader, he has always been a visionary leader, one of his long-term colleagues told The Indian Express. This is also evident from his public speeches. He has consistently emphasised the need for a balanced mix of traditional and modern weapon systems in the militarys inventory, arguing that conventional aircraft must be complemented by emerging technologies such as drones and missiles to ensure long-term operational effectiveness. In a separate speech, he highlighted the lesson from Operation Sindoor that technology has fundamentally altered the relationship between distance and vulnerability in modern warfare, underscoring the importance of real-time surveillance. Over a distinguished career spanning four decades, the decorated officer has held several critical appointments, including Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee CISC at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff HQ IDS, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Central Air Command and Deputy Chief of Air Staff. As CISC, he consistently worked to promote jointness and integration among the three services, according to an earlier government statement. As a commanding officer, he re-equipped No. 9 Squadron with Mirage-2000 aircraft and later commanded a frontline fighter base in the Western Sector and a premier fighter training base in the Southern Sector. He has also served as Directing Staff at the Air Force Test Pilots School and as Principal Director, Air Staff Requirements, at Air Headquarters. The Air Marshal has served as Air Defence Commander of Southern Air Command and held the appointments of Assistant Chief of the Air Staff Projects, Assistant Chief of the Air Staff Plans at Air Headquarters, Vayu Bhawan, and Senior Air Staff Officer at Headquarters South Western Air Command. During his four-decade-long service career, he has been actively involved in several operations and exercises, including Operation Safed Sagar, Operation Rakshak and Operation Sindoor. Born on December 9, 1966, he was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force on December 6, 1986. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, the Defence Services Staff College in Bangladesh and the National Defence College.

articleTitle: ‘Don’t sleep…’: How dentist Shota Musaev helped save flydubai captain Smit Machchhar after cockpit attack
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai, smit machchhar, dentist
description: Dentist Musaev said he and other passengers rushed towards the flydubai's FZ1073 plane cockpit after hearing screams. Inside, he saw Machchhar on the floor, bleeding heavily from wounds to his head.
body_raw: Dr Shota Musaev, a Georgian dentist living in Israel, boarded flydubai flight FZ1073 as an ordinary passenger. Minutes later, after the co-pilot attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit, Musaev found himself treating the badly wounded pilot as the aircraft diverted to Saudi Arabia. Speaking to ABC News, Musaev said he and other passengers rushed towards the cockpit after hearing screams. Inside, he saw Machchhar on the floor, bleeding heavily from wounds to his head, neck and hands. How Dr Shota Musaev treated injured Indian pilot Saying that he didnt hesitate to do something, the dentist said, I think, how can I help this situation for all the passengers on the plane? How can I help? And I see one pilot on the floor, with.blood. After passengers subdued the co-pilot, Musaev turned his attention to Machchhar and treated the injured captain for about 45 minutes, according to an interview with The National. He also helped passengers restrain the attacker using headphone cables. The aircraft had been cruising at about 34,000 feet when the cockpit confrontation sent it into a steep descent before it was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Two standby flydubai pilots who had been travelling as passengers then entered the cockpit and helped stabilise the aircraft before it landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. I used T-shirts to press the wounds There was heavy bleeding from his head and left hand. I used T-shirts to press the wounds, but it the bleeding didnt stop, so I asked the stewards for ice, Dr Musaev told The National. Musaev also monitored Machchhars vital signs. At one point, he said, the captains pulse became dangerously low, prompting him to raise Machchhars feet. Later, when he noticed that the pilots lips had turned blue, he told a steward We need to land quickly. He doesnt have much more time. The Israel-based dentist added, He had very, very deep cuts and we needed many ice packets. But every time I opened the T-shirt to check the bleeding, it would bleed more. So I pressed not very hard and used ice. All through the 45 minutes, I kept the pressure on. How Musaev kept captain Machchhar conscious Dr Musaev said that he was trying to keep Captain Machchhar, who was seriously wounded in the attack by the Omani co-pilot, conscious by talking to him as he gave emergency aid to the Indian pilot. I told him, Please dont sleep, we need you. I asked how many children he had and their names. I kept telling him, Dont be afraid you will go back to your family we are landing soon.He was cut badly and would say, Im feeling hot on my hands. I kept telling him that he would be OK, Musaev said. Musaev said Machchhar repeatedly asked for help and told him he wanted to live. The captain also complained of pain in his head and a burning sensation in his hands, according to the dentist. Captain Machchhar wants to meet the dentist In a phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on October 3, Machchhar said he would like to meet Musaev, who had treated him after the attack. Musaev has rejected the idea that he alone was responsible for saving Machchhar, instead crediting the passengers and crew who intervened during the crisis. Everyone in the plane is a hero, he told The National. Smit saved our lives and we saved his life. Musaev, 47, was travelling with his wife, Sigalit, from China via Dubai to Israel when he heard screams and later a call for a doctor. After the emergency landing in Tabuk, Musaev said the experience continued to affect him and his wife. He told The National that they were sleeping only about two hours a night and that he had lost three kilograms in three days.

articleTitle: Visakhapatnam naval base staffer, driver held for ‘sharing information with Pakistan’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Visakhapatnam naval base staffer, driver held for 'sharing information with Pakistan'
description: Andhra Police said the module comprises 18 suspects of which 13 are from the Navy. The arrests are part of “Operation Firewall–2026”, launched by the Counter Intelligence Cell on October 1.
body_raw: Busting a module allegedly involved in sharing sensitive defence information with Pakistan Intelligence Operatives PIOs, the Andhra Pradesh Polices Counter Intelligence Cell has arrested two persons associated with the naval base at Visakhapatnam, officials said. Police said the module comprises 18 suspects of which 13 are from the Navy. The arrested accused include Pradeep Mukharjee, an employee of Visakhapatnam base, who was held in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, for his alleged involvement in sharing an OTP for activation of a WhatsApp account by a PIO, communicating with them, and sharing sensitive information relating to NavalDefence establishments, officials said. He was produced before a court in Vijayawada on Tuesday, which sent him to judicial remand till October 14. The other person to have been arrested is Annam Sai Varaprasad, a civilian contractual driver engaged for naval officers at Visakhapatnam, who was allegedly involved in sharing sensitive information with a PIO in lieu of money, officials said. He was produced in a court in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, which also sent him to judicial remand till October 14. The arrests are part of a coordinated operation, titled Operation Firewall2026, launched by the Counter Intelligence CI Cell on October 1. As part of this, 12 teams of the CI cell were deployed across 10 states and Union Territories, namely Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Goa, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh and Bihar. A case was registered in this regard at the Counter Intelligence Police Station, Vijayawada, on September 2 under Sections 612, 147 and 148 read with Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS pertaining to charges of criminal conspiracy, waging war, and conspiring to wage war or overawe the government, committed with a shared common intention. Besides, sections of the UAPA and Official Secrets Act have been slapped on the accused. According to the FIR, the CI cell received credible information regarding certain persons in India allegedly maintaining direct contact with PIOs and their suspected involvement in an espionage conspiracy prejudicial to Indias national security. The suspects were allegedly collecting and sharing the sensitiveclassified information relating to defence establishments and strategic locations in Visakhapatnam and other parts of the country through encrypted communication channels, the FIR stated. In coordination with Anti-Terrorist Squads of the respective states, Naval officials and local police, the AP CI Cell investigation teams examined the alleged complicity of the 18 suspects and seized electronic gadgets from them. The two suspects were arrested after prima facie their role was established in this case, said officials. Further investigation is underway for the remaining suspects.

articleTitle: Punjab is among India’s top grain producers. So why is it unable to store it?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The immediate concern is that the backlog is carrying forward: old stocks are not moving out while new paddy continues arriving. (Express photo)
description: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has sought transportation of grain out of Punjab to create storage space, warning of possible law and order issues. Why is this a persistent challenge for the state?
body_raw: With paddy harvesting now underway in Punjab, the states grain storage problems are again in focus. This seasons crop has begun arriving even as stocks from the previous procurement season remain to be fully cleared, leaving the state to potentially manage fresh arrivals alongside a backlog. The procurement chain normally begins with government agencies purchasing paddy, which is stored in rice mills for custom milling to prepare it for sale in the market. Milled rice is then delivered to government agencies and forms part of the central pool. The Centre has extended the deadline for delivery of Custom Milled Rice CMR from the 2025-26 crop season to November 30 - after the 2026-27 procurement season would have ended. Two cycles are thus overlapping 6 lakh tonnes LT of old paddy is still being milled and rice delivered to the government, while fresh paddy is arriving in mandis and being allotted to mills. Recently, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann sought transportation of grain out of Punjab to create storage space, warning of possible law and order issues. The problem could worsen as Punjab targets 180 LT of paddy procurement, against 156 LT last year. So, why does the crisis persist, why might it worsen, and what is the solution? We explain. Why is grain storage in Punjab under pressure? Essentially, a mismatch exists between grain supply and space. Punjab has around 175 LT of covered storage capacity, including what is available with the Food Corporation of India FCI, state procurement agencies and private facilities, besides 75 LT of plinth storage an open-air storage platform primarily used for wheat, where rice cannot be stored similarly. However, rice from previous kharif cycles June to October occupies most covered space. Consequently, 17 LT of wheat from the previous rabi season October to March remains in rice mills and mandi yards due to a lack of storage. Around 6 LT of previous-cycle rice is also pending for delivery by mills. Punjab handles 300320 LT of paddy and wheat annually, making regular movement to other states essential to create space for the next procurement cycle. How much grain needs to move out of Punjab - and how much is actually moving? Rice millers and state procurement agencies traditionally prefer paddy milling to be completed by March 31, as prolonged summer and monsoon storage increase infestation and deterioration risks. The Centres prescribed milling period generally runs from December 1 to June 30, though extensions are given when stocks remain pending. Even by June 30, Punjab would need to deliver about 120.6 LT of rice if it procures the targeted 180 LT of paddy. Over seven months, that means clearing around 17 LT a month. Against this target, officials say that current grain movement out of Punjab averages 1112 LT a month, comprising rice and wheat. The proportion varies, sometimes roughly 5050, while at other times one-third is rice. Could the problem worsen in the coming years? The immediate concern is that the backlog is carrying forward old stocks are not moving out while new paddy continues arriving. Last year, milling went on until September this year, the problem is more visible, with around 6 LT of previous-season rice pending for delivery, while 17 LT of wheat still occupies rice mills and mandi yards. With this trend of no movement, the overlap could double or triple in the coming years. What could be the solution? Both storage capacity and slow movement of grain are to be blamed, according to FCI and state procurement officials. Officials say constructing additional storage in Punjab is expensive because land rates are high. Punjab already has a substantial storage network, but it is not enough to handle the volume of grain procured in the state without regular emptying. When both the Centre and state governments are aware of the amount of grain procured from Punjab, why not create additional storage capacity - if not in Punjab, then outside Punjab? said a senior FCI official. Even if storage capacity is available in any part of the country, wheat can be transported directly from mandis to those locations. In the case of paddy, which is entirely housed by rice mills, the rice can be transported directly from mills to storage facilities elsewhere after milling. Officials point to Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, where land rates are comparatively lower and many storage facilities can be built. They argue that Punjab produces for the nation around 80 of the wheat produced and almost the entire paddy in Punjab goes to the central pool. Therefore, officials say, the storage burden need not be concentrated in Punjab, and suggest faster movement of grain to additional storage capacity outside Punjab.

articleTitle: Anti-EC protest | ‘They have entire career lying ahead’: Delhi court grants bail to 17 protesters arrested
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jantar Mantar protest
description: In four separate orders, Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Animesh Kumar of the Patiala House Court granted bail to the 17 accused.
body_raw: Granting bail to 17 people arrested by the Delhi Police during a protest in the Capital against Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Monday, a Delhi court late in the night sought a report from the DCP New Delhi on allegations that two of those arrested were beaten up at the Parliament Street police station. In four separate orders, Judicial Magistrate First Class JMFC Animesh Kumar of the Patiala House Court granted bail to the 17 accused. The accused persons are of very young age and do not appear to be habitual offenders. They have their entire career lying ahead, JMFC Kumar said. The police had submitted before the court that the protesters were part of an unlawful assembly and had blocked the public space when Section 163 of BNSS was in place, prohibiting public gatherings of five or more people, demonstrations and other activities without prior written permission. httpswww.youtube.comwatch?v-Hjn02Ty0kfeatureyoutu.be After two protesters told the court that they sustained injuries as they were beaten inside the Parliament Street police station after they were detained, JMFC Kumar sought that CCTV camera footage from inside the police station be preserved. Since accused Dharmender and Samarth have levelled allegations regarding custodial torture, let report be called from DCP New Delhi regarding the same. The relevant CCTV footage of PS Parliament Street be also preserved, he said. The Delhi Police submitted that when the accused were being detained to manage the law and order situation, they manhandled and assaulted police officers, during which one woman officer sustained injuries. Seeking 14 days of judicial custody, the police told the court that the protesters broke the glass of a bus in which they were being detained. They alleged that the protesters did not cooperate during the course of the investigation and failed to disclose their complete personal details. JMFC Kumar said, It should be noted that allegations against the accused are serious in nature. One police official has allegedly sustained injuries as per the MLC produced by the IO. While any person has right to protest peacefully, however, assaulting police officials on duty is serious concern which cannot be permitted under the garb of peaceful protest. However, it cannot be ignored that all the offences involved in the present case except offence punishable under Section 132 of BNS are bailable in nature. Even the offence punishable under Section 132 of BNS assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty provides for maximum imprisonment of 2 years only, he added.

articleTitle: Rahul Gandhi’s stand-on-barricade moment came with a Led Zeppelin track
articleFeaturedImageAlt: LoP Rahul Gandhi climbs barricades during a protest in New Delhi for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on October 6. (Express photo by Abhinav Saha)
description: Rahul Gandhi's Led Zeppelin Instagram reel went viral Tuesday as the INDIA bloc marched on the Election Commission demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the SIR voter roll revision.
body_raw: Jimmy Page and Robert Plant came a-visiting Tuesday while the Congress-led INDIA opposition bloc protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Ok. So they werent actually there. But Congress MP Rahul Gandhi served up some Led Zeppelin spirit in an Instagram reel the clip showed the Leader of the Opposition standing astride Delhi Polices yellow metal barricades, hands on hips while a sea of protesters swarmed around. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rahul Gandhi rahulgandhi At 6.45 pm - three hours after it was posted - the reel had been viewed over 2.7 million times. And if you want to check out the full song its a banger you can do so here But the day began with less hard rock and more political sloganeering opposition MPs led by Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, as well as Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and the Trinamool Congress Abhishek Banerjee, set off on a march from parliament to the EC office. The purpose? To confront CEC Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision of stateUT voter rolls. The substance of these allegations - that the EC helps the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party win elections - have been made frequently by Gandhi and other opposition MPs, though there was little by way of public response. However, last month The Indian Express published an investigation that said two of Indias three Election Commissioners - Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - had repeatedly objected to decisions related to the voter re-verification exercise, including illegal changes to Form 6 and the push to centralise control of ECINET, the software that manages voter rolls. The Express investigative reports prompted a furious response from the opposition and democracy activists, including the Abhijeet Dipke-founded Cockroach Janata Party, all of whom are now demanding Gyanesh Kumar resign as the CEC and the voter lists be rolled back. On Tuesday afternoon those protests led to tense showdowns between Delhi Police and the protesters, with dozens of the latter group herded away into police buses and detained. Both Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were also briefly detained. She was sitting in a bus, parked outside Akashvani Bhavan - the headquarters of All India Radio - and Rahul was about to get in. Suddenly, they looked at each other and walked past the cops and into that compound. The move seemed off-script and the police were caught flat-footed. This sort of off-the-cuff thinking seems to have become part of Rahul Gandhis personal gameplan in cornering the government during public protests. Remember the impromptu sit-in outside Prime Minister Modis home in July to protest police violence against NEET protesters? In fact, till they walked into Akashvani Bhavan, most Congress leaders said they thought the protest was over - squashed by the authorities who seemed better prepared this time than last, when the CJP protested at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG exam paper leak. We dont know what happened. This was not part of the plan, one of them said. Clearly Rahul had a plan, though.

articleTitle: Ashok Lavasa: Can the Election Commission untie knots of its own making?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: election commission
description: With high courts questioning some of its decisions, serving judges exhorting against mass disenfranchisement, former ECs/CECs questioning its conduct, the clouds over the ECI become thicker
body_raw: The Election Commission of India ECI is in a bind like never before. That it worked hard to get here is a pity. An organisation that endeared itself by its friendly approach over the years finds itself friendless. Its only friend, the ruling party, pushes it further into a corner each time it comes to its defence. The ECI is under attack from almost all quarters - people, civil society organisations, retired civil servants, former judges, practising lawyers, political parties. The print media has written hard-hitting editorials against the Special Intensive Revision SIR, and YouTubers have ready-made content as the ECI rides through this mire of its own making. The war within the ECI is in the public square with the Indian Express revealing cracks in an organisation in which confidence is crumbling. The 14 letters by the two Election Commissioners EC have pushed the Chief Election Commissioner CEC in the eye of the storm, even if the storm might rock their boats too. Every attempt of the ECI to explain away the controversy drags it deeper into the morass. With high courts questioning some of its decisions, serving judges exhorting against mass disenfranchisement, former ECsCECs questioning its conduct, the clouds over the ECI become thicker. The Shakespearean platitude, when sorrows come, they come not single spies, but in battalions, seems to be playing out, with petitions seeking the suspension of the CEC for his authoritarian ways admitted by the Supreme Court SC. As if this wasnt enough, hearing the petitions on October 5, the Chief Justice of India reportedly observed, No modified Form 6 has been approved by us. It is these modifications in Form 6 that one of the ECs termed illegal and unauthorised in his letter of August 14. The ECIs responses to the Indian Express report added to its miseries. The first response on September 23 was I plead not-guilty, claiming all decisions were unanimous. In its second response of September 26, the ECI climbed down but created confusion by admitting it used two versions of Form 6 for SIR and non-SIR purposes, asserting the SC upheld the changes. Soon, the ECI wilted and withdrew the declaration attached to Form 6 as if it was hiding the weapon used in the crime. The CJIs remark has fuelled the fire, with critics calling it a vindication of their allegations of arbitrary, illegal action of the CEC. However, supporters quickly found a shield in para 152 of the SCs May 27 judgement wherein it observed that Form 6 sets out a framework of documentation however, the same is tailored to the process of revision contemplated under Section 212 of the RP Act and may not, in all situations, be capable of literal application to an exercise of the present nature. The Commission, therefore, retains a degree of residual authority to formulate an appropriate documentation framework suited to the exigencies of a Special Intensive Revision. Such authority, however, is not unbounded. In devising such a framework, the Commission must remain cognisant of the existing statutory scheme, and any departure therefrom must be informed by a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved. The formulation of the documentation regime must thus reflect a calibrated balance in drawing from the statutory framework, while adapting it, where necessary, to effectively serve the purpose of ensuring the accuracy and integrity of the electoral roll. This is legalese at its ambivalent best. Is the SC merely recognising the ECIs authority to formulate, not approve, an appropriate documentation framework for the SIR? At the same time, is it affirming the guardrails by stating that such authority is not unbounded, reminding it of the existing statutory scheme? If the ECI was deriving legitimacy from this SC order for the Form 6 changes it unilaterally made, why did the EC, nearly three months after the SC order, call them illegal and unauthorised? Did the ECI examine his objections and reaffirm its belief that the SC had legitimised the changes? One must try to untie a few knots the ECI has tied itself in and separate the strands in its most controversial decisions in the 75 years of its existence, namely conducting the SIR. Arguably an abrupt, aggressive and ambitious decision, it was largely perceived as unfair, exclusionary and arbitrary. If the ECI wants the people to believe the decision to conduct SIR was unanimous, it must put the minutes of the relevant ECI meeting in the public domain. The letters revealing the rift within the ECI dont necessarily oppose the SIR. The ECs apparently referred to the illegalities committed in changing Form 6, and denying access to the Electoral Registration Officers to the ECINet, impeding the performance of legally mandated duties. The ECs were already smarting as they felt excluded from the decision-making process, and the ECI neither held meetings for four months, nor circulated the agenda and minutes of meetings for a year. They were understandably perturbed that without their knowledge 16 lakh appeals were filed before the appellate tribunals against inclusion in the purified electoral roll of West Bengal. These made the ECIs functioning questionable. It is difficult to predict how the current drama will end but there is no doubt that it is tragic for Indian democracy. In its withering away, the once-hallowed institution of the ECI resembles Miltons Fallen Angels. It has itself to blame for its sorry plight and the opprobrium heaped upon it. The SC may set aside the ECIs decisions if it finds them illegal but whether that would lead to the CECECs losing their paradise will depend on whether a sin against democracy can be punished by a man-made system. Impeachment is politically fraught the call of the conscience is a far cry. Glory lies not in never falling but rising every time you fall, was a motivational quote inscribed on the walls of my school. I recently learnt it is from Oliver Goldsmiths The Citizen of the World 1762. Now I realise this applies as much to institutions as to individuals. The walls of many constitutional bodies qualify to have this quotation pasted on them. Let Nirvachan Sadan take the lead. The writer is a former election commissioner

articleTitle: On Rentiya Baras, university founded by Gandhi to take charkha to 350 schools
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rentiya Baras 2026
description: The Vidyapith has been celebrating Gandhi’s Hindu calendar birthday as Rentiya Baras for the past 90 years.
body_raw: Gujarat Vidyapith, the university founded by Mahatma Gandhi in Ahmedabad, will celebrate his birthday as per the Hindu calendar on Wednesday October 7. It will mark the celebration by taking charkha to 351 municipal schools to spread Gandhis message of Swadeshi, the university said. As per the Vikram Samvat calendar, Gandhi was born on Bhadarva Vad Baras the 12th day of the sixth month of the Hindu calendar, which is also known as Bhadrapada in 1925. The period corresponds to October 2, 1869, in the Gregorian calendar. The Vidyapith has been celebrating Gandhis Hindu calendar birthday as Rentiya Baras for the past 90 years. Rentiya is Gujarati for spinning wheel, which Gandhi used to spin khadi, turning it into a movement for self-reliance. Gandhi wanted to dedicate the day to charkha Gandhi had wished that his birthday be celebrated as Rentiya Baras. Associate Professor of Social Work at Gujarat Vidyapith Ravindra Pancholi said, When he was alive, Gandhis followers wanted to celebrate his birthday. However, Gandhi said that he did not like the idea of people remembering his birthday. Then, he suggested that the day his birthday as per the Vikram Samvat calendar could be marked as Rentiya Baras. Pancholi 55, who is the grandson of noted Gujarati writer and educationist Manubhai Pancholi Darshak, said Gandhi told his followers that if they loved him, then they should shun foreign clothes and adopt khadi and spin charkha. So, this tradition of celebrating Gandhis birthday, as per the Vikram Samvat calendar, as Rentiya Baras, and not as Mohan Jayanti or Gandhi Jayanti, started around 1929-30, Pancholi said. The celebration this year Around 200 volunteers and over 1,800 students of Gujarat Vidyapith are expected to visit 351 schools in 48 wards of Ahmedabad city. They will demonstrate the spinning wheel and explain its significance to students. Through this, they will talk about Mahatma Gandhis ideas of Swadeshi and self-reliance and reach out to more than 1,35,000 students, according to a statement by Gujarat Vidyapith. Vidyapith Public Relations Officer Advaita Dave said the university had been celebrating Rentiya Baras in different ways every year. Last year, our staff and students spun charkha at Sabarmati Riverfront for around one and a half hours. Apart from Swadeshi, the motive behind the celebration is to spread the message that spinning the charkha is a kind of yoga as well, Dave said. Pancholi said previously, students performed akhand kantan non-stop spinning on Rentiya Baras. They would take turns in batches of 20-25 and spin charkha continuously for 12 hours.

articleTitle: ‘I laughed hard after a long time’: Madhavan heaps praise on Tamil film Modha Rathiri
articleFeaturedImageAlt: R Madhavan, Modha Rathiri
description: R Madhavan has praised Raja Karuppasamy’s Tamil film Modha Rathiri starring Rishikanth and Anishma Anilkumar. The film has also received appreciation from Kamal Haasan, Dhanush and Silambarasan.
body_raw: Actor-filmmaker R Madhavan has heaped praise on the Tamil film Modha Rathiri, calling it brilliant and saying he had enjoyed a Tamil film after a really long time. He also praised the films screenplay, visual storytelling and performances. Madhavan wrote on Instagram, What a brilliant brilliant film. Enjoyed a Tamil film after a really long time. Brilliant screenplay, wonderful visual storytelling, extraordinary performances. I laughed hard after a long time and cheered and clapped as well. A big standing ovation to the entire team, Cast and crew. God bless you with more power. Take a look at Madhavan Instagram post here View this post on Instagram A post shared by R. Madhavan actormaddy Kamal Haasan, Dhanush and Silambarasan praise Modha Rathiri Madhavan is not the only actor from the Tamil film fraternity to appreciate Modha Rathiri. Dhanush had earlier called it a heartwarming film and applauded the work of the first-timers. He also urged audiences to watch it with their families. Check out Dhanushs tweet ModhaRathri is such a heartwarming film. Have to applaud this wonderful effort by a bunch of first-timers. Please dont miss it in theatres with your families RajaKaruppasamy iamrishikanth AnishmaAnilkumar - Dhanush dhanushkraja September 8, 2026 Silambarasan, too, spoke about Modha Rathiri and urged audiences and producers to support smaller Tamil films. He particularly praised the films writing. Watched ModhaRathri and really enjoyed it. We often discover small, beautiful films from other languages and celebrate them so much. When a Tamil film attempts something fresh with a new team, I feel we should give it the same love and support. A story unfolding over a single night, set around a village wedding, with so many characters and little moments that felt so real. The writing, the humour, the way people react to each other, and the characters were all handled really well. Really happy to see a new director and team make something so rooted and interesting. My appreciation to director RajaKaruppasamy, the entire cast and crew and everyone who backed this film. A small request to our producers too. films like these need that extra push to reach the audience. Good content deserves to be discovered. And to all my fans and everyone who loves cinema, do watch ModhaRathri in theatres and support the team. Wishing the entire team lots of success. Keep making good cinema iamrishikanth AnishmaAnilkumar MythriOfficial - Silambarasan TR SilambarasanTR August 28, 2026 Also Read Seen him shouting at stars Raza Murad compares perfectionists Bhansali, Raj Kapoor Ahead of Modha Rathiris OTT release, Kamal Haasan invited debutant director Raja Karuppasamy to meet him personally. The filmmaker later revealed that the veteran actor encouraged him and told him to show the industry what he was capable of. About Modha Rathiri Written and directed by Raja Karuppasamy, Modha Rathiri stars Rishikanth and Anishma Anilkumar in the lead roles. Set against a rural backdrop, the film revolves around a newly married couple and the chaos that unfolds on their wedding night. The cast also includes Chetan, Bagavathi Perumal, Abdool Lee, A Venkatesh and Shelly Kishore. Produced by Mythri Movie Makers, Modha Rathiri hit theatres on August 21 and premiered on Netflix in September.

articleTitle: Telangana registers first FIR on ‘illegal’ Form 7s, BJP agent booked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ‘Was doing my duty’: BLO who stopped bulk submission of Form 7
description: The BJP booth level agent filed 30 Form 7s for deletion of names from electoral roll in Musheerabad Assembly constituency, all against Muslim voters.
body_raw: Police in Chikkadpally, Hyderabad, have registered an FIR against a Booth Level Agent BLA of the BJP for filing allegedly fraudulent form 7s against 30 people, all of them Muslim, in the Musheerabad Assembly constituency. The action comes a day ahead of the end of the claims and objections phase of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral roll in the state. The FIR was filed against the BJPs S Balachander, on a complaint by Musheerabad Electoral Registration Officer ERO T Praveen Kumar Reddy, after a preliminary inquiry reportedly showed that the Form 7s submitted by him were pre-printed with names of the voters concerned. BJP rivals have called this proof that the Form 7s had been centrally generated from the BJP office. Similar forms with pre-printed voter information have also been reported in Bahadurpura and Goshamahal constituencies in Hyderabad. The 30 people against whom Balachander is said to have submitted Form 7s-for the deletion of names from electoral roll-include a Congress BLA. According to the FIR, the BJP BLA brought 30 pre-printed Form-7s and made efforts to submit them to the BLO, Polling Station No. 210, on September 28, 2026, with a mala fide intention for deleting voters not connected to him. The FIR adds that when the BLO and BLO Supervisor collectively refused to receive the forms, in spite of repeated requests from the said BLA of BJP, Balachander left the forms on the BLOs premises and fled. The officials said that a personal field verification by them on October 1 showed that all the 30 people whose names were flagged by the BLA were residents of Hyderabads Musheerabad. Therefore, the form-7s in question cannot be accepted and are liable for rejection, the FIR says. Balachander has been booked under Sections 217 and 3182 of the BNS, pertaining to giving false information to a government officer and cheating, and Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act 1950. On Monday, Telangana Chief Electoral Officer CEO C Sudarshan Reddy issued a memo asking district collectors and District Election Officers of the state to take action against those filing false Form 7s, saying instances of this had come to their notice. AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi claimed that in Goshamahal constituency too, false Form 7s had been filed to delete names of Muslim voters. Our request to the CEO is to not spare anyone who is spreading this hatred against Muslims, Owaisi said. BJP state president N Ramchander Rao has denied any attempts by the party to delete voters, accusing the Congress of misguiding the public against a constitutional institution like the Election Commission. Telangana had 3.39 crore voters before the Special Intensive Revision SIR process started on June 15. In the draft list, 73.39 lakh voters names were deleted and 92 lakh voters were sent notices. The final electoral roll is to be published on November 9.

articleTitle: ‘You need partners for strategic autonomy, you can’t do everything by yourself’: Finland envoy to India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Russia-Ukraine war Finland envoy
description: We are living in quite a turbulent time, when it comes to geopolitics and geoeconomics, said Finland Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski.
body_raw: As he weighs on the global consequences of the Russia-Ukraine war, new Finland Ambassador to India, Mikko Kivikoski, says they appreciate Indias efforts, and it is a situation where everybody else is ready to negotiate to stop the war except the Russians. He says the global community should incentivise Russia to come to the negotiation table and then to have this war ended. In an interview with Divya A, weeks after presenting his credentials to the President Alexander Stubb, Kivikoski weighs in on lessons from global conflicts and the US protectionism, why the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor IMEC is stuck, and the imminent need to reform the UN Security Council. Excerpts With protectionism rising from big powers like the US, what would be Finlands priorities in terms of the India-EU FTA, set to be operationalised in the coming months? The Free Trade Agreement FTA sends a clear and strong message that when it comes to international trade, rules-based trade is still beneficial for all of us. This applies to all the FTAs that both India and the European Union EU are signing with other partners as well. So, there is a strong signal that there are several countries that want to have rules in international trade. The US has imposed steep reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods and even on several EU goods. So, how does Finland assess the impact of all of this on global supply chains and on small, open economies? We are living in quite a turbulent time, when it comes to geopolitics and geoeconomics. Everybody is looking at partners and diversifying things - to make sure you have the freedom of manoeuvre, and also certain amount of predictability. We are all doing that - be it India, the EU or Finland. That is one of the lessons learned. India has been seeking from the EU to ease the CBAM, visa norms for professionals and even data protection. What is Finlands position on this? We are part of the EU, so we have been part of the decision making on the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism CBAM, and the same applies to the EU data protection laws. But we believe it is about level playing field, and sustainability in the long run. Many Indian companies are already adapting something I personally noticed is that sustainability issues are more on the agenda in India. Should India and Finland collaborate more on critical minerals and batteries? Because Finland has large reserves, India has demand. That is also part of the EU-Finland-India partnership. Again, it all comes down to the supply chain and strategic autonomy. And in that context, the EU and India see each other as trusted partners. And you need partners when it comes to strategic autonomy. You cannot do everything by yourself. With navigation disrupted due to war, especially in the Red Sea and the Black Sea, is there a scope for cooperation on alternative routes, maybe IMEC, mooted by India in 2023? Definitely, one of the consequences of the recent geopolitical, geoeconomical changes in the world is that, again, it all comes down to the supply chains and strategic autonomy. All the countries are looking for new logistic routes. They want to cut down dependencies. When it comes to this particular corridor, we all understand that there are several geopolitical issues at the moment. We have been supporting it from the beginning, but one has to be realistic. And when it comes to logistic routes, it must be feasible. For the time being, there are certain geopolitical issues in West Asia that are hindering it at the moment. You have been talking about resilient supply chains and strategic autonomy. Do you think globalisation, as we know, will change forever? I hope not. For a small country like us, we would like to see sort of rules and institutions when it comes to the international order. We would also like to see that world trade would be free. So, we are partnering with countries that have similar views. Finland, India and the EU have similar views when it comes to international order, as well as on multilateralism. India and Finland are definitely natural partners when it comes to multilateralism, the UN charter and the UN-based multilateralism. We would like to see India as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, and we believe that the Council needs to be reformed. India said that it is in touch with Russia and Ukraine to find a solution to the ongoing war, and the Ukrainian Foreign Minister has said they support Indias proposal. Have there been discussions between Kyiv and other EU partners on the proposal? Yeah, sort of two remarks on that. Firstly, all the attempts to bring the war to an end are highly appreciated and needed. As we all know, it has been underway, and it is already the 5th year. The global consequences are clear.
