Your External Minister has talked about the consequences multiple times, so that is clear. We are in a situation where everybody else is ready to negotiate - to stop the war - except the Russians. So basically, what we need is that the global community incentivises Russia to come to the negotiation table, and then to have the war ended. Incentivise, as in how would that work? To incentivise in terms of sanctions, or trade? Incentivise - that they would understand it is also for their best to stop the war because it is clear that the consequences for the Russian economy and the society are huge. At the end of the day, too many human beings are being lost in the war. You have arrived in New Delhi at a time when the India-EU relations are getting stronger, and the India-EU FTA is in the last leg before being signed. What do you think about the collaboration between New Delhi and Helsinki at this point? We have been witnessing record-high activities this year Finland Prime Minister Petteri Orpo visited India, President Alexander Stubb made a state visit to India, as well as we also had the Nordic-India Summit in Oslo. Then a few weeks ago in Gandhinagar, there was the 10th edition of the World Circular Economy Forum - organised for the first time in South Asia, by the governments of Finland and India. And when you add to that the FTA and the perspective of the agreement to be enforced next year, this creates a great momentum to deepen our collaboration. And therefore, our task here will be to turn this framework into concrete activities.

articleTitle: Union Cabinet hails 25 years of Modi at helm, flags ‘mandate, trust, his governance’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ‘Sir, please fix IRCTC captcha’: Students’ plea prompts Ashwini Vaishnaw to promise new railway ticketing website
description: Vaishnaw said the Prime Minister received a standing ovation from all Cabinet colleagues during the meeting.
body_raw: The Union Cabinet adopted a resolution Tuesday, hailing the enduring trust that the public have reposed in Narendra Modi and his governance achievements over the last 25 years, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and later as Prime Minister of the country. Briefing reporters on the decisions of the Union Cabinet at its meeting Tuesday, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution covers Modis unbroken public service record, spanning the period from October 7, 2001, when he first assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat, to his continuous tenure as Prime Minister up to October 7, 2026. Vaishnaw said the Prime Minister received a standing ovation from all Cabinet colleagues during the meeting. The resolution congratulated Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. An official statement on the resolution stated Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by the principle of Nation First and Citizen First. Three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the enduring trust that the public have reposed in PM Narendra Modi. The statement listed ten salient features of his leadership of Gujarat and India. The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarats successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigrams separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarats experience across India. His sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels, it stated. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity, it stated. His determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for womens reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind, it stated. The resolution lays particular emphasis on Modis willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. His appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose, it stated. Under Modis leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen Indias ability to meet its needs, it stated. Modis faith in technology, it said, emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. Developing Indias own Covid vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moons south pole demonstrated PM Modis vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities. The resolution highlights Modis ability to give India direction through global upheavals. During Covid, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. His leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times. The resolution cited the 2016 surgical strikes, the 2019 Balakot air strikes and the 2025 Operation Sindoor as national security red lines established under Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staffs post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust, the statement said. The resolution links Indias rising stature with Modis ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Unions G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how Indias capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and Indias growing influence and contribution to shared solutions, it stated. Modis vision, it said, unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarats dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lallas consecration strengthened Indias connection with its heritage. The resolution culminates in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047, it stated. Modis approach to disaster management was also hailed Tuesday. Gujarat was recovering from the devastating Bhuj earthquake that struck just months before Modi became Chief Minister. He set a three-year recovery target and a move towards mitigation. An Institute of Seismological Research was established in 2003. As Prime Minister, he released the countrys first National Disaster Management Plan in 2016. He articulated a 10-point agenda for Disaster Risk Reduction at the Asian Ministerial Conference in New Delhi, calling for technology and mobile-based warnings, wider risk coverage and greater international cooperation. The governments focus also moved to early warnings and zero casualty. A multi-hazard early warning system was launched under Modis tenure and the India Meteorological Department has been providing district-level, impact-based and risk-based warnings while an indigenous multi-hazard decision support system has been operational since 2023. At the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019, India also launched the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, which today has 59 member countries and 13 partner organisations. India has also deployed search and rescue teams at disaster sites, notably in Nepal in 2015 and 2026, in Turkiye and Syria after the 2023 earthquake.

articleTitle: Cabinet clears Rs 10,000 crore fund to support small, medium enterprises
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SME Growth Fund
description: The fund, first announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27, aims to provide enterprises with equity support.
body_raw: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the Small and Medium Enterprise SME Growth Fund SGF with an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore to provide equity support to small and medium enterprises. The fund was first announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27. According to the government, while several existing funds provide equity support to businesses, most of them focus on early-stage enterprises and largely cater to micro enterprises. This has left a structural gap in the availability of growth-stage equity capital for small and medium enterprises. While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders, the government said in a statement. The SME Growth Fund is designed to address this critical financing gap by providing patient growth equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability, it added. Under the initiative, the government will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund AIF established under the SGF framework. A majority of the funds investments will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing enterprises, with a focus also on SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities, it said. The Centre expects the fund to help SMEs scale up, improve productivity and strengthen export competitiveness by enabling manufacturing enterprises to expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies and achieve greater scale. India SME Forum in a note said the fund is critical for the MSME as they are facing structural and severe capital gaps. They have been over-dependent on debt financing and have weak integration with the global value chain, the forum said. The SME growth fund could help mobilisation of institutional capital and creation of globally competitive mid-sized champions, it said. Vinod Kumar, President, India SME Forum said the Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund can set in motion a powerful cycle, where stronger manufacturers place larger and more consistent orders with smaller suppliers, enabling those businesses to invest in better machinery, improve quality, build skills and create jobs. As these capabilities deepen across industrial clusters, more MSMEs can meet the standards required by large domestic buyers and global supply chains. The cumulative outcome can be higher domestic value addition, greater export competitiveness and reduced dependence on imported components and finished products, Kumar said. Experts said the fund is critical for the MSME as they are facing structural gaps and severe capital gaps and have been over-dependent on debt financing and have weak integration with the global value chain. Sandeep Jain, an auto-component manufacturer and former President of Federation of Indian Micro and Small Medium Enterprises FISME said the growth fund would give motivation to SMEs to grow and not be overtly concerned with the financing. The route of investment via an AIF is also very innovative. I am sure it will give great dividends,Jain said. The SME growth fund was announced by the Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during the Budget presentation earlier this year, to ensure timely payments to SMEs. I propose to introduce a dedicated Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund, to create future Champions, incentivising enterprises based on select criteria. I also propose to top up the Self-Reliant India Fund set up in 2021, with Rs 2,000 crore to continue support to micro enterprises and maintain their access to risk capital, Sitharaman said while presenting the Budget.

articleTitle: CBI books OSD to Punjab CM for graft, searches Mann’s ‘camp office’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajbir Singh Guman, an OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann
description: Searches come hours after Supreme Court agreed to hear a Punjab govt challenge to HC order directing CBI probe into corruption allegations
body_raw: The CBI on Tuesday registered a corruption case against Rajbir Singh Guman, an OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, and other senior officials and conducted searches at eight locations, including Manns camp office in Chandigarh, officials said. Mann said that the BJP has started preparing for Punjab elections and was now resorting to central agencies to target him and his government. The CBI, in a statement, said that following the orders of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, and receipt of report from the Enforcement Directorate, it has registered an FIR to investigate the allegations of corruption against OSD to Punjab Chief Minister CM and his associates for influencing and manipulating postings of officers including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits. It is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the government, the CBI statement said, adding the agency has booked six persons, including two public servants. They include Ghuman, alleged middleman Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and unknown public servants and private persons, it added. The central agency carried out raids at House No. 50, the camp office allotted to Mann under the Chief Ministers pool, where Ghuman had been staying. It also conducted searches at Ghumans residence in Gharachon in Sangrur district apart from locations in Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, and Jalandhar connected with the accused persons. Incriminating evidence such as laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized. These are being scrutinized for evidence of bribery and impropriety. Further investigation in the case is in progress, read the CBI statement. The raids came hours after the Supreme Court agreed to hear a Punjab government plea challenging a Punjab and Haryana High Courts order directing the CBI to investigate Ghuman and others. The high court, in its order on Monday, had held that material shared by the ED with Punjab DGP in the matter prima facie indicated their involvement in acts of corruption, including cash for transfers and cash for favourable orders. The state filed a Special Leave Petition at around 2am in the Supreme Court against the HC order. Reacting to the development, Mann, in a post on X, said, BJP has started preparing for the Punjab elections.CBI raided my camp office. Now, ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab, so that Punjab government and I can be defamed. Seeing the love we are getting from the people, BJP is nervous, Mann said. The high court order came on on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who had sought an independent probe into the matter raised by the ED with the Punjab Police in its letters to the DGP. The ED had written to the DGP seeking registration of an FIR against an alleged middleman and others, reportedly linked to the Chief Ministers Office, for allegedly influencing transfers and postings of government officials, facilitating arms licence approvals, leaking confidential government documents and securing government approvals in lieu of alleged monetary and other benefits. The EDs letters stem from a money laundering investigation linked to the submission of alleged fake consent letters for obtaining Change of Land Use CLU in a case involving a housing society. The ED had conducted searches on the premises of Nitin Gohal, Ajay Sehgal of Indian Cooperative House Building Society, the Suntec City Project and some others in May. The agency had submitted 200-page affidavit in the high court on the PIL filed by Saraf. The searches took place against the backdrop of an escalating confrontation between the Punjab government and central investigative agencies. The Mann government has repeatedly accused the Centre of using the ED and CBI to target opposition-ruled states, while the BJP has rejected such allegations and maintained that investigative agencies act independently.

articleTitle: Arvind Swamy says wife Aparna is ‘bubbly and energetic’: ‘I am introverted, need my space’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arvind swamy photo with second wife aparna
description: Arvind Swamy opened up about his marriage to Aparna, saying she is extroverted while he is introverted, and explained how they make their differences work.
body_raw: Actor Arvind Swamy has opened up about his marriage, his equation with his wife Aparna Mukerjee and the understanding that keeps their relationship strong. Describing himself as an introvert and his wife as an outgoing, bubbly and energetic person, the Meiyazhagan actor spoke about how they have learnt to respect each others differences, give each other space and trust each others judgement. He also opened up on parenting, saying that children may remember how their parents treated them far more than the sacrifices they made for them. She knows that I need the space In a conversation with Gobinath, Arvind Swamy said Aparna is very different from him when it comes to their personalities. While he considers himself an introvert, he described his wife as someone who is naturally social and comfortable around people. My wife knows me. She talks a lot. She is a very extroverted person. She is friendly with everyone. Everyone likes her. She is a very bubbly and energetic character. I am very introverted. I am extroverted when it comes to my friends otherwise, I am a very quiet person. I dont engage a lot, he said. According to Arvind, understanding this difference has helped them give each other the space they need. He said Aparna does not force him to attend social gatherings when she knows he would rather stay away. She knows that I need the space, so she wont force me to come. This usually happens. There is not much pressure, he said. However, there are times when she tells him that it would be nice if he accompanied her. The actor said he trusts her enough to understand that such a request usually has a reason behind it. At times, she says that it would be nice if I come. I trust her that she has put a lot of thought into it. I trust that it is important to her, so I would go, he said. The actor said he can also recognise when his presence is important at a family function, birthday or another occasion. I have analysed it, and there seems to be an obligation or a requirement behind wanting me to come, either for a function, event or a birthday. If they call me to meet family or anyone, I have that trust. I wont say that I wont come, he said. Arvind said such requests should not become a source of resentment or something partners keep track of. We must not register it like an obligation. If you want to go, you can go. If not, you can tell them. There should not be any issue because of this. Similarly, I would be happy. She can be happy only if I can be happy I can be happy only if she is happy, he said. Arvind Swamy believes that partners need to complement each other and be willing to acknowledge their mistakes. Both must complement each other. When you make a mistake, you must have the courage to admit it. There must be a positive contribution, where you suggest an alternative to the other person. Similarly, they must be understanding of each other as well, he said. ALSO READ Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity Arvind Swamy on parenting The actor also spoke about how stress from work and other responsibilities can affect family relationships. He admitted that there was a point when the pressure he carried would spill over into his interactions with his children. At one point, due to a lot of tension and pressure, when I am with my kids, the tension and pressure gets translated into the relationship, he said. He explained that people can unconsciously transfer their stress to those around them. When she sees me, I would either be irritated or preoccupied, or I might be in a situation where I have to address a few important things. We will unconsciously transfer it. The kids or people around us will feel that, he said. Arvind said he eventually realised that taking care of himself was important not just for his own well-being but also for his relationships. Only if I take care of myself and be happy can I transfer this happiness. I understood that after a long time. The actor, however, does not believe that being responsible towards a family means giving up every personal need. The mindset of having to sacrifice everything - Let me work out for an hour or I have to get some fresh air - all this is important for sanity. When you come back from this, your interaction will be better with the people around you. If you constantly live in tension, how will your interaction be? Everything will be work-related problems, everything will be an interference. You will be giving out these messages, he said. Your kids will only remember how you spoke to them Arvind Swamy went on to speak about what children eventually remember about their parents. He said parents may spend years thinking about the sacrifices they made, while children may remember something much more basic - how their parents spoke to them. Thirty or 40 years will pass by quickly. At that point, you might not be working. At that point, your kids will only remember that whenever they tried to speak to you, you only spoke out of irritation, he said. He pointed out that parents can become focused on the hard work they put in for their children without realising that their children may have a very different memory of those years. You will be thinking of all the hard work you put in. You will be thinking that you sacrificed your happiness for them. This disconnect - you would have worked and done stuff, but could have spoken to me with a smile. Isnt that what makes them happy? According to Arvind, this difference in perspective is often at the heart of the disconnect between parents and children. So this disconnect happens because people have different perspectives. How much I have sacrificed is not whats important. Do what is important to you, he said. He believes making time for things that bring personal happiness or peace is important because otherwise that frustration can spill over into relationships. For that, do whatever makes you feel better. You have to allocate some time to it. If not, you will be transferring all that to others, he said. Arvind Swamys first marriage, children and custody Arvind Swamy married Gayathri Ramamurthy in 1994. The couple have two children, daughter Adhira and son Rudra. They separated in 2003 and later sought divorce by mutual consent. During the divorce proceedings, the couple agreed that their children would remain in the actors custody, while Gayathri would have visitation rights. Their divorce was granted in 2010. Arvind married lawyer Aparna Mukerjee in 2012.

articleTitle: UPSC Prelims 2027 Polity Quiz (Week 183): MCQs on removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, Mahanadi water dispute, and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Prelims 2027 Polity Quiz (Week 183)
description: Are you preparing for UPSC CSE 2027 Prelims? Check your progress and revise your topics through this quiz on Polity and Governance.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative of daily subject-wise quizzes. These quizzes are designed to help you revise some of the most important topics from the static part of the syllabus. Attempt todays subject quiz onPolity and Governanceto check your progress. As we mark the 3rd anniversary of the UPSC Essentials magazine, we thank our readers for being part of this journey. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. Share your views and suggestions in the comment box or write to us at manas.srivastavaindianexpress.com. QUESTION 1 With reference to the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner CEC, consider the following statements 1. A motion for the removal of the CEC can be initiated in either House of Parliament through a notice of motion signed by at least 100 members of the Lok Sabha or 50 members of the Rajya Sabha. 2. The CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. 3. The CEC can be removed only on the ground of proven misbehavior or incapacity. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question tests the constitutional provisions governing the appointment, tenure and removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. It is relevant to Article 324, particularly the special protection accorded to the CEC to ensure the independence of the Election Commission. Explanation - Article 3245 of the Constitution states that the CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Going by Article 1244 of the Constitution, which contains the process for removing a Supreme Court judge, removal can only be on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity. Misbehaviour can comprise any corrupt practices or abuse of office. Over the years, courts have interpreted this to include actions which are incompatible with the office of the CEC or the CECs failure to discharge her official duties. Incapacity refers to a situation where the officer is unable to perform her duties. Hence, statement 3 is correct. - To initiate the removal of the CEC, members of both Houses must bring a notice of motion explicitly alleging misbehaviour or incapacity. To be admitted, an impeachment motion needs to be signed by at least 100 MPs in the Lok Sabha and 50 in the Rajya Sabha. They can consult people and materials to refuse or admit the motion. If the motion is admitted, an enquiry is conducted to examine the validity of the charges. This involves forming a committee to investigate evidence of misbehaviour or incapacity. Hence, statement 1 is correct. - The motion for removal must secure the support of a majority of the total membership of each House and be passed by a two-thirds majority present and voting in both Houses of Parliament. Once passed successfully, the President orders the removal of the CEC. - There is no discretion once the constitutional requirements are met, since the President acts on the advice of Parliament in this context. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 2 Which of the following states are involved in the Mahanadi water dispute? 1. Telangana 2. Odisha 3. Madhya Pradesh 4. Chhattisgarh Select the correct answer using the codes given below a 1 and 2 only b 2, 3 and 4 only c 2 and 4 only d 1, 2, and 4 only Relevance The question tests knowledge of inter-State river water disputes and the geographical course of the Mahanadi River. It is relevant to Indian Geography, federalism and mechanisms for resolving inter-State water disputes. Explanation - The Mahanadi water dispute between Odisha and Chhattisgarh is back in the spotlight, with the Odisha government signalling that the two BJP-ruled states are moving closer to an amicable solution, even as the Opposition BJD has called this bid an eyewash. The Mahanadi is a lifeline for millions of people in both the States. - A meeting between the two CMs was also held in July under the chairmanship of the Union Jal Shakti Minister. At the meeting, the states agreed to share data and information on their respective water requirements with the Central Water Commission. - For Odisha, the Mahanadi is more than a water-sharing dispute. The river is central to irrigation, drinking water, flood management, hydropower and the states broader negotiations with Chhattisgarh and the Centre. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 3 Consider the following Articles of the Constitution of India 1. Article 1943 - It grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. 2. Article 191b - It guarantees freedom of speech and expression. Which of the articles given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question tests knowledge of Fundamental Rights under Article 19 and privileges and immunities of State Legislatures under Article 194. It helps strengthen understanding of constitutional provisions relating to State Legislatures and legislative privileges. Explanation - The Supreme Court will begin hearing a long-pending reference on the scope of legislative privileges, special powers and immunities enjoyed by Parliament and state legislatures to protect their functioning, and whether they can be invoked against citizens, journalists and others on breaching the privileges of the House. At the heart of the case is whether these privileges, under Articles 105 and 194 of the Constitution, can override fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and expression under Article 19. - A seven-judge Constitutional Bench comprising the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Chandrashekhar and V Mohana will hear the matter. - Article 1943 of the Constitution grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. Article 191a guarantees freedom of speech and expression, including press freedom. The case turns on the interplay between these two rights and whether legislative privilege can override the right to free speech. Hence, 1 is correct and 2 is not correct. - Articles 14 and 21 provide for the right to equality and the right to life. The petitioners argue that when legislatures order arrests or imprisonment for alleged breaches of privilege, they affect personal liberty. According to them, any action affecting liberty must satisfy constitutional guarantees of fairness, due process and protection against arbitrariness. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 4 With reference to the Bye-Elections also known as bypolls, consider the following statements 1. The winner of a by-election serves a full 5-year term. 2. A bypoll is not mandatory if the remaining term of the house is less than 1 year. 3. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by-elections must be held within 3 months of the vacancy occurring, barring specific legal exceptions. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question tests understanding of the constitutional and statutory framework governing by-elections in India. It is relevant to Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, including the time limit and exceptions for conducting bypolls. Explanation - Bye-Elections also known as bypolls are used to fill elected offices that have become vacant between general elections. - The elected representative serves only the remainder of the term left by the predecessor. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - A bypoll is not mandatory if the remaining term of the house is less than 1 year, or if the Election Commission certifies that holding it is impractical due to extraordinary circumstances. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Under Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by-elections must be held within 6 months of the vacancy occurring, barring specific legal exceptions. Hence, statement 3 is not correct. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. Source www.eci.gov.in QUESTION 5 With reference to the Legislative Councils in India, consider the following statements 1. The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-half 50 per cent of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. 2. The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than forty. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question tests knowledge of the constitutional provisions governing Legislative Councils under Article 171. It is relevant for understanding State legislature, bicameralism and constitutional provisions related to State legislatures. Explanation - The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-thirdof the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - Provided that the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than forty. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Of the total number of members of the Legislative Council of a State- a as nearly as may be, one-third shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify b as nearly as may be, one-twelfth shall be elected by electorates consisting of persons residing in the State who have been for at least three years graduates of any university in the territory of India or have been for at least three years in possession of qualifications prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament as equivalent to that of a graduate of any such university c as nearly as may be, one-twelfth shall be elected by electorates consisting of persons who have been for at least three years engaged in teaching in such educational institutions within the State, not lower in standard than that of a secondary school, as may be prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament d as nearly as may be, one-third shall be elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State from amongst persons who are not members of the Assembly e the remainder shall be nominated by the Governor. Therefore, option b is the correct answer.
