articleTitle: After nudge from selectors, Harmanpreet Kaur quits as India skipper in all formats
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from captaincy of Indian women's team. (CREIMAS FOR BCCI)
description: The selectors felt it was time to build for the next World Cup cycle. India failed to progress to the knockouts of the T20 World Cup for the second time in a row under Harmanpreet's captaincy
body_raw: A year after leading India to the ODI World Cup, Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as captain of the national womens cricket team in all formats - a surprise decision that she announced through an Instagram post Tuesday, a day after attending a team review meeting with BCCI officials and selectors in Guwahati. The 37-year-old also said in the post that she was ready to continue playing for the country. Now, I am ready to play for the love of the game. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, she posted. The ODI World Cup at home last year was the teams first ever ICC title. But this July, the side failed to progress to the knockout rounds of the T20 World Cup for the second time in a row, prompting the selectors to decide on a change in leadership - although Harmanpreet was keen to continue, BCCI sources told The Indian Express. The decision to move on from Harmanpreet as captain was by the selectors. After the end of the T20 World Cup, a review meeting was planned. But it took place after the Asian Games where the team won gold. Harmanpreet wanted to continue as captain, but the selectors prevailed. The selectors felt it was time to build for the next World Cup cycle. There was no question of split captaincy, the sources said. ALSO READ Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup The Indian Express has learnt that womens team coach Amol Muzumdar, vice-captain Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet met separately with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and womens selection committee chief Amita Sharma in Guwahati. Mandhana 30 took over the captaincy reins from Harman. Harmanpreets last assignment as captain was the Asian Games campaign, where India defended its title. She captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, and also led the team to three Asia Cup titles. She was appointed T20 captain in 2016 and took over the reins of the ODI team in 2022 after Mithali Rajs retirement. India had reached the ODI World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 under Mithali. With Harmanpreet at the helm, India became a top contender in the international arena 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, 2020 T20 World Cup final, 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal and, eventually, the 2025 ODI World Cup title. However, India were knocked out in the group stage of the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups. Not easy decision This is not an easy decision, Harmanpreet wrote on Instagram. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life. I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian womens cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first. In an official statement, BCCI president Mithun Manhas said Harmanpreets contribution as captain will always hold a special place in the history of Indian cricket. ALSO READ Harmanpreet will be able to bat with freedom Coach Kamaldeesh She took on the responsibility at an important stage in the growth of womens cricket and helped the Indian team build on the strong foundation laid by those who came before her. Over the years, she led India through some very important moments and helped the team compete with confidence against the best in the world. The World Cup victory in 2025 will undoubtedly be the defining achievement of her captaincy, Manhas said. Saikia also highlighted the World Cup win in his tribute. Harmanpreet, you can be immensely proud of what you have achieved as captain of India. You embraced the responsibility from the very beginning and went on to lead India through some of the most important moments in its journey, while playing an important role in the growth of Indian womens cricket, he said. You experienced the disappointment of falling short, but continued to believe in the team and its ability to achieve more. That is what made the World Cup victory in 2025 so special. You had been part of the journey for many years and eventually had the opportunity to lead India to its first womens cricket World Cup title. That will always remain one of the great moments in Indian cricket, Saikia said.

articleTitle: Trump suggests Iran to ‘take out’ Los Angeles, San Diego; sparks backlash in US
articleFeaturedImageAlt: trump on Iran
description: The Republican leader was swiftly criticised by California’s Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump has courted controversy for suggesting to a crowd of his supporters in the state of Nebraska that Iran could take out major cities like Los Angeles and San Diego, the two cities held by Democrats that had been a target of his administration. The Republican leader was swiftly criticised by Californias Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans. During a political rally in Nebraska on Monday night, Trump talked about the upcoming midterm elections in November and said that he hoped to see a tremendous victory for his party. Trump cites war costs, upcoming midterms The US President discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and suggested that high prices of fuel, fertiliser, and other products due to the war with Iran that began in February were a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. Referring to Iran, Trump said in Grand Island, Its a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let em take out Los Angeles, let em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and its going to be over with very soon, amid applause from the crowd. Referring to the seven-month-old war, the US President said, Its essentially almost over with. But its going to end very soon, and its going to end one way or the other. California leaders condemn Trumps remarks Californias governor and mayor were quick to criticise Trumps comments. California Governor Gavin Newsom, in an X post, said, After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should take out Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass attacked President Trump for making the remarks, calling them irresponsible threats that could potentially compromise the safety of Americas second-largest city. The role of a president is to protect the country, not to actively threaten it and encourage attacks on American lives, Bass said. Republican leader distances himself from Trump Jim Desmond, a Republican leader running in a redrawn California district near San Diego, distanced himself from President Trumps remarks. I vehemently disagree with President Trumps comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander-in-Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland, Desmond wrote on X. White House defends Trumps comments The White House on Tuesday defended Trumps comments. The media freakout over President Trumps comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadnt been stopped, White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung wrote in a social media post. America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money.

articleTitle: ‘Now I don’t even look at start list’: Gulveer Singh on not fearing other runners
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gulveer Singh became the first Indian to win three middle and long-distance medals in one edition of the Asian Games. (AP)
description: India’s long-distance runner looks to level up after winning a combined five medals at the Commonwealth Games and Asiad
body_raw: There are no starting blocks in long-distance running events like 5000m and 10000m. False starts, like in the faster sprints, isnt a primary worry for a runner, but there are other fears that take its place. Indian long distance runner Gulveer Singh admits that it was only recently that he overcame the fear of the competitors around him. Pehle thoda sochta tha baaki competitors ke baare me. Earlier, I used to think about other competitors. But now I dont even look at the start list, Gulveer told The Indian Express in an interaction facilitated by SAI Media. Gulveer was one of Indias best athletes at the Asian Games 2026 with three medals - silver in 1500m, silver in 10000m and bronze in 5000m. The transformation is visible in the results. He has five major medals this year and will be eyeing the World Athletics Championships next year. Gulveers mindset has changed over the years. Now, he knows that he is operating at the same level as compared to others. So, that really helps when the athlete knows that they belong at the top level, his coach Scott Simmons had told this paper earlier. ALSO READ 5 days, 4 races, 3 medals Gulveer Singhs hectic, but productive, Asiad The other thing that has helped Gulveer is competing regularly with the top athletes who were better than him. The result you see today has come from the fact that I regularly compete with athletes who are better than me. It takes away the fear of competing against better athletes and also keeps pushing me whenever I am against these guys, Gulveer said. Late bloomer shines In the world of long-distance running, Gulveer is a late bloomer who started participating in competitions at the age of 24 after joining the Army and has never competed at the junior level. However, his rapid strides to the top echelons of Indias running depict that he was always meant to be in the space he occupies. When I started running, I had no idea that these strides would take me this far. I ran only to get selected in the army, Gulveer recalled. There is a positive to Gulveer picking up running late-he already possessed a calm mind, and the maturity that the sport needed. When I started competing, I was clear in my head about what I had to do. I think that really helped me at the international level, he said. Learning from past Gulveers participation at the World Athletics Championships in 2025 is something that helped open his eyes to the vast difference between the competition at the Asian level, and the behemoths who competed at the highest echelons of long-distance running. When I competed at the 2025 Worlds, it was my first taste of global competition. It was very different from competing at the Asian Games or Asian Championships, said Gulveer. Before competing at the World Championships in Tokyo, Gulveers only major appearances were at the Asian Games and the Asian Championships. At the Tokyo World Championships, Gulveer was well placed to qualify for the final in the mens 5000m heat but faded away at the end, losing his qualification spot. I think that was a big learning for me. I learnt there how to hold your position in a race. Long-distance running is all about the last few meters and if you fade away in that, all the hard work is gone, said Gulveer. That he learned from his mistake at the World Championships was visible in all of the races at the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games. After the Worlds, I specifically worked on my last kick and staying patient. One needs to know when that last kick has to come, if the athlete doesnt time it right, the athlete will fade away, Gulveer explained. Now, it will be some rest for Gulveer before he travels back to Colorado Springs to train under Scott Simmons for the next season. Ill be back to training soon. Once, the celebrations and felicitations are over here in India, said Gulveer. I have my eyes set on the World Championships next season and as one can see, the progression is on the right path for me at the moment.

articleTitle: 3 children suffer head injuries as ceiling collapses at government school in Udaipur
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Udaipur school ceiling collapse
description: The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party whose members visited different campuses in August.
body_raw: Three children suffered head injuries after the ceiling of their classroom collapsed at a government primary school in Udaipur on Tuesday. Two other students sustained minor injuries in the incident that took place in the Bhindar area. The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party CJP whose members visited campuses in different parts of Rajasthan in August. Tuesdays incident took place around 11 am at Government Primary School, Narada, under Vaniyatalai gram panchayat in the Bhindar police station area, when a portion of the plaster from a classroom ceiling suddenly came down. There were 32 children in the classroom at the time. Headmaster Lal Singh Shaktawat told The Indian Express, Class 1 students Krishna Kumari and Kartik, and Class 5 student Ganeshlal suffered head injuries. All three were taken to Bhindar Government Hospital for treatment and later sent home. Two other students sustained minor injuries. The ceiling collapsed suddenly, injuring the students. Thankfully, no one was severely injured. We sent the children back to their homes by evening. The school, which runs up to Class 5, has 37 students in all, which is why it is common for students of different classes to study in the same room. Authorities were informed of schools condition Shaktawat said the education department had earlier been informed about the poor condition of the building. The building was constructed in 2001 and had become dilapidated. We had already informed the education department about its condition. The last time the school building was repaired was in 2020, he said. Following directions from the education department and the local administration, the school building has now been locked as a precautionary measure. Classes will be shifted to a temporary location near Matajis mandir nearby. The incident comes just over a year after one of Rajasthans worst school-building tragedies. On July 25, 2025, the roof of a government school in Piplodi village of Jhalawar district collapsed, killing seven children and injuring 28 others. The National Human Rights Commission subsequently took cognizance of the incident and sought a report from the Rajasthan government, noting allegations that authorities had been informed about the buildings dilapidated condition. The safety of government schools has again emerged as a major issue in Rajasthan in recent months following the School Thik Karo campaign by the CJP. Its teams visited government schools across the state and highlighted problems ranging from unsafe and dilapidated buildings to schools functioning without proper infrastructure. Some CJP workers were also attacked while visiting a government school in Bagru. The government school at Rampura-Kanwarpura in Jaipurs Bagru area, which had been declared unsafe, was demolished after the CJP campaign highlighted its condition. The government sanctioned around Rs 18 lakh for construction of a new building.

articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer slams maiden T20I ton, leads India to 8-wicket win over West Indies in 1st T20I
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer slammed maiden T20I ton during first India vs West Indies T20I. (CREIMAS)
description: Iyer scored the fastest ton by an Indian in T20Is against West Indies as India chased down 172 in just 14.4 overs with 8 wickets in hand.
body_raw: Playing a captains innings, Shreyas Iyer led from the front by slamming his maiden T20I century to lead India to a comfortable 8-wicket victory over West Indies in the first T20I at Ekana International Cricket Stadium in Lucknow on Tuesday. Iyer scored the fastest ton by an Indian in T20Is against West Indies as India chased down 172 in just 14.4 overs with 8 wickets in hand. Chasing the total, India didnt have the best of starts as they lost both openers Abhishek Sharma 21 and Sanju Samson 11 inside four overs with the scoreboard reading 35. Roston Chase picked up Abhishek in the third over, with Shimron Hetmyer taking a brilliant diving catch while running in from long-off. An over later, Sanju Samson departed, extending his lean patch since the Asian Games, as he sliced a short delivery back to Akeal Hosein, who took the catch off his own bowling. AS IT HAPPENED INDIA VS WEST INDIES 1ST T20I HIGHLIGHTS Thereafter, skipper Shreyas Iyer and Ishan Kishan stabilised the innings with a 137-run partnership. Earlier, all-rounder Naman Dhir had a dream T20I debut, picking up three wickets with his off-spin to help India bowl out West Indies for 171. Dhir finished with impressive figures of 331, while Kuldeep Yadav also scalped 2 for 33 to help India restrict West Indies to a manageable total. Sent into bat, West Indies skipper Shai Hope started the innings in a flurry, smacking Mayank Yadav for four boundaries in the second over to set the tone. The four boundaries forced skipper Shreyas Iyer to replace Mayank with Axar Patel in third over. Arshdeep got the first breakthrough for India, cleaning up Kamil Pooran with a pitch-up delivery. West Indies were dealt another blow in the sixth over when Shimron Hetmyer was run out while going for an unnecessary single. It turned out to be double blow for the West Indies as Axar cleaned up Rovman Powell in the sixth over with a pitch-up delivery after the right-hander went for a huge heave over square-leg. Sherfane Rutherford 56 off 34 gave the much needed impetus to West Indies innings with the left-hander hitting Kuldeep Yadav for two sixes in the ninth over and then smashing Axar for two boundaries and a six in the 11th over. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Tried to softly bend law towards justice: CJ D K Upadhyaya as he bids farewell to Delhi High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Justice DK Upadhyaya
description: With CJ Upadhyaya bidding farewell to the Delhi HC, the second senior-most judge of the High Court — Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre — will now preside over as the acting Chief Justice of Delhi HC.
body_raw: Following his elevation as a judge of the Supreme Court, Delhi High Courts outgoing Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya on Tuesday remarked that he tried to softly bend the law towards justice for deserving litigants when law failed to ensure a just outcome in a case. With CJ Upadhyaya bidding farewell to the Delhi HC, the second senior-most judge of the High Court - Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre - will now preside over as the acting Chief Justice of Delhi HC. As a judge, Ive always tried to bind justice, law and compassion together. Like other judges, I came across unforeseen situations when law was not able to ensure a just outcome in the case, and it appeared isolated from justice. In such situations, I tried to softly bend the law towards justice for the deserving litigant, and to be able to do so has been a blessing for me, he said. CJ Upadhyaya, with his parent high court at Allahabad, has been in charge of Delhi HC since January 2025. Appointed as a judge of the Allahabad HC in November 2011, CJ Upadhyaya is due to retire in June 2027. Prior to Delhi HC, he also served as Chief Justice of Bombay HC. During CJ Upadhyayas tenure at HC, 85 advocates of the Delhi HC were designated as senior advocates. His tenure at Delhi HC was also marked with several important orders. Nearly two months after he took charge, HC judge Justice Yashwant Varma was embroiled in the controversy after alleged unaccounted cash was found at his official residence during a fire, in March 2025. In its aftermath, CJ Upadhyaya had submitted a report on the incident following a preliminary inquiry to then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna with the prima facie opinion that the entire matter warrants a deeper probe.

articleTitle: 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hits Uttarakhand, tremors felt in Delhi-NCR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand earthquake map (Credits: Credits: National Center for Seismology)
description: The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology.
body_raw: A 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hit Uttarakhands Chamoli on Tuesday night, with its tremors felt in the Delhi-NCR region. The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology, which characterised its status as reviewed. Delhi-NCR has experienced several noticeable earthquakes this year. On January 19, 2026, a mild 2.8-magnitude earthquake struck New Delhi, with its epicentre in North Delhi at a shallow depth of about five kilometres. Brief tremors were felt across parts of the capital, but no damage was reported. On April 3, 2026, tremors were felt in Delhi-NCR after a 5.9-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan. The epicentre was near Darawan, and mild shaking was also reported in Punjab, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir and Kargil. No casualties or property damage were immediately reported. For more information Download the BhooKamp App DrJitendraSingh OfficeOfDrJS tummalasrini GSureshNCS ndmaindia - National Center for Seismology NCSEarthquake October 6, 2026 And on June 27 a stronger 6.2-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan, causing tremors in Delhi-NCR and other parts of northern India. The National Centre for Seismology placed its depth at approximately 215 kilometres. What to do during earthquake Here is a quick refresher from the National Disaster Management Authority NDMA on how to stay safe when the ground shakes. If youre indoors Drop, cover and hold on. Get down on the floor, take shelter under sturdy furniture and hold on until the shaking stops. If there is no shelter nearby, crouch in an inside corner and shield your head and face with your arms. Keep away from windows, glass, exterior walls and anything that could topple, such as shelves or light fixtures. If you are in bed, stay there and cover your head with a pillow. If a heavy fixture hangs above you, move carefully to a safer spot. Use a doorway only if it is close by and structurally strong. Stay inside until the shaking stops completely. Most injuries happen when people try to move around or rush out during a quake. Be prepared for power cuts, and for fire alarms and sprinklers to go off. If youre outdoors Stay where you are, but move away from buildings, trees, poles and wires that could collapse or fall. Remain in the open until the shaking ends. Many injuries occur near exterior walls and exits because of falling debris. If youre in a vehicle Pull over as soon as it is safe, avoiding overpasses, power lines and buildings. Stay inside the vehicle until the shaking stops. Afterwards, drive carefully and avoid damaged roads and bridges. If youre trapped under debris Do not light matches or kick up dust. Cover your mouth with a piece of clothing. Signal for help by tapping on a pipe or wall, or by blowing a whistle. Shout only as a last resort, since it can make you inhale dust.

articleTitle: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi detained after hours-long anti-CEC protest, released later
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday evening
description: INDIA bloc MPs alleged 'vote chori', and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
body_raw: Led by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, leaders of INDIA bloc Tuesday stepped up their attack on the Chief Election Commissioner, demanding his resignation before they were detained late in the evening after staging a protest for hours near the Election Commission office in the heart of New Delhi. The leaders were released later in the night. Parliament Street shut down as Gandhi and others tried to march towards the EC office with their supporters, and climbed atop police barricades, before finding their way into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. Through much of the day, Gandhi and Vadra were holed up inside the AIR premises, demanding they be allowed to meet the CEC. They were joined by SPs Akhilesh Yadav, TMCs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, and CPIMs John Brittas. All I want to do is meet the Chief Election Commissioner and tell him that he has done vote chori. I can continue to sit here. I am comfortable here. If they dont want us to sit here, give us some other site, Gandhi said. The march was the latest in a series of protests to press for CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation in the wake of a report in The Indian Express that the two Election Commissioners had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under the CEC, from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. Targeting the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and the RSS chief, Gandhi alleged that the country had been hijacked with the vote chori. What has been done to our country is treason. Nobody is going to escape, he said. The day-long protest began with the march being stopped soon after it started from Parliament House around 10 am, following which the opposition MPs sat on the street outside Akashvani Bhavan, very close to the EC office. As MPs were being detained, Gandhi spoke to his sister seated inside one of the buses and both went inside the Akashvani Bhavan, taking all by surprise. Besides the Gandhi siblings, the Congress leaders who joined them inside the AIR premises included Deepender Hooda, Charanjit Singh Channi, Praniti Shinde, K C Venugopal and Pawan Khera. Several MPs returned to the protest site after being released from detention. In a post on X, Gandhi said, Gyanesh its done bro. Time to resign. MPs from the BJD, which has not been part of the INDIA bloc, also joined the march. DMK and AAP leaders stayed away from the protest.

articleTitle: Anirudh Thapa scores but Uruguay run away 6-1 winners in friendly against India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anirudh
description: Maxi Araujo scores a brace as two-time world champions show more ruthlessness than Brazil on Saturday
body_raw: At around the 22nd minute, Anirudh Thapa found himself in the Uruguay penalty box. His eyes suddenly lit up. Goalkeeper Thaigo Cardozo had spilled a Ryan Williams shot and the ball was bobbing on the ground. Its almost as if time stood still. And sped up in real time as Thapa pounced, saw the resignation in Cardozos eyes and put the ball in the Uruguay net. The Salt Lake Stadium exploded. 138th-ranked India had pulled one out of the hat. The goal mattered little in the context of the 1-6 rout at the hands of the South Americans. But when the final whistle blew, 37,000 spectators seemed content as Thapas goal had allowed them to dream bigger for a while. Ahead of the clash, India coach Khalid Jamil and defender Akash Mishra had stressed on maintaining focus and not conceding early against the 20th-ranked team. With India managing to restrict Brazil in the initial stages, a Uruguay team which had just one win in their last nine international fixtures didnt seem an insurmountable barrier. Especially when they were playing without their star player Federico Valverde, ruled out due to injury. While the hosts couldnt prevent an early goal after Pramveer Singhs errant challenge resulted in a penalty that Darwin Nunez duly converted in the 10th minute, it prompted them into action as India managed to level matters through Thapa. Soon after, inclement weather and lightning forced the match to be stopped for around 35 minutes. That interruption hurt Indias cause as Uruguay struck right after when a low cross by Nahitan Nandez was met by Maxi Araujo and stroked into the India net in the 28th minute. Uruguay had more chances to surge ahead but Araujo shot one over the bar before Nunez, who was through one-on-one with goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu, had his attempted chip blocked. That must have felt good for the custodian after his two individual errors led to goals for Brazil on Saturday. India brought on Sahal Abdul Samad and Bijoy Varghese in the second half while Uruguay added some more steel to their midfield and defence with Lucas Torreira and Guillermo Varela. It made a difference straight away as Torreiras ball was nodded into Rodrigo Zalazars path, who slammed one into the bottom corner to make it 3-1 in the 53rd minute. The proverbial floodgates had opened and Uruguay slotted in another in the 59th minute when Araujo caught Abhishek Singh Tekcham flat-footed. Substitute Juan Manuel Sanabria finished calmly after a superb transitional play to make it 5-1 in the 70th. That was followed by a well-placed goal by Rodrigo Aguirre in the 87th minute as Uruguay showed a more ruthless streak than Brazil managed against the Blue Tigers. Indias best chances in the second half came from Mohammed Sanan, whose check-back left Torreira in his wake but the shot was saved by Cardozo, before the Uruguay keeper was called to action once again when he saved Williams first-time volley.

articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer finds perfect timing for his first T20I century
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer couldn't have timed his maiden T20I ton better. (Express photo by Vishal Srivastav)
description: India were in trouble at 35/2 when the skipper came to bat, but with an unbeaten 102 from 43 balls, he ensured they would be only one winner
body_raw: The last time Shreyas Iyer scored a T20I half-century before Tuesday was nearly three months ago - an unbeaten 80 against England at Bristol. Since then, he had not crossed 30 in 10 matches, with Indias top three often taking the pressure off him. The script changed dramatically at the Ekana Stadium in Lucknow. Chasing 172, Iyer walked in with India 35 India had lost both openers inside the first 21 balls. Roston Chase and Akeal Hosein had found early rhythm with the ball. Iyer absorbed the early pressure before turning the game decisively in Indias favour. The opening came in the sixth over. Shamar Joseph needed to build on the spinners start. Instead, he gave Iyer and India a release. He conceded 12 runs as Iyer went aerial over cover before repeating the treatment against Romario Shepherd. The West Indies kept bowling outside off, but on a pitch offering little movement, Iyer was able to free his arms and find the gaps. AS IT HAPPENED INDIA VS WEST INDIES 1ST T20I HIGHLIGHTS It forced the bowlers to go short. That had been regarded as a weakness in Iyers game. On Tuesday, he repeatedly brought out the pull against the rising delivery and found success. He reached his fifty in 28 balls, but the acceleration was only beginning. After seeing off the pacers, Iyer turned his attention to spin. Hosein was brought back in the 13th over and Iyer gave himself room before launching him over extra cover. The next over brought an assault on Forde, as Iyer struck two sixes before pulling another delivery over the boundary. He was given a reprieve when Joseph could not hold on to a miscued shot towards long-on. He reached his maiden T20I hundred with a six before India completed the chase in just 14.4 overs. Kishans role At the other end, Ishan Kishan found himself playing a different role. Walking in at No.3, he did not try to match Iyers aggression. Instead, he played the perfect supporting act, rotating the strike and waiting for opportunities to attack. His first boundary came when he went back to a slightly short delivery from Chase and whipped it through the leg side. Against Joseph, he then found the boundary through cover before taking advantage of another hit-me delivery from the pacer. He pulled Shepherd for a boundary and later cut Hosein through the off side, while his running kept the chase moving. There was one moment of drama when Kishan miscued a full toss towards deep cover. Forde appeared to have taken the catch, but the TV umpire ruled that the ball had touched the ground. By then, however, the partnership had taken complete control. Kishan stayed unbeaten as he and Iyer added 137 for the third wicket, allowing India to race home with 32 balls to spare. Earlier, Indias spin trio did the heavy lifting after the West Indies threatened to set a daunting score in good batting conditions. After Arshdeep Singh and Mayank Yadav failed to hit their straps early, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav and Naman Dhir combined to take seven wickets for 90 runs, recovering from a middle-overs assault by Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford to keep the total manageable. After Shimron Hetmyer was run out, Axar dismissed Rovman Powell for nought to leave the West Indies 443 after six overs. But Hope and Rutherford then shifted the momentum, taking on Kuldeep and forcing Iyer to look elsewhere. Kuldeep, playing his first T20I since February, conceded 24 in his first two overs as Rutherford lofted him over cover and Hope swept him over wide long-on. Iyer brought him back after Hopes dismissal at 107 Then came the turnaround. Kuldeep found his lengths and Roston Chase fell lbw, going back to a delivery he should have played forward to. His final two overs cost only nine runs and brought two wickets, including Matthew Forde. Dhir, meanwhile, made an immediate impact on debut. After being handed the ball, he dismissed Hope for 52 before returning to remove Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer. His three wickets gave India the control they needed. Axars miserly spell, Kuldeeps comeback and Dhirs three wickets ensured India recovered despite the pacers indiscipline. The late 36-run stand between Rutherford and Akeal Hosein gave the West Indies something to defend, but the spinners had already done enough to keep the target within reach. Brief Scores West Indies 171 all out in 19.1 overs Sherfane Rutherford 56, Shai Hope 52 Naman Dhir 331, Axar Patel 226, Kuldeep Yadav 233 lost to India 1722 in 14.4 overs Shreyas Iyer 102 not out, Ishan Kishan 37 by 8 wickets.

articleTitle: 2026 Physics Nobel: The science of ‘neutrinos’, ‘ghost’ particles that can reveal universe’s mysteries
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, Nobel Prize in Physics 2026, Francis Halzen, IceCube Neutrino Observatory, high-energy neutrinos, astrophysical origin neutrinos, Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, University of Wisconsin Madison, South Pole ice neutrino tracking, cosmic particles discovery, physics Nobel winner 2026, Francis Halzen Nobel Prize, Nobel Physics Prize 2026, Francis Halzen, IceCube Neutrino Observatory, high-energy neutrinos, astrophysical neutrinos, Nobel Prize Physics winner 2026, neutrino discovery, Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, University of Wisconsin, South Pole neutrino observatory, 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, Nobel Prize in Physics 2026, Francis Halzen, IceCube Neutrino Observatory, high-energy neutrinos, astrophysical origin neutrinos, Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, University of Wisconsin Madison, South Pole ice neutrino tracking, cosmic particles discovery, physics Nobel winner 2026, Francis Halzen Nobel Prize, Nobel Physics Prize 2026, Francis Halzen, IceCube Neutrino Observatory, high-energy neutrinos, astrophysical neutrinos, Nobel Prize Physics winner 2026, neutrino discovery, Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, University of Wisconsin, South Pole neutrino observatory
description: Francis Halzen, who was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, found a new way to study neutrinos — by turning a block of ice under the Antarctic into a detector for these tiny, elusive particles
body_raw: Neutrinos, very small sub-atomic particles produced mainly in nuclear reactions in stars, are among the most abundant particles in the universe, second only to photons or light particles. And they can reveal a huge amount of new information about the universe. The problem has been that they are extremely difficult to detect, the reason they are often described as ghost particles. The quest to detect neutrinos, and attempts to study them, have already led to several Nobel Prize wins. Another one was added on Tuesday, with the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics being awarded to Francis Halzen, a Belgian-American scientist who designed an elaborate set-up under ice sheets in Antarctica to detect these elusive particles. The IceCube facility in Antarctica is not the first observatory to detect neutrinos. Neutrinos were first proposed in the 1930s and first detected in the 1950s. Several observatories around the world are dedicated to detecting and studying these particles. Studying distant space What the IceCube facility managed to do was something unique. It was successful in detecting a special variety of high-energy neutrinos that was coming from far away in space. Till now, only those neutrinos that originated in the close vicinity of the Earth, primarily being produced in the Sun, were being detected. Most of the neutrinos passing through the Earth are produced in the nuclear processes inside the Sun. For scientists, the detection of extra-galactic neutrinos has opened a new source of information about the universe. Initially, visible light was the only tool available to scientists to study the cosmic phenomena. Then, detectors were developed for the full electromagnetic spectrum of radiation and for cosmic rays. The detection of gravitational waves in 2015 opened an entirely new window for scientists looking at the universe. Extra-galactic neutrinos add another dimension of possibilities. Together these different kinds of signals enable what is called multi-messenger astronomy, the ability to study the same cosmic event using different kinds of signals, said D Indumathi, a scientist at the Bengaluru-based Indian Institute of Astrophysics who was formerly associated with Indias effort to build a neutrino detector. Shy particles The reason neutrinos are so difficult to detect is that they have an extremely low propensity to interact with matter. The Nobel Prize committee described them as the shyest particle. They simply pass through very dense regions of matter without any disturbance. A very common example often cited is the fact that nearly 65 billion neutrinos pass through human finger nails every second without anyone ever noticing. Because they are also electrically neutral, they do not respond to electromagnetic fields the way charged particles do. The detections happen on the very rare occasions that they do interact with matter. That happens to, maybe, one in billions or trillions of neutrinos. That is why neutrino observatories the world over are very large facilities, built in extremely isolated, often underground locations, that maximise the chances of interaction and minimise noise. The elusive nature of neutrinos is also what makes them particularly interesting to study. They pass through regions of cosmic space that other signals may never be able to cross. Very dense regions in space, for example, can absorb or scatter all electromagnetic radiations, but neutrinos simply flow through. They can thus reveal processes happening within or beyond that dense region, which are otherwise inaccessible to scientists. The IceCube facility The 82-year-old Halzen, who had been studying cosmic rays since the 1960s, came to know of the attempts of Soviet researchers to build a neutrino detector in Antarctica, a press release from the Nobel Prize committee said. When a neutrino collides with an atomic nucleus in the ice, it creates an electric spark. This produces radio waves which could be detected using radio antennas. Halzen thought of a slightly different idea. He realised that light sensors could be installed in glacier ice. These sensors could produce flashes of light from collisions of neutrinos with the nucleus of ice atoms. The area around the South Pole was a favourable location. It was isolated and, at significant depths, there was a lot of darkness with no disturbance from other radiations or signals. He discussed his ideas with some of his colleagues and did most of the theoretical work on designing an observatory deep below the ice-sheets. IceCube is one cubic kilometer of ice equipped with over 5,000 light sensors on long cables, along with an overground facility where signals are collected. On the rare occasion when the neutrino interacts with an atomic nucleus of ice, a charged particle is produced. If that charged particle travels faster than the speed of light in ice, it produces a faint glow. From the characteristics of this glow, scientists are able to reconstruct the energy and direction of the neutrino involved in the collision. This exquisite set-up became operational in 2011. By that time, it had already recorded a couple of events that suggested the involvement of extra-galactic neutrinos. In 2013, the observatory presented the first evidence of having detected very high-energy neutrinos. Since then several such incidents have been recorded and verified. Its a very special detector and the work that Halzen has done is really very exciting. It has opened new avenues for astronomy and astrophysics, said Naba K Mondal, former project director of India-based Neutrino Observatory INO, a much-delayed effort to build a neutrino detector in India. In neutrino research circles, this award to Halzen was expected for a few years. INO was supposed to be located initially in Kerala and then in Tamil Nadu but ran into opposition from local and political groups over land acquisition and environmental grounds. A new location is yet to be finalised.

articleTitle: Police issue notices to MPSC protesters, coaching classes; Commissioner calls protest ‘illegal’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MPSC paper leak, MPSC protests, MPSC protests intensify, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Protest enters Day 6, AAP's Sanjay Singh joins protesters
body_raw: Terming the ongoing protest in Pune over the MPSC paper leak illegal, Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar said that police issued over 70 notices to protesters, coaching classes, and Telegram channels in connection with the protest. The notices were issued two to three days ago, he added. The protest is illegal, there is no permission to do it. It is causing inconvenience to the general commuters and the leaders are coming and giving provocative speeches inciting students. This is not proper and not within the legal framework. So please withdraw from the agitation is what we have said in the notices, Kumar told The Indian Express. On the future course of action of the police and whether the protesters had been given any time period to withdraw the protest, Kumar said, Time period, not really. But we are keeping a close watch on the developments and we have been exercising extreme tact and patience so as to not let a conflict situation happen. We are hoping that the agitating students realise that they are doing something illegal and in contravention of rules and regulations. But well intervene appropriately as and when required. Leaders including Rohit Pawar, who has been leading the protest, had not been issued any notice, the commissioner added. He said that no FIRs had been filed, other than an FIR filed by a journalist who was allegedly attacked by a person at the protest. The protest demanding resignation of Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar continued for its sixth day on Tuesday. Students gathered at the SM Joshi bridge in large numbers at night as various political leaders addressed them. Earlier in the day, the protesters carried out a symbolic last rites ceremony targeting the MPSC Chairman. Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh joined the protesters on Tuesday. I have been told that along with MPSC, papers of talati, drugs inspector, health recruitment, PMC, BMC, teacher recruitment, MMRDA, and MH-CET, all papers have been leaked. And the paper leak that got the whole country on the ground, NEET paper was also leaked. This is a paper leak government, Sanjay Singh alleged. He added, When I asked why is Vivek Bhimanwar MPSC chairperson not resigning, I was told that Bhimanwar and Devendra Fadnavis jodi is like Jai and Veeru. There is a lot of love between them. And he is not ready to take his resignation. Beware of the poision of Hindu-Muslim that they try to fill in your brain during elections. And remember, those who could not be of God Ram referring to the Ram Mandir donation theft, they can never be yours either, said Singh. The protesters are occupying the area near SM Joshi bridge. Two other protest spots have also emerged at Lal Bahadur Shastri Road, and Alka Talkies chowk, with all groups having different demands. Protesters have been demanding the resignation of the MPSC chairperson over the leak of the Drug Inspector examination held in March this year.

articleTitle: As MPSC protests intensify, Pune BJP warns Rohit Pawar against bandh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MPSC paper leak, Pune BJP warns Rohit Pawar against bandh, Pune BJP, Rohit Pawar bandh warning, Rohit Pawar, MPSC protests, MPSC protests intensify, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Pawar along with aspirants of MPSC is holding the protest seeking the resignation of MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar.
body_raw: BJP in Pune on Tuesday warned NCPSP MLA Rohit Pawar against holding a bandh, as part of ongoing protest by MPSC aspirants in the city. Pawar along with aspirants of MPSC is holding the protest seeking the resignation of MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar. The NCPSP leader reportedly said that if their demand is not met in the next two days then they will call Pune bandh, stopping all activities in the city as part of protest. Reacting to Pawars statement, Mayor Manjusha Nagpure and BJP leader Ganesh Bidkar said, We have heard of Pune bandh likely to be called for MPSC protest. We warn those who will do it. We will come on streets against bandh to ensure normal life is not affected by citizens. Nagpure said it was democratic right of anyone to protest and we are not against it but this is politically motivated. The participation of political leaders MNS chief Raj Thackeray and Shiv SenaUBT leader Sanjay Raut along with Congress and NCPSP leaders indicate its politicisation, she said, adding the MPSC aspirants should discuss their issues with the Maharashtra government and not cause problem to citizens of Pune. Chief Minister Devendra Fadanavis has held discussion on the issue of demands by MPSC aspirants so there is no meaning holding a protest in Pune, Nagpure said.

articleTitle: Congestion ahead: Accurate Google Maps update on Barapullah traffic expected soon
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Google Maps, Google maps app, Google Maps accurate traffic update on Barahpullah, Google maps app accurate traffic update on Barahpullah, Google Maps accurate traffic update, Google maps app accurate traffic update, Delhi Traffic Police, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Police also examining the possibility of regulating or diverting traffic towards NH-24, wherever feasible
body_raw: The Delhi Traffic Police is coordinating with Google Maps to ensure that the traffic situation on the newly opened Barapullah Phase-III corridor is accurately reflected on the app, officers said on Tuesday. This comes a day after the Delhi Traffic Police on Monday said in a post on X that with the app showing the route as relatively clear, commuters are being directed towards the already congested stretch.A drone survey had identified a major bottleneck at the Sundial Park merger near Sarai Kale Khan where lanes merge into the existing Barapullah corridor. Traffic Police officers said this is adding to the traffic load as vehicles that would otherwise use DND or NH-24 turns towards the new corridor, choking it further. The newly opened corridor is attracting substantial traffic that would otherwise use NH-24 and DND, thereby increasing the traffic load, an official said. The Traffic Police said the issue on the navigation app will be sorted out in a few days. PWD flags misinformation Public Works Department PWD officials have also blamed Google Maps for feeding misinformation to commuters, exacerbating the lockjam. There is some misinformation on Google Maps apparently, it is not updating real-time traffic information for commuters to properly navigate, causing more congestion on the stretch, PTI quoted an official as having said. Officials also said that despite a recent meeting with the Traffic Police and the National Highways Authority of India NHAI, no solution has been reached so far. Appropriate traffic-control measures and signals at suitable merging points may also be considered to regulate the inflow of vehicles and prevent excessive accumulation, Traffic Police officers said. The Traffic Police is also examining the possibility of regulating or diverting traffic towards NH-24, wherever feasible. Officers, meanwhile, also pointed to a traffic signal on the corridor that has no electricity connection yet, stating that once functional, it is expected to help regulate traffic entering the corridor. A request for an electricity connection has been sent to the BSES, the official said. Barapullah Phase-III flyover was inaugurated on September 29 and opened to commuters on September 30. The corridor has since witnessed heavy traffic and congestion. Senior Traffic Police personnel and PWD officials had on October 1 conducted a joint aerial inspection using drones. It was attended by Joint Commissioner of Police Traffic Sanjay Tyagi, Additional Commissioner of Police Traffic Dinesh Kumar Gupta and Deputy Commissioner of Police Southern Range Sandeep Gupta. The survey identified a sharp, almost rectangular geometry at the merger, resulting in an abrupt convergence of traffic and a bottleneck. There is a significant mismatch in lane capacity at the merging point. Multiple streams of traffic are converging towards the existing Barapullah corridor, which has comparatively limited lane capacity, an official had said. A senior traffic police officer said that they had asked the PWD to work on the curvature near Sundial park patch of the Barapullah flyover. articleTitle: Buying medicines at a UP hospital? The price will be on display from Nov 1
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UP government, UP government hospital pharmacies, UP government hospital pharmacies display prices of medicines, prices of medicines, Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (UPFSDA), Lucknow news, Uttar pradesh news, Indian express, Current affairs
description: The move is aimed at improving price transparency, particularly for patients buying medicines from hospital pharmacies where they may have limited alternatives
body_raw: The Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration UPFSDA has directed pharmacies operating from hospitals across the state to display price lists based on the actual procurement and sale rates of medicines from November 1. This comes after an inspection by the Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration UPFSDA found a staggering gap between the procurement prices of medicines and the maximum retail prices MRPs printed on their packs, with the MRP of some drugs found to be several times higher - as high as 67 times-than the price at which hospitals procure them. The department has also directed all retail pharmacies to create public websites displaying their licence number, appointed pharmacist, licensed premises and stock details. The information will have to be updated on weekly basis, it is learnt. The move is aimed at improving price transparency, particularly for patients buying medicines from hospital pharmacies where they may have limited alternatives, officials said. The department has pointed to the cost-plus model followed in some government medical colleges for expensive medicines, including cancer drugs, high-end antibiotics and costly injections. Under this model, the price charged to patients is linked to the hospitals actual procurement cost rather than simply the printed MRP. Seeks action against drug overpricing The UPFSDA also sought action by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority NPPA on drug pricing after inspections found that patients at some hospitals were being charged up to 67 times the procurement price of medicines. The department has written to the NPPA, seeking a review of drug trade margins, MRP fixation and price controls on high-margin medicines and medical devices. The findings followed inspections of more than 200 pharmacies in 22 medical colleges and 30 government and private hospitals across the state. The UPFSDA said the wide gap was found between the price to retailer PTR paid by hospitals and the price ultimately charged from patients. It argued that patients should receive the benefit of the high discounts the hospitals often get from manufacturers and suppliers. Under the present system, the MRP is printed on the package while institutional purchases are often negotiated on the basis of the highest discount. This could leave patients unaware of the actual procurement cost, reads the letter written by UPFSDA Commissioner and Secretary Roshan Jacob. The UPFSDA also flagged instances where medicines of the same brand and manufacturer carried different MRPs for different institutional supplies. It has raised concerns over contract-manufactured brands supplied to hospitals that may not be readily available in the general retail market. The UPFSDA has asked the NPPA to consider capping trade margins on high-MRP medicines and medical devices after reviewing margins across the supply chain. It has also sought a rationalised system for fixing MRPs that factors in manufacturing costs and permissible post-manufacturing expenses. The department has further suggested bringing high-margin medicines supplied to hospitals under the price-control framework of DPCO-2013. It has also sought stronger enforcement of DPCO provisions, including consideration of bringing violations within the ambit of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The department argued that the issue is not merely about pharmacy margins but also about transparency in the drug supply chain and ensuring that the benefit of institutional procurement reaches patients.

articleTitle: Naman Dhir had barely bowled in IPL. Then came his 3/31 on India debut
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Naman Dhir
description: Despite limited IPL bowling under the Impact Player rule, Naman Dhir showed on his T20I debut that he remains a genuine bowling option, taking 3/31 against West Indies in Lucknow.
body_raw: For a player who had bowled just 8.4 overs without a wicket in his IPL career, Naman Dhir could hardly have made a stronger case for his bowling. The Impact Player rule may have reduced his opportunities at Mumbai Indians, but the 26-year-old insisted he was ready. Ive been bowling for a long time. Its not like Ive just started. In IPL, yes, theres an impact player rule, so you see me bowling less. But its not like I havent bowled, Ive bowled a lot and Ive had a great experience here too. Ive got wickets, I hope Ill keep doing well in the future, he said after taking 331 on his T20I debut against West Indies in Lucknow. IPL prepares you for international cricket. Theres a lot of competition there. So I guess if youre playing IPL with a team like Mumbai Indians, then youre prepared for a big level, so you dont feel so much pressure coming here, as I feel right now, he added. His performance also showed that the lack of bowling in the IPL had not left him short of match practice. Dhir said he has continued to bowl regularly in practice and is comfortable handling different workloads. Theres an impact player rule in IPL. Its not like I dont practise I practise there too. Its the same here too. So theres nothing new for me if I get 4 overs, 2 overs, if I get 6 or 7 overs in one-day, theres nothing new for me. Its a normal thing for me. I just have to focus on my plans and try to execute them. Dhirs three wickets came after he watched Axar Patel bowl in the powerplay and felt the slower pace was helping him on the turning pitch. I saw Axar bhai bowling in the powerplay, so he was bowling a little slow. It was turning. And in my mind, I thought if I bowl a little slow with the wicket gripping, I can get them out. So I just stuck to my basic plans and bowled, and I got good results, he said. There was a personal side to the call-up too. Dhir was at the Ranji Trophy camp in the PCA when he got the news, having just come off a good tournament for himself and his team. Obviously, it was a great feeling when I got the call. I was in the Ranji Trophy camp, in PCA, our tournament had just ended, a very good tournament had gone for me, for our team, so it was a surreal feeling. I was with my friends, so right away I called my father, he was emotional I got a little emotional. Obviously, every kid has a dream to play for the country, so if you represent the country, if your name is mentioned in the team, its a big deal, especially, I am from a small town, so especially for me, no one has played from there yet, so its a big deal for me, its a big deal for the area around us. Dhir also made it clear that while his batting may get more attention, he has continued to work hard on his bowling. Even if you havent seen me bowl, but Im bowling as much as Ive come here Ive practised as much as Ive come here, so its not like Im a batting all-rounder or a bowling all-rounder, yes, my batting is a plus point, but at the same time, Im working as hard as Im bowling.

articleTitle: ‘Nothing (left) to say’: Delhi court pulls up police for lax MCOCA probe
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Crime syndicate leader free for 6 years, delhi Crime syndicate leader free for 6 years, Delhi Police, Delhi judge police efforts mockery, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Leader of alleged crime syndicate ‘roamed free’ for 6 years; police claims of making ‘best efforts’ to investigate are ‘nothing short of mockery’, says judge
body_raw: More than six years ago, Delhi Police invoked one of the toughest laws at their disposal against an alleged leader of a crime syndicate who was named in at least two cases of murder at the time. When police finally arrested him in February this year, another eight cases had been registered against him. This week, a Delhi court expressed exasperation at the delay in the investigation-and rejected the polices claim that they had made their best efforts. If according to the Addl. DCP this is the best effort, then this court has nothing to say, Special MCOCA Judge Gaurav Rao of Rouse Avenue Court said in his order passed on Monday October 5. The court pulled up all the officers who have investigated the case for the last six years, and ordered an inquiry into the delay in the investigation. Three Additional Deputy Commissioners of Police-Lokeshwaran, Ravinandan BM, and Rishi Kumar-and the Investigating Officers IOs, Assistant Commissioners of Police ACPs Rakesh Kumar, SK Gaur, and Vipin Kumar Retd were present in court. The fourth IO in the case, ACP Vivek Bhagat, was not present physically. Earlier in the day, ACP Bhagat and 11 other officers had been promoted as Addl DCPs. However, in view of an ongoing inquiry on an allegation of sexual harassment against Bhagat, the promotion was put in abeyance late on Monday evening. Judge Gaurav Rao was perusing a report submitted by police on their investigation against Mukesh, an alleged leader of a crime syndicate operating from Outer Delhis Narela. Police had booked him under the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 MCOCA in September 2020. Mukesh was accused in 20 FIRs at the time, including two cases of murder, one case of attempted murder, and cases of robbery and dacoity. By the time he was arrested in February 2026, he had been named in another eight cases, including cases of murder, robbery, and kidnapping. Mukesh allegedly had close links with the gang led by the notorious Jitender Mann alias Gogi, who was once one of Delhis most feared gangsters. Gogi was shot dead inside Rohini Court in September 2021. The report submitted by police failed to address the query by this court, and though the lapses as well as the considerable delay in the investigation is writ large from the record, still the Addl DCP, Outer North District, said the police officials have made best efforts in the present case and are still making their best efforts. If according to the Addl. DCP this is the best effort, then this court has nothing to say, the judge said. Perhaps the Addl. DCP is insensitive to the legislative intent behind MCOCA. MCOCA was enacted to put a halt to the menace of organized crime which posed poses a serious threat to civil society. However, if despite invoking the strongest provisions of MCOCA, the accused persons are allowed to roam free, commit heinous offences, including murder as per their whims and fancies, then.it defeats the legislative intent behind the.statute, he added. The court had asked the DCP, Outer North District to file a report listing the cases against the accused, who were allegedly part of the syndicate. It had also sought an explanation as to why arrests were not made in the case. The Additional DCPs had appeared in court on behalf of the DCP. The claims of Best Efforts of the Addl. DCP is nothing short of mockery, the judge said. In fact, in his report, the DCP, Outer North District, made a reference to a circular dated 11.07.2024 issued by the Police Headquarters.for expeditious investigation and timely arrest of accused persons. Yet in the 6 years during which the accused persons were not arrested, investigation qua them was not completed, and the same gave the accused persons more time and opportunity to commit more crimes, he added. It seems that the Addl. DCP feels opines that he is not answerable to either the court or the general public who have all this while borne the brunt of the criminal activities of the crime syndicate, the court said. The court also mentioned an accused named Pradeep, who is alleged to be involved in a large number of cases including murder and robbery. Yet he Pradeep was arrested only on 16.4.2026. Hence, just like accused Mukesh, the said accused kept indulging in criminal activities even after invoking MCOCA, the judge noted in his order. The court described the report of the DCP as an eyewash, and directed that a detailed inquiry and appropriate action be taken against all erring officials and IOs for the delay in the investigation, and for not working in sync with the intent of the statute MCOCA, which permitted more crimes to happen. He directed a copy of the order be sent to the Commissioner of Delhi Police. In an earlier order dated September 18, the judge had said MCOCA was invoked in September 2020 and accused persons were arrested only in February 2026. It emerges from the record that the accused persons continued to be involved in other criminal activities during this period of around 5 and years. One of the purposes of invoking MCOCA is to curb organized crime, however, if the accused persons, despite invoking MCOCA keep roaming free, are not arrested for the period of 6 years and most importantly keep indulging in criminal activities then the entire rational behind invoking MCOCA gets frustrated, is rendered futile. Mukesh has a criminal record going back more than a decade, and is suspected of heading a syndicate involved in murder, attempt to murder, robbery, extortion, Arms Act offences, and criminal conspiracy in parts of Delhi and Haryana. He first came on the radar of police in 2012 and was soon seen as a habitual offender. Cases have been registered against him at several police stations, including Narela, Alipur, Swaroop Nagar, Bawana, Kanjhawala, Samaipur Badli, and Shahbad Dairy in Delhi, and in Jhajjar and Rewari in Haryana.
