articleTitle: Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case: Supreme Court closes proceedings; keeps questions of law open
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case, TN Assembly privilege case, Supreme Court, Supreme Court Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case, Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case proceedings closed, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Disposing of the matter as having become infructuous, the bench, however, said that the questions of law would remain open to be decided in appropriate proceedings in the future.
body_raw: WITH THE 2003 Tamil Nadu case that triggered a reference to its seven-judge bench on the question of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech having been withdrawn, the Supreme Court on Tuesday closed proceedings in the matter, while leaving the question of law open to be decided on a future occasion. The bench presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu Assembly, which formed the basis of the reference, was withdrawn by the Assembly in 2004. The bench, also comprising Justices Aravind Kumar, P K Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul Pancholi, Shree Chandrashekhar and V Mohana, said that the July 30, 2004 Assembly resolution withdrawing the earlier resolution of November 7, 2003 was not specifically brought to the notice of this Court. It also escaped notice when it made the reference to the seven-judge bench. Disposing of the matter as having become infructuous, the bench, however, said that the questions of law would remain open to be decided in appropriate proceedings in the future. The sequence of events dates back to a 2003 article in the The Hindu newspaper, criticising the then CM J Jayalalithaa and her government. Taking offence, the Assembly concluded that it amounted to a breach of privilege of the House. Soon after the November 7, 2003, resolution, police arrested The Hindu Editor N Ravi, Executive Editor Malini Parthasarathy, Bureau Chief V Jayant, Special Correspondent Radha Venkatesan and Publisher S Rangarajan. The journalists challenged this before the Supreme Court, which stayed the arrest on November 10, 2003. But with the matter raising significant constitutional questions of the privilege of the House vis-a-vis right to free speech, the top court in December 2003 referred it to a five-judge bench. The five-judge bench in turn referred it to a seven-judge bench, noting that there were conflicting views on the issue.

articleTitle: Woman held for abducting homeless infant, planned to sell baby to UP man for Rs 6 lakh: Ahmedabad Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Woman held for abducting homeless infant, Woman arrested for abducting homeless infant, abducting homeless infant, homeless infant abduction, Ahmedabad news, Gujarat news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Although Parmar intended to hand over the abducted child to another individual, they panicked, abandoned the infant in the New Ranip area and attempted to flee. The child was soon reunited with the relieved parents.
body_raw: AT 315 am on October 2, a homeless couple reached Sabarmati railway station in Ahmedabad, requesting the police to find their 37-day-old child who was allegedly abducted from their sleeping spot on a footpath outside Ahvadiya lake in the citys New Ranip area. Several teams of the local police, including the crime branch, were coordinated, and the first step of investigation, checking the CCTV footage, showed a female suspect, now identified as Jinal Govind Parmar 21, abducting the child from its bed. Checkpoints were established at all railway stations, bus terminals and the airport to apprehend her. Although Parmar intended to hand over the abducted child to another individual, they panicked, abandoned the infant in the New Ranip area and attempted to flee. The child was soon reunited with the relieved parents. Once the child was identified, we tracked the movements of the female accused and apprehended her, said Ahmedabad City Commissioner of Police Anupam Singh Gahlaut at a press conference on Tuesday. Jinal Parmar, a resident of Wadhwan, Surendranagar, was apprehended near Sabarmati Railway Station and subjected to detailed interrogation. Following the emergence of preliminary facts confirming her involvement, legal action was taken against her she was handed over to the Sabarmati Police Station and scheduled to be produced before the local court, said a statement from the Crime Branch. Plot Unravels From Kidnapping to Trafficking Police said, Interrogation of the arrested female accused revealed that two individuals from Uttar Pradesh, who were juveniles in conflict with the law, had assisted in the crime. Before they could flee back to their hometown in Uttar Pradesh, the Crime Branch team, acting on the basis of photographs found on the female accuseds mobile phone, conducted searches at bus and railway stations, promptly apprehended both juveniles, and handed them over to the Sabarmati Police Station. The police also claimed that Jinal Parmar told them that an individual from Uttar Pradesh, a former colleague from a quick commerce platform, lured her with a financial reward of Rs 6 lakh to illegally arrange for a child under the age of 1 years, on behalf of a person named Bhuvaneshwar alias Bhanu. She had thus allegedly executed the crime with the help of the two juveniles in conflict with the law. To carry out the child abduction, the arrested female accused had initially conducted reconnaissance in the New Ranip area and its surroundings, as well as in the vicinity of Sola Civil Hospital, said the police. The Source of the Demand Since the man who has contacted Jinal Parmar and the man who had contacted him in turn, were both located in Uttar Pradesh, a Crime Branch team was dispatched to apprehend them. The team successfully arrested the accused-identified as Bhuvaneshwar alias Bhanu Jatav a resident of Badaun currently residing in Noida - who was involved in the childs abduction and had offered Rs 6 lakh for the child. Interrogation is underway to trace the prime conspirators, said the police.

articleTitle: Nagaland woman pulled towards car by 3 men at 5-star hotel, friends attacked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nagaland woman pulled towards car, Nagaland woman harassed, Nagaland woman friend harassed, Chanakyapuri, Nagaland woman friend harassed in Chanakyapuri, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Police said the woman’s friends intervened, following which the accused allegedly attacked them with hockey sticks and iron rods. "One of the friends suffered injuries to his teeth...," an officer said.
body_raw: A woman from Nagaland was allegedly harassed and forcibly pulled towards a Mercedes car by three men in the parking lot of a five-star hotel in Chanakyapuri early Sunday. When her friends intervened, the men allegedly assaulted them with hockey sticks and iron rods, police said. The incident took place around 3.30 am Sunday, police said. According to a complaint filed by the woman, she had visited the hotel with friends. While they were leaving, three men, who were travelling in a white Mercedes, allegedly approached them, tried to stop the woman and attempted to pull her into the vehicle. Police said the womans friends intervened, following which the accused allegedly attacked them with hockey sticks and iron rods. One of the friends suffered injuries to his teeth., an officer said. The accused allegedly fled from the spot in their car after police reached the location. The complainant had noted down the cars registration number, which helped investigators trace the men, police said. The three accused were booked at Chanakyapuri police station. The woman was taken to RML Hospital, where she underwent a medical examination. Police said the case was registered on the basis of her complaint and the medical report. Police are examining CCTV camera footage from the hotel and other evidence to establish the sequence of events. The medical reports are also being examined to ascertain the injuries suffered by those involved, they said.

articleTitle: Divorce, isolation, extremist videos: Inside the chargesheet of Mumbai ‘lone wolf’ case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mira Road stabbing case, lone wolf attack Mumbai, Mira Road stabbing case, Devendra Fadnavis self-radicalisation, Zaib Zubair Ansari arrest, self-radicalisation India, Maharashtra ATS probe, Devendra Fadnavis statement, religious hate crime Mumbai, Zaib Zubair Ansari arrest, Thane security guards attack, ISIS radicalisation suspicion, online extremism India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita charges, Mumbai crime news, Indian express
description: Zaib Ansari, accused of stabbing two guards after asking their religion, was radicalised by videos of preachers like Anwar al-Awlaki, says the ATS. His lawyer says he has schizophrenia
body_raw: A recent divorce, being asked by his landlord to leave his rented home, and his obsessive food habits, including a distrust of food cooked by strangers, drove a US-returned man to further despair before he carried out a lone wolf attack in Mumbais Mira Road, stabbing two security guards near his residence on April 27 after asking their religion, says the nearly 2,500-page chargesheet filed by the Anti-Terrorism Squad ATS last week. Zaib Ansari 31 had been self-radicalised by watching online videos of extremist preachers, the chargesheet says. The two guards were injured and later discharged from hospital. The ATS has invoked the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act UAPA against Ansari, who is in jail, and claimed that a note found at his home said lone wolves will pounce on you. Investigators first examined whether anyone had guided Ansari but found no such evidence, an official said. Based on his interrogation and other evidence, we have ruled out any outsider being involved in this. Ansari was mentally disturbed, the official said, and watching videos of preachers such as Anwar al-Awlaki on social media radicalised him. Al-Awlaki was a radical American Muslim cleric of Yemeni descent linked to a series of terror attacks globally. He was further disturbed by reports of killings of children in Palestine, the official said. Ansari moved from the US in 2019. In the US, he made money coaching students in tennis, but he had no regular source of income in India, the agency found. After his divorce, he was living alone, and his landlord asked him to leave because she did not want to rent to bachelors. These factors, along with the attacks on Palestine, drove him to extreme content online, which radicalised him over six to eight months, an officer said. While his family members are based in the US, we have recorded the statement of his mother who had come down to visit him and his Kurla-based uncle with whom he was initially staying, the official said. During earlier court proceedings, Ansaris lawyer told the court that he has schizophrenia and was previously on medication. The lawyer also said Ansari eats only vegetarian food that he prepares himself, and never eats food cooked by others, not even at a relatives home or a family gathering. Police officials too initially faced trouble over his food while he was in custody.

articleTitle: IIT Bombay puts ceiling fans to a vote after student’s suicide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT-B student dies by suicide, iit Bombay student dies by suicide, IIT Bombay, IIT Bombay students protest, ChatGPT, examination question paper on ChatGPT, Mumbai news, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The survey is part of a wider wellness overhaul after Sahil Wakode's death, as his parents, who allege caste discrimination, continue their hunger strike
body_raw: As part of ongoing efforts to improve student safety, comfort and hostel living conditions, feedback is being collected regarding possible alternatives of ceiling-mounted fans in hostel rooms, the form states. Its purpose, it adds, is to understand students preferences regarding fan type, quantity and placement, so that practical and effective configurations can be evaluated. Wakode died by suicide on September 18, hours after he was allegedly found using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination. His death triggered massive student protests, after which Director Prof Shireesh Kedare held an open house to hear students concerns. The survey offers four alternatives to the ceiling fan wall-mounted, pedestal, table or desk, and tower fans. Students can also choose no alternative if they prefer to keep the existing ceiling fan. They are asked to pick from configurations such as two wall-mounted fans, one wall-mounted and one table fan, or two table fans, and to give the main reason for their choice. The options include better air circulation, cooling while studying or sleeping, space efficiency, convenience and safety. Students can also raise concerns about their safety, well-being or hostel experience if they wish. The survey is part of a wider overhaul of student wellness at the institute. The new measures, to be rolled out in phases from this week, include wellness secretaries in hostels, more play areas in residential areas, deterrents against exam malpractice and a new associate dean for student wellness. They were communicated to students in an email from the Dean of Students Affairs on behalf of Prof Kedare. According to the email, the institute drew up the plan after discussions with students and their representatives on academic, career and well-being concerns. It urges students to take part in surveys and consultations, with more to follow. On fans, the email says options have been identified, but a final decision will be taken after student feedback. Under the plan, the institute is working on a system to appoint wellness secretaries at the hostel level and to identify committees where student participation can be increased. Meetings with heads of departments have also focused on greater student participation at the department level and on strengthening support for students. For the play areas, general secretaries, sports councillors and wardens will be consulted to identify suitable spaces, understand residents concerns and assess access. Wakodes parents, Ravindra and Sonali Wakode, have alleged that their son was a victim of caste-based discrimination on the IIT Bombay campus. They are continuing their hunger strike at Mumbais Azad Maidan, demanding the arrest of those they hold responsible for his death.

articleTitle: In Bihar, an experiment for the young that bets on them
articleFeaturedImageAlt: In Bihar, an experiment that bets on the young
description: The present effort is the construction of an ecosystem in which access, teachers, leadership, technology and academic discipline reinforce one another. Bihar has begun assembling these parts at unusual speed and scale.
body_raw: Bihar is Indias youngest state, with a median age of approximately 26. That fact is usually invoked in discussions about employment, migration and the demographic dividend. Yet, before any of these comes education. Unless Bihars young people can access credible colleges, complete their courses on time and acquire useful knowledge and skills, youthfulness alone will confer little advantage. This is why an unusual experiment now unfolding deserves wider attention. The direction is significant Expand access rapidly, recruit teachers transparently, improve university leadership and use technology to make a fragmented system more visible and accountable. The most visible step has been the opening of 211 government degree colleges, largely in areas without convenient access to higher education. Distance is not a minor issue. For a rural family, particularly one educating a daughter, a nearby college can determine whether education leads to a degree or ends after Class XII. These colleges are still young. Many have begun with a few rooms, small faculties, limited support staff and enrolments below their eventual capacity. They cannot yet be judged as finished institutions. They are foundations upon which institutions must now be built. To give them an academic core, Bihar appointed 2,451 contractual assistant professors. The recruitment, drawn from more than 23,000 applications, was completed in about 30 days through a centralised process. Speed attracted attention, but transparency matters even more. Public confidence begins when a qualified applicant believes that merit, rather than influence, will determine selection. The newly appointed teachers are joining colleges without established systems and traditions. Their initiative over the next two years will determine whether these colleges acquire academic energy or remain administrative units with classrooms. Reform at the college level cannot succeed if universities remain weakly led. Bihar is also revisiting how vice-chancellors and pro-vice-chancellors are selected. Nearly 8,000 applications were received for 10 V-C positions through an online process. Numbers alone cannot guarantee good appointments. Careful scrutiny, credible search committees and matching of individual capabilities with institutional needs are essential. Yet widening the field is itself a reform. Technology is providing the connective tissue for this effort. Samarth, the e-governance platform developed under the Ministry of Education, is being energised across Bihars higher-education system. For students, a common digital window improves awareness of institutions, courses, admissions and opportunities that were once confined to notices on distant campuses. For administrators, its modules can connect admissions, registration, examinations, results, employee records and finance. For those responsible for oversight, it can reveal where a process has stalled. The introduction of a uniform academic calendar across state universities follows the same logic. A calendar has value only when classes, examinations and results occur when promised. For students, a delayed result can mean losing a job, scholarship or admission elsewhere. Timeliness is, therefore, an element of educational justice. The reforms will ultimately be tested inside classrooms. New colleges must attract students, particularly women and first-generation learners. Teachers must teach regularly and create cultures of reading, writing, discussion and mentoring. Libraries and laboratories must grow. Curricula must connect knowledge with employability without reducing education to vocational training alone. Buildings, portals and appointments create capacity they do not automatically create quality. That requires faculty development, fair assessment, research support, institutional autonomy accompanied by accountability, and academic leaders willing to take difficult decisions. Bihar also has Nalanda University. Although outside the state-university system, it provides an important beacon. Its evolving Nalanda Approach - connecting civilisational knowledge with contemporary challenges - can encourage Bihars universities to be locally rooted, nationally relevant and globally engaged. Indias demographic future will be decided not only in metropolitan universities but also in public colleges serving small towns and rural districts. The present effort is the construction of an ecosystem in which access, teachers, leadership, technology and academic discipline reinforce one another. Bihar has begun assembling these parts at unusual speed and scale. The challenge is to turn momentum into institutional habit. A Viksit Bharat will require a Viksit Bihar, and that journey must begin by equipping its young people with credible, accessible and high-quality higher education. The writer is Governor of Bihar

articleTitle: Three years later, in West Asia, a peace still out of reach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Three years later, a peace still out of reach
description: No lasting settlement is possible without Israel's participation, or without Hamas giving up arms in Gaza
body_raw: The horrific terror attack on Israel by Hamas three years ago, in which almost 1,200 were killed and 251 taken hostage, set in motion a war that continues to ripple far beyond Gaza. The devastation that followed has left Israel isolated internationally, with several Western nations formally recognising the State of Palestine. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus decision to conduct joint military operations with the US against Iran, perceived to be weakened by internal turmoil and the decimation of its proxies, has plunged West Asia into further chaos. No lasting settlement in Gaza is possible without Israels participation, or without Hamas giving up arms - peace still doesnt look within reach. The situation in Gaza, where more than 70,000 people have been killed in the last three years, continues to be enormously disturbing. The humanitarian crisis remains acute, with shortages of supplies, displacement and military strikes by the Israel Defence Forces IDF despite the ceasefire that began almost a year ago. The much-touted peace plan of US President Donald Trump has made little progress. Only two weeks ago, the Board of Peace announced a 2.45 billion recovery plan for the Strip - a fraction of the 71.4 billion that the UN estimates will be required for recovery and reconstruction over the next decade. Hamass disarmament remains an issue locked in an impasse Israel says reconstruction cannot proceed without disarmament, while Hamas, which prolongs the stalemate and the suffering of Gazans, resists disarmament without a full Israeli withdrawal first. The first phase of the Trump plan envisaged Israel retaining control of 53 per cent of Gaza since then, however, IDF forces have expanded their presence to two-thirds of the Strip. The power to enforce meaningful progress lies ultimately with the White House, but the US President seems consumed by the political fallout of the war with Iran. At the same time, the once-unbreakable US-Israel alliance is fraying Public support for Israel in America has fallen to historic lows, and the bipartisan consensus around military aid shows signs of weakening. Within Israel, the Gaza war has exposed deep divisions over the governments conduct - especially in light of revelations that Netanyahu ignored warnings from Egypt and the UAE about an impending Hamas attack - and the countrys entanglement in regional conflicts, including in Lebanon and Syria. In 20 days, Israel will hold an election, giving citizens their first chance since the terror attack to pronounce a verdict on Netanyahu. The coalition that emerges after October 27 will help shape not only the future of Gaza, but also Israels trajectory. It will indicate whether three years of militarism can give way to a path that leads away from war.

articleTitle: Reminder from Cornell: Silence enables sexual violence
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Cornell reminder on impunity, sexual violence
description: Reluctance to confront rape, not just as a singular act but also as the culmination of everyday violations, emboldens would-be perpetrators and ensures that the cycle of violence continues
body_raw: A woman was sexually assaulted by seven men at a fraternity house in a US university which, when informed of the crime, allegedly did little to punish the perpetrators. This is the bare outline of a case that has rocked the US for over a week. The survivor filed a civil suit last month against Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity as well as the seven men who allegedly raped her in 2024, following which state prosecutors in New York, where the university is located, reopened a criminal inquiry into the incident. Horrific as the assault was, what stands out in the Cornell case is that other men with knowledge of what was unfolding did nothing to inform the authorities or stop the assault evidence from a fraternity group chat points to encouragement of the crime. Whether this range of disturbing reactions is rooted in a misplaced sense of loyalty, fear of offending ones peers or causing social discomfort or just indifference is immaterial. The larger picture they paint is one of impunity, where the cost of silence and inaction is paid, over and over, by women. This is why it is also a mistake to limit the conversation to what unfolded on one US university campus or treat it as the aberrant behaviour of a handful. That would risk underplaying the extent to which everyday sexism and gender stereotypes, normalisation of rape in the form of jokes and the sexualisation of women shape views about consent, about who deserves to be punished and who is shamed for what was done to them - across cultures and borders. Its echoes can be heard everywhere, from the cases brought to light by the global MeToo movement to the long battle of Indias women wrestlers to bring a powerful man to account. The survivor of the Cornell case had to drop out of college the university closed the case after a half-hearted investigation. Two of her attackers were expelled while the rest were asked to write essays to mitigate the harm they had caused. This stark asymmetry speaks of a structural injustice where reluctance to acknowledge and confront rape emboldens would-be perpetrators and ensures that the cycle of violence continues. The conversation that has revived with Cornell must continue everywhere.

articleTitle: Jeffrey Archer: The storyteller and the twists in his tale
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The storyteller and the twists in his tale
description: The writer understood that public life, like fiction, runs on appetite — for money, power, recognition and redemption — and he had a keen instinct for all four.
body_raw: British writer Jeffrey Archer, who died at 86 on October 5, might have been the first to admit that his life was the sort of script that could have been rejected by an editor for being far too dramatic. Athlete, MP, political aspirant, bestselling novelist, convicted perjurer, comeback artiste - the arc of Archers life showed a great talent for reinvention, a phoenix-like ability to rise from the ashes. He understood that public life, like fiction, runs on appetite - for money, power, recognition and redemption - and he had a keen instinct for all four. Even his death, arriving on the eve of the publication of Adam Eve, carries the theatricality of a final twist. Archers literary life began after a personal setback, a financial defraud that had rendered him bankrupt. But Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less, published in 1976, and followed in succession by A Quiver Full of Arrows 1980, First Among Equals 1984, and novels such as Kane and Abel 1979 and Shall We Tell the President? 1986 led to a reversal of fortunes. Despite a lukewarm reception by critics, his books sold over 300 million copies in a career spanning five decades. His appetite for drama, however, proved ruinous in politics - his ascent through Conservative ranks and his ambitions for high office ended in disgrace after a libel case, followed by his conviction for perjury and imprisonment. But prison turned into more source material, a new chapter in another new beginning that brought more bestsellers. In an interview to fellow writer Anthony Horowitz for The Sunday Telegraph Magazine in 2011, Archer had said, The people who survive are storytellers. In death as in life, Archer put the twist in the tale.

articleTitle: Cameras on uniforms, speakers on streets: Delhi Police changes approach amid claims of manhandling
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Police, Delhi Police changes approach, Delhi Police approach claims of manhandling, delhi claims of manhandling, Delhi Police Cameras on uniforms, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The cameras, along with speakers blaring announcements and police personnel largely without batons, were part of a visibly more cautious approach adopted by the force, as protests in Central Delhi entered their fifth day.
body_raw: The cameras were hard to miss. Attached to the uniforms of police personnel deployed on Parliament Street on Tuesday, the small body-worn devices were recording as officers prepared to deal with another round of protests near the Election Commission headquarters. This has been given to the ground staff so that no one makes false allegations, a Delhi Police constable said, pointing to the camera fixed to his uniform. He was deployed to maintain law and order during the INDIA blocs protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. The cameras, along with speakers blaring announcements and police personnel largely without batons, were part of a visibly more cautious approach adopted by the force, as protests in Central Delhi entered their fifth day. The measures come after three days of criticism and allegations over the handling of protesters, including sexual assault allegations made by three female journalists. By Tuesday, around 80 body-worn cameras had been distributed among ground staff, according to a senior officer. They were deployed among almost all ground-level personnel up to the rank of DCP, with officers told to record their interactions while managing crowds. If required, more cameras will be given to the ground staff, the officer said. Body-worn cameras are not new to the Delhi Police. Traffic personnel have used them for several years to record interactions while issuing challans, while local police sometimes use them when dealing with members of the public, but not on such a large scale. Their deployment on this scale during crowd-control duties is a recent measure, another officer said. Further, police personnel were largely seen without batons or other weapons as Opposition leaders approached the barricades. Speakers repeatedly urged people not to gather in the area, with prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS in force across Parliament Street and adjoining areas. More than five companies of paramilitary personnel, along with local police, were deployed along the routes expected to be taken by the protesters from Makar Dwar of Parliament to the Election Commission office. Multi-layered barricades came up outside the EC offices main entrance and around Jantar Mantar. The New Delhi district has been witnessing protests since October 2, with Opposition parties holding demonstrations. Police have registered nine FIRs in connection with the protests held near Jantar Mantar over the last five days. The cases include alleged violations of prohibitory orders, rioting and attacks on police personnel while they were discharging their duties. Eighteen people have also been arrested, while more than 300 people detained and later released. Police are, meanwhile, bracing for another protest. The Cockroach Janta Party has called another demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10 as part of a nationwide stir demanding Kumars resignation.

articleTitle: Expanded ANMOL scheme, hike in ASHA incentive — Delhi launches health initiatives
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Expanded ANMOL scheme, hike in ASHA incentive, ANMOL scheme, ASHA incentive, newborn screening programme for newborns, State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (SOTTO), GB Pant Hospital, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The programme also saw the virtual inauguration of the State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (SOTTO) building at GB Pant Hospital.
body_raw: Expansion of the ANMOL scheme, which raises the free newborn screening programme for newborns, from 56 to 63 diseases, doubling of the monthly incentive for ASHA workers from Rs 3,000 to Rs 6,000 - these were among the several new healthcare initiatives launched by the Delhi Government on Tuesday under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan programme, organised at Thyagraj Stadium. The programme also saw the virtual inauguration of the State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation SOTTO building at GB Pant Hospital. Further, a Nursing Home Management System portal was launched, which moves registration and renewal for private nursing homes online, officials said. The hike in incentives is set to benefit 6,690 ASHA workers in the Capital, officials said, adding that the increment is a recognition of the dedication with which the workers bring Delhis health services to households. ASHA workers act as the link between the community and the public health system. They register pregnant women, push for institutional deliveries, track immunisation, counsel families on nutrition and sanitation, and accompany patients to health facilities and work under the National Health Mission. On the development, Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said, The incentive had been pending for nearly a decade. Through the Covid years, the workers kept serving. The steps to recognise them did not come. This government has addressed it. On Tuesday, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta also felicitated outstanding workers at the ASHA Sammelan-2026 and ASHA Samman Samaroh. She said she expects them to reach every family like an elder sister, and announced a special dandiya programme for them during Navratri. Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu said, ASHA workers stand on the front lines of the healthcare system, taking health services and awareness to pregnant women, children and families. On the expansion of Mission ANMOL, officials said that it now covers 63 congenital health conditions, with screening to be carried out within 24 to 72 hours of birth. Since Mission ANMOL was made operational in March this year, more than 75,000 newborns have been screened and over 700 children have been treated in time, officials said. The government aims to increase the annual coverage under the scheme around 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh newborns. Last month, The Indian Express had reported that more than 14,000 newborn genetic samples arrive every month at the LNJP genetic lab, the only genetic lab run by the Delhi government.

articleTitle: From ‘chalta hai’ to ‘badal sakta hai’, changing the way India thinks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The journey from ‘chalta hai’ to ‘badal sakta hai’
description: If the aim is to become ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047, this is the mindset to be cultivated
body_raw: Prime Minister Narendra Modi belongs to a rare breed of people who refuse to accept inherited challenges. He believes, and his actions show, that no problem in public life is too difficult to solve. I distinctly remember an Independence Day address in which he said that India must move away from the chalta hai attitude towards a badal sakta hai attitude. I have known him first as a colleague in the party and later in the government. For those of us who worked in the BJP for decades, Article 370 and Ram Janmabhoomi were matters of profound conviction, for which we made sacrifices. But I would be honest to admit that there were moments when even some of our own karyakartas doubted whether they would see these issues resolved in their lifetime. Article 370, described in the Constitution as a temporary provision, had come to be seen as virtually impossible to abrogate. I had the privilege of presiding over the Rajya Sabha when the historic legislation relating to its abrogation was passed. The Ram Janmabhoomi journey was much longer. Generations had lived with the hope that one day a grand temple would stand at the birthplace of Prabhu Shri Ram. On January 22, 2024, that hope became a reality. Modi became Gujarat Chief Minister a few months after the state had been hit by a terrible earthquake. Kutch, already a region beset by great difficulties, had suffered severe losses. Modi understood that the first task was to restore confidence. He spent his first Diwali as CM with the areas earthquake-affected families. Over the years, his policies helped Kutch reinvent itself, and it came to be known for its tourism potential, industrial growth and agricultural achievements. Water presented another seemingly permanent challenge to Gujarat. The Sardar Sarovar Project, conceived decades earlier, was mired in complications. Modi pursued it and saw to it that the dam reached completion and Narmada water travelled to water-scarce parts of Gujarat. Other, smaller structures, including check dams, made water conservation a mass movement and helped Gujarats farmers achieve remarkable results. Modi became PM at a time when India had been labelled one of the Fragile Five economies and its banking system was burdened with serious problems. He initiated a process of resolving these challenges through measures including the Asset Quality Review, banking reforms and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. India went on to become the fastest-growing major economy in the world. Many believed that the political consensus required for the GST would prove elusive. Yet it became possible because Modi was willing to invest political capital and see the reform through. Today, India is a leader in digital payments. Technology was not a challenge. The seemingly impossible task was to persuade crores across cities, villages, generations and income groups to change a deeply ingrained habit. Experienced political leaders asked how a street vendor could be brought into a digital payments ecosystem. PM Modi made that transformation possible. Poverty was another problem India had come to accept as permanent. Today, 25 crore Indians have moved out of multidimensional poverty. This happened through the painstaking work of creating a broad safety net and then giving the poor the means - bank accounts, direct benefit transfers, housing, sanitation, electricity, cooking gas, food security, health insurance and economic opportunities - to move out of poverty. For decades, Naxalism cost our nation thousands of lives. Through a twin approach of security and development, it has now been brought to an end. It is not that every problem has disappeared. But Modi has ensured that the assumption of helplessness in the face of problems has disappeared. During the pandemic, he brought the nation together. The Indian economy bounced back faster than many other major nations. The West Asia crisis brought another set of challenges involving energy security, shipping and trade. Indias approach, involving government and society, has been mature and responsible. The BJP was once branded as a party restricted to certain areas and social constituencies. PM Modi worked assiduously to change this perception. The BJPs growth in the Northeast and East India, and its deepening support among poor, rural and marginalised sections, have changed the countrys political map. For those who have watched his journey closely, it is clear that Narendra Modi begins by asking what the nation needs, and then works to create the circumstances to deliver it. This mindset is extremely important for a country that wants to become Viksit Bharat by 2047. The writer is former vice president of India

articleTitle: Chasing illicit liquor traders, cops land in Bihar village. 50 locals jump into river, 2 drown
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chasing illicit liquor traders, cops land in Bihar village. 50 locals jump into river, 2 drown
description: Police said 39 accused, including women, were arrested while around 1,000 litres of illicit country-made liquor were seized, along with equipment allegedly used for liquor production.
body_raw: It was supposed to be a massive crackdown on alleged illicit liquor trade, coming two days after a police party was allegedly attacked and five liquor traders were freed by local residents. On Sunday, police came better prepared. Teams from four police stations along with armed police forces descended upon Beherawan Chakia Musahri village, looking to arrest those allegedly involved in the case. What they didnt anticipate was this In order to evade arrest, around 50-60 people jumped into the Punpun river. Next day, the bodies of two of them were recovered. Locals claimed some of the villagers were still missing. The incident took place under Pipra police station in Patna district. In a video statement, Masaurhi Sub-divisional police officer-1 SDPO-01 Raghav Dayal said that on October 1, five alleged liquor traders were freed after a police team conducting an anti-liquor operation in Beherawan Chakia Musahri was attacked. Three policemen were injured and a case was registered, he said. According to Dayal, on Sunday, a large-scale search operation was initiated during which the police team was again attacked and several vehicles were damaged. Police said 39 accused, including women, were arrested while around 1,000 litres of illicit country-made liquor were seized, along with equipment allegedly used for liquor production. About 61,00 litres of mahua-based fermenting mixture was destroyed, and a country-made pistol and three live cartridges were recovered from the house of one accused, Dayal claimed in the video. For their part, local residents alleged that the police operation triggered panic in the village due to which 50-60 people jumped into the Punpun river while attempting to evade the police. They alleged that stones and bricks were thrown during the confrontation and that police also hurled stones towards people in the river, making it difficult for some of them to reach the opposite bank. Residents further alleged that police entered homes and took away several belongings. Repeated calls and messages to SDPO Dayal and Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma, seeking their response to the allegations, went unanswered. The two deceased were identified by local residents as Akash Manjhi, around 25, from Dhibra in Phulwari Sharif, and Ram Manjhi, around 60. Police confirmed receiving information on October 5 about the deaths of two people by drowning in the Punpun river but did not disclose the circumstances in which they drowned. Villagers place bodies on roads After the bodies were recovered, local residents placed them on the Bihta-Sarmera road, blocking traffic and creating a law-and-order situation, police said. Officers reached the spot, eventually persuaded the protesters to clear the road and sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. Local residents said the road remained blocked for hours as protesters demanded the release of those arrested, compensation of Rs 4 lakh for each deceased persons family, and a search for people they alleged were still missing.

articleTitle: Rajasthan smuggler began new life in Madhya Pradesh as furniture trader. Then police closed in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajasthan smuggler began new life in MP as furniture trader. Then police closed in
description: After he was named a wanted drug smuggler, Vishna Ram stayed at different locations in Rajasthan, including rented accommodation in Jodhpur and houses of relatives.
body_raw: A wanted drug smuggler from Barmer, who has been evading arrest for nearly two years, was arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Task Force ANTF from Mandsaur in Madhya Pradesh. The accused, identified as 32-year-old Vishna Ram, son of Madaram, a resident of Kudla in Barmer, was carrying a reward of Rs 1 lakh. Police said he had changed his identity and had been running a furniture business in Madhya Pradesh to avoid arrest. According to police, Vishna Ram had been involved in criminal activities for around 12 years and has over 18 cases including those under the NDPS Act, attempt to murder, assault, Arms Act, theft and fraud, registered against him in different police stations of Rajasthan. ANTF Inspector General Vikas Kumar said, Vishna Ram had studied up to Class 12 and initially worked as a driver. He later came into contact with drug smugglers while working as a labourer. His grandfather was addicted to poppy husk, and Vishna Ram initially began procuring small quantities for him. He subsequently came into contact with smugglers in Neemuch and entered the drug trade himself. Over the years, he allegedly established links with smugglers in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana and supplied drugs in the Marwar region. Police said he eventually became a key link in the trafficking network operating between Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, police said. After he was named a wanted drug smuggler, Vishna Ram stayed at different locations in Rajasthan, including rented accommodation in Jodhpur and houses of relatives. With repeated police raids making it difficult for him to remain in the state, he eventually shifted to Madhya Pradesh, which he believed would be a safer place to hide. There, he started a furniture business and began living like an ordinary businessman to conceal his past. However, the ANTF continued tracking him. The breakthrough Police officials said the breakthrough came after information was received that Vishna Ram was running a furniture business in Madhya Pradesh and had called artisans from Jodhpur to work. The ANTF team began monitoring the movement of the artisans and followed the trail to Umaria village under the Pipliy Mandi police station area of Mandsaur district. When the team reached the location, Vishna Ram was allegedly partying with his friends and some of the artisans at the house of his smuggler associates uncle. The premises were surrounded and Vishna Ram was arrested.

articleTitle: Goa’s anti-BJP coalition teeters as AAP ally makes a case for ‘grand unity’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Goa’s anti-BJP coalition teeters as AAP ally makes a case for 'grand unity'
description: Goa Forward Party says alliance cannot work if Congress is targeted; AAP says BJP-Congress “joint venture” destroyed state.
body_raw: Weeks after the Aam Aadmi Party AAP and the Goa Forward Party GFP announced a joint alliance for the 2027 Assembly elections in the coastal state, the alliance seems to be fracturing in less than a month. The AAP and the GFP had announced the Goa First alliance on September 13, calling it a non-BJP, non-Congress platform, which would offer an alternative to the BJP-Congress collusion in the state. In the days leading up to the alliance, hoardings bearing the AAP and GFP symbols came up along the national highway in the state. The hoardings targeted the BJP and the Congress over the issue of defections, saying, Congress and BJP cheated you twice. Dont let them cheat you the third time. On Tuesday, some of these hoardings were pulled down. In the past few days, GFP president Vijai Sardesai has reiterated that the people of Goa want a grand alliance of all the parties to defeat the BJP, leading to speculation of allying with the Congress. On Tuesday, Sardesai said, In politics, the voter is the King. From Goan voters, I can hear only one call.that a grand alliance is necessary. They want a grand alliance of all parties coming together to defeat the BJP. This echo is such that even if you are hard of hearing, you will be able to hear it. If you brought mangoes to Goa and instead of Mancurad, you begin selling Alphonso or Dasheri from Delhi, will that sell? It wont. Because Goans dont like their taste. What do the Goans want? They want a Mancurad, be it a Cardozo Mancurad or a Bardez Mancurad. But they want an original Mancurad, he said. Sardesai said no final decision was taken though. There is a call for a greater unity of all those who are genuinely opposed to the BJP. So, if this alliance is to be brought together, it cannot be through targeting the principal Opposition party. This is what the people feel. And we have to do what the people feel. AAP seeks clarification The AAP has now asked Sardesai to clarify his stand on the alliance. In a statement on Monday, the partys core committee said the BJP-Congress joint venture had destroyed Goa in the last decade and that Sardesai must decide whether he stands with the BJP-Congress joint venture or with the people of Goa. AAP Goa president Valmiki Naik said it was clear and agreed upon from the start that there would be no place for the Congress in the Goa First Alliance. Naik said Congress candidates had deep roots in the BJP and all the signs point to a hat-trick of defections by the Congress. On Tuesday, the AAP reiterated that Goa First is a non-BJP non-Congress platform. In 2022, the BJP emerged as the single-largest party, winning 20 of the states 40 seats, while the Congress returned with 11. The GFP contested the 2022 Assembly polls in alliance with the Congress and won one seat, represented by Sardesai, the Fatorda MLA. The AAP won two seats. Subsequently, in September 2022, eight Congress MLAs defected to the BJP, bringing the Congresss tally down to three. Earlier, in 2019, 10 Congress MLAs had defected to the BJP.

articleTitle: Parliament street shuts down for much of the day; opposition parties step up protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, leaders held
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gyanesh Kumar resignation, rahul gandhi, priyanka gandhi vadra, gyanesh kumar, election commission of india, cec resignation protest, india bloc protest new delhi, voter list deletion row, parliament street protest, akashvani bhavan detention, vote chori allegations, india bloc, election commissioner dissent report, akashvani bhavan, election commission news
description: Demand CEC’s resignation as Rahul alleges ‘vote chori’
body_raw: Escalating the bitter political fight over the special intensive revision of electoral rolls by the Election Commission, INDIA bloc MPs, led by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, staged a protest Tuesday and attempted to march to the Commission headquarters, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The standoff with the police through much of the day ended in the evening with the detention of Gandhi and several leaders including Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. Among those who joined the march from Parliament towards Nirvachan Sadan-it was the second such joint street protest since the rollout of the SIR-were SPs Akhilesh Yadav, TMCs Abhishek Banerjee, NCP SPs Supriya Sule, RJDs Manoj Kumar Jha and CPMs John Brittas. Gandhi and Congress MPs including Vadra, K C Venugopal, Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi, Charanjit Singh Channi, Praniti Shinde and Deepender Hooda forced their way into the premises of the Akashvani Bhavan, situated next to the EC headquarters, where they staged a sit-in there for several hours before being detained by police. All roads leading to the Nirvachan Sadan were heavily barricaded by police. The standoff began when Gandhi and others were stopped by police near Akashvani Bhavan. Gandhi, who climbed atop the barricades, was detained and was seen walking towards a parked police bus. He then spoke to his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and they, along with some Congress MPs, entered the Akashvani Bhavan complex. All I want to do is meet the Chief Election Commissioner and tell him that he has done vote chori. I can continue to sit here. I am comfortable here. If they dont want us to sit here, give us some other site, Gandhi said. Targeting the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and the RSS chief, he alleged that the country had been hijacked with the vote chori. What has been done to our country is treason. Nobody is going to escape, he said. In a post on X as the march began, Gandhi said, Gyanesh its done bro. Time to resign. The standoff ended eight hours later when police detained the leaders after several rounds of discussions, and heated exchanges. Posting a video of his detention, Gandhi said, To save the traitors of democracy, the remnants of democracy have been dragged. There will be a reckoning-not a single traitor will be spared. Late in the evening, the detained leaders were taken to the Kingsway Camp police facility. After one set of leaders were taken inside, police had to close the gate as scores of Congress workers reached the spot. Vadra, who was in another bus, could not be taken inside because of the surging crowd. She was seen climbing the gate after which the police opened the gates to let her in. The Opposition stepped up its demand for CEC Kumars resignation after an investigation by The Indian Express last month revealed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under the CEC, from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. While the DMK, which was part of the protest last year, was missing Tuesday, the Opposition camp got unexpected support from the BJD. The Naveen Patnaik-led Odisha party sent two of its MPs to participate in the march. For many years, the BJD had maintained equidistance from the NDA and the INDIA bloc. But there were rumblings within the INDIA bloc after the protest. Some allies of the Congress felt mistreated because the Gandhi siblings stole the show by sitting in protest at Akashvani Bhavan. Around noon, all INDIA bloc MPs were in buses and were subsequently taken to different police stations, but the Gandhis and their close aides stayed back. Sources said Congresss Venugopal later conveyed to the INDIA bloc parties that the party leadership had acted on the spur of the moment, and that he regretted the mistrust that had been created by not keeping allies in the loop. Only after calls from the Congress did the TMC leaders reach the AIR office later. Some Opposition leaders also said that the Congresss decision to demand a meeting with the Election Commission was not something that the allies would have agreed to. Why would we meet the ECI when we are demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar? If this was discussed with the allies, we wouldnt have agreed, a Left MP said.

articleTitle: Munich Security Conference CEO Benedikt Franke: ‘India has said right things for years… not often lent its weight… It’s finally walking the talk’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ‘India has said right things for years… not often lent its weight… It’s finally walking the talk’
description: “It’s okay to buy Russian oil, but I wish when you go into the shop, you don’t kiss the shopkeeper,” says Franke, as he welcomes India’s proposals on Russia-Ukraine war, hopes Delhi can use its “special relationship” with Moscow to end stalemate.
body_raw: India is ready to put its diplomatic weight and relationship into efforts to bring the Russia-Ukraine war to an end, says Benedikt Franke, Vice-Chairman and CEO of the Munich Security Conference MSC. In an expansive interview with The Indian Express, Franke, who is in Delhi for the Munich leaders meeting a chapter of the MSF held in different locations every year, spoke about the war and Indias active role in trying to resolve the conflict, Indias import of Russian energy, the US-Iran conflict, as well as the rise of the far right party AfD in Germany. Excerpts India has moved a proposal to end the war in Ukraine, going beyond advocating for dialogue and diplomacy. How do you see this? Im absolutely thrilled that India is finally walking the talk. Prime Minister Modi has said the right things for a while on this issue, that there is a need for dialogue, for negotiations. However, India didnt vote accordingly in the UN. Now, not just the Ukrainian foreign minister but also President Putin have has said that the proposals received from the Indian side were the only ones he was seriously considering. I hope more countries take note of this development. We Europe believe that our best hope lies with countries like India and China that have a special relationship with Russia. These countries are now finally ready to use their diplomatic weight and their relationship to support efforts to bring this war to an end. We hope it doesnt lead to a situation in which the aggressor Russia is rewarded and the victim Ukraine is punished. We, Europeans, will do everything we can to ensure that the Ukrainians end up in the strongest possible negotiation position. I just hope India sort of doubles down on these very promising signs. Why do you think the needle has moved for India? The Ukraine-Russia war comes at a cost for everyone. Countries like India need stability and predictability in global trade and relations. India needs to continue on its growth trajectory, to pull hundreds of millions out of poverty. Another reason is that multi-alignment is great on paper. It also comes to a natural limit at some point. Civilians are dying every day in Ukraine, civilian infrastructure is destroyed. How can you be a liberal democracy, position yourself as a leader in this world on inter-State cooperation, on development, and not act on blatant breaches of international law? And then, India is becoming more ambitious in a lot of fields, putting stuff in space, being an economic or technological powerhouse. But, on the diplomatic front, I dont think Indias actions to date matched its self-perception. Critics in Europe and the West say India is still buying Russian energy. India argues that it is acting in self-interest. Its perfectly okay to buy Russian oil and gas, but I wish that when you go into the shop to buy it, you dont kiss the shopkeeper. Why do we need selfies at the BRICS summit? Why do we need the embrace between Modi and Putin? Maybe we are underestimating the close emotional ties between India and Russia. We just hope that this special relationship can be, in a way, used to end the stalemate we are seeing. And by putting a little pressure on its favourite shopkeeper, India could make a major difference in the war. What do you make of US President Donald Trumps efforts for peace in the Russia-Ukraine war? I have been criticised in the past for praising President Trump for trying. I think trying is better than not trying, and I wish there were a European-led effort, but there is not. And so, everyone that tries to solve this without throwing the Ukrainians in front of the bus deserves praise. I am not 100 sure that President Trumps efforts and the focus on or connection to business interests of the United States in Russian resources was very helpful. It is perfectly okay for the United States to do business with Russia. At some point, I hope the European Union and India will do more business with Russia. At the end of the day, we want a stable, prosperous and constructive Russia. No one wants a tumbling giant like Russia. But first, it is based on an expectation that this war comes to an end, that aggression ends, that the sovereign territory of Ukraine is restored. If we have no agreement on that, having an agreement on business sends the wrong signal. But I could imagine that if you Indians broke the ice now, the US joining such an effort would make a huge difference. Is it still a stalemate after four-and a-half-years of the Ukraine war, and what does it mean for European security? For Ukraine, to be perfectly honest, its quite a success that they are still there. Europe has not done enough to help Ukraine win. Hence, it has not won. But we have done a lot to help them survive, get their house in order, and become a leader in defence technology. They are now producing most of the stuff they need themselves. We need to appreciate that this country, which is only a quarter of the population of Russia and only a fraction of its economic potential, has held out for four years. I dont want to paint a rosy picture. The winter will be terrible. The Russians have destroyed so much energy and other infrastructure. But they the Ukrainians are still there on a lot of sovereign territory, and here and there, they actually win battles, produce what we call iconoclastic victories and deep strikes into Russian territory. They, by the way, never attack civilian infrastructure. Now the question is, will Europe step up its effort to bring Ukraine into a good negotiating position? Will the US realise once again who the actual aggressor is? Will India and other powerhouses put a little pressure on Putin? I have no answer. How do you see the energy security issue playing out given the war in West Asia, on top of the Russia-Ukraine conflict? I am quite pessimistic that without a larger alliance of countries working, this conflict will be solved any time soon. I do not believe in some American predictions. I do not believe in the miraculous disappearance of the Houthis. I do not believe in a sudden end to Iranian ambitions. I wish for a stronger European role, a stronger American role, and a stronger Asian role in finding a diplomatic solution. I fear there is an implicit assumption of a division of labour globally in these conflicts. Europeans believe that is American-caused and it needs to be American-solved. Americans believe that Ukraine is Europes problem. If we continue this silo thinking. I dont think we will see a solution. The Iran conflict is also driving up prices in Germany at a time when our domestic politics are in a difficult place, when our industry is in a difficult place. That increases the chances of the right or the left fringes of the political spectrum to win. Do you think the rise of the right and the extreme right is here to stay, especially in Germany? As long as the political centre doesnt find clear answers to some of the worries that the population in Germany, but also across the world, has-personal security, job prospects, prosperity for their kids, crime, migration, culture-and enters into a national debate on these, the political extremes will be further empowered. Global governance, global multilateralism, will not be revitalised. How many Indians believe that the UN is their best chance? How many Indians put real faith into the World Bank and the IMF?. Take their worries, justified or not, seriously, and provide real, value-added solutions. If we dont, the extreme ends will win, and whether its left or right really makes no difference. In Germany, the extreme left is pretty close to the extreme right. Germany has a very close relationship with China, and the recent meeting between US President Trump and President Xi Jinping indicates some kind of rapprochement. The two superpowers need to de-escalate, need to clear the air occasionally. Hence it is to be welcomed. Its perfectly okay to be friends with China and the US at the same time, as it is perfectly okay for India to try to be friends with everyone at the same time. I mean, if multi-alignment works for you, why shouldnt it work for us? There is still an issue with human rights. But, at the end of the day, we want a strong, prosperous China that engages constructively in international relations. You have been coming to India for at least a decade now. How do you see Indias perception about itself, and its perception from where you sit in Germany? I love coming to this country because the feeling of dynamism, of optimism, is just infectious and great. Indian interlocutors have become more confident. They see their economic growth rate. They see the many Indian success stories, the space programme.. But With superpower status come responsibilities. At some point, multi-alignment will come to a natural limit. You will have to choose sides on certain issues at some point. India has said the right things for many years. It hasnt necessarily put its full weight behind these statements.

articleTitle: As Andhra Pradesh declares drought in 21 districts, Opposition YSRCP asks ‘why so late’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chasing illicit liquor traders, cops land in Bihar village. 50 locals jump into river, 2 drown
description: Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said that interlinking of Godavari and Cauvery river systems can make southern states drought-free.
body_raw: The Andhra Pradesh government recently declared early drought in 21 of its 28 districts. These include 388 of 688 mandals of which 283 have been classified as severely affected and 105 moderately affected in the government order GO issued on October 1 for the South-West Monsoon 2026 Kharif season. Now, Opposition YSRCP has slammed the government, alleging that it delayed drought declaration despite conditions becoming severe from the first week of September itself. Meanwhile, Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said that interlinking of Godavari and Cauvery river systems can make southern states drought-free. Former Agriculture Minister Kurasala Kannababu and YSR Congress Party YSRCP State General Secretary Gadikota Srikanth Reddy said Rayalaseema region has been facing the brunt of the rainfall deficit, with 186 of the 388 drought-declared mandals located in the region. As many as 159 of the 283 severe-drought mandals are also situated there, he said. He further alleged that nearly seven lakh borewells had dried up by August, while mango and citrus orchards were withering and farmers were relying on tankers to save plantations. The YSRCP also slammed the government for not including Nellore in the drought-hit districts, claiming that several mandals there received less rainfall. Rayalaseema region will flourish if. Referring to the drought-like conditions in the state, CM Naidu on Monday said, While drought conditions prevail, 2,000 TMC thousand million cubic feet of river water is flowing into the sea. If at least 200 TMC of Godavari floodwater is utilised, the Rayalaseema region will flourish with abundant greenery and crops. He was speaking at the launch of the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0-Amarajeevi Jaladhara programmes in Proddatur in YSR Kadapa district. A high-level committee, in a meeting held on September 30, recommended early declaration of drought in 21 of the states 26 districts, instead of waiting for the October 31 deadline for declaration of the 2026 Kharif season drought. The 21 districts included in the list are Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR district, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Prakasam, Markapuram, Kurnool, Nandyal, Ananthapuramu, Sri Satya Sai, YSR Kadapa, Annamayya and Chittoor. The order, issued by the Revenue Disaster Management Department, comes amid a sharp deficit in rainfall across the state, amplified by prevailing El Nino conditions. Due to a 53.4 rainfall deficit recorded during the months of June-August, 2026, and the prevailing El Nino conditions, by taking into consideration the relevant drought indicators based on data available for the period from June to August, 2026, it is proposed to undertake an early declaration of drought for Kharif-2026. An average rainfall of 197.6 mm has been received against the normal rainfall of 424.3 mm from June 1 to August 31, the order states. The declaration was made as per the Manual for Drought Management, 2016, issued by the Government of India.

articleTitle: Three with Bhatti links held in J&K, one in Punjab; items ‘drone-dropped from Pakistan’ seized
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narcotics 'drone-dropped from Pak', four with Shahzad Bhatti links held
description: Officials said the Pakistani gangster used to send them consignments of arms, ammunition and narcotics through drone. The items were supposed to be delivered to members of the module in Punjab, they said.
body_raw: The Jammu Kashmir Police on Tuesday claimed to have arrested four people, including a Punjab resident, for allegedly being members of a cross-border narco-terror module with links in Pakistan. Police claimed the accused had links with Pakistan-based gangster Shahzad Bhatti. The arrested persons included two residents of Talhar, both called Ajay Kumar who went by the aliases Rabb and Sam, respectively, and one Rahul from Treva. Police claimed they have seized an Italian-made Bretta pistol along with two magazines and four live rounds, besides 500 grams of heroin and opium each from them. The seized items were reportedly dropped by drone from Pakistan, a police official said. Police said all three accused are in their early 20s and are drug addicts. Following their interrogation, a man called Jaganpreet Randhawa alias Jaggi was arrested from Punjab. The lid was taken off the module after a police party apprehended Rabb and Rahul on October 3 and seized a pistol along with ammunition and nearly 500 grams of heroin. On their disclosure during preliminary questioning, police nabbed Sam and seized nearly 500 grams of opium from him, officials said. Shahzad Bhatti link Officials said that the accused had links with Bhatti, a Pakistani handler operating under the patronage of ISI, who used to send them consignments of arms, ammunition and narcotics through drone from across the international border for further delivery to members of the module in Punjab. During questioning, they admitted having received two drone-droppings - the first one containing nearly half-a-dozen pistols a few months ago. While delivering that consignment to some people who had come to the region from Punjab, Rahul had kept one of the pistols for himself, which later led to his arrest, a police official said. The second drone-dropping, this time containing narcotics, was received a few days ago, which the accused had buried near a tubewell to avoid detection, police added. A case has been registered under relevant sections, and further investigation is in progress to unearth a wider network and members of the cross border narco-terror module. Security agencies have already raised concern over the use of drones by terrorist handlers and cross-border smugglers in Pakistan to send weapons and narcotics into Jammu and Kashmir. The agencies, in a massive pre-Independence Day operation launched simultaneously across 14 states, detained nearly 250 people allegedly linked to the Bhatti network. Arms, grenades and surveillance material were collected from them. The operation followed intelligence inputs, warning of attempts by terror operatives of strikes ahead of I-Day celebrations.
