description: In a letter to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dinesh Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Virat Kohli’s first visit to the ashram in 2023.
body_raw: Cricketer Virat Kohli has dismissed claims that he first visited the ashram of spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj in exchange for money, calling the allegations baseless and factually incorrect. He emphasised his deep faith as the reason for his visits, along with actor wife Anushka Sharma, to the ashram. The allegations began after the death of a disciple of Premanand Ji Maharaj, Rasik Dulari, under mysterious circumstances at his Radha Keli Kunj Ashram. Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma, president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, claimed that Virat Kohli was paid Rs 5 crore to visit the ashram for the first time. Kohlis team, however, has categorically refuted the claim. The cricketers spokesperson issued an official statement saying, We would like to categorically state that the claims made by Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma in regards to Mr Virat Kohli are completely false, baseless and factually incorrect. The statement further read, Mr Virat Kohli visits Premanand Maharaj Ji purely out of his deep faith and reverence for Maharaj Ji. It concluded, We strongly refute these claims and urge the media to exercise due diligence, verify facts before reporting or amplifying such statements, and report responsibly. What sparked the controversy? Following Rasik Dularis death, Sharma alleged that the builder lobby and land mafia had been using the name of Premanand Maharajs ashram for public relations and running an alleged extortion racket. ALSO READ Soundarya Rajinikanth says parents changing male-dominated dynamic at home My rocks during divorce In a letter to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dinesh Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Kohlis first visit to the ashram in 2023. He alleged that the motive was to boost the popularity and reach of the ashram. The investigation into Rasik Dularis death is underway. When Virat-Anushka first visited Premanad Maharaj Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma first visited Vrindavan on January 4, 2023, to seek the blessings of Premanand Maharaj. Since then, the couple has made several visits to meet the spiritual leader, including before and after IPL matches and during their trips to India from London. Multiple videos from the couples visits to the spiritual leader often go viral on social media. Their most recent visit was on July 22, 2026, when they visited Premanand Maharaj at his ashram in Vrindavan. The couple made headlines after they were seen walking barefoot through the drizzle to seek his blessings.

articleTitle: ‘Only rate hike or pause ahead’: RBI Governor rules out rate cut in near-term
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rbi governor
description: The MPC’s shift to ‘calibrated tightening’ signals that the RBI is prepared to act if inflationary pressures persist
body_raw: After hiking the repo rate by another 25 basis points bps to 5.50 on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank of Indias RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC has sent a hawkish message the era of easy money is far from over, and borrowers should brace themselves for more pain. The MPCs decision to shift its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening is not a mere change in terminology - it is a clear warning that the central bank is prepared to tighten the screws if inflationary pressures refuse to ease. It MPC underscored that given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near-term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said after the MPC meeting. With borrowing costs already elevated, another rate hike would pile additional pressure on households, businesses and an economy struggling to sustain momentum. The central banks message leaves little room for complacency. By signalling further tightening, the RBI has effectively chosen to prioritise inflation control over the immediate concerns of growth and credit demand. The outcome could be particularly punishing for consumers and businesses carrying existing debt, as higher interest rates translate into steeper EMIs, costlier working capital and weaker investment. If the MPC follows through on its hawkish stance, the next round of tightening could expose just how much economic pain the RBI is willing to tolerate to bring inflation under control. Malhotra said the duration and extent of the rate hike cycle would be contingent on the actual growth-inflation developments and outlook, especially that of underlying inflation, the extent of broadening of price pressures and second round effects of the supply shock, as also the impact of demand impulses. The MPC observation clearly indicates that another rate hike might be in the offing in the December policy review, depending on the economic conditions, analysts said in initial reactions. Recalibrating policy rate, supply side inflation He further observed that in the light of available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year, with headline CPI inflation expected to average almost 5.8 in the next three quarters and core inflation projected at 4.4 per cent this financial year. In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative, Malhotra said. As regards supply side inflation, the MPC noted that monetary policy primarily acts by curtailing second round effects inflation expectations and firm level pricing behaviour, etc., which take time to manifest and are difficult to extract from available data. Apart from data related to inflation expectations and firm level pricing behaviour, indicators of generalisation of inflation like core inflation and diffusion indices are used for this purpose, he said. According to him, it is difficult to distinguish between the second-round effects and the indirect impact of supply side pressures in production cost through energy and other inputs as both are present in these indicators. While there is some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and generalisation of inflation, there are limited signs of supply side pressures getting embedded in pricing behaviour. Similarly, while there is limited evidence of demand side pressures, risks in view of strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates exist, he said. Considering all these factors, the MPC unanimously voted to increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50, he said. Global uncertainty, supply chain disruptions Looking ahead, global economic uncertainty and supply chain disruptions are expected to have some bearing on domestic economic activity, he said. Furthermore, weak southwest monsoon along with strong El Nino conditions may impact the upcoming rabi season and rural demand, he said. The near-term outlook on inflation points towards continued pressures from the supply side, on account of the deficient Southwest monsoon, El Nino conditions and high volatility in international oil prices. Price pressures are increasingly becoming visible across a range of commodities within the food component, apart from oil, he said. In addition, early signs of inflation becoming generalised are also evident from the increase in core inflation and higher inflation across a larger segment of the CPI basket. Further tightening of global financial conditions, uncertainty about fair valuation of AI stocks, and an elusive resolution of the West Asia conflict pose significant downside risks to the global economic outlook, Malhotra said.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn doesn’t rule out Drishyam 4, says Mohanlal film ‘most suited for their audience’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn says Mohanlal's Drishyam 3 is "most suited" for the Malayalam audience.
description: Ajay Devgn reveals the Hindi and Malayalam teams of Drishyam 3 discussed their scripts with each other, before going in completely different directions.
body_raw: Abhishek Pathaks Bollywood crime thriller Drishyam 3 took a different route from Jeetu Josephs Malayalam counterpart, which released earlier this year, marking a departure from the previous two instalments of the franchise. That risk seems to have paid off, with the Ajay Devgn-starrer now crossing Rs 340 crore at the worldwide box office. But the actor maintains that it was a natural chain of events, instead of a cinematic rebellion, to tread a different path than the Mohanlal-starrer, which didnt get the rave reviews the franchise is otherwise known for. Ajay Devgn says Hindi and Malayalam teams discussed their stories After Abhishek and his father Kumar Mangat Pathaks production house Panaroma Studios acquired the Drishyam franchise from the Malayalam makers, the Hindi and Malayalam teams began working in tandem. Honestly speaking, they had not decided to make a third one. We were toying with the idea, and I think all the writers worked out some ideas and they didnt work. And finally, things fell into place, Devgn revealed in a recent interview. We spoke to them, and we were like, Lets make it, we have a script. And then they said that theyre also working on something, and they had a script. So we thought, lets hear each ot her out and decide what to do, Devgn told Gulf News. After that, Drishyam 3 Hindi co-writers Abhishek, Aamii Keeyan Khan, and Parveez Shaikh, and Drishyam 3 Malayalam writer Joseph exchanged scripts. Finally we came to the conclusion that this is a fabulous script, but it is most suited for their audience. And we were very confident about our script. So, then we decided that we will go ahead, recalled Devgn. When you work hard and then you get something which is to the point, then youre confident enough to make it the way you want to make it, he added. Ajay Devgn hints at Drishyam 4 After the underwhelming response to the Malayalam version of Drishyam 3, Joseph seems to be developing the fourth instalment. Though Drishyam 3 was billed as The Conclusion of the epic trilogy, Devgn hinted that like his deceptive character Vijay Salgaonkar, the makers may have a trick up their sleeve as well, hinting at the remote possibility of Drishyam 4. At the moment, it is a conclusion, he said, before adding, I cant predict it. However, when pressed about the possibility of another instalment in the blockbuster franchise, Devgn didnt deny it outrightly. The decision was, this is the conclusion. The decision right now is that this is the conclusion. Right now, he added. Spoilers ahead In the Malayalam version of Drishyam 3, when Siddiques character, troubled by his wifes depression treatment in the US, vows to finally get back at Georgekutty Mohanlal and his family, the protagonist ends up having the last laugh yet again, even though that comes at the grave cost of physically hurting his elder daughter. Also Read - Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 5 Updates Ajay Devgns film makes it to top 5 highest-grossing Bollywood films of 2026, earns Rs 341 crore worldwide However, the Hindi version of Drishyam 3 avoids taking that road, and instead uses Salgaonkars influence in the Goan Catholic community and his love for making movies as his weapons of choice. Also starring Tabu, Rajat Kapoor, Shriya Saran, Ishita Dutta, Jaideep Ahlawat, Prakash Raj, and Kamlesh Sawant among others, Drishyam 3 has earned Rs 217 crore at the domestic box office within just five days.

articleTitle: Travel firm ‘denies refund’ as Australia tour cancelled amid Covid, man wins Rs 2.3 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: travel tour firm agency australia covid pandemic
description: The complainant had booked a 15-night, 16-day Australia–New Zealand tour with the agency in 2020 and paid an advance of Rs 2 lakh, but it was cancelled due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
body_raw: A West Bengal consumer commission has directed a travel company to refund Rs 2 lakh paid for an Australia-New Zealand tour cancelled during the Covid-19 pandemic, noting that it deliberately failed and neglected to refund the advance amount to the complainant. A bench of president Manoj Kumar Rai and member Ashoka Guha Roy Bera of the Kolkata District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission also awarded Rs 20,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation costs, holding that failure to refund the advance despite repeated requests amounted to deficiency in service. The complainant had paid Rs 2 lakh for the tour package but did not avail the services of the opposite party due to cancellation of the proposed tour. Though several requests, reminders, and personal visits were made to the opposite party by the complainant from time to time regarding refund of the advance amount, the opposite party deliberately failed and neglected to refund the advance amount to the complainant, the September 29 order read. The ruling highlighted that the conduct and irresponsible attitude of the travel company caused significant disruption and financial loss to the complainant. The said act of the opposite party proves the fact that the opposite party is deficient and negligent in rendering service to the complainant, it said. 2-week Australia, NZ tour The complainant had booked a 15-night, 16-day AustraliaNew Zealand tour with an international travel and tourism agency, scheduled to begin on October 14, 2020, and paid an advance of Rs 2 lakh. However, the tour was cancelled due to the Covid-19 pandemic and international travel restrictions. After the cancellation, the complainant sought a refund from the travel company and was assured that the amount would be returned. However, despite repeated requests and a legal notice dated February 10, 2022, the company did not refund the money. The complainant then approached the consumer commission in May 2022, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The travel company contested the complaint, arguing that under the contract the complainant was not entitled to a refund and that it had offered a credit voucher for future services after the tour was cancelled because of Covid-19 restrictions. Company failed to refund Order The commission found that the complainant had paid Rs 2 lakh for the AustraliaNew Zealand tour and was therefore a consumer of the travel companys services. It noted that the tour was cancelled because of the Covid-19 pandemic, cancellation of international flights and travel restrictions. Despite the cancellation, the travel company did not refund the Rs 2 lakh even though the complainant had made repeated requests, reminders and personal visits, the commission observed. It further observed that the company had failed to take any positive steps towards refund, which it described as a primary duty of a service provider. Takeaway The order underscored that travel companies cannot retain customers money after cancellation of services, even when disruptions arise from extraordinary circumstances. It reinforces consumers right to timely refunds and holds service providers accountable for financial loss and harassment caused by failure to return advance payments. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states West Bengal 1800-345-2808 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Delhi is India’s No. 2 concert market. So why are global artists skipping it?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cold play
description: Organisers say state incentives, venue readiness, pollution, permissions and differences in audience behaviour are making cities beyond Delhi more attractive.
body_raw: In the past year, Delhi-NCR has seen a spate of mega concerts, from hip hop star Travis Scott and English singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran, and is set to host upcoming shows by Fred Again and Khalid. It is currently Indias second-largest concert market, accounting for nearly 17 of concerts and live events in the country - about half the share of Mumbai. Yet some international artists planning India tours are skipping the national capital altogether, choosing Mumbai and Bengaluru - and, in some cases, smaller cities such as Guwahati and Ahmedabad - instead. For instance, English rock band Gorillaz is heading to Guwahati, Bengaluru and Mumbai in January next year. Post Malone performed at Guwahati last year while Coldplay only did shows in Ahmedabad and Mumbai. Many other artists like Enrique Iglesias and John Mayer only did concerts in Mumbai. Guns N Roses is headed to Guwahati in November after Bengaluru. For organisers and industry executives, the choice of city is increasingly about more than just audience size. They pointed to several factors behind the decision, from state subsidies and audience spending patterns to concerns around womens safety and air pollution in Delhi. To be sure, the Delhi government has been pushing to strengthen the Capitals concert economy, seeking to attract major international and homegrown artists and the wider economic activity that comes with them. After it emerged that high stadium rentals were an issue, in October last year, the Sports Authority of India SAI made it cheaper to host events at its venues by 40-50. Cities compete for global artists Deepak Choudhary, managing director of the event company Eva Live, said different states are increasingly seeking to attract concerts through subsidies. Speaking about the Guns N Roses tour, he said, Mumbai, theyve already done. Then they are going to Bengaluru, which is an automatic number two. Subsequently, instead of Delhi, they are headed to Guwahati because Assam subsidised the cost. The state government supported in a large way through sponsorship, Chaudhary explained. In 2024, Canadian artist Bryan Adams had performed in Meghalaya. Both Meghalaya and Assam have concert tourism policies, which subsidise part of the cost of organising the concert and simplify related processes, in return of expected gains to the states economy. Naman Pugalia, Chief Business Officer, Live Events, BookMyShow, disagreed. What we are seeing is a very robust and continuous decentralisation of demand. Delhi continues to be a strong and important market, while these other cities have also shown endeavor and initiative. He added that this is the story of India. We are growing in all directions and we are going fast. But that does not mean Delhi is any less important, he said. Why putting on a show is harder in Delhi An industry executive argued that the condition of venue infrastructure is not good in Delhi and a lot of money is spent on refurbishment. For instance, the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium is a great venue. All it needs is to be maintained, have clean toilets, well educated and well spoken, helpful staff who have answers. When we go and ask them about the rigging capacity, they dont know. They dont have basic layouts on digital files, so we have to make even the basic models ourselves, the executive said. He added that coordinating with government agencies is much easier in other states. Mohit Bijlani, Founder of events management company Team Innovation, agreed. In a massive metropolitan capital like Delhi, traffic, venue accessibility, permissions and crowd movement can make large-scale shows more complicated to execute. Because it is the seat of administration, the capital naturally requires meticulous coordination across multiple regulatory bodies, which can add layers of administrative planning for a promoter, he said. Upneet Bhatia, who has worked as a project director for Ed Sheeran, Post Malone and Backstreet Boys, among other artists, said people dont come to a concert just for the artist. They come for the whole experience, she said. If they are spending so much money and time, venues need to have proper hygiene, free drinking water, a medical professional on ground, and support for traffic and parking. The industry executive also said air pollution is a key factor which weighs on the minds of artists and their teams. It is very important for an international singer to justify the ticket price by giving his heart and soul, and building a great production, right? So, they have to sing live. But they also need to be protective of their voice. This is why the artist could be a little apprehensive, she believes. Different cities, different concert crowds Organisers also feel that different audiences have different tastes. For instance, a rock band will prefer going to Bengaluru rather than Delhi, since it has a South-Indian based audience which is well travelled. Shillong will also be a strong option, since it is known as the rock and music capital of India. On the other hand, a Punjabi artist will prefer Delhi and may not be able to sell out in Bengaluru, Chaudhary of Eva Live said. He also said paying capacity is another consideration. If a person from Mumbai is willing to pay Rs 10,000 for a ticket, the audience will be willing to pay Rs 9,000 in Bangalore, and the same will be Rs 8,000 in Delhi. Another industry executive said Delhi also has a larger market for complimentary tickets, which can affect advance sales. In Bengaluru and Mumbai, if people know an artist or festival is coming, they are excited and buy tickets. In Delhi, people tend to wait until the last minute, hoping they will get a complimentary ticket from someone, the executive said.

articleTitle: College withholds security money over lost receipt, MBBS student wins Rs 2.40 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Medical college security money refund MBBS student
description: A man who took admission in a private medical college and deposited refundable security money was later shifted to another college after the institute was closed for administrative reasons.
body_raw: A Rohtak consumer commission ordered a private medical college to pay Rs 2.40 lakh to a former MBBS student after it withheld his refundable security and library deposits because he could not produce the original receipt. The commission held that the mere failure to produce the original receipt was not, by itself, sufficient ground to permanently deny the refundable security amount, especially when the payment was supported by documentary evidence. President Nagender Singh Kadian, along with members Dr Tripti Pannu and Dr Vijender Singh, was hearing a complaint filed by a 26-year-old man who had completed his MBBS degree, including internship, in January 2019. The mere non-production of the original receipt, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, cannot by itself be treated as sufficient ground to permanently deny the complainant the refundable security amount, particularly when the payment is otherwise supported by documentary evidence and the respondents colleges have not established that the said amount was adjusted, refunded or otherwise utilised towards any lawful liability of the complainant, the September 24 order read. Shifted to another college The man claimed that he took admission in the private medical college in 2012 and deposited Rs 2 lakh as refundable security and Rs 25,000 as refundable library security with the institute on September 15, 2012. The man added that the said Institute was subsequently closed due to administrative reasons and its students were shifted to various medical colleges in Haryana. The complainant, along with other students, was shifted to another college at Hisar in 2017, where he completed his MBBS degree, including internship, in 2019. However, the man added that the security money was lying with the said college and he submitted a request letter in 2019 to the principal of the said colleges seeking refund of the security amount of Rs 2.25 lakh and enclosed a copy of the receipt. However, he was asked to produce the original receipt, which the complainant stated had been lost and was not traceable. Despite repeated requests, the security amount was not refunded, and the colleges ultimately refused to release the amount. Aggrieved, he moved the commission seeking refund and compensation for deficiency in service, causing him mental agony and harassment. The complainant was represented by advocate Anurag Malik before the commission. Colleges defence The college submitted that the complainant has not produced or furnished the original receipt of depositing the said security amount with the college, and in the absence of the original receipt of the security amount, it cannot be refunded, as the college is non-functional. It was further submitted that it was also instructed to all the candidates of each batch to submit the original fee receipts, but the complainant has not deposited the original fee receipt despite the direction to do so. Some students got refund The commission noted that it was an admitted position that the complainant had been a student of the erstwhile college and was subsequently shifted to another college. It also highlighted that the colleges themselves admitted that security amounts of other similarly situated students had been refunded pursuant to the government decision. The documents placed on record further show that even some students who subsequently submitted their receipts were thereafter granted refund, it noted. The commission further noted that the record demonstrates that the said security amount was refundable and that the university had undertaken the process of refunding the same to similarly situated students. In these circumstances, withholding the refundable security and library security amount of the complainant merely on account of non-production of the original receipt, despite the availability of a copy of the receipt and the affidavit furnished by him regarding its loss, amounts to deficiency in service on the part of the respondents colleges, it added. The commission also found that the colleges had not established that the amount had been adjusted, refunded or used towards any lawful liability of the complainant. Accordingly, the commission directed that said college pay Rs 2.25 lakh to the complainant along with Rs 10,000 towards compensation for mental agony and harassment and Rs 5,000towards litigation expenses. Takeaway This ruling highlights that non-production of the original receipt cannot, in the particular circumstances of the case, by itself justify denial of a refundable security amount when payment is otherwise supported by documentary evidence. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Haryana helpline 1800-180-2087 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Supreme Court to consider hearing plea to recall split verdict on law to appoint CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CEC appointment law Supreme Court, Supreme Court CEC appointment law, Chief Election Commissioner appointment law, Election Commissioners appointment law, 2023 CEC law, Constitution Bench CEC case, Supreme Court election commissioners case, Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, Election Commission appointment case, CEC EC appointment law challenge, SC Constitution Bench reference, judicial propriety plea, Supreme Court news, EC news, Indian Express news
description: The applicants have said Justice Satish Chandra Sharma did not disclose that his son is EC’s standing counsel in Madhya Pradesh.
body_raw: The Supreme Court said Wednesday it would consider a request to list for hearing an application seeking to recall or modify its September order referring petitions challenging the 2023 law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners to a Constitution Bench. The application contends that the son of one of the judges who delivered the order is a standing counsel for the Election Commission before the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Appearing for the applicants, Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. We will examine and then take a call, the CJI said. A two-judge bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered a split verdict on September 23 on the Centres request to refer the matter to a Constitution Bench. While Justice Datta rejected the prayer, Justice Sharma favoured the reference. Unable to reach a united view, the bench finally agreed to refer it to the CJI for a Constitution Bench. What the plea says The application said it is seeking recall of only Justice Sharmas opinion and recall or suitable modification of the common order on account of coming to light of a subsequent and material circumstance bearing upon judicial propriety, disclosure and the touchstone of impartial adjudication. The plea said that after the judgment was pronounced, news reports said Justice Sharmas son, Siddharth Sharma, is the standing counsel for EC before the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The applicants said they independently verified the information with the High Court and found that Siddharth Sharma has been engaged as EC counsel since July 10, 2024. The plea said this information.makes it clear that.Siddharth Sharma.was appointed.after the appointment of Gyanesh Kumar.and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu as Election Commissioners and engagement has continued since the elevation of.Kumar as CEC and appointment of Vivek Joshi as EC. It is prudent to assume that the incumbent members of EC and specifically.Kumar and.Sandhu had a direct role andor had direct knowledge about the appointment of.Sharma.as the standing counsel for the ECI before the Madhya Pradesh High Court, it said. Despite the appointment of.Gyanesh Kumar and.Sukhbir Singh Sandhu being directly under challenge before a bench in which.Justice Satish Chandra Sharma was a member, the appointment and engagement of Mr Siddharth Sharma was continued, it added. What petitioners want The applicants said this information was not disclosed to the parties by Justice Sharma at any point in time during the 5 hearings in the matter and that if it was disclosed during the hearings, they would have requested that.Justice.Sharma recuse from the hearing. The question is whether the established circumstances, viewed objectively, give rise to a reasonable apprehension concerning impartiality, the plea said, adding that proof of actual bias or of prejudice in the decision is not necessary for that purpose. The application said it does not impute actual bias, motive or want of good faith to Justice Sharma and the grievance is much narrower whether in view of an existing professional engagement of an immediate family member of the Honble Judge concerned with the institution whose statutory composition and with the functionaries of such institution whose appointments were directly under challenge, the Honble Judge ought to have disclosed the fact of such engagement to the parties when the proceedings were ongoing? The applicants added that they make no allegation concerning the manner in which Siddharth Sharma was engaged or his conduct as counsel. They also said they are not seeking a recall of Justice Dattas opinion. Madhya Pradesh Congress leader Jaya Thakur has also filed a curative petition seeking recall of the September 23 verdict.

articleTitle: How ‘Hanuman Ansh’ turned Neem Karoli Baba’s ‘quiet’ Kainchi Dham into a crowded, littered hotspot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh Kainchi Dham
description: The surge has prompted concern among locals, with influencer Aishwarya Kandpal speaking out about the growing crowds, traffic, litter, and social media activity around the ashram.
body_raw: Kainchi Dham, the Uttarakhand ashram associated with Neem Karoli Baba, has seen a sharp rise in attention in recent months, with the site drawing larger crowds following the success of the film Hanuman Ansh, which has reportedly crossed Rs 400 crore worldwide. The surge has prompted concern among locals, with influencer Aishwarya Kandpal speaking out about the growing crowds, traffic, litter, and social media activity around the ashram. Kandpal, who identifies herself as a local and has a personal connection with Kainchi Dham, shared a lengthy note on Instagram urging visitors to be more mindful of the sites religious significance and its fragile mountain environment. Idk why Im posting this at almost midnight by maybe I just couldnt hold it back? As a local Im so enraged, so angry, so upset. If youre visiting - which I know A FEW HUNDREDS OF YOU ARE- read this before you go, she wrote in the caption. Explaining why she chose to speak about the issue, Kandpal began by acknowledging that the post was unlike the content she normally shares. She then described how dramatically Kainchi has changed from the place she remembers growing up around. I was at Kainchi two days ago. Most of you probably know it as Kainchi Dham - a name that the media and the internet latched onto post-2020, and then ran into overdrive after a recent feature film, she wrote. For us locals though, its always been the quiet, nondescript Kainchi. And the ashram of my Gurus, Maharajji and Siddhi Maa, she added. According to Kandpal, the site was once a relatively quiet place where locals would visit for prayer and religious activities. She also spoke about her familys longstanding association with the ashram. She said she has been fortunate enough to stay there and deliberately chose not to turn those personal experiences into social media content. My retreats, my experiences are personal, and I would like to keep it like that. Same goes for my parents and brother. Read the post View this post on Instagram A post shared by aishwarya kandpal skincare haircare indianskinblog Both my parents have been serving at the ashram for years, and post-retirement, been spending a considerable part of the year staying within the sanctum sanctorum, helping with the ashrams day-to-day activities and being a part of the management. Their visits, however, much like those of scores of other locals, have become increasingly difficult, Kandpal said. Sacred place not meant to hold so many people Kandpal described roads packed with vehicles and constant honking, saying that her father, who is over 65, gets migraines from the noise. However, she stressed that her concern goes beyond the inconvenience caused to her family. Its about the ecology of a sacred place that wasnt exactly meant to hold so many people. According to her, the change is visible across the area, from roadside waste to the rapid growth of shops and traffic. The constant honking leaves birds and animals disturbed. The sides of the roads are lined with plastic bottles, wrappers, cigarette butts-you name it The whole area suddenly has a sea of new shops selling religious artifacts and the flood of people doesnt seem to end. Everyones scrambling, everyones in a rush. Theres pollution, extreme congestion, endless selfies and endless litter. Inside the ashram, Kandpal said she has also noticed visitors ignoring restrictions on photography and filming. I dont remember it being like this at all. And then you enter the ashram and see people doing exactly what theyve been asked to not do Phones out, cameras rolling, people filming themselves inside the premises and vlogging loudly on mics You cannot do that. Kandpal pointed out that photography, filming, and excessive noise are prohibited on the premises. Youre disturbing the sanctity of a hill thats been the tapobhumi of several revered saints since pre-independence times. Theres a strict no-photography, no noise, no film rule. For a reason. Kandpal also recalled what she described as the understated nature of the ashram and the teachings associated with Maharajji and Maa. Maharajji and Maa were always against any kind of lavish show of wealth Cellphones didnt exist for a long time so naturally they werent part of the ruckus. But photography, loud noise, donations, camps, flashy visits from VIPs or ministers were all STRCITLY prohibited in the ashram and still are, she said. The simplicity was a CHOICE. Precisely why the whole culture of coming here, filming everything, putting it online, turning every visit into content feels so completely at odds with the place. Concerns extend to surrounding hills Kandpals concerns also extend to the surrounding hills, where she said the increase in vehicles and visitors is putting additional pressure on the local environment. And then there are the mountains. There are cars and taxis backed up for miles, people honking constantly, bikes revving, trying to squeeze through whatever little space is left. Our fragile hills arent meant to handle so many people and so much litter left in their wake. No points for guessing how this leaves the birds and animals in the area completely, irrevocably disturbed. And I know this probably sounds like Im asking people to not come. Im not, she added. Kandpal clarified that she was not against people visiting Kainchi Dham. Instead, she said she wanted visitors to experience the place with the same sense of quiet and simplicity that she remembers from her childhood. Because firstly, I dont think I have any right to do that. Secondly, God belongs to everyone. And thirdly, its heartening that so many people have discovered the grace of this tiny ashram. So you shouldnt have to NOT come here. I ever so SIMPLY want you to experience the Kainchi I grew up around - quiet, nondescript, no frills and miles away from the prying eyes of the media and the internet, she said. Kandpal ended her post with a request for visitors to make small changes to their behaviour while travelling to and visiting the ashram. So maybe, just maybe Leave the phone on silent for a few, leave it in your bag, come in a group instead of taking five cars, keep the honking to a minimum, take your plastic back with you, and once you enter the ashram, remember why you came here, she said. The post has gained significant attention, with several users sharing similar experiences visiting Kainchi Dham and other spiritual destinations. One more thing to add. People must not visit a pilgrimage or ashram just because their a buzz around it - a famous person endorsed it or their is a superhit movie related to that place .people must visit ashrams or temples or sacred places only when they have an inner calling to visit . And people who are actually spiritual know the fact that God and his grace are present everywhere and every being , they just need to be a good person not to show off . Visiting such places brings peace and calm but finding God and receiving his grace is a totally different thing, an Instagram user wrote. Another user compared the situation with Kasar Devi, saying, You said it so well. I recently went to kasar Devi and can understand what you are saying. The only solution to this problem is banning phones and cameras completely and you will see the rush dropping by 80. I pray for nature. A third user wrote, I am from Rudrapur and i have to think 10 times when i want to go there now.. its so much crowded now.. I miss the old Kainchi dham.. It was so peaceful few years back.

articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Mains Answer Practice — GS 2
description: UPSC Civil Services Mains Exam 2027: This week’s GS 2 answer practice explores the role of community participation in water governance and Legislative privileges. Check out our thought process.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative for the practice ofMains answer writing.It covers essential topics of static and dynamic parts of the UPSC Civil Services syllabus covered under various GS papers. This answer-writing practice is designed to help you as a value addition to your UPSC CSE Mains. Attempt todays answer writing on questions related to topics ofGS-2to check your progress. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. QUESTION 1 How can decentralisation and community participation improve the effectiveness and sustainability of water governance in India? QUESTION 2 Legislative privileges are intended to secure the effective functioning of legislatures, not to insulate them from public scrutiny. Discuss. QUESTION 1 How can decentralisation and community participation improve the effectiveness and sustainability of water governance in India? Relevance The question links with GS Paper 2 Governance, decentralisation, local self-government and participatory governance. It also provides scope to discuss cooperative federalism and multi-level governance in addressing water challenges. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction - Indias water challenge is multifaceted, encompassing not only infrastructure development but also governance, institutional capacity, and sustainable service delivery. - The Gujarat example demonstrates that water security improves when governance, infrastructure, and community ownership are pursued simultaneously. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer Role of decentralisation and community participation - Water-related decisions can be decentralised to reflect local variables such as availability, quality, location, and household requirements. The notion of subsidiarity states that functions should be carried out at the lowest appropriate level. This strategy is used by Gujarats WASMO and other similar initiatives. - Institutions like Pani Samitis can help communities become active participants rather than passive beneficiaries. The Gujarat model demonstrates how local water governance institutions, with suitable infrastructure and external aid, may improve water conservation, harvesting, and recharge. - Decentralisation can improve operation and maintenance since local institutions are directly involved in water system management. This is especially critical as the task switches from simply providing tap connections to guaranteeing consistent, adequate, and dependable water service. - Community participation can assist ensure that taps are accompanied by steps to protect the underlying water source. Groundwater recharging, rainwater collection, and water supply must all be addressed simultaneously, rather than considering water provision as a standalone engineering project. - When local communities participate in planning and implementation, they can check service quality and continuity, as well as file grievances. This can help close the gap between administrative claims of infrastructure coverage and real service delivery on the ground. - Water availability and infrastructure requirements vary greatly by region. Local institutions can tailor responses to local hydrological and socioeconomic conditions rather than depending solely on centrally designed techniques. Conclusion - Effective water administration necessitates a shift from a centralized, infrastructure-centric strategy to participatory and decentralized service governance. Indias experience, particularly the Gujarat model and the developing Jal Jeevan Mission strategy, illustrates that infrastructure becomes more sustainable when people play an active role in planning, managing, and monitoring water systems. - Thus, decentralization can transform water governance from a government-provided function to a shared institutional and community duty. Sources From India to Global South, a Gujarat water-governance model, Many challenges of Jal Jeevan Mission Decentralisation is the only way ahead, Centre asks district collectors to regularly review Jal Jeevan Mission works, address gaps Points to Ponder What institutional mechanisms can facilitate effective participation in water management? What are the major challenges to decentralised water governance in India? Related Previous Year Question What are environmental pressure groups? Discuss their role in raising awareness, influencing policies and advocating for environmental protection in India. 2025 QUESTION 2 Legislative privileges are intended to secure the effective functioning of legislatures, not to insulate them from public scrutiny. Discuss. Relevance The question directly relates to GS Paper 2 Parliament and State Legislatures, constitutional provisions and legislative privileges. It helps to analyse the role of legislative privileges in preserving parliamentary functioning while protecting democratic scrutiny. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction - Legislative privileges are constitutional provisions designed to ensure that Parliament and state legislatures may carry out their tasks independently and effectively. - Articles 105 and 194 provide privileges and immunities to Parliament and State Legislatures respectively. However, these privileges are meant to facilitate legislative functioning, not create an unrestricted sphere of immunity from constitutional scrutiny or legitimate public criticism. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer Why are legislative privileges necessary? - Privileges protect legislators from external interference and enable them to participate freely in legislative proceedings. Article 1051 provides freedom of speech in Parliament, subject to the Constitution and parliamentary rules corresponding protection exists under Article 194 for State Legislatures. - Collective privileges allow Houses to govern their proceedings and deal with conduct that disrupts their operation. - Immunities enable lawmakers to carry out their constitutional duties without fear of legal ramifications from valid legislative speech or voting. Why cant privileges be used as a barrier against scrutiny? - The Supreme Court must decide whether privileges under Articles 105 and 194 can supersede fundamental rights like free speech and expression under Article 191a. The position made before the Court is that privileges exist to defend the Houses operation rather than the reputations of MPs, governments, or ruling parties. - India adheres to constitutional supremacy rather than the model of unrestrained parliamentary authority. As a result, legislative privileges function within the constitutional framework and cannot automatically take precedence over fundamental rights. - The Supreme Courts jurisprudence has gradually acknowledged limits to legislative privilege. In Raja Ram Pal 2007, the Court determined that the exercise of parliamentary privilege is subject to judicial review. In Amarinder Singh 2010, it was determined that privilege could not be utilised to punish conduct unrelated to the operation of the House. - When privilege proceedings culminate in the arrest or imprisonment of citizens or journalists, Articles 14 and 21 are invoked alongside Article 19. The exercise of legislative power over personal liberty creates issues of fairness, due process, and arbitrariness. - A free press allows individuals to monitor legislative activity. The 2003 Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege event, which involved actions against journalists from The Hindu and Murasoli, exemplifies the conflict between legislative privilege and press freedom. The Supreme Court suspended the arrest warrants and referred serious constitutional matters related to Articles 1943 and 191a for review. Conclusion - Legislative privilege is a tool for protecting legislative democracy, not an end in itself. Its credibility is ultimately tied to the legislatures ability to function effectively. - A constitutional balance must consequently protect legislative authority while ensuring that privilege is not used to repress valid criticism, journalistic freedom, or fundamental rights. Such a balance strengthens, not diminishes, the authority of democratic institutions. articleTitle: Mathura gurukul students went inside water tank after foul smell, 4 dead
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mathura ashram tragedy: 4 students die after inhaling toxic gas inside water tank
description: Police said two owners of Maharishi Panini Sanskrit Gurkulam have been taken into custody. A fifth student who also fell unconscious is stable
body_raw: Four students died after inhaling suspected poisonous gas inside an unused underground water tank at a gurukul in Mathuras Vrindavan late Tuesday night, when a group of students went into the tank to investigate a foul smell, police said. Two owners of Maharishi Panini Sanskrit Gurkulam have been taken into custody. The incident came to light after 11.30 pm. Mathura Senior Superintendent of Police SSP, Shlok Kumar, told The Indian Express that preliminary investigation so far has revealed that a group of students were cooking food on the ground floor of the ashram when a foul smell wafted out of the water tank nearby. The water tank, about 15 ft deep, was unused and was covered with a concrete lid. The SSP said the students initially tried to get rid of the smell by removing the small amount of water inside the tank with a bucket. One of the students then volunteered to go inside. He climbed down the stairs built into the tank but did not return or respond when the other students called out to him. Four others went down one after another in an attempt to bring him out. All of them fell unconscious, causing panic among other students waiting outside. Staff members and local residents then pulled all five students out of the tank, the SSP said. A police team had rushed to the gurukul by then. Policemen tried performing CPR and gave first aid to the students, but it did not help they were all rushed to the hospital. Four of the students - Manu Katare, 21, of Jabalpur Vishu and Aryan, 18, of Meerut and Kaushambi and Devansh, 17, of Vidisha - died during treatment in the early hours of Wednesday. The fifth student survived and is currently stable, Kumar said. SSP Kumar said they are waiting for families of the victims to file a complaint so they can register a case.

articleTitle: ‘Unrest, poverty brought them to India’: Court cuts jail term of 3 Bangladeshis
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bangladeshi nationals illegal immigrants detention madras high court
description: The Madras High Court, while considering the sentence, noted their economic hardship, migration from Bangladesh for employment, daily-wage work and several years of residence in India.
body_raw: The Madras High Court has upheld the conviction of three Bangladeshi nationals for residing in the State without valid travel documents however, observing that the appellants, owing to the unrest in Bangladesh and the uncertainty of their future, came to India to sustain themselves and their families, it modified their fine-default sentence and ordered authorities to complete their deportation within 30 days. Justice N Nirmal Kumar was dealing with a plea of three Bangladeshi nationals challenging their conviction under the Foreigners Act, 2004. It is not in dispute that the appellants, owing to the unrest in Bangladesh and the uncertainty of their future, and being unemployed and impoverished, came in search of employment and livelihood to sustain themselves and their families. Admittedly, they are neither involved in nor convicted of any economic offence, nor have they enriched themselves so as to assume that they possess the means to pay the fine, the court said on September 28. The court further emphasised that the appellants had come to India in search of livelihood they had stayed in Tiruppur for quite some time, and the first and second accused had also given birth to two children. It noted that the appellants had also been employed in banian factories in Tiruppur on a daily-wage basis. Three Bangladeshi nationals arrested The case arose from the arrest of three Bangladeshi nationals by the Veerapandi Police in Tiruppur in February 2025. Police found them with two children at Iduvampalayam and, during inquiry, they admitted that they were Bangladeshi citizens who had entered India without valid passports, visas, or other travel documents. According to the accused, they had been living and working in Tiruppur for over six years and had twin sons born at Tiruppur Government Medical College Hospital in September 2023. They said they had migrated from Bangladesh because of political unrest, unemployment, and poverty and had come to India in search of livelihood. The police registered a case, and the prosecution examined six witnesses and produced 12 exhibits. The trial court convicted all three under the provisions of the Foreigners Act, 2004. It sentenced each to two years rigorous imprisonment and a Rs 10,000 fine, with three months simple imprisonment in default. They challenged the conviction before the high court. Appearing for the petitioners, advocates M Mohamed Saifulla and R Bakiyalakshmi argued that they had not committed any other offence, had lived peacefully in Tiruppur, and were willing to return to Bangladesh. They also questioned whether proper procedures had been followed regarding their detention and deportation. They stated that due to political unrest, unemployment, and poverty, they moved from Bangladesh to Tiruppur seeking employment for their livelihood. At the time of crossing the border post, they informed their entry. They are very poor Court The court held that the prosecution had established that the three appellants were Bangladeshi citizens. Their Bangladeshi national identitycitizenship documents and birth certificates were produced in evidence, and they had entered India without valid travel documents. The court found no reason to interfere with their conviction under the Foreigners Act, and confirmed the two-year rigorous imprisonment imposed by the trial court. They hold, to date, a Bangladesh voter ID and citizenship card. They are natural citizens living here and have also begotten two children for their livelihood and subsistence, they are living in Tiruppur to make earnings and livelihood. They are law-abiding citizens and have not come under any adverse notice from the law-enforcing authorities. Now they are willing to go back to their country, the court noted. However, while considering the sentence, the court took note of their economic hardship and circumstances. They had migrated from Bangladesh in search of employment, worked as daily-wage workers in Tiruppur, and had been living there for several years. Two children were also born to the first and second accused at a government hospital in Tiruppur. The court observed, There is no doubt that they are very poor, are seeking livelihood, have migrated in search of employment, and are in penury and unable to pay the fine amount. Considering their financial circumstances, the court reduced the default imprisonment for non-payment of the Rs 10,000 fine from three months to one week, while retaining the fine and two years rigorous imprisonment.

articleTitle: Man caught recording Bombay HC proceedings; fined, phone confiscated
articleFeaturedImageAlt: bombay high court video recording
description: The high court also noted that such recordings are "manipulated in ways unimaginable, and then distorted versions are posted on social media" and "in fact, it has become quite rampant."
body_raw: Noting incidents of court proceedings being recorded without permission, the Bombay High Court has ordered the confiscation of the mobile handset used and imposed a Rs 10,000 fine on a man after he was caught doing so. Emphasising that the incidents have been unfortunately on the rise, the Bombay High Court also noted that such recordings are manipulated in ways unimaginable, and then distorted versions are posted on social media and in fact, it has become quite rampant. A bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale took suo motu on its own cognisance on October 5, noting that while the court was in session, around 1223 pm, a person sitting in the last row held a mobile phone, with its flash on. Suspecting he was recording court proceedings, the court staff, on the judges instructions, seized his phone and sent it for examination. The person, identified as Dilip Wagh, who works at the Education Inspectors office, was visiting the Government Pleader. He deleted the video recording after being caught. The video was later retrieved by the courts IT department. The HC noted that except for the HC registrys written permission, there was an express bar under HCs Rules to record court proceedings, which Wagh did not obtain, and he was fully aware of these basic expectations. There cannot be any objection for any member of the public to attend the Court and witness the Court proceedings, as they are open proceedings. However, certainly, restrictions on any member of the public to adhere to the rules and regulations governing the Court proceedings, when inside the Courtroom, need to be followed in letter and spirit, the HC noted. Thus, considering the seriousness, casualness and frequency of such instances happening, it is high time that actions as the law would mandate are taken by the Court, the order added. The judges stated they would be falling in our duty if they overlook the Rules by not taking any action. While the court accepted Waghs apology and did not initiate contempt proceedings, it ordered confiscation of the mobile handset, removal of all data with a registry panchanama, and its disposal as per legal procedures. He was also ordered to pay Rs 10,000 to the High Court Legal Services Authority within two weeks, and compliance was sought by October 19.

articleTitle: Paying Rs 5,000 by UPI after Oct 15? Who pays new charge and what RBI governor said today
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra
description: Starting October 15, select high-value UPI person-to-merchant transactions will attract an merchant discount rate (MDR) of 0.4%
body_raw: The National Payments Corporation of Indias NPCIs recent decision to introduce a merchant discount rate MDR on select Unified Payments Interface UPI transactions marks a significant shift in the economics of the countrys digital payments ecosystem. However, the Reserve Bank of Indias RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has sought to make one thing clear - the new charge, according to him, is unlikely to dent the enormous scale of UPI. On UPI-MDR, a decision has already been taken, Malhotra said on Wednesday. As of now, we do not see any drop in UPI volumes, and I dont personally think that a small fee will have a major impact on the volumes. Starting October 15, select high-value UPI person-to-merchant P2M transactions will attract an MDR of 0.4. The charge will apply to transactions above Rs 2,000, with a cap of Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. RBI repo rate news LIVE The crucial point, however, is where the burden falls. The MDR will be paid by merchants within the digital payment ecosystem, while consumers will not be charged. That distinction is important. UPI has become synonymous with frictionless digital payments, and any change to the cost structure of transactions inevitably raises questions about whether users and merchants will alter their behaviour. The RBI, at least for now, does not appear concerned that the introduction of a fee for certain transactions will undermine the platforms momentum. Growing volumes The latest numbers offer some support to that assessment. UPI transaction volumes grew 22.2 in the second quarter of 2026-27, although this was slower than the 24.2 growth recorded in the first quarter. While the central bank regulates the payment system, the government has created the legal framework. The current UPI MDR structure has been introduced by NPCI under that framework. The numbers point to continued expansion, but they also underline the scale of the challenge. UPI is not merely another payment mechanism. Its strength lies in its reach and volume, and the policy question is whether introducing MDR on a segment of transactions can coexist with that growth without altering the behaviour that has made UPI so pervasive. Malhotras argument is straightforward a small fee should not materially change volumes. But the real test begins after October 15, when the new framework will move from policy announcement to actual transactions. Bankers said the fact that consumers will not bear the charge directly could help limit any immediate impact on usage. Yet merchants are at the centre of the MDR framework, and the eventual effect on the digital payment ecosystem will depend on how they respond to the additional processing cost, they said. For now, the RBI is betting that UPIs scale and convenience will outweigh the impact of the new charge. The data shows that volumes continue to rise, even as the pace of growth has moderated. The coming months will reveal whether the RBIs confidence is justified. If UPI volumes remain resilient, the MDR may prove to be a limited adjustment to a rapidly expanding payments ecosystem. If growth weakens sharply, however, the decision could face tougher questions.

body_raw: Three men who allegedly harassed a woman from Nagaland and forcibly pulled her towards a Mercedes car in the parking lot of a five-star hotel in Chanakyapuri have been bound down by the Delhi Police, sources said. To be bound down means to be required to appear before an investigating officer on a given date. The incident took place around 3.15 am Sunday, police said. According to police officers, the three men were sitting in the car parked at the hotel and were playing loud music. As the woman and her friends came towards the parking lot, one of them objected to the music. When the woman moved towards the exit gate, one of the men sitting in the car pulled her hand towards the vehicle. When my friend came to save us, they beat him with hockey sticks and punched his face. When my two other friends came, they beat them with hockey sticks as well, the woman alleged in the FIR. One of the friends suffered injuries to his teeth., an officer said. The medico-legal case report of one of the victims friends cites swelling in the right hand. The accused allegedly fled from the spot in their car after police reached the location. The complainant had noted down the cars registration number, which helped investigators trace the men, police said. The three accused were booked at Chanakyapuri police station. articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | Why does a dedicated growth fund matter for SMEs?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | Why does a dedicated growth fund matter for MSMEs? upsc, upsc cse, upsc ias, upsc 2027
description: The Union Cabinet has approved Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Growth Fund recently. Why was this fund needed? How significant are MSMEs to India’s economy and what are other government supported credit support initiatives for them? Go beyond the nugget to understand updated MSMEs classification.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on Small and Medium Enterprise SME Growth Fund. Knowledge Nugget Small and Medium Enterprise SME Growth Fund. Subject Indian Economy Why in the news? The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the Small and Medium Enterprise SME Growth Fund SGF with an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore to provide equity support to small and medium enterprises. The fund was first announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27. Key takeaways 1. Under the initiative, the government will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund AIF established under the SGF framework. 2. A majority of the funds investments will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing enterprises, with a focus also on SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. 3. As per the government Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities. Why was a dedicated SME fund needed? 5. According to the government, while several existing funds provide equity support to businesses, most of them focus on early-stage enterprises and largely cater to micro enterprises. 6. This has left a structural gap in the availability of growth-stage equity capital for small and medium enterprises. 7. While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders, the government said in a statement. 8. The SME Growth Fund is designed to address this critical financing gap by providing patient growth equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability, it added. 9. The Centre expects the fund to help SMEs scale up, improve productivity and strengthen export competitiveness by enabling manufacturing enterprises to expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies and achieve greater scale. 10. Vinod Kumar, President, India SME Forum said the Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund can set in motion a powerful cycle, where stronger manufacturers place larger and more consistent orders with smaller suppliers, enabling those businesses to invest in better machinery, improve quality, build skills and create jobs. 11. As these capabilities deepen across industrial clusters, more MSMEs can meet the standards required by large domestic buyers and global supply chains. The cumulative outcome can be higher domestic value addition, greater export competitiveness and reduced dependence on imported components and finished products, Kumar said. Why are MSMEs significant? 12. Small-scale industries make up about 95 per cent of all industrial units and form a significant part of the economic structure of the nation. Mahatma Gandhi said that The salvation of India lies in cottage and small scale industries. 13. Indias 63 million MSMEs employ more than 320 million people, contribute about 31 per cent of GDP, 35 per cent of manufacturing output, and 49 per cent of exports. 14. MSMEs are one of Indias most important non-farm employment generators, particularly for semi-skilled and less-skilled workers. 15. MSMEs are also particularly important for labour-intensive exports such as textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, handicrafts and processed products. 16. They can i spread industrial activity beyond metropolitan centres. ii create employment closer to workers homes. iii support smaller towns. iv integrate rural economies with manufacturing. v create opportunities for women, artisans and first-generation entrepreneurs. What are the major government credit support initiatives for MSMEs? 1. In India, micro and small enterprises benefit from a 25 per cent public procurement quota and MSMEs overall are eligible for priority sector lending, with a sub-target for micro firms. 2. Banks and other financial institutions including NBFCs are guaranteed to offer collateral-free credit to MSMEs. 3. The scheme covers up to Rs. 5 crore w.e.f. 01.04.2023 per borrowing unit of collateral-free credit facilities term loans andor working capital provided to micro and small businesses by qualified lending institutions. 4. Budget 2025 proposed customised credit cards with a 5 lakh limit for micro enterprises registered on the Udyam portal. 5. In May 2026, the government approved ECLGS 5.0, with a credit guarantee cover of 2.55 lakh crore to support businesses affected by external shocks. 6. ECLGS 5.0 provides additional credit of up to 20 of an MSMEs peak working capital used in Q4 FY26, subject to a ceiling of 100 crore per borrower. The government provides a 100 guarantee on this additional credit, with a one-year moratorium and a five-year repayment period. 7. Budget 2026 proposed an additional 2,000 crore top-up for the Self-Reliant India Fund SRIF to maintain access to risk capital for micro enterprises. SRIF was established in 2021 as a fund-of-funds vehicle to infuse equity and risk capital into viable MSMEs. 8. An MSME can be profitable on paper and still fail if a large buyer doesnt pay on time. Delayed payments to MSMEs were estimated at 8.14 lakh crore in FY24, down 7 from the previous figure of 10.76 lakh crore.At the same time, the estimated unmet credit requirement was around 25 lakh crore. 9. Budget 2026 proposed several measures to expand the use of the Trade Receivables Discounting System TReDS. TReDS allows MSMEs to receive finance against their unpaid invoices instead of waiting for buyers to make payments. BEYOND THE NUGGET Updated MSMEs Classification 1. The Government of India updated the classification limits for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises MSMEs effective April 1, 2025. 2. The criteria use a composite measure of investment in plantmachineryequipment and annual turnover for both manufacturing and service units. 3. Investment limits have been increased 2.5 times and turnover limits are doubled from previous thresholds. 4. The investment limit to be classified as a micro enterprise is now up to Rs 2.5 crore. For small enterprises, this limit is up to Rs 25 crore, and for medium ones, it is Rs 125 crore. 5. Similarly, the turnover limit for these classifications goes up to Rs 10 crore for micro enterprises, Rs 100 crore for small ones, and Rs 500 crore for medium enterprises. The same limits apply equally to manufacturing and service sector businesses. Post Read Questions Consider the following statements with reference to India UPSC CSE, 2023 1. According to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development MSMED Act, 2006, the medium enterprises are those with investments in plant and machinery between 15 crore and 25 crore. 2. All bank loans to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises qualify under the priority sector. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Answer b Faster economic growth requires an increased share of the manufacturing sector in GDP, particularly of MSMEs.
