articleTitle: ‘No one believed in Hanuman Ansh, declared flop on day 8’: Producer on miracle that saved it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh sequel update by Anupriya Nagar
description: In an exclusive conversation, Anupriya Nagar shared an update on the second instalment of Hanuman Ansh, she even spoke about start a production house.
body_raw: After successfully running for 62 days at the box office and earning over Rs 425 crore, Hanuman Ansh has emerged as more than a film - it has become a moment in Indias cinematic history, a lot like Jai Santoshi Maa that once gave competition Sholay back in the day. The devotional film, based on Neem Karoli Baba, was made on a budget of a shade less than Rs 2 crores. Amid its massive commercial success, SCREEN spoke to its co-producer, Anupriya Nagar, about its trajectory at the ticket windows, and how that Hanuman Ansh has been planned as a trilogy. It has also become the catalyst for Anupriya, who is 22, to write a book on it and set up a production house. Anupriya Nagar on the success of Hanuman Ansh The film, which started its journey with Rs 10 lakh collection, has emerged as the best return on investment seen in the Hindi film industry in decades. Talking about this feat, Anupriya shared, To be very honest, I didnt become a part of this film for it to become a financial project, for me it was an emotional project. There were no expectations. Even the team never expected the film to do so well. We just wanted the devotees and kids to watch the film and learn about Indian culture. The first two weeks, the film didnt work at all, and on the eighth day, the industry declared the film a flop. We became a little nervous and thought, If devotees are not supporting us, how will the rest of the audience watch the film? Also Read A 21-year-old gave up Zurich job to fund Hanuman Ansh, earned Rs 50 cr on Rs 50 lakh share We knew that this film would only work through word-of-mouth since it had no known faces, a first-time director. While Maharajji is the biggest superhero of the film, from a general perspective, this was the thought. Even before I came on board, people never believed in the film. They asked how this film would work. While people were craving this kind of content, not too many films were made like this. When the screens went down from 300 to 30, we were told that only a miracle could save the film from being pulled down at theaters. I couldnt sit with my hands tied, I did whatever I could, Anupriya Nagar added. I gave all my savings for Hanuman Ansh Talking about how the film has been loved for its simplicity, Anupriya shared they initially thought of releasing the film on OTT. Hanuman Ansh doesnt align with the formula in which films are made these days. Its a simple period film, so its normal to question if the audience will relate to it. Everyone thinks before the release they have made a Mughal-e-Azam, its only when it releases do you understand how the film is received. There were also conversations about taking the film to OTT first. But we wanted to build a community, so we went with a theatrical release, she said. Giving up a job opportunity at Zurich was not the only risk Anupriya took she even invested her lifes savings in Hanuman Ansh. When Ragini Sona told me they needed funds, I decided to give what I had saved. I used to work during Christmas holidays and get extra salary so I could invest it I thought I would go to Zurich and live a comfortable life. Later, I used all of those savings for Hanuman Ansh, Anupriya shared. Sharing what she plans to do with the profit of Hanuman Ansh, she said, After Hanuman Ansh, people started calling me Chasmewali Producer bespectacled producer fame has come my way. But I am still the same. Everyone is telling me to get a holiday house with the money Hanuman Ansh has made. I am not going to gift myself anything. I have everything I want. It is only because of the people that the film is doing so well, so I just want to give it back to society. I want to help children and provide proper education and health facilities and I am in the process of starting my foundation. It will be my greatest gift. I celebrated the films success with my family and we all went to Kaichi Dham after a really long time. It was the best celebration. Hanuman Ansh would be a trilogy While Anupriya shared how the film and political industry have come to support the film now, she recalled a conversation she had with Premanand Maharaj. Anupriya shared, I met Premanand Maharajji after the film released and was doing well. I thought he wouldnt recognize me. But he was so happy to see me. He told me, main bohot khush tha ke aap aaye, film ke pehle, aur uske baad bhi. Apne santo ke liye bohot bada kaam kiya hai He told me I am very happy you came here before the film and after its success. You have done a great service to the spiritual leaders. It was such a huge thing to say. Sharing that Hanuman Ansh is supposed to be a trilogy, Anupriya added, I am writing a book on my journey with Hanuman Ansh and with Maharajji. I am in the process of establishing my own production house, where I can tell these wonderful stories. We will take the film to OTT now. Regarding the rest of the stories, even 10 films will not be enough for it. From the very beginning, we thought of making a trilogy, this is the first part. We have to sit and plan the second film, and now the responsibility is greater. We need to decide the timeline. Right now we are trying to do justice to the film. The numbers are increasing, and we are still trying to reach more and more people. The film has now gone global as it was released overseas on September 11. Hanuman Ansh was released in theaters on 7 August 2026.

articleTitle: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis and women’s team coach each other
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis returns to coach a women's football team.
description: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis' titular character returns to Richmond to coach a women's football team -- only to learn life lessons in return.
body_raw: Ted Lasso season 4 was an afterthought. Ted Lasso, having hung his UK boots and relocated back to his home turf of the US, is summoned back to Richmond, this time to coach a womens team. The premise was enough for the Indian audience to churn out memes of Ted Lasso delivering the climactic sattar minute speech in the womens locker room, a la Shah Rukh Khans hockey coach Kabir Khan in Shimit Amins 2009 seminal Bollywood sports drama Chak De India. But Ted Lasso is no vindictive, defamed coach trying to get back his lost glory. Hes just an average American Joe pulled back to a land thousands of miles apart to do what he does best - live. Fish out of water - two times over Co-creator and lead actor Jason Sudeikis had signed off as the titular buoyant football coach after season 3 of Apple TVs Emmy Award-winning show before he had an epiphany. As he returns to Richmond to coach its second-division womens football team - he faces resistance, particularly from their coach Alice Chilton Tanya Reynolds. And just like that, its like season 1 all over again. A soccer player roped in to train a British football team? Heck, he doesnt even like tea. But thats not important. Whats key here is how Lasso makes his way in, not by blending into the British way of life, but by dialling up his infectious, charming self. Hes inherently a team player, so divisions - whether theyre nationality or gender - have little bearing on his being. Not that he vowed to, but instead of relishing tea, he ends up getting Rebecca Welton Hannah Waddingham, the uptight AFC Richmond owner, addicted to shortbread biscuits. Coach Alice is too messed up and amour-propre to exchange her head position with a man - however ebullient and chivalrous he may be - for the womens football team. The way episode 1 ends, one does feel that the male wagon of creators and showrunners - Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Brett Goldstein - are using the audiences unabating love for Ted to shortchange Alice. Take it or leave it with a shrug of shoulders - that seems to be Teds tone, even though hes trying to be as unobtrusive and friendly as possible. So, when Alice caves in - and doesnt accept Teds farewell gift - it feels like feminism just walked backwards by a few steps. Its natural then that Alice feels a strong surge of jealousy when she sees Ted warm his way into the womens locker room - even though it was she who handheld him and Coach Beard the first time, making them close their eyes and wait until the women are dressed. Ted isnt even the most abhorrent of men who mansplain women into learning football. Hes considerate, patient, and most crucially, in touch with his feminine side. He urges his players to cry out their emotions - theres crying in football - and not bottle them up like Alice. Hes also as conscientious - cleaning up a bar with the women after they make a mess out of it during an impromptu brawl with a bunch of men did Kabir Khan and the Chak De India girls clean up the McDonalds? No. Learning from life - and everything that it throws at you But theres something that Ted is bound not to get as a man. In an affecting and strikingly relevant episode, we see members of the team deal with personal crises - from taking up odd jobs to make ends meet since second-division womens football doesnt exactly pay handsomely, or doubling up as a mother of two because your husband treats her ambition as inconvenience. Teds go-to magic word - Believe - doesnt exactly cut it here, as thats easier said than done. It then takes an Alice to step in and make a tiny addition to get the women all pumped up - Believe. and win. Its this added adrenaline and call to action that season 4 of Ted Lasso needed to make it as effective as its predecessors. The individual arcs of all the women players couldve made for a far more impactful and well-rounded season than wasting it on side plots like a secret investor buying their way into AFC Richmond. Not all side plots are as tepid though. Rebecca giving new love a chance, before sabotaging it, and then giving it yet another lease of life, couldve made the most patient of men run out of the virtue. But it makes the audience comfort her like Phil Dunster does in his memorable cameo. Roy Goldstein and Keeley Juno Temple are arguably the Ross and Rachel of Ted Lasso, though even the Friends pair couldnt pull off the downright adorbs football commentary scene with a makeup set, including what Roy calls a squishy pencil makeup brush, as Keeley corrects him. Also Read - When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood bunch of thieves for stealing his bestseller plots The strength of Ted Lasso, thus, remains in the quiet, slow change it brings about, just like its central character and his constant nudging towards a fair, equal, and kinder world. The audience is invited into the heads of all characters as they struggle with their feelings. But when they finally let them out to the ones theyve been wanting to confide in, were gently drawn out. That not only prevents the show from getting preachy, but also helps us come to terms with leaving the beloved characters to their lives, if this is indeed the last season. A voiceover from the grave - one for the ages - by the shows old guard surely helps you tug it into the bed like its a child you want to kiss goodbye - I think of each name as a comfortable music in the mouth. tending, as all music does. towards silence.

articleTitle: Flydubai wants to be back in Tel Aviv after attack on Indian captain Smit Machchhar; Israel refuses
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pilot Indian Capt. Smit Machchhar was at the controls of a FlyDubai flight that was diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing. (Israel's Foreign Ministry via AP)
description: Flydubai said its investigation into the reported attack was concluding and many employees had been fired.
body_raw: Flydubai has sought permission to resume flights to Israel a week after an Omani co-pilot attacked Indian captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit of flight FZ1073 on a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, but Transportation Minister Miri Regev has so far declined the request, Channel 13 reported on Wednesday. Flydubai told Israeli authorities that its investigation into the September 30 incident was nearing completion and that several employees had been dismissed. Officials from Israels transportation ministry have also been invited to Dubai next week, the report added. The Omani co-pilot, Hammam al-Hammami, attacked Smit Machchhar during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The aircraft, with 182 people on board, was subsequently diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after the wounded captain managed to open the cockpit door and passengers helped subdue the attacker. Israels new screening rules for foreign airline crew According to Channel 13, the draft requirements, formulated after the attack, would require non-Israeli citizens, including pilots and crew, to complete and submit a form 48 hours before flights for government review. Citizens of countries classified as red under the proposed screening rules would also be subject to checks by Mossad and Shin Bet. Flydubai suspended operations to Tel Aviv Flydubai suspended its flights to Tel Aviv after the September 30 incident, saying the move had been made at the request of the authorities. At the request of the authorities, we have temporarily suspended operations to Tel Aviv until further notice, Flydubai CEO Ghaith Al Ghaith said in a statement. Our teams are working around the clock to support disrupted passengers and help them reach their final destinations, he said. Al Ghaith said a full official investigation into the incident was underway and was being led by the relevant authorities, with Flydubai supporting the process. I know there are many questions about what happened on board FZ 1073. A full official investigation, led by the relevant authorities and fully supported by flydubai, is underway. It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts, he said. Flydubai said all 172 passengers and crew on board were safe. The airlines captain had also returned to the UAE after receiving medical clearance. The incident has triggered wider scrutiny of how foreign airline crews are screened before operating flights to Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has separately ordered a review of the security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel following the attack.

articleTitle: Rate hike was expected. But RBI reinforces hints that more are coming
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Members of the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra (centre); and (from left) Deputy Governors Shirish Chandra Murmu, Swaminathan Janakiraman, Poonam Gupta, and Rohit Jain in Mumbai on October 7. (PTI)
description: The RBI has tightened its stance from "neutral" to "calibrated tightening". But neither inflation figures nor the central bank’s own forecasts have changed dramatically since August. So what explains the shift?
body_raw: It was almost a foregone conclusion that the Reserve Bank of India RBI would increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points bps to 5.5 on Wednesday. What was not as widely expected was that the RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC would also make the policy stance more restrictive - from neutral to calibrated tightening. This shift is important. As Governor Sanjay Malhota pointed out, the change in the stance means interest rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook. According to Madhavi Arora, Chief Economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, the change in the stance feels more like a forward guidance and the RBI has clearly prepared markets for a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. While some economists did and continue to predict only a shallow rate hike cycle of 50 bps one basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point or so, financial markets had - even before the MPC decision to increase the repo rate for the first time in more than three-and-a-half years on Wednesday - already priced in a long-ish hiking cycle of at least 100 bps. This was despite the MPCs unexpectedly dovish statement and language on August 5, when the central bank said there were little signs of generalisation of price pressures so far. Generalisation of inflation means higher prices spreading to other parts of the CPI basket. We have already seen a stark example of this generalisation with commercial cooking gas getting expensive after the start of the West Asia war, restaurants and cafes sharply increased their menu prices. Consider the following the number of items in the CPI basket whose inflation was more than 4 was 65 in January and rose to 110 in August. Moreover, prices of 314 of the 358 items were higher in August compared to July. In February, this number was 236. Data for September, which will be released next week, may show more of the same. Little change in data When the MPC last met, it had with it the Consumer Price Index CPI inflation data for June, which had risen to 4.38 from 3.93 in May. Meanwhile, Wholesale Price Index WPI inflation had edged up similarly to 9.87 from 9.68. Since then, inflation developments on both fronts have not been outsized while retail inflation has risen to 4.82 in August, wholesale prices rose by 9.92. The RBI is mandated to target a CPI inflation rate of 4 in the medium-term in a band of 2-6. Of course, the MPC must be forward-looking and cant decide interest rates based on data for two months ago - it needs to take a view on what it thinks inflation might be a year or so down the line because interest rate changes impact growth and inflation in the economy with a delay of 9-12 months. However, the RBIs own projections have not moved dramatically, as the chart below shows. Governor Malhotra said in his statement on Wednesday that recalibrating the policy rate is imperative because headline inflation is seen averaging almost 5.8 over the next three quarters and core inflation is projected at 4.4 in 2026-27. The Governors statement emphasising that average Inflation of 5.8 over the next three quarters with core inflation projected at 4.4 needs policy recalibration reinforces the hawkishness, said Puneet Pal, PGIM India Mutual Funds Head of Fixed Income. Pal expects incrementally 75-100 bps of rate hikes over the next nine months. But even back in August, these forecasts were not markedly different CPI inflation or retail inflation was expected to average almost 5.6 in the three quarters starting October, while the RBI had predicted an average core inflation rate of 4.3 this fiscal. But it is only now that the MPC sees some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and generalisation of inflation after saying in August that there were little signs of the same. Economists were not convinced by the assessment made in August. On the monsoon front, the rain deficit this season has been 13, not very far off from 11 or so at the time of the August policy. And the West Asia conflict has never really shown crystal-clear signs of resolution, with matters remaining uncertain. New developments What has materially changed is the growth outlook, with the GDP seen expanding 7.1 this fiscal versus 6.7 in August following the unexpectedly high 7.8 growth in April-June. However, the MPC has noted on Wednesday that there is limited evidence of demand side pressures, although risks in view of strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates exist. Apart from faster-than-anticipated domestic growth, what has also changed since August 5 is that central banks around the world have increased their policy rates, including the US Federal Reserve, which last month raised the federal funds rate target range by 25 bps to 3.75-4 - its first rate-hike in three years. Like the MPC now, all 12 voting members of the Fed favoured this rate hike. Another one is expected in what remains of 2026. Other central banks to have raised interest rates last month include the Bank of Japan, the European Central Bank, and the Reserve Bank of Australia, among others. But the RBI focuses on domestic inflation and growth developments. And signs have been apparent for a while now that price pressures are spreading due to weak rains, the El Nino, and higher memory chip prices, among others. The reasons behind the MPCs turn between August and now may explain what lies ahead.

articleTitle: 83-year-old Lonavala man held for ‘shooting dead’ grandson over property dispute
articleFeaturedImageAlt: grandfather kills grandson
description: Officers from Lonavala City Police Station reached the spot and initially registered the case as an accidental death.
body_raw: Lonavala city police have arrested an 83-year-old man for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, a lawyer, following a property dispute in Bhushi village, and then trying to pass off the killing as an accident. A case has been registered against five members of the family. The deceased has been identified as Advocate Abhay Manik Marathe. The accused, his grandfather Motiram Marathe, was arrested after police found inconsistencies in the familys version of events. Abhays father, Manik Marathe, is a former Lonavala municipal council corporator. The family owns Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Superintendent of Police Sandeep Singh Gill said, Motiram Marathe holds a valid arms licence for a 12-bore gun, which he used for hunting. According to the family, the incident took place on Monday. They told police that Abhay was cleaning his grandfathers gun when the trigger was accidentally pulled and a bullet hit him in the chest. Officers from Lonavala City Police Station reached the spot and initially registered the case as an accidental death. However, police grew suspicious on inspecting the scene. The injury on Abhays chest, the bloodstains and the firearm itself did not appear to match the familys account. The body was sent to Sassoon Hospital for a post-mortem examination, and police consulted medical experts. Officers also questioned the Marathe family members, along with the manager and staff of the hotel. The inquiry revealed that Abhay and his grandfather had been involved in a property dispute. Motiram wanted to sell their land and distribute money among family members, however, Abhay had different plans for the land development, which led to the dispute, Gill said. Police said that the two had a heated argument and that the grandfather allegedly shot Abhay when the latter charged at him. Abhay was reportedly inside the hotel premises. Based on these findings, police registered a case against five people, including Motilal Marathe, and arrested him. Attempt to destroy evidence According to police, the family tried to cover up the crime after the shooting. CCTV cameras near the spot were allegedly removed, along with the DVR unit that stored the footage. Hotel staff were also allegedly threatened against speaking about the incident. Officials are now probing the property dispute within the Marathe family, the sequence of events after the shooting, and the attempts to destroy evidence, inspector Pramod Kshirsagar of the local crime branch said.

articleTitle: Between starlight and Antarctic ice — another neutrino is on its way
articleFeaturedImageAlt: physics, nobel, ice
description: Thanks to Nobel Prize winner Francis Halzen and his team, the ice is ready
body_raw: For an astronomer, light is the easy part Hold up a lens or a mirror and starlight is yours. Neutrinos are another matter. Born in the most violent places in the cosmos, these ghost-like particles pass through planets, people and most detectors almost without a trace. It took decades to turn a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a telescope for these deep-space messengers. This years Nobel Prize in Physics goes to the man who stayed with that hunt Francis Halzen, a Belgian-born physicist at the University of WisconsinMadison. Why chase a particle so hard to catch in the first place? You could see things in the universe you couldnt see any other way, Halzen once said in an interview. Neutrinos barely interact, so they escape from deep inside their sources while light gets stuck on the way out. Think of a journalist trying to reach the one official who was in the room where a major policy was made. The press conference is easy to attend that is astronomy with visible light. But the insider who knows what was really decided avoids reporters. Catching a neutrino is harder still. The gigantic IceCube Neutrino Observatory near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole station in Antarctica has lowered 86 cables into the ice, the deepest reaching almost 2.5 kilometers down. To place them, scientists had to melt holes in the ice with hot water. Each cable sports sixty sensitive light detectors, like beads strung on a thread. On rare occasions, a neutrino strikes a nucleus of an atom in the ice, and the collision generates high-energy particles. The resulting particles move faster than light travels in ice, and generate an eerie, bluish flash, much like a sonic boom of a supersonic jet. That glow, the signature of a far traveling neutrino, is what the sensors on the strings pick up. Such an instrument couldnt be built overnight. What Halzen himself once called a cute idea took smaller trials to hone the skill and show what a larger detector could potentially deliver. Conceived in the 1980s, the last cable in IceCube was dropped in 2010. Since then, it has been eavesdropping on far-away violent phenomena in the universe. Some strange galaxies, unlike our own Milky Way, host massive black holes that churn the gas in their cores and spew spectacular jets. These jets accelerate high energy particles called cosmic rays, which collide and produce neutrinos. These neutrinos point back to where cosmic rays are produced. The discoveries at IceCube have been helping astronomers to peek inside the core of these galaxies. In 2017, a single neutrino hurtled through the observatory, and its path indicated it was coming from the direction of the constellation Orion. Alerted astronomers worldwide swiveled their telescopes in that direction and found a blazar, a giant galaxy whose central black hole, weighing hundreds of millions of suns, spits out a jet aimed straight at Earth. The discovery gave a major boost to multi-messenger astronomy, where scientists use visible light, neutrinos, and gravitational waves to study the same cosmic event, pulling together the clues from all the light we cannot see. IceCube has also confirmed a prediction from the 1960s about how an antineutrino interacts with an electron. Halzen, the principal investigator of this unique venture, has long been drawn to astroparticle physics, the area of research that marries astronomy with particle physics. Born in 1944, he studied at KU Leuven, Belgium, where he completed his masters degree and PhD. Then, while working at CERN, Geneva, in early 1970s, he was invited to the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he has been since. But IceCube was never a one-man project It is the work of an international collaboration of hundreds of scientists and engineers. Starlight can be caught with a mirror. Neutrinos take patience. IceCube received its first major expansion only this year, and physicists are already proposing a successor eight times its size. Somewhere out there, another neutrino is on its way. Thanks to Halzen and his team, the ice is ready. The writer, visiting professor, IISER Mohali, was an astrophysicist at the Raman Research Institute, Bengaluru

articleTitle: Digger: Tom Cruise and Hollywood are done saving the world; time to embrace the end
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tom Cruise in Digger
description: Digger could be seen as the age-old story where a wealthy industrialist has destroyed the world but unlike those stories which often ended with someone saving the day, there are no heroes anymore.
body_raw: Tom Cruise has been single-handedly saving the world for decades, and now, with Digger, he has single-handedly destroyed everything. Of course, this is not Tom Cruise the person or the actor, but the characters he has played that have dominated Hollywood, and by extension, the rest of the world. Digger can easily be labelled as Toms best performance, but it also makes you wonder how the American soft power that Tom peddled for decades is now a thing of the past and they seem to have accept the fact in the film. Tom Cruises Digger is a cartoonish, but equally conniving villain Alejandro Inarritus Digger has Cruise playing Curtis, an actor whose daughter is the center of his life. And in the play within the film, he is playing Digger, the oil magnate who one might imagine runs the Illuminati and controls everything that goes on in the world from his garish mansion. Presidents of major countries are at his beck and call as Digger makes decisions that destroy the world, without any supervision whatsoever. Such characters have traditionally been cartoonish villains in films, and here too, Cruise plays Digger like a caricature. He knows how to gaslight the audience into feeling that they are equally responsible for the climate crisis that was triggered by him. He puts on an exaggerated performance just so he can trap them in a web of self-reflection and get away with his crimes, one more time. Digger is the obvious villain of the story here for he brought the entire world to a halt. But the film goes a step further when it introduces Jesse Plemons Kenny, who is a wolf in sheeps clothing. Kenny reveals he is Diggers nephew in the third act and this is when we also find out that the play is based on a real-life chapter from recent history where millions of people lost their lives and livelihoods, all because of Digger and the many governments who chose to look away while he was running the show. Kenny, like his uncle, gives an impassioned speech where he paints Digger as the biggest villain there ever was, and claims that he is producing this hyper-realistic play so the people can process their grief, with a dash of laughter. Just like Digger made the people self-reflect, Kenny does too, and thats where he, like his uncle, wins again. Kenny is fooling the world, just like Digger It is only at the end of the film that we actually see the reality of how the climate apocalypse triggered by Digger has changed the reality of the world. The cities are literally falling apart as people walk around the ruins of a civilisation wearing giant masks that cover their faces, for all the necessities of life have ceased to exist. And Kenny, the nephew of the disgraced oil tycoon, residing in his ivory tower, is using his immense wealth to put on expensive plays. Kenny thinks of himself as a supporter of the arts in a world where human life cant survive anymore he has fooled the people into believing that he is the good guy, the man who hates Digger just as much as anyone. Of course, Kenny is self-aware and knows that he cant be seen singing praises of his uncle anymore, even though he was the guy who set him up for life rather, set the family up for generations. So he does the next best thing turn into a hypocrite and dictate how the public must feel. Putting up plays is not his sole job duh, as he also runs some secret Mossad-like organisation where he can trace any individual in any part of the world but Curtis, who is playing Digger, cant see through the farce of this man because, just like the rest of us, he too is busy putting food on the table and worrying about his familys survival. Kenny, meanwhile, is gathering more wealth through the many businesses he continues to run as the world slowly comes to an end. Industrialists have been running the world ever since the Rothschilds formalised banking systems. Digger, surely, does not tell us anything new in that department, but it surely does tell us that we, the masses, are too gullible for our own good. What else could explain our fascination with the uber-wealthy people who have the resources to actually help millions around the world, but choose not to? And no, this isnt about them doing charity work to keep their conscience clean, but about taking steps to stop harming the world. ALSO READ Is Chris Hansen a hero or villain? Primetime explores his god complex to get to the answer Digger could be seen as the age-old story where a wealthy industrialist has destroyed the world but unlike those stories which often ended with someone saving the day, there are no heroes anymore. The Tom Cruise-like saviour who could have ended the tyranny of someone like Digger no longer exists, because the situation is so far in the dumps that the Kennys of the world are now pretending to be our new saviours.

articleTitle: Thai woman accuses Kanpur ‘husband’ of Rs 60 lakh fraud, hiding another marriage
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kanpur
description: The businessman was arrested after the woman alleged he assaulted and pressured her to convert; police invoke anti-conversion law
body_raw: Travelling 3,000 km from Thailand to Kanpur, a 35-year-old woman went looking for the man she said she married - and the Rs 60 lakh she had lent him. The man, a tannery businessman named Mohammad Irfan, had stopped answering her calls and cut off contact. When she went to his Kanpur home, she allegedly discovered that he was already married and had children. The woman approached Kanpur Police on Tuesday, alleging that Irfan and his family members assaulted and threatened her when she confronted him and pressured her to convert to Islam. Based on her complaint, Kanpur Police arrested Irfan and registered an FIR against him at Anwarganj police station under charges including assault. Police also invoked provisions of the anti-conversion law against him. We have arrested Irfan in connection with the case. The womans allegations are being examined, and necessary verification is being carried out, said Assistant Commissioner of Police, Kanpur, Manjay Singh. He added that Irfan has admitted to marrying the woman and is being produced before the court. The woman has been sent for medical examination and the report is awaited. We got married two years ago According to police, the woman, who runs a restaurant and a canteen in Thailand, met Irfan through social media around four years ago. She told police he introduced himself as a prominent Kanpur businessman involved in the tannery business who frequently travelled abroad for work. The woman said Irfan would stay at her house whenever he travelled to Thailand and that they subsequently entered into a relationship. Around two years ago, he proposed to her and the two later married in Thailand, she claimed. She said Irfan continued visiting her every two months. During this period, he allegedly took around Rs 60 lakh from her in several installments, saying he needed the money to expand his business. She told police that she arranged the money by borrowing from relatives and friends. When she later asked Irfan to return the money, he allegedly gave her different excuses. She also said she asked him to stay with her in Thailand, but he refused. She alleged that Irfan returned to India this year and stopped responding to her calls and messages. With her businesses in Thailand facing financial difficulties and her struggling to repay the loans she had taken to provide money to Irfan, she decided to travel to India to recover the money. She came to Kanpur with an acquaintance on a tourist visa on October 5 and visited Irfans house as she knew his address. It was there that she allegedly learned for the first time that he was already married and had children. She alleged that when she confronted Irfan, he and his family members abused and insulted her, and Irfan told her that she would first have to convert to Islam if she wanted to stay with him.

articleTitle: ‘Your money is Ata Pata Laapata’: Supreme Court to Rajpal Yadav in cheque bounce case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Rajpal Yadav
description: The Supreme Court directed actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore by October 13 in a long-running series of cheque bounce cases.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Wednesday took note of actor Rajpal Yadav arranging Rs 1.15 crore in a long-running cheque bounce case and told him to make some good movies to entertain people that will rebuild his image. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing the actors plea in connection with cheque bounce cases in which the Delhi High Court sentenced him to three months imprisonment. The court directed the actor to deposit Rs 2 crore by October 13. During the hearing, the actor produced demand drafts of Rs 1.15 crore, and the court was told that the remaining Rs 85 lakh would be paid by a prospective buyer of his property. The petitioner has finally brought demand drafts in the sum of Rs 1.15 crore, which is directed to be deposited with the Registry during the course of the day. As regards Rs 85 lakh, the petitioner claims that the prospective buyer of his property is present in Court. Mr Anant Prakash Yadav is present in Court and he is willing to pay a sum of Rs 85 lakh. He is willing to deposit the sum of Rs 85 lakh by way of demand draft with the registry on October 13, the CJI said while dictating the order. The CJI also made a light-hearted remark, Your money is Ata Pata Laapata, gayab. During the hearing, actor Yadav, who personally appeared before the court, said that he had suffered losses of around Rs 250 crore over the past 13 years, including Rs 17 crore in the dispute arising from his film Ata Pata Laapata. He said that although the total amount involved was around Rs 22 crore, the dispute over a cheque of about Rs 5 crore had resulted in his losing Rs 17 crore and had also caused substantial damage to his branding and career. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant struck a lighter note and advised Yadav to rebuild his image by making a good film and entertaining audiences again. Koi achi si movie banake logo ko dobara entertain karo. Aapki image dobara ban jaegi. Humare yahan kuch advocate bhi ache actor hain, unko bhi role de dijye, the CJI said. Make a good movie and entertain people again. Your image will be rebuilt. We also have some lawyers here who are good actors give them roles as well What happened in the previous hearings? The Supreme Court had earlier allowed Yadavs request for a last opportunity to deposit Rs 2 crore with its registry as part payment toward clearing dues owed to a production house. A three-judge bench, presided over by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, had also extended Yadavs interim protection from surrendering until October 5 in connection with cheque bounce cases in which the Delhi High Court sentenced him to three months imprisonment. Before that the Supreme Court had granted Yadav exemption from surrendering on the condition that he deposit Rs 5 crore with its registry. The senior counsel had stated that Yadav plans to dispose of some immovable properties belonging to his mother to raise the money. He promised the actor would deposit at least Rs 2 crore of the outstanding dues in court by then and present a concrete proposal to settle the remaining amount. Cheque-bounce case against Rajpal Yadav Recalling what led to the ongoing dispute, the complainant alleged that in 2013, Yadav tendered seven cheques of Rs 1.05 crore each to settle financial assistance of Rs 5 crore for a film in 2010. The cheques were, however, dishonoured. Subsequently, an agreement was reached between the parties in 2012, stating that the actor, his wife, and their company would repay around Rs 11 crore, including interest. However, that repayment has also yet to occur.

articleTitle: ‘I won’t stop’: In PM’s Viksit Bharat pledge, a message for Opposition
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narendra Modi
description: The Prime Minister has often spoken about his vision for India becoming a developed country by 2047, when it celebrates 100 years of Independence. But these remarks are significant against the backdrop of political developments
body_raw: Contrasting the gloom and immense challenges under the UPA era with the energy, enthusiasm, self-confidence of India in the current global order, Prime Minister Narendra Modi Wednesday coined the mantra of we will do it, saying the country will not stop, nor tire, nor waver on the road to a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Speaking at the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha-Seva Jyoti Yatra, organised at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi to mark 25 years of his continuous leadership as head of government, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and then as Prime Minister, Modi said, Even today, I consider myself a student. I try to learn something new each day. That is why today, I prayed. that my power to learn does not wane. The more I learn, the more my capacity to do something for the nation will increase. I am beholden to every person and every incident which taught me something or the other. What brought me victory taught me to be humble, and what made me stumble made me learn how to stand up. Well-wishers encouraged me and critics taught me to look within. Those who supported me showed me the strength of belief. Whoever opposed me taught me the power of democracy. Every crisis was a test of my patience, every success expanded my sense of responsibility. Everything I accomplished gave me the strength, the drive to move towards larger goals, he said. Stating that he began his day with a visit to the Shri Vinayak temple where he prayed for the nation and its 140 crore citizens, he said, I express my gratitude to all of you and to all my fellow countrymen. When I took the oath as Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, I never imagined that this milestone would also come. Today, I have completed 25 years of continuously serving as head of government. This is the result of the continuous blessings of the janata janardan. I express my gratitude to all political colleagues of the BJP, NDA and all those who hold immense reverence for democracy. I bow my head at the feet of the people of the nation, he said. He said the Morbi floods inculcated in him a spirit of service and showed him the path to round-the-clock relief and service work, the Bhuj earthquake taught him to remain steadfast on reconstruction, and the Chandrayaan taught him to rise after failure. Similarly, the Covid pandemic, he said, underlined the importance of the nations collective consciousness, and the media gave him the inspiration to move forward through both bitter and sweet experiences. Praising the RSS swayamsevaks, whom he called the guardians of the countrys cultural soul, he said he never felt alone on his journey of selfless service. Modi said the occasion was not one of merely recalling memories but also of adding new energy to predetermined goals and commitment. Hum kar ke rahenge we will do it. Viskit Bharat by 2047, we will do it. Top three economies, we will do it. Aatmanirbhar Bharat, we will do it. Global manufacturing hub, we will do it. Organising the Olympics, we will do it. Steps in outer space, we will do it. This energy, this enthusiasm, this self-confidence is incredible, he said. That we have been born in this timeless land of Bharat is amrit itself, he said, saying while high office can be obtained anywhere, there is no sacred land such as Bharat. Taking a swipe at the UPA years, he said, In 2014, the nation expanded my responsibility as Pradhan Sevak. The nation was confronting immense challenges, only problems were visible. Each citizen was seeking a new path. Regarding Bharats economy, the world had begun saying its a gone case, growth was nowhere to be seen. Adding that a nation facing such severe disappointment needed a new confidence, he said he responded by doing the only thing he knows I urged the janshakti, repeated to them we will do it. And today, 12 years later, the picture has changed entirely. Earlier, when a crisis used to emerge, Indias economy jolted. When a crisis comes now, Bharats perseverance is discussed. Its resilience is discussed, he said. Back then, policy paralysis used to be discussed. Now the Reform Express is discussed. Back then, new avenues of imports used to be discussed. Today, records of exports are established. Back then, we used to import mobile phones even for our own use. Now, there is a jalwa of Made-in-India mobile phones, he said. Referring to flydubais Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, hailed as a hero for averting a catastrophe despite being attacked and wounded in the cockpit, he said, There will come a time when Made-in-India planes will be discussed. There are problems in our country, but we also have 140 crore solutions. This time is not to rest, but to move forward with enthusiasm. Today, the youth of Bharat have a huge opportunity. I want to tell the youth Your children will not go through the trials that your grandparents and parents were put through. That is what I am working for, he said. Asking the gathering to take a pledge, Modi said, Nation First will be my commitment. Serving the nation will be my goal. And the mantra of nagrik devo bhava will be my mantra, karma will be dharma, delivering on my responsibilities will be my commitment. Until Bharat become viksit, I will not stop, nor tire, nor waver.

articleTitle: Punjab Kings teammate decodes change in Iyer’s hitting technique: ‘When Shreyas came at the start…’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Iyer
description: Recalling his own bowling experience against Iyer, the bowler said: "When I bowled to him in the nets, I had to bowl wider, or else he used to easily hit me over cover for a six
body_raw: One standout aspect of Shreyas Iyers century on Tuesday was his ability to accelerate after reaching his half-century, which he reached in 26 deliveries, and scoring the next 50 runs in just 16 deliveries. His power-hitting and technique seemed quite flawless against the spinners. His Punjab Kings teammate, Yuzvendra Chahal, decoded what has changed in Iyers approach to his innings. Definitely, attacking the mind. When Shreyas came at the start, he used to go back and play the cut. Now he comes across, and if the midwicket fielder is up, he has that option as well. If you bowl outside the off-stump, his reach is so good that he plays over cover and mid-off. So, the bowler gets slightly stuck there as to what he should do when he is not getting any help from the wicket, the Punjab Kings PBKS bowler said on Star Sports. Recalling his own bowling experience against Iyer, Chahal said When I bowled to him in the nets, I had to bowl wider, or else he used to easily hit me over cover for a six. One or one-and-a-half years ago, he used to hit hard, but nowadays he times the ball, and thats the specialty because of which his batting has improved so much, he added. Batters go back and across toward the off-stump, but he was going outside the off-stump because he knew Shepherd would try to bowl only outside the off-stump. Thats why he played the lofted extra cover drive and lofted off-drive. He read the bowlers mind, and thats why he was able to get into those positions. Brilliant batting, sensational batting, former batting legend Sunil Gavaskar elaborated on the same show. Iyers century helped India beat West Indies by eight wickets, chasing a target of 172 runs in 14.4 overs. If its your day, make sure that you win the match for the team. And today it was me. Previous couple of games, it was the batsmen who finished off the game. So yeah, overall I feel it was a comprehensive performance, and I think if we continue with the same mindset, we will be one of the destructive teams in T20s, Iyer said.

articleTitle: Is Trump’s ‘forever war’ a liability in the US midterm elections?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: us midterm elections
description: Contrary to Trump’s expectations, the prolonged war in Iran has gradually crept into domestic prices
body_raw: President Donald Trump seems anxious about the upcoming US midterm elections-voting is on November 3. So much so that he confused Brazil with India in a recent social media post when comparing the vote-counting process, an issue that has seen intense debate in the current American political zeitgeist. Since Trumps loss to Joe Biden in the 2020 election, which the former has called rigged, he has repeated the claim more than 100 times publicly and has taken the fight to the US Supreme Court. At the heart of the issue is the vote-by-mail provision that Trump has railed against. At least four developments have riled up Trump Early and mail voting are already underway in more than 40 states almost one-third of American voters vote by mail Trump is reeling under one of the lowest approval ratings on the back of rising energy prices and a new forever war in Iran there is a sense that the Democrats may just edge out the Republicans in both the House and the Senate, and finally, the Supreme Court has just begun a new term with the anticipation that it may take up new cases on election issues like gun control, immigration and religious issues. In March 2026, Trump issued an Executive Order that sought to limit how Americans could vote, particularly through mail, and vowed to do away with voting machines. Consequently, the Supreme Court struck down Trumps attempts to restrict mail ballots. More than 23 states came together to appeal against Trumps Executive Order, which now remains blocked by a nationwide injunction and will almost certainly not apply this November. Then, there is the question of nationwide popularity. Trumps average approval rating fell to 38 per cent in late September, the lowest in his second term. A little over 35 per cent of Americans believe the country is headed in the right direction. On the generic congressional ballot, Democrats average 52 per cent against 43 per cent for Republicans, the widest margin since Trump returned to office. If the numbers and the sentiment do translate into votes, Democrats may likely win. To Trumps advantage, however, the actual voting may vary state-wise, altering some of these expectations. For the Democrats, the historical record may be more favourable. Since the 1950s, the presidents party has lost an average of more than 25 House seats in midterm elections, with losses plummeting further when the presidential approval rating is below 50 per cent. In his first term, Trump himself lost 40 House seats in 2018 Barack Obama lost 63 in 2010 and Bill Clinton 54 in 1994. Perhaps the exceptions are 1998 and 2002, which are attributed to the popularity of a president or an era-defining post-911 rallying of sentiments. Trump, on the contrary, has been sucked into a war abroad and is struggling to keep price rises at home under control. The economy, along with the cost of living, lies at the heart of the political contestations. Contrary to Trumps expectations, the prolonged war in Iran has gradually crept into domestic prices. While rising petrol prices gas and electricity bills are affecting households, a spike in diesel prices is impacting the truckers supply chain and farming, adding pressure on Republicans. Republicans hold a narrow House majority, and Democrats need a net gain of only three seats to win it-making the House win a stronger possibility than the Senate. What has complicated the picture is a gerrymandering war between the two parties. The process, which can happen once every decade, could give the Republicans an edge with new maps in Texas, Florida, Ohio, North Carolina, Missouri, among others, which could yield Republicans around 16 seats on paper, against roughly six for Democrats, mostly from California. What may prove decisive in the end is how many Republican-held seats turn Democrat, if any. In the Senate, the current Republican lead may prove to be a steeper climb for the Democrats. Republicans hold 53 seats, so Democrats need a net gain of four for an outright majority, along with the two independents who caucus with the latter. Although international issues tend to weigh less in midterms, given the prolonged nature and continued US commitments to the Middle East, this November could be different. On October 1, Trump ordered a third carrier strike group, led by the USS Theodore Roosevelt, and another 10,000 troops to the region. The carrier is not expected to arrive until late November, after the polls have closed, but the political signalling has been dire. The deployment follows the virtual collapse of efforts to secure a workable ceasefire or any modus vivendi with Tehran. The war has also spread beyond Iran with the Houthis renewing missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, drawing Riyadhs ongoing response. China adds a layer of contradiction in US politics. As Trump has sought constructive strategic stability with China, extending their trade truce to January 2027, many see the stability as structurally incongruent. For the soyabean farm-state Republicans in Iowa and Nebraska, the truce with China is a lifeline, but for China hawks, it looks like accommodation. For Americas partners, including India, the more consequential question is not who wins in November but what follows. The writer is Deputy Director of the Strategic Studies Programme at ORF
