articleTitle: Barefoot in a blue saree, a widow ran for a job, and the stadium roared
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jharkhand widow
description: Kavita Kumari, whose video has gone viral, says she knew she had done well once people started cheering her on
body_raw: Everyone in the stadium started clapping and hooting as soon as a woman in a blue saree, tucked at the waist, removed her slippers and ran barefoot to finish a 1,600-metre run. Someone watching the trial run amid the Home Guard recruitment shot a video, focusing on the woman as she passed other candidates one by one. It went viral on social media. The woman is Kavita Kumari, a widow from Jharkhand for whom a Home Guard job could spell a change in fortunes. Kumari starts her day with an early-morning practice run on uneven ground near her village, Soso, in Ramgarh district. On October 4, she travelled to Sidhu Kanhu Stadium for a free trial conducted by an academy run by athletes, where candidates could get a sense of the ground and assess their fitness in conditions closer to those they would face in the recruitment test. The same stadium is scheduled to host the physical test for the Home Guard recruitment from October 24 to November 5. Barefoot, in a saree, Jharkhand widow runs 1,600m in 8 minutes. The finish line A Home Guard job - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 7, 2026 Kumari, clad in a saree and chappals, was among those who showed up. I was very nervous as soon as I reached the stadium. People were looking at me in a saree, and I was looking at them in tracksuits with bags, bottles and shoes on their feet. This just made me uncomfortable, but I took part in the run, she said. To pass the running test in the female category, a candidate has to run 1,600 metres in 10 minutes. Kumari said she completed it within eight minutes, earning an Excellent grade with full marks. Till people applauded me, I had no idea about what I had done. I just removed my chappal and started running barefoot. While I was running, I had no thoughts other than the Home Guard job. Someone took my video and posted it on social media. I hope I will run with the same energy and confidence on the physical exam day, she said. Ankit Singh 25, who runs Ankit Runner Academy in Ramgarh and organised the October 4 trial, said the purpose was not merely to conduct a practice run but to familiarise candidates with the stadium. The ground, he said, has a slope on one side, with portions that are sandy, gravelly and uneven. Candidates need to know how the ground behaves before the actual physical test. That is why many of them come from 15 to 20 kilometres away to practise here. That day, around 1,900 candidates took part, including nearly 1,100 women. Many of the women came from rural areas, and some wore sarees. There were around 50 to 60 women in sarees that day, he said. He said that for women from rural areas, wearing a tracksuit and running shoes and going out to practise is not always easy. The idea was to give candidates an experience of the actual ground so that they would know what to expect on the recruitment day, he said. The notification for Jharkhand Home Guard recruitment was issued in April this year, with 284 vacancies in Ramgarh district against more than 16,000 applications. The first phase of the recruitment includes a physical test comprising a 1,600-metre run, long jump, high jump and shot put, following which the written examination will be conducted. The recruitment also reserves 50 per cent of the overall posts for women, with 5 per cent reserved for widows. A long list of misfortunes Kumari said she got married in 2009 while she was a minor. Now around 30, she lost her husband, Deepak Kumar Mahato, three years ago. Deepak was a migrant worker in Gujarat after working in Mumbai, she said. During Covid, he was unwell, and he returned home. He continuously fell sick and died in 2023. I had to look after my in-laws, maintain the home and children and run the home financially, she said. Six months after Deepaks death, the family also lost his younger brother. My sister-in-law left home after her husbands death, she said. Kumari told The Indian Express that the family has a debt of around Rs 6 lakh after spending a substantial amount on treatment. She said she worked as a security guard at private offices in Ramgarh town but left the job as her shifts ended late and she could not find transport back to her village. Now she works as a labourer, mostly at a brick kiln, to repay the debt and support her two children, who study at a private school in Ramgarh. While preparing for the physical test, Kumari said she relied on YouTube to learn and practise. I ask my children to open YouTube and play the videos for me, as I hardly know how to use it. I watch the videos and prepare for the exam. I do not have a single penny to spend on dresses, shoes or tuition fees, so I have to prepare on my own, she said. After the video reached a wider audience, several people and politicians reached out to support her. Dumri MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato spoke to Kumari over the phone and sent her a tracksuit and running shoes. Ajay Karmali 38, a Home Guard posted in Ramgarh, is Kumaris coach and runs the HMT Physical Academy in Dulmi, about 5 km from her village. He started the academy around four or five months ago, offering free physical training to villagers. Kumari found him through his social media posts and called him to ask if she could join. Karmali said he encouraged her to run at the stadium before the recruitment test so that she could become familiar with the ground and gain confidence. Though she did not have a running uniform, she hopes that she will soon get the Home Guard uniform, he said.

articleTitle: Two days to election: Can Maharashtra opposition alliance stop infighting?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A meeting of Maha Vikas Aghadi at Tilak Bhavan, to discuss the Legislative Council elections and other important issue, in the presence of Congress State President Harshvardhan Sapkal, NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule, NCP (SP) State president Shashikant Shinde, Shivsena (UBT) leader Anil Parab, Shivsena (UBT) leader Ambadas Danve, and Shivsena (UBT) leader Milind Narvekar, in Mumbai on Wednesday
description: With the October 9 deadline for withdrawals approaching in the Legislative Council elections, allies have little time to avert “friendly fights”
body_raw: Opposition parties may be trying to remain on the same page nationally when it comes to taking on the BJP, but a recurring problem has been resolving their differences at the regional level. In Maharashtra, the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadis MVA plan to contest the October 23 Legislative Council elections together is under strain, with the Congress and the Shiv Sena UBT set to face each other in Amravati Teachers constituency, while the Sena UBT and the NCP SP are pitted against each other in the Marathwada Graduates constituency. The other seats where elections are being held are Pune Graduates, Nagpur Graduates, and Pune Teachers. The differences have cropped up within days of the three parties deciding to contest the five Council seats together. With Tuesday the last day to file nominations - candidates have till October 9 to withdraw their nominations - the parties have failed to reach an agreement in these two constituencies. In Amravati Teachers constituency, the Congress has fielded Aditi Pohare, while the Sena UBT has put up Dattatray Lahane. Lahane filed his nomination on October 6 in the presence of Sena leaders. The Congress had announced Pohare along with sitting MLCs Abhijit Wanjari from Nagpur Graduates and Jayant Asgaonkar from Pune Teachers on October 3. Pohare joined the Congress days before her candidature was announced. She is the daughter of Harshvardhan Deshmukh who heads the Shri Shivaji Education Society in Amravati. The society has a large number of teachers among its staff, giving Pohare a local base in a constituency where the candidates are elected by registered teachers. The Sena UBT, however, says it was Lahane for the Amravati seat. After announcing his candidature, Sena UBT MP Sanjay Raut made it clear that the party would not give up the seat simply to avoid a contest with the Congress. We are contesting two seats, Amravati and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Marathwada. You call it a friendly fight or whatever you want. We are contesting them, he said. Raut argues that the Sena UBT was not seeking all the seats the Congress was claiming. He said his party was willing to leave the Nagpur Graduates and Pune Teachers seats to the Congress and was even prepared to give up Pune Graduates to the NCP SP, despite the work done by its leaders to register voters there. All three parties have worked separately to build their voter base in the Graduates and Teachers constituencies and each has its own claim to some of the seats, Raut has said. Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar said voter registration was an important factor in these elections. These elections are not based on ordinary voting. The side that registers more membersvoters has greater weight, he said. He said the Congress had not claimed Pune Graduates when the Sena UBT had a sitting member there, while the Sena UBT had not claimed Pune Teachers as the Congress had a sitting member there. When there is a sitting member, it is not right for another party to demand that seat, he said. The position of the NCP SP in Amravati remains less clear. On Monday, one of its district presidents attended Lahanes nomination programme, while another local leader said the senior leadership had not taken a final decision. The contrasting positions suggested that the party was not comfortable with the situation. A direct contest The second dispute has become more direct. The Sena UBT has fielded Dilip Ghuge from the Marathwada Graduates constituency. Ghuge filed his nomination on October 5. The following day, Dr Pratapsinh Patil of the NCP SP announced that he was filing his nomination as the authorised candidate of the Sharad Pawar-led party and the MVA. Patils campaign also shows how the contest could play out. In a social media post on Tuesday, he said his candidature was not merely about filing a nomination but about starting a new fight for graduates, students, unemployed youth, and ordinary people in Marathwada. Taking aim at Satish Chavan, who has represented the seat since 2008 and is contesting this time as the candidate of the NCP and ruling Mahayuti alliance, Patil asked what had changed for graduates in the past 18 years, raising issues such as employment, education, examination paper leaks, and students future. However, the Sena UBTs decision to contest the seat has complicated the equations and upset the NCP SP, which has traditionally regarded Marathwada Graduates as an NCP seat. NCP SP leaders in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar have argued that the party won the constituency for three consecutive terms and should therefore continue to contest it. NCP SP MP Supriya Sule sought to play down the differences. Asked about the disagreement over the Council seats, she said there was no dissatisfaction within the MVA and that the issue will become clear after further discussions. Raut has rejected the argument that the NCP SP somehow has an automatic claim over the seat. He has pointed out that before joining the NCP following the split in the party, Chavan was a Congress member and the political situation has changed since then. Understanding fails to hold Earlier this month, the MVA decided to contest the five seats going to polls on October 23 together. The Opposition alliances strategy was discussed at a meeting attended by Congress leaders Naseem Khan and Harshwardhan Sapkal, NCP SP leaders Shashikant Shinde and Harshwardhan Patil, and Raut. The Congress at the time said the parties were looking at the constituencies held by the NCP, the NCP SP, and an Independent, and would take a call on the candidates after determining their chances of winning. That understanding now appears to have failed in two constituencies. In both cases, the parties have moved ahead with nominations rather than waiting for a final decision at the alliance level. However, the Opposition alliance still has time till October 9 to avoid friendly fights and give itself the best possible chance to defeat the Mahayuti. Otherwise, the folly of friendly fights might become apparent when the votes are counted on October 27.

articleTitle: Barapullah Phase III traffic mess: Delhi plans U-turn, road widening, Google Maps fix
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Barapullah Phase 3 traffic jam, Barapullah Phase 3 congestion, Barapullah flyover traffic,
description: The corridor opened last week but has already seen long traffic snarls, prompting the Delhi government to look at short-term measures.
body_raw: With congestion building up soon after Barapullah Phase III opened last week, the Delhi government is now relying on a series of quick measures-deployment of traffic police at merging points, a new U-turn, redesigning the point where traffic merges, widening the road and removing a footpath, while also working with Google Maps to ensure real-time route information is provided to the commuters. Citing an engineering flaw in the construction, which had not taken into account the traffic situation expected after 10 years, PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh said on Wednesday, The government is currently working on immediate traffic-management measures, while discussions on a longer-term solution continue. see box Singh blamed the previous AAP-led Delhi government for the flaw in the construction. The Barapullah Phase III flyover project began in 2015. That means its design had already been approved in 2014-2015, when the AAP government had come to power in Delhi. The entire design was approved during their tenure. How many lanes the flyover would have, all of this was decided by them, he said. Asked whether there was any warning sign that such a situation could arise, Singh said, We had no such study. We had no estimate. The new corridor connects Mayur Vihar with Sarai Kale Khan and links to the existing Barapullah network, creating a continuous stretch of around 10 km towards the AIIMS roundabout. However, the promise of a 15-minute, signal-free ride has run into a bottleneck at Sarai Kale Khan, where vehicles arriving from Mayur Vihar, those joining from the Sundial loop, and traffic approaching from the DND side converge before entering the older and narrower Barapullah flyover. The project was originally scheduled for completion in 2017 but opened only in 2026 after construction delays. Over these nine years, while vehicle numbers rose significantly, East Delhi and the wider NCR also grew, changing vehicular movement between East Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, and South Delhi. Singh also said that the issue was not limited to the road itself. The interaction of Barapulla with DND Flyway, NH 24, Ring Road, RRTS connectivity, Sarai Kale Khan and the surrounding railway and Metro network has created a much larger integrated traffic movement. Traffic Police had earlier flagged another problem Google Maps was showing the new corridor as relatively clear, directing motorists towards a stretch that was already congested. This was adding to the load as some vehicles that could otherwise use DND or NH 24 were being routed towards Barapullah. Singh said the PWD was in touch with Google Maps and that its algorithm could take about 15 days to reflect the changed traffic situation. He also raised questions over the financial and contractual decisions taken during the previous AAP government. An additional payment of around Rs 640 crore was made to the contractor through arbitration. The projects prolonged delay, cost escalation, and arbitration-related payments need to be examined together, Singh said. The AAP called for a CBI investigation. The BJP government itself admits that Barapulla Phase nIII has serious issues of planning, design and traffic integration. It must answer why it sanctioned Rs. 1,635 crore without a proper technical assessment. The CBI must investigate the matter, an AAP spokesperson said. Instead of blaming the previous government, the BJP should explain the technical assessment and the basis on which Rs. 1,635 crore of public money was sanctioned, the spokesperson added. The quick fixes Traffic police deployment Personnel to be deployed at peak hours to regulate the three merging traffic streams. Sundial merge Traffic Police has suggested redesigning the merger point to improve vehicle flow. New U-turn A dedicated U-turn near Gurdwara Bala Sahib for Siddharth Extension residents, reducing dependence on the ramp to the old Barapullah. Footpath removal A footpath between Sarai Kale Khan and ITO is being removed to improve traffic movement. Road widening The government is working on widening the affected stretch to accommodate the increased flow. Google Maps changes PWD is coordinating with Google Maps to ensure routing reflects the current congestion and traffic patterns.

articleTitle: As reservoirs shrink, this Maharashtra district moves to guard remaining water
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Beed reservoir levels water crisis
description: Officials from the revenue department, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, and the police will check water theft from reservoir backwaters in Beed three times a day.
body_raw: As water levels in reservoirs in Maharashtras Beed have sunk to 16.38 per cent and groundwater levels are falling sharply, the district administration has ordered inspections of waterbodies and stepped up action to protect drinking water sources. Speaking to The Indian Express, District Collector Vivek Johnson said dedicated teams comprising officials from the revenue department, Maharashtra State Electricity Board MSEB, and the police have been formed to check water theft from reservoir backwaters and monitor the situation. The inspections will be conducted three times a day. There are 164 reservoirs across the district, including small, medium, and large projects. We have been facing water theft from certain locations in the backwaters of reservoirs. To check these thefts, we have ordered joint inspections, Johnson said. According to Johnson, the officials have been checking illegal water theft for the last three months. However, it was found that some farmers were reconnecting pump connections even after action was taken against them. As part of the intensified action, the administration has started dismantling electricity distribution points at select locations from where water is being stolen. These transformers are being removed and stored in the MSEB godown, while transformers supplying power to regular connections will remain operational, the collector said. Johnson also directed talathis and gram sevaks to maintain a strict vigil over water theft from small and medium water supply projects. At larger reservoirs, including Majalgaon and Manjara, dedicated teams have been deployed to monitor illegal water lifting, he said. 37 rainfall deficit in Beed The intensified monitoring comes at a time when Beed is facing a significant rain shortfall and declining water availability. Data from the district information office shows that against the expected average rainfall of 566.1 mm till September 30, the district received only 356.6 mm, or about 63 per cent. The rainfall deficit has also translated into a sharp decline in groundwater levels. The average water level recorded in observation wells has fallen to 7.36 metres, which is 4.55 metres deeper than the average level recorded in September over the past five years. A decline in groundwater levels was recorded in all 126 wells surveyed, with Georai tehsil recording the steepest fall of 6.64 metres. Reservoir storage also remains low. Of the 164 projects in the district, usable water storage is at 16.38 per cent. The Majalgaon project has 28.53 per cent storage, while medium projects have 12.49 per cent and minor projects only 5.49 per cent. As many as 32 projects have completely dried up. Currently, the average capacity of all 164 large, medium, and small reservoirs is roughly 16 per cent. Apart from these, there are several minor sources such as open wells, borewells, jackwells and small lakes. Their water availability in the coming months depends on the groundwater table, Johnson said. The administration is therefore already relying on tankers to meet drinking water requirements. As many as 150 tankers are currently supplying water twice a day across the district, Johnson said. 40of water sources acquired As of September 29, wells or borewells had been requisitioned in 28 villages and at 32 other locations. We have acquired 40 per cent of water sources, he said. The pressure on drinking water supplies is particularly evident in Parli Vaijnath, where the municipal council has begun planning for the coming months. We have a population of roughly 1.2 lakh. Considering the current reservoir capacity and evaporation rate, we have planned to supply water once every eight to 10 days to ensure water availability till June 2027. The implementation will start on October 8, Trimbak Kamble, Chief Officer of the Parli Vaijnath Municipal Council, told The Indian Express. Livestock and fodder stock also affected The water shortage is also affecting livestock. Available fodder stocks are expected to last for an average of only 37 days. The situation is particularly critical in Patoda, where stocks are estimated to last 21 days, and Ashti, where they are expected to last 27 days. Parli has the highest availability, with fodder stocks estimated to last around 70 days. The impact of the rainfall deficit has also been felt during the Kharif season. Sowing was completed on 7,87,218 hectares, or 97.31 per cent of the expected 8,08,946 hectares. Soybean sowing exceeded the target at 137.90 per cent, while cotton sowing stood at 78.36 per cent. Preliminary assessments have indicated crop damage of more than 75 per cent across all 11 talukas, with the affected area estimated at around 5.14 lakh hectares. Amid the water and agricultural stress, the district has also received funds for irrigation-related works. A total of Rs 2,341.33 lakh has been sanctioned for three projects in Ashti, Beed, and Georai under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 2.0. The projects are expected to cover 10,642 hectares. For the administration, however, the immediate challenge remains protecting the limited water available in reservoirs and groundwater sources. We are now making a drought management plan for all villages in the district and mapping their primary and secondary water sources. Around 40 sources are currently being regularly monitored, Johnson said.

articleTitle: ‘6-7 police stations called me’: Mumbai, Nagpur CJP members allege pressure
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Protesters stage a protest under the leadership of CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke, seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll deletions at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park, Dadar, in Mumbai on Friday. (ANI Photo)
description: Plainclothes police noted names at a Mumbai meet and visited homes in Nagpur, members allege, ahead of the Jantar Mantar protest seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Police say they are "doing our job".
body_raw: Even as Cockroach Janta Party CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday accused the Chandrapur police of serving notices on party workers to keep them away from the partys Delhi protest, members in Mumbai and Nagpur alleged similar pressure. In Mumbai, members said plainclothes police noted names at a party meeting and warned of FIRs. The partys city coordinator said six or seven police stations had called him. In Nagpur, a coordinator said police came to his home. The CJP has called the protest at Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 10 to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Dipke announced it after a rally at Mumbais Shivaji Park on October 2. On September 23, The Indian Express had published an investigation on the rupture within the Election Commission, with two Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu flagging 14 objections in 10 months on issues that strike right at the heart of the electoral process. At a press conference in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Dipke had alleged that the Chandrapur notices asked workers not to join the protest, and that police questioned them on how they would pay for the trip. He called this dictatorship and asked how police could already say, as the notices did, that the agitation would turn violent. In Mumbai, CJP member Mayur Sharma said police in plain clothes came to the partys meeting at Sana Banquet Hall in Dongri on Wednesday. We had a meeting at the Banquet hall, and the police had arrived in plain clothes and noted the names of the people present in the meeting. They showed us Dipkes post in which he had posted the notice. 7-8 police officers in plain clothes threatened us with an FIR if we attend the protest, which is scheduled to be on October 10 at Jantar Mantar, he told this newspaper. Pranay Ahire, the CJPs Mumbai coordinator, told The Indian Express I have received a call from 6-7 police stations asking what my plans for the 10th of October are. I have not revealed my plan for that day. This is very sad that they are tracking our movements. Another member, Azzaruddin, said he was told a notice would be served on him. Many comrades have received calls or threats that notice will be served if we are planning to attend the protest. I received an ultimatum too, he said. In Nagpur, CJP west zone coordinator Durgesh Kuhike told The Indian Express that police visited his home and asked how many people from the city were likely to travel to Jantar Mantar. CJP volunteers alleged that officials also indirectly sought the numbers and identities of those planning to join. Samya Korde, a Bombay High Court advocate and member of the Shetkari Kamgar Paksh, said police may have identified protesters from records of protests in July. Many of us had attended protests in July. Some of us might have been detained, some of us came under surveillance and FIRs were registered in July. Based on that they might have tracked down protesters. Calling regular citizens is completely unconstitutional. If they are doing that it should be stopped, Korde said. Asked about the allegations, a police official said, We are doing our job.

articleTitle: ‘Sympathy can’t be misapplied’: Gauhati High Court rejects woman’s citizenship plea
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gauhati High Court Foreigners’ Tribunal woman citizenship
description: The Foreigners’ Tribunal considered the electoral rolls and other documents but found that Bhanu had failed to establish her link with the persons she claimed were her father and grandfather.
body_raw: The Gauhati High Court has said that sympathy cannot be misapplied when courts and tribunals deal with the issue of illegal migrants and foreigners, and the interest of the country should be of paramount consideration. The observation came as it dismissed a womans challenge to a Foreigners Tribunal order declaring her a foreigner of the post-March 25, 1971 stream. The court said she failed to establish her family link through sufficient documentary evidence and declined to interfere with the tribunals decision. Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund were hearing a petition filed by one Mustt Hasena Bhanu against the May 19, 2017 verdict of opinion of the Foreigners Tribunal. When the Courts and Tribunals are dealing with the issue of illegal migrants and foreigners, sympathy cannot be misapplied. The interest of the Country should be of paramount consideration, the court said on October 5. The observation came after the court examined the evidence produced by Bhanu and the legal burden on a person whose citizenship is questioned. The case arose from proceedings before the tribunal. Bhanu maintained that she was an Indian by birth and relied on electoral rolls of 1966 and 1970 in which the name of the person she claimed was her father appeared. She also produced later electoral rolls carrying her own name, a link certificate issued by a village panchayat secretary and a PAN card application. Tribunal found family link unproved The tribunal considered the electoral rolls and other documents but found that Bhanu had failed to establish her link with the persons she claimed were her father and grandfather. It also discarded the panchayat certificate because its issuing authority had not been examined. It then declared her a foreigner of the post-March 25, 1971 stream, recording a finding that she had entered India illegally from Bangladesh after that date. Bhanu argued that her evidence had not been effectively challenged because neither she nor her witness had been cross-examined. Her counsel also argued that the tribunal had accepted material showing her relationship with her claimed father. She examined herself as a witness and produced Md Imam Hussain, whom she described as her uncle. Hussain supported her claim that she was the daughter of Hasen Ali, whose name appeared in the older electoral records. The authorities opposed the petition, arguing that the burden was on Bhanu to establish that she was not a foreigner and that she had failed to provide sufficient family details and documentary evidence to prove the claimed lineage. Citizenship claim must be proved The high court held that a person appearing before a tribunal cannot avoid making a complete disclosure simply because the proceedings are described as a representation rather than a written statement. The bench said a person claiming Indian citizenship must plead the foundational facts supporting the claim and prove them through cogent, reliable and admissible evidence. The court referred to the burden under the Foreigners Act, under which the person asserting that they are not a foreigner has to establish that position. The court said the relevant disclosure would include facts such as when and where the person was born, who their parents were, where the parents were born and other family details necessary to establish the claimed lineage. It said that her written statement did not disclose the names of her grandparents, parents, her fathers siblings, her own siblings or her children. It also did not state where and when her parents were born or when and where she herself was born and brought up. The court then examined the electoral rolls relied upon by Bhanu. Although the 1966 and 1970 rolls contained the name of the person she claimed was her father, the bench found that those documents did not establish that she was his daughter. The bench noted that she was not shown as a voter along with her parents in those records. It further found that the family of the claimed grandparents and parents could not be established from the electoral rolls. The court, therefore, held that Bhanus statement that she was Hasen Alis daughter, along with the village panchayat link certificate, was insufficient to establish the relationship through cogent and admissible evidence. The bench also rejected the argument that the absence of cross-examination meant Bhanus evidence had to be accepted as truthful. The court said a disputed fact does not become proved merely because the opposing side did not cross-examine a witness. It also reiterated that oral testimony alone cannot constitute proof of citizenship in proceedings before a Foreigners Tribunal and that relevant facts must be established through documentary evidence. The bench further held that simply mentioning a persons name as the father of a suspect in a summons does not establish parentage. Such a reference cannot be treated as an admission of the relationship. The high court ultimately held that the tribunals opinion did not warrant interference and dismissed Bhanus writ petition. It also revoked the interim bail granted to her on August 25, 2017 and directed that the consequences of the tribunals May 19, 2017 opinion declaring her a foreigner of the post-March 25, 1971 stream would follow.

articleTitle: Cramped spaces, deposit disputes: Delhi students tell cops what’s wrong with their PGs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police interact with students at a PG in Delhi. (Express Photo)
description: Students in Delhi’s major PG hubs raised concerns during a police outreach drive after the Satya Niketan hostel collapse.
body_raw: Tushar wants to leave his paying guest accommodation in East Delhis Laxmi Nagar after seven months of living there and move in with a friend. But the second-year Delhi University student is worried he will have to forgo the Rs 20,000 security deposit he paid when he moved in. His rent agreement has an 11-month lock-in clause. My warden says that if I leave the PG before the lapse of 11 months, my Rs 20,000 security deposit will not be returned. Im not sure how to deal with this, said Tushar, a B.Com student from Uttar Pradesh. His concern was among several issues raised during a Delhi Police drive to meet students living in PGs and rented accommodation in the Capitals major student hubs - Mukherjee Nagar in North Delhi, Laxmi Nagar in East Delhi, Rajinder Nagar, Karol Bagh and Patel Nagar in Central Delhi. The drive, undertaken by police teams from every police station, followed the September 6 collapse of a building housing a private hostel in Satya Niketan, which claimed seven lives, including those of five students. Waterlogging, wires and poor maintenance Thousands of students who flock to Delhi to study in colleges and coaching institutes live in PGs because of the acute shortage of on-campus accommodation. Kuldeep, who studies at a coaching institute in Karol Bagh and stays in a nearby PG, said, For most students, security deposit is the most common problem because people sometimes have to leave or change their PGs, he said. Cramped spaces in many private hostels have also been worrying, Kuldeep said. But the Satya Niketan incident has made students more worried about safety and accountability. Its cramped inside the PGs. But what is bothering us most after this incident is the question of who is accountable to us, he said. Muskan, who has been living at a PG in Old Rajinder Nagar for over a year, said her concerns revolved around basic standards of living poor hygiene, inadequate water supply and electricity maintenance, sagging electrical wires and waterlogging her PG. After meeting students at PGs, reading rooms and libraries in these student hubs, police compiled the issues raised by students and prepared an Action Taken Report ATR, which was submitted to the Delhi Police Headquarters, according to the officials sources. Officers said the most frequent grievance aired by students in these interactions was over security deposits. Apart from these, students also flagged waterlogging, seepage, cleanliness in kitchens, maintenance of the buildings, and dark or poorly lit stretches around PGs. Rohit Rajbir Singh, DCP Central, said police were briefing PG owners and property dealers about the issue of security deposits, which he said was a major concern for students who spend considerable amounts on accommodation. Letters were sent to civic agencies seeking structural audits of properties for the safety and security of students. The Delhi Fire Services was approached for fire-safety surveys. Libraries were directed to follow safety norms, obtain fire no-objection certificates and install CCTV cameras, Singh added. Police also began regular engagement with Residents Welfare Associations to improve CCTV coverage and ensure that PGs and rented accommodation followed safety guidelines, he said. Steve, a B.Com student living in Mukherjee Nagar, said that police had also shared contact numbers with them during their interaction at his PG. The police officers had come to my PG a few days ago and told us about precautionary measures in case an emergency situation arises. They also gave us the contact number of the station house officer, he said. The officer also told us to take precautions to prevent incidents of mobile phone snatching. He also told us to not befriend strangers, Rudra said.

articleTitle: Anushka Sharma, parents buy Rs 25.8 cr flats in same building; own Rs 44.1 cr property in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anshima, Ajay Kumar Sharma and Anushka Sharma
description: Anushka Sharma and her parents, Ashima and Ajay Kumar Sharma, have bought two adjoining apartments in Mumbai’s Versova for a combined Rs 25.80 crore.
body_raw: Anushka Sharma and her parents, Ashima and Ajay Kumar Sharma, have purchased two adjoining apartments in Mumbais Versova for a combined Rs 25.80 crore. According to registered agreements for sale accessed by real estate data analytics firm CRE Matrix, both transactions were registered on July 8, 2026.The apartments are part of Godrej Skyshore, a luxury residential project by Godrej Properties. Since the project is still under construction, possession of both apartments is expected on or before June 30, 2031. The payment schedule is linked to the progress of construction. Anushka Sharma, family now own 3 flats on same floor Anushka Sharma has purchased a 2,153 sq ft apartment in the project for Rs 14.89 crore. She paid a stamp duty of Rs 74.47 lakh for the transaction. The apartment comes with three covered basement parking spaces. On the same day, Anushkas parents purchased the adjoining apartment on the same floor. Their 1,577 sq ft apartment cost Rs 10.91 crore. They paid Rs 65.44 lakh as stamp duty and the apartment comes with two covered basement parking spaces. With these two purchases, Anushka and her family now own three apartments on the same floor at Godrej Skyshore. The combined value of the three properties is close to Rs 44 crore. Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma also own an apartment in the project Earlier in July, Anushka and her husband, Indian cricketer Virat Kohli, purchased a 2,644 sq ft apartment in the same project for Rs 18.29 crore. According to property registration documents accessed by Zapkey, the transaction was registered on July 21, 2026. The apartment comes with 316 sq ft of exclusive area and three car parking spaces. The couple paid Rs 1.09 crore as stamp duty and Rs 30,000 as registration fees. Based on the transaction value and carpet area, the deal works out to around Rs 69,159 per sq ft. Also Read Virat Kohli refutes claim he visited Premanand Ji Maharaj for Rs 5 cr Out of deep faith Tabu also bought a flat in Godrej Skyshore Anushka and Virat are not the only Bollywood celebrities to have invested in Godrej Skyshore. Actor Tabu, whose full name is Tabassum Fatima Hashmi, also purchased a 2,153 sq ft apartment in the same building in April 2026. Tabu reportedly bought the apartment for Rs 10 crore from Godrej Properties, according to property registration documents accessed by Liases Foras. The purchase came to light months before Anushka and Virats transaction in the same project. On the professional front, Tabus latest release is Drishyam The Conclusion whereas Anushka Sharmas last big screen appearance was Zero 2018 with Shah Rukh Khan and Katrina Kaif. Anushka has shifted base to London with her husband, Virat and two children, Vamika 5 and Akaay 2.

articleTitle: As PM Modi completes 25 years in office, key takeaways from his speech
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narendra Modi 25 years, PM Modi speech, Modi 25 years in public life,
description: PM says he continues to be a learner and exhorts people to achieve the country’s dream of “Vikst Bharat” by 2047.
body_raw: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday completed 25 years in public life, having served as Gujarat Chief Minister from 2001 to 2014 and as Prime Minister since then. On the occasion, Modi asserted that the country had grown from strength to strength and exhorted people to ensure that the nation achieved its dream of becoming Viksit Bharat by 2047. Here are the key takeaways from the PMs speech. Here to stay Modi said he would not stop, get tired, or get diverted from his path until India became a developed country. We will do it, he repeatedly said in his speech, asserting that India would become a developed nation by 2047. 25 years of serving the people. I bow to 140 crore Indians for their trust and look forward to serving the nation with greater commitment in the times to come. - Narendra Modi narendramodi October 7, 2026 The assertion that he was willing to continue came amid speculation over the past year about whether the Prime Minister, who turned 76 on September 17, would gradually bow out of active politics. His remarks suggest he is looking to remain at the helm for a long time and that the job of building his political legacy is far from over. Peoples blessings at the core At a time when his government has been facing protests from Gen Z, Modi said the blessings of the people had been at the core of his political journey. When I became CM of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, I had not thought that this moment would come. Today, I have been consistently serving as head of the government for 25 years. This is a result of the blessings of the people, Modi said. I thank the BJP, NDA. and bow my head before the people of the country. So many elections happened in between, and the people always chose me to serve them. I bow before Indian democracy and the Constitution., he said. Today, I have prayed for 140 crore Indians and myself too. I prayed that God would give me the strength to serve my countrymen day and night. The biggest contribution to what I am today is that of the people of the country. They have been my biggest strength. The nation has given me everything, and so the biggest responsibility for the nation and its citizens is mine, the PM said. He said his accumulated political capital of 25 years belonged to the nation. Still learning Recalling that he was the first student to reach class in school in Vadnagar, Modi said, The hunger to learn became part of my life, and I still consider myself a student. Today, I prayed to God that my ability to learn should never diminish. He said, When I look back, I only feel gratitude. I feel gratitude to every person and event that taught me anything. Those who made me win made me humble. Those who made me fall taught me to stand up. Those who supported me showed me the power of faith, and those who opposed me taught me the strength of democracy, the PM said. He underlined, Today I can say that no event in my life was useless each taught me something. Modi mentioned the Bhuj earthquake, the Covid-19 pandemic and the medias portrayal of him as experiences he continued to remember. Acknowledging RSS Modi acknowledged the contribution of swayamsevaks, describing them as people who had served the country selflessly. I have got the support of countless Swayamsevaks in this journey, and I bow before them, he said. He added that the day was not only one to cherish memories, but also to say, We will do it. He reiterated Viksit Bharat by 2047. We will do it. None can stop a nation that brims with such self-confidence, Modi added. For me, 25 years is not about individual achievement. I spent my life in jungles and in mountains. I spent my life working for the organisation. Had I wanted to shine in electoral politics, I would have taken the plunge long ago. But my education taught me to live not for ambition but for the nation, Modi said. Karma is my Dharma. Karma is my worship for the country, Modi said, adding, In Gujarat, my mantra was Indias development through Gujarats development. But I had little experience all I had was faith in the people - something that became my strength. We did it in Gujarat the world is watching it. Post-2014 years The PM said that after 2014 his responsibilities grew and he faced multiple challenges. The economy was being described as a gone case, the PM said. A desperate country wanted new confidence, he said, adding that he told the country, We will do it. He said the picture had changed again and that Indias resilience, rather than policy paralysis, was now discussed when the country faced problems. Modi asserted that agricultural growth had broken all records over the past decade. He said people from all communities faced common difficulties and that the solutions should also be for all. All labharthis beneficiaries should benefit from saturation, he said. Revive Indias glory We have to revive Indias ancient glory, Modi said, adding that there was a time when India was synonymous with development. India showed the world the direction, but invaders burnt its universities and libraries, the PM said, adding that the countrys courage never collapsed even then. Swami Vivekananda had said that a great Bharat would rise one day, the PM said. He said Sri Aurobindo had also said that the sun of Indias destiny would rise one day and light the world. The PM said there should be a resolve to make India the greatest nation in the world. He said the whole world was discussing Indias pilot today, and that a day would come when the world would discuss a Made in India plane. We have problems but 140 crore solutions, he said, adding that this was a time to move forward with hard work. He recalled how India had thrown off the British yoke, adding that he was confident that India would become a developed nation by 2047. The PM also recalled how Article 370 was abrogated and how Naxalism and terrorism had been countered. Humne ghar mein ghus kar maara hai We have hit them in their homes, he said. Modi said it was important to decide today what had to be done to build a developed India by 2047, adding that India was moving in that direction. He said it was necessary to live and die for the country to become Viksit Bharat.

articleTitle: Today News Headlines for School Assembly, October 8, 2026: Henri Kagan, Kenso Soai win Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Today News Headlines for School Assembly, October 8, 2026
description: Today News Headlines for School Assembly, October 8, 2026: Know important National, International, Sports, Business, and GK current affairs updates especially curated for students, teachers, and morning assemblies.
body_raw: SchoolAssembly News Headlines for Today, October 8, 2026 Here are the top school assembly news headlines. Todays highlights include Andhra Pradesh declaring a drought in 21 of its 26 districts following a major rainfall deficit, while the Reserve Bank of India RBI has raised the repo rate to 5.50 in its first hike since February 2023. On the international stage, Kenya has reported its first Ebola death, Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, and more. National News The Andhra Pradesh government has declared drought in 21 of the states 26 districts, with 388 of 688 mandals classified as drought-affected. Of these, 283 have been categorised as severely affected and 105 as moderately affected after the state recorded a 53.4 per cent rainfall deficit between June and August. Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders headed to Jantar Mantar for a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Around 300 opposition MPs were expected to join the protest, with the leaders demanding Kumars resignation. The Press Council of India is operating with only half of its sanctioned members, and currently has no working journalist or newspaper editor among its members. The Information and Broadcasting Ministry is yet to formally notify 13 of the 28 members nominated by the Council. An Amritsar District Consumer Commission has directed payment of Rs 1.06 lakh to a passenger after a flight to Frankfurt was cancelled during the Covid-19 pandemic and a dispute arose over the ticket refund. World News The Nobel Prize in Chemistry for 2026 has been awarded to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. Flydubai has sought permission to resume flights to Tel Aviv after an incident involving Indian pilot Smit Machchhar. Israel has so far refused the request, following the reported midair attack on the Indian captain during a flight that was later diverted to Saudi Arabia. The move is expected to increase borrowing costs and could lead to higher EMIs, while the RBI also raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1 per cent. Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs 10,000 crore fund to provide equity support to small and medium enterprises. The fund will focus largely on small and medium manufacturing enterprises, including those operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Education News The National Medical Commission has clarified that medical graduates from Georgia must hold a licence to practise medicine there to be eligible for the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination in India. Merely working as a supervised junior doctor in Georgia will not meet the requirement. The University of Colorado Denver is set to establish a degree-granting campus in Hyderabad, with its first student intake expected in August 2027.
