articleTitle: Forced bigamy, Gujarat woman’s bold escape, and a chilling ‘purification’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ASP Bihani and her team had rescued the battered woman who had undergone a brutal, humiliating, public ordeal the previous day
description: Woman, lover forced to perform sexual acts in public, filmed while doing so; man claiming to be her husband among 9 arrested by Surendranagar Police
body_raw: When the police team entered the house in Surendranagar in Gujarats Saurashtra region, they saw a woman cooking at the stove. She seemed to be just another rural housewife, making lunch. But the officers knew she was not any woman-she was a woman whom they had seen in a horrific video that had been circulating in the area. As the woman turned toward them, the officers saw that the right side of her face and her right hand were swollen, and her eye was bruised. As soon as she saw us, she broke down in tears, and started to plead with us to take her away from there, Additional Superintendent of Police ASP Vedika Bihani told The Indian Express on Wednesday October 7. On Tuesday, ASP Bihani and her team had rescued the battered woman who had undergone a brutal, humiliating, public ordeal the previous day at the hands of a man who claimed to be her husband, and members of the mans extended family. Bihani and her team from the jurisdictional police station had managed to locate the woman less than an hour after Surendranagar Superintendent of Police SP Premsukh Delu received a call on October 6 morning from a community leader who told him about a certain video circulating on social media. The purported video, shot in a semi-rural locality of Surendranagar, showed an alleged purification ritual, in which a woman and her alleged lover were subjected to abject humiliation in public, SP Delu was told. The video had allegedly been shot around 9 am on October 5. Police said it showed nine persons, including two women, forcing the victimised woman and her alleged lover to engage in sexual acts while being tied with rope. The acts in the purported video included making the man lick the womans private parts, followed by making the woman urinate in a vessel and the man being forced to drink the urine, police said. All nine accused, including the man claiming to be the womans husband, have since been rounded up. Police officers said they had been booked under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 BNS relating to gangrape, voluntarily causing hurt, and wrongful confinement, as well as sections of the Information Technology Act, 2000 IT Act. All the accused are members of the extended family of the man who has been claiming to be the husband of the woman, police said. Notably, police said that the prime accused in the case cannot be legally considered to be the husband of the victim, considering that he already had a wife and children in his home in Vapi city of Valsad when he married the victim. The complainant woman was married in a traditional manner to the main accused in this case, and had gone to live with him in Vapi. But she ran away from there, and came back to live with her lover, ASP Bihani told The Indian Express. However, Bihani said, the woman was sent back to Vapi, where she would be put in chains inside the house. Somehow, the woman managed to get her hands on the key and free herself. She returned to Surendranagar a second time just a week ago, the officer said. She started to live in the community with her lover and his extended family. But the accused persons found her again and informed the main accused in Vapi. They then took her to the place where the incident took place, and filmed her punishment as well, ASP Bihani said. Asked about the use of the section relating to gangrape, the officer said, Forcing someone to commit oral sex is considered rape in law. And since nine people were involved here, we have booked them for gangrape. Following the rescue of the woman from the house, the police also managed to locate the male victim her alleged lover in the video who had managed to escape from the locality. He remains under medical treatment, while the woman is currently in the protection of the state. Surendranagar Police have found the first wife of the main accused and their children living in Vapi. That is why we have not called the main accused the husband of the complainant woman, ASP Bihani said.

articleTitle: WHO issues first ever guidelines on child & teen obesity: No weight loss drugs for under-10 kids
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WHO obesity guidelines for children
description: The development comes following the increasing cases of Type 2 diabetes and related complications in the younger age group.
body_raw: For the first time, the World Health Organisation WHO on Wednesday released guidelines on management of obesity in children and adolescents, strongly recommending against use of any weight loss drugs or surgery in children below the age of nine and only in very select cases in adolescents between the ages of 10 and 19. The guidelines allow the use of drugs and surgery for adolescents who are morbidly obese with lifestyle conditions such as type-2 diabetes, insulin resistance, or uncontrolled hypertension, and for those among whom lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise have failed to achieve any results after six months. Children and adolescents living with obesity are likely to develop lifestyle diseases much earlier in life and have to live longer with complications arising from them. We now know that losing weight can help prolong their lives. This is the reason we need to intervene aggressively in the early years, says Dr Jothydev Kesavadev, chairperson, Jothydevs Diabetes and Research Centre. What do the guidelines recommend? What are they against? The guidelines have looked at existing evidence on diet, exercise, use of digital technologies, drugs, surgeries, as well as the use of a combined behaviour change programme for effective obesity management in children and made the following recommendations. Based on evidence, the guidelines have strongly recommended the use of structured diets, physical activity and behaviour change, or all of these together for managing obesity in both children and adolescents. They recommend against the use of surgeries such as gastric bypass and drugs such as GLP-1 in children up to the age of nine years. While the guideline on the use of drugs is not specifically meant for GLP-1 alone - with these drugs being an area of interest when it comes to obesity - Dr Luz Maria De Regil, Director of the Department of Nutrition and Food Safety at WHO, said that there was no long-term data on the efficacy and effects of these drugs in children yet. She said that while the research was ongoing, WHO will continue to monitor the emerging evidence and change the guidelines in the future if necessary. The guidelines conditionally recommend the use of surgeries and drugs in adolescents between the ages of 10 and 19 years. These interventions, as mentioned above, are recommended only in those with severe obesity, living with conditions linked to obesity, or in whom other interventions have failed after six months. Dr Luz says that there is a lack of consensus because of a lot of pending questions on how long the medicines should be taken, when they should be stopped and when the maintenance dose should be reduced. The guidelines conditionally recommend the use of digital interventions such as active video games, exergames, exercise activity applications, pedometers or accelerometers among others that may increase physical activity and promote behavioural changes. While the evidence is not too strong, the guidelines say that such activities may be desirable while sedentary use of screens may be limited. Why are the guidelines necessary? Effective ways of addressing obesity in children and adolescents have become essential given the data. There were 170 million children and adolescents aged 519 years living with obesity in 2024, which include 70 million children aged 59 years and 100 million adolescents aged 1019 years, according to WHO. More so for countries such as India. Dr Luz says, While obesity is on the rise globally, the trends show that it is still growing at a rapid pace in low and middle income countries and arresting in high income countries. It has not started going down in any of the WHO regions. In India, there was a three percentage point increase in obesity in girls and 3.7 in boys over a three decade period up to 2022, according to a Lancet study. While 0.2 million boys and 0.2 million girls were obese in 1990, 7.3 million boys and 5.2 million girls were obese in 2022. By 2020, India is expected to be home to over 27 million children and adolescents between the ages of 5 and 19 years living with obesity, accounting for 11 of the global burden, according to the Comprehensive National Nutrition Survey CNNS 2016-18. What do Indian physicians say? Dr Anurag Bajpai, president of the Indian Society for Paediatric and Adolescent Endocrinology, says that he has seen a three-fold increase in the number of children coming to his clinic with obesity. Most of them come in with other co-morbidities such as fatty liver, prediabetes, and high cholesterol levels. So far, there were very limited treatment options but now the use of semaglutide has been approved in children over the age of 12 years by CDSCO Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation. This should not be used by everybody and limited to children living with morbid obesity and complications, he says. In fact, his society is currently in the process of drafting guidelines for the use of GLP-1 drugs in children and adolescents to ensure that it is not over-used and yet is offered to those who require it. Diet, exercise, and other lifestyle changes - even the most rigorous ones - can reduce only 3 to 5 of the body weight in children. This can be effective in those who are borderline but will not be sufficient in many of the patients that we see today - teenagers weighing 140 to 150 kg with other co-morbidities, he explains. According to Dr Bajpai, surgeries are generally not recommended in children and adolescents because they can result in improper nutrition and hamper their growth.

articleTitle: Darshan kicked Renukaswamy, paid Rs 30 lakh for false confessions: Approver
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Renukaswamy murder case actor Darshan
description: Pradosh Subba Rao, the accused-turned-approver in the Renukaswamy murder case, recounted in a Bengaluru court what he said he had witnessed.
body_raw: Kannada actor Darshan Thoogudeepa kicked Renukaswamy in the neck and burnt his chest with a cigarette, an accused-turned-approver said in a court statement recorded over five days in the murder case. Pradosh Subba Rao recounted what he said he had witnessed at a shed where Darshan and his co-accused allegedly assaulted Renukaswamy, who had allegedly sent lewd comments to the actors friend Pavithra Gowda on Instagram. Bengalurus 59th City Civil and Sessions Court recorded Pradoshs statement starting September 28. Pradosh, who worked as a finance manager at Oracle and was an acquaintance of Darshan for about 20 years, was the 14th accused in the case. He has now become a prosecution witness after turning approver. Besides Darshan and Pavithra, the others named in the chargesheet are Pawan K, 29 Raghavendra, 43 Nandish, 28 Jagadish, 36 Anukumar, 25 Ravi Shankar, 32 Dhanraj D, 27 Vinay V, 38 Nagaraju, 41 Laxman, 54 Deepak, 39 Pradhosh, 40 Karthik, 27 Keshavamurthy, 27 and Nikhil Nayak, 21. Lunch at a pub and a video call to Pavithra Gowda In a 128-page statement, Pradosh stated that on June 8, 2024, he visited Darshans home to join him for lunch at the Stony Brook pub, owned by Vinay. At the pub, Pawan showed Darshan some photographs on his phone and whispered something. He asked Pawan to video-call Pavithra and assured her that he would handle the matter, according to Pradoshs statement. Pradosh said he later drove Darshan, Pavithra, and Vinay in his Scorpio, with Vinay giving directions to a shed at Pattanagere in Bengaluru South. There, he said, Renukaswamy was sitting on the ground, bleeding from the head, surrounded by members of Darshans Chitradurga fan club, including Raghavendra. According to Pradosh, Pavithra told him the man had been sending her obscene messages. He told the court, Darshan abused, slapped and kicked Renukaswamy, made him apologise, and hit him with a nylon rope, while Pawan and Nandish beat him with a baton and a stick. He said he warned Nagaraj that matters could go out of hand. He later tried to pull Darshan away when the actor allegedly pressed the mans neck with his foot and burnt his chest with a cigarette. Darshan panicks and threatens to kill himself Pradosh said he left the shed and received a call later around 7 pm from Laxman saying that Renukaswamy was dead. When he told Darshan about the death, he testified, the actor panicked and threatened to kill himself. Darshan told him that Pawan had got Renukaswamy brought from Chitradurga on his instructions. While his associates tried to console Darshan, they came up with the plan that they would ask others to surrender before the police claiming they were the killers. Pradosh said that Rs 30 lakh would be needed to meet expenses related to lawyers, family, and jail. He said Darshan handed Rs 10 lakh to Vinay and arranged Rs 5 lakh for Raghavendra, and gave him a bag with 60 bundles of Rs 500 notes totalling Rs 30 lakh. The police recovered Rs 30 lakh from his Girinagar home on June 11, 2024. A cover story that didnt hold up Pradosh further said in his statement that he knew a sub-inspector named Vinay who worked at the Kamakshipalya police station. On the same day, Pradosh called Vinay, who was in Kerala with his family then, and made up a story about a money dispute among three people in which one was beaten to death. Aware that Sattva Apartment on Magadi Road would fall under the Kamakshipalya police limits, Pradosh said that he helped to dispose of the body near it. Pradosh stated that the accused removed number plates and a D-Boss sticker from a white Scorpio and used the vehicle to transport Renukaswamys body, which was then left by a service road near a drain. He said he threw Renukaswamys and Raghavendras phones into the drain and lied to the police officer about what had happened. On June 9, SI Vinay sent Pradosh CCTV footage of a white Scorpio going to and from the spot with its rear door open and three people walking. Pradosh told Vinay that those three seen in the video were his people but did not divulge any more information. Vinay told him to surrender at the earliest. Raghavendra, Karthik, Nikhil Nayak, and Keshavamurthy surrendered at the Kamakshipalya police station on June 10. But SI Vinay got to know the Scorpio was traced to the Pattanagere shed. He also learnt that the four men were telling a different story, involving Darshan, Pavithra and Pawan. Pradosh and Vinay later met near NICE Road, where he revealed the part about Darshan. But when he learnt about Pradoshs involvement, Vinay told him to never call him again. On June 10, 2024, Vinay called Pradosh to check where he and Pawan were. On learning that they were returning from Mysuru, the police intercepted them near the Bidadi toll. The next day, Assistant Commissioner of Police Chandan took Pradosh around 3 am to Mysuru looking for Darshan. Around 5.30 am, they reached the Radisson Blue hotel. They took Darshan into custody and returned to Bengaluru, the witness said in the court. On the same day, the police arrested Darshan, Gowda, and 15 others in connection with Renukaswamys murder.

articleTitle: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026: What this year’s winners have done, why it matters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026
description: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026: What are chiral molecules? Why does life choose one sort of molecules over the other? And how does all this relate to the Nobel winners’ work? We explain.
body_raw: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 has been awarded to Henri B Kagan and Kenso Soai for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. For those who found this line almost incomprehensible, the scientists work led to the creation of a way to produce more of one type of molecules and less of its mirror image in chemical reactions where the product was the same as the catalysis, the agent causing the reaction. A reaction of this sort had been one of Chemistrys most famous puzzles for years, and when Soai finally came up with the reaction, called Soais reaction, it was considered one of the most elegant chemical experiments ever. While Henri Kagan, 96, is Professor Emeritus at Universit Paris-Sud, France,Kenso Soai, 76, is Professor Emeritus at Tokyo University of Science, Japan. Why were scientists so concerned about mirror images of molecules? To answer an old and engrossing question why life overwhelmingly chooses one sort of molecule when its mirror image exists. Chiral molecules The Nobel Prizes official press release explains chiral molecules using the example of a lock and key. Imagine making a key for a lock, only to discover that your manufacturing process produces two keys that are mirror images of each other. They look almost identical, but only one fits the lock. The other may do nothing - or, in some cases, cause damage. This is roughly the problem chemists face with chiral molecules. Many molecules can exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, known as enantiomers. They have the same chemical composition, but their three-dimensional arrangements are different. The mystery of lifes one-handed chemistry The story goes back to Louis Pasteur of the rabies vaccine fame, who was studying tartaric acid, found in grapes and thus in wine, in the mid-19th century. Pasteur found that tartaric acid crystals existed in two forms that were mirror images of each other. But bacteria that fermented tartaric acid consumed only one of its enantiomers - the one found in grapes- and left its mirror image untouched. This pointed towards a much bigger mystery life itself appeared to be one-handed. When scientists later examined lifes building blocks, they found that naturally occurring amino acids bend polarised light to the left, while sugars found in DNA bend it to the right. In other words, life overwhelmingly uses one of two possible mirror-image forms. Why? When chemists tried making chiral molecules in the laboratory, they generally obtained an equal mixture of the two enantiomers. So what happened at the dawn of life that made biological chemistry choose one? Marckwald makes the first breakthrough The next important step came in the early 1900s, when German chemist Willy Marckwald carried out the first successful asymmetric reaction. An asymmetric reaction is simply one in which more of one enantiomer is produced than the other. In Marckwalds experiment, the difference was small, and did not explain how such an imbalance could become much larger. Charles Frank adds the theory In 1953, Charles Frank, a theoretical physicist at the University of Bristol, provided the next crucial link. Frank proposed a mathematical model for how homochirality could arise. His idea required three things. First, there had to be a chiral catalyst and an asymmetric reaction. Second, the formation of one mirror image had to be enhanced while the other was suppressed. Third, the reaction had to produce the catalyst itself. The third condition is called autocatalysis. Autocatalysis creates a kind of chemical snowball effect. Imagine that a reaction produces a tiny excess of one molecular form. If that form can then help make more of itself, the initial imbalance can grow rapidly. Franks model became a famous chemical puzzle could anyone actually create a reaction that fulfilled all three conditions? Henri Kagan finds the missing piece This is where Henri B. Kagan enters the story. In the 1980s, Kagan was working on asymmetric reactions, with the aim of producing enantiomers as purely as possible - something particularly important in pharmaceutical manufacturing. Chemists commonly used catalysts containing a metal atom and a chiral substance. They assumed that if the catalyst contained equal amounts of the two mirror-image forms, the resulting product would also contain equal amounts of its two enantiomers. Kagan questioned this assumption He realised that the metal atom might interact with at least two chiral molecules at the same time. If both forms were present, this could produce three kinds of catalyst one containing two molecules of one handedness, one containing two of the other, and a mixed form. The crucial discovery was that the mixed catalyst behaved differently. It drove the reaction much more slowly than the other two. This meant that the relationship between the handedness of the catalyst and that of the final product was not linear. In 1986, Kagan described three asymmetric reactions displaying these non-linear effects. He had supplied the second missing piece of Franks model a way to amplify an initial asymmetry. Kenso Soai makes the chemistry self-reinforcing The final step came from Kenso Soai at the Tokyo University of Science. Soai was studying an asymmetric reaction that showed a strong non-linear effect. He noticed similarities between the catalyst and the product and wondered whether he could design a reaction in which the catalyst actually produced itself. In the early 1990s, Soai experimented with many molecules before finding one that could do this 5-pyrimidyl alkanol. In a 1995 experiment, he began with just a 2 per cent excess of one enantiomer and ended with an 87 per cent excess. The reaction was self-reinforcing the slight initial advantage became a much larger one. But Soai continued searching for something even more striking. In 2003, he presented a reaction in which an excess of one enantiomer was formed and that enantiomer then helped produce copies of itself. This became known as the Soai reaction. Why does this matter? As the Nobel press release says, The non-linear effects that Kagan discovered have become an important tool for chemists when they design new reactions. The fact that a reaction is non-linear provides chemists with information about how it occurs. This information can be used to optimise the reaction, so they can obtain the purest possible enantiomers of the product. This is vital for every company that manufactures substances that are intended to interact with living beings, such as pharmaceuticals, flavours, scents and agricultural chemicals.

articleTitle: Doctor fined Rs 2 Lakh by Karnataka High Court for ‘luxurious litigation’ against wife
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court divorce doctor maintenance
description: The court warned the husband against suppressing income details and said that the family court needs to look into the statement of assets and liabilities of both the parties and take action.
body_raw: Criticising a husbands plea as luxurious litigation, the Karnataka High Court has dismissed a petition against an order directing him to pay Rs 1.10 lakh monthly interim maintenance to his estranged wife. The court also imposed a Rs 2 lakh penalty on the man for wasting judicial time. Pointing out that the petitioner has no patience to even look at the order, where the maintenance is only granted to the wife and not to the major son, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti said it is a fit case to impose costs for wasting judicial time. The judicial process is intended to resolve genuine legal grievances and not to provide a ground for settling the ego of the parties. Such use of judicial proceedings deserves to be deprecated, where the valuable time of the court is wasted. This is nothing but luxurious litigation, the September 22 order reads. The court also warned him against suppression of income details and said that the family court needs to look into the statement of assets and liabilities of both the parties and take appropriate action. Husband challenges maintenance award The doctor couple married under the Special Marriage Act and have a son. Following differences between them, they began living separately, and the husband filed a divorce petition before the family court. During the divorce proceedings, the wife sought interim maintenance of Rs 1.45 lakh per month for herself and her son, besides Rs 1 lakh towards litigation expenses, under the Special Marriage Act. She said she had resigned from her job as a prosthodontist because of health issues and the difficulty of travelling about 50 km daily, and was earning only around Rs 35,000 a month through professional consultations. Appearing for the wife, advocate Satyen Bajaj stated that the husband is a very famous doctor. He has two clinics in Bengaluru, one in Goa, one in the Maldives, and another in London. It was submitted that the petitioners father lives in an apartment worth Rs 4 crore and has several movable and immovable assets. The husband opposed the plea, arguing that the wife was a qualified postgraduate medical professional with around 15 years of experience and was capable of earning at least Rs 2 lakh per month. He also claimed that he was already providing financial support to her and their son. The family court nevertheless directed the husband to pay Rs 1.10 lakh per month as interim maintenance to the wife and Rs 50,000 as one-time litigation expenses. Aggrieved by this order, the husband approached the high court. Husband cant deny capacity to pay Order Noting that the husband has not revealed his actual income, but stated that after the deductions he was getting Rs 80,000, the court said that the party is supposed to first mention what his income is from different sources and what the expenditures are, but it appears that the husband had failed to disclose the complete particulars of his statement of assets and liabilities before the court. Pointing out the fact that the family court, in its order, clearly recorded that maintenance is given to the wife, the court asked why did the man then state that it had recorded the son as an adult but granted him maintenance, and questioned the courts alleged inability to understand his stance. Stressing that when the husband himself was contributing to the wife an amount of Rs 1.03 lakh before the family court order, the ruling said, It shows that she is not in a position to maintain herself and he has the capacity to pay the maintenance. Having paid the amount, now he cannot submit before this Court that she is capable of earning and he is not capable of paying. The high court accordingly dismissed the husbands petition, upholding the family courts direction to pay Rs 1.10 lakh a month in interim maintenance to his wife. It also imposed Rs 2 lakh in costs and cautioned the husband against withholding or suppressing material details about his income and assets.

articleTitle: Karan Johar says ‘no cricketers’ amid demand for Virat Kohli on Koffee With Karan Season 9
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Despite huge fan demand for Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma, Karan Johar has confirmed that no cricketers will appear in Koffee With Karan Season 9.
description: Despite huge fan demand for Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma, Karan Johar has confirmed that no cricketers will feature as guests in Koffee With Karan Season 9.
body_raw: Ever since director-producer Karan Johar announced that he is all set to return with his widely popular chat show, Koffee With Karan, for the ninth and last time, social media has been abuzz with speculation about who all will show up as guests. Meanwhile, one section of netizens has been strongly demanding that power couple Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma be brought on as guests in one of the episodes. Unpacking Koffee With Karan Season 9s latest teaser Now, the producers of the show have unveiled a new teaser, categorically denying the presence of any cricketers this time. The clip features Karan speaking on the phone with various unnamed people, hinting at his plans for Koffee With Karan Season 9. Reiterating that this will be the final time he hosts the chat show, the director insists, Im not acting, Im not pretending this will be my last. Must Read Lost Rs 250 cr in 13 years Rajpal Yadav to SC, hints at film on cheque-bounce cases Karan then slips into his signature wit with, What? What do you mean it should have ended 10 years ago? How rude In conversation with another person, he says, Thank you for asking, but I havent invited you for eight seasons. So, I dont plan to invite you for the ninth either. Sorry, are you crying? Karan Johar puts end to Virat Kohli rumours Indirectly refuting speculations about Virat Kohlis presence on the show, he notes, Cricketers are not invited. Theyre also not coming. Theyre actually refusing. As the conversation continues, someone on the other side of the phone asks the director for the couch cushions as a gift. He wonders, Isnt that creepy? He then quips to someone else, I wont be calling her at all. God knows what else will come alive if she comes. Next, he is shown speaking to his mother, who worries he is being sacked from Koffee With Karan. No, Mumma, theyre not cutting my money. Its my decision to end the show. I will buy you that diamond, I promise, he tells her. Teasing what to expect from the show this time, he assures someone, You can manifest a relationship. But no, it doesnt help with divorce. Although Karan maintains that this season will be controversy-free, he ends the promotional video with a wink, suggesting he will wrap up his beloved chat show with a bang. ICYMI Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity While Virat Kohli has never been on the show, Anushka Sharma has appeared three times. She made her Koffee With Karan debut in 2011 during Season 3, alongside her Band Baaja Baaraat 2010 and Ladies vs Ricky Bahl 2011 co-star Ranveer Singh. She made her comeback the very next season, sharing the floor with veteran director Anurag Kashyap. Anushka Sharmas last Koffee With Karan appearance was in December 2016, when she arrived on Season 5 of the show with her Jab Tak Hai Jaan 2012 co-star Katrina Kaif. Why Karan Johar avoids inviting cricketers now In a conversation with Sania Mirza on her podcast last year, Karan had admitted that hes never actually invited Virat to be on the show. I have never asked Virat. And now, I am not asking any cricketers after what happened with Hardik Pandya and KL Rahul. There are many who I just felt wouldnt come, so I never asked them in the first place, he said. Karan had previously hosted KL Rahul and Hardik Pandya on the show, and Pandyas comments during the episode recieved a lot of flak. Both players also faced a suspension by BCCI. Soon after, the episode was pulled down from the streaming platform.

articleTitle: Bihar court convicts police officer of contempt for flouting orders, fines him Re 1
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rohtas court ias ips training bihar sp police officer dig contempt case kidnapping
description: The court observed that the Superintendent of Police, Rohtas, had habitually, deliberately and intentionally failed to comply with court orders, despite being given repeated opportunities.
body_raw: A Bihar court has found a senior police official guilty of contempt for flouting its orders and slapped a symbolic Re 1 fine. The court also directed the Ministry of Personnel and Training to overhaul the training system for IAS and IPS officers in alignment with the democratic system. Additional Sessions Court Judge Anil Kumar had iniciated contempet proceeding against the then SP Rohtas, Raushan Kumar, on August 17, under the provision concerning wilful disobedience of court orders, after observing that the SP had failed to comply with its directions and had not responded to a show-cause notice. Criticising his conduct, the court directed the fines recovery from his salary and ordered that the conviction be entered in his service record. The opposite party has not only failed to comply with the court orders habitually, deliberately and intentionally but also tried to overawe and overpower the court by approaching several eminent persons. His antecedent conduct as well as conduct during trial, especially not appearing for his evidence, shows his haughty, arrogant and egoistic attitude and thereby deprives him of any sympathy of this court, the court observed while convicting the then Rohtas SP. Directing its office to send a copy to the Ministry of Personnel and Training to draw attention to the need to overhaul the training system for IAS and IPS officers so that it is aligned with the democratic system, the order said, This problem is not confined to Bihar only. In an execution matter, Namakkal Tamil Nadu D.M. was sent several orders, including show-cause notices, but he did not reply even once. Then, the petitioner was asked to withdraw it and approach the Madras High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India. He did the same. Unconditional apology of DM, Namakkal sent to this court. Drawing reference from various instances and pointing out serious flaws in the training of such IPS officers, Justice Anil Kumar said, Even this court has no good experience with IAS officers, especially district magistrates. In the Periyamal Case, the Supreme Court directed that execution cases must be disposed of within six months. Noting that even after the issuance of notices and disciplinary action recommendation against the then Rohtas SP, the court said, Till date, neither the DGP nor the chief secretary sent even a single chit of paper This shows the apathy, indifference and respect of the Bihar Administration for the District Court While initiating the contempt proceedings, the court remarked, As the court found the whole administration unresponsive, it was compelled to launch a proceeding for wilfully disobeying the court orders, lowering the dignity of the court and flouting the majesty of law. The court highlighted that, on the states request, four dates were given, i.e., on August 28, September 7, September 11, September 14, and September 22, but he did not appear to give his evidence. Rather, he used this time to pressurise the court to drop the proceedings by approaching an eminent person. A kidnapping case and order to SP The court made these observations while dealing with a case related to kidnapping. The Rohtas District Court had convicted the 10 persons, noting that even when the victim and his complainant son turned hostile. The court had subsequently directed the then Superintendent of Police, Rohtas, Raushan Kumar, to obtain the accused persons latest criminal antecedents, register an FIR and initiate action against the victim for alleged perjury. According to the court, the victim was allegedly kidnapped for a ransom of Rs 1.5 crore and had then turned hostile after allegedly receiving Rs 20 lakh. The court also directed an inquiry into the victim and his son after evidence suggested their involvement in illegal activities. During the trial of the Session Case, it has come on record that the victim was involved in the business of Ganja Cannabis and became rags to riches from that illegal business, it said. It added that just before the incident of kidnapping, his informant-son won one crore rupees in gambling before the Diwali Puja, which was cited as the immediate reason for his fathers kidnapping. Expressing displeasure, the court said that the then SP did not realise the urgency and submitted the report a month after the disposal of the case that, too, was merely a formality because his report was just copied from the case diary. No recent criminal antecedents were provided. The court later found that the SP had failed to comply with these directions and did not respond to a show-cause notice issued in July. It therefore initiated contempt proceedings, alleging wilful disobedience of court orders and conduct lowering the dignity of the court.

articleTitle: Indian-origin woman arrested in Canada after confrontation with pedestrian turns physical
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian origin woman arrested in Canada
description: In the video, the woman is seen getting out of the passenger side of the vehicle and confronting the pedestrian. She appears to tell him that recording her was illegal before reaching for his phone.
body_raw: An Indian-origin woman was arrested in Calgary, Canada, after a confrontation with a pedestrian, who filmed the act on his phone and later circulated it online. The incident reportedly started when the vehicle carrying the woman allegedly failed to give way to a pedestrian crossing the road. The man began filming the encounter on his phone, after which the situation appeared to escalate. In the video, the woman is seen getting out of the passenger side of the vehicle and confronting the pedestrian. She appears to tell him that recording her was illegal before reaching for his phone. Its not legal to make a video, she can be heard saying in the footage. The confrontation then turned physical, with the woman allegedly grabbing the mans backpack and dragging him across the pavement. The police arrived at the scene soon after and arrested her. In the video, the man at the receiving end of the assault claimed that the womans husband, who was behind the wheel, was driving without valid insurance. Authorities have not publicly provided further details about the viral video or the circumstances surrounding the arrest. Watch the video View this post on Instagram A post shared by BodyCamDDE bodycamdde The footage has since been viewed thousands of times on social media, prompting a debate over the confrontation and whether a person can legally record an incident taking place in a public space. Before you mess with people, make sure your papers are legit, one user commented. Why do they always think that theyre above the law? Probably because they usually get away with it, another wrote. You have no right to act superior in a country that isnt yours, a third user said, while another added, She forgot that shes not in India anymore. The Calgary incident comes weeks after another case involving an Indian-origin woman in Canada also drew attention online. Raj Tiwana was arrested following a confrontation with her tenant, who later posted a series of videos alleging that his landlady had repeatedly harassed him and interfered in his life. The dispute reportedly began after Tiwana objected to the tenant using a barbecue in the garden while a friend was visiting. She allegedly accused him of trying to burn down her property.

articleTitle: ‘Bankra Masjid land belongs to Centre’: Airport Authority of India to Calcutta High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bankra mosque
description: 136-year-old Bankra Masjid is located inside the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport compound in Kolkata.
body_raw: The Airport Authority of India AAI on Wednesday informed the Calcutta High Court that the land housing the 136-year-old Bankra Masjid inside the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport compound in Kolkata was officially acquired by the Central Government decades ago, leaving the mosque committee with no legal claim over the property. The submissions came during a hearing regarding a petition filed by the Bankra Masjid Committee seeking interim relief to allow devotees to offer prayers-particularly Friday prayers-at the shrine. Access and public entry to the mosque have been suspended since July following security issues flagged by the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security BCAS. AAI told the court that the Central Government had acquired the land for the extension of the runway and had paid compensation to the residents concerned. Senior Advocate S N Mukherjee, appearing for AAI, submitted, This land has been acquired long ago there is a notification dated Feb 7, 1961.One can practice their religion but cannot insist that they will do it in a particular place. They are not entitled to any relief, and they do not have any legal right. Where security is involved, there is no natural justice. They further submitted that in May a meeting was held with all stakeholders, including Bankra Masjid Committee, with a view to ensuring foolproof security of the airport. It was stated that there was hindrance to flight operations. Take-off and landing were being affected also, submitted Mukherjee. Additional Solicitor General Dheeraj Dwivedi, appearing for Central Industrial Security Force CISF, submitted, There was no law and order situation when it prayers were stopped. A confidential report by an international aviation authority was given in 2024. National security will always override public interest. Places of Worship Act will not come into play. Basically, the mosque is crossing the runway. As per the topography. This cant be allowed. On the city side, in Jessore, we provided them land, but they are not ready to move their mosque from the airport area. Additional Advocate General of West Bengal Billwadal Bhattacharya said the dispute involved neither conversion nor a heritage structure, but land acquired long ago and national security concerns. Bhattacharya also mentioned that if such security lapses continue, another 911 incident can happen and also referred to the recent Flydubai incident where Indian pilot Smit Machchar was attacked. However, the petitioners counsel submitted, There were no issues for 136 years. People only enter here in the morning after proper security checks. Worshippers were allowed access to Bankra mosque solely based on Aadhaar cards. According to sources, before the restriction, around 70 devotees were allowed to offer prayers at the mosque each day at different time slots after producing their Aadhaar cards before CISF personnel. The next date of hearing is on October 9.

articleTitle: Flydubai Omani co-pilot trained in UK, New Zealand, Australia: How Hamam al-Hammami slipped through aviation safety nets
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News
description: The Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, 29, is believed to have attended one of the UK’s biggest flight schools between 2018 and 2019.
body_raw: Flydubai flight FZ1073s Omani co-pilot, who allegedly stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar in a midair cockpit brawl last week in an apparent attempt to crash the Dubai-Tel Aviv plane, reportedly trained to become a professional pilot in Britain. The Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, 29, is believed to have attended one of the UKs biggest flight schools between 2018 and 2019, The Telegraph reported. The report added that Hammami received the training from England-based L3 Airline Academy, a pilot training firm that is a part of Acron Aviation. Acron Aviation declined to say whether Hammami had trained with the company, citing its policy of not publicly commenting on individual current or former students. The company said it would assist authorities with any investigation. Crash axe attack on Indian pilot The Omani co-pilot, who attacked Machchhar with a crash axe that is usually kept in the cockpit in case of emergencies, reportedly trained at one or more centres of L3 Airline Academy in England, which includes major training facilities in Southampton and Bournemouth, as well as a simulator centre near Gatwick. Israeli passenger Yaniv Hayoun, with blood stains on his shirt, who was aboard a Flydubai aircraft that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, is welcomed at the arrivals gate at Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv, Israel. AP Photo The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, which had been bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said, calling the incident a terrorist attack. Co-pilots New Zealand training stint The co-pilot was in New Zealand from November 2018 to May 2019 on a six-month student visa, according to New Zealand Police. Police said he was there to complete part of his flight training for a UK-based company that no longer operates in New Zealand. Australia links investigated The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team, comprising the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police and the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation ASIO, is investigating the mans links to Australia, the Australian Federal Police said. Melbourne University connection Reuters, citing sources, reported that the co-pilot had studied at RMIT University in Melbourne. RMIT separately confirmed that a former student alleged to be involved in the Flydubai incident had been enrolled at the university but did not complete an engineering qualification. The university did not identify the former student.

articleTitle: Why DMK is blowing hot and cold on Rahul Gandhi over protest against CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gyanesh Kumar resignation, rahul gandhi, priyanka gandhi vadra, gyanesh kumar, election commission of india, cec resignation protest, india bloc protest new delhi, voter list deletion row, parliament street protest, akashvani bhavan detention, vote chori allegations, india bloc, election commissioner dissent report, akashvani bhavan, election commission news
description: While DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai has sharpened his attacks on the LoP, senior leader TKS Elangovan has “defended” Gandhi’s right to protest.
body_raw: Months after the Congress walked into the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK camp to form the government in Tamil Nadu, the DMK is blowing hot and cold on Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi over his campaign against the Election Commission EC. While a section of the DMK has sharpened its attacks on Gandhi, a marked contrast that reflects the changed relationship between the two parties, another section has defended the LoPs right to protest. DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai on Wednesday cited a media report on the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls to question why Gandhi, who has forcefully raised allegations of electoral manipulation elsewhere, had not spoken similarly about Tamil Nadu. Daro Mat Dont be scared, Annadurai wrote, claiming that constituencies with large numbers of deletions disproportionately went to Vijays TVK. According to Annadurai, the TVK won 84 of the 135 constituencies where more than 20,000 voters were deleted and all 10 constituencies where deletions exceeded 80,000. He asked Gandhi whether he believed the SIR had affected Tamil Nadu and the DMK, and whether the EC had acted fairly. The figures and the claim about their electoral effect were cited by Annadurai from the media report-the inputs provided do not include an ECs response to them. Measured criticism Even as Annadurai attacked Gandhi, senior DMK leader TKS Elangovan defended the Congress leaders right to protest. It is the right of citizens to fight against the governments wrongdoings. That is what Rahul Gandhi did yesterday, Elangovan said on Wednesday. He also demanded Kumars removal and fresh elections in states where, he alleged, the electoral process had been compromised. The apparent contradiction is partly explained by the political rearrangement since Tamil Nadus April election. The DMK subsequently left the Congress-led INDIA bloc. The TVK now governs with support from Congress and other smaller parties. That has given the dispute over electoral rolls another layer. The DMK and Congress may still attack the same institution over the SIR, but they now approach Tamil Nadu from opposite sides of the political field. The DMK leaders reactions came as Gandhi and other Opposition leaders intensified their confrontation with the EC in New Delhi. On Tuesday, Gandhi was detained at Akashvani Bhavan after police stopped Opposition MPs from marching to the poll bodys office. He subsequently staged a nine-hour sit-in. The Opposition has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar following Express report last month that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally recorded objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions they said had been taken without their knowledge, including matters relating to the SIR. Afraid of Vijay Annadurai had been even more personal a day earlier. While Gandhi was staging his Delhi protest, the DMK spokesperson asked whether he was reluctant to raise Tamil Nadus deletions because he was afraid of Vijay. He also called Gandhi duplicitous and used the phrase Once a skunk, always a skunk. He further questioned why Gandhi had not endorsed what he described as Congress president Mallikarjun Kharges position that state governments elected after the SIR should be dissolved. For the DMK, the argument is therefore no longer simply whether electoral-roll revisions deserve scrutiny. It is why Gandhis campaign against the SIR, in the partys telling, appears to stop when it reaches a state governed by his new ally.

articleTitle: After Janhvi Kapoor’s deepfake controversy, Peddi producer says ‘youth is polluted’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor
description: Peddi producer has condemned the misuse of AI following the Chuttamalle deepfake targeting Janhvi Kapoor, saying the youth have become polluted.
body_raw: Days after deepfake content featuring actor Janhvi Kapoor was widely circulated on the internet, Mythri Movie Makers co-founder Y Ravi Shankar has spoken out against the growing misuse of artificial intelligence AI to generate deepfake content. Janhvi was last seen in Peddi, which was produced by the same production house. It has become really easy to sling mud at each other on social media. On top of that, they are now misusing AI, and no one knows whats real or fake, Ravi Shankar said. The youth have become polluted, be it online or otherwise. It is at a time like this that we need films with divine power that instil a fear of God. It is only beneficial to society. The deepfake that prompted his remarks was an AI-manipulated version of the Chuttamalle song from Jr NTRs Devara Part 1, in which Janhvi Kapoors likeness was digitally altered to create sexually explicit imagery. Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor both issued public statements against such videos. It is to be noted that his own film Peddi was also severely criticised for sexualising Janhvis character and normalising assault. Some of the scenes featuring her character were changed after viewers raised objection. Also Read Janhvi Kapoor calls her Chuttamalle AI video with NTR assault Reality of being a woman Talking about Hanuman Ansh, the Neem Karoli Baba biopic whose Telugu release was being announced at the same press event, he said, We are very happy that this film not only conveys a message and shows God and reality, but has also become a commercial superhit. Rs 400 crore for Rs 2 crore is a slap in the face Ravi Shankar announced that Hanuman Ansh will release in Telugu on October 9. Made on a budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has already earned Rs 425 crore worldwide at the box office, and is continuing to make money at the ticket counters. It is like a slap in the face to see a film with a Rs 2 crore investment gross Rs 400 crore in collections, he said. We are spending crores of rupees with not much to show for it. But to get Rs 400 crore for Rs 2 crore, thats a real pan-Indian film. He urged producers across the industry to ensure the film reaches every possible audience. Wherever possible, if you have skipped releasing it in any language, please release it in all languages. This film is a massive hit, not just revenue-wise. Its a much-needed film, he said.

articleTitle: Gukesh’s coach Gajewski: ‘Good for him to be reminded he can play really well’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gukesh
description: Chess-wise the recent Olympiad was 'good' not 'great' for Gukesh but mentally he was strong, which is a good thing, says his coach Grzegorz Gajewski
body_raw: One of Indian chesss biggest positives at the recent Chess Olympiad was the uptick in form of world champion D Gukesh, who had seven wins and three draws in the first 10 rounds at a staggering performance rating of 2,797, before he lost his final round clash with Hungarian GM Gleb Dudin. The tournament was likely the world champions last appearance in an over-the-board tournament before he hunkers down to prepare for his upcoming World Chess Championship battle against the Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov. For Gukesh, the Olympiad proved to be a slump-buster. Since he has become the world champion in December 2024, hes not won a tournament, coming close at the Tata Steel tournament in Wijk aan Zee in January 2025 and then the Norway Chess tournament that same year. But in recent tournaments, his form has dwindled, at Norway Chess in 2026, he was last in the six-player field, while at the Chennai Grand Masters, he did not taste victory in a single game. These Olympiad results are definitely good for the confidence, its good for Gukesh to be reminded that he can play really well, Gukeshs coach, Polish grandmaster Grzegorz Gajewski, tells The Indian Express in an interview. Before the tournament began, there was some criticism about Gukesh playing on Board 4 for India with Praggnanandhaa on Board 1, Arjun Erigaisi on Board 2 and Nihal Sarin on Board 3. In the previous two Olympiads, Gukesh had excelled on Board 1. Later, Gukesh had revealed that it was his call to play on the fourth board, which in hindsight looks like a masterstroke. I wouldnt call it this way a masterstroke. His teammates performed better in some of the previous events and they were also higher rated so it just seemed like the right thing to do, says Gajewski. Ask Gajewski for his assessment of Gukeshs form at the recent Olympiad, and he says Chess-wise the Olympiad was good but not great. Gukesh can definitely do better. Mentally he was strong and thats the most important thing right now. Chess-wise the recent Olympiad was good not great for Gukesh but mentally he was strong, which is a good thing, says his coach Grzegorz Gajewski The world also saw a different side of Gukesh at the Olympiad. A much easy-going side. He made jokes with the rest of the team. He posted a hilarious video with Praggnanandhaa about a fan mistaking the both of them. He was even at the Bermuda Party an Olympiad tradition where players from all nations come together for an evening party just before the only rest day of the tournament despite the Indians having lost to Uzbekistan that day, a result which more or less ascertained that the Indians would not be able to defend gold. Ask Gajewski whats changed about Gukesh, and he replies For sure his routines during the Olympiad werent as strict as they used to be and I think its a positive thing. The last year was really difficult for Gukesh and in general achieving so much comes with a price. I think that he managed to figure it out and indeed he seems really happy now

articleTitle: Account aggregator ‘interoperability’: What RBI’s move means for your asset statement
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI investments
description: Account aggregators are NBFCs that act as a secure bridge for banking data, allowing lenders to access all relevant data swiftly for faster loan disbursements, or manage consent for other companies attempting to fetch your data.
body_raw: Dematerialised accounts have made it easy for investors to track their investments across financial markets, be it stocks, mutual funds, debt instruments, or commodities. This has made investing quite hassle-free for the common man, eliminating the need to track statements through different apps or depositories. The Reserve Bank of Indias RBI move to now allow interoperability between financial account aggregators AAs could also get your bank holdings into the singular consolidated statement, eliminating the need to track different bank statements to keep a check on deposits. The central bank on Wednesday October 7 allowed interoperability among NBFC Account aggregators, enabling aggregation of financial information through all account aggregators from one account aggregator. What RBI said about account aggregators After the monetary policy statement, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said, We are also facilitating SEBI regulated depositories to include information related to deposit accounts in their consolidated account statement CAS. The measures will be implemented by December 31, 2026. Account aggregators are non-banking financial companies NBFCs who store and move the users banking data without having the permission to access it. They act as a secure bridge for banking data, allowing lenders to access all relevant data swiftly for faster loan disbursements, or manage consent for other companies attempting to fetch your data. The account aggregators are basically people with whom banks enter into a contract for the purpose of sharing information. You can basically get onboarded as a bank customer, consenting to provide your information. And on the basis of your information, they will be able to pull data, explained Vivek Iyer, Partner and National Leader for Financial Services at Grant Thornton Bharat. What changes for you Currently, a consolidated account statement gives an overview for either your banking assets such as deposits, or for demat holdings like stocks, mutual funds, and bonds. There are around 17 account aggregators registered under the RBIs NBFC-AA categorisation, each separately operating in these two spaces. With the RBI opening the door for interoperability between these aggregators, investors will now get a single CAS capturing fixed deposits, recurring deposits, mutual funds, and all other financial instruments regulated by the RBI and the Securities and Exchange Board of India SEBI. This will simplify tracking investments for an average investor. The bottomline, thus, is a comprehensive overview of all investments across the banking and financial markets. On the banking side, this consolidated overview will only be limited to the assets you hold like deposits, and not your loans. Currently, they account aggregators do not have permission to view bank deposits. Why? Because bank deposits sit under banking, the regulator for whom is RBI. And depositories sit under SEBI. So, what RBI has done with this reform is they have spoken to SEBI and told them that this is the reform we will implement. I will handle the aggregators from the banking end, you handle them from the depositories end, explained Iyer. This interoperability may also help smaller businesses that need loans, which are hampered by the lack of standardisation of information across different AAs. A more interoperable AA ecosystem can materially reduce this friction by enabling consent-based access to verified financial data and making the underwriting process faster and more efficient, according to Varoon Naidu, Co-founder of Capital Stack. This can be particularly meaningful for MSMEs and smaller businesses. Better access to banking and other financial data can allow lenders to assess actual cash flows and financial behaviour rather than relying predominantly on traditional bureau scores, collateral or borrower-submitted information. Over time, this should improve both the availability and quality of credit, reduce turnaround times and potentially allow lenders to price risk more accurately, said Naidu. Further scope for interoperability While the central bank has taken initial steps towards a comprehensive asset overview for each person with the announcement on Wednesday, there is further scope going ahead. For example, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India IRDAI could also come on board so that an individuals CAS also reflects the insurance policies they hold. This can be done through cooperation between the RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI. See, for that, the insurance market needs to be matured. So, one step at a time. They SEBI and RBI said let us just first integrate the bank deposits with the investments. And then we can get into the whole insurance aspects also. At some point in time, you will see an integration of your insurance also coming into it, said Iyer. So, the goal is basically a single comprehensive list of assets held by each investor. And the RBIs permission for interoperability between AAs marks an important step towards achieving this.

articleTitle: Was Cathy born evil? Netflix’s East of Eden rewrites Steinbeck’s most notorious villain
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A still from East of Eden. (Source: Netflix)
description: Netflix’s East of Eden, starring Florence Pugh as Cathy Ames, gives John Steinbeck’s infamous ‘psychic monster’ a traumatic past, reigniting a decades-old debate over whether she was born evil or made monstrous.
body_raw: Are monsters created, or is one born evil? In East of Eden, future Nobel laureate John Steinbeck backs innate evil through Cathy Ames, one of the most ruthless femme fatales ever written. Now, a woman screenwriter has challenged his take on that chicken-and-egg ouroboros in Netflixs seven-episode adaptation of the American classic. Steinbecks Cathy is a serpent-tongued Eve who leads men astray, leaving only death and regret in her wake. Zoe Kazan-granddaughter of Elia Kazan, who directed the 1955 adaptation starring James Dean-tells the story from the villains perspective. To the delight and dismay of Steinbecks readers, Kazan gives Cathy, played by Florence Pugh, a villain-origin story. Here is what you should know about how Steinbeck wrote Cathy, what the series changes, the split verdict on the adaptation, and the novel itself. Steinbecks Cathy I believe there are monsters born in the world to human parents. From the outset, Steinbeck describes Cathy as something inherently evil, calling her a psychic monster with a malformed soul. He says Cathy learns early to use sex as power. In Steinbecks telling, she gets two older boys punished for assaulting her.As a teenager, she seduces her Latin teacher, who kills himself. She sets fire to the family home with her parents inside, empties her fathers safe and fakes her own death. She sleeps with her husbands brother on her wedding night, tries to end her pregnancy, takes over a brothel by poisoning its owner, and turns it into a house of sadomasochism and blackmail. With such a litany of crimes, she is portrayed as a soulless monster, a seductress, with Steinbeck reaching for Satanic descriptors to describe her her feet are small and stubby, with fat insteps almost like little hoofs, and on one occasion, her tongue flickers like a serpent. What the series changes In the Netflix adaptation, Cathy commits nearly all the same crimes, but Kazan tries to rationalise it as a traumatic response of a child violated. The aforementioned carriage-house frame-up is replaced with a scene in which an older boy lures Cathy with candy when she is but a child. In her teens, her lovesick teacher becomes a predator, and her timid father is portrayed as a tyrant who whips her and treats her as his property. In Kazans telling, Cathy is a woman exposed to the worlds cruelty at a young age, and rather than be exploited, she decides to manipulate the world and be cruel in turn. Her ambition to be free from the restrictions of society and family spurs her to escape all kinds of bonds, often through murder. She takes over a brothel through underhanded means, and uses it to gather blackmail. This is a perverted rebellion against the ambition of her contemporaries, motherhood and marriage, which in the mid-20th century would make her villainous even without the murders. Pugh told Radio Times that despite the empathetic treatment granted to a woman who in the original text is an irredeemable psychopath, Cathy is not given absolution she does not get away scot-free. For better or worse Many commentators have argued that the changes defang Cathy and reduce her to a traumatised victim, when she actually is an unrepentant perpetrator. It also robs the story of its originality by allowing a female villain with criminal tendencies who isnt driven by a moment of desperation or a last resort. As the influential critic Louis Owens, who wrote in John Steinbecks Re-Vision of America, says, Cathy is evil thats simply the way it is. Many of Steinbecks detractors believe the changes to be an improvement, as they prevent Cathy from staying a one-dimensional character, the archetypal personification of the original sin that cost Adam Paradise, or even Lilith, who refuses to bend. The change allows the character to be more than an unflattering caricature of his ex-wife Gwen, with whom he had an acrimonious split, with allegations of infidelity thrown on either side. Besides the novels central idea, timshel, the Hebrew word Steinbeck translates as thou mayest, gives the male characters the luxury of choosing their own path, but denies the same to Cathy, who is sentenced to be a monster from birth to death. Sarah Appleton Aguiar also argues in a 2005 essay that Cathys malevolent nature tends to present itself only when she is feeling cornered or trapped. Does Steinbeck hint at abuse Bibliophiles who have already watched the adaptation point out that Steinbeck himself writes that Cathy learned very young that sexuality is the most disturbing impulse humans have. In chapter 17, the narrator doubts himself, admitting that without knowing what Cathy wanted, it is easy to call her bad and hard to say why. In the letters to his editor later published as Journal of a Novel, Steinbeck went further To that extent I am a monster like Cathy. And when a correspondent told him that Cathy only became believable at the end of the book, he replied that this was when, through fear, she became like us. What is East of Eden? Published in 1952, East of Eden is a 600-page American saga, which Steinbeck wrote for his two sons. Reception was mixed, with some calling Steinbeck moralistic, melodramatic, and misogynistic, but it quickly became a bestseller within two months. The book has never gone out of print, and it saw another burst of popularity in 2003, when Oprah Winfrey chose it to relaunch her book club. The Trask story retells the biblical tale of the rival brothers Cain and Abel twice first through Adam and his violent half-brother, Charles, then through Cathys twins, gentle Aron and moody Cal. Villain or antihero, Cathy remains its most argued-over character. Whatever ones view of good versus evil, or nature versus nurture, a book that still sparks this much debate almost a lifetime after publication has earned its place among American classics.

articleTitle: Tracing Uttarakhand’s 8.27 lakh ‘missing’ voters: What EC’s camps, house visits will check
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The exercise, details of which were presented to all district election officers this week, will begin with three-day camps at all 12,543 polling stations from October 8 to 10, followed by house-to-house verification between October 12 and 20.
description: Days after the final rolls were published, the Election Commission of India will trace voters missing from the final roll, verify their status and enrol eligible electors through Form 6
body_raw: The Election Commission has launched a special drive to trace and verify 8.27 lakh electors who were marked ASDD uncollectible during Uttarakhands Special Intensive Revision SIR, with officials now being instructed to identify those whose names figured in the pre-SIR electoral roll but are missing from the final list. The exercise, details of which were presented to all district election officers this week, will begin with three-day camps at all 12,543 polling stations from October 8 to 10, followed by house-to-house verification between October 12 and 20. The drive is aimed at correcting omissions after the SIR rather than undertaking another revision officials will specifically trace people who were on the pre-SIR roll, verify their current status and enrol them through Form 6 if they remain eligible. The data presented by the Chief Electoral Officers office shows that 8,26,977 electors were marked ASDD during the SIR. The highest number was recorded in Dehradun 1,86,008, followed by Udham Singh Nagar 1,77,673, Haridwar 1,30,203, Almora 55,485, Pauri Garhwal 51,359 and Tehri Garhwal 43,625. The development comes days after Uttarakhand published its final electoral roll on October 3, with 71,58,949 electors - around 8 lakh fewer than the electorate before the SIR. Chief Electoral Officer BVRC Purushottam said Wednesday that the exercise would specifically look for people who were on the pre-SIR roll but are absent from the current roll. BLOs shall compare the current electoral roll with the pre-SIR electoral roll and identify such electors whose names were there in the pre-SIR roll but who are not included in the current electoral roll and prepare a list of such electors. House-to-house verification Following the three-day camps, BLOs will visit the homes of identified electors between October 12 and 20 to ascertain their present status and facilitate enrolment through Form 6 wherever they are found eligible. The exercise will also cover other left-out voters and first-time voters who became eligible with reference to October 1, 2026. Purushottam said the BLOs would also assist those who turned 18 on October 1 in filling Form 6, and that the exercise will involve not just election officials but also representatives of political parties. During the three-day camps, BLOs, Booth Awareness Group BAG members and Booth Level Agents BLA-2 will be present at polling stations. During house-to-house visits, BLOs will be accompanied by BAG members and, as far as possible, BLAs. The lists prepared by BLOs will be shared with BLAs of recognised political parties. At the end of the exercise, Electoral Registration Officers will again share booth-wise lists with political party representatives, giving them another opportunity to identify eligible voters left out of the roll. 8 lakh-plus drop after SIR The fresh exercise assumes significance against the scale of deletions during the revision. According to data by the CEOs office, Uttarakhand had 84,29,459 electors on the January 6, 2025 roll. Between January 2025 and August 13, 2026, there were 4,01,276 additions but 17,05,130 deletions across the revision process. The final roll published on October 3 contained 71,58,949 electors. During the claims-and-objections period between July 14 and August 13, 1,29,872 additions and 1,04,708 deletions were recorded. The Indian Express had earlier reported that 1,30,382 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names were filed during the claims-and-objections period, with more than 85 percent of these coming from Udham Singh Nagar, Haridwar, Dehradun and Nainital. The Electoral Registration Officers will process the applications under the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The presentation also draws their attention to Rule 20, which provides for a summary inquiry into claims and objections and an opportunity for the concerned persons to be heard.

articleTitle: Rural consumer confidence worsened for six straight months: RBI survey
articleFeaturedImageAlt: market
description: RBI’s Current Situation Index — which captures perceptions of the economy, employment, prices, income and spending — fell to 90.6 in September, from 91.7 in July
body_raw: Rural consumer sentiment in India has weakened steadily through 2026, with households becoming increasingly pessimistic about the economy, jobs and their own incomes, even as they continue to expect spending to rise. The Reserve Bank of Indias RBI September 2026 Rural Consumer Confidence Survey RCCS points to a widening gap between how rural and semi-urban households view their current circumstances and what they hope will happen over the next year. The RBIs Current Situation Index CSI, which captures perceptions of the economy, employment, prices, income and spending compared with a year ago, fell to 90.6 in September, from 91.7 in July. This is the sixth consecutive decline from 100.5 in January, and marks a sharp deterioration from 100.9 in September 2025. The deterioration is broad-based. The net response on the general economic situation declined from -11.9 in July to -14.1 in September. On the employment front, the net response worsened from -8.0 to -10.5, while the income measure slipped from -8.7 to -9.9, the survey shows. These figures mean that the share of respondents who felt conditions had worsened exceeded those who saw an improvement by an increasingly large margin. Income data, inflation The income data is particularly revealing. In September, only 20.6 of respondents said their income had increased compared with a year earlier, while 30.5 said it had decreased. A year earlier, the corresponding figures were 24.5 and 26.5. The net response has consequently moved from -2.1 in September 2025 to -9.9 now. Inflation is another major source of pressure. Rural households median perception of current inflation rose to 6.8 in September, from 6.1 in July and 5.9 in May. Their one-year-ahead inflation expectation also climbed to 7.9, from 7.4 in July and 6.8 in March. The September reading is particularly striking because it is 70 basis points bps higher for current inflation and 50 bps higher for future inflation than in July. The price-level responses underline this anxiety. As many as 93.2 of respondents said prices had increased compared with a year earlier, up from 91.6 in July. For the next year, 85.9 expect prices to increase. Net spending improves, squeeze on household confidence Yet the survey does not point to a collapse in household spending. The spending net response improved to 79.6 in September, from 77.4 in July. Spending on essential items remained particularly strong, with a net response of 84.2, while the corresponding figure for non-essential spending rose to 39.3. The disconnect between weak present sentiment and relatively strong expectations is captured by the Future Expectations Index FEI. Although it eased to 112.8 from 113.6 in July, it remains firmly above 100, indicating optimism about the year ahead. However, this too has declined substantially from 129.3 in January. What the survey shows, therefore, is not simply rural pessimism but a squeeze on household confidence. Rural consumers are spending, but their perceptions of incomes, employment and economic conditions are deteriorating while inflation expectations are rising. The fact that future expectations remain optimistic provides some cushion. But if weak income growth and elevated price expectations persist, that optimism could come under further pressure. The September RBI survey, based on 8,799 responses collected across rural and semi-urban India, thus offers a cautionary signal the rural economy may still be supporting consumption, but households increasingly feel that their financial position is not keeping pace with the cost of living.

Yes, when he played a couple of games in Australia, he was also finding it a little difficult, but he had some fitness issues. With the bat, he could contribute really well. He has very, very good hands and is a good catcher, Ashwin said. He is going to New Zealand now.
