articleTitle: How Amitabh Bachchan & Amish Tripathi are taking Indian mythology global through gaming
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Age of Bhaarat - Visual (1)
description: The Age of Bhaarat is a dark fantasy action adventure game that draws on Indian epics and traditions.
body_raw: Ancient India is a land of noble heroes and glittering cities. But, where heroes rule, villains will attack. Where wealth is plentiful, plunderers will pillage, says Amitabh Bachchan in the trailer of the game, The Age of Bhaarat. Your time has come to declare war, he says as the screen crackles with images of fire bursting out of the ruins of grand sculptured pillars. Bachchan is the co-founder of Tara Gaming Ltd, gamemakers for PCs and consoles that features mythical landscapes and magical characters and stories drawn from the Indian epics. The other eminent founder is Amish Tripathi, author of Shiva Trilogy. Tara Gamings vision is a large franchise that is aimed at telling Indian stories in a way that resonates worldwide. The Age of Bhaarat, for instance, is a dark fantasy action-adventure game that draws on Indian epics and traditions to inspire an international audience to undertake a journey of an ordinary person who becomes a powerful Forest Warden armed with magical capabilities. This is possibly Indias first AAA action adventure game, which is the hallmark of a high profile, big-budget game of top production capability. The game is currently under development and is expected to hit the markets in a couple of years. The studio where the game is being developed is in Pune. There is an immense combination of the richness of mythology, their novelty to the West, their relevance in India and the talent in India and, particularly, in Pune. When we started, the first thing we did was hiring a head for a studio in Pune, Siddharth Singh. In about 18 months, we grew the studio to 85 people, says executive chairman Nicolas Granatino. Gaming has caught the interest of the Central government as well. In the Union Budget this year, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had spoken of the rapid growth of Indias animation, visual effects, gaming and comics AVGC sector, he added. Singh said, a lot of times, the Indian industry has worked as vendors or outsourcers for foreign companies. They come in and give us a part of the work. Not a lot of companies in India have done this kind of large-scale execution, from the initial ideation and concept phase all the way through to the final launch. So, not many people have actually seen or experienced the entire lifecycle of game development in India, and thats where Tara Gaming is different. We have also managed to bring together the right kind of talent, says Singh. While Tripathi is responsible for crafting the lore of the game, Bachchan is involved in the creative process and provides the voiceover for the games trailer. The rest of the team is equally rooted to the story. Success is not only bringing a successful game and these stories to the world. For us, success is that some of the people in the studio in Pune will leave a few years from now and create their own studio, because they will have seen the production of the game from scratch. Thats a very different way to train and upskill and work with talent in India, says Granatino.

articleTitle: Sujeet Kalkal wants the mat, not the functions, before the World Championships
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sujeet
description: The Asian Games champion, who has won 19 bouts in a row, says the ground game is what he must fix before Kazakhstan
body_raw: Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal has had a great week. He brought the mens 65 kg freestyle gold home from the Asian Games after defeating Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semi-final and winning the final from 2-9 down. He also won the Raja Randhir Singh award for the best Indian male athlete at the Asian Games 2026. However, the 23-year-old from Charkhi Dadri doesnt want to lose himself in the celebrations right now.After winning the Asian Games medal, there are some distractions like functions and everything. But I want to go back to the mat as soon as possible, Sujeet said at an interaction organised by SAI Media. He is right to want to get back to the mat a tough World Championships awaits him in Kazakhstan, starting October 24. Sujeet is on a dominant run in the mens 65 kg category. He is the reigning U23 World Champion, Asian champion and Asian Games gold medallist. Since losing the bronze-medal match at last years World Championships, Sujeet has won 19 bouts in a row and is unbeaten at the national level too. The World Championships will bring new challenges the Iranian powerhouse Rahman Amouzadkhalili, to whom Sujeet lost last year, and the American prodigy Bowen Bassett, who beat Worlds bronze medallist Real Marshall Ray Woods in the US trials. The competition level in the World Championships is very tough and it is not going to be easy for me. It is certainly more competitive than the Asian Games and that is what makes it more exciting. This is the most important competition for me, Sujeet said. But he has a few things to fine-tune before he goes for a world title. I need to learn from the mistakes that I made in the past competitions. So, I am going to focus on that, he said. Sujeets Asian Games campaign was near flawless, but he gave away easy points at the start of bouts, especially in positions played out on the mat. One of the reasons that Sujeet trailed in the final was that he gave a more advantageous position to the opponent on the ground. That is something we are going to work on in this small time frame we have got, his coach Kuldeep Singh told The Indian Express. Sujeet agrees. Both my coaches Kuldeep and Shako have asked me to take a strong position on the ground. I am working on it. Right now, I need to attack on the ground well and also defend if I lose the attacking position, he explained. The other thing he has to do more of is attack, something national coach Bentinidis Shako also insists on. Before the Asian Games, I had played a tournament in Russia. I won that tournament and every bout in it. But coach Shako was not happy with it, Sujeet said. He told me to attack more as I have a variety of attacks. He did that at the Asian Games, but will need to do more of it at the World Championships. I worked on it and executed it during the Asian Games. That is why I was able to score so many points. I think I will need to continue doing this at the World Championships, said Sujeet. Shako, who also coached Bajrang Punia to an Olympic medal, has brought attacking changes to Sujeets game. One of the highlights of Sujeets Asian Games campaign was his use of the dhobi pachad in the bout against the Iranian wrestler. It is a classic Indian kushti technique that uses the opponents momentum and a tight upper-body grip to lift and arc them over the shoulder or back. I have to thank coach Shako for that. I used to try the technique in practice but never really executed it on the mat. But coach Shako made some corrections to it. He asked me to practice it over and over. I think I executed it because of the regular practice of the move, said Sujeet. Sujeet has less than 15 days to finish with the functions, work on his ground wrestling and head to Astana, Kazakhstan, where he could become only the second Indian to win a wrestling world title.

articleTitle: Expert Explains | How Eastern Maritime Corridor can diversify India’s energy flows
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India energy security
description: The EMC is relevant given India’s quantum of Russian oil imports and energy import bias towards the west coast. It can reduce transit time to a Russian port by one-third via Chennai-Vladivostok, compared with the Mumbai-St Petersburg route.
body_raw: The conflict between US-Israel and Iran impacting the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait have brought Indias energy security into sharp focus. India is the worlds third-largest energy consumer and second-largest energy importer, importing around one-third of its total energy supply. It ranks as the worlds third-largest crude oil importer and the fourth-largest importer of liquefied natural gas LNG. Oil imports stand at approximately 240-250 million tonnes annually, with an import dependency of nearly 85-90. LNG imports are about 26-27 million tonnes, with roughly 50 dependency, while liquefied petroleum gas LPG imports are around 20-21 million tonnes, with approximately 60 dependency. This clearly establishes that Indias energy system is structurally dependent on maritime supply chains. This vulnerability is further exacerbated by Indias coastal imbalance. Approximately 65-70 of Indias oil imports, 75-80 of LNG imports, and 55-60 of LPG imports are handled on the west coast. This concentration is reinforced by infrastructure nearly 60-65 of refining capacity and about 70-75 of LNG regasification capacity are located on the West coast. Regasification refers to the industrial process of warming LNG from its cryogenic storage temperature -162C back into its standard gaseous state for distribution and consumption. As a result, Indias energy system is overwhelmingly dependent on the Arabian Sea and exposed to the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab-el-Mandeb chokepoints. The westward tilt also creates a serious national security vulnerability, as the Jamnagar and Vadinar refineries, which together represent a third of Indias total refining output, are within striking distance of swarm drone attacks from Pakistan. Indias unique advantage with Russia In recent years, Russia has emerged as a critical energy partner for India. Since 2023, Russian imports have accounted for roughly 30-40 of Indias total oil imports. In 2025, India imported approximately 45.38 billion of crude oil from Russia, averaging around 1.7 to 1.9 million barrels per day. This trend continued into 2026, with Indias oil imports from Russia peaking in mid-2026 at an estimated record share of about 50.8 of total imports 2.47 million barrels per day in July 2026. This energy relationship, however, is also coast-asymmetric. India has diversified its suppliers but not its routes. Russian oil is largely shipped from its Baltic ports via the Suez Canal - which connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through Egypt - to Western Indian ports. As a result, even diversified supplies remain exposed to maritime chokepoints and broader geopolitical disruptions. It is in this broader context that Indias unique connectivity advantage with Russia becomes particularly significant. The Russians have subsumed the erstwhile Northern Sea Route, which ran from Murmansk to Provideniya, into the Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor TATC project, which spans from St Petersburg in the west to Vladivostok in the east. Along its route, the TATC aims to integrate major Russian ports, including Murmansk and Arkhangelsk, to create a unified transport system combining sea, rail, road and inland waterways, connect the key economic centres of Eurasia and form a seamless logistics corridor. India is connected to both ends of the TATC. On the western side, it is linked via the International North-South Transport Corridor INSTC, and on the eastern side via the Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor, also known as the Eastern Maritime Corridor EMC. The critical internal connector in this system is Russias Unified Deep-Water System, which integrates inland waterways, links European Russia to Arctic ports, and carries approximately 75 of Russias internal cargo. Relevance of Eastern Maritime Corridor The EMC is particularly relevant given Indias energy import bias towards the west coast. Launched in 2019 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, the EMC was accompanied by Indias announcement of its Act Far East Policy and a 1-billion credit to Russia. The EMC can reduce transit time to a Russian port by one-third via Chennai and Vladivostok, compared with the route between Mumbai and St Petersburg. Trade will take only 24 days to traverse the 10,470-km-long EMC at a speed of 10 knots, compared with 36 days required to cover the 16,070-km conventional route to St Petersburg through the Suez. This efficiency is increasingly vital amid persistent geopolitical disruptions and chokepoint vulnerabilities in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz. In 2024, around 94 million tonnes of Russian exports, including 63 million tonnes of oil and petroleum products and 21 million tonnes of bulk cargo, were delivered to Indian ports via the Suez Canal. Even partial diversion of these flows through the EMC could significantly reduce exposure to chokepoints and enhance supply resilience. Through the EMC, India will gain direct access to the mineral-rich Russian Far East and the Arctic, one of the worlds last largely untouched resource repositories. These resources are becoming increasingly accessible for exploitation as ice melts due to climate change-induced global warming and other local factors. They include 13 of the worlds undiscovered conventional oil reserves and 30 of its undiscovered natural gas, as well as large deposits of coal base metals such as nickel, copper, zinc, lead, iron ore, and tin precious metals and stones, including gold, silver, platinum, palladium, and diamonds and industrial minerals such as phosphate for fertilisers, bauxite for aluminium, and rare earth elements. Russias Arctic Zone is the countrys largest territory. At 4.9 million sq km, it is 1.5 times the size of India, yet has fewer than one-twelfth as many people as Delhi. The Russian Arctic is larger than the combined Arctic regions of the other seven Arctic countries. It accounts for 15 of Russias gross domestic product and 20 of its exports, and holds three-quarters of the countrys natural gas resources and more than one-fifth of its oil reserves. Given the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia, a long-term partnership in energy and minerals through the EMC could strengthen Indias energy security and help address its rare earth and mineral shortfalls. Ocean freight through the EMC is also expected to be more than 50 cheaper compared with the Suez route, thanks to the shorter distance and the absence of canal transit charges. Indias major trading partners, China, Japan, and South Korea, also lie along the EMC, while more than half of Indias trade passes through the South China Sea. India and Russia have explicitly linked the EMCs development to their ambitious goal of reaching 100 billion US dollars in annual trade by 2030. While the EMC holds transformative potential for bilateral trade, its commercial success hinges on one critical missing piece a predictable, scheduled direct liner shipping service, where cargo vessels operate on fixed schedules, predefined routes, and regular stopovers at designated seaports. The corridors economic potential cannot be realised at scale without addressing its systemic constraints. The EMC was announced as operational in November 2024 by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, and cargo is moving. Yet there is no direct, regular liner service connecting the major ports of India and the Russian Far East. India-Russia trade reached a record high of 68.7 billion in FY 2024-25 but remains highly asymmetric. Indian exports stood at merely 4.9 billion, dwarfed by Russian exports to India of about 63.8 billion. Challenges and possible solutions In the absence of a direct scheduled service from Vladivostok to Chennai, container logistics often rely on inefficient transhipment via third-party Asian ports such as Ningbo or Shanghai. For instance, recent services organised by operators such as FESCO have recorded transit times of around 34 days due to these indirect routings. This lack of a direct schedule results in unpredictable transit times and volatile freight rates, making it impossible for exporters to commit to delivery schedules or accurately calculate logistics costs. Consequently, many businesses are forced to rely on slower yet more predictable western routes. Compounding these logistical hurdles are physical infrastructure gaps, such as a lack of specialised transhipment terminals in Vladivostok for key commodities, alongside ongoing banking sanctions that create friction in payment mechanisms. This creates a classic chicken-and-egg problem. Shipping companies are reluctant to launch a dedicated, high-frequency service until cargo volumes are large enough to make it profitable. At the same time, exporters hesitate to shift their supply chains to the corridor without a reliable, published sailing schedule. This dilemma is closely linked to the severe imbalance in trade flows EMCs current cargo profile consists almost entirely of Russian bulk commodities, including crude oil, coal, and fertilisers. To be commercially viable, a scheduled container service must address the critical backhaul problem. EMCs economic purpose must therefore evolve. Vladivostok must become not only a Russian export gateway to India but also a viable distribution hub for Indian goods, including pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, and agricultural products, destined for the Russian Far East and the wider domestic market. Overcoming these constraints requires shifting the focus from mere infrastructure announcements to practical, collaborative logistics solutions. To break the chicken-and-egg cycle and absorb the initial commercial risk, several policy and market measures can be deployed. Governments and port authorities could offer temporary subsidies, preferential port charges, and guaranteed berthing windows to incentivise early adoption. Minimum-volume commitments from major exporters and importers could provide the baseline assurance shipping lines need. Furthermore, joint service agreements between Russian and Indian shipping companies could distribute financial risk, while an anchor-cargo model could allow containerised freight to utilise the same maritime corridor established by bulk trade. Recent industry dialogues in 2026 emphasise that authorities and logistics partners must act immediately to organise reliable routes. Businesses need a clear understanding of the schedule now, not next year, to make the corridor competitive with established alternatives. Ultimately, the EMC should be seen not as a fully operational maritime route but as a logistics platform whose commercial potential is constrained by the lack of regular sailings. An occasional voyage is not the same as an economically viable corridor an irregular vessel may carry a single cargo, but only a scheduled service can sustain trade flows. The EMCs next stage should be judged not by whether ships can sail from Chennai to Vladivostok, but by whether exporters and importers can rely on a vessel departing every week or two. Establishing this reliable, direct liner service is essential to turning the EMC from a strategic aspiration into a genuine, sustainable driver of diversified bilateral trade between India and Russia.

articleTitle: Inside Gukesh’s transformation from ‘lone wolf’ to being the life of team meetings at Chess Olympiad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: World champion D Gukesh on a sail boat during the Norway Chess Games day in Oslo during the recent Norway Chess tournament. (Express Photo by Amit Kamath)
description: At the Chess Olympiad, the world saw a different side of Gukesh. As Vidit Gujrathi and Sankalp Gupta, who have been with the Indian team for multiple Olympiad editions say: “On-the-board Gukesh and off-the-board Gukesh are almost like two different people.”
body_raw: During the recent Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, world champion Gukesh D did something he had rarely ever done in public before. He cracked a joke. Sitting at the airport on his way back after helping Indias open section team to a silver medal, Gukesh shot a video with Praggnanandhaa where he told his teammate that a fan had approached him for a photo but could not recollect his name, before eventually mistaking him for Pragg. Guys remember, this is Gukesh, he said cheekily pointing at Pragg, . and Im Pragg, Gukesh joked, while his compatriot smiled good-naturedly. In that short, one-minute clip, Gukesh had shown the world a glimpse of his other side the goofier, 20-year-old version of himself that fans have seldom seen during chess tournaments. On-the-board Gukesh and off-the-board Gukesh are very different, explains Vidit Gujrathi, who was also a part of the Olympiad team. Sankalp Gupta, who has also been a coach with the Indian team for multiple editions and has seen Gukeshs fun-loving side first hand during the Turkish League in 2023, adds On-the-board Gukesh and off-the-board Gukesh are almost like two different people. But even those who have seen both sides of Gukesh were pleasantly surprised by the version of him that they saw at this Olympiad. For the past 18 months, the 20-year-old looked like he was struggling under the twin burdens of dwindling form and the weight of expectations. At the Chennai Grand Masters, his last tournament before the Olympiad, he did not win a single match. Then, something changed. Around August, after he played the Chennai Grand Masters, I started seeing a change in Gukesh. He was learning surfing, doing a bit of skating, trying all these new things. He was spending some time away from chess trying to have fun. The same thing carried over to the Olympiad as well. He was having a lot of fun. When we had our online training camp for the Olympiad, as soon as Gukesh joined, the vibe got lighter, says Srinath Narayanan, the captain of the Indian mens Olympiad team. ALSO READ Gukeshs coach Gajewski Good for him to be reminded he can play really well Srinath traces how Gukesh changed over successive Olympiads. Theres been an incredible difference with Gukesh every year. In 2022, when I was not captain of the team Gukesh was in India 2, the story I heard was that Gukesh wouldnt participate in team meetings. He would just turn up to play and win his individual games. In 2023 during the Asian Games, the players were not the best of friends. But before the Budapest Olympiad, I had a chat with the players. I felt something changed in Gukesh internally, that he really wanted to get along with the team and spend time with everyone, indulge in banter, attend team meetings, which became a ritual starting from the Budapest Olympiad, says Srinath. Sankalp Gupta adds At the 2022 Olympiad, Gukesh used to be completely different than he is currently. Im not saying this approach is better or that one was. Its just a different approach. He used to be like a lone wolf back in 2022. He would eat meals by himself, stay by himself. But in 2024, he would join team meetings. We had great team bonding that time, but Gukesh was still a bit reserved. Srinath explains that the distance that the players kept from each other a few years ago was understandable. For most of the year, they would be fighting for the same titles, facing off against each other repeatedly, and chasing the same opportunities. It was a scenario that previous members of Indias Olympiad teams had not faced. Bond between players But since Budapest 2024, the camaraderie and the banter in the India camp grew as have the bonds between players. Helping solidify the bond were multiple game-day rituals, like team walks, long meetings and a player-of-the-round award which Srinath points out was also an idea from Gukesh. At Samarkand, the banter was unparalleled, say Srinath and Sankalp. Much of it was initiated by Gukesh, who the coaches say was the funniest member of the Indian mens team at this edition, taking over the baton from Pentala Harikrishna, who would lighten the mood in previous Olympiad teams. Team meetings had a vibe that you would find in a typical boys hostel, says Srinath. At Budapest Olympics, the team meetings for initial rounds were just 5-10 minutes. By the time we played USA in round 10, meetings would just go for 40-45 minutes with a lot of casual banter, says Srinath. Srinath says at the ongoing Olympiad, Gukesh was professional when discussion turned to chess, but he also knew when to switch off. Gukesh felt that we should be more chill as a team. Players keep certain things, like opening preparation, personal. But they can still hang out together as friends outside of that, says Srinath. The biggest surprise came at the traditional Bermuda Party held after the 6th round. The team atmosphere was a bit gloomy that day because India had lost to Uzbekistan. Gukesh had taken a draw and Nihal had lost a game that he could have won. That evening, Gukesh and Vidit turned up at the Bermuda Party and Gukesh did another thing you would not expect him to do in the middle of a tournament. He danced. He even did an impression of Michael Jacksons moon walk. With the amount of cameras and attention on him, it was difficult for Gukesh to be able to do that in the past. But in Samarkand, he made a conscious decision that he is not going to care about all those things and he will just have fun like a normal 20-year-old, says Srinath.

articleTitle: ‘Charles Sobhraj of Kashmir’ sold land he didn’t own, tracked via newspaper subscription
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kashmir: The Crime Branch sleuths got alerted. “Why would someone tap on a door with no one inside?” said an official connected with the probe. (File Photo)
description: J&K Police arrested an 80-year-old former Ayurvedic doctor accused of cheating buyers in fake land deals using multiple identities and forged documents.
body_raw: In hot pursuit of this man, JK Police arrived at a house in Zewan area in Srinagars outskirts on September 24. A woman who answered the door told them that he had already left. The personnel asked her to show them the room where he stayed. The woman led them and, gingerly, tapped on the door. This was when the Crime Branch sleuths got alerted. Why would someone tap on a door with no one inside? said an official connected with the probe. The team instinctively spread out some barged into the room, others secured the windows. Inside,an elderly man sat under a dim light, his favourite Urdu newspaper in hand, with little knowledge that it was this love for the broadsheet that landed police at the door of the house where he had been hiding all this while. He is Somnath Koul. Or Mohan Lal Dhar. Or Brijnath Bhat. Or Hadinath Dhar. It depends on whom you ask, or which identity document he chooses to produce. But the police department in the Union Territory already had a moniker for him Charles Sobhraj of Kashmir. Police say that for almost a decade now, Koul, now 80, had been swindling Valley residents with promises of selling them land left behind by Kashmiri Pandit migrants like himself. To some, he would pose as an attorney facilitating the sale. In other cases, he would pose as the owner himself, beguiling the potential buyers with his story of having to leave his home due to the onset of militancy in the 1990s. None of the land that he wanted to sell belonged to him in the first place, said a police officer. Koul would identify the land left behind by the Pandits, strike a deal with prospective buyers with forged documents, collect the money and disappear, the officer added. That was until January this year when police found Kouls photograph affixed to one of the fake sale documents. It set off a nine-month-long hunt that eventually uncovered a trail of fraudulent land deals dating as far back as 2017. The hunt In November last year, a south Kashmir resident approached the Economic Offences Wing EOW of the Crime Branch, stating that he had bought five kanals a little over half an acre of land at Drusoo village in Pulwama and 300 poplar trees planted on a parcel of land in Bijbehara after paying Rs 93 lakh. The complainant said that when he went to court for ratification of Agreement to Sell, he was told that the land doesnt belong to the person shown as seller in the agreement. On April 1 this year, the Crime Branch registered a formal FIR against Koul, setting off an investigation in motion. It was a piece of land belonging to a migrant Kashmiri Pandit and Koul had posed as the owners attorney. In the case of the Bijbehara property, he claimed to be the owner himself, said an investigating officer. When we contacted the actual owner, he told us he had not given anyone a power of attorney. The Agreement to Sell listed Koul as a resident of a locality in Jammu with an alternate address in Bengaluru. But when police teams reached the two addresses, Koul was nowhere to be found. But the so-called agreement offered police a crucial clue. The witness Ghulam Mohidin Dar, a resident of Budgam in central Kashmir, had signed the document as a witness. In August, Crime Branch sleuths reached his house. Dar told the officials he would change his clothes and accompany them. We were waiting for him when his family members attacked us, an officer said. In the melee, Dar managed to escape. On September 17, after a 10-kilometre chase from Rajbagh to Kanipora, Dar was nabbed. Police investigations revealed that Dar, himself an influential land broker, would lure the buyers for Koul. This is when police started learning about Kouls multiple identities. Said to be a retired Ayurvedic doctor, Kouls name in his service records is Brijnath Bhat. He owns two Voter Identity cards and two Aadhaar cards each. In one voter card, he is Brijnath Bhat. In the other, he is Hadinath Dhar. His two Aadhaar cards identify him as Somnath Koul and Mohan Lal Dhar, respectively. Of the four documents, only one could be genuine. We checked with the Aadhaar database, his name was recorded as Somnath Koul, says an officer. It was a mystery for us. If his name in so-called service records was Brijnath Bhat, how could he make an Aadhaar in the name of Somnath Koul? Finger tips damaged, iris altered As the mystery about his identity deepened, police decided to go for biometrics. It threw up more surprises. He had destroyed his fingertips. When we asked him about it, he said he had accidentally burnt them, the officer said. His iris scans too failed many times. The official at the Aadhaar centre said he most likely had an eye surgery. We really had a hard time getting one of his iris scans matched. The officials went through his Aadhaar records and were left befuddled once more. In 2016, Koul applied for an Aadhaar card in the name of Brijnath Bhat, a resident of Muthi in Jammu. The name matched his service records. In 2022, he, however, changed the name on his Aadhaar to Somnath Koul. We are checking how it happened, the officer said. The Agreement to sell also showed his name as Somnath Koul. The man himself, though, remained elusive, prompting JK police to liken him with Charles Sobhraj-the famous con artist. But interrogating Dar, police came upon a curious piece of information. Koul was an avid reader of newspapers. Apart from his favourite one published from the Valley, he would also subscribe to a bunch of newspapers from Jammu. Police began keeping a track of this unique bunch of reading material, which finally landed them at the house of his acquaintance in Zewan. Back at the Crime Branch, officials went through its own database to check cases against different identities assumed by Koul. They found at least four other cases, the oldest one dating back to 2017 and registered at the EOW of the Crime Branch. The three other cases were registered in the EOW and Special Crime Wing from 2021 to 2026. Past cases The complainant in the first case, police said, knew him as Brijnath Bhat. In his complaint, a villager stated that Koul posed himself as an attorney for a piece of land at Goshabugh in Pattan, Baramulla. A deal was done for 11 kanals and 3 marlas, a little less than one-and-a-half acre, for Rs 55 lakh. The parcel included some pieces of land belonging to Kashmiri Pandit migrants. After the complainant paid Rs 9.17 lakh in advance, Koul disappeared without a trace. In 2021, Koul again posed as an attorney, out to sell one-and-a-half kanal of Pandit land at Gulab Bagh Pandach in Srinagar. This time, he again identified himself as Brijnath Bhat. After allegedly taking Rs 47 lakh from the buyer, he disappeared. Police filed a chargesheet in absentia. Two years later, police received two more complaints. Koul allegedly promised the same piece of land to two different buyers at Humhama near the Srinagar airport. To one man, he identified himself as Brijnath Bhat. To the other, he was Hadinath Dhar. He took a combined total of Rs 1 crore from the two men and disappeared, said police. In the latest case, he had taken Rs 15 lakh from his buyer before doing the vanishing act, and being arrested months later. With his arrest, JK Police have finally learnt that the man they compared with Charles Sobhraj, a criminal known for his flamboyance, is a frail former Ayurvedic doctor with a penchant for the good old newspaper. Koul, or Bhat, is now in Srinagar Central Jail serving judicial custody. It was his love for the newspapers that finally proved to be his undoing, said an officer connected with the probe. SSP Speaks Senior Superintendent of police, Crime branch Economic Offices Wing Kashmir Abdul Waheed Shah said that they are taking the activities of this land mafia very seriously because it has been ruining lives and families. We ensure that every such complaint is investigated thoroughly so that the perpetrators of such crime are brought to justice. When a family buys a piece of land, they spend most of their hard earned savings. Once they are defrauded, it completely ruins that entire family, he said. We are taking strict action against the brokers as well as any officials involved in such frauds. We have been focused on exposing these fraudsters and dismantling their networks. Our law enforcement also helps raise awareness among public to stay vigilant against such fraud.

articleTitle: Justice Jalan recuses himself from hearing Gymkhana Club’s plea against eviction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Gymkhana Club (Image: Wikimedia Commons)
description: Delhi High Court Justice Prateek Jalan recused himself from the Delhi Gymkhana Club eviction case, citing concerns over his own judgement.
body_raw: Delhi High Court judge, Justice Prateek Jalan, on Wednesday recused himself from hearing a civil suit over the Centres proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club for its eviction from the 27.3-acre premises on Safdarjung Road. I am going to recuse myself from this matter. I would be more comfortable if somebody else hears this, Justice Jalan orally remarked. There are matters where one does not trust ones own judgement. There is too much personal involved, he said without elaborating, reported PTI. Justice Jalan directed that the lawsuit by the Delhi Gymkhana Club Ltd Staff Welfare Association be listed before another bench on Friday. Several suits have been filed challenging a May 22 notice by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs MoHUA, initiating re-entry in the Club premises in the heart of Lutyens Delhi. The Centre, invoking Clause 4 of the perpetual lease deed that allows such re-entry by the government, had stated that the land is critically required for strengthening and securing of defence infrastructure and other vital public security purposes. In May, Justice Avneesh Jhingan had issued summons in the suit while refusing any interim relief by staying the governments proceedings against the Club. The government had assured the court that no eviction shall be undertaken at the Club without adhering to due process of law. Apart from seeking re-entry through the conditions of the lease deed, the Union government has also initiated eviction proceedings against the Club under the Public Premises Act.

articleTitle: ‘They have come for me’: Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh ‘detained by ICE agents’ at US airport
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arafat sheikh
description: Arfat grew up in the Valley and moved to the US as a student in 2019. As per a campaign seeking his release, he filed for asylum in 2020 and has been living in Virginia.
body_raw: A Kashmiri-born filmmaker, Arfat Sheikh, has allegedly been detained by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement ICE agents in the United States. Sheikhs film, Saffron Kingdom, has won several awards at American film festivals, and his storytelling is widely acclaimed. In a statement, filmmaker Tara Dorabji, who was accompanying Sheikh, said they were travelling together from San Francisco International Airport to Dulles on September 24. When we landed at Dulles, I was sitting towards the back of the plane, and Arfat exited before me. As I got off the plane, I walked by Arfat, without realising that he had been pulled aside on the jetway. Dorabji says that Arfat called out to her, and as she turned around, he was surrounded by numerous men. Arfat said to me, Tara, Tara. This is ICE. They have come for me. The men were in plain clothes and not wearing any uniforms that indicated that they were federal agents. During the entire interaction, I never saw any of the men present a warrant or say why they were taking Arfat. They took Arfat Sheikh off the jetway onto the tarmac. He did not resist. I was shaking and could barely move, she claimed. Dorabji is an author and filmmaker. Her documentary film series on human rights defenders in Kashmir won awards at more than a dozen film festivals in Asia and the US. The two were on their way to Washington, DC, for the Art as Resistance event at Busboys and Poets. A campaign to free Arfat has been launched by friends and acquaintances. In her statement, Dorabji emphasised that Arfat dedicated his life to speaking truth and defending human rights He is one of the kindest and most courageous people I know. He came to the United States legally as a film student to share about the human rights atrocities in Kashmir. She also talked about his film, Saffron Kingdom, created as a form of collective memory and truth-telling to tell the story of his people. It is devastating that someone who spent years bringing stories of human rights violations in war-torn regions to international audiences is in ICE detention, facing the conditions Arfat has dedicated his life to end, she said. The 42-year-old filmmaker is the son of Ghulam Nabi Sheikh, a celebrated Kashmiri folk singer. Sheikh died in 2003 from falling off a train when he was travelling from Jammu to Delhi with his daughter. Over the years, the family has called the official version of the events surrounding his death into question. Arfat grew up in the Valley and moved to the US as a student in 2019. As per the campaign, he filed for asylum in 2020 and has been living in Alexandria, Virginia.

articleTitle: In Andhra, poll officers told to make videos of voter recertification exercise
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The ECI has also said that anyone whose name is left out during or after SIR, including young and first-time voters, can apply for inclusion through continuous updation.
description: Authorities said this was meant to ensure transparency, with the CEO also directing DEOs to keep their social media handles active and post at least two photos and two videos each day.
body_raw: Andhra Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Vivek Yadav has asked District Election Officers to post photos and videos of the re-verification of Absentee, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others ASDDO category electors, officials said - a development that comes as election officials embark on an exercise to re-verify the status of the electors not included in the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision process. According to officials, DEOs have been asked to record photos and videos of BLOs testimonials during the door-to-door re-verification exercise, as well as those of young and first-time voters, and voters whose names were deleted from the draft rolls but eventually added after the notice phase. Testimonials relating to claims, objections and the notice phase, videos of Electoral Registration Officers EROs briefing BLOs, and those of DEOs campaigns in colleges for first-time voters are also to be recorded. Authorities said this was meant to ensure transparency, with the CEO also directing DEOs to keep their social media handles active and post at least two photos and two videos each day. The posts must tag the CEO and the ECI, mention the names of polling stations, the Assembly constituency and district, and carry the tagline No eligible voter is left out. The CEO said that from October 8, BLOs will conduct door-to-door visits with lists of electors who were not included in the draft roll for verification. The lists include 44,89,512 electors who were not found at their given addresses during the enumeration phase from June 15 to July 24 this year, as well as another 1,73,071 electors found ineligible during the notice phase. Eligible voters whose names were inadvertently left out will be facilitated to submit Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls. The final roll will be published on October 16. Any voter left out of the final October 16 roll and voters becoming newly eligible to vote can submit Form 6, the office of the chief electoral officer said.

articleTitle: UPSC Essentials | Daily subject-wise quiz : Science and Technology MCQs on neutrino, pneumonic plague and more (Week 183)
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Essentials | Daily subject-wise quiz : Science and Technology
description: Are you preparing for UPSC CSE Prelims 2027? Check your progress and revise your topics through this quiz on Science and Technology.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative of subject-wise quizzes. These quizzes are designed to help you revise some of the most important topics from the static part of the syllabus. Attempt todays subject quiz onScience and Technologyto check your progress. As we mark the 3rd anniversary of the UPSC Essentials magazine, we thank our readers for being part of this journey. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. Share your views and suggestions in the comment box or write to us at manas.srivastavaindianexpress.com. QUESTION 1 With reference to the neutrino, consider the following statements 1. It is a subatomic particle with no electric charge and almost no mass. 2. Exploding stars can produce enormous numbers of neutrinos. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance It covers the basic properties and astrophysical sources of neutrinos, an important topic in particle physics. It helps understand the role of neutrino observations in studying otherwise difficult-to-detect cosmic phenomena. Explanation - Francis Halzen has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. - A neutrino is a subatomic particle with no electric charge and almost no mass. The Nobel Prize official release calls it the shyest particle in the universe, because it passes through matter almost without a trace. Every second, 65 billion neutrinos from the Sun pass through our bodies, and we do not notice. Hence, statement 1 is correct. - Neutrinos are produced in enormous numbers by the Sun, exploding stars, nuclear reactions and radioactive decay. The same processes also produce protons, but because protons carry electric charge, their paths change by the time scientists can study them. Neutrinos interact so little with the world around them that studying the particles can give scientists a window into the processes that created them. Hence, statement 2 is correct. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 2 The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 has been awarded for a the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. b the development of metalorganic frameworks. c the discovery and synthesis of quantum dots. d the development of asymmetric organocatalysis. Relevance The question covers a significant recent development in chemistry and scientific research, linked to the Nobel Prize. It tests awareness of recent Nobel Prize-winning scientific discoveries and their broader applications. Explanation - The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 has been awarded to Henri B Kagan and Kenso Soai for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. - The scientists work led to the creation of a way to produce more of one type of molecules and less of its mirror image in chemical reactions where the product was the same as the catalysis, the agent causing the reaction. - The Nobel Prizes official press release explains chiral molecules using the example of a lock and key. Imagine making a key for a lock, only to discover that your manufacturing process produces two keys that are mirror images of each other. They look almost identical, but only one fits the lock. The other may do nothing - or, in some cases, cause damage. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 3 With reference to the pneumonic plague, consider the following statements 1. The pneumonic plague is caused by bacteria. 2. Pneumonic plague is primarily transmitted through the bite of infected fleas, in the same manner as bubonic plague. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question helps understand the causative agent and modes of transmission of different forms of plague. It tests the ability to distinguish between pneumonic and bubonic plague based on their transmission mechanisms. Explanation - Hundreds have been quarantined after a 28-year-old laboratory technician reportedly died of pneumonic plague in the Siberian region of Irkutsk in Russia, according to Moscow Times report. - The pneumonic plague is caused by bacteria. Pneumonic plague generally requires close exposure to respiratory droplets from an infected person, and person-to-person spread is much less common. Hence, statement 1 is correct. - Pneumonic plague is primarily acquired through inhalation of respiratory droplets from an infected person or animal with pneumonic plague. Flea bites are the principal route associated with bubonic plague, not primary pneumonic transmission. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. - Antibiotics are effective against plague bacteria when given promptly. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 4 Consider the following statements regarding TAPAS-1, recently launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket 1. It is a commercial thermal infrared imaging payload developed by an Indian private startup. 2. It was carried into Low Earth Orbit as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. 3. It is designed primarily for weather forecasting and atmospheric monitoring. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question links with Earth-observation technologies, thermal infrared imaging and satellite applications. It tests awareness of SpaceX rideshare missions, Low Earth Orbit and emerging space-based imaging capabilities. Explanation - Minutes after midnight in India on Thursday, a partially reusable Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. This was the second of three space launches completed by Elon Musks SpaceX in a 13-hour window on October 1, a remarkable third triple-header from the company in the last two and a half years. - Among the 130 payloads on the flight was TAPAS-1, Indias first commercial private thermal-imaging payload, developed by Ahmedabad-based space technology startup Satleo Labs. - The Thermal Access Platform for Analytics Solutions TAPAS is a thermal infrared camera developed over a period of about 12 months by Satleo, a company founded in Ahmedabad in 2023 by spacetech entrepreneur Shravan Singh Bhati, retired ISRO scientist Dr Ranendu Ghosh, and sales and business development strategist Urmil Bakhai. Hence, statement 1 is correct. - TAPAS-1 is a CubeSat-category payload, which are a class of cubical nanosatellites that typically measure 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm-roughly the size of a Rubiks Cube-and are built using modular units and commercial components that are acquired off the shelf. - LEOs can be at altitudes between 160 km and 2,000 km above the surface of the Earth, and TAPAS-1 has been injected into an orbit 500 km high, from where the satellite will capture high-resolution images of heat and temperature variations at locations across the planet. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - TAPAS-1 has been designed to capture changes in the heat emitted from the Earths surface in the form of images. This data can be analysed using artificial intelligence AI, Bhati, the CEO of Satleo, told The Indian Express. Hence, statement 3 is not correct. Therefore, option b is the correct answer. QUESTION 5 The LDCT low-dose computed tomography is used to determine a The presence of early-stage lung cancer b The functioning of the hearts electrical conduction system c The blood glucose level and insulin response d The bone mineral density and risk of osteoporosis Relevance The question covers the application of Low-Dose Computed Tomography LDCT in modern medical diagnosis and screening. It helps distinguish LDCT from other diagnostic techniques based on their medical applications. Explanation - Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer deaths in India. In 2024, it accounted for 10.9 of all cancer deaths, or 98,687 deaths, up from 75,031 in 2022, when it ranked fourth. - Between 2022 and 2024, new lung cancer cases increased from 81,748, or 5.8 of all cancer cases, to 1.12 lakh, or 7.2, taking it from fourth to third place in terms of incidence. Mortality, meanwhile, increased from 8.2 of all cancer deaths to 10.9, shows the latest data from Global Cancer Observatory, a cancer statistics platform maintained by the World Health Organisations International Agency for Research on Cancer IARC. - But lung cancer is a disease that is not usually screened for - and has no easy way to screen for - it is usually diagnosed when it has already spread. We have seen that 93 of all the lung cancer cases are diagnosed in advanced stages, said Dr Abhishek Shankar, who was one of the authors of a perspective on lung cancer screening published by the IARC in September. - When diagnosed in late stages, the likelihood of surviving five years with lung cancer is just 7 to 18. This can increase to 80 if the disease is detected in the first stage. LDCT low-dose computed tomography based lung cancer screening can reduce the mortality from lung cancer by treating the disease at an early stage. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. articleTitle: Delhi High Court orders filing of complaint, probe against 6 CBI officers over false statement in court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi HC CBI perjury case
description: The Delhi High Court found a preliminary case against the six officers: Sushil Dewan, Vineet Vinayak, Prem Kumar Gautam, Amit Kumar, Md Azad and Raman Tyagi.
body_raw: The Delhi High Court, having found a preliminary case of perjury, has directed a Central Bureau of Investigation CBI court to file a complaint against six officers of the probing agency and initiate a magisterial inquiry. The officers have been accused of making a false statement in court in 2016 on correspondence with the government in relation to the discharge of IRS officer Ashok Aggarwal in a separate case. Aggarwal was chargesheeted in a disproportionate assets case in 2002 and discharged in 2016 on the ground that the sanction to prosecute him was invalid. Following his discharge, Aggarwal had requested the trial court to permit release of documents that were seized during the investigation, including those relied and not relied upon by the prosecution. However, on August 2, 2016, the CBI filed a reply, submitting that though it has no objection to the return of the documents not relied upon, it opposed the release of other documents. The CBI had stated that the correspondence with the administrative Ministry with respect to further legal action in the matter was underway and that it would not be prudent to return the seized documents as they might be required in further legal proceedings. Aggarwal then moved the trial court with an application seeking initiation of perjury proceedings, alleging that the reply was factually incorrect as no actual correspondence with the administrative Ministry was then underway. The trial court had dismissed it. Justice Madhu Jain, in an order on Tuesday, overturned the trial courts decision. The Delhi HC found a preliminary case against the six officers Sushil Dewan, Vineet Vinayak, Prem Kumar Gautam, Amit Kumar, Md Azad and Raman Tyagi. Sushil Dewan prepared, incorporated and filed the altered statement, Vineet Vinayak is prima facie connected with its handwritten introduction and final approval, Prem Kumar Gautam, Amit Kumar and Md Azad possessed knowledge of the earlier position and participated in processing the draft whereas Raman Tyagis recorded role is related to processing the final reply, the court observed. In view of the individual roles . the successive drafts and file-notings, considered cumulatively, prima facie indicate that each concerned officer, to the extent attributed to him, participated in the preparation, alteration, vetting, processing, approval or filing of the reply dated 02.08.2016 with knowledge of the actual position. The difference in the nature and degree of their respective participation does not warrant the exclusion of any officer at the stage of directing a complaint, their precise knowledge and culpability are matters for determination by the competent Court, Justice Jain reasoned. Noting that there is a reasonable foundation in the contemporaneous record for the allegations levelled under IPC Section 191 read with 193 false statement and forgery and 209 dishonestly making a false claim in court against the officers concerned, the court opined that an inquiry into the aforesaid alleged offences is expedient in the interests of justice.

articleTitle: Zero sugar, zero gluten, zero lactose – what fuelled Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar putting in the hard yards with his physio Ramneesh Vohra. (Instagram & Special Arrangement)
description: Veteran seamer last played for India four years ago but always had the drive for excellence, which prompted him to make big sacrifices to regain swing, which had been his hallmark in his heyday
body_raw: I want to be like that again. Will it be possible? A few months had passed in calm silence. Bhuvneshwar Kumar and his physio Ramneesh Vohra had not let their association be disrupted by the snub that struck him 12 days after Indias 2022 T20 World Cup semi-final exit. He was taken off the national radar after a New Zealand tour. His 37 T20I wickets in 2022 remain the most by an Indian man in a calendar year. We met regularly but never had a word about it for almost 2-3 months, Ramneesh, a BCCI-qualified physiotherapist, tells The Indian Express from his clinic in Noida. We never discussed what went wrong. Bhuvneshwars stillness was perplexing, even for Ramneesh. His thoughts finally came out in the open one morning. I want to be like that again, Bhuvneshwar told Ramneesh. He pointed to a mobile screen that replayed the booming in-swingers that rattled Pakistans Nasir Jamshed and Mohammad Hafeez on his T20I and ODI debuts in December 2012 on a loop. That was 10 years earlier. The confidence had undeniably taken a hit. Could he bend the ball to his will again? Will it be possible? he asked Ramneesh. Bhuvneshwar wasnt searching for swing to wear the India blues again. He just wanted to enjoy and give his best no matter where he played. The chat was all about that, Ramneesh recalls. The hard yards put in, alongside Bhuvneshwars personal trainer Surya Yadav, helped the veteran seamer complete a circle on Tuesday. At 36, he found himself back in the T20I squad for Indias New Zealand tour, the country where he played his last international game in November 22. The platform was laid by two victorious IPL seasons with Royal Challengers Bengaluru RCB. Nerve-less control in the Powerplay and at the death yielded him 45 wickets at a sub-9 economy, the best among all pacers in the league over that period. Ramneesh first crossed paths with Bhuvneshwar during the COVID lockdown at a Noida academy in 2020. Suryas technical inputs came in about four years later. He never wanted to increase pace. He only wanted to regain his swing. We first put in work to help regain that swinging capacity. The technical aspects were handled by Surya. I would handle his joints, which had to be opened up first. Only then could he proceed to strengthening, do functional activities and later enter game-pattern activities. His priority was to get his foot landing at the crease like in 2012, when his contact was on his toe and not the entire back foot, says Ramneesh. The transformation was in full flight during RCBs triumphant Playoffs run in May. Two near-140 kph deliveries froze Shubman Gill and Sai Sudharsan, Bhuvneshwar getting them with his rejuvenated bouncer and nip-backer. Earlier, he used to be a bowler, like many others. Now, he can run a marathon if he wants, Ramneesh says proudly. Hard yards The sacrifices were big but not impossible for Bhuvneshwar, who, according to Ramneesh, has had no fun activities or parties outside cricket. Zero sugar, zero gluten and zero lactose for the last six years. He has shed fat from his visceral organs. Thats the main thing. He weighed 80 kg earlier, with 22-25 percent body fat. Now at 75 kg and 16 percent body fat, Bhuvneshwar has improved his muscle mass. Thats the beauty when you develop a bond with an athlete, Ramneesh adds. The two have transcended the player-doctor relationship to brothers and neighbours in the same society of the city. We strictly keep our work off social media and often train at my home or his, he says. Ashish Winston Zaidi raves about Bhuvneshwars comeback. Zaidi, a former Uttar Pradesh seamer, retired in 2006, a year before Bhuvneshwars debut. The two later caught up regularly during the UPT20 league. In 2009, Zaidis straight talk was Bhuvneshwars greatest counsel, a day before he dismissed Sachin Tendulkar for his only duck in the Ranji Trophy and burst to fame before the IPL. Maine bola usse Tendulkar jaan thodi ley lega I told him Tendulkar wasnt going to kill him. He was a nervous teenager then but a very mature cricketer now, recounts Zaidi. He made a mistake somewhere trying to increase pace. Moving back to swing, and line and length have helped his comeback. His bowling amazed me this season. Nowadays, a lot of boys are bowling quick but have no swing. If you look at the batting tracks today, if you dont have swing or movement, you are in trouble, the former cricketer says. Ramneesh recalls only one instance of Bhuvneshwar expressing disappointment over his exit from the national team in late 2022, when Bhuvi sir arrived as the chief guest on his revamped clinics inauguration. Someone asked him why he got the keeper up to the stumps during that Adelaide T20 World Cup semifinal against England. He said that it wasnt his call and the decision didnt go well. He always used to say, I dont want to think about it or its consequences. I am not doing anything to get somewhere. But he got himself somewhere on Tuesday. Back in an India shirt, with the avenues opening up further as they enter a 50-over World Cup year. 37 Bhuvneshwars T20I wickets in 2022 are still the most for an Indian man in a calendar year. 45 Bhuvneshwar is the highest wicket-taker in the IPL since 2025. 105 T20I matches Bhuvneshwar would have missed by the start of the New Zealand tour, the most for an Indian between two appearances. 363 Bhuvneshwar is the highest wicket-taker among Indian pacers in all T20s

articleTitle: SIR row leaves young voters divided: Some doubt electoral process, others says trust intact
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Not all young voters, however, see the controversy as enough reason to lose faith in elections themselves.
description: SIR controversy has divided young Indian voters, with some questioning election fairness while others continue to trust the Election Commission and electoral process.
body_raw: Written by Sameer Anasingaraju The controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls and the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar have left young voters divided over their confidence in Indias electoral system. While some Gen Z voters say the developments have deepened doubts about the fairness of elections, others believe the controversy stems partly from a lack of understanding of the purpose of SIR and say their faith in the electoral process remains intact. For some, however, the current controversy has only reinforced doubts that already existed. An investigation by The Indian Express has revealed that 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written emails to bring to note decisions taken without their approval with regards to centralisation of ECINET portal, changes in Form 6, and other issues. Pratik Agarwal, 23, who recently completed his MBA in Sports Management, has a contrasting view. He said his trust in the electoral process has not reduced and argued that young people should understand why SIR was introduced before forming an opinion about it. My trust hasnt been reduced at all, because people need to understand why the SIR was implemented. Most of the youth do not know and they are just getting influenced by the Cockroach Janta Party CJP supporting content creators. SIR was implemented to delete dead, duplicate, migrated, or fake voters from the list. The ECI is responsible for making sure every valid citizen of India gets to vote and they are doing that, he added. For 22-year-old political science student graduate Nikhil Kumar, however, the controversy has made it harder to maintain confidence in the electoral process. Yes, my confidence has gone down, because its hard not to doubt with everything happening. If our votes are taken before we even start, what kind of democracy is left for us? Kumar said. My trust in free and fair elections was gone long before the SIR and CEC controversy, this just confirmed it, said Rohan Shinde, 21. Sharwari Potdar, 23, described the issue as more complicated, saying that both the functioning of the Election Commission and the SIR process have raised questions for her. It is quite a tricky situation. For a layman like me, this entire SIR is also quite confusing, Potdar said. She also expressed concern over voters being removed from electoral rolls. Valid voters are getting deleted. This is not right. Not all young voters, however, see the controversy as enough reason to lose faith in elections themselves. My trust in the elections is still resolute, as at the end of the day the votes are counted by the EVMs, said 19-year-old Mehek Yadav. I do not think they have been tampered with, and the opposition is only raising SIR issues as the government seems vulnerable after the recent CJP protests. For Gen Z, the debate over SIR appears to have raised more questions than it has answered. While some young voters continue to place faith in the Election Commission and the electoral process, others say the recent controversies have made them question whether every eligible vote will be protected. With young voters forming an increasingly important part of the electorate, how they perceive the credibility and transparency of the election process could have wider implications for public trust in Indian democracy.

articleTitle: Plague scare in Russia, tourism season in Goa, and a screening demand from opposition leader
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The tourism season in the coastal state officially commenced last week with the arrival of the first charter flight from Russia’s Yekaterinburg, carrying 162 passengers to Goa.
description: In Goa, which sees a significant number of Russian tourists, the development has sparked concerns.
body_raw: With the death of a 28-year-old laboratory worker in Russias Irkutsk region in Siberia sparking public health concerns about pneumonic plague during Goas tourist season, the states Opposition Leader has called for health screening of all tourists arriving in the coastal state from Russia. This comes as Goas tourist season kicks off, with the first batch of international tourists arriving last week. A woman working at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East died of plague last week. While 200 people who came into contact with her have now been quarantined, Russian authorities claim the worker died on October 2 of pneumonia of an as-yet-unestablished origin, and that there is no risk of an epidemic breaking out. In Goa, which sees a significant number of Russian tourists, the development has sparked concerns. On Wednesday, Congress leader Yuri Alemao, the Leader of Opposition in the Goa Assembly, said the government must immediately introduce precautionary health screening for tourists from Russia. The remarks come a day after the World Health Organization WHO sought more information on the death from Russia, saying that timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks. I demand surveillance for passengers arriving from Russia, in coordination with Central health authorities. Tourism is vital to Goa, but public health and the safety of Goans must come first. Prevention is always better than crisis management, said Alemao in a post on X. Alemao said the government cannot afford complacency regarding concerns after the death of the laboratory worker in Russia. With regular charter flights now bringing tourists from Russia to Goa, I demand the government immediately introduce precautionary health screening, he said. For his part, Kedar Naik, the Goa governments director of tourism, said the department is yet to receive any advisory from the WHO or any other health organisation regarding the issue. As of now, the tourist season is going well. We are welcoming all the tourists to Goa. There is no concern since we have not received any advisory from the WHO or any other organisation. If the health regulators issue any advisory in this regard, we will look into it and accordingly initiate corrective measures, Naik said. The tourism season in the coastal state officially commenced last week with the arrival of the first charter flight from Russias Yekaterinburg, carrying 162 passengers to Goa. Another charter with 285 passengers from Moscow arrived on October 4. After the arrival of the first charter flight from Russia on September 30, Tourism Minister Rohan Khaunte said the tourism departments approach is to strengthen the traditional source markets such as Russia and the UK, while simultaneously widening Goas international footprint. As connectivity grows, we also want international travellers to discover more of Goa.our heritage, culture, wellness, nature, cuisine, spirituality and the diverse experiences that lie beyond our beaches. Our focus is on building Goa as a better-connected, responsible and year-round global destination, Khaunte had said.

articleTitle: 22-year-old victim of Chhattisgarh acid attack may lose vision
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Balod acid attack
description: The woman suffered severe burn injuries on her face and hand, including deep wounds on her right cheek and right eye, which is likely to lead to a complete loss of vision.
body_raw: A 22-year-old woman was the victim of an acid attack in Chhattisgarhs Balod district after she spurned the attackers requests to marry him. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon, when the victim, who was preparing for competitive exams, was returning home from the library. The attackers, Yash Kumar Sonkar and his friend Karan Kunjam, waylaid the woman and threw acid on her face before fleeing. The woman suffered severe burn injuries on her face and hand, including deep wounds on her right cheek and right eye, which is likely to lead to a complete loss of vision. The woman has suffered injuries on her face and both eyes. Her right eye is badly affected. She has a total of 8 per cent burn injuries on her body. She will recover, but the vision in her right eye will take time to restore. At present, she does not have vision in her right eye, said a doctor who wished to remain anonymous. The incident, purportedly the first acid attack in Balod, sparked outrage in the region, and in a swift response, police traced and arrested within just eight hours both the 20-year-old accused and his aide, also 20. Their heads were also tonsured before the duo was paraded to the court complex. There, a mob, mostly women, sat, gheraoing the complex and awaiting them. Some held placards and shouted slogans, demanding justice for the victim and capital punishment for the attackers. Harshita Sahu, a childhood friend of the victim, said, We want immediate hanging of the accused. Now, this has happened with someones daughter, and tomorrow, can happen to anyones daughter. Such an incident acid attack has occurred for the first time in the history of Balod. We will not rest till they get capital punishment. Another girl, Vidya Sahu, a BA student, told the media, She was our colleague. She was innocent and has done nothing wrong. Till now, no woman here has ever been attacked with acid. This has happened for the first time. During the investigation, Sonkar told the police that he knew the victim and had requested her to marry him. However, when she refused his many attempts, the man plotted to carry out an acid attack with the help of his school friend Kunjam. The two bought the acid on September 27 and had planned to carry out the attack during the Ganesh immersion procession. However, the tight security arrangements on the day dissuaded them from carrying it out. Later, on October 5, they waylaid the woman and attacked her. She was first rushed to a local hospital and subsequently shifted to DKS super-speciality hospital in Raipur.

articleTitle: ‘Some of them need a job, so they go after us’: Travis Head hits back at former Oz players
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Australia opener Travis Head in action. (Reuters)
description: Opener accuses past greats of "putting a bullet" through current team after Matthew Hayden's scathing assessment of selectors
body_raw: Australia opener Travis Head has launched a strong defence of his team and the national selectors, accusing former players turned critics of putting a bullet through the current side ahead of the first Test against South Africa in Durban on Friday. Heads remarks came a day after Matthew Hayden, the former Australia opener, described the selectors recent picks as the greatest pile of mediocrity that weve seen in a generation of cricket. Haydens criticism, made on a podcast, was aimed at the recall of Nic Maddinson, who is back in the Test squad after nearly 10 years following injuries to Josh Inglis and Cameron Green. Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Head did not name any pundit directly but made his feelings clear. I think its unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much that put the bullet through a lot of players, which I think is unfair, he said. But thats what theyre paid to do. Some of them need a job, so they go after us, and thats totally fine. Head added that the current group was equipped to handle the scrutiny. This group is strong enough to deal with those sorts of things. Thats how it is. Its unfortunate sometimes to have some of that feedback from a generation of players that we have huge respect for, but thats the caper. Hayden had accused the selectors of disrespecting first-class cricket, arguing that batters should average 45 or more before being considered for Test selection. Maddinson, 34, carries a first-class average of 37.11. Head, however, backed the decision to bring in an experienced campaigner. We need mature guys that know what they need to be doing, he said. And I think that revolves back to why weve been so good over a period of time and why Australian cricket was so good back then in that era, because youd bring in the Mike Husseys of the world, who are 30, who are tried and tested and know what they need to do. Former Australia captain Allan Border also weighed in, suggesting that Head, 32, would face his toughest challenge as an opener against the South African attack and might be better suited to batting at number five. Head brushed that aside too. I have laughed at a fair bit of it because if a traditional opening batter had pushed out the same sort of numbers in his first 20 innings, I think hed be pretty safe and not talked about in the way that it has been talked about, he said. Its a lot of headline stuff.
