description: “The building measured 225 sq ft. Some people have been rescued and sent to hospitals, but we suspect that two to three people are still trapped under the debris. They are talking... rescue operation is underway,” DCP R P Meena said.
body_raw: A pregnant woman and two children were killed and eight people, including a three-year-old, injured after a four-storey building collapsed in Northeast Delhis New Seemapuri on Wednesday afternoon, trapping people under the rubble. On Tuesday, when Delhi experienced earthquake tremors in the evening, the building had developed cracks, officials said. Within minutes of the collapse, residents started pulling people out of the rubble and took them to hospitals. Among those who rushed between the collapse site and hospitals looking for their loved ones was Reshma 24. She was looking for her younger sister Gulfisha 22, who was four months pregnant. Gulfisha had been walking through E Block with her four-year-old daughter Zoya when the building came crashing down around 3.10 pm. Her father received a call from Gulfisha after the collapse. She told him she was stuck under rocks. And she cant breathe, Reshma said. Reshma rushed to Rajiv Gandhi Hospital after being told that Gulfisha had been taken there. At the hospital, they say she is here at the collapse site. I came back, she said. Gulfisha was later identified as the pregnant woman who died. The identity of the two deceased children, one of whom is 12-years-old, had not been established by Wednesday evening. Zoya was among those initially feared trapped. Another one trapped was Hazra Khatun 42. She had been taking a walk near the building when it collapsed. She was just taking a walk here. Then I heard that a building had collapsed. When she didnt return, I came here, Haseena, her daughter, said. The collapse took place near the Idgah Machhli Mandi area. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot. The building measured 225 sq ft. Some people have been rescued and sent to hospitals, but we suspect that two to three people are still trapped under the debris. They are talking. rescue operation is underway, DCP R P Meena said. In a statement, the MCD described the structure as a ground-plus-three-floor building located in a jhuggi jhopri area on about 25 square yards of DUSIB land. It said the building was around 20-25 years old and occupied. The building stood next to the mosque in the densely packed locality. The boundary wall of the mosque also collapsed in the impact, while walls of an adjoining building were damaged, the MCD added.Officials said demolition work was being carried out in the adjoining building. Three- and four-storey structures surround the mosque on three sides, leaving little open space. Much of the debris fell inside the mosque compound, said local residents. The building was owned by Anwar. His family members who stayed on the first three floors included his wife Salma 50 son Rehman 28 and wife Sakeena his daughters Nushrat and Ameena as well as Nushrats three-year-old son Abdaan. While Anwar, Ameena and Rehmans wife were not at home when the building collapsed, Nushrat is stuck under the debris, officials said. A tenant, also named Sakeena 35, lived on the upper floor, according to relatives. Ameena said the family had moved into the house around four months ago. My father has a junk shop on the ground floor, while my brother has another shop in a lane almost half a kilometre away. All of them were inside the house when it collapsed, she said.

articleTitle: Firing distance raised suspicion: How an ‘accidental’ shooting in Lonavala turned into a murder case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: accidental shooting in Lonavala, Lonavala accidental shooting, Lonavala police murder case, Motiram Marathe arrested, Advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, Lonavala lawyer shooting, Bhushi village property dispute, Hotel Motiram Lonavala, Sassoon Hospital post mortem, Sandeep Singh Gill SP, Lonavala city police station, family property dispute murder, 12 bore gun shooting Lonavala
description: Lonavala City police have arrested Motiram Marathe for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, at Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village on Monday.
body_raw: A shooting initially reported as an accidental firing at a hotel in Lonavala turned into a murder investigation after the post-mortem examination found that the bullet had been fired from a distance of around 30 centimetres, police said. The investigation subsequently revealed a property dispute between the deceased and his 83-year-old grandfather, who later allegedly confessed to shooting him. Lonavala City police have arrested Motiram Marathe for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, at Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village on Monday. Police have also booked four other family members for allegedly attempting to destroy evidence and conceal the crime. Family initially claimed accidental firing According to police, Motiram, who holds a valid licence for a 12-bore rifle that he used for hunting, was at the hotel when the incident took place. Motiram Marathe holds a valid arms licence for a 12-bore gun, which he used for hunting. The family said that the incident took place on Monday. They told police that Abhay was cleaning his grandfathers gun when the trigger was accidentally pulled and a bullet hit him in the chest, Superintendent of Police Sandeep Singh Gill said at a press conference on Tuesday. Lonavala City police initially registered the case as an accidental death after reaching the spot. However, officers began to suspect that the familys account did not match the circumstances at the scene. Police examined the firearm, the injury to Abhays chest and the bloodstains on the wall, and sent the body to Sassoon Hospital for a post-mortem examination. The post-mortem findings further raised suspicion. Police said doctors found that the bullet had been fired from a distance of around 30 centimetres, making the claim of an accidental firing while cleaning the rifle difficult to establish. Property dispute emerges during probe As part of the investigation, police questioned family members as well as the hotel manager and staff. They found that Abhay and his grandfather had been involved in a dispute over land and its development. Motiram wanted to sell their land and distribute the money among family members however, Abhay had different plans for the land development, which led to the dispute, Gill said. Gill said the nature of the firearm also added to the suspicion. Also, a 12-bore rifle, which is around 4 to 4.5 feet long, so using it to fire towards self is difficult. So the suspicion increased. Even when inquired with the hotel staff and manager, they also said that for quite some time there have been quarrels between the two regarding financial and land-related matters, he said. Police said the two were at the restaurant counter of Hotel Motiram around 11 am on Monday when they had a heated argument. During the argument, Motiram allegedly took his licensed 12-bore rifle and shot Abhay in the chest. The bullet proved fatal. Police said the two had a history of disagreements over land and financial matters. Police allege attempt to destroy evidence The investigation also led police to suspect an attempt to cover up the shooting. According to Gill, CCTV cameras near the spot were allegedly removed and the DVR containing the footage was taken away. Police also alleged that hotel staff were threatened against speaking about the incident. The body was displaced to a different location and even the weapons were taken away to a different location. So we have booked five of the family members, Gill said. Police said that while it was initially difficult to determine whether the shooting was accidental or deliberate because family members maintained that it was an accidental firing, the post-mortem findings and subsequent investigation strengthened the murder suspicion. Police said Motiram later confessed to the crime. Initially the family members denied but the accused Motiram confessed to the crime. The three family members-Motiram Marathe, Hiraman Motiram Marathe, and Manoj Hiraman Marathe-have been granted police custody till October 12, Sachin Patil, senior police inspector, Lonavala City police station, told The Indian Express. Police have also booked Kavita Hiraman Marathe and Rajashree Dashrath Pawar, sister of Hiraman Marathe. Marathe familys business political links Abhay was the son of Manik Marathe, a former councillor of the Lonavala municipal council. The Marathe family owns Hotel Motiram and Manik Moti in Bhushi village and is involved in the beer bar business. The family also runs a petrol pump in Lonavala, according to people familiar with the family. Macchindra Kharade, former Shiv Sena Pune district chief and a close associate of Manik Marathe, said the family had been living together for several years. The Marathe family has always been involved in business. Motiram Marathe has three sons and a daughter-Rajashree, Hiraman, Manik, and Ratan, the youngest son. All the family members, even Motirams brother, used to live together. It was rare to see such a huge joint family still living together, Kharade said. He said Manik had been active in local politics while also managing the family businesses. According to Kharade, Manik had contested the Lonavala municipal council election on an NCP ticket in 2011 and later won as a Shiv Sena candidate in 2016. He contested the 2025 election from Shiv Sena UBT but was defeated. Ratan is currently the Bhushi ward chief of Shiv Sena UBT, Kharade said. Though Manik had been in politics, he had limited presence as he also used to manage family businesses. Abhay was married and also used to help in their family business. And it was shocking for Lonavala residents that such an incident had happened, Kharade said. A tea stall owner in Lonavala said, The Marathe family had been prominent in the area for several decades and had also been associated with religious and community activities during the annual Kanifnath Maharaj yatra held in Lonavala during Rangpanchami.

articleTitle: Microsoft, Nvidia unveil new AI PCs with RTX Spark chip at San Francisco event
articleFeaturedImageAlt: microsoft, Nvidia, Microsoft unveil new AI PCs with RTX Spark chip, Nvidia unveil new AI PCs with RTX Spark chip, Nvidia unveil new AI PCs, Microsoft unveil new AI PCs, Nvidia’s RTX Spark chipset, Satya Nadella, Jensen Huang, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was joined by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on stage alongside Windows and Devices head Pavan Davuluri.
body_raw: Microsoft launched a new class of Windows-powered laptops featuring Nvidias RTX Spark chipset, in an effort to take on Apple Inc.s MacBook Pros. The new laptops are aimed at developers and creators who want high-end machines capable of running demanding AI workloads locally rather than in the cloud. At an event on Wednesday in San Francisco, Microsoft and Nvidia unveiled a new category of laptops, headlined by the new Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark, alongside new features in Windows 11 that leverage the new system chips capabilities. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was joined by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on stage alongside Windows and Devices head Pavan Davuluri. It took more than 4,000 engineering years. This is a massive project. We have reinvented the personal computer. For the first time, we took all the capabilities that used to be in a gaming laptop, a workstation, a supercomputer or the cloud, unified the architecture and made it run on one superchip, Huang said. For the first time, Microsoft showed the Surface Laptop Ultra, the companys new 15-inch premium laptop featuring Nvidias RTX Spark chip. Pricing for the Ultra starts at 2,599, with up to 128 GB of unified memory. The Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a device designed for hardcore developers and creators, starts at 5,999.They, along with PCs from Asus, Dell, Lenovo, HP, and MSI will ship next Friday, October 16. The new Surface Pro Ultra has been marketed as the most powerful Windows computer designed for everything from local AI computing, creative workloads, and ray traced gaming and its all thanks to Nvidias new CPU the RTX Spark. Davuluri showed the Surface Laptop Ultra running GitHub Copilot and playing Gears of War E-Day at 60 frames per second. He said that hundreds of AAA and indie titles will be available on day one, and that Call of Duty will come to RTX Spark in 2027. The laptop has the brightest peak HDR display on a laptop, Duvuluri said. The system also features a magnetic USB-C charger called Magnetic Connect. The connector plugs in similarly to Apples MagSafe, except that it uses a standardised port. Microsoft compared the Spark with the M5 Pro in the MacBook Pro, promising performance of up to 2.1 times faster time to first token, 4.3 times faster image generation, and 6.2 times faster video generation. Microsoft gave a video demo using multiple local and cloud models across Blender, Photoshop, ComfyUI, and Unreal Engine. The demo showed a workload that took hours instead of days. Hybrid Intelligence With new high-performance laptops, Microsoft is bringing an updated Windows 11, adding new quick actions in the Search menu in the Task Bar, making quick changes to settings, taking screenshots, or arranging windows using natural language. Microsoft also pushed hybrid intelligence, which allows Copilot to access your files, take actions and use local AI models as well as those on the cloud. In this new structure, Copilot will only tap into the cloud for difficult AI tasks, while running local models to save your precious tokens. Beyond Copilot, Windows 11 will be able to host multiple AI agents locally including Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, and even Facebook Muse. Nadella describes the event as building the frontier ecosystem, centered on Agent 365, Microsoft IQ, and Copilot. Davuluri described Windows 11 as the most secure platform for AI agents, emphasisng built-in containment. The writer is in San Francisco on the invitation of Nvidia

articleTitle: 2027 first: Why Congress walked away from UP MLC polls after a year’s prep
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 2027 first: Why Congress walked away from UP MLC polls after a year’s prep
description: After months of groundwork and preparations, the Congress decided to stay out of the 11-seat contest, prioritising its alliance with the Samajwadi Party and the 2027 Assembly polls.
body_raw: After a year of preparations for the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections, the Congress has decided not to field candidates in 11 Graduate and Teachers constituencies going to polls, choosing instead to focus entirely on the 2027 Assembly elections. Newly appointed state Congress president Aradhana Misra told The Indian Express that the decision had been taken before she assumed office. The party had decided not to contest the MLC elections, keeping the 2027 Assembly elections in mind. Our focus is entirely on the Assembly polls. If those who had been preparing to contest wish to fight as independents, that is their decision. The party, however, has decided not to contest, Misra said. The elections will take place on October 23. Five Graduates constituencies - Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut and Allahabad-Jhansi - and six Teachers constituencies - Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut, Bareilly-Moradabad and Gorakhpur-Faizabad - will go to polls. A campaign already in motion The partys withdrawal comes as the nomination process has concluded. It had undertaken considerable preparations for the Council elections. In October last year, the Congress had indicated probable candidates for several seats, appointed observers and coordinators, and set up a control room. Several aspirants had begun working nearly nine months ago, when the process of preparing voter lists for these constituencies began. In these constituencies, where only registered graduates and teachers can vote, prospective candidates generally begin their campaigns well ahead of polling, helping eligible voters get enrolled and building constituency-level networks. Unlike Assembly or Lok Sabha elections, MLC elections in these constituencies are not fought on party symbols. However, candidates backed by political parties are counted as part of their respective partys electoral strength. With the Congress staying out, the contest is now largely between the BJP and Samajwadi Party, though a number of independents are also in the fray. Some within the party feel that preparations by the state unit to contest the MLC elections were not adequately coordinated with the central leadership, particularly amid discussions over organisational changes in the UP unit. With little time left before the election process, party sources said, the leadership eventually decided it was better to leave the contest to the SP. The partys calculation is that avoiding a direct contest with the SP in the Council elections will help maintain the alliance ahead of 2027 and allow it to concentrate its organisational and political resources on the larger electoral battle. Probable candidates stay in the race Several candidates who had been preparing to contest on the Congress ticket have decided to contest as independents. Arvind Singh Patel, who had been preparing to contest from the Varanasi Graduate constituency, filed his nomination on October 5. Speaking to The Indian Express, he said, I filed my nomination on October 5. Congress leaders from the district and adjoining districts accompanied me. I will not withdraw and will instead contest as an independent. I have put in a lot of effort and money into preparing for this election. October 6 was the last date for filing nominations, with 51 candidates filing their papers on the final day. The total number of nominations across the 11 Graduate and Teachers constituencies rose to 188 from 137 till October 5. Scrutiny of nominations was on October 7, while October 9 is the last date for withdrawal of candidature. The 100-member Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council currently has 10 SP members, putting the party at the 10 per cent threshold required for the Leader of the Opposition LoP post in the Upper House of the state legislature. The BJP-led alliance, meanwhile, has 83 members in the Council - 79 of BJP, and one each from Apna Dal S, RLD, Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, and Nishad Party - giving it a clear majority.

articleTitle: WhatsApp chats to CBI raids: How Punjab’s ‘graft network’ with CMO links unravelled
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WhatsApp chats to CBI raids: How Punjab's 'graft network' with CMO links unravelled
description: CM Mann’s OSD, a former health official, and a businessman among people CBI has booked following Punjab and Haryana High Court's directions.
body_raw: Following a directive from the Punjab and Haryana High Court to register an FIR and conduct an impartial probe into the alleged corruption network linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office, the CBI zeroed in on six individuals, including Rajbir Singh Ghuman, Manns Officer on Special Duty OSD. On Tuesday, the CBI booked Ghuman and five others in connection with the case. An FIR has been registered to investigate the allegations of corruption against OSD to Punjab Chief Minister and his associates for influencing and manipulating postings of officers including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits, the agency said in a statement. The move has triggered sharp reactions from the ruling AAP, which has accused the BJP of tarnishing Manns image by misusing central agencies ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. Mann himself on Wednesday said he was not scared of any probe. Here is a look at the six people who are under CBIs scanner and the allegations against them. Despite repeated attempts by The Indian Express, all six remained inaccessible. Rajbir Singh Ghuman Manns longtime aide Ghuman is among Manns closest aides. An engineer by qualification, he worked as an assistant professor at a private engineering college in Sangrur before joining Mann. He hails from Gharachon village, around 40 km from Manns native village Satoj. His association with Mann dates back to the Chief Ministers days as Sangrur MP and has continued even after the AAP came to power in 2022. The ED has alleged that Nitin Gohal, another of the accused, routed requests for transfers, postings and other matters through Ghuman. The OSD has denied the charges, saying Gohal is an old friend and that he would not break ties with him over fear of the ED. The High Court noted that despite being at the centre of the allegations, Ghuman was not part of the preliminary inquiry of the Punjab Bureau of Investigation. Nitin Gohal The intermediary The ED describes Gohal, who owns Fortec Web Solutions Private Limited, as a key intermediary in the alleged chain. In his statement to the agency, Gohal said he has known Ghuman for over two decades and visited his office. On being asked why he was approached for transfers and postings despite not being the competent authority, Gohal said he merely prepared lists and forwarded them to the concerned people. The ED said Gohals seized phone revealed 21 WhatsApp chats relating to transfers and postings of officials between September 2023 and March 2026. Another 11 chats were interpreted as concerned with policy formulation, departmental rule changes, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing and other government decisions. Other conversations allegedly involved land transactions, change of land use, Greater Mohali Area Development Authority GMADA approvals and property disputes. The ED also cited 11 chats which it interpreted as showing payments, kickbacks or other benefits for official favours. Jitin Gohal The Markfed link Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Nitins brother, is a Markfed manager posted in Jalandhar. His premises were searched by the CBI. Officials said he had been attached to the CMO and worked from the CMs camp office. The ED alleges Nitin facilitated Jitins placement in the CMO through Dr Mahajan and Ghuman. It cited a January 23, 2026 WhatsApp conversation, besides chats in which lists of officers and draft transfer-related material allegedly moved between the brothers. Dr Romi Raja Mahajan Retired officer with political links Dr Romi Raja Mahajan retired in September as Deputy Medical Commissioner at Gurdaspur. An MBBS doctor, he had served at Civil Hospital, Gurdaspur, before becoming Deputy Medical Commissioner. Officials said he too had been attached to the CMO. A senior bureaucrat described him as very active, saying he frequently called officials regarding transfers. The ED cited alleged communications between Mahajan and Nitin Gohal concerning postings and linked Mahajan and Ghuman to Jitin Gohals alleged placement in the CMO. Mahajan allegedly had political links across parties in Gurdaspur. He was allegedly close to former Congress MLA Sukhbans Kaur Bhinder and later served an adviser to BJP leader Swaran Salaria before differences allegedly cropped up between them. He subsequently came to know Ghuman through AAP leader Jagrup Singh Sekhwan of Qadian. Bir Devinder AAP leader Bir Devinder hails from Ballan village in Morinda and is associated with the AAP youth wing. He is known for organising the partys programmes against drugs. The ED material records Nitin Gohal saying he had known Bir Devinder since 2004 and that the duo were partners in a company. Citing a travel agents ledger, the agency also alleged that Nitin Gohal arranged air tickets and hotel accommodation for Ghuman and Devinder, with payments allegedly made in cash. R S Nagra Businessman Hailing from Patialas Nabha Road area, Nagra runs a rice-shelling business. His alleged link to the network largely runs through Nitin Gohal, who allegedly told the ED that he met Nagra in 2022-2023 through a common friend. Nitin Gohal also allegedly told the agency that following the meeting Nagra sent him requests concerning transfers and postings on WhatsApp. The ED cited requests involving officers in the police, taxation, food and civil supplies and other departments, besides references to foodgrain transport policy, tenders, licences, land and GMADA approvals. The CBI also raided premises linked to Nagra. How ED probe led CBI to them The EDs material emerged from its investigation of builder Ajay Sehgal and associates of the Indian Cooperative House Building Society. Searches of Nitin Gohals premises led to the seizure of his phone and examination of WhatsApp chats, call records and documents following which the agency sent its dossier to the Punjab DGP. The Punjab Police examined the material and issued notices but did not register an FIR. The High Court subsequently held that the material disclosed cognisable offences and ordered a CBI probe. It described the state police process as a journey with all travel and no reaching and said an FIR ought to have been registered. The CBI then registered the FIR and searched eight locations across Chandigarh and Punjab, including Manns camp office and premises in Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar. Laptops, mobile phones and documents were seized. The ED allegations remain under investigation. The CBI probe will now determine whether the personal relationships, administrative access and communications cited by the ED amount to the organised corruption network.

articleTitle: Average 73% decline in wildlife population sizes between 1970 and 2022: WWF report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: wildlife population, wildlife population sizes, wildlife population sizes decline, wildlife sizes decline, wildlife, Wildlife Protection, wildlife conservation, World Wide Fund for Nature, Indian express news, current affairs
description: There has beena 73% decline in the average population sizes of monitored vertebrates — mammals, fish, birds and amphibians — over 52 years between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) biennial Living Planet Report, 2026.
body_raw: The average size of monitored vertebrate - mammals, fish, birds and amphibians - populations declined 73 over 52 years between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature WWF biennial Living Planet Report, 2026. As part of the Living Planet Index LPI, average changes in the size of wild populations of vertebrate species are measured over time, tracking variations in relative abundance rather than absolute numbers. This means that the size of these populations fell by, on average, 73 during the assessment period, and it does not reflect the number of individual animals lost, nor the number of populations lost. Habitat loss and degradation, overexploitation of resources, climate change, impact of invasive species, pollution and disease are some of the dominant drivers of changes across ecosystems and wildlife populations, the Living Planet Report stated. The way the world produces and consumes food is the single largest driver of biodiversity loss. The food and agriculture system is the leading cause of habitat destruction, overharvesting, and a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. Even as the report noted the declining trends in wild populations, it also noted that nature can recover if society follows a clear pathway to trigger positive tipping points in the energy, food and finance systems that drive biodiversity loss. The Living Planet Report 2026 is both a stark reminder of the scale of the biodiversity crisis and a message of hope. While the Living Planet Index continues to highlight significant declines in monitored wildlife populations, the report also shows that these declines are not inevitable, said Ravi Singh, Secretary General and CEO, WWF-India. Species recoveries, including those of tigers in India and globally, demonstrate what sustained conservation action, collaboration and long-term commitment can achieve, he added. The LPI, produced by the Zoological Society of London, includes 35,803 population trends of 5,790 vertebrate species from 1970 to 2022. The strongest declines, 85, were seen in freshwater ecosystems, followed by terrestrial ecosystems, at 69 and marine ecosystems at 59. Although the overall trend is negative due to the magnitude of the declining trends, half of the populations included in the LPI are stable or increasing, WWF said. The report highlights recoveries in populations of green turtles, bluefin tuna, tigers and southern African elephants, which, it said, demonstrate that targeted conservation interventions can deliver proven results. The report noted rise in global wild tiger numbers between 2010 and 2025 - from 3,200 to around 5,700 individuals.

articleTitle: Leaked papers, cancelled government exams, no new dates: MPSC protests grow in Maharashtra
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MPSC protests continue, MPSC paper leak, MPSC protests, Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), Devendra Fadnavis government, MPSC protests intensify, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Fadnavis tries to damage control, indicates also open to change of MPSC chief. But problems with successive exams, including those held last year for which recruitment is in motion, fuel anger
body_raw: Rahul Mahale, 29, had a simple plan give the State Services Main Exam this month, write the Group-B Main in December, exit the long preparation phase finally, and end the monetary drain it caused on his parents. Then, his hopes vanished. Mahale is among the thousands of aspirants sitting for exams conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC, who have been protesting in Pune-an MPSC exam hub-since October 2. The exam that Mahale was preparing for, having passed the Prelims for the State Civil Services, has been postponed with no new dates announced, since irregularities were found in tests conducted by the MPSC. My demand is that the wrongdoers be removed, and the commission adhere to strict exam schedules and transparent conduct, Mahale says. Topping the demand for him and others is the resignation of MPSC Chairman Vivek Bhimanwar. With the government on the backfoot since the NEET paper leak protests, the Opposition, including the Congress, NCP SP, Maharashtra Navnirman Sena and the Cockroach Janta Party, has lent its weight to the MPSC protests. Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil has also spoken up for the aspirants. At least one leader of the ruling coalition, Shiv Sena MP Omraje Nimbalkar, has visited the protest site. He promised the aspirants that he would take up their demand to remove the MPSC chief personally with the CM. On Monday, in one of its biggest concessions to the demands of the aspirants, the Fadnavis government sent a recommendation to Governor Jishnu Dev Varma proposing a committee to examine the conduct of former and incumbent MPSC chairpersons and members. The CM had earlier said Bhimanwar held a constitutional post and hence could not be removed arbitrarily. His recommendation to the Governor was made under Article 317 of the Constitution, which deals with the removal and suspension of chairpersons and members of public service commissions. On Wednesday, hearing a petition by some Pune residents, the Bombay High Court said it was the governments duty to ensure that public recruitment exams are conducted impartially, adding If they students lack opportunities and believe there has been hanky panky, they have the right to agitate. Because they have given hours of study. The protesters are students. not anti-social elements. A drug inspector exam On June 12, results were declared for the drug inspector posts exam conducted by the MPSC in March, selecting 506 applicants for the interview round. A little over a month after the results came out, NCP SP MLA Rohit Pawar held a press conference claiming that the paper had been leaked. It took another month before the MPSC admitted this had happened, and on August 25, it cancelled the recruitment process. By then, of the 506 who qualified for the interview stage, interviews had been conducted for 488 and a provisional general merit list of 485 had been declared. Soon after, the State Services Main Exam 2025 conducted by the MPSC in November last year for 139 vacancies, whose result shortlisting candidates for interviews was declared on August 25 this year, came under a cloud. Widespread protests alleged irregularities in the evaluation of questions requiring descriptive answers-a new format introduced only last year-and questioned the unusual variations in marks. On September 10, Rohit Pawar held another press conference, where he claimed MPSC chief Bhimanwar was close to Fadnavis, and that his record was marked by several controversies. Bhimanwar defended himself saying he took charge of the MPSC only in April this year, and that the alleged irregularities predated his tenure. On September 11, in a further escalation, members of the Maratha outfit Sambhaji Brigade blackened the face of then MPSC secretary Mahendra Harpalkar at the commissions head office in Navi Mumbai. On September 28, the MPSC announced postponement of the State Services Main Exam 2026, which was to begin on October 3, citing requests from aspirants, parents, student organisations and elected representatives. It also said it would re-evaluate the answer sheets for the 2025 exam, and deferred the Maharashtra Civil Engineering Main Examination 2026 and the Maharashtra Group-B Non-Gazetted Main Examination, without announcing revised schedules for any of the three. Damage control By mid-August, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis had already announced a complete review of the MPSC system. As part of this, a seven-member committee was asked to visit each Revenue Division, consult students, representatives of educational institutions and other stakeholders, and submit a report by the end of the year. With tempers rising, on October 2, the government transferred Harpalkar. While the government seems to have relented on its position regarding Bhimanwar now, the protesters are also divided over their main demands. If for one group, the main thing is the MPSC chiefs removal, another wants the descriptive pattern of exams scrapped, while yet another opposes any return to the objective format. One of the members of the second group of protesters, Dhuldev Tele, 27, says the wide variation in the Mains marks showed that the MPSC lacked the mechanism and experts to evaluate descriptive papers fairly. But Amar Khose 21, who says he has spent lakhs of rupees preparing for the State Services Main Exam since 2023, is opposed to a change in format. Preparing for an optional subject alone cost him Rs 70,000, he says, and now the MPSC has decided it will not be a part of the 2027 exam. If the Mains shift to the objective pattern too, it will be a major setback for lakhs like me who have studied hard for the descriptive format, Khose says. Madhuri Netake 29, an aspirant from Karjat, says the cancellations could not have come at a worse time. Most protesters belong to agrarian families from rural regions like Marathwada, Vidarbha and Western Maharashtra, which are already battling drought. The financial burden is just getting heavier, she says.

articleTitle: JD(U) vs JD(U) in MLC polls: How a feud handed Prashant Kishor a chance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JD(U) vs JD(U) in MLC polls: How a feud handed Prashant Kishor a chance
description: Mokama MLA Anant Singh, who has a long-standing rivalry with JD(U)’s official candidate Neeraj Kumar, has thrown his weight behind Jan Suraaj Party’s Anuj Singh.
body_raw: Even as elections to eight MLC seats in Bihar are set to be held on October 23, the Patna Graduate constituency has emerged as the most closely watched contest not because of a conventional face-off between political rivals, but due to the fight effectively turning into a JDU versus JDU battle. The Janata Dal Uniteds official candidate, Neeraj Kumar, is facing an open challenge from fellow party MLA from Mokama, Anant Singh, who is campaigning for the Jan Suraaj Party JSP nominee, Anuj Singh. Neeraj, who is also the JDU chief spokesperson, is seeking a fourth-consecutive term from the Patna Graduates seat. But Anant, who shares a long-standing rivalry with Neeraj, has been campaigning for Anuj. What has made the situation particularly awkward for the JDU is the reluctance of its top leadership to intervene. Both Neeraj and Anant are from Mokama and their rivalry predates their association with the JDU. In the 2015 Assembly elections, Neeraj had unsuccessfully contested against Anant, who won as an Independent. Singh, who has faced several criminal cases, had also drawn criticism from Neeraj in the past. Now, with Singh openly campaigning against the partys official candidate, the JDU has so far stopped short of taking disciplinary action against him. The rebellion has given JSP founder Prashant Kishor an opening. Kishor has thrown an open challenge to Neeraj, saying the JSP would withdraw its candidate if former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar issued an authentic video message backing Neerajs candidature. If Neeraj Kumar gets Nitish Kumar to issue an authentic video message supporting his candidature, we will withdraw our candidate from the Patna Graduates seat, Kishor said, stressing that the video should not be AI-generated. Kishor smells chance Kishor has stepped up his campaign, making education the centrepiece of his pitch. He has also promised job guarantees, drawing on his campaign in Bankipur, where he had promised to facilitate at least 10,000 private-sector jobs over five years. The JSP believes Anants support could significantly alter the dynamics of the contest. With Union minister Rajeev Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh and JDU national working president Sanjay Kumar Jha refusing to intervene and Anant fully backing us, who knows, we could do a Bankipur in the Patna Graduate seat, a JSP source said. For Neeraj, the contest is a sharp departure from his earlier elections. The Patna Graduates seat, covering parts of Patna, Nalanda and Nawada and around 80,000 registered graduate voters, was virtually a cakewalk for him in the 2008, 2014 and 2020 MLC elections. Neeraj, once considered close to Lalan Singh, is now fighting the election without the organisational backing he might have expected. A source close to him said the partys inaction over Anant Singhs campaigning was difficult to understand. It is not rocket science to understand who is goading Anant. It is also surprising that the party has not initiated any disciplinary action against him for anti-party activities. However, Neeraj has faced party infighting in past elections and still won, the source said. Anant, for his part, remains unapologetic about backing the JSP candidate. Neeraj has opposed me in at least four of my elections despite being a fellow JDU member. I faced the Ladma Arms Act case because of him. There is no question of backing out of my support for the JSP candidate, he said. Not my battle Jha, meanwhile, sought to distance himself from the dispute. It is a matter concerning areas under the Lok Sabha seat Munger of Lalan Singh. It is up to him to see how the matter can be sorted out, he said. Lalan Singh, however, also ruled out direct intervention. We heard what our national working president said. But Anant has his own concerns. It is not for me to intervene in such matters, he told reporters. There are, nevertheless, factors that could work in Neerajs favour. Anants influence remains largely confined to pockets of Mokama and parts of Nawada. Neeraj has also played a significant role in enrolling graduate voters. Besides Lalan Singh, senior JDU leaders, including Jha, Bihar minister Shravan Kumar and Nishant Kumar, have campaigned for him. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is also expected to campaign for Neeraj in the final phase. The RJD has fielded Dilip Kumar, who contested the previous election as a Congress candidate. The internal JDU battle is creating confusion among voters and will definitely help our candidate. It also tells a lot about the internal problems within the NDA and JDU, RJD national spokesperson Subodh Kumar Mehta said. The elections to four Graduates constituencies - Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi - and four Teachers constituencies - Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran - cover 30 districts and around 150 Assembly constituencies. A total of 164 candidates are in the fray across the eight seats, the results for which will be declared on October 27. The Bihar Legislative Council has a strength of 75.

articleTitle: RBI’s focus on inflation is timely
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI’s focus on inflation is timely
description: On Wednesday, with the Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India raising the repo rate by 25 basis points, it moved up from 5.25 per cent to 5.5 per cent. A higher repo rate is expected to make borrowing more costly for everyone and thus acts as a drag on economic activity. The […]
body_raw: On Wednesday, with the Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India raising the repo rate by 25 basis points, it moved up from 5.25 per cent to 5.5 per cent. A higher repo rate is expected to make borrowing more costly for everyone and thus acts as a drag on economic activity. The decision to make the first hike of the repo rate since February 2023 was not only unanimous - all six members of the MPC voted in favour - but also widely expected. The less obvious but perhaps more consequential change was the shift in the RBIs stance from neutral to calibrated tightening. The last time the RBI assumed this stance was exactly eight years ago. The RBIs primary mandate, as Governor Sanjay Malhotra has underlined, is to ensure price stability while keeping in view economic growth. Since the last policy review in August, the situation has changed on both these counts, necessitating a change in policy. On economic growth, the Indian economy has surprised everyone by showing resilience despite a worsening global context. The 7.8 per cent growth in Gross Domestic Product during the first quarter April, May, June surprised on the upside when the data was released at the end of August. This has led the RBI to bump up the full-year 2026-27 forecast from 6.7 per cent, as pencilled in the August policy, to 7.1 per cent now. But notwithstanding the domestic growth momentum, the situation has become considerably more challenging from the point of view of inflation, thanks to the sudden re-escalation of the West Asia conflict in September and the consequent hardening and volatility in global crude prices. Making the domestic inflation outlook worse are the deficient Southwest monsoon and El Nino conditions. Retail inflation has been going up steadily through the year, breaching the 4 per cent RBI target level. In fact, the RBI now expects it to touch 6 per cent by the end of December with full-year inflation around 5.2 per cent. Given that growth is robust even as inflation is trending upwards and beyond the RBI target, raising the repo rate in a bid to dampen overall demand in the economy and prevent inflation becoming more broad-based is timely. What is even more welcome is the shift in the RBIs stance. It suggests that the RBI is squarely focussed on dealing with a possible spike in inflation. Simply put, interest rate cuts are off the table for the time being, and the RBI has signalled the start of a rate hike cycle, given that globally other central banks are expected to raise interest rates in the coming months.

articleTitle: The universe whispers through ghost particles
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The universe whispers through ghost particles
description: His work has used neutrinos to probe some of the universe’s hitherto most inaccessible environments, helping open a new window on the cosmos.
body_raw: For centuries, astronomy has essentially been the science of observing light. However, some of the universes most consequential events take place in environments so dense or violent that photons cannot escape. Could the universe be observed through something other than light? In 1930, when Austrian physicist Wolfgang Pauli proposed the existence of an elusive particle to explain a mystery in radioactive decay, he was laying the foundations for a new way of exploring the cosmos. The ghost particle called the neutrino was detected two decades later, and the quest to understand it has since been rewarded with a string of Nobel Prizes. On Tuesday, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, which awards the Nobel Prize in Physics, recognised another pioneer in the field - Belgian-American astrophysicist Francis Halzen. His work has used neutrinos to probe some of the universes hitherto most inaccessible environments, helping open a new window on the cosmos. Neutrinos have tiny masses, carry no electric charge and interact so weakly with matter that billions pass through the Earth - and our bodies - without leaving a trace. These particles can escape from the dense interiors of exploding stars and other extreme cosmic environments, carrying information about places that conventional telescopes cannot see. Halzen recognised this potential. His pioneering work led to the IceCube Observatory, an enormous neutrino detector buried deep beneath the Antarctic ice. Rather than building a conventional telescope, scientists effectively turned a cubic kilometre of natural ice at the South Pole into a detector, embedding more than 5,000 optical sensors in it. Almost every neutrino passes straight through the ice. But on the rare occasion when one sheds its shyness, the resulting flash of light can give information on the particles travel path. In 2013, IceCube provided evidence for a flux of high-energy neutrinos originating beyond the solar system. Halzens work demonstrated that sometimes the way to see farther is not to build a more powerful eye, but to learn to detect what the universe is whispering through particles that pass silently through it. The next frontier is multi-messenger astronomy, in which neutrinos can be studied alongside light, gravitational waves and cosmic rays. Together, these cosmic messengers could reveal the workings of black holes, exploding stars and other extreme objects that remain invisible to any single form of observation.

articleTitle: She led the way to the top, that’s her legacy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: She led the way to the top, that’s her legacy
description: Harmanpreet helped India believe it belonged at the top. Mandhana has to make sure that belief does not fade — and turns into a habit of winning.
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaurs contribution as captain of the womens cricket team cannot be measured only by the ODI World Cup trophy she lifted last year. It can be seen in the way the team began to carry itself on the biggest stages. When Harmanpreet took over, India had already reached two ODI World Cup finals. But there was still a sense that the team had to prove it belonged among the best. During her captaincy, the results began to follow more consistently. India reached the 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, the 2020 T20 World Cup final and the 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal before going all the way in the 2025 ODI World Cup. The journey was not smooth. Harmanpreets batting became less consistent, and her decisions were often questioned. But she remained at the centre of the team through the difficult periods. Her leadership was driven by her passion for the game and a strong belief in the players around her. The World Cup win turned that belief into reality. Now, as Smriti Mandhana takes over, she inherits a team that has tasted success and knows what is expected at the highest level. Mandhana cannot and should not try to recreate Harmanpreets leadership style. She will have to lead in her own way. But she will be expected to protect the confidence that has been built and take it further. That is the challenge. Harmanpreet helped India believe it belonged at the top. Mandhana has to make sure that belief does not fade - and turns into a habit of winning. After back-to-back group-stage exits at the T20 World Cup, winning a title in the shortest format will be a priority.

articleTitle: Protect the referee, even as you question the decision
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Protect the referee, even as you question the decision
description: The ECI is our archon. Its job is not to decide who should win — 140 crore Indians decide that.
body_raw: In every game, you can abuse the player. You cannot abuse the referee. If you do, the game ends. Today in India, we are abusing the referee. The Election Commission of India ECI is not just another bureaucracy. It is the core of democracy. To protect it is not to support any party it is to support the game itself. This wisdom is not new. It is in our Vedas, it was in Rome, and it was in Greece. The Rig Veda does not start with a king. It starts with two institutions Sabha and samiti. Samiti was the people - the voters. Sabha was the council of elders, the learned, the impartial who ensured the samiti could meet freely and choose freely. The Atharva Veda prays Sabha cha me samiti cha ma avatu - may my sabha and samiti protect me. The sabha had no army, no kingdom. Its power came from only one thing - trust. If the sabha was seen as biased, the samiti collapsed and the janapada broke. The ECI is our modern sabha. It has no seats to contest, no vote bank to protect. Its only capital is credibility. When we chip away at that credibility for political points, we are not hitting at an office in Nirvachan Sadan, but at the idea of sabha itself. The Vedas also gave us a method Tarka and shastrartha. Debate fiercely, but accept the decision of the sabha. The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad shows King Janaka hosting a great debate where Yajnavalkya is questioned by everyone, including women scholars like Gargi. He answers. The debate ends, and his authority is higher, not lower, because he submitted to questioning. The ECI must be questioned. But after questioning, it must be obeyed. That is dharma. The Romans were the greatest bureaucrats. They knew democracy needs a clean voter list more than a popular leader. They created the office of censor. The censor was not the consul who fought wars. He was more powerful. He prepared the census - the list of citizens. He could remove a senator by marking him with nota censoria. He was elected for 18 months, but his list lasted for 5 years. Why did Romans give so much power to two men who did nothing but count? Because they understood If the voter list is corrupt, the republic is corrupt. When we in India politicise the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, or the deletion and addition of voters, we forget Rome. A clean roll will always be painful. Someones name will be deleted. Someones booth will shift. That pain is the price of a republic. Attack the error with data, appeal to the ECI, go to court - but do not attack the censor itself. If the censor falls, the republic becomes an empire. Athens, the mother of democracy, had a brilliant safeguard. They did not even trust elections fully. Most offices in Athens were filled not by election, but by lot - by lottery among citizens - under the supervision of the eponymous archon. Why? Because they feared that elections could be manipulated by orators. Their safeguard was procedure. The archon did not decide who won he ensured the procedure was followed. The ECI is our archon. Its job is not to decide who should win - 140 crore Indians decide that. Its job is to ensure the lottery of democracy - the EVM, the VVPAT, the ink, the booth - remains pure. Every dharma is two-sided. If the players must not abuse the referee, the referee must also remember why it wears black. In the Vedic sabha, the elder did not speak more than necessary - he spoke through decisions, after listening to both sides. In Rome, the censor was respected because he applied nota censoria equally, even to his own kin. In Greece, the archon was trusted because he drew lots in the open agora, not behind closed doors. The referee protects itself best by transparency, by same-rule-same-speed for all jerseys, and by a dignified restraint that lets the order speak louder than the press note. The moment a referee starts explaining too much, defending too much, or being seen too much, the crowd begins to doubt the whistle. The referees work best when we see them stable, silent, and steady. I am a doctor, not a psephologist. In the ICU, I see what happens when sodium - a single ion that no one notices - falls from 141 to 123. The body seizes and the brain starves. Sodium is invisible till it is low. The ECI is the sodium of our democracy. Invisible when it works, catastrophic when it fails. You can disagree with an order. That is your right in a democracy. File an affidavit, produce data, go to the Supreme Court. That is Vedic tarka, Roman provocatio, Greek elenchus. But do not call for burning down the office that guards the list. Rome tried that. When Augustus destroyed the power of the censors, the republic never returned. Protect the referee, even as you question the decision. That is the only way the game continues. The writer is an endocrinologist and public health physician based in Mumbai

articleTitle: Centre approves Rs 65 crore for geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies
articleFeaturedImageAlt: geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies, unauthorised colonies, Delhi Revenue and Imaging Survey, Spatial Technology Initiative, DRISHTI, GIS-based survey, Rekha Gupta, Manohar Lal, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Delhi government is implementing the PM-UDAY (Pradhan Mantri-Unauthorized Colonies in Delhi Awas Adhikar Yojana), aimed at granting property rights to residents of the city's over 1,500 unauthorised colonies.
body_raw: Nearly three months after Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta wrote to Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal requesting an assistance to regularise unauthorised colonies, the Centre has approved Rs 65 crore under Delhi Revenue and Imaging Survey, Spatial Technology Initiative DRISHTI for GIS-based survey and mapping of such colonies. Delhi government is implementing the PM-UDAY Pradhan Mantri-Unauthorized Colonies in Delhi Awas Adhikar Yojana, aimed at granting property rights to residents of the citys over 1,500 unauthorised colonies. Moreover,PM-UDAY cells in 13 districts, and a headquarter, will be set up to expedite registration of properties in unauthorised colonies. The geographic information system GIS survey is required under PM-UDAY scheme to verify, map and authenticate property boundaries and geo-coordinates within Delhis notified unauthorised colonies. The technology-driven survey will make mapping of properties more transparent, systematic and time-bound. The project has an estimated total cost of Rs 65 crore, of which Rs 52 crore, or 80 per cent, will be provided as a grant from the Urban Development Fund UDF of the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, the CMO said. The remaining Rs 13 crore, will be contributed by Delhi governments revenue department that will be responsible for implementing the project, it said. The initiative will help make the mapping and documentation process related to properties under PM-UDAY scheme more systematic and time-bound. The chief minister said the PM-UDAY scheme is not merely a process of issuing property-related documents but also an important means of providing legal security over homes and property rights to lakhs of families living in Delhis unauthorised colonies.

articleTitle: Caught cheating? Let student finish exam: IIT Bombay panel after suicide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT-B student dies by suicide, iit Bombay student dies by suicide, IIT Bombay, IIT Bombay students protest, ChatGPT, examination question paper on ChatGPT, Mumbai news, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The aim was to have guidelines in place before the remaining mid-semester papers are held this weekend. The committee presented its interim report at a special meeting of the IIT Senate on Wednesday.
body_raw: If a student is caught cheating during an exam, the invigilator should take away the related material and record the incident, but allow the student to complete the paper with a fresh answer booklet. The quick response team QRT helpline should be alerted so the student has support after the exam. These are among the proposals put forward by a committee, set up after the recent student suicide at IIT-Bombay, in its interim report, The Indian Express has learnt. IIT Director Shireesh Kedare had set up the eight-member commitee - four faculty members and four students - to revisit exam conduct rules, days after Sahil Wakode, a Second Year BTech student who was allegedly found using a cellphone during a mid-semester exam, died by suicide on September 18. The aim was to have guidelines in place before the remaining mid-semester papers are held this weekend. The committee presented its interim report at a special meeting of the IIT Senate on Wednesday. The Senate has also decided to go back to the institutes2015 punishment rules until a new set is drafted, putting on hold the stricter rules it adopted this year. Under the July rules, a student found carrying a phone into an exam got an FR or fail and repeat grade and suspension for a semester. Under the 2015 rules, carrying a phone in the exam hall would mean loss of one grade, and using it would mean an FR. A student caught talking to another during an exam got a straight FR under the July rules. In 2015, it meant loss of one grade unless there was other evidence, such as identical answers. The interim report proposes that the invigilator should record the incident in a prescribed form, give the student a chance to give their version, and alert a quick response team QRT so the student has support, it has said. Seized items such as phones may be photographed. The report proposes limits to the invigilators role. An important point to note When a suspected unauthorised academic practice is noticed, the invigilators responsibility is to stop that activity, collect related material and record details to the extent possible. Further proceedings will be carried out later by the Disciplinary Action Committee as per norms, it says. Protesting students have alleged procedural lapses in how Wakodes case was handled. The invigilator is to seize the material with as little conversation with the student as possible. If there is doubt about the students identity, the invigilator can photograph them at the desk, the report says. When the exam ends, the invigilator should fill a form describing the incident and the evidence collected. The student can record their version on another form, at a designated venue with additional staff present. The forms, which the report is prescribing for the first time, are meant to keep a complete record of each case, sources said. These will be sent to the head of the department conducting the course, along with the seized material and the original answer book. When the student leaves the exam hall, the invigilator must alert the QRT helpline, giving the students name, roll number, course and venue, the report says. The idea is to ensure the student isnt alone after such an incident, sources said. Until now, the institute followed procedures framed in 2015, which had a single paragraph on what an invigilator should do. With no central monitoring, each department handled cases in its own way, sources said. The committee has also proposed stricter exam hall rules. No phones, smartwatches, earphones or other gadgets, and no bags, notes or books will be allowed inside the exam building. Teaching assistants cannot bring phones into the hall. Halls are to be monitored through CCTV, only one student can step out at a time for bio-break, and entry will close 30 minutes after the exam begins. According to sources, members broadly agreed with the report but made several suggestions, and a final version will be prepared once these are considered. Senate meetings are usually open only to members, but given the importance of the matter, all faculty members were invited, sources added.

articleFeaturedImageAlt: GST regime, GST regime Arrest powers, GST Council meeting today, GST defaulters, Goods and Services tax (GST), GST, GST rates, GST returns, GST impacts, GST Council meeting, Indian express business, business news, current affairs
description: Back provision for ‘civil arrest’ in serious GST violation, warn of ‘toothless’ regime
body_raw: As states and the Centre converge in Delhi for the 57th Goods and Services Tax GST Council meeting Thursday to discuss process reforms that include a proposal mandating the removal of the arrest provision, at least five major states are learnt to have expressed concern over any sweeping curtailment of the taxmens powers. Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh are among states that have expressed reservations regarding the scrapping of arrest powers under GST in multiple meetings held between the state and Central government officials in the run-up to the Council meeting. A key demand by states has been that the indirect tax regime should not be rendered toothless, and pre-prosecution arrests should be graded with an additional layer enabling civil arrest in cases of serious violations, a state minister told The Indian Express. While the proposal entails removal of arrest altogether, except for prosecution, states are asking for an additional layer of arrest powers even in the pre-prosecution stage. Many states feel that taking away such powers will make it completely toothless. While there can be a provision for no arrest in normal cases, there can be a provision for civil arrest in cases of serious violations under GST, the minister said. The Council meeting got deferred by a day to Thursday, and the additional day in between is learnt to have been utilised by Union government officials to reach out to GST chief commissioners across zones to iron out residual issues, especially concerns over the no-arrest proposal. On Thursday, the Council, in a bid to boost investor sentiment and allay concerns about overreach by tax authorities, is set to take up the proposal to decriminalise offences including removal of arrests, as was reported by The Indian Express last Sunday. The underlying intent, an official said, is to make enforcement work through money rather than custody, and through a system that detects fraud rather than a provision that deters it. As per the proposal to be discussed at the Council meeting, tax disputes are aimed to be resolved through civil consequences, namely recovery of tax, interest for the delay, and penalty, while keeping prosecution available for a higher threshold of Rs 5 crore as against Rs 1 crore at present. The idea is to focus on detection and not deterrence. The proposal is to remove pre-prosecution arrests and the Council will debate it. In the last 8-9 months, several rounds of discussions were held between states and the Centre, including three national coordination meetings. So far, 3-4 states have expressed their concerns, especially about how they will get to trace offenders. The Council will take a final call on the form that the arrest powers should take, keeping in mind the criticism regarding threats of criminalisation, the official said.

articleTitle: In every trans woman’s life, there is a Dorothy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: In every trans woman’s life, there is a Dorothy
description: To shift the collective consciousness and urge the public to view every person as human, Tamil cinema needs hundreds of more films like Dorothy, Super Deluxe, and Natchathiram Nagargiradhu
body_raw: A society disturbed by a kiss must first ask why it is unable to see a trans womans pain, love, and humanity. The Tamil film Dorothy, directed by Karthik Subbaraj, engages with a society still struggling to recognise transgender people as complete human beings. What troubles us is not the debate surrounding the film, but what this has chosen to focus on. A story exploring caste, patriarchy, family, systemic violence, toxic masculinity, and gender politics has been reduced to one question How can a trans woman kiss a man? Why does that kiss spark such moral panic? Calling it two men kissing reveals a refusal to recognise a trans woman as a woman. But beyond that, why should intimacy cause such discomfort? Set in the 1990s, Dorothy reminds us of the real-life Dorothys whose stories were never documented, living through an era where gender, caste, and class inflicted severe violence on womens bodies. Through a sharp intergenerational lens, Subbaraj confronts a centuries-old system now struggling to digest the truth. This conflict forces a deeper inquiry into identity Who is Dorothy to Subbu? Is she a mother? A sister? A sister-in-law? Before demanding answers, society must face a simpler question Do you accept Subbu as Dorothy? Change is not an overnight process, but opposing and ignoring the struggles of another human remains deeply inhumane. A section of viewers forgets how Subbu struggled to guard her kaitiakitanga, her protective, nurturing femininity in a male-dominated world, only to obsess over a single kiss in the final scene. In truth, Dorothy represents the collective feminine that nurtures and protects a trans womans emerging identity. In real life, Dorothy takes many forms Mothers, mentors, female educators. In every trans womans life, there is a Dorothy most often, she is another woman. Music is a vital pillar of this sanctuary. For decades, mainstream Tamil cinema offered transgender and queer people little more than ridicule. In Dorothy, Ilaiyaraajas score feels like a balm to those wounds. Music provides a space where trans women safely explore their identity, historically through Ilaiyaraaja and Swarnalatha compositions like Enulle enulle, and Muthumani, now a trans anthem. In many ways, Ilaiyaraaja himself embodies Dorothy through the emotional shelter his art bestows. The films visual grammar speaks volumes. Karthiks choices such as the slow-motion parotta and salna sequence or the sharp presence of the chappathi kalli prickly pear cactus vividly convey the weight of toxic masculinity enforced upon trans bodies. This depth extends to performance and casting. Sanaths performance deserves appreciation for its vulnerability and commitment. Yet, when cisgender actors consistently receive accolades for portraying transgender characters, it raises an undeniable question Where does that leave trans actors who have spent years fighting simply to be cast? At the same time, Dorothys inclusion of trans actors and the international platform given to artists like Jeeva is meaningful. True representation must extend beyond who plays the lead it must be about who gets access to opportunities. Dorothy is a gift and a necessary step forward. To shift the collective consciousness and urge the public to view every person as human, Tamil cinema needs hundreds of more films like Dorothy, Super Deluxe, and Natchathiram Nagargiradhu. Negha is an actor, writer, and co-founder of Queer Casting, Angamuththu is a law student

articleTitle: Up to 30% of cotton area under ‘illegal’ GM hybrids, finds study
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GM cotton hybrids, GM cotton varieties, cotton area under illegal GM hybrids, cotton, cotton production, cotton farmers, FSII-NSAI study, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Farmers planting hybrids incorporating unapproved herbicide-tolerant and Vip3 Bt genes.
body_raw: More than a quarter of the total area cultivated under cotton in India comprises illegal hybrids incorporating unapproved genetically modified GM traits, including resistance to glyphosate herbicide. Out of the 114.8 lakh hectares lh area sown under cotton by Indian farmers in 2025-26, an estimated 26.2-29 lh, i.e. 24-30, was of hybrids containing unauthorised herbicide-tolerant HT or Bacillus thuringiensis Bt genes, according to a field-based study commissioned by the Federation of Seed Industry of India FSII and National Seed Association of India NSAI. India currently allows farmers to grow GM cotton hybrids varieties containing only two genes - cry1Ac and cry2Ab - that are isolated from Bt, a soil bacterium. These genes code for proteins toxic to certain bollworm insect pests. But the FSII-NSAI study shows farmers are also planting the seeds of hybrids that contain cp4-epsps and Vip3A genes. Both these are alien genes, whose harbouring in any crops has not been approved by the government. The cp4-epsps gene, sourced from another soil-dwelling agrobacterium, makes cotton plants tolerant to glyphosate. This herbicide cannot be sprayed on normal cotton, as the chemical does not distinguish between the crop and weeds. The Vip3A gene is derived from Bt, but works differently from the cry1Ac cry2Ab genes and is said to effectively control a broader spectrum of bollworm larvae. The FSSI-NSAI study has been based on 227 geo-tagged seed leaf samples collected from fields of 984 farmers across 16 districts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh AP and Rajasthan. The 16 hotspot districts were identified using a combination of secondary data sources, including glyphosate sale trends, farmer interactions and seed market intelligence. The testing of the samples for gene identification was conducted using dipstick lateral flow assays and ELISA enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. We found the HT cp4-epsps gene to be present in 72.69 of the field samples, with this as high as 88.64 for Telangana, 70.92 for Maharashtra, 62.86 for AP and 57.14 for Rajasthan. It indicates widespread adoption of HT technology by farmers for weed management, despite the government not authorising this GM trait, said Bhagirath Choudhary, director of the Jodhpur Rajasthan-based South Asia Biotechnology Centre that undertook the study. The demand for the unapproved HT gene technology has been driven by the acute shortage of labour and high manual weeding costs. Farmers have decisively shifted towards glyphosate-based weed management enabled by illegal HTBt cotton technology. They are typically applying 2-3 sprays per season that costs Rs 750-850 per acre, as against Rs 12,000-15,000 through manual weeding, Choudhary noted. Laboratory analysis of samples apart, the decline in sales of legal Bt cotton hybrid seeds - from 596 lakh packets in 2022-23 to 463 lakh packs in 2025-26 each packet contains 450 grams of seeds - is also proof of the high acceptance of HT hybrids by farmers. This has been accompanied by a significant 29 jump in imports of glyphosate, from 27,721 kilolitres in 2024-25 to 35,642 kilolitres in 2025-26. The FSSI-NSAI study has estimated the unauthorised HTBt seed market in India to have expanded from around 35 lakh packets in 2017-18 to 82-88 lakh packets in 2025-26. At an average price of Rs 1,000 per packet, this market would be conservatively valued at Rs 820-880 crore. Equally interesting is the planting of cotton hybrids expressing the Vip3 Bt gene. We found 53.74 of our 227 field samples testing positive for this next-generation insect-resistance gene. Its presence was 58.16 in Maharashtra, 54.29 in AP, 57.14 in Rajasthan and 38.64 in Telangana. The driver here seems to be effectiveness against pink bollworm, with the first-generation Bt hybrids becoming vulnerable to this insect pest, said Choudhary. Simply put, the market for illegal GM cotton seeds is growing, with both farmers and a sophisticated supplier network bypassing the countrys established biosafety and regulatory approval system.

articleTitle: First hike in over 3 years may not be last; repo rate can rise by another 75 basis points
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI repo rate, RBI repo rate hike, RBI monetary policy, RBI MPC, Monetary Policy Committee, RBI policy stance, calibrated tightening, RBI interest rate hike, India interest rates, India inflation, CPI inflation India, WPI inflation India, retail inflation India, wholesale inflation India, core inflation India, inflation expectations, inflation generalisation, RBI inflation forecast, RBI GDP forecast, India GDP growth, India economic growth, Sanjay Malhotra RBI, RBI policy October 2026, RBI policy August 2026, hawkish RBI, dovish RBI, interest rate cycle India, rate hike India, inflation and interest rates, El Nino India inflation, weak monsoon inflation, memory chip prices India, West Asia war inflation, US Federal Reserve rate hike, global interest rates, bank rate India, policy repo rate, Express Explained,
description: RBI is likely to tighten the monetary policy with a series of rate hikes if the situation on the price front doesn’t improve in the coming months. This means interest rates on loans will increase further, which in turn can dampen the demand conditions in the economy.
body_raw: THE 25 basis points hike in key policy rate, the first in more than three years, may not be the last. A shift in the monetary stance from neutral to calibrated tightening is a clear warning that the central bank will tighten the screws if inflationary pressures refuse to ease. Bankers and economists are now expecting another 50-75 basis points hike in the policy rate in the coming reviews. In other words, the RBI is likely to tighten the monetary policy with a series of rate hikes if the situation on the price front doesnt improve in the coming months. This means interest rates on loans will increase further, which in turn can dampen the demand conditions in the economy. It MPC underscored that given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said after the MPC meeting. With borrowing costs already elevated, another rate hike would exert additional pressure on households, businesses and an economy trying to sustain momentum in a challenging external environment. The RBIs message leaves little room for complacency. By signalling further tightening, the central bank has effectively chosen to prioritise inflation control over the immediate concerns of growth and credit demand. The consequences could be particularly punishing for consumers and businesses carrying existing debt, as higher interest rates translate into steeper EMIs, costlier working capital and weaker investment. If the MPC follows through on its hawkish stance, the next round of tightening could expose just how much economic pain the RBI is willing to tolerate in its battle to bring inflation under control. Malhotra said the duration and extent of the rate hike cycle would be contingent on the actual growth-inflation developments and outlook, especially that of underlying inflation, the extent of broadening of price pressures and second round effects of the supply shock, as also the impact of demand impulses. The MPC observation clearly indicates that another rate hike might be in the offing in the December policy review, depending on the economic conditions, analysts said in initial reactions. HDFC Bank economists expect the RBI to hike rates by another 50-75 bps over the coming meetings expect back-to-back increases in consecutive meetings instead of a staggered approach. The need for a more aggressive rate hike cycle greater than 100-125bps hinges on how the West Asia conflict progresses from here on how durable and strong is the second order impact of inputs costs increases on retail inflation evolution of El Nino conditions and impact on winter crop and finally and how growth and demand impulses hold up in the face of global volatility and rate increases, the bank said. Given these factors, while a longer and higher rate hike cycle cannot be ruled out completely at this stage, we see it as a lower probability event, it said. While ICRAs baseline GDP growth projection 7.1 per cent for FY2027 is in line with the MPC, it believes that there are risks to the outlook arising from deficient monsoon rainfall, impact of rising global energy prices on corporate profits, and an adverse base owing to GST rate cuts in September 2025. ICRAs baseline estimate pencils in the CPI inflation at 5.0 per cent in FY2027, lower than the MPCs forecast. However, elevated crude oil prices could push inflation to 5.3-5.5 per cent, with the GDP growth moderating to 6.8 per cent in the fiscal. At present, we expect another rate hike of 25 bps in the December 2026 meeting, and a pause thereafter, unless there are sizeable negative surprises on the inflation front, ICRA said. Our estimates suggest that headline inflation will remain above 5.5 per cent YoY for three consecutive quarters starting in Q3 FY27, significantly above the RBIs medium-term target of 4 per cent YoY. As inflation accelerates, real policy rates are likely to turn negative, necessitating a recalibration of monetary policy, UBS Chief India Economist Tanvee Gupta Jain said. We expect a cumulative 50-75 bps rate hike cycle, with another 25bps hike likely in the December policy. Namrata Mittal, Chief Economist, SBI Funds Management, expects another cumulative 75 bps of hikes through the cycle, potentially taking the repo rate to 6.0 per cent, though she highlights that the global environment remains highly fluid. Malhotra further observed that in light of available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year, with headline CPI inflation expected to average almost 5.8 per cent in the next three quarters and core inflation projected at 4.4 per cent this financial year. In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative, he said.
